Query Parameters

API calls support the following query parameters, that will help you paginate and sort responses based on your specific data needs:

Name

Description

Type

Required

Default Value

Constraints

updated_since

A timestamp used to filter only the entities updated after the specified date and time.

string

No

One month prior to the current date.

It should be in the UTC timezone. ISO8601 format.

page_size

Specifies the number of entries returned per page.

int

No

50

Maximum of 100 entries per page.

page_cursor

Encodes the position for fetching the next page of results.

string

No

N/A

It must be a valid base64 string.

sorting_column

Column used to sort the results, based on the queried entity.

string

No

updated_at

Depending on the queried entity, only a limited array of sorting columns will be allowed.

sorting_order

Specifies the sorting order.

string

No

desc

Allowed values: asc, desc

Requests

The base URL of the API service follows the format:

/edu//

All requests should have x-api-key as a Header entry with the value of the API key. You can get the API key in the Developer Portal, from the Subscriptions section.

Example: To fetch two records per page for the applications entity, using a given cursor, filtering for records updated after January 1, 2024, and sorting by job_id in descending order, the API request would be:

curl –location ‘edu-api.joinhandshake.com’

–header ‘x-api-key: ’

Responses

The API follows standard HTTP status codes as per RFC 9110, and all responses are returned in JSON format.

Successful Response

Upon a successful request, the API returns a JSON object containing the queried entities and metadata for pagination with the following format:

  • data - an array containing the queried entities, where each record adheres to the structure described in the corresponding entity section from this resource.
  • meta - contains metadata related to the results:
    • next_cursor - cursor that can be used to navigate forwards in the dataset.
    • prev_cursor - cursor that can be used to navigate backward in the dataset. Example: For the request above, an example response would be:

{

“data”: [

{

“id”: 18797,

“job_id”: 11933,

“student_id”: 92579,

“employer_id”: 2423,

“status”: “pending”,

“applicable_type”: “Job”,

“withdrawn”: true,

“created_at”: “2025-03-19T10:14:44.90493-05:00”,

“updated_at”: “2025-03-19T10:14:51.908777-05:00”

},

{

“id”: 18793,

“job_id”: 11933,

“student_id”: 92579,

“employer_id”: 2423,

“status”: “pending”,

“applicable_type”: “Job”,

“withdrawn”: true,

“created_at”: “2025-03-17T14:29:29.617135-05:00”,

“updated_at”: “2025-03-17T14:29:34.236529-05:00”

}

],

“meta”: {

“next_cursor”: “eyJpZCIgOiAxODc5MywgInNvcnRpbmdfY29sdW1uX3ZhbHVlIiA6ICIyMDI1LTAzLTE3VDE5OjI5OjM0LjIzNjUyOSIsICJwYWdpbmF0aW9uX29yZGVyIiA6ICJmb3J3YXJkIn0=”,

“prev_cursor”: null

}

}

Error Response

In case of a failure, the API response has the following key-value format:

  • errors - an array of error objects. It supports handling multiple errors in a single response. Each error will adhere to the following structure:
    • status - The HTTP status code related to the error, represented as a string (e.g., “400”, “404”). It matches the HTTP response status code but is included in the body for clarity.
    • code - A custom, application-specific error code that provides a unique identifier for the type of error
    • detail - A detailed explanation of the error, providing specific context Example:

{

“errors”: [

{

“status”: 400,

“code”: “INVALID_PARAMETER_PAGE_CURSOR”,

“detail”: “The ‘page_cursor’ parameter is not valid.”

}

]

}

Applicant & Interview Management

Download Applications / Create a Resume Book

You can download applicant resumes, often referred to as a “resume book,” for one or more applicants from a job posting or on-campus interview.

Who can download application documents?

Basic employers

  • Owners and Recruiters can download applications only for jobs they have personally created. Jobs posted by other teammates will appear on your list, but are view-only.

  • After a job you personally created closes, the ability to download applications remains accessible for 30 days. To download applications beyond this period, you must upgrade to an eligible paid plan.

  • To download applications for jobs you did not create, you must upgrade to an eligible paid plan. On-campus employers, Plus, Pro, Essentials and Enterprise (formerly TES) customers

  • All users, except Representatives, can download applications for both their own jobs and those posted by teammates indefinitely, provided they have the appropriate permissions.

How do I access applicants?

Navigate to the job or interview where you want to download applications, then click the Applicants tab.

For a job, click the Applicants tab in the navigation bar at the top of the job posting page.

For an on-campus interview, the Applicants tab is in the upper-right corner of the page. Alternatively, click the Review Applicants button in the center of the page.

How do I download applications for a job?

  1. Check the box next to each applicant whose documents you want to download. To select all applicants, check the box in the upper-left corner of the table.

  2. Click the More dropdown above the applicant list.

  3. Select your preferred download format:

  • Download applicant packages (PDF): Downloads selected applicants’ documents as a single PDF file.
  • Download applicant packages (ZIP): Downloads selected applicants’ documents in ZIP format.
  • Download applicant data (CSV): Exports applicant data as a CSV file. Note: If no additional documents were requested (for example, a resume), the only option available will be Download applicant data (CSV).
  1. A black banner at the bottom of the page will confirm that your request is being processed, followed by “Download complete.” You can open the downloaded file immediately or access it later from your email.

How do I download applications for an on-campus interview?

  1. Check the box next to each applicant whose resume you want to download. To select all applicants, check the box in the upper-left corner of the table.

  2. Click the Export Documents button or the text Download Applicant Packages above the table.

  3. In the pop-up modal, select which documents you want to download (for example, resumes or cover letters), then click the Next button.

Note: Non-required documents may not be available for all applicants. For example, if you select “Cover Letter” but cover letters were not required in the application, they may not be included in the download.

  1. Click the Confirm button to confirm the action on the selected results.

  2. Handshake will prepare your download. Once it’s ready, click Your download is ready to review it immediately, or access it later via your email inbox.

Will I receive an email notification when my download is ready?

Yes. The applicant package will also be sent to the email address associated with your Handshake account.

The email includes the following:

From: Handshake handshake@notifications.joinhandshake.com

Subject: Handshake download: JOB TITLE Applications

Body:

“Hello NAME,

The bulk download you recently requested has completed. You can access the file below.

Bulk Download (blue hyperlinked) File type and size

Thank you,

The Handshake Team”

Note: If Handshake encounters issues converting some PDF documents, the email will include the following message: “Please note the following: there were issues converting PDF documents for some students. Please try downloading this package as a ZIP.”

Employer Missing Applications

If an applicant no longer appears in your list after you receive an application notification, there are a few possible reasons.

Why would an applicant disappear from my list?

The application was withdrawn

Applications in Handshake can be withdrawn by either the student or their school’s Career Center. When this happens, the student is removed from your applicant list.

The application was never fully submitted

Some schools require that documents, such as resumes, be reviewed and approved by the Career Center before an application is considered complete.

If the student confirms they applied and did not withdraw their application, their resume may still be pending review. In this case, the student should contact their Career Center to check the status of the resume review.

Why did I receive an application notification but the application is now missing?

If your notification preferences are set to receive an email each time a student applies, you will be notified when an application is first submitted.

However, you will not receive a notification if the application is later withdrawn or if it is pending document approval.

How do I follow up on a missing application?

If you have questions about an individual application, you can contact the applicant directly through Handshake. For instructions on how to send a message, read How to Send a Student a Message.

Guidelines for Writing Smart, Compliant AI Matching Criteria

Our AI-powered recommendations help you efficiently prioritize applicants by highlighting those who best meet the criteria you define for the role.

To ensure fairness, accuracy, and legal compliance, this guide will help you write effective, EEOC-compliant criteria and avoid common mistakes.

When using this feature, you must adhere to all applicable federal and state laws, including those that prohibit discrimination against protected classes.

What makes for good criteria?

High-quality sorting criteria should be:

  • Job-related: Clearly tied to the responsibilities or qualifications for the role.
  • Specific: Clear enough for the AI to understand and make meaningful matches.
  • Measurable or observable: Based on objective, verifiable factors, not subjective impressions.
  • EEOC-compliant: Aligned with equal opportunity hiring practices.

Examples of strong criteria

Here are a few examples that demonstrate how to write effective criteria:

  • “Proficient in Excel or Google Sheets”: This highlights a specific, job-relevant skill.
  • “Located in California or open to relocation”: A clear geographic preference.
  • “Has or is in progress of obtaining a Bachelor’s degree in Marketing or related field”: An objective educational requirement.
  • “1+ years of experience in customer support”: A measurable and observable qualification.

Common mistakes to avoid (with examples)

The system does not allow the following types of criteria inputs.

1. More than 10 criteria

Limit your criteria to 10 or fewer, per job.

✅ Focus on the most important requirements, such as top skills or location preferences.

2. Non-EEOC-compliant criteria

Avoid criteria that reference protected classes or could lead to discriminatory impact.

❌ Don’t write: “Looking for recent grads only,” “Must be under 30,” “US-born candidates”

✅ Instead say: “Must have graduated by May 2025,” “Open to early career professionals,” or “Authorized to work in the US”

Review the EEOC laws.

3. Subjective or vague language

Avoid criteria based on personal judgment or vague terms.

❌ Don’t write: “Must be a culture fit,” “Great attitude,” “Energetic and enthusiastic”.

✅ Instead say: “Experience collaborating in team environments,” or “Excellent written communication skills”.

4. Too little information

Single words or unclear phrases can’t be interpreted correctly.

❌ Don’t write: “Experienced” or “Ice cream”. The system will not understand what this means.

✅ Instead provide full context: “Experience working with frozen dessert products” (if relevant).

5. More than 100 characters per criteria

Limit each criteria to 100 characters or fewer, and focus on a single requirement, experience, or skill.

❌ Don’t write: “Experience in customer service, retail sales, order fulfillment, and using POS systems and CRMs”.

✅ Instead: Split into separate inputs. For example:

  • “Experience in customer service”
  • “Familiar with POS systems”
6. Phone number usage

Contact information is not relevant to applicant evaluation.

❌ Don’t write: “Call 555-123-4567”.

✅ Instead: Provide an actual qualification or experience instead.

7. Email address usage

The system cannot act on contact instructions.

❌ Don’t write: “Contact me at jane@company.com”.

✅ Instead: Use the employer contact options provided in your job posting or profile.

8. URL usage

The system does not extract information from links.

❌ Don’t write: “www.example.com/requirements”.

✅ Instead: Paste in the relevant information directly from the website into the edit field.

Tips for writing strong criteria

  • Start with skills, certifications, qualifications, or location preferences
  • Keep each input under 100 characters and focused on a single requirement
  • Ensure every criterion is job-related, objective, and non-discriminatory

Improving Applicant Response Rate

If you have received few or no applications, low response rates, or no candidates for a job posting on Handshake, use the steps below to increase applicant interest.

  1. Complete your brand page and job posting details

Fill in every available field on your brand page and job postings. Students are more likely to apply to a detailed job from a company with a complete brand page.

For your brand page:

  • Add your company mission, values, and culture so students can evaluate fit before applying

  • Include employee testimonials, videos, and behind-the-scenes content, since students research employer reputation before applying

  • Post relatable content such as day-in-the-life stories, career tips, and application advice

  • Respond to student comments and messages to build engagement and make your brand more approachable For your job descriptions:

  • Use a job title that matches how students actually search for the role, and keep it consistent everywhere you post it

  • List required skills rather than years of experience, since most entry-level candidates have limited work history

  • State the salary range, benefits, work schedule, and work location directly in the posting

  • Outline the application steps and estimated timeline so candidates know what to expect

  • Use inclusive language and avoid gendered terms, for example “engineer” instead of “hacker” Related resources:

  • Customizing your Brand Page

  • How to build an employer brand early talent loves

  • 5 tips to improve your job description to attract early talent

  1. Post your job to additional schools

Widen your talent pool by posting your job to more schools on Handshake. Review school recommendations to identify schools with student profiles that match your role.

Related resources:

  • How to Post a Job to Additional Schools
  • Posting a Job to Recommended Schools
  1. Search for and message qualified students directly

Rather than waiting for candidates to apply, search Handshake for students who match your job qualifications and message them directly. Use Talent Lists to save and organize candidates you want to reach. Personalize your outreach and include a clear call to action to increase reply rates.

Related resources:

  • A Guide to Talent List
  • How to Send a Student a Message
  • Messaging Best Practices
  1. Contact the Career Services Center at each school

If applicant numbers remain low after completing the steps above, contact the Career Services Center at each school where you posted the job. Career Services staff can share insight into low applicant volume or suggest ways to attract more candidates.

Related resources:

  • How to Contact a School

Managing Applicant Status

In Handshake, you can track and update each candidate’s progress throughout the application process.

Keeping applicant statuses up to date ensures you always have a clear view of where candidates are in the hiring process.

Who can access and manage applicants?

Basic employers:

  • Owners and Recruiters can update the status of applicants only for jobs they have personally created.

  • For jobs created by other teammates, applications will appear in the applicant list as view-only and cannot be updated. On-campus employers, Plus, Pro, Essentials and Enterprise (formerly TES) customers:

  • All users, except Representatives, can update the status of applicants for both their own jobs and those created by teammates, provided they have the appropriate permissions.

How do I access applicants?

Select the job for which you want to update the applicant status, then click on the Applicants tab.

  • Updates to an applicant’s status do not affect the job posting itself, including the application open and close dates.
  • Applicants are displayed in chronological order, with the most recent application at the top and the oldest at the bottom.
How applications are marked as reviewed

Applications with a blue dot are considered unreviewed. When you click on an applicant’s profile, the application automatically moves to Reviewed, and the blue dot is removed.

Note: Applications cannot be manually moved to Reviewed in bulk.

Mark an application as unreviewed

If you need to mark a reviewed applicant as unreviewed, open their profile and click the … menu in the upper-right corner, then select Mark as unreviewed.

Move applications to hired or rejected

Update status for a single applicant

  • Open the applicant’s profile.

  • Click the Move to dropdown in the upper-right corner of the profile panel, then select Rejected, Rejected (with message), or Hired. Update status for multiple applicants

  • Check the box next to each candidate’s name, or click Select all in the header to select every applicant in the list.

  • Click the More dropdown in the action bar above the applicant list, then select Move to hired, Move to rejected, or Move to rejected (with message).

Move applications to interviewing

Update status for a single applicant

  • Open the applicant’s profile.

  • Click the Move to dropdown in the upper-right corner of the profile panel, then select Interviewing or Interviewing (with message). Update status for multiple applicants

  • Check the box next to each candidate’s name, or click Select all in the header to select every applicant in the list.

  • Click Move to interviewing in the action bar above the applicant list for a standard status update, or click More and select Move to interviewing (with message) to include a message.

How do I correct an applicant’s status?

If an applicant is moved to the incorrect status, you can update their status at any time.

  • Navigate to the Applicants tab for the relevant job.
  • Locate the applicant whose status you want to change.
  • Update the status:
    • Single applicant: Open the applicant’s profile and click the Move to dropdown to select the correct status.
    • Multiple applicants: Check the box next to each candidate’s name, or click Select all in the header. Then use the action bar above the applicant list to select the appropriate status.

Do applicants receive notifications when their status changes?

Students can track the status of their application. However, they will not receive any notifications when a decision is made.

Messaging Applicants

You can contact your applicants directly in Handshake or via external email to share job opportunities, provide information about your organization, or promote employer-hosted events.

Who can access and message applicants?

Basic employers

  • Owners and Recruiters can message applicants only for jobs they have personally created. Jobs posted by other teammates will appear on your list, but are view-only.

  • After a job you personally created closes, you can continue messaging applicants for 30 days. Messaging beyond this period requires an eligible paid plan.

  • To message applicants for jobs you did not create, you must upgrade to an eligible paid plan. On-campus employers, Plus, Pro, Essentials and Enterprise (formerly TES) customers

  • All users, except Representatives, can access and message applicants for both their own jobs and those posted by teammates indefinitely, provided they have the appropriate permissions.

How do I access my job or on-campus interview?

Click Jobs or Interviews from the left navigation bar, select the job or interview where you want to message applicants, then click the Applicants tab.

How do I filter applicants?

You can use filters to narrow your list of applicants based on criteria such as application status, education, and engagement.

The filters available vary based on both the type of page you’re viewing (job or on-campus interview) and your Handshake account type.

Jobs

All employers

  • Application status
    • Applied
    • Interviewing
    • Rejected
    • Hired
  • Matching qualifications
    • Latest graduation date
    • Minimum GPA
    • Majors
    • Work authorization
      • Note: When this filter is applied, candidates who meet your criteria or choose not to disclose their status will appear.
  • Application date range
  • Sourced through
    • Promotions
    • Automated Outreach
    • Other Messaging
  • Education
    • Skills
    • Majors
    • Schools
  • Profile attributes
    • Labels
    • Not labels *Additional filters for Pro employers
  • Recommended match
    • Filter by 3-star, 2-star, or 1-star matches *Additional filters for Essentials and Enterprise customers
  • Screening questions (Enterprise only)
  • Where candidate applied
    • Handshake
On-campus interviews

Filters for on-campus interviews differ slightly and do not vary by account type.

Available filters include:

  • Scheduling
  • Status
  • Label / Not Labels
  • Employer Division
  • Job Applied For
  • Job Type / Employment Type
  • Skills
  • Majors / Individual Majors

How do I message applicants in Handshake?

Jobs

Message a single applicant:

  1. Open the applicant’s profile.

  2. Click Message in the upper-right corner of the profile panel.

  3. The message composer will automatically generate a personalized outreach message based on your job. You can:

  • Click Rewrite message to generate a new version.
  • Delete the generated message and compose your own.
  1. When you’re ready, click Send in the lower-right corner of the window.

Message multiple applicants:

  1. From the Applicants tab, check the box next to each applicant you want to message. To select all applicants, click Select all in the header.

  2. Click Message in the action bar above the applicant list.

  3. Compose your message in the message window. Use the formatting toolbar to add links, format text, or insert a saved template.

  4. When you’re ready, click Send in the lower-right corner of the window.

On-campus interview

  1. From the Applicants tab, check the box next to each applicant you want to message.

  2. Click the text Message Applicants above the applicant table.

  3. Compose your message in the message window.

  • Use the formatting toolbar at the top to add links and format text.
  • To insert a saved message, click Insert Template. To save your message for future use, click Save to Template.

  1. When you’re ready, click Send in the lower-left corner.

  2. In the pop-up modal, review your message, then click Confirm to send.

How do I message applicants outside of Handshake?

To email applicants outside of Handshake, export their data as a CSV file.

Jobs
  1. Check the box next to each applicant you want to export.

Tip: To export all applicants, skip this step. Handshake will include all applicants by default.

  1. Click the More dropdown above the applicant list, then select the download format you need:
  • Download applicant data (CSV): Exports applicant data as a CSV file for use outside of Handshake.
  • Download applicant packages (PDF): Downloads selected applicants’ documents as a single PDF file.
  • Download applicant packages (ZIP): Downloads selected applicants’ documents in ZIP format.
On-Campus Interviews
  1. Check the box next to each applicant you want to export.

Tip: To export all applicants, skip this step. Handshake will include all applicants by default.

  1. Click the Export CSV button above the applicant table.

  2. A pop-up will appear indicating the download is building. This may take longer for larger applicant pools. You will also receive the CSV file via email. You can close the window if you prefer not to wait.

  3. Once ready, click Your download is ready to access the CSV.

Tip: Use Chrome or Firefox for the best experience. If you’re having trouble downloading, clear your cache, close all Handshake tabs, and try again in a new browser window.

The exported CSV file includes the following fields:

  • Application ID
  • Application Date
  • Application Status
  • Student ID
  • First Name / Last Name
  • Email
  • Fully Qualified? (TRUE/FALSE)
  • School Year
  • School / Primary College
  • Graduation Date
  • Majors
  • Applied To ID / Type / Name
  • Job Applied For
  • Employer ID / Name / Division
  • Document IDs

How do I use the exported data to message applicants?

For jobs, use the email addresses in the exported CSV, PDF, or ZIP file to contact applicants outside of Handshake.

For on-campus interviews, use the email addresses in the exported CSV file to contact applicants outside of Handshake.

Reviewing Applications in Handshake

Once your job is approved and candidates begin applying, you can review, evaluate, and manage applicants directly in Handshake.

Who can access and manage applicants?

Basic employers

  • Owners and Recruiters can view and manage applicants only for jobs they have personally created. Jobs posted by other teammates will appear on your list but are view-only.

  • After a job is closed, applicant data remains accessible for 30 days. To view applicant data beyond this period, you must upgrade to an eligible paid plan. On-campus employers, Plus, Pro, Essentials, and Enterprise customers

  • All users, except Representatives, can access and manage applicant data indefinitely for both their own jobs and those posted by teammates, provided they have the appropriate permissions.

  • On-campus employers: You must be designated as an on-campus employer in your profile settings to review and manage applications for jobs created by teammates. This designation is enabled by the owner of the company profile. Learn more about Identifying as an On-Campus Employer on Handshake. Features marked with an asterisk (*) are available only to Premium partners. For more information, please check out this resource.

How do I access applicants?

  1. Click Jobs from the left navigation bar in Handshake.

  2. Choose the job you want to review and manage.

  3. On the job posting page, click the Applicants tab to view everyone who has applied.

How do I filter applicants?

Filters help you narrow your list so you can focus on candidates who match your criteria.

The filters available to you depend on your Handshake account type.

Filters available to all employers

  • Application status
    • Applied
    • Interviewing
    • Rejected
    • Hired
  • Matching qualifications
    • Latest graduation date
    • Minimum GPA
    • Majors
    • Work authorization
      • Note: When this filter is applied, candidates who meet your criteria or choose not to disclose their status will appear.
  • Application date range
  • Sourced through
    • Promotions
    • Automated Outreach
    • Other Messaging
  • Education
    • Skills
    • Majors
    • Schools
  • Profile attributes
    • Labels
    • Not labels *Additional filters for Pro employers
  • Recommended match
    • Filter by 3-star, 2-star, or 1-star matches *Additional filters for Essentials and Enterprise customers
  • Screening questions (Enterprise only)
  • Where candidate applied
    • Handshake
    • ATS To view a candidate’s profile, click directly on their name. Learn more about Viewing Student Profiles.

How do I view and download application documents?

View documents

Documents submitted by the candidate are listed in the Documents tab of the candidate’s profile.

  • If the job was updated to require documents after candidates applied, documents may not be available for all applicants.
  • Only documents submitted directly through Handshake will be available. Files shared via external links cannot be accessed in Handshake.
Download documents

To download documents for a single candidate:

  • In the Documents tab of the candidate’s profile, click the download icon, then choose the document you wish to download. To download documents for multiple candidates:

  • Select the checkbox next to each applicant, or use Select all in the header to select everyone.

  • Click the More dropdown in the action bar at the top of the list.

  • Choose Download applicant packages (PDF) to download the selected candidates’ documents as a single PDF file, or Download applicant packages (ZIP) to download them in ZIP format.

How do I manage applicants?

You can take action on one or more applicants directly from the Applicants tab.

  1. Check the box next to each applicant’s name. To select all applicants, check the box in the header of the table.

  2. Once applicants are selected, an action bar appears at the top of the list with quick-access buttons and a More dropdown.

Quick-access actions (visible in the action bar)

  • Message

  • Move to interviewing Additional actions available in the More dropdown

  • Move to interviewing (with message)

  • Move to hired

  • Move to rejected

  • Move to rejected (with message)

  • Manage labels

  • Download applicant data (CSV)

  • Download applicant packages (PDF)

  • Download applicant packages (ZIP)

Additional resources

  • Need help crafting or sending messages to applicants? Read more about Messaging Applicants.
  • Not sure which status to choose or what each one means? Review Managing Applicant Status.
  • Looking to categorize or organize applicants? Learn more about Using Labels to Manage Applicants.
  • Want to export applications or create resume books? Refer to Download Applications / Create a Resume Book.

Setting up Candidate Criteria for AI Applicant Ranking

With AI Applicant Management, you can set up candidate criteria to guide how applicants are ranked. This helps you focus your time on those who best match the qualifications and preferences that matter for your role.

This feature is available only to Pro employers with Recruiter or Owner roles and applies to all jobs in the account.

What are candidate criteria?

Candidate criteria are the specific qualifications or preferences you can add for a job. These criteria guide how our AI evaluates and ranks applicants for you to review.

Examples include:

  • Structured inputs such as GPA, major, graduation year, location, or answers to screening questions
  • Skills inferred by AI from your job description (for example: “thrives in team environments” or “attention to detail”)
  • Your own criteria that you add, not previously mentioned in your job description (for example: “Internship experience at a Big 4 firm”) You can combine all types of criteria for a more accurate applicant ranking experience.

Add or edit candidate criteria

You can add, edit, or delete up to 10 candidate criteria for each job.

Note: Each job must include at least 3 candidate criteria.

  1. From your job postings, select the one where you want to add or edit candidate criteria.

  2. On the job posting page, click the Applicants tab.

  3. Above the applicant list, click the black Refine your criteria button.

  4. A pop-up window opens with AI-suggested criteria based on your job posting. Within this window, you can:

  • Star criteria: Click the star icon to mark a criterion as most important. These receive higher weighting in rankings.
    • Note: You must star at least one criterion to receive recommendations.
  • Edit criteria: Click the pencil icon to make changes to an existing criterion.
  • Delete criteria: Click the delete icon to remove a criterion.
  • Add criteria: Click + Add criteria to create a new criterion in plain language.

  1. When finished, click the black Update criteria button.

  2. Handshake will refresh your applicant recommendations, typically within a few minutes. While the system refreshes, the message “Preparing recommendations based on criteria” displays.

  3. Once refreshed, a link will appear: “View updated recommendations.” Click this link to open your updated list of applicants that best match your criteria.

Criteria validation and errors

Handshake automatically checks that criteria are:

  • Objective, measurable, and job-related

  • Free from discriminatory language (aligned with EEOC guidelines)

  • Under 100 characters per item

  • Not containing personal information (such as emails, links, or phone numbers) If your criteria do not meet these standards, you will receive an error message before saving. Depending on the issue, one of the following messages may display:

  • “This criterion has insufficient information. Try adding more descriptive words.”

  • “This criterion violates fair hiring guidelines.”

  • “This criterion is too subjective. Try using clear, measurable qualifications.” Update your criteria as suggested, then save your changes.

Not sure how to phrase your criteria? Refer to our Guidelines for Writing Smart, Compliant AI Matching Criteria.

How AI ranks applicants

When you post a job, Handshake generates candidate criteria from your job posting to evaluate each applicant.

Note: You can update these criteria at any time.

  • Applicants are automatically ranked from those who most closely match your criteria to those who least match.
  • Applicants who meet a high number of your criteria are placed in the Recommended category, making it easier to focus on top matches.
  • Recommended applicants include a short AI-generated summary and highlighted traits that explain why they’re a strong match.
  • You can provide feedback (thumbs up/down) on recommended applicants to improve future results.

Application Status & Notifications

Definitions: Application Statuses

In Handshake, students can view the status of their applications for jobs and on-campus interviews.

Application statuses

Applied: The application has been submitted and is either awaiting employer review or has already been reviewed.

Hired: Indicates that the employer or career services center marked the applicant as hired for a job posting.

Declined: Indicates that the employer or career services center marked the applicant as not selected for a job posting or interview schedule.

Primary: The applicant has been selected as a primary candidate for an interview schedule.

Alternate: The applicant has been selected as an alternate candidate for an interview schedule.

Hide Declined Applicants

When reviewing applications, you can hide rejected applicants so you can easily track active candidates.

How do I access my job or interview?

Click Jobs or Interviews in the left navigation bar, then select the job or interview where you want to hide declined applicants.

For more information on reviewing applications, read Reviewing Applications in Handshake.

How do I hide rejected applicants for a job?

  • From the Applicants tab, click the Status button in the filter bar above the applicant list.
  • Deselect Rejected to hide declined applicants.
  • The applicant list will update automatically based on the statuses you select.

How do I hide declined applicants for an on-campus interview?

  1. Navigate to the Applicants tab, then click View all within the Status filter on the left.

  2. In the pop-up modal, select the application status(es) you want to review. Make sure to leave the box for Declined unchecked.

  3. Click Done to save your selections. This will filter out any declined applicants from your Applicants view.

What happens when I decline applicants?

When you decline an applicant in Handshake, they will not receive a notification informing them of the decision. However, applicants can track the status of their application at any time.

Will applicants be notified if they are declined?

Applicants will not receive a notification if their application is declined or rejected from a job posting.

However, if an applicant was scheduled for an interview but not selected, they will receive a notification informing them that they are no longer being considered.

What is the difference between “Rejected” and “Declined”?

The action to remove an applicant from consideration is labeled differently depending on where you are reviewing applications in Handshake.

  • On the Jobs page, the action is labeled Rejected.
  • On the Interviews page, the action is labeled Declined.

Appointments

About Appointment Notification Timelines

Appointment notifications are available for both career services users and students who are added to an appointment in Handshake.

Career services notification preferences

Career services users receive appointment-related notifications based on their individual notification preferences. For supported activities, users can choose to receive:

  • In-app notifications in Handshake
  • Email notifications sent to the email address associated with their Handshake account
  • Both, when those options are available for the activity Career services users can review and update their notification settings in Handshake. To learn more about this, refer to Career Services User Settings: Manage Your Notifications.

Student Notifications

To learn more about when students receive notifications and reminders for appointments, refer to Student Appointment Notifications.

Pre-appointment surveys

If a custom pre-appointment survey is attached to the appointment type, students are prompted to complete the survey while they schedule the appointment, within the booking flow.

Post-appointment surveys

If a post-appointment survey is configured for the appointment:

  • A post-appointment survey notification is generated after the career coach selects Complete on the appointment.
  • If the appointment is edited and the status is changed to Completed only by using the status radio button, the post-appointment survey notification is not generated.

Drop-in appointment notifications

Career services users receive notifications for drop-in appointments when:

  • They have the waiting room page open (we recommend this in another browser tab or window), and
  • They have the following notification preference enabled in their user settings:
    • “When I am viewing the waiting room page, notify me when a student checks in for a drop-in appointment” Students do not receive additional notifications when they check in to a drop-in appointment using a kiosk.

Reducing or bypassing student notifications

Updates to an existing appointment, including past appointments, can generate new notifications for attendees.

If an appointment needs to appear on a calendar without creating new notifications for students:

  • Create the appointment as a past appointment.
  • Set the appointment status to Completed when you create it.

Appointment Availability Troubleshooting

If you’ve set up your appointments in School Settings, yet you are unable to view all or some of your appointment categories when you switch to your student account, you may not have your school year added to your student account.

Here’s how to troubleshoot why the appointment category isn’t showing up when viewing as your student account.

First, viewing as Career Services, look at the qualifications on the appointment type associated with that category. You can do this by going to School Settings, and then Appointment Types.

The next step is to see if there are any qualifications set on the Appointment Type(s) associated with the Appointment Categories that you’re not able to see as a student. Select Edit on an appointment type, and the check the qualifications.

In the above example, Freshmen, Sophomores, Juniors, and Seniors are able to view and request Resume Reviews as an appointment type.

Now that you’ve seen that there are qualifications on the Appointment Types you’re not able to view, you can check your own student account to see if you have a school year set.

So, still viewing as Career Services, view your student account, by going to Manage Students and searching your name. Once you are viewing your student profile, click the Account tab to look to see if you have a school year set on your student account. If you don’t, you can then set one.

Now, because you are one of the school years allowed to see this type/category, you should now be able to see the category when you view as your student account and select Create New Appointment.

Appointment Kiosk Updates 2020

We’re excited to share changes to the appointment kiosk, live in June 2020!

Appointment Only Kiosk

When launching a new kiosk from the Appointments Overview page, you’ll see the last option allows for an “Appointment Only Kiosk”. This will only display appointments for your career center, and no other events, fairs, or on-campus interviews that may be occurring simultaneously.

New check-in view

When students enter their email into the kiosk, they will be presented with a new view which may vary, depending on if the kiosk is launched is a general kiosk or for appointments only.

If a student is checking in for a drop-in appointment, students will no longer see the option to select drop-in. They will see categories to choose from, then can select from drop-in enabled appointment types on the next page.

Here’s an example of what those categories and types could look like:

Offline Mode

If your kiosk is launched, and you happen to lose access to internet, the kiosk will continue to function in Offline Mode. You’ll see that Offline Mode is working via a banner at the top of the kiosk page.

Appointments System Setup Checklist and Testing Guide

This guide will help your office configure appointments in Handshake, then test the workflows involved in everything from scheduling to managing appointments. Use the Help Center links within this article for detailed guidance!

Note: If you’d like to create a group appointment, you can create an event and set the event type to Group Appointment. Set the event to invite-only and invite students that will be attending the group appointment. Learn more about creating events in Events: Creating an Event.

Step 1: Configure Appointment Settings in Handshake

Create Your Appointment Types

  • Appointment types are the kinds of appointments that can be scheduled for your office, i.e resume checks, mock interviews, career planning, etc. You can define which groups of students can select certain appointment types by setting qualifications. Learn more on how to Set Appointment Qualifications. To access your appointment types in Handshake, navigate to “School Settings” > “Appointment Types”.

For more information on creating and managing types, refer to School Settings: Appointment Types.

Best Practice: If you have multiple career centers, add the location in the name of the appointment type. This way the location is included in student reminder emails. It may make sense to duplicate appointment types for this purpose - that’s ok!

Best Practice: If you want standardized information when students are scheduling or staff members are running appointments, configure your pre-appointment, post-appointment, and staff member survey in your appointment type set-up. If you’d like to learn more about setting up surveys, please refer to Creating and Testing Surveys.

Best Practice: If each advisor in your office works with a different group of students, and you would like to make sure that students can only select appointments relevant to them, then we recommend to create appointment types for each of those groups. This particular setup works best if each advisor creates appointment types with the same naming conventions.

Create your Appointment Categories

  • Appointment Categories provide first-level appointment type organization for students to choose from, making it easier for the student to choose the appropriate appointment. To access your appointment categories in Handshake, navigate to “School Settings” > “Appointment Categories”.

For more information on creating and managing categories, refer to School Settings: Appointment Categories.

Best Practice: Categorize appointments by college, career center, or subject area and standardize your categories. We highly recommend having a standard naming convention across campus to reduce confusion.

Create Your Appointment Mediums

  • Appointment Mediums are the methods you will use to conduct your appointments. These may include: Face to face, phone call, video call, etc.
  • You can activate the Handshake provided medium “Virtual on Handshake” to use integrated video for your appointments, providing a seamless experience while generating useful reporting data! Read more about Virtual Appointments on Handshake. To access your appointment mediums in Handshake, navigate to “School Settings” > “Appointment Mediums”.

For more information on creating and managing mediums, refer to School Settings: Appointment Mediums.

Best Practice: As an alternative to adding the location to the appointment type, consider adding the location in the medium if you are having an in person appointment, for example: “In person - Career Center, Fisher Hall”. The appointment medium is included in the reminder emails that are sent 24 hours and 1 hour prior to the appointment.

Configure Your Appointment Preferences

  • Configure different appointment related settings like auto-approval, request timeframe and permission labels. For more details on how to configure these settings, please see the article linked out above. To access your appointment preferences in Handshake, navigate to “School Settings” > “Appointment Preferences”.

For more information on creating and managing preferences, refer to School Settings: Appointment Preferences.

Best Practice: If you need to exclude a subset of students from accessing appointments altogether, talk to your IT team about importing a label called “no appointments” (or something similar) onto those student profiles. You can then use that label to set a restriction on the Appointment Preferences page. Read more on Importing Labels.

Set your maximum open appointments & Appointment Cancellation Timeframe

  • The maximum open appointment setting is the maximum number of concurrent appointment requests a student may have at once.
    • This setting includes all future appointments (approved, pending, etc), based on the appointment start date. Until the start date has passed, the system won’t allow the student to schedule any new appointments beyond the limit set.
  • The appointment cancellation time frame allows your to specify the period of time in which a student can cancel their appointment prior to the appointment start time. To manage these settings in Handshake, navigate to “School Settings” > “Details”. For more information, refer to School Settings: Details.

Step 2: Have each Career Center Staff Member Configure their own Appointment User Settings

Add Appointment Types

  • Choose the types of appointments that students will be able to schedule with you by clicking the green “Add” button. Students will only be able to schedule these types of appointment with you. Add Appointment Blocks

  • Designate blocks of time that students will be able to schedule appointments with you. Within each block, you can designate specific appointment types that you will conduct, as well as specific mediums available during that time.

    • Students will not be able to schedule an appointment with you until you set up available appointment blocks. Note: If a block is made available for drop-ins, the appointment block will not be available for scheduled appointments.

Configure Your Personal Appointment Availability (Appointment Blocks & Types) for more information and guidance on adding appointment blocks.

Best Practice: Sync your calendar with two-way calendar sync. Keep in mind this will impact your availability. Events in your external calendar that are “busy” will pull into Handshake, and your scheduled Handshake appointments will pull into your external calendar. Check with your IT team to find out what server you are on.

Step: 3 Think you’re ready? Run through these tests to make sure!

Ensure the correct appointment categories and types are visible to students

  • Navigate to a student’s profile and click “View As This User” in the actions section.
  • Go to Career Center > Appointments and click “Schedule a New Appointment”.
  • Verify that the correct categories, types, dates/times, and mediums are visible to that student. Best Practice: If you have qualifications set on your appointment types, repeat this process with multiple students of varying qualifications and for each impacted appointment type.

Sign up for an appointment as a student and approve it as a career services user

  • Request an appointment with your test student account. Note: As of May 2023, staff member names will be randomized when selecting an appointment. Previously, staff names were listed alphabetically. This change increases the likelihood that students will schedule appointments with a variety of different staff members.

  • Switch users back to your career services view.

  • Navigate to the appointments page and approve the appointment. Launch the check-in kiosk and check-in for your appointment as a student

  • For in-person appointments, navigate to Appointments and click the “Check-in Kiosk” tab.

  • Select your office location, career center, and if you will allow drop in appointments. Note: if you do not click “allow drop-in appointment”, students will only be able to check in for scheduled appointments.

Important: choosing “Keep me logged in” will allow students checking in to have access to your account. For testing, this is fine, but proceed with caution if you decide to choose this option outside of testing.

  1. Enter the email address or username of the student you are testing with.

  2. Select the scheduled appointment.

Start and complete the scheduled appointment

  • Click “Appointments” > “Manage” > Click on the row pertaining to the appointment that you want to start.
  • To start the appointment, click “Appointment Started”. If you’re testing a Virtual on Handshake appointment, joining video will trigger the appointment start.
  • To complete the appointment, click “Complete Appointment”. Note: marking the appointment complete is critical to ensure post-appointment surveys are sent as well as reporting accuracy.

Check-in for a drop-in appointment as a student

  • Launch your check-in kiosk and select “Allow Drop-In Appointments”.
  • Check-in as a student and select the drop-in option. Tip: If you aren’t able to select a drop-in option, make sure there is at least one appointment block available at that time with “drop-in” selected.

Start a drop-in appointment from the waiting room

  • Viewing from your career services user, navigate to the waiting room via “Appointments” > “Waiting Room”.
  • Click “Start Appointment”.
  • Verify information about the appointment and click “Create”. (If you’re planning to send a post-appointment survey, remember to only mark the appointment as ‘started’ on this screen, then click ‘Complete Appointment’ to trigger the email!)

Additional Resources

  • Appointments Troubleshooting Guide
  • Handshake Community - Appointments
  • Appointments Help Center:
    • Operations > Setup & Configuration
    • Student Engagement & Usage
