Attendee Resources

Attendee Requirements for Integrated Video

Prior to attending a session with integrated video on Handshake, we recommend reviewing the requirements included in this resource and adjusting your setup as needed.

To join a session as an attendee, you must have an active student account on Handshake.

Topics:

  • System setup and settings minimum requirements
  • Mobile settings and capabilities
  • Mac system requirements for screen sharing
  • Windows 10 required settings for camera and mic

System setup and settings minimum requirements

  • An internet connection — broadband wired or wireless (3G or 4G/LTE)
  • Speakers and a microphone — built-in or USB plug-in, or wireless Bluetooth
  • Optional, but required if you’d like to use video — a webcam or HD webcam — built-in or USB plug-in
    • Tip: before your scheduled virtual session, make sure that any additional permissions or settings are configured if you’re using a webcam that isn’t built into your device.
  • Desktop or laptop computer — mobile devices (smart phones and tablets, e.g. iPads) are only supported for students using our mobile app on iOS and Android.
  • Modern desktop web browser that supports WebRTC — make sure pop-ups are allowed in the browser.
    • We support the latest versions of:
      • Chrome 75 and above
      • Safari 13.1 and above
        • Note: the only sharing option available on Safari is for the entire screen, not for specific apps or browser windows.
      • Firefox 91 ESR and above
      • Microsoft Edge 75 and above
        • Note: non-Chromium versions of Microsoft Edge (versions less than 79) do not support screen sharing capabilities.
      • Electron 6 and above
    • The security and privacy settings of each browser may require you to grant Handshake permission to use your microphone and camera.

Mobile settings

Handshake is currently working on enhancing the mobile experience for users, ensuring that attendees can participate in virtual interactions wherever they may be.

  • iOS 12.1 and later versions
    • If you’re using the mobile app via an iOS device, you’ll be directed to your device’s web browser to participate in the virtual interaction.
      • Note: you’ll only be able to engage via Safari, as Apple does not allow third-party browsers access to the device’s camera or microphone
  • Android 5.0 and above with current security and platform updates
    • If you’re using the mobile app via Android device, you’ll have access to an embedded mobile web experience within the app — this means you won’t need to leave the app to participate in the virtual interaction. If prompted for permission to access the camera or microphone, you must allow access in order to use video or audio.

For the best experience, we recommend using Chrome on your desktop.

Mac system requirements for screen sharing

To share a screen or window on a Mac, you must give each specific browser or app permission.

  1. Open System Preferences, then select Security & Privacy.

  2. Click the lock in the lower-right corner to authenticate for changes.

  3. Select the Privacy tab, select Screen Recording, then check the box for the desired browser.

If the browser is open when you change this setting, you must quit and reopen the browser for the changes to take effect.

  • Tip: for a smooth experience, make sure this permission is granted prior to your session start time!

Windows 10 required settings for camera and mic

Windows has its own privacy settings for microphone & camera that are independent of the browser. In most cases, this is turned off by default.

There are two settings pages:

  • Settings > Privacy > Microphone

  • Settings > Privacy > Camera Both pages have two toggles:

  • Allow apps to use my microphone/camera (used for built-in Microsoft apps from their app store)

  • Allow desktop apps to use my microphone/camera (used for things like browsers and Zoom) The second toggle (for desktop apps) can only be enabled if the first is enabled, so you will need to turn both toggles on in both places for your browser to be able to access their mic and camera.

If you are having issues connecting your AirPods on Windows 10, follow the steps below:

  • Open the Windows Device Manager.

  • Click the View tab and select the ’devices by type‘ option.

  • Once there, open the Human Interface Devices and locate the 2 AirPods entries below:

  • (Name) AirPods Audio/Video Remote Control HID

  • (Name) AirPods Hands-Free Call Control HID

  • For each of the above entries, right-click and select Properties.

  • Click the Power Management tab and uncheck the box next to Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power. If the Airpods do not appear under Human Interface Devices, follow the alternate steps below:

  • Open the Windows Device Manager and click on Bluetooth.

  • Right-click Intel(R) Wireless Bluetooth and click the Power Management tab.

  • Uncheck the box next to Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power. Note: You will need to have administrator access to the computer in order to adjust these settings.

Attendees: Audio & Video Issues

When attending a session via integrated video on Handshake, experiencing audio or video issues are typically due to common configuration or permission issues with your browser or device (desktop/mobile).

To assist you in resolving your issues, we have outlined a comprehensive sequence of steps to follow for troubleshooting purposes.

Troubleshooting audio and video

Attendees can join virtual interactions via desktop or mobile device.

Handshake Mobile
  • Update the app to the most recent version. The Handshake app is supported on both iOS and Android devices.
  • Grant permission for the app to use audio and video.
    • iOS: Open the Settings app, then scroll down and tap “Handshake” — make sure the Microphone and Camera are toggled on. Alternatively, navigate to Settings > Privacy > Camera or Settings > Privacy > Microphone, then toggle Handshake on.
    • Android: Open the Settings app, then navigate to Apps > Handshake > Permissions, then choose “Allow camera and microphone access”. Alternatively, navigate to Settings > Privacy > Permission Manager, then choose Camera or Microphone and allow access.
  • Make sure there’s a reliable network connection to your mobile device.
    • Use the Daily Network Test to check if your browser can effectively connect to the necessary networks, network-test.daily.co
    • If you’re using a cellular data connection, grant permission to the app to use the network:
      • iOS: Open the Settings app, then scroll down and tap “Handshake” — make sure Cellular Data is toggled on. Alternatively, navigate to Settings > Cellular, then toggle Handshake on.
      • Android: Open the Settings app, then navigate to Wireless & networks > Data usage > Network access, then make sure Handshake is checked for Mobile data.
Computer (desktop web)
  • Make sure you’ve granted your browser permission for audio and video on our site. If you have started the session, you will likely notice that some features might not work. For example, chat might work, but audio or video might not.
    • For browser-specific troubleshooting steps, click on the browser name to be directed to the appropriate collapsible header for more details.
      • Chrome (Mac or Windows)
      • Firefox (Mac or Windows)
      • Safari (on Mac only)
      • Edge (on Windows only)
  • For Windows 10 users, additional settings may need to be configured. To help with Windows 10 specific settings, click on the following link to be directed to the appropriate collapsible header for more details: Windows 10 required settings for camera and mic
  • Something else specific to your setup is causing a problem. Minimize the number of resources (i.e., turn off blurry background, close unused tabs and applications) on the computers/devices when using video. Click on the following link to be directed to the appropriate collapsible header for more details: System Troubleshooting.

Browser-specific troubleshooting

Chrome (Mac or Windows)

Open Chrome. Navigate to Preferences, then click on Security and Privacy from the menu on the left of the page. From the list of options, click on Site Settings, then scroll down to Permissions. From this section, you can manage camera and microphone settings overall and per site.

  • Double-check that the correct Camera or Microphone device are selected from each of the respective dropdown menus.
    • If the expected device isn’t listed, make sure any external devices are configured for your computer.
  • Our main site should be listed under “Allowed” in order for video and audio to work: app.joinhandshake.com:443 Chrome > Preferences > Privacy and security > Site Settings:

Site Settings > Permissions:

Site Settings > Permissions > Camera:

Site Settings > Permissions > Microphone:

Firefox troubleshooting (Mac or Windows)

Open Firefox. Navigate to Preferences, then click on Privacy & Security from the menu on the left of the page, then scroll down to Permissions. From this section, you can manage camera and microphone settings overall and per site. Make sure the following options are not checked:

  • Camera > Settings: “Block new requests asking to access your camera”
  • Microphone > Settings: “Block new requests asking to access your microphone” Firefox > Preferences > Privacy & Security > Permissions:
Safari troubleshooting (on Mac only)

Open Safari and navigate to Preferences, then click on Websites, the third icon from the right at the top of the pane. Follow the steps below, based on the behavior you experienced:

  • Unable to use microphone: Click on Microphone from the left menu, locate the joinhandshake.com list item, then click the dropdown menu and select Allow.
  • Unable to use camera: Click on Camera from the left menu, locate the joinhandshake.com list item, then click the dropdown menu and select Allow.
  • No sound output from session: Click on Auto-Play from the left menu, locate the joinhandshake.com list item, then click the dropdown menu and select “Allow All Auto-Play”.
    • If the setting is on “Stop Media with Sound” or “Never Auto-Play”, the sound is automatically restricted. To help quickly solve this while you’re in the session, select Allow in the permission pop-up window. Safari > Preferences > Websites > Camera:

Safari > Preferences > Websites > Microphone:

Safari > Preferences > Websites > Auto-Play:

Edge troubleshooting (on Windows only)

Open Edge. Navigate to Settings, select Site Permissions on the left side, and then select Camera or Microphone.

For both options, make sure that:

  • “Ask First” is selected as default.
  • the correct camera or microphone device is selected in the drop down menu.
  • the joinhandshake.com site is allowed (not blocked). To read more on these settings, refer to Windows camera, microphone, and privacy.

Note: if you are using Edge on Windows 10, you may also need to follow the steps below for Windows 10, in addition to changing Edge settings.

Windows 10 required settings for camera and mic

Windows has its own privacy settings for microphone & camera that are independent of the browser. In most cases, this is turned off by default.

There are two settings pages:

  • Settings > Privacy > Microphone

  • Settings > Privacy > Camera Both pages have two toggles:

  • Allow apps to use my microphone/camera (used for built-in Microsoft apps from their app store)

  • Allow desktop apps to use my microphone/camera (used for things like browsers and Zoom) The second toggle (for desktop apps) can only be enabled if the first is enabled, so you will need to turn both toggles on in both places for your browser to be able to access their mic and camera.

If you are having issues connecting your AirPods on Windows 10, follow the steps below:

  • Open the Windows Device Manager.

  • Click the View tab and select the ’devices by type‘ option.

  • Once there, open the Human Interface Devices and locate the 2 AirPods entries below:

  • (Name) AirPods Audio/Video Remote Control HID

  • (Name) AirPods Hands-Free Call Control HID

  • For each of the above entries, right-click and select Properties.

  • Click the Power Management tab and uncheck the box next to Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power. If the Airpods do not appear under Human Interface Devices, follow the alternate steps below:

  • Open the Windows Device Manager and click on Bluetooth.

  • Right-click Intel(R) Wireless Bluetooth and click the Power Management tab.

  • Uncheck the box next to Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power. Note: You will need to have administrator access to the computer in order to adjust these settings.

Windows > Settings > Privacy > Camera and Microphone (adjust one at a time):

System troubleshooting

If you’re still experiencing audio or video issues after confirming that your browser preferences are configured correctly, follow the steps below to further isolate the cause.

  1. Confirm the hardware is working as expected:
  • Confirm that your speakers and volume control both work.
    • Test the sound and microphone by using another platform or application through your device.
  • Confirm that your device can play video.
    • We recommend testing this by watching a video on Youtube (or other known-good sites).
  1. Make sure that you have a reliable Internet connection. Use the Daily Network Test to determine if your browser can successfully access the required Daily resources: network-test.daily.co
  • If you’re experiencing video issues while using a blurry background, try turning blur off to improve performance.

  1. Refresh the page and re-launch the video session.

  2. Fully quit and restart the browser.

  3. Restart your computer.

  4. Try a different supported browser.

Attendees: Test audio and video

Before joining a virtual career fair, event, or interview on Handshake, you can take a network test. This test will provide detailed information about your network, and whether you’ll have issues using the platform to attend a virtual session on Handshake.

Test your Network

Handshake uses Daily as its video provider for virtual sessions — Click on the following link to be directed to Daily’s network test: network-test.daily.co

Once on Daily’s network test, click the green button Start Test.

Your browser may prompt to allow access to your microphone and camera. You’ll need to allow this access to use audio and video in the session.

The results from your test are listed as Pass or Fail. If the test indicates your network has issues, Daily may provide tips for how to resolve them.

Attending via Video on Handshake

When you join a video session on Handshake, you’re able to connect virtually with employers and your school’s career services team online.

Handshake uses Daily as its video provider for virtual sessions. Daily is built using WebRTC and all multimedia traffic is routed through their media servers. Because of this, there may be some settings that need to be adjusted for you to attend. We recommend reviewing the Attendee Requirements for Integrated Video in advance of your scheduled session!

For the best user experience, we recommend using Chrome as your browser.

Handshake is currently working on enhancing the mobile experience for users, ensuring that everyone can participate in virtual interactions wherever they may be. For the initial launch:

  • If you’re using the mobile app via iOS device, you’ll be directed to your device’s web browser to participate in the virtual interaction.
  • If you’re using the mobile app via Android device, you’ll have access to an embedded mobile web experience within the app — this means you won’t need to leave the app to participate in the virtual interaction. Attending a video session begins once you click the button Join on your desktop and a new tab in your browser opens.

In the new tab, your browser may prompt to allow access to your microphone and camera. You’ll need to allow this access to have audio and video in the session.

💡Note: some employers may host webinars for larger audiences. In such cases, your video and audio will be automatically turned off, and you won’t be able to control your camera or microphone. To interact during the webinar, you’ll need to use the chat feature.

Topics:

  • Video session preview page
  • Participating in the video session
    • Adjust settings
      • Audio
      • Video
    • Video display options
    • View participants
    • React in your session
    • Turn on Auto captions
    • Share your screen
    • Pin a user
    • Report a Technical issue
  • Report a user
  • Leave a session

Video session preview page

When a new tab opens in your browser, you can adjust your videos settings before joining!

A preview of your video will be available in the center of the page. If your video is off, your profile photo will display instead — If you do not have a profile photo, a gray person icon is present.

Settings

Your settings are located below your video preview screen.

  • Video: control your camera by turning it on and off, managing your visibility.
  • Audio: use this to mute or unmute your audio.
  • Effects: apply a background from a preselected library of images, or upload a custom background from your computer.
    • Adding a background offers more privacy or a consistent and professional feel for virtual interactions. Available options include: Soft blur, Strong blur, Coffee shop, Library, Lounge, Office, and more!
  • Reduce (Noise Reduction): activate this to minimize background noise, making your voice clearer when you’re speaking.
  • More: access your audio/video setting
    • Audio and Video: confirm your camera, microphone, and speaker devices
    • Video quality: select the video quality that’s best for your network
    • User preferences: choose your language, control your notifications, and select a default emoji skin tone. Once you’re ready to join, click the black button Join, located in the upper-right corner of the video preview.

Note: you can join a video session up to 5 minutes before the session’s start time.

Participating in the video session

Once you’ve clicked the button Join, from your video preview, you’re directed to the video session in Daily.

For larger gatherings, the host may choose to turn off audio and video for attendees during your session — this is to preserve the video quality of the virtual interaction. If this is the case, your audio and video will automatically be turned off upon entering the session, and you won’t be able to turn your camera on or unmute without being called on.

If you still need to adjust your settings, you may do so after you’ve joined the video session!

Adjust audio and video settings

In the audio and video settings, make sure the correct devices are selected for your Microphone, Speakers, and Camera if you have more than one.

Click the carrot icon (down arrow), located to the right of each to then select the devices you wish to use during your session.

Tip: click Video Settings from the menu to adjust your audio and video from the settings window, or choose to Hide self view from the video option. Hiding yourself removes your video display from your screen, allowing more room to view other participants on your screen. If you turn off Hide self view, your own video display reappears on your screen, showing how you appear to others attending the session.

You can also access your audio and video settings by clicking the gear icon, located in the upper-left corner of the video screen to open your settings window.

Video display options

Located in the upper-right corner of your screen, these options allow you to choose how you want to view other attendees.

  • Grid View: Shows a grid of video tiles for all participants, perfect for group conversations.
    • Note: shows up to 16 video tiles on the screen at once via desktop.
  • Speaker View: The active speaker’s video tile is enlarged while other attendees are displayed in a carousel on the right side of the screen, making it ideal for presentations or lectures.
  • Start Picture-in-Picture: when sharing your screen or presenting during a virtual interaction, this feature will show the hosts video in a small tile outside the browser. This can be helpful, as it allows you to stay visually connected with them throughout your screensharing.
    • Note: picture-in-picture is only available in Chrome.
View participants and chat

To view the participants list during the session, including the host, click the participant icon (People) in the bottom middle of the screen. A list of participants displays on the right of the screen.

To chat with your host and other attendees, click the chat icon (message box) in the bottom middle of the screen. The chat window will appear on the right of the screen — If others type in the chat, and your chat isn’t open, a red dot over the chat bubble will indicate there’s unread messages.

Note: messages have a 256-character limit.

Before the host ends the session for all, you can download the chat to refer to later! To download the chat, click the link Download chat, located in the lower-right corner of your chat box — the chat will automatically be downloaded to your computer.

React in your session

Reactions float upwards on the video screen as an effect expressing how you and others feel. To send a reaction during the session, click the heart icon, located in the bottom middle of the screen, then choose from the preselect emoji options such as a hand clap, wave, celebration, heart, and fire.

Turn on Auto-captions

To turn on auto-captions, click the Captions icon, located to the right of React. Once auto-captions are enabled, they’ll be displayed in the upper-left corner of the video screen.

Tip: If auto-captions do not automatically start showing, click Captions again.

Auto-captions make content easier to understand and follow by automatically making captions for spoken dialogue in real time. This feature uses speech recognition technology to transcribe audio to text, which is then displayed as subtitles during a video call or recording.

To stop auto-captions, click the red Captions icon.

Share your screen

For 1:1 interactions (appointments, virtual fairs 1:1, and employer-hosted meetings) you’ll have the option to share your screen.

For group sessions (virtual fairs and events) the host will need to enable the screen share option to you. This is done by promoting you to “host” for you to have the option.

Screen sharing in a session is currently possible via Desktop only.

- If you are using a Mac, additional settings need to be configured–refer to [Mac system requirements for screen sharing](https://support.joinhandshake.com/hc/en-us/articles/4423738147607#01FVMPY0Z8AE396FXC4ZYV0HH2).

To share your screen, the host must choose to enable this feature for attendees per session. If enabled, click the computer icon button to start screen-sharing.

Sharing options depend on the browser you’re using.

For example, in Chrome, you can choose to share your full screen, a particular application window, or a specific tab within your browser window. In other browsers, you may be limited as to what you can share.

🚀Tip: to maximize your screensharing abilities on the platform, here’s a few suggestions:

  • Use the picture-in-picture feature (available on Chrome only). This allows you to maintain a visual connection with the other person while also sharing information from your screen.
  • If you have one screen, use a second window for your presentation. You can arrange your windows on the screen to view both your presentation as well as the chat and attendee carousel.
  • If you have two separate screens, use a second window for your presentation and showcase each window on its own screen.
Pin a user

If you would like to pin a user on the screen (such as an ASL interpreter) you can do so by clicking the participant icon (People) in the bottom middle of the screen.

From the list of participants displayed on the right of the screen, locate the user you want to pin, then click the three-dot menu icon, located to the right of their name. Click Pin participant from the dropdown to pin their video to your screen.

Report a problem (Technical Issue)

You can report an audio issue, video issue, chat issue, or other. This will generate a ticket for our support team to review, as well as help us continue to improve our product.

For more details on this process, refer to Reporting an Issue as an Attendee.

Report a User

To guarantee a safe and respectful environment while attending video sessions on Handshake, the you may choose to report a participant if necessary.

To Report a user, click the three-dot menu icon, located in the upper-right corner of the video screen, then click Report User from the dropdown menu.

In the pop-up that appears, enter the following information:

  • The user name (choose from dropdown)
  • Reason (select one)
    • I think this user is fake or fraudulent
    • This user is harassing me or someone else
  • Details (type in textbox) Once everything is added, click Submit report, located in the lower-right corner to send to our team for further review.

Leave a session

When the video session is finished, click the red exit icon, Leave to exit the session.

Note: if you leave the session before it’s scheduled end time, you’ll be able to rejoin it at any point as long as the interaction (appointment, virtual fair, 1:1, etc) is still going‌ on and hasn’t been ended by the host. However, once the session is over, the button to join the virtual interaction will no longer be active.

For additional details on participating in virtual Handshake sessions and resolving audio and video issues, refer to our Attendee Resources.

Reporting an Issue as an Attendee

Participants of virtual sessions have the ability to report technical issues, concerns of fraud, or any other inappropriate activity via Handshake video session, either on the web or through the Handshake app.

Our reporting method is fast and easy, and provides key information to help facilitate a resolution. We monitor issues across multiple schools or users as needed.

Note: Handshake uses Daily as its video provider for virtual sessions. If the technical issue is related to Daily’s website being down, there is limited action we can take to resolve the issue. To verify if Daily is up and running, use the following link to their status page: status.daily.co

Reporting a technical issue

If you’re experiencing a technical issue during your session, you can report the issue at that time, directly from your video session.

Click the three-dot menu icon, located in the upper-right corner of the video screen, then click Report a technical problem from the dropdown menu.

Within the pop-up, choose the type of technical issue you’re experiencing (audio, video, chat, other), then describe what happened in the text box. Once complete, click the blue button Submit report.

Once reported, it’ll be immediately directed to our team for review and followup. We’ll also use these reports to make continuous improvements to the product.

If there are widespread technical issues, we’ll display a message in the product and post it to our status page.

Reporting a Trust & Safety issue

Participants can report any user (including the host) for fraudulent, spam, or other inappropriate activity — this can be done via web or mobile.

When another user is reported, the session host will receive a notification, and hosts can decide whether to remove the participant from the meeting.

Hosts and participants will have additional controls to ensure a safe experience:

  • Hosts and attendees will all need to have Handshake accounts and be on the participants (registration/attendee list) to access your fair. So if someone doesn’t have either of those, they can’t access your fair or sessions.
  • Participants can turn video on/off and leave sessions at any time, and hosts can also turn video on/off and end sessions at any time. Once the host has ended the meeting and the scheduled start time has passed, the meeting can’t be re-started.
  • Participants or hosts can’t edit participant names in sessions.
  • Hosts can mute or remove participants from a session and once removed they can’t rejoin
  • Group and 1:1 sessions will be encrypted via DTLS/SRTP protocol.

Report user from desktop

To Report a user, click the three-dot menu icon, located in the upper-right corner of the video screen, then click Report User from the dropdown menu.

In the pop-up that appears, enter the following information:

  • The user name (choose from dropdown)
  • Reason (select one)
    • I think this user is fake or fraudulent
    • This user is harassing me or someone else
  • Details (type in textbox) Once everything is added, click Submit report, located in the lower-right corner to send to our team for further review.

Report user from mobile

Users can be reported from the participants list on the mobile app.

To report a user, tap the people icon, located in the upper-right corner of the screen.

Find the user you want to report from the list, then tap the three dots to the right of their name.

Tap Report… at the bottom of the screen.

Within the popup, choose one of the following options, then describe the situation (if needed):

  • I think this user is fake or fraudulent
  • This user is harassing me or someone else To submit the report, tap the blue button Submit report.

Sessions Display Wrong Times

If unexpected start times are displayed or you’re missing upcoming sessions, you may need to update your computer’s timezone.

Handshake does not have a timezone setting that may be adjusted on the platform — we pull the timezone from your computer’s selected timezone.

We recommend setting the timezone to update automatically to ensure the most accurate display in Handshake.

To adjust your timezone on your computer, refer to the relevant article below:

  • Mac - Set the date and time automatically on your Mac
  • Windows - How to set your time and time zone

Unable to Join Sessions

If you are unable to join a scheduled session that you’re registered for, refer to the following troubleshooting steps to assist you in joining!

Handshake mobile app on iOS or Android

  • Make sure your device has a reliable Internet connection. If you’re using cellular data, confirm you’ve granted permission for the app to use that connection.
    • iOS: Open the Settings app, scroll down and tap “Handshake”, then make sure Cellular Data is toggled on. Alternatively, navigate to Settings > Cellular, then toggle Handshake on.
    • Android: Open the Settings app, then navigate to Wireless & networks > Data usage > Network access, then make sure Handshake is checked for Mobile data.
  • Close and reopen the app
  • Restart your mobile device

Computer (desktop web)

  • Make sure your computer has a reliable Internet connection
    • Minimize the number of resources (i.e. close unused tabs and applications) on the computer
    • If you’re on wifi, move closer to your router
    • If you’re using ethernet, try unplugging the cable and reconnecting it
    • Daily provides a network test to test your internet, audio, visual, etc: network-test.daily.co
  • Use the latest version of a supported browser.
    • We recommend Chrome for the best experience!
  • Make sure that pop-ups are allowed in the browser. Video sessions will open in a new tab or window, so pop-ups will need to be allowed.
  • Refresh the page in your browser
  • Quit and restart the browser
  • Restart your computer

Automated Emails & Notifications

About Student Emails

Handshake sends several types of emails to students for a variety of different reasons. These messages help students activate their accounts, stay informed about activity, and discover relevant opportunities.

Use the expandable headers below to learn about each email type and the domains they come from.

Activation Emails

Activation emails introduce Handshake to students who have not yet logged in and encourage them to access their accounts.

These emails:

  • Are sent to students who have been added to Handshake but have not logged in yet.
  • Are timed based on account creation and ongoing activation campaigns.
  • Share the value of using Handshake and can include curated job recommendations based on student information. All activation emails are sent from noreply@joinhandshake.com.

For more information about activation emails, refer to Student Emails: Activation Email Campaigns (for 4-year institutions) and Student Emails: Community College Activation Campaigns (for Community and technical colleges).

Notifications Emails

Notification emails alert students about activity related to their Handshake accounts (events, jobs, messages, applications, and more).

Key details:

  • Many notification emails can be turned on or off individually by students in their Notification Preferences.
  • These messages are triggered by activity on the platform (for example, event invitations, document updates, application confirmations).
  • Most notification emails are sent from notifications.joinhandshake.com.
  • Event and career fair invitation emails are sent from mail.joinhandshake.com. For a detailed list of optional notification emails and subjects, refer to Student Emails: Optional Notifications.

Transactional Emails

Transactional emails support sign-in and account security. They are sent directly in response to specific student actions on Handshake.

Examples include:

  • Request to set password
  • Request to reset password
  • Temporary passcode
  • Magic link All transactional emails are sent from m.joinhandshake.com.

For more information on transactional emails, refer to Student Emails: Transactional Emails.

Virtual Fair Emails

Virtual fair emails help students prepare for and follow up on virtual career fairs hosted in Handshake.

Key details:

  • A series of notifications is sent to students who register for a virtual fair (registration confirmations, reminders, and updates).
  • All virtual fair emails are sent from mail.joinhandshake.com. For more information on virtual fair emails, refer to Student Emails: Virtual Fair Notifications.

Marketing Emails

Marketing emails are automatically generated to students after they’ve activated their Handshake account.

These emails encourages students to:

  • Fill out their profiles
  • View job postings
  • Apply to jobs in Handshake
  • Is sent from g.joinhandshake.com. For examples and timing of this series, refer to Student Emails: Newly Activated Student Onboarding Series.

Engagement Emails

Engagement emails (also known as Job recommendation digests) are generated to students based on their career interests and job search activity in Handshake.

If a student hasn’t been active for 27 days on the platform, Handshake will send a re-engagement email with a list of dynamic jobs and event recommendations (if available).

Digest emails can include:

  • Engagement digest emails with blog or video content and recommended jobs, employers, events, and fairs.
  • Events recommendation digests that highlight upcoming events and fairs based on student skills and interests.
  • Job recommendation digests that feature recommended jobs based on a student’s profile, career interests, and job search activity.
  • Career fair digests summarizing employers a student connected with at a career fair. Note: if your institution has opted out of marketing emails, students won’t receive these emails.

For additional detail, check out Student Emails: Digest Emails.

Targeted Emails

Targeted emails are messages created and sent by institutions through Handshake to specific groups of students.

Key details:

  • Career services teams compose the content and choose recipients based on filters (such as major, class year, or labels).
  • Content varies by institution and campaign goals (for example, promoting career fairs, workshops, or resources).
  • These emails are sent from mail.joinhandshake.com. To learn how to create and send a targeted email, refer to Creating and Sending Targeted Emails.

Employer Emails: Virtual Fairs Notifications

After employers register for a virtual fair, a series of notification emails are sent to the employer automatically. All emails are sent from “mailer@joinhandshake.com” or “handshake@notifications.joinhandshake.com”. Employers who have not registered for the virtual fair will not receive these emails.

If you’re looking for student virtual fair notifications, check out our dedicated article Student Emails: Virtual Fair Notifications!

Registration approved, create a schedule

Create a schedule: 1 day reminder

Notifications for Students Requesting to Connect to a School

When a student requests to connect with your institution in Handshake, a series of notifications help your team review and respond efficiently. This article outlines when and how career services staff are notified about new connection requests, what each notification includes, and where to manage related settings so you can keep student access accurate and up to date.

Career Services Email Notification

When a student or alum creates their own Handshake account and requests to connect with your school, Handshake sends an email and in-app notification to career services staff so you can review and approve (or reject) the request.

The email includes:

  • From: Handshake handshake@notifications.joinhandshake.com
  • Subject: “You have a new notification on Handshake”
  • Message: lets you know that [Student name] has registered as a student from your school and is waiting for approval, with a link to view and respond to the request in Handshake. If you are not receiving these messages, check your career services notification settings and confirm that “A student from my school has registered and needs approval” is enabled for email (and/or in-app) notifications. For more information on this, refer to Career Services User Settings: Default Notification Preferences.

Student Email Notifications

When a student or alum creates their own Handshake account and requests to connect with your school, Handshake also notifies the student about their request status by email.

While the request is pending

  • From: Handshake handshake@notifications.joinhandshake.com
  • Subject: “Handshake School Registration Information”
  • Message:
    • Greets the student by name and indicates the school they submitted the request to.
    • Confirms that administrators at [School Name] have been notified and will review the request.
    • Directs the student to contact their school at the listed email address if they need further assistance. While their request is pending, the student has limited access to Handshake until they are approved. For more about this limited access experience, refer to Connect to Your School for Full Handshake Access.

When the request is approved

If the connection request is approved (either automatically or by a career services staff member), Handshake sends a second email to the student:

  • From: Handshake handshake@notifications.joinhandshake.com
  • Subject: “Approved Student Registration”
  • Message: Confirms that the request to join [School Name] has been approved. If a student’s request to connect is rejected, they do not receive an email notification about the rejection.

Student Emails: Activation Email Campaigns

Handshake partners with schools to send timely and relevant email messages to undergraduate and community college students who have not yet logged into Handshake. These students are referred to as “unactivated”.

The purpose of these emails is to engage with unactivated students throughout the year and encourage them to start using Handshake.

🚀 Fact: Activation campaigns have historically performed up to 4x higher than industry benchmarks and have led hundreds of thousands of students to start using Handshake!

The content of these campaigns varies depending on what resonates most with students. Some examples of content we’ve featured in past campaigns include:

  • Curated job recommendations
  • Curated lists of employers to follow
  • Tips on navigating your job search
  • Suggestions for getting the most out of Handshake

Initial Activation Emails

After a student is uploaded through the Importer, they will receive activation emails on:

  • Day 1 of account creation
  • Day 4 after the account is created
  • Day 10 after the account is created Below are examples of the emails that they will receive, asking them to activate their accounts:

Day 1 Email

Day 4 Email

Day 10 Email

Activation Campaigns

Afterwards, if they still haven’t activated their account, they will receive emails via our activation campaigns. Activation campaigns are sent weekly and typically consist of 4-6 emails to encourage them to log into Handshake.

Once a student logs into Handshake, they are removed from the campaign.

When a new activation campaign is launched, all unactivated students are included, receiving all 4-6 emails weekly, unless they log into Handshake. If an unactivated student receives all of the campaign emails and doesn’t log into Handshake, we won’t email them again until the next iteration of the campaign launches.

Handshake updates activation campaigns two times a year — before the start of the fall and spring seasons to ensure emails are fresh and engaging.

💡Note: if a new unactivated student is added to Handshake after a campaign has been launched, they’ll start receiving the activation campaign emails the following launch.

Student Emails: Community College Activation Campaigns

Handshake’s Activation Email Campaigns helps supplement your team’s marketing efforts. The campaign targets unactivated community and technical college students to encourage them to log into Handshake for the first time.

With messaging honed over the last two years, these emails have historically yielded student engagement 3-4x above industry averages. Last fall, over 230,000 students logged into Handshake for the first time as a result of receiving these emails.

If a student activates their Handshake account during the campaign, they will stop receiving activation emails.

Fall 2020 Timeline

The campaign itself consists of 2 emails sent 7 days apart. Any unactivated students will get emails on the following cadence:

  • Email 1: Week 1 — October 8-12, 2020
  • Email 2: Week 2 — 7 days after receiving Email 1 If a student activates their Handshake account during the campaign, they will stop receiving activation emails.

We will run additional activation campaigns in future semesters to include future students.

Participation

To manage your preferences for the campaign, navigate to your feature preferences tab. As a Handshake partner school, your institution has been automatically opted in, but you can opt out or in to these emails at any time.

  • Please note! Only individuals who have the “Manage Feature Preferences” permission can opt out of these campaigns. To learn more about this permission level, please refer to this help center article.

Student Emails: Transactional Emails

Transactional emails support student sign-in and account security in Handshake. They are sent directly in response to specific actions a student takes, such as setting or resetting their password.

These emails:

  • Are triggered immediately by student activity on the Handshake platform.
  • Are sent from m.joinhandshake.com.
  • Go to the student’s primary email address on their Handshake account (the address where they receive emails from Handshake and Targeted Emails from your team). Transactional emails are system messages and are separate from optional notification or marketing-style emails.

Types of transactional emails

Handshake currently sends the following student transactional emails related to login and account access.

  • Request to reset password
    • When it sends: A student selects the reset password option.
    • Subject: “Password Reset Request”
  • Password Changed
    • When it sends: A student changes their password
    • Subject: “Your password has been recently changed”
  • One-time password
    • When it sends: A student requests a one-time password to log in quickly.
    • Subject: “Here’s your one-time password”.

Student Emails: Virtual Fair Notifications

Virtual fair notifications are sent to students who register, helping them prepare for and follow up after virtual career fairs hosted in Handshake. This article outlines the emails students receive, when they’re delivered, and what career services users can customize.

Overview

  • A series of notification emails is sent to students who register for a virtual fair in Handshake (similar to in-person fairs).
  • All student virtual fair emails are sent from mail.joinhandshake.com.
  • Students who have not registered for the virtual fair do not receive this registered-student series.

Emails to registered students

Once a student registers for a virtual fair, they receive the following emails:

  1. Fair invite
  • Sent when: student is invited to a fair.
  • Subject: “You’re invited to a career fair”
  • Body: “Your school invited you to [VIRTUAL FAIR NAME]” with a link to register for the fair.
  1. Registration confirmation
  • Sent when: student registers for the fair.
  • Subject: “You’re registered: Summer Sunset Job Fair”
  • Body: “You’re registered! Confirming you’ve registered for [VIRTUAL FAIR NAME] on [DATE].” Includes a link to view the fairs details as well as some “What’s next” steps to prepare. If you added a custom student message when creating the fair, it appears at the top of the email.
  1. Reminder – 2 days before the fair
  • Sent when: student is registered and the fair is 2 days away.
  • Subject: “Two days away! Get ready for [fair name]”.
  1. Reminder – day of the fair
  • Sent when: student is registered and it is the day of the fair.
  • Subject: “Today is [fair name] – get ready!”.
  1. Session cancellation emails (employer-initiated)

These are sent when an employer cancels sessions that the student is already signed up for:

  • 1:1 session canceled
    • Subject: “Career fair 1:1 session canceled: [employee name]”
    • Body: Lets student know their 1 on 1 session with the company is cancelled with a link to browse other other open sessions.
  • Group session canceled
    • Subject: “Career fair group session cancelled: [employer name]”
    • Body: Lets student know their group session with the company is cancelled with a link to browse other other open sessions.
  1. Post-fair follow-up email
  • After the fair ends, Handshake sends a follow-up email to students who attended the virtual fair.

“Just in time” email to unregistered students

To help fill employer sessions, Handshake may send a separate promotional email to students who have not registered for the virtual fair:

  • Purpose: drive additional student signups so employers have students to meet with.
  • Timing: sent the day before the fair when less than 50% of available employer session slots are taken.
  • Audience:
    • Activated, undergraduate students whose activity in Handshake (companies they follow, career interests, etc.) suggests they may be interested in one or more employer sessions at that fair.
    • Qualifications respected: if you set student qualifications for the virtual fair, the system respects those when selecting students for this email.
  • Invite-only events: Handshake does not send this “just in time” email for invite-only events. This email recommends specific employer sessions and calls them out in the body of the message.

What career services can configure

You can influence parts of these emails when setting up your virtual fair:

  • Custom student messaging
    • The Student welcome message you enter in fair setup is emailed to students after they register for the career fair and appears in the registration confirmation email. Learn more about adding a custom student message in Career Fairs: Creation.
  • Invite students email from the fair page
    • You can send invitation emails based on filters such as school year, major, and labels. To learn more about inviting students to a fair, refer to Fairs: Inviting Students.

Brand Page Customization

About your Brand Page

Your Handshake Brand page helps you enhance your employer brand and attract top talent. Use it to share your company’s story and give prospective candidates a deeper understanding of your organization.

Your Brand page features employee testimonials, job listings, upcoming events, and more, giving job seekers valuable insights before they apply.

Brand page tabs

Your Brand page includes three tabs:

  • Overview
  • Jobs
  • Posts

Overview

The Overview tab includes customizable and non-customizable sections to highlight key aspects of your company.

All employers have access to the following sections:

Banner, logo, and company details

The company header sits at the top of your Brand Page and includes two editable elements:

  • Banner: The large image displayed at the top. The banner can only be customized by Essentials and Enterprise (formerly TES) customers with a Professional or Advanced Brand page. Basic, Plus, and Pro employers will have a gray banner by default.
  • Company details: Displays your logo, company name, industry, location, company size, company type, and website URL. About

The About section introduces your company to potential candidates with a brief overview of who you are and what you do.

Work life

The Work life showcases your company’s benefits, perks, and culture, highlighting what makes your workplace unique to potential candidates.

Jobs

The Jobs section displays up to four featured jobs on your Brand page. You can manually select which jobs to highlight, and unused slots are automatically filled with jobs relevant to each viewer.

Events

The Events section displays the four most relevant events or fairs for each student, based on their profile and search activity.

Attendees or invitees can only view events that their school has been invited to, or that are being held at their school. To ensure the most relevant events are displayed, regularly update and manage your events.

Note: This section cannot be customized or edited.

Essentials and Enterprise customers have access to the following additional sections. Features vary based on their brand page tier and any added modules.

Subpages (available only with an Advanced Brand Page)

Subpages give students an in-depth view of specific teams, departments, or programs within your company.

Each subpage functions as a mini Brand page, with a banner, media gallery, and featured jobs, people, and events. Each subpage also supports custom sections for additional flexibility.

Learn more about Branding your Subpages.

Posts (available only with a Professional or Advanced Brand Page)

The Posts section displays up to two featured brand posts from you, your teammates, or your company.

A View all link directs students to the Posts tab, where all company posts are listed in reverse chronological order.

Employers with an Advanced Brand page can also feature up to two posts on each subpage.

Testimonials (available only with a Professional or Advanced Brand Page)

The Testimonials section displays reviews and reflections from current employees, giving candidates insight into the employee experience at your company.

People (available only with a Professional or Advanced Brand Page)

The People section displays individuals at your organization, allowing candidates to connect with them directly.

You can manually select up to four people to feature, and unused slots can be automatically filled with teammates relevant to each viewer.

Jobs and Posts

To the right of the Overview tab, you will find the Jobs and Posts tab.

Jobs (tab)

The Jobs tab displays up to 50 of your company’s active job postings, listed by relevance.

Candidates can click any job title to view the full posting and apply.

Posts (tab)

The Posts tab displays all of your company’s content and community posts from the Feed, arranged in reverse chronological order.

Learn more about Managing Content on the Feed.

Additional resources

  • To update your company details, refer to How to Edit Your Company Profile Settings.
  • To customize your Brand page sections, including featured jobs, refer to Customizing your Brand Page.
  • For subpage setup and customization, refer to Branding your Subpages.
  • To create or manage posts, refer to Managing Content on the Feed.

Create up to six subpages, each featuring a banner image, media gallery, and highlights of jobs, people, and events.

Subpages are only available to Essentials and Enterprise (formerly TES) customers with an Advanced Brand Page. For more information, please check out this resource!

Subpage details

  • To remove a selected event or fair, click the red bin icon to the right of the event or fair name.
  • To change the order in which events are displayed on the subpage, click the up or down arrows next to each item.
  1. After selecting and arranging the events or fairs in the order you want them displayed on the subpage, click the black Save button.
Gallery

To share images and videos specific to this subpage, click the plus icon to the right of the Gallery section.

To view the guided steps, refer to Manage your Brand Page Gallery.

Customizing your Brand Page

Your Handshake Brand Page helps you build your employer brand and attract the right talent. Use it to showcase your company’s culture, values, people, and opportunities for early talent.

Features available to Essentials and Enterprise (formerly TES) customers only are indicated by an asterisk (*). For more information, please check out this resource.

Who can view and edit your Brand Page

  • Only account owners or admins can customize the Brand page.
  • Your Brand Page is only visible to early talent with active Handshake accounts unless you enable the “Allow public pages (SEO)” setting in your company settings.
  • Brand Pages are viewable by candidates, career services, and other employers.

Access your Brand page

To access your brand page, click Brand page from the left navigation bar in Handshake.

Edit your banner, logo, and company details

The company header appears at the top of your Brand page, above the Overview, Jobs, and Posts tabs.

To edit it, click the pencil icon in the upper-right corner of the header.

The following fields can be edited:

  • Industry
  • Primary location
  • Locations
  • Company size
  • Company type (optional)
  • Contact email (optional)
  • URL To update your company name, contact Support.

When finished, click Save in the lower-right corner.

For logo and banner uploads, refer to the Employer Logo & Banner Guide.

Customize your Overview tab

The Overview tab contains all customizable Brand page sections. Click each header below to learn how to personalize them.

About

Click the pencil icon to the right of the About section.

In the pop-up, provide a brief overview of who your company is and what it does. Keeping it short and sweet is best to ensure it captures the reader’s attention quickly.

Note: The character limit is 2000.

When finished, click the black Save button in the lower-right corner.

Work life

Click the pencil icon to the right of the Work life section.

Note: If left blank, this section will not appear on your page.

In the pop-up, enter a description that highlights your specific benefits, perks, and workplace culture.

Note: The character limit is 2000.

  • You can select specific benefits using the available radio button options, or add custom benefits in the Additional benefits field. When finished, click the black Save button in the lower-right corner.

*Testimonials

The Testimonials section is only available to Essentials and Enterprise (formerly TES) customers with a Professional or Advanced Brand page.

To manage testimonials, click the pencil icon to the right of the Testimonials section.

Add a testimonial

To add a new testimonial, click Create testimonial.

Note: There is no limit to the number of testimonials you can add.

In the pop-up, enter the following fields:

  • First name
  • Last name
  • Role
  • School name
  • Major (optional)
  • Graduation year (optional)
  • Testimonial

Edit testimonial

Click the pencil icon to the right of the employee’s name.

In the pop-up, edit the necessary fields, then click Save in the lower-right corner.

Delete testimonial

Click the red bin icon to the right of the employee’s name. This action is immediate and cannot be undone.

Jobs

The Jobs section always appears on your Brand page, even if you have no active jobs.

To feature specific jobs, click the pencil icon to the right of the Jobs section. You can highlight up to four jobs.

  • Use the search field to find and add jobs by name or ID.
  • Use the up or down arrows to change the display order.

When finished, click Save in the lower-right corner.

*People

The People section is only available to Essentials and Enterprise (formerly TES) customers with a Professional or Advanced Brand Page.

To manage which teammates appear on your Brand page, click the pencil icon to the right of the People section. You can add up to four people.

  • Use the search field to find and add teammates by name.
  • Use the up or down arrows to change the display order.
  • Click the red bin icon to remove a teammate. If this section is not customized, or if your account type does not allow customization, up to four relevant teammates will appear here.

The Automatically fill unused slots with people relevant to each viewer toggle is on by default.

  • When enabled, any unfilled spots are populated automatically based on each student’s interactions, such as teammates who have recently messaged them.
  • Turn this off if you want only your manually selected teammates to appear. When finished, click Save in the lower-right corner.

*Gallery

The Gallery section is only available to Essentials and Enterprise (formerly TES) customers with a Professional or Advanced Brand Page.

To manage visual content on your Brand page, click the pencil icon to the right of the Gallery section. For guided steps, refer to Manage your Brand Page Gallery.

Each subpage supports custom sections, giving you more flexibility to tailor the experience for different audiences.

Learn more about Branding your Subpages.

*Posts

Essentials and Enterprise (formerly TES) customers with a Professional or Advanced Brand page can feature up to two posts on their Brand page.

Additionally, Essentials and Enterprise customers with an Advanced Brand page can feature up to two posts on each subpage.

To feature a post:

  1. Navigate to the Posts tab on your Brand page, or go to your profile or a teammate’s profile and click the Posts tab.

  2. Click the three-dot menu in the upper-right corner of the post.

  3. Check the Brand page box to feature it on your main Brand page. With an Advanced Brand Page, check the box for the relevant subpage to feature it there.

*Affiliated employers

Affiliated employers show the relationship between your brand and related companies on Handshake. Students can follow or explore affiliated brands directly from your Brand Page.

Note: This feature is only available to Enterprise (formerly TES) customers with an Advanced Brand Page. To set it up, contact your account team or Support.

  • Up to six affiliated employers are displayed. If there are more than six, a More option appears to view the full list.
  • To add or remove affiliates, contact Support.
  • If left blank, this section will not appear on your page.
Display order

To change the display order, click the pencil icon next to the section title and use the up or down arrows.

Note: Your parent company always displays at the top.

Access brand page

Add your company logo

New logo

New banner

  1. Click the white Edit banner button in the upper-right corner of the banner.

  2. In the pop-up window, click the white Upload photo button, then choose a photo from your computer.

  • Upload an image around 2340 x 400 pixels (a 6:1 wide ratio) for the sharpest, crispest result.
  • Use a centrally focused image so important elements remain visible across screen sizes.
  • Avoid including text elements, since they may be cropped at different screen sizes.
  • The banner image must be at least 1200 pixels wide. Images smaller than this get upscaled and may appear blurry.
  1. Use the Zoom In (+) and Zoom Out (-) buttons to adjust the photo’s magnification within the pop-up window. Once your photo is adjusted, click the black Save button in the lower-right corner.

  2. In the pop-up window, adjust the photo’s magnification or click Remove to delete the current photo.

  • To adjust the magnification, click the black Save button once satisfied with the new size.
  • To remove the current photo and upload a new one, click the white Remove button. In the pop-up window, click the red Yes, remove button.
  1. Once the photo is removed, upload a new banner. If needed, refer to the steps outlined for New banner.
