Build Your Network

Access Employer User Profiles on Handshake

Handshake gives you access to employer user profiles that highlight work experience, education, bios, and professional affiliations. Taking time to review this information helps you understand who you’re reaching out to and craft a more thoughtful, personalized message.

Before contacting an employer, exploring their profile demonstrates initiative, preparation, and genuine interest in their role or organization—setting the stage for a more meaningful connection.

Here are two ways to access employer profiles on Handshake:

  • Through their company profile
  • From your messages

Employers Company Profile Page

Up to four employer users may be displayed on a company profile. These users have either chosen to make their profiles visible or are shown automatically based on relevance and prior interactions.

To find an employer associated with a specific company, select Employers from the left navigation menu and search for the company you’d like to explore. Open the company profile, scroll to the People section, and click the employer’s name to view their profile.

From the employer’s profile, select Message to start a conversation or Follow to stay connected on Handshake.

To learn more about sending messages to employers, refer to Messaging Employers in Handshake.

From your Messages Inbox

If you receive a message from an employer on Handshake, you can access their profile directly from the conversation.

While viewing the message, click the employer’s profile photo or their name and title at the top of the message to open their profile.

If you receive an introduction message to connect with a teammate, you can also view that person’s profile. Click the teammate’s name within the message to open their profile in a new tab.

From the employer’s profile, select Message to start a conversation or Follow to stay connected on Handshake.

To learn more about sending messages to employers, refer to Messaging Employers in Handshake.

Accessibility for Virtual Interactions on Handshake

Handshake is committed to making its platform accessible to all students, recognizing the importance of inclusivity in virtual interactions. This article provides guidance on how to navigate virtual events, appointments, and fairs with all users’ needs in mind.

Handshake’s Virtual Accessibility Features

Handshake has implemented several features to support students with disabilities. This includes the ability to request a transcriber for live captioning or an ASL interpreter during virtual events.

Requesting a Transcriber or ASL Interpreter

If you are in need of a transcriber or ASL interpreter for a virtual event, you’ll need to contact your school’s career center or accessibility office.

Your school will collaborate with the Handshake Support team to arrange for a transcriber or ASL interpreter to participate in your online interactions on Handshake.

🚀Tip: the sooner you can contact your school, the better!

To find your school’s career center information in Handshake, refer to How to Locate your School’s Contact Information in Handshake.

Requesting additional accommodations

If you require any additional accommodations or special arrangements, you’ll need to reach out to your school’s career services or accessibility office. They will assist you in arranging your specific request to ensure that you can participate in your virtual interaction.

To find your school’s career center information in Handshake, refer to How to Locate your School’s Contact Information in Handshake.

Handshake is continuously working to improve its accessibility features. It’s a priority of ours to make sure all users can participate in all virtual interactions across the platform.

Closed Captioning Functions

The option for closed captioning during a live event is coming soon!

Additional Resources

For more information on connecting virtually with employers on Handshake, check out Connecting Virtually with Employers and Your School via Handshake.

To learn more about attending a virtual appointment with your career services, refer to Attending Virtual Appointments on Handshake.

Campus Profiles in Handshake

Campus Profiles are an integral part of the peer-to-peer learning and sharing experience. A Campus Profile is a student or alumni profile that is visible to other Handshake students.

💡Note: you can only view other profiles if your profile’s privacy settings are set to Employers or Private. To message a peer and engage on the platform, you’ll need the Community setting in Handshake.

To learn more about the privacy options for your profile, refer to Profile Privacy Options in Handshake.

To access the Student Community page, navigate to Handshake, then click People on the left navigation menu.

Click on the expandable headers to learn more!

Why are Campus Profiles important?

Campus Profiles are designed to foster peer-to-peer learning among students and alumni!

For instance, you might be unsure of what work experience or projects to include on your profile, or you may wonder about potential career paths for a specific major. By connecting with others, you can learn from their experiences! Get valuable advice on choosing a major, building a resume, and much more.

Campus Profiles also offer a chance to connect with students and alumni working in fields of interest. You can ask them about their experiences, gain insights into different industries, or even start building your professional network for the future!

How do Campus Profiles work?

All students on Handshake have profiles and can access the People page. However, to engage with peers on the Explore Students page, you must set your privacy settings to Community. Without this setting, you won’t be able to view full profiles or send messages.

Campus Profiles include the following sections:

  • Profile Picture
  • *Pronouns - only if they have chosen to share their pronouns with peers
  • School Year and Grad Date
  • Education
  • Work & Volunteer Experience
  • Organizations/Extracurriculars
  • Courses
  • Projects
  • Skills
  • A Message button Important: certain fields cannot be viewed by other students - these include your GPA, Work Authorization, Email address, Ethnicity, Gender, Hometown, or any documents you’ve uploaded.

To update your profile in Handshake to help other students find and connect with you, refer to Completing your Profile in Handshake.

Explore the People Community page

On the People page, Handshake displays two sections:

  • Peers you might know
  • Alumni to follow Each section shows up to 3 peer suggestions, each with a Follow button. Next to every suggestion, you’ll find a profile summary that includes their name, school, school year, major, two most recent employers, and two most recent organizations.

For more details on following users on Handshake, check out Following Users on Handshake.

You can also use the filters at the top of the page to discover more peers to connect with:

  • Keyword Search
  • School
  • Employer
  • Job role
  • All filters (opens as a side sheet)
    • Major
    • Degree
    • Grad year
    • Skill
    • Organization If your profile’s privacy is currently set to Employers or Private

If your privacy setting is currently set to “Employers” or “Private,” you can access the Explore People page and use the search filters. However, you will not be able to send messages to other students.

When you click on a student’s name, you’ll be taken to their profile, but the option to message them will be unavailable.

To enable messaging, you’ll need to update your profile’s privacy setting to “Community.” For instructions on how to change your privacy settings, refer to How to Change Your Student Profile Privacy Setting.

Once your privacy setting is set to Community, you will be able to send messages both from the People page and from individual profiles.

For more information on sending messages, refer to Peer Messaging in Handshake.

When your profile’s privacy is set to Community

When you find a peer you’d like to message on the People page, click their name to view their profile in Handshake. From their profile, click the button Message on the left side of the page to start a conversation!

For more information on sending messages, refer to Peer Messaging in Handshake.

Additional Resources

To complete your profile in Handshake, refer to Completing your Profile in Handshake.

To edit the information on your profile, check out the following articles:

  • How to Edit Education Information on Your Profile
  • Update Personal Information on Your Profile
  • How to Edit the Summary on Your Profile

Discover Events & Fairs in Handshake

The Events page is designed to help you find the most relevant events for your career journey.

Whether you’re looking for career fairs, employer info sessions, networking events, or skill-building workshops, you can use filters, browse by groupings, or search by keyword to discover opportunities that interest you.

Access the Events page

To start discovering events and fairs, click Events in the left navigation menu.

Filter your results

There are numerous filters available to help narrow your search.

  • Keyword search: Search for an event or fair using the keyword search bar.
    • Note: Keyword search may not filter the results, but it does affect the ordering.
  • Career Center collections: Search for events and fairs curated by your school’s career services department.
    • To learn more about your school’s career center collections, check out Career Center Collections at your School.
  • Category: Filter your results by identifying a particular category:
    • Career Fair: Hiring events with numerous employers at your school
    • Hiring: Find opportunities with employers that want to hire you now
    • Guidance: Resources for your career, job skills, resume, interviewing, and more
    • Conference: All-day and multi-day events like expos, summits, and tradeshows
    • Networking: Social events with people who can help grow your professional network
    • Employer Info: Learn about companies, like day-to-day life, culture, and teams
    • Academic: Resources and info related to your school
    • General: General topics of interest
  • Medium: Filter results by Virtual or In-Person.
    • Note: All mediums are displayed by default.
  • Date: View results by date:
    • When are you looking?
      • All upcoming (automatically selected)
      • Today
      • Next 10 days
      • Next 30 days
      • Past year (allows you to view events and fairs from the previous year)
    • Time of Day
    • Morning
    • Afternoon
  • Days of the week (Monday–Sunday)
  • Employer: Use the keyword search to find results with a specific employer.
  • More filters:
    • Labels: Use the keyword search to locate results using a specific label
    • Events: Check the box to only view results posted by your school
    • Career Center: Select events at a specific career center
    • Sort: Use the three-lines icon to sort results by Relevance or Date

Browse by grouping

You can also discover events and fairs by specific groupings. Click on the tiles located below the filters:

  • Career fairs at your school
    • Shows all career fairs hosted by your school only
  • Career center employer events
    • Shows any school-hosted events with attending employers. This includes:
      • School-owned and school-hosted events (virtual, in-person, hybrid)
      • Employer-owned and school-hosted events (on campus, in-person, hybrid)
    • Note: This group does not include career fairs.
  • Career center guidance events
    • Shows school events with the category of “career guidance,” such as resume reviews
  • Events hosted by employers
    • Shows employer-owned and employer-hosted events approved by the school 💡Note: If you use one of the filters, the grouping tiles will be hidden to display the results of your search.

Access saved, registered, and past events

To quickly access your Saved, Registered, and Check-in events, click the following icons in the upper-right corner of the Events page:

  • Bookmark icon (Saved)
    • Any event you’ve saved but not registered for
  • Calendar icon (Registered)
    • Any event you’ve registered for but have not attended yet
  • Checkmark icon (Check-ins)
    • Any event you’ve attended

Register for an event

Once you find an event or fair that interests you, click on the tile to load the overview page, where you can review details and register!

For more information on registering for an event in Handshake, refer to Registering for an Event.

Following Users on Handshake

Following users on Handshake is more than just a social feature—it’s a way to actively shape your educational and professional journey. By choosing to follow users, you stay up-to-date with their most recent content posted to the feed and so much more!

Topics:

  • Benefits of following users on Handshake
  • How to follow users
  • Locate the users you’re following
  • Unfollow users

Benefits of following users on Handshake

  1. Stay Updated with Relevant Content: Our algorithm prioritizes content from users you follow. This ensures their new posts will appear at the top of your feed.

  2. Gain Insights and Inspiration: The feed is a rich source of career advice, tips, and inspirational stories from alumni and professionals. Following users can make the feed an engaging space to learn, grow, and stay inspired within your career journey!

  3. Expand Your Network: By following users, you can engage with their content and build professional connections with them. These connections may be helpful for future opportunities and collaborations in your career.

  4. Receive Personalized Recommendation: Our algorithm tailors recommendations to your interests. By following users who align with your academic and professional goals, you help the platform offer more relevant content and connections, making your experience more valuable.

How to follow users

You can follow users via two ways on Handshake:

  • Directly from the feed
  • The user’s profile
Directly from the feed

Click the plus icon on their profile icon. To confirm your follow, a black banner will appear in the lower-right corner of the page, displaying the message ‘Following [User NAME].’

💡Note: once following, the plus icon will no longer be available to click.

The user’s profile

Access users profiles from the feed or the People section in Handshake.

  • From the feed: click on the user’s name to be directed to their profile.
  • From the People section: click People on the left navigation menu, then use the filters on the left of the page to find students and alumni on Handshake. Click on their name to be directed to their profile.
    • To learn more about campus profiles and exploring the People community page, check out Campus Profiles in Handshake. Once on the user’s profile, click the black button Follow. To confirm your follow, the button will be grayed out and changed to Unfollow.

Locate the users you’re following

To locate users your following in Handshake, click on your icon located in the upper-right corner of the screen. Then click My Profile from the dropdown.

Once on your profile, click following, located below your name and school information within your header.

A pop-up will appear with a list of users you are following. Here, you can click on their name to be directed to their profile or click Unfollow to unfollow them.

Click the X in the upper-right corner of the pop-up to return to your profile.

🚀Tip: access your followers via your profile by clicking followers, located to the left of following. In the pop-up that appears, click the black button Follow back to those you want to follow!

Unfollow users

Unfollowing users can be done directly from the feed, the user’s profile, or from your following list.

  • From the feed, click on the three dots menu located to the right of their name, then click Unfollow from the dropdown.
  • On the user profile, click Unfollow, located to the right of the message button.
  • From your following list, accessed from your profile, click Unfollow to the right of the user you don’t want to follow. If you’d like to post to the feed, refer to Posting Content to the Handshake Feed.

To post on the feed, your profile visibility must be set to Community. Learn more about your profile visibility options in Profile Privacy Options in Handshake, and find step-by-step instructions for updating your visibility settings How to Change Your Student Profile Privacy Setting.

Handshake’s Guide to Attending a Virtual Fair

Virtual fairs offer an incredible opportunity to connect with employers from wherever you may be. Whether you’re a seasoned attendee or joining for the first time, this guide will provide you with essential tips and strategies to make the most of your experience!

Virtual Fairs overview

Schools may choose to host career fairs virtually via Handshake. Similar to in-person fairs, employers that recruit from your school can register to attend.

Once the employer’s registration is approved by the school, the employer creates a schedule for the virtual sessions they plan to host.

Employers can host two types of sessions to interact with students:

  • Group Sessions: intended for multiple attendees
  • 1:1 Sessions: intended for one student and one employer representative The session length for both group and 1:1 sessions may vary! We recommend paying attention to session length when signing up — sessions may be 10, 15, 20, 30, 45, or 60 minutes.

In these sessions, employers will be identified as the Host, and they’ll be able to share their screen with participants.

Identifying Virtual Fairs

Click Events on the left menu, then click Medium from the filters located at the top of the page. From the dropdown, check the box next to Virtual.

All virtual fairs that your school is hosting or was invited to will be displayed on the page.

Note: you can click on More Filters, then check the box for Posted by my school to discover events posted by your school only.

To save an event to review later, click the bookmark icon to the far right of the name to save it. When you’re ready to access your saved events, click Saved, located in the upper-right corner of the event page.

To load the fair’s overview page and review available sessions, click on the fair’s name.

To register for the Fair, click the button Register on the fair’s overview page.

Sign up for sessions

  • From the overview page, click on the Available Sessions tab to review and sign up for sessions.
    • For details on this process, refer to Signing Up for & Managing Virtual Fair Sessions.
  • To sign up for Group or 1:1 sessions, you may be prompted to update your profile’s privacy settings. We recommend using Community to make the most of your Handshake experience, as this will allow you to participate in all fair sessions and engage with other students/alumni!
    • For more information on profile privacy, refer to Profile Privacy Options in Handshake.
  • Review which employers are attending the fair (follow the employers you want to check back in with)!
    • For more information on following an employer, refer to Following an Employer in Handshake. You’ll be able to sign up for sessions at any point, even during the fair (as long as the session hasn’t ended).

Preparing for the Fair

To help you prepare for a successful fair, check out the following tips and resources!

  • Make sure you have the right setup to support session audio and video.
    • Attendee Requirements for Integrated Video
    • To request an ASL interpreter, refer to Requesting an ASL Interpreter or Transcriber for Virtual Interactions and Virtual Fairs: Accessibility.
  • Complete your profile
    • How to Drive Profile Completion For tips on attending a virtual fair, check out our blog post Attending a virtual career fair? Here are 10 tips you need to know.

Participating in the Fair

All sessions will have the option for Handshake video, audio, and text-based chat. There’s no customization for types of interaction. It is up to the employer and student joining the session to decide how they’d like to connect.

For details on day-of participation, refer to Participating in a Virtual Fair.

As long as you’ve signed up for the session successfully, you’ll be able to join up to 5 minutes before the session starts and throughout the duration of the session.

We want you to feel as safe as possible while attending virtual fairs and interacting with employers, so we’ve taken several steps to ensure your safety. Read more about these steps in Reporting an Issue at a Virtual Fair.

Following up after the Fair

Once the fair has wrapped up, you can followup with employers in Handshake immediately after your session via the pop-up that appears automatically.

  • If the session has multiple hosts, click the Send a message button to the right of the hosts name you’d like to continue a conversation with.
  • If the session has one host, the text box will load immediately. Type your message within the text box, then click the Send button in the lower-left corner to continue the conversation.

Not sure what to say? We suggest to:

  • Follow up on something you found interesting or helpful from the event.

  • Show your enthusiasm for a role, this company, or the industry.

  • Ask questions about the company. You can follow up with recruiters later by:

  • following their company profile (receive notifications of employer activity at your school)

  • messaging other students or alumni that have worked for the employer or a publicly listed point of contact for the company

  • responding to an employer message

  • applying for an active job

  • participating in an interview schedule

  • attending an event To review who you’ve attended sessions with, navigate back to the fair in Handshake with the direct link to the fair or browse using the Date filter on the Events overview page, then selecting “Past year”.

Click on the Your schedule tab for a list of past sessions you signed up for. The session host’s name, job title, and company will display.

Click the Send a message button, to the right of the host’s information, to send a follow-up message.

FAQ’s

Will students be able to submit their resumes to employers? Without joining sessions?

  • Yes! When students sign up to meet with employers in 1:1 and/or group sessions, they’re added to a RSVPs list, and employers will have access to these students’ public resumes (featured on profile) before and after the fair. Refer to Understanding Document Visibility for more details and steps to quickly change visibility. Will students who live internationally be able to participate?

  • There are no restrictions by location, so as long as the student has logged into Handshake, they’ll be able to participate. Will students, employers and career staff have access to transcripts of the chats they had during the virtual fair?

  • Yes! At the end of the session, click the download icon located in the lower-right corner of the chat to download the chat.

How Peer Messaging Flags and Content Moderation Work

Handshake provides students with the opportunity to connect and communicate about career-related topics on the platform. To maintain a safe and professional environment, Handshake moderates messages exchanged between users.

To learn more about peer messaging on the platform, refer to Peer Messaging in Handshake.

Moderation

Messages sent on Handshake are passed through an automatic text analysis system. This system checks for profanity, discriminatory language, and other content that may violate Handshake’s content guidelines. Messages that are reported through the automatic text analysis are reviewed my our Content Moderation team.

If a message is flagged, this will send a report to our Content Moderation team, who will then review the message, and loop in the school as needed for awareness and/or followup.

Note: when a message is flagged, this blocks the conversation from continuing until further review.

To learn more about how to flag a message, refer to Peer Messaging in Handshake.

Messaging Guidelines

Handshake has guidelines students must agree to before messaging others on the platform.

  • Be professional and career focused.
  • Use appropriate and respectful language.
  • Understand that messages may be moderated by Handshake.

Protection from University Liability

Our corporate counsel has verified that universities are not liable for student messaging on Handshake due to the following reasons:

  • Settled law: Universities provide email services and other student-to-student messaging services. They are not responsible for the student’s communication on the services.
  • Handshake services are neutral: Handshake Messaging does not encourage or specifically enable gender-based targeting of students.
  • Handshake TOS/PP governs: Only students that agree to Handshake’s Terms Of Service, Privacy Policy, and Messaging Guidelines can use student messaging.
  • Handshake Moderation Policy: Designed to focus conversation on career-related topics, and prevent issues from escalating.

How to Use Messages in Handshake

Messaging on Handshake is a powerful tool for networking, building relationships, and advancing your career! Once your account is activated, you’ll be able to send and receive messages from employers, fellow students, alumni, and career services professionals.

This article will guide you on how to maximize your messaging experience on Handshake.

Employers and students cannot send messages to you if your profile is private. To send and receive messages, you’ll need to update your privacy settings. Learn more about your profile privacy options in Profile Privacy Options on Handshake.

Accessing Messages

You can access your messages on both the website and mobile app.

Types of messages you may receive on Handshake include:

  • Personal messages from peers and alumni.
  • Follow-up messages from employers about a fair, event, or job application.
  • Promotional messages from employers highlighting job openings or upcoming events/fairs they’re attending.
  • Handshake Matchmaker messages, which are AI-generated by Handshake to share relevant opportunities with you To check your inbox and view your messages, follow the steps below.

Note: to ensure you don’t miss important opportunities, bulk actions (like marking all messages as read) are not available.

Website

  1. Click Inbox on the left navigation menu to view your conversations with employers and peers.

  2. Conversations are sorted by the most recent message received. Click on the conversation to display the message.

  3. At the top of the message thread, the following sender information is displayed:

  • Employer: name, job title, and company.
  • Student/Alumni: name, major, degree, school, and school year.
  1. When using messages via desktop web, you can filter conversations by:
  • Inbox
  • Unread
  • Archived To filter, click on the desired tab above your messages.

Tip: To adjust the size of your message, you can zoom in to make the text larger or zoom out to make it smaller and view more of the message at once.

  • On Windows or Linux: Press Ctrl and + to zoom in, or Ctrl and - to zoom out.
  • On Mac: Press ⌘ (Command) and + to zoom in, or ⌘ and - to zoom out.

Mobile app

  1. Tap Inbox in the lower-right corner of your device’s screen.

  2. Conversations will appear in order of the most recent message. You can also use the search bar to look for a specific sender or keyword within a message.

  3. Tap on the conversation to open the message thread. At the top of the message thread is information about the sender:

  • Employer: name, job title, and company.
  • Student/Alumni: name, major, degree, school, and school year. Responding to a Message

To respond or continue the conversation, start typing your message in the available text box, then click or tap Send to the right of the text box.

To learn more about responding to employer messages, check out Responding to an Employer Message on Handshake.

If you’ve received a campaign message from an employer, and you’d like to respond that you’re not interested in the opportunity, refer to “Not Interested” in Employer Campaign Messages for more details.

Trust and Safety of Messages

At Handshake, your safety is our top priority. To help ensure a secure experience, all messages sent through the platform automatically go through Handshake’s text analyzers to detect and prevent inappropriate content.

When using Handshake’s messaging feature, you have the option to report or flag message threads. Our Trust and Safety team carefully reviews all reported or flagged messages. This allows our team to research the flag and followup as needed.

We strongly recommend keeping all conversations within the Handshake platform. If messages are exchanged outside of Handshake, our guidelines can no longer be enforced, and we won’t be able to assist in ensuring your safety.

Additional Resources

  • Get advice, build your network, and more with Peer Messaging in Handshake.
  • Learn how to connect with employers in Messaging Employers in Handshake.
  • Find out more about Receiving Employer Messages in Handshake.
  • Learn more about messaging limits in Message & Feed Activity Limits on Handshake.

Messaging Employers in Handshake

If you’re interested in connecting with employers, we highly recommend using Handshake’s messaging feature. Handshake is the only platform where employers actively make themselves available to students, eager to connect and assist you in your career journey.

Messaging on Handshake provides a safe, direct way to build relationships with employers. It shows initiative and can help you:

  • Gain more details about a job you’re interested in
  • Learn more about a company
  • Prepare for interviews
  • Get answers to any questions you may have You can only send messages to Employers if your profile’s privacy is set to Employers or Community. For more information on privacy settings on Handshake, refer to Profile Privacy on Handshake.

Click on the expandable headers to learn more about the benefits of messaging employers in Handshake and how to message to employers!

Messaging Benefits

There are many advantages to messaging employers on Handshake! For instance, employers who are open to connecting with early talent can:

  • Recommend jobs that may be a good fit for you
  • Share their availability and schedule virtual meetings
    • For additional information, refer to Virtual Chats with Employers
  • Inform you about upcoming employer-hosted events or meetings If you want to learn more about which employers can message students or how employers find students to connect with, check out Receiving Employer Messages in Handshake.

How to Message an Employer

If you’d like to reach out to an employer you’ve never interacted with before, you can message them through:

  • An active job posting
  • The company’s profile page
  • A message attachment*

Active job posting

If an employer is open to receiving messages, you can contact them directly from the job posting.

Click the white button Message, located midway down the page under the section titled “Ask [Employer Name]”

Tip: consider asking about the role, company culture, or tips for succeeding in the application process.

In the pop-up that appears, type your message in the text box then click the blue button Send message to send!

A confirmation message will appear, letting you know you message was successfully sent. To review your message thread, go to your Handshake Inbox. For more details on accessing your messages, refer to How to Use Messages in Handshake.

For step-by-step instructions on how to apply for a job, check out Apply for a Job in Handshake.

Company Profile

Employers can be found on the Overview page of the company profile under People. This section includes employer users who have made themselves available to receive messages.

Note: if no employer users have made themselves available to receive messages, the People section will not be visible.

To message an employer, click on their name to be directed to their profile, then click Message.

In the pop-up, type your message and click the Send button when you’re ready!

Message attachment*

Some employers may recommend a team member for you to connect with—this could be someone you’ve not yet interacted with from the company. If this happens, the employer will send you a message with the recommended team member’s profile attached.

Click on the attached user to be directed to their profile and send a message.

To learn more about receiving messages from employers, refer to Receiving Employer Messages in Handshake.

Mute Employer Campaign Messages

If you’ve received a campaign message from an employer or location that doesn’t interest you, you can temporarily remove yourself from the send-list to avoid receiving any similar outreach for 90 days.

You can mute yourself from campaign messages by choosing one of the following options:

  • Employer outreach
    • You won’t receive any campaign messages from the employer for 90 days. This includes messages sent from other users at the company.
  • Location outreach
    • You won’t receive any campaign messages for the specific job location for 90 days. This applies to any Handshake-hosted jobs associated with the specified job location.
    • Note: To mute a location, the job promoted in the campaign must have a location listed. Muting yourself only applies to campaign outreach. You may still receive bulk outreach or 1:1 messages.

Campaign messages are used by employers to highlight opportunities they think may interest you.

If you need to report a message in Handshake, refer to Safety: Report a Message.

Mute a Message via Campaign

  1. In your inbox, locate the message you’d like to mute and click on it to open the full message.

  2. At the bottom of the message, click the white button Not Interested.

  3. In the pop-up that appears, select what you’d like to mute:

    • The company for 90 days
    • The location for 90 days
    • (If the campaign does not specify a work location, the option to mute by location will not be available. In that case, you can only mute messages from the company.)

  4. Once you’ve selected your preferred option, click the black Confirm button in the lower-right corner of the pop-up. The campaign message will then be moved to your Archived messages.

Note: Muting a campaign message temporarily does not affect your job preferences, and employers will not be notified that you’ve muted them.

Unmute or Unarchive messages

To access your archived messages and unmute a campaign, click the Archived tab under Inbox. Locate the muted campaign message and click the blue Unmute link.

To unarchive the message, click the three dots in the upper-right corner of the message and select Unarchive. This will move the message back to your All inbox.

Peer Messaging in Handshake

Handshake allows you to message fellow students and alumni on the platform, enhancing your ability to connect and learn from your peers.

To send and receive messages from other students and alumni, your profile’s privacy settings must be set to Community. For more information on privacy options and steps to update, refer to Profile Privacy Options in Handshake.

Finding Peers to Connect with

You can find peers to message via the following ways in Handshake:

  • An active Job Posting
  • The Handshake Home Feed
  • The Explore People page

An active Job Posting

To encourage students to learn about jobs and employers they’re interested in, Handshake offers the ability for students to message peers directly from a job posting.

Note: message-able peers are only displayed if the job doesn’t have a message-able job poster, and will be displayed as “Alumni at this company” or “Alumni in similar roles” — Not all jobs will have message-able peers displayed.

Message-able peers are based on numerous factors in Handshake: recent activity, messaging volume, response rates, job role similarity with current job, etc.

Jobs with message-able peers can be identified directly on the Jobs overview page, located at the bottom.

  • “Alumni at this company” is surfaced if there’s alumni working at the company your viewing a job for.
  • “Alumni in similar roles” is surfaced if there’s not enough alumni that work at the company. Thus, we display alumni in similar roles for you to connect with; they just don’t work at the company. Click on the user’s name to be directed to their profile, then click the button Message, located in the upper-right corner of the page.

Within the pop-up, click in the text box to add your custom message, then click the button Send to send!

The Handshake Home Feed

To message a user from the feed, click on their name to be directed to the profile. Alternatively, the feed may promote a section titled “Get advice from peers” — Click the button Message to be directed to the their profile.

From the user’s profile, click the button Message, located to the upper-right corner of the page.

Within the pop-up, click in the text box to add your custom message, then click the button Send to send!

To learn more about the discovering content on the feed, refer to Handshake Feed: Overview & Interactions.

Explore People page

To explore peers on Handshake, click People in the left menu. A list of recommended students and alumni will appear in the center of the page, displaying the following information: name, school, school year, and major.

You can use the filters at the top of the page to search for specific students or alumni:

  • Keyword
  • School (all participating students and alumni will be listed by default, so you can use this filter if you’d like to only view peers connected to your current school.)
  • Employer
  • Job role
  • Additional Filters
    • Degree
    • Grad year
    • Skill
    • Organization To send a message, click on a peer’s name to view their profile and send a message. Alternatively, click the Follow button to follow them.

Receiving a Message

When a student or alumni sends you a message, you’ll be notified the following ways:

  • A red notification bubble with a number will appear next to your Inbox in the left navigation menu.
  • An email will be sent to your Handshake email address.
    • Click View Request and Accept/Decline to access the message in Handshake. Once you open a message in your inbox, you’ll have the option to either Allow or Decline the message. Click the arrow icon on the far right side of the message request to expand it.

To respond to the message request, click one of the following buttons:

  • Allow (black button): This will enable you to respond to the message.
  • Decline (white button): You’ll be prompted to provide a reason for declining.
    • Note: the sender won’t receive a notification that their message was declined. Flagging a Message

If you receive a message that violates Handshake’s guidelines, you can report it for review by flagging the message.

Flagging a message will prevent the sender from messaging you further. The conversation will then be reviewed by Handshake’s Trust and Safety team, and your school may also be looped in if necessary.

Note: when a message is flagged, the sender will not be notified.

To report a message, click the three dots menu in the upper-right corner of the message, then click Flag Conversation from the dropdown.

Help us maintain a safe environment on Handshake by letting us know why you’re flagging this conversation. Please select one of the following options:

  • Scam or spam
  • Inappropriate content
  • Abusive or threatening
  • Something else Add any additional details about the action in the text box, then click the black button Submit in the lower-right corner of the pop-up to flag it.

Responding to an Employer Message on Handshake

If you’ve received a message from a recruiter on Handshake, responding can offer a variety of benefits!

Connecting with a recruiter is an excellent opportunity to learn more about specific roles at their company, as well as events they’ll be attending. It also helps you build a personal connection with the companies you’re interested in for future opportunities.

For tips on replying to recruiters, check out our blog post How to wow recruiters that message you.

Respond directly to a recruiter

Employers may send a variety of messages, including event invitations, promotional campaigns, and recruiting inquiries.

To respond to a message from an employer, type your reply in the text box within the message. Once you’re ready, click Send to the right of the text box.

Tip: click Aa to access formatting options like Bold, Italic, Underline, bulleted lists, or numbered lists. To insert a link, click the paperclip icon.

If you’ve received a campaign message from an employer that you’re not interested in, such as regarding a specific company or location, you have the option to mute further communication for 90 days. For more information on muting campaign messages, refer to Mute Employer Campaign Messages.

If you’ve received an introduction message to connect with an advocate and would like to reply directly to the recruiter who sent it, type your response in the text box below the introduction, then click Send. To respond to the advocate, follow the steps below!

Respond to an advocate via recruiter’s introduction

If you’ve received an introduction message from a recruiter, you can reply directly to the advocate they introduced you to!

These messages includes a prompt at the bottom of the message like: “Next step! Talk to an advocate.” Click the up arrow to expand the message.

To respond, click the white Message advocate button. A pop-up will appear, allowing you to type your reply.

Advocates are available to provide insights and advice. Use one of the following prompts to help start your reply:

  • What does the day-to-day look like for this role?
  • How can this role support my professional development?

Build Your Network & Company Brand

Building Your Company Network with Handshake as an Alumni

As you transition from being a student to a professional, your relationship with Handshake evolves as well.

To strengthen your relationship with both your alma mater and current company, we encourage you to create an employer user account on Handshake.

Let’s explore the benefits that await you as an employer on Handshake:

  1. Strengthening alumni connections:

When you create an employer account on Handshake, you can add your alma mater to your profile. By doing so, Handshake automatically creates an alumni contact entry at your former school if it is partnered with Handshake.

By staying connected with your alma mater, you not only strengthen your personal connection but also create opportunities for potential recruitment and networking opportunities between your company and your alma mater.

  1. Enhanced personal branding:

Your name, job title, alma mater, and graduation year are displayed on your Handshake user profile. If you choose to showcase your user profile on your brand page, students can view your user profile.

This visibility enhances your personal branding and allows students to connect with you based on shared educational backgrounds, which fosters mentorship and professional networking relationships.

  1. Streamlined account management:

With an employer account on Handshake, you can use the same email address for both your alumni and employer account. With this feature, you can easily switch between your employer and alumni accounts, which simplifies the process of managing your online presence.

While you can use the same email address, it’s crucial to update it to a personal email as most school email accounts are deactivated after graduation.

  1. Active engagement in Talent Acquisition:

Alumni who create an employer account on Handshake gain access to various recruiting tools and features. You can post jobs, participate in career fairs, and engage in various recruiting activities.

By being actively involved in talent acquisition strategies, your company can greatly enhance its recruitment efforts, resulting in access to top-tier talent and ultimately contributing to the organization’s growth and success.

Additional potential benefits

In addition to the benefits mentioned, creating an employer account on Handshake unlocks a wide range of additional advantages. These may include exclusive networking events, access to industry insights and trends, and the opportunity to collaborate with other alumni in your industry.

By leveraging Handshake’s features and functionalities, you can not only strengthen your professional presence but also cultivate meaningful connections between your alma mater and workplace.

Ready to unlock a world of possibilities for career advancement, networking, and professional success? Learn How to Create an Employer Account on Handshake.

Handshake’s Content Policy (Build Your Network & Company Brand)

Handshake is committed to keeping our platform safe for all users. Content that falls into the categories below is strictly prohibited and may result in enforcement action.

Important: These policies may evolve over time as our platform grows and as our team’s moderation capabilities expand.

This policy applies to all text, images, audio, and video posted, uploaded, or messages on Handshake, including user profiles, résumés, job postings, video descriptions, comments, reviews, peer messages, and external links (both clickable URLs and references shared verbally in content).

Community Standards

Handshake is a platform for career-related discussion and opportunities. Content should contribute to users’ professional journeys, encourage authentic discourse, and remain respectful.

  • Content not broadly career-related, or lacking context to be informative, may be removed.
  • While political and social issue discussions are prohibited, job postings or discussions about jobs related to political campaigns, elections, or candidates are allowed.
  • Threats or harassment against individuals, groups, or Handshake staff are strictly prohibited—both on and off the platform.

Prohibited Content

The following are broad categories of content that may be removed if we determine they apply, even if not explicitly listed here.

Violent Content

  • Depictions or promotion of physical harm, injury, or violence against individuals, groups, or animals.

  • Content that glorifies or threatens violence. Harassment and Bullying

  • Repeated, harmful, or intentional behavior meant to intimidate, harass, or cause distress.

  • Insults, slurs, or degrading language targeting another person or group.

  • Impersonating someone with the intent to harass, deceive, or harm. Hate Speech

  • Content that discriminates against, degrades, or incites violence or prejudice toward individuals or groups based on protected attributes (race, ethnicity, nationality, religion, gender, sexual orientation, disability, or similar characteristics). Self-Harm

  • Content that promotes, encourages, or depicts self-harm or behaviors that put an individual’s physical or mental well-being at risk, including eating disorders. Sexually Explicit Content

  • Content that explicitly depicts or describes sexual activity, genitalia, or intimate body parts. Harm to Civil Discourse

  • Behaviors or content that disrupt healthy, respectful discussion and undermine a safe community environment.

  • Derailing discussions by posting off-topic, unrelated, or repetitive content that interferes with healthy, respectful conversation. Illegal or Regulated Activities

  • Promotion, facilitation, or engagement in unlawful actions or activities restricted by applicable laws or regulations. Misinformation

  • The spread of false, misleading, or inaccurate information that could cause harm or confusion. Fraud, Scams, and Spam

  • Phishing attempts, malicious links, malware, or other deceptive tactics.

  • Repetitive or irrelevant content, including automated/bot-generated content.

  • Content designed to disrupt discussions or overwhelm the platform.

  • Recruitment content from non-employer accounts may be treated as fraud. Learn How to Spot and Report Scams on Handshake.

Other Restricted Content

Jobs from Unapproved Employers or Recruiters

  • Job postings, internships, or other opportunities from employers or recruiters not verified by Handshake. All employers on Handshake go through a verification process. Learn more about How to Create an Employer Account on Handshake.

Commercial Content

  • Buying or selling of products or services, including fundraisers, ads, or attempts to move users off-platform for transactions.

  • “Get rich quick” schemes or similar solicitations. Content Posted in Bad Faith

  • Content created with the intent to mislead, deceive, or circumvent Handshake policies.

  • Irrelevant or off-topic content unrelated to career development.

Authenticity

We expect users to be truthful about who they are and what they share. Fake or misleading information undermines trust on Handshake and will be removed.

  • You may not use or attempt to use another person’s Handshake account, create a profile for someone else, or share your account credentials.
  • Any attempt to buy or sell Handshake accounts will be reported to relevant law enforcement agencies.
  • Custom URLs must represent you or your business. We may revoke URLs that belong to registered trademarks.
  • You may not post or share false or misleading information, including fabricated credentials, achievements, or job opportunities.
  • You may not impersonate another individual, business, or organization, or misrepresent your affiliation with them.

Enforcement

If your content violates this policy or our Terms of Service, it may be removed. You will be notified by email, and in some cases, your school or employer partners may also be informed.

Consequences for violations may include:

  • Warnings

  • Account limitations

  • Temporary suspension

  • Permanent removal from the platform For certain types of violations, Handshake may restrict your account for the duration of an investigation. In these cases, your account will remain restricted until the investigation is complete and a final decision is reached. Some investigations may also require user action prior to accounts being reinstated. User action may include:

  • Email responses to Trust & Safety outreach

  • Supplemental account verification through Persona or phone

Reporting

If you come across content that violates this policy, please report it to our team by flagging the content in Handshake.

For more on how to flag content and details on how we moderate, refer to How Handshake Moderates Content on the Home Feed.

How to Sponsor Content on Handshake

Handshake’s Sponsored Content feature allows you to boost your content visibility by targeting specific student audiences.

This article provides an overview of key details, the sponsorship process, and available targeting options.

Sponsored Content is available exclusively to Premium partners with the paid Brand Bundle package. For more information, please check out this resource.

What is sponsored content?

Sponsored content appears in a dedicated “promoted slot” in the student feed. These slots give your posts priority visibility and can be targeted to specific groups based on defined criteria. Promoted posts are prioritized by audience match and engagement, helping you reach the most relevant students.

Key details

  • Employers can sponsor content posted on behalf of their company or on behalf of individual employees.
  • Sponsored content appears in exclusive promoted slots. Each post can be customized with multiple targeting filters.
  • You can sponsor videos, images, text, or links.
  • You may have access to 1 or 3 sponsored posts at a time, depending on your purchased package.
  • Sponsored posts should stay live for at least 2 weeks. Content can be rotated on a biweekly basis.
  • Changes to content will be implemented within 2 business days after your request is submitted.
  • After the promotion ends, you can choose to remove the post from the feed or keep it as organic content.
  • There’s no limit on the number of organic (non-sponsored) posts you can upload.

Sponsoring content

  • Log in to Handshake, navigate to the Feed, and create your content as usual.
  • Every other Monday, you’ll get an automated email asking which posts you’d like to sponsor and for what audience.
  • Reply to the email with your selected posts and targeting criteria by Wednesday of the same week.
  • Handshake will update the content within 2 business days of your submission and will send a confirmation email once the update is complete.

Targeting criteria

You can tailor your sponsored content to specific audiences using the following seven criteria:

  1. Major Group

Examples include:

  • Computer Science
  • Business & HR
  • Engineering
  • Arts & Design
  • Health Professions
  1. School Year

Includes:

  • Freshman through Postdoctoral
  • Certificate and Accelerated Master’s programs
  • Alumni
  1. School

Use the School Lists feature in Handshake:

  • Create a list of schools to target.
  • Use unique lists for each sponsored post, if necessary. Learn more about Creating and Managing School Lists.
  1. Location

You can target by:

  • Current location (typically the physical location of the student’s school.)
  • Location preference (desired future locations from their profiles) Note: Targeting includes candidates within a 50-mile radius of the selected city.
  1. Demographics

Examples:

  • Black or African American
  • Hispanic or Latine
  • Asian or Pacific Islander
  • LGBTQIA+
  • Women/female-identifying
  • Veterans
  • Indigenous or Native American
  1. Industry Interests

Examples:

  • Technology
  • Education
  • Financial Services
  • Healthcare
  • Arts & Entertainment
  1. Job Role Interests

Target based on student interests in specific job roles.

🔗 For a comprehensive list of job roles, refer to the file “Job Role Groups in Handshake 2.2.21.xlsx” in the Help Center article About Job Roles and Job Role Groups (Employers).

Tips for success

  • Video performs best. Use it whenever possible.
  • Keep posts live for at least 2 weeks for maximum visibility.
  • Reply to the biweekly sponsorship email by Wednesday to guarantee timely updates.

Candidate Qualifications & Analysis

Candidate Analysis

Candidate analysis helps employers understand how external candidates from their ATS engage with their company on Handshake, and measure the ROI of their recruitment efforts.

If you haven’t already, please reach out to your Handshake CSM before using this tool.

This feature is available to Premium partners only. For more information, check out this resource!

How do I access Candidate Analysis?

Click Analytics from the left navigation bar, then select Candidate analysis from the Applicants tab.

  • Handshake anonymizes the information imported to preserve your data privacy.
  • Candidate accounts will only be displayed if the candidate has an active, public student or alumni account. Accounts that are not activated or are set to private will not be included.

How do I upload a candidate list?

Step 1: Prepare your file

The headers below are mandatory and must be present in your file. Create a spreadsheet in CSV format with the following headers:

  • First Name
  • Last Name
  • Email Address First Name

Last Name

Email Address

Note: The file cannot exceed 150,000 candidate records. If you need to analyze more records, separate the file into multiple uploads.

Tips:

  • Before preparing your list, discuss with your Customer Success Manager which categories of candidate data to analyze:
    • Interns, Full-Time Early Talent Roles
    • Stage in the recruitment funnel:
      • Candidate leads
      • Applicants
      • Qualified applicants
      • Applicants who received offers
      • Hires
  • Upload files based on the most recent hiring season, typically 4 months to a year. For example: All Summer 2024 Intern Applicants.
  • Upload candidates who graduated from an academic institution in the past year or are currently enrolled in an academic institution.
  • Only include candidates for US-based roles. Do not include global or international candidates.
  • Use descriptive file names (for example: Handshake_2026_fulltime_offers.csv).
Step 2: Upload your file

  1. Click the Get started button.

  2. A pop-up will appear with the Data Privacy Policy. Click I understand in the lower-right corner to proceed. To stop receiving this message, check the box for “Don’t show this again.” .

  3. Choose your file (maximum file size: 20 MB). To obtain a sample file, click Download sample file. After selecting your file, complete the following fields:

  • Candidate status
    • Hired
    • Offered
    • Applied
    • Interviewed
    • Other
  • Starting and ending dates
  • Role type
    • Full-time
    • Internship
    • Part-time
    • Co-op
    • Management trainee
    • Other
  • Information about candidates (optional)
    • e.g., Accounting candidates, candidates within our e-commerce division only, etc. Once all fields are completed, click Continue in the lower-right corner.

  1. The data will be hashed. The hashing process may take up to 20 seconds.

  2. Once hashing is complete, a message will confirm that the data has been hashed. A sample of the file will also be displayed for review.

  3. Click the Import and launch analysis button to import the data into Handshake.

  4. Handshake will begin searching for candidates with matching hashed values:

  • First, Handshake searches using the hashed candidate email against its own database of hashed user emails.
  • Next, all remaining records not found by email are searched using hashed names.
  1. Handshake will retrieve details on your historical interactions in the last 24 months with matched candidates. Results will be shared through your Customer Success Manager.

Note: Handshake does not report on candidates you have not interacted with in the last 24 months. Because of limitations inherent in the matching process, results may be incomplete. To ensure that employer-provided hashed data is not stored indefinitely, Handshake regularly deletes all uploaded files.

How does Handshake anonymize candidate data?

Once you have prepared a file with a list of candidates and validated its format, Handshake will anonymize all fields in the file that could be used to identify a specific candidate. Handshake runs an SHA-256 hashing algorithm on the First Name, Last Name, and Email fields in the file. This process transforms plaintext names and emails into 64-character hexadecimal values that are functionally impossible to decrypt.

For example, “John Doe” would appear as “6cea57c2fb6cbc2a40411135005760f241fffc3e5e67ab99882726431037f908” after hashing. A preview of these hashed values is available for verification before any data is transferred to Handshake.

File validation and hashing take place in your browser on your computer. Handshake does not receive any data from your local system until after hashing and you explicitly click the button to upload.

What happens to hashed data after it is uploaded?

Handshake matches student and alumni accounts with the hashed fields by identifying matching values produced by the hashing algorithm against its own set of hashed data, in the same way that web passwords are securely validated.

Handshake compiles an output report summarizing your historical interactions with the matched Handshake accounts in the past 24 months. This output report is emailed to your Handshake success team.

Once the above process is complete, the original hashed file is deleted from Handshake’s system. Handshake keeps the original file only for as long as needed to match Handshake accounts. Unmatched records are never shared or stored.

Understanding Job and Candidate Qualifications

Setting job and candidate qualifications helps you efficiently filter and prioritize the most relevant applicants.

Note: Qualifications are optional. Adding them will not prevent candidates from applying for your job.

What candidate qualifications can I set?

You can specify the following candidate qualifications in a job posting:

  • Work authorization (candidates who meet the requirement or choose not to disclose will be included)
  • Skills
  • School year
  • Latest graduation date
  • Major groups
  • Minimum GPA To add or update these qualifications, read How to Edit a Job Posting.

How do I use qualifications when reviewing applicants?

When reviewing applicants, you can quickly identify those who meet your qualifications using the Matching qualifications filter in the Applicants tab.

The filter includes the following criteria:

  • Latest graduation date
  • Minimum GPA
  • Majors
  • Work authorization This allows you to focus your review on candidates whose backgrounds align with your preferences.

For more information on reviewing applicants, read Reviewing Applications in Handshake.

EDU: Understanding the Job Seeker Experience - Connected vs. Not Connected

Job seekers can access the Handshake feed, search for and view public career fairs, manage their profiles, message with others, and search for and apply for some jobs before they are connected to an educational institution or independent of an educational institution. We encourage job seekers to connect with educational institutions so they can have a more curated experience on Handshake, and enjoy access to exclusive jobs, fairs, events, appointments, resources, and collections. This article will assist you with understanding the different levels of access for job seekers depending on their connection to a school.

Encouraging Alumni Accounts and Maintaining Your Network

Maintaining alumni involvement on Handshake is essential for fostering a strong and supportive network that positively impacts both recent graduates and current students.

Alumni on Handshake can provide valuable insights, mentorships, and connections for those currently enrolled at your institution. Their ongoing involvement on the platform can also improve the reputation and scope of your institution’s network, drawing in a greater number of employers and opportunities to the platform.

To learn about the benefits alumni may experience on Handshake after graduation, refer to Using Handshake After Graduation.

💡Note: It is generally not recommended to deactivate alumni accounts unless requested by the user or required.

Consider the following before archiving student accounts:

  • Students accounts should be archived upon student request or if absolutely necessary.

  • Accounts can be unarchived - however, if other career services members at your school are unaware of a student’s account being archived, they may suggest that the student create a new account. At this time, accounts cannot be merged unless they meet the qualifications as listed in Managing and Merging Duplicate Student Accounts. If they don’t meet those qualifications, the data cannot be connected between two accounts.

  • Data and information from an archived account may include: appointment history, fair participation, job applications, experiences, and more. These key points could help shape their career growth.

  • Your school will be unable to view archived students on the Manage students page if the students log in to their account after being archived. Learn more about the student archive process in What Happens When I Archive a Student?

  • Alumni with archived accounts can still use Handshake post-graduation, they just won’t be connected to your school.

  • If your school currently runs automated jobs through Importer, the file will need to be updated to reflect students whose accounts have been archived. If a student requests reactivation, the file will need to be updated once more to reflect this change. To ensure a smooth transition in managing student accounts to alumni on Handshake, we recommend the following:

  • Update Data Through Student Sync: regardless of whether students keep their institution’s email address or not, you’ll need to update their records via the Importer. For more information on this, refer to Importer: Updating Graduating Students to Alumni.

  • Encourage Email Changes: To ensure students can access Handshake long after their institution’s email address is archived, send an email requesting they update their primary email address in Handshake. This may involve sending targeted emails and providing a deadline before archiving accounts. Check out Creating and Sending Targeted Emails for more information on creating and sending targeted emails.

  • SSO Access for Alumni: Alumni can continue to use Single Sign-On (SSO) if their account is not disabled after graduation and if the institution allows continued SSO access. If SSO access isn’t an option, inform alumni to create a new Handshake-specific password. Refer to Log In as an Alum: Set your Handshake Password for steps on how students can create a Handshake password.

Handshake AI Fellowship Overview & FAQs (for EDU Partners)

The Handshake AI Fellowship is an initiative from Handshake that offers highly skilled students, graduates, and researchers paid, part-time opportunities to contribute to the training and evaluation of large language models (LLMs).

While Handshake AI is a distinct initiative within Handshake, it is fully supported by our platform, infrastructure, and commitment to student protections.

Handshake AI Overview

The Handshake AI Fellowship connects selected candidates, known as Fellows, with AI labs to validate and improve model outputs. Fellows contribute by designing and evaluating AI prompts and responses in their academic fields.

Goals:

  • Enable Fellows to showcase domain expertise in collaboration with leading AI labs

  • Support skill development in advanced AI prompting and evaluation

  • Offer competitive compensation for contributing to innovative AI research Responsibilities:

  • Creating prompts in the Fellow’s field of expertise

  • Evaluating or comparing AI-generated responses

  • Correcting and improving content with academic citations Employment type:

  • Part-time, remote, and asynchronous

  • Fellows set their own schedules (typically 5 - 20 hrs/week)

  • Projects vary in length from 2 weeks to 3+ months

  • All Fellows are hired as 1099 independent contractors This setup supports participation by international graduate students, where visa conditions permit. More details available in Fellowship Work Authorization Eligibility.

Compensation:

  • Hourly rates are $30–$125, based on education level, expertise, and project
  • All compensation is transparent before project acceptance
  • Fellows are contracted and paid directly by Handshake, not the partnering AI lab
    • More information available in Handshake AI Fellowship Program Payment Policy.
Application & Selection Process

Jobs are listed both on:

  • The Handshake AI Fellowship website
  • Handshake, under the Handshake AI employer profile
    • Note: The Handshake AI employer account follows the same rules for relevancy, messaging limits, and outreach that apply to all employers. We encourage you to promote these roles to students at your institution!

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis according to partner lab needs, and candidates are selected based on their academic background and domain knowledge.

  • Most roles require graduate-level expertise (Master’s, PhD, or Postdoc).
  • In some cases, individuals without a formal degree but with demonstrated subject-matter expertise may be considered. Selection timelines vary–just because a candidate has not heard back does not mean they were not selected! When there’s a project that matches their expertise, our team will reach out with an invitation via email.

More details are available in the following resources:

  • From Application to First Project: Your Complete Handshake AI Fellowship Program Journey
  • Apply to the Handshake AI Fellowship
  • Handshake AI Fellowship Onboarding Checklist
Program Structure & Expectations

Selected Fellows are offered tasks based on their availability and subject matter expertise.

Commitment expectations are made clear at the beginning of each project, and participation in individual projects can be accepted or declined depending on scheduling needs.

Each project determines its own onboarding and training requirements, as outlined by the Project Lead. These details and instructions are communicated once fellows are accepted, and Fellows are compensated for project onboarding time.

Every Fellow who is accepted goes through our general onboarding flow, which has ~2 hours of learning modules on Canvas. They then complete a knowledge quiz, and are passed along to a live practice task where they get feedback from reviewers. They are compensated for this time.

Handshake plans to continue to add more courses to help candidates upskill as they think about their careers in this new AI workforce.

  • Details on general expectations are available in Introduction to the Handshake AI Fellowship.
  • More resources for current Fellows are available in the Help Center section Project Participation & Expectations.
  • Options for getting help are outlined in Handshake AI Fellowship Support Guide.

Additional FAQs

Will Fellows be exposed to sensitive or explicit content?
  • No. Handshake does not engage in projects involving vulgar, violent, or sexually explicit material. Students are only hired to contribute based on their subject-matter knowledge.
Are there ethical considerations?
  • Fellows play a key role in:
    • Identifying inaccuracies and bias in model outputs
    • Validating information with trusted, academic sources
    • Supporting the development of accurate, inclusive, and responsible AI We believe ethical AI starts with ethical training and diverse academic voices.
What safeguards are in place?
  • Every project is internally reviewed before launch
  • Tasks are regularly monitored for clarity, fairness, and accuracy
  • Contributors come from a wide range of institutions and backgrounds, helping to reduce bias in training and feedback
Are fellows allowed to use external AI tools like ChatGPT or Claude?
  • No. The use of external AI tools for prompt ideation, solution writing, or editing is strictly prohibited. All work must be original. An internal LLM and Grammarly integration are provided when needed. Fellows are provided clear guidelines about LLM usage and IP during onboarding.
What are the IP considerations for Handshake AI?
  • There is no transfer of any previous or future IP from the fellows to Handshake or any of our partnering labs. Any materials created within the Program, on official Program channels, are owned by Handshake and their partnering labs.
  • If fellows cite original works in their AI prompting, they grant royalty-free license to both Handshake and our partners to use their works for upcoming model training. Fellows do not transfer any IP in that situation.
Who are the AI labs you’re partnering with?
  • While we can’t share names due to confidentiality agreements, we are working with leading labs focused on building general-purpose LLMs.
How long has Handshake been doing this?
  • HandshakeAI is a new initiative launched in response to rising demand for academic expertise in AI training. While still small compared to our core business, we believe this is a meaningful way to offer students valuable real-world experience.
Is this a long-term focus for Handshake?
  • We’re still in the early stages. While our long-term direction will evolve, we’re still relying on feedback from Fellows and schools.

Helping Students Get the Most From Handshake

This resource will help you to answer common questions students ask about Handshake.

Why should I make a Handshake account if I already have a LinkedIn account?

Handshake has the most opportunities for students and new college grads of any job platform, and is the only one that lets employers recruit specifically at your school

All the jobs are posted just for students, which means you aren’t competing against professionals with 5+ years of experience. No experience required.

Why should I fill out my Handshake profile?

Handshake will give you personalized job recommendations based on the information you provide on your profile—so you can find jobs and internships that are right for you.

Recruiters are five times more likely to proactively reach out to you with job opportunities and event invitations if your profile is complete.

Which parts of my Handshake profile are most important to fill out?

In addition to your major, Handshake also uses your job interests to recommend opportunities to you. Job interests include:

  • Job type: Looking for an on-campus job, internship, part-time job, or full-time job? You can choose more than one.
  • Preferred location: Select the cities you would like to work in, and Handshake will show you jobs in that area.
  • Job role: Choose at least three positions you would like to explore, like “marketing associate” or “data analyst.” TIP: Don’t forget to let students know that they can change and update interests whenever they want!

What are the top things employers search for?

Beyond your job interests, employers want to know:

  • Previous work experience: Have you had a part-time job, internship, work study, research position and or volunteered? Employers like to see that you’ve taken on responsibility, and that these experiences have helped you develop valuable skills.
  • Skills: Add technical skills like SQL along with soft skills like communication. The more skills you list, the better your chances are of showing up in an employer search.
  • Clubs and organizations: These signal your specific interests, affinity groups, and participation and involvement on campus. CALL OUT: Employers use a combination of job interests, work experiences, skills, organizations, and courses to find candidates they’d like to connect with. Show up in more searches—fill them out!

Why should I care about other students on Handshake?

Chat with students and alumni who’ve been there. When you view a job or employer page, you can see other students who have worked there and reach out to them with your questions.

Get an inside look at company culture, interview tips, and more through company reviews. You can also find answers to common career questions (or ask your own!) in Q&A. TIP: Search for students to connect with based on their major, work experiences, and more!

Why should I make my profile public?

Help employers find you. If your profile is public, you’ll show up in searches when they’re recruiting for jobs and internships.

Connect with and mentor other students. Help other students along their career journeys by making your own visible. And give them the opportunity to reach out.

Don’t worry, your profile will not be public to employers that have not been approved by your school or to anyone without a Handshake account.

Can I use Handshake on my phone?

Yes! Download the Handshake App to search and apply to jobs right from your phone. Get notified and never miss a message from an employer, be first to see new job postings, and apply in two taps with Quick Apply.

What is the best way to use keyword search and filters?

Narrow down and customize your job search. Filter through jobs by criteria such as job type, location, work authorization, and industry.

Keyword search helps you find jobs whose description includes a word that you’re looking for. For example, if you search for the keyword “accounting,” you will see jobs where the word accounting appears in the posting.

PRO TIP: Save your searches to quickly access a set of filters you’ve used in the past!

How to View as a Student

You may need to experience Handshake from a particular student’s perspective to:

  • Troubleshoot issues that a student brings to your attention.
  • Check any postings, fairs, events, etc. that you’ve posted.

  1. First, ensure that you have permissions to view as a student. Head to your settings by clicking your name in the upper-right corner of the screen and selecting User settings

  2. Next, select Roles and scroll down until you find View/Act as Student. This must be checked, if it’s not and you’re not able to enable it yourself, reach out to someone who has Manage Staff permissions or your RM to request this role.

  3. Click Manage on the left navigation bar, under the Students category.

  4. Type the student’s name in the search bar on the page, located under the Manage students page heading, in the upper left corner.

  5. Click on the student’s name to open their profile.

  6. On the left side of the page, locate and click the View as this student button.

When viewing as a particular student, you’ll have access to most Handshake content from their perspective.

Note: There are certain fields on the student profile that you will not be able to either access or edit. These can only be accessed/edited by the student themselves:

  • Work Authorization settings
  • Viewing additional email addresses that the student added
  • Accessing or editing a student’s profile picture
  • Editing the “get to know me” section
  • Accessing their inbox
  • Editing a student’s institution email address
    • If the student’s account is connected to a career services or employer account, contact Support to change the institution email address. Once you are finished, click the Normal View button, located in the upper-right corner of the screen to return to your account.
