Student Career Center Page

The student career center page helps students find resources that are related to their interests in Handshake!

Displayed Collections

Collections posted to the Career Center page are based on student engagement on the platform, and ordered by relevance to them — we want to make it as easy as possible for students to get to the collections they engage with the most!

Depending on the student engagement, they may have access to the following collections:

  • Virtual Group Events (upcoming virtual events)
  • Virtual Employer Sessions (available sessions with 1:1 meetings)
  • New Jobs recommended for you (jobs recommended to the student based on views and applications)
  • Jobs with Connections (an employer contact is attached)
  • Personalized Jobs for you (jobs recommended to the student based on views and applications)
  • Job Roles (jobs with roles of interest)
  • Major Groups (jobs that pertain to a certain major)
    • When students have more than one major, the suggested jobs will be based on either the primary major selected, or if no primary major is designated, they’ll be based on the first major listed.
  • On Campus Jobs (jobs posted by your school for campus employment)
  • Expiring Jobs (jobs expiring within 2 weeks)
  • Interested Industries (jobs within the industries the student is interested in)
  • Application Reminder (jobs where the application was started but not finished) Institution contact information

On the right side of the screen, information regarding the school or institution will be provided. This includes:

  • Contact Information (Website URL, Phone and email contact, and the location of the career center)
  • About (Institution’s description and history, as provided in Handshake)
  • Public Staff List (members of the staff that have opted to have their information shared for student reference)

Virtual Accessibility via Integrated Video on Handshake

At Handshake, we are committed to making virtual interactions accessible to all students. To do this, we have partnered with a consulting firm to review our product in its entirety.

To learn more about virtual accessibility on the platform, refer to Virtual Accessibility in Handshake.

For virtual interactions, using our Integrated Video on Handshake, we provide students with the opportunity to request a transcriber or ASL interpreter to participate in all virtual instances.

For more information on how to request a transcriber, refer to Requesting an ASL Interpreter or Transcriber for Virtual Interactions.

To uphold our dedication to accessibility, this article provides details on our guidelines, recommended best practices, and additional resources to ensure that everyone can actively engage in virtual sessions on Handshake.

Accessibility Guidelines

Read more about our commitment, efforts, and software conformance reports in Handshake’s Accessibility Statement.

Recommendations

Below are a few recommended methods that your school can implement to ensure that students who may require accommodations are aware of what to expect and can be prepared when participating in a virtual interaction on Handshake.

Event Disclaimer

Use the Event disclaimer feature to include accommodation and accessibility statements from your institution in the event settings.

To provide students with a clear understanding of how your institution supports them for virtual events, we recommend connecting with your accessibility office (if you have one), to develop official language that can be used in the event disclaimer.

Tip: when marketing an interaction (online or print) it is important to include an opportunity for individuals to reach out to you. For virtual events on Handshake, we recommend clear instructions on how to contact your career services center to request a transcriber if needed.

For examples of accessibility statements that can be used in your event’s disclaimer and descriptions, check out the University of Arizona’s Disability Access Statements.

To add an event disclaimer, refer to School Settings: Event Preferences.

Appointment and Career Fair Description

Similar to the Event disclaimer feature, you may choose to add an accessibility statement to your virtual appointment and fair descriptions.

We suggest working with your accessibility office (if available) to collaborate on creating language for your virtual interactions on the platform. This will give students a better understanding of how they can reach out to you to make arrangements for their participation requests.

Handshake Integrated Video

Handshake uses Daily as our video provider, which supports both transcribers and ASL interpreters to attend via video.

To support ASL interpreters, students can pin the interpreter’s video tile on the screen — this will not pin the video for other student participants.

If a student requires a transcriber or ASL interpreter for a video session hosted on Handshake, contact Support.

💡Note: requests should be submitted to Handshake Support 2 weeks in advance of the virtual interaction to ensure everything is ready in time!

For more information on how to request a transcriber, refer to Requesting a Transcriber or ASL Interpreter for Virtual Interactions.

External Video Host

Hosts have the option to host their video sessions outside our integrated video platform, using platforms such as Zoom. External video sites each have their own offerings to support accessibility.

To learn more about Zoom’s accessibility features and how to make the most of it, check out their website dedicated to accessibility Zoom is for Everyone.

Additional Resources

To learn more about what we’ve done towards our accessibility goals, how we’re continuing to evolve, and our updated VPAT, refer to Accessibility and VPAT.

For the student’s process of requesting a transcriber or inquiring about accommodations, refer to Accessibility for Virtual Interactions on Handshake.

Virtual Meeting Best Practices & Resources

With the shift to online engagement, Handshake would like to offer a collection of best practices, tips for staying safe, and resources to help you navigate virtual meetings safely and effectively.

We’ve also attached a PDF copy of our slide deck from the March 24th webinar, Basics of Video Conferencing, or click the link to download it now!

Best Practices

  • Use Waiting Room in Zoom (you can see people waiting to join your meeting and choose who to allow in)
  • Set recording on cloud or computer (in Zoom you can set them to automatically record)
  • Co/alternative hosts
  • You can transfer hosting ability even after meeting has started
  • Hosts can mute all attendees
  • When possible, ensure that only the host is capable of sharing screens
  • Breakout rooms for larger groups
  • Add staff members to large meetings to help monitor the chat room for questions
  • Leverage the dial in feature (you can call someone and participants can dial in) - very helpful when in case there are audio issues
  • Test Meetings: these can be set up to test audio before large events

Stay safe!

Please note: The tips below are related to Zoom specifically. Different tools have different setting capabilities, and you should utilize the tools’ help centers and support teams!

  • Disable “Join Before Host” so people can’t begin before you arrive.
  • Enable “Co-Host” so you can assign others to help moderate.
  • Disable “File Transfer” so there’s no digital virus sharing.
  • Disable “Allow Removed Participants to Rejoin” so booted attendees can’t slip back in.
  • Require meeting password (to restrict who can join)

Meeting Resources

Please note these are not Handshake tools and must be downloaded from each site to be used and supported by that application!

Zoom:

Tip Resource: support.zoom.us

Google Meet:

Tip Resource: support.google.com

GoToMeeting:

Tip Resource: gotomeeting.com

Cisco Webex:

Tip Resource: webex.com

Career Exploration

Attending Virtual Appointments on Handshake

Virtual appointments with your career center can happen in one of two ways, depending on how your school has set things up: through Virtual on Handshake, Handshake’s integrated video tool, or through an external link (such as Zoom or Google Meet) provided by your career center. The method used for your appointment is set by your career center and will be listed on your appointment details confirmation.

  • Virtual on Handshake — Join your appointment directly inside Handshake. No external meeting link or download is required.
  • External link — Your career center schedules the appointment using an external Zoom meeting, and you’ll join via a link they provide. If you haven’t scheduled a virtual appointment yet, follow the steps in Request an Appointment with your Career Center.

💡Note: attending virtual appointments is supported on mobile, web and iOS/Android devices with app version 3.26.0 or later.

Preparing for your appointment

Virtual on Handshake

The integrated video used for virtual appointments is the same service provided for some virtual events/fairs on Handshake — if you’ve previously used our video integration, your system should be all set!

To ensure your device is ready for the scheduled appointment, refer to Attendee Requirements for Integrated Video.

External Link

Some career centers choose to hold virtual appointments over Zoom, Google Meet, or another video platform instead of using Handshake’s integrated video. In this case, your appointment medium will show as a link for an external meeting link rather than “Virtual on Handshake.”

Notifications and reminders

Handshake sends three notification emails for your appointment depending on your notification preferences:

  • Appointment confirmation: Sent when your virtual appointment is confirmed or approved in Handshake.
  • 24-hour reminder: Sent 24 hours before your appointment start time.
  • One-hour reminder: Sent one hour before your appointment start time. If your virtual appointment is being held through Virtual on Handshake, the final reminder email includes a “Go to my appointment” button. Click the button to log in and access your appointment.

If your virtual appointment is being held on an external site, the final reminder email includes a link provided by your career center instead of the “Go to my appointment” button. This link will take you to the external video platform, such as Zoom or Google Meet.

Note: We don’t include the office location in the reminder email if the appointment is Virtual on Handshake.

Joining your virtual appointment

You can access your appointment in two ways:

  • From your reminder email: For appointments held through Virtual on Handshake, click the button in your final reminder email. You’ll be directed to Handshake, where your appointment overview page will open. For appointments held on an external site, click the link provided in your final reminder email to access your appointment.
  • From Handshake: Click Career Center in the left navigation menu, then select Appointments. Find and select your upcoming appointment from the list. Note: The Join button becomes available five minutes before your appointment’s start time.

For appointments held through Virtual on Handshake, you can join directly from the appointment overview page by clicking Join now. Alternatively, click the appointment to open the appointment details page, then click Join.

Alternatively, click the appointment to open the appointment details page, then click Join.

To learn more about the available settings and options using Handshake’s integrated video, including screen sharing, refer to Attending via Video on Handshake!

Note: Because external appointments are hosted outside of Handshake, features like Handshake’s built-in screen sharing controls won’t apply — you’ll use the external sites own in-meeting tools instead.

If you require a transcriber or ASL interpreter during the virtual interaction, you must contact your school’s career services to have them included in your appointment. To learn more about Handshakes’ accessibility options, refer to Accessibility for Virtual Interactions on Handshake.

Connecting Virtually with Employers and Your School via Handshake

Handshake offers the option to attend career fairs, events, and appointments virtually! This may be done via integrated video on Handshake or an external link (e.g. zoom).

💡Note: the host chooses the video platform they’d like to conduct the career fair session, event, or appointment.

Click on the expandable headers below to learn more about the following topics.

Integrated video on Handshake

Fairs, events, and appointments can be conducted via integrated video on Handshake for a seamless experience!

For more information on using integrated video, check out Attending via Video on Handshake and Handshake Video Requirements & Troubleshooting (Students).

Attending virtual career fairs

Schools are able to host virtual fairs in Handshake, and employers can register to attend the fair similarly to in-person fairs.

If interested in attending a virtual career fair, you can search for these specifically using the “Career Fair” and “Virtual” filters located within the Event search on the right side.

To meet with an employer at a virtual career fair, you will need to log into your Handshake account and create a schedule. The schedule will include all 1:1 and group sessions that you are interested in attending.

For more information on virtual career fairs, check out Handshake’s Guide to Attending a Virtual Fair.

Attending virtual events

Virtual events are shared in Handshake just like on or off campus events, with the only real change being the location. When an event is being hosted virtually, look for the link to join in the Location or Description.

Note: links are not hyperlinked, so you’ll need to copy/paste the link into your browser window.

If interested in attending virtual events, you can search for these specifically using the Event Type filter on the right of the Event Search page; just check “Virtual” to narrow down your search.

Scheduling virtual appointments

Appointments can now be conducted with integrated video on Handshake as well as other virtual mediums from your career center.

If you are attending an appointment via video, check the appointment location on the appointment in Handshake or in the reminder email for a link from your school. If your school is using the integrated video on Handshake, you can access the video directly from the appointment in Handshake by clicking the “Start Video Appointment” button.

If you schedule an appointment via phone, make sure you provide your phone number if requested in the survey when scheduling an appointment. If it’s not requested, you can leave a comment on the requested appointment with your phone number as well. (This is only seen by you and the Career Services users at your school.)

Check out Request an Appointment with your Career Center for help requesting an appointment, and if you’re attending a Virtual on Handshake appointment, refer to Attending Virtual Appointments on Handshake.

Following an Employer in Handshake

Following an employer on Handshake offers several benefits, including notifications when key activities occur that may interest you. These notifications include:

  • New job postings at your school from the employer
  • Employer-hosted events
  • Employer participation in a fair at your school Note: some of our Premium employer partners can view which students have followed their company profile. This information may help them reach out to students more specifically.

Click on the expandable headers to learn more about how to follow an employer in Handshake and the notifications details you’ll receive.

How to follow an employer

Handshake offers multiple opportunities to follow an employer throughout the product. The Follow button can be located:

  • on the explore Employers page
  • on the employer’s company page
  • job postings page
  • the sessions tab for a virtual fair
  • after attending a virtual event or career fair session in Handshake
  • after checking into an employers booth at an in-person event or career fair via QR code

Explore Employers page

Click Employers in the left-hand navigation menu. A list of employers is listed—find employers you’re interested in and click the Follow button to the right of their name. Additionally you can use the filters to narrow your search and discover employers on the platform!

Employers company page

When viewing an employers company page, click the Follow button located in the upper-right corner of the page within the header.

Job Posting

When viewing a job post, scroll to the middle of the page to the “About the employer” section and click the Follow button.

Sessions tab for a virtual fair

In the Available Sessions tab for a virtual fair in Handshake, you can search for an employer’s name in the search bar. If that employer is approved at your school and has an approved registration at the fair but no available sessions, the following message will load:

“COMPANY NAME doesn’t have any available sessions. This could mean they haven’t set up their schedule yet, or all sessions you qualify for are filled.”

Below the message is a prompt for “Get notified when sessions are added.” Click the Follow button to begin following the employer. You’ll be notified when their schedule is updated.

After a virtual event or session

If you attended a virtual event or session hosted through Handshake, you’ll be able to follow the employer immediately afterwards! A pop-up will appear with additional steps, including an option to follow the employer. Click the Follow button in the upper-right corner of the pop-up.

After checking in via QR code

After scanning the QR code to check into an employer’s booth at a career fair, and completing the check-in process, the employer’s company profile will load. Click the Follow button to follow the employer.

Notification emails sent

If you’re following an employer, there are 4 potential notification emails you could receive:

  • Employer posts a new job at your school(email sent when job posting is approved by your school)
    • Note: the notification email won’t be sent if:
      • the employer renews an expired job posting
      • the employer extends the job posting expiration date
  • Employer is hosting an info session event at your school (email sent when event is approved by your school)
  • Employer’s registration for a career fair is approved (only for in-person career fairs)
  • Employer sets their schedule for a career fair (only for virtual fairs)
    • All registered students also get an email 48 hours ahead of a virtual career fair if qualifications are lifted for any employer schedules at the fair. All notification emails described will be sent from “handshake@notifications.joinhandshake.com”.

Examples

Employer posted a new job

Title: “[Employer Name] just posted a new job

Body: “Hi [Name], we wanted to let you know that [Employer Name], and employer you’re following, just posted a new job. Here are the details:

Job: [Title]

Employer: [Name]

Apply before: [Expiration Date]”

On-Campus Info Session

Title: “[Employer Name] just signed up to host an event on your campus

Body: “Hi [Name], we wanted to let you know that [Employer Name], and employer you’re following, will be hosting an event on campus. Here are the details:

Event name: [Title]

Date: [Day of week, month, date, year]

Time: [Start - End]”

Handshake Feed: Overview & Interactions

Handshake’s home feed is a feature that transforms Handshake from a job search tool to a comprehensive career destination. It’s designed to help you launch your career by providing you with relevant content, social interactions, and assistive features.

Whether you’re looking for a job now or planning for your long-term career development, the home feed offers an enjoyable experience that lets you access content whenever and wherever you want!

To learn how to post content to the feed, check out Posting Content to the Handshake Feed.

To post on the feed, your profile visibility must be set to Community. Learn more about your profile visibility options in Profile Privacy Options in Handshake, and find step-by-step instructions for updating your visibility settings How to Change Your Student Profile Privacy Setting.

Access Handshake home feed

To access the home feed, and interact with a wide range of content, log into your Handshake account via desktop or your mobile device.

Desktop

On your desktop, click Feed, located in the upper-right corner of the screen.

Mobile Device

On your mobile device, tap Feed, located in the lower-left corner of the screen.

To learn more about Handshake’s mobile app, refer to About Handshake Mobile for iOS and Android.

💡Note: Our algorithm customizes the content displayed in your feed based on your profile, interests, and platform activity. This provides you with the most relevant and valuable resources for your professional growth. The content displayed is constantly updated with the latest job opportunities, career advice, and industry insights to keep you informed and motivated.

Engage with content in Handshake’s home feed

By utilizing the home feed, you can engage with your institution and employers, fostering a sense of connection and community.

🚀Tip: Use the filters at the top of the feed to find relevant posts that you’re interested in!

Filters

  • All
  • Employers (content posted by employers only)
  • Top Posts (content with high engagement)
  • Intros (content tagged as introductions, portfolios, etc.) 💡Note: If there is no content available for the filter, the filter will not be available.

To react to a post, choose the following:

  • Heart icon to “like” posts
  • Bookmark icon to “save” jobs, events, and posts
  • Three dots to either “hide” or “report” content, or “unfollow” a user
  • User or employer’s name to be directed to their profile in Handshake
  • The plus sign on a users icon to follow them
    • To learn more about following users on Handshake, refer to Following Users on Handshake. Important: If you come across content in the home feed that you believe violates our Content Policy or Terms of Service, you can report it directly within the app. We take all reports seriously and will review them promptly.

To review our Content Policy, check out Handshake’s Content Policy.

To learn more about how we moderate content in Handshake’s home feed and how to report content in the app, refer to How Handshake Moderates Content on the Home Feed.

Comment on a post

To comment on a post, select the message bubble located below the post—this will open the related thread.

Type your comment in the text box, then click the button Comment.

To maintain an authentic experience on the feed, Handshake enforces daily comment limits. For more information on this refer to, Message & Feed Activity Limits on Handshake.

Turn on audio descriptions for videos (if available)

If audio descriptions are available for a video, you can enable them directly from a video post.

Click the three dots menu to the right of the video post, then select Turn ON audio descriptions if available. Once turned on, your preference will be saved for future browsing sessions.

To turn off audio descriptions, click the three dots menu, then select Turn OFF audio descriptions.

Access your saved posts

Saving posts allows you to revisit important or interesting content from the feed. All posts that have been saved by clicking the bookmark icon can be accessed via desktop later.

This is particularly useful for posts that contain valuable information such as job opportunities, career advice, or educational resources.

On your desktop, click Feed on the navigation menu, then click the tab Saved in the upper-center of the screen.

💡Note: saved posts are arranged in descending order, with the newest ones on top and the oldest ones at the bottom.

Handshake Q&A - Student Content Guidelines

We’re so excited to have you on Handshake Q&A (Questions & Answers)! The goal of Q&A is to democratize information and help every student get the information and insights they need to be successful in their job search process.

Content Policy and Guidelines

We’re sure you have amazing information to contribute! In order to make sure we create a community that is relevant, valuable, and appropriate, here are some content guidelines.

Questions - Major Policies

  • Clearly address a specific employer and/or job position when applicable If you’re asking a question about a specific company or job, please make sure to clearly identify the employer and/or job position you are referring to. Asking what the interview process is like for “this company” or for “this job” is not enough for readers to understand what exactly you are referring to. So, if you happen to ask a question about a specific company or job position, make sure to name them!

  • Have not been asked before Before asking a question, make sure it (or a similar question) has not previously been asked.

We’ll build a better community if we have answers to similar questions consolidated in one single place where we can all build upon each other’s experiences and opinions.

  • Are appropriate Please read below for more information on what is considered “inappropriate content.”
Answers - Major Policies

  • Address the question that was asked Valuable answers specifically address the topic under question and also take into consideration the perspective of the asker — What do they want to know? What they are unsure about? What kind of context do they need? Valuable answers are relevant and will usually draw from your own personal experience.

  • Support their arguments with examples and details Valuable answers are substantiated with supporting details. Just saying that a company’s culture is “positive” or “fun!” does not provide other students enough information to paint a picture of this workplace. Good answers will provide details on what it is that makes the culture “positive” (i.e.: strong collaboration, supportive managers, transparent leadership team).

  • Are clear and easy to read It’s completely acceptable to have the occasional typo or spelling error, we all do that! But please make sure your answers are easy to read and understand and don’t contain any jokes or sarcasm.

  • Are appropriate Please read below for more information on what is considered “inappropriate content.”

Categories of inappropriate content

  • Contains personal information “Personal Information” is information that can identify a specific individual, creating a privacy risk. We will reject any Q&A that contains the following:

  • First and last name

  • Any phone number

  • Any email address

  • Any home address

  • Indirect information which clearly identifies a specific individual in a negative light

  • Negative comments about individuals not involved in leadership Q&A should not discuss specific people, unless those individuals are leaders or senior executives who have broad influence over the organization’s culture and environment. We will reject Q&A if:

  • It criticizes specific people instead of the internship experience or company culture We will not reject Q&A if:

  • It is critical of the highest levels of leadership in the company. It’s ok to identify and/or criticize the owner, founder, president, vice president, executive director, etc., as long as it’s related to the company culture or internship experience

  • Profane, vulgar, discriminatory, hurtful or illegal content We will reject Q&A if it contains:

  • Profanities or swear words

  • Inappropriate sexual comments

  • Comments about a person or group based on gender, race, national origin, or sexual orientation unrelated to the company culture or internship experience

  • Contains confidential information We will reject Q&A if it contains:

  • Information on upcoming products or services

  • Non-public information about the company

  • Research & Development activities

  • Budgets or detailed financial information

  • Names of the employer’s clients or customers We will not reject Q&A because it contains:

  • Internship compensation

  • References to public information or published negative press about a company

  • Spam Q&A should not contain any commercial or promotional content. We will reject Q&A if it contains:

  • Content advertising or promoting a product or service

  • Links to products, services, or other companies, even if related to the internship

  • Links to other job listings or other job listing services

How to Search Using Labels

Labels are tags that your career services office can apply to data in Handshake to help classify, organize, and elevate the information in Handshake!

If you were provided a label, you can use the label to search within the Jobs and Events sections in Handshake.

Jobs

  1. Click Jobs on the left navigation menu, then click All Filters.

  2. Scroll to the bottom of the pop-up and locate the section titled Labeled by your school.

  3. Click in the box to view the labels created by your school, or type in the box to find the desired label.

  4. Click the blue button Show results to explore jobs with the chosen label!

Events

  1. Click Events on the left navigation menu, then click More Filters.

  2. Within the pop-up, locate the Labels section, then type in the search box to locate the desired label.

  3. Check the box to the right of the label you’d like search, then click View results.

Interviews

  1. Click on your accounts icon, located in the upper-right corner of the screen, then click My Meetings from the dropdown.

  2. Click On-Campus Interviews.

  3. Locate the Label section on the left menu, then click the arrow to expand the section.

  4. Click the blue link View all.

  5. In the pop-up, check the boxes to the left of the label you’d like to search interviews with, then click the blue button Done.

Job Roles (Students)

During your job search, you may have an idea of what you want to do, and feelings around what you don’t want to do.

To help you with your search, our team has identified and created Job Roles in Handshake.

Job Roles are incorporated in Handshake via:

  • Job postings
    • When employers create a new job, job roles are automatically assigned based on details in the job posting, and employers can edit added roles or choose to add more.
  • Job digest emails
  • Job search alert emails
  • Multiple blog posts in the Job Roles category Note: while Job Roles are used mostly on the backend to provide you with relevant jobs, you can search for jobs based on their Job Roles in Handshake. To learn more, refer to Searching for Jobs and Internships.

Navigating the Employer Brand Page on Handshake

When you visit a company’s profile on Handshake, you’ll land on their employer brand page. This page offers an in-depth look at the company’s culture, values, people, and career opportunities.

You can access an employer’s brand page in several ways:

  • Employer Search
    • Click “Employers” on the left navigation menu, then search for a specific company profile.
  • Feed Posts
    • Click on the company’s name or logo directly from a feed post.
  • Job Listings
    • Click on the company’s name from any job posting to view their brand page. The employer brand page is organized into several key sections that give you a comprehensive view of the company.

Header

The header displays the employer’s name, logo, industry, location, company size, type, website URL, and a “Follow” button.

To learn more about following an employer, check out Following an Employer in Handshake.

Overview Tab

The Overview tab is the default landing page, offering a comprehensive snapshot of the company. It includes:

  • About Section: A brief description of the company, including details on its mission, values, or culture.
  • Posts: Content the company has previously shared in the feed and chosen to highlight. To view all of the company’s posts, click View All to be directed to the Posts tab, or click on the Posts tab itself.
  • Work life: Information on company benefits, perks, and the work environment.
  • Testimonials: Reviews from current or former employees, including their role, school, major, and graduation year.
  • Jobs: Current job openings at the company. If there are multiple listings, the most relevant ones to your career interests will be highlighted.
  • Events: Upcoming events hosted or attended by the company at your school.
  • Gallery: Photos showcasing the company’s culture and workplace.
  • Affiliated employers: Shows the relationship between the brand and other companies within Handshake.

Jobs Tab

The Jobs tab on an employer’s brand page is designed to showcase the company’s current job openings. It serves as a key resource for you to explore career opportunities with that employer.

Posts Tab

The Posts tab on an employer’s brand page is a space where you can access all of the content the company has posted to the feed on Handshake. The posts are arranged in reverse-chronological order, with the most recent appearing at the top.

Posting Content to the Handshake Feed

The feed on Handshake is a place where you can share content with other users on the platform, as well as find career-related posts by fellow peers, employers, and your career services department. This exchange of knowledge between users can be incredibly empowering while exploring ones career path.

The feed may consist of text, images, videos, and links.

To post on the feed, your profile visibility must be set to Community. Learn more about your profile visibility options in Profile Privacy Options in Handshake, and find step-by-step instructions for updating your visibility settings How to Change Your Student Profile Privacy Setting.

Topics:

  • How to post content
    • Desktop
    • Mobile
  • How to change your content audience
  • How to delete a post To learn more about Handshake’s home feed, refer to Handshake Home Feed: Overview & Interactions.

How to post content

You can post content to Handshake’s feed via your desktop or mobile app!

Important: once a post is shared to the feed, you won’t be able to edit it.

Desktop

  1. Click Feed on the left navigation menu.

  2. Click on the box Share something with the community…, located at the top-center of the page.

If you’ve never posted to the feed before, you’ll receive a pop-up encouraging you to share your first post — Click the button Got it to proceed.

🚀Tip: sharing content helps you build your brand and stand out to employers. Remember that content can be viewed by peers, employers, and career centers on Handshake. Anything you post should contribute to the spirit of our community and be respectful. All posts are subject to our Terms of Service and we may remove political content.

You can post content in the form of text, images, video, and links.

Text

In the pop-up that appears, click the link text post, located in the lower-left corner within the sentence “write a text post instead”.

💡Note: the text character limit is 3,000.

Click in the text field and begin typing your message. Once your text is added, review your content and confirm it’s what you want to share, then click the button Post to share to the feed on Handshake!

Image/Video

In the pop-up that appears, click the button Choose file or drag and drop your image or video into the drag-and-drop field to upload.

Want to celebrate your wins on Handshake’s feed? Whether you’ve landed a new job, completed an internship, or attended an awesome career event, Handshake’s got you covered with fun, premade stickers to celebrate your progress. Head over to our blog post Celebrate your college and career wins on the feed, to discover a sticker that can be shared as an image.

💡Note: the video upload limit is 30gb.

When you record videos in HDR, Cloudflare automatically converts them to SDR for compatibility, which can make colors look less vibrant. To keep your video looking its best, export it directly to SDR in your video editing app before uploading, so you can avoid Cloudflare’s automatic conversion.

While the content loads, a “processing” image is displayed within the center of the pop-up with a spinner — this may take a few moments to upload.

Once the image or video is uploaded, it will appear within the content box.

🚀Tip: add text to your image or video if you wish! Click in the text field above your uploaded media, then type in your message.

Add alt text

To add alt text, click the button Add alt text, located in the lower-right corner of your uploaded content. In the text space below your content, describe your image or video to those with image impairments. To save, click the button Save! A check mark in the lower-left corner will indicate that alt text has been added.

To remove the uploaded media, click the X in the upper-right corner of the upload.

When you’re ready to share, click the button Post!

Audio description

To add an audio description to your video, hover over the video to reveal the menu icon, then click Add audio description.

Links

Any content posted to the feed on Handshake can include hyperlinks. When added, the post will show a preview associated with the link.

  • If your post includes multiple links, the last link will take preview precedence.
  • If your post includes a video, the video will take preview precedence.
Emojis and Mentions

To add an emoji, click the smiley face icon. To mention someone, use the @ symbol on your keyboard or click the @ button in the post or comment composer.

You can mention any user whose name appears in People Search, including other students and employer users—in both posts and comments.

When a user is mentioned, they will receive both a push notification and an in-app notification.

Mentions are visible across all platforms. Clicking on a mention will take you to that user’s profile.

To post to the feed, click the Post button or use the keyboard shortcut Command + Enter.

Mobile

  1. Tap Feed, located in the lower-left corner of the screen.

  2. Tap the + icon, located in the lower-right corner of the screen.

  3. Type the content you wish to share in the provided space.

  • To upload a video, click on the video camera icon.
  • To upload an image, click on the picture icon. 💡Note: the text character limit is 3,000 and the video upload limit is 30gb.

How to change your content audience

By default, all users on Handshake will have access to your posts through the feed. To change your audience, click on the eye icon, located below your name.

In the pop-up that appears, select who can access your post, Everyone or People at your school, then click the button Done.

How to delete a post

If you would like to remove a post, you may do so at anytime via your desktop.

Click your icon, located in the upper-right corner of the screen on Handshake, then click My profile from the dropdown.

Once on your profile, click Posts, located to the right of About, below your header information.

All posts are listed, with the most recent at the top and the oldest at the bottom. Navigate to the post you want to delete, then click the three dots menu, located to the right of your post. From the dropdown, click Delete.

Within the pop-up, confirm you want to permanently remove the post by clicking the red button Delete, or click Cancel to cancel.

Public Reviews and Q&A Pages

We have temporarily taken out this feature from Handshake. However, we may plan to bring it back in a new way in the future!

Receiving Employer Messages in Handshake

Employers may send you messages on Handshake, which may include event invitations, promotional campaigns, and recruiting messages.

  • If your school is a Handshake partner, employers must have at least one approved or expired job posting at your school before they can message you.
  • If your school is not a Handshake partner and you are a part of the open network, employers will need to have at least one approved or expired job on the Handshake platform before they can message you. Employers can only send proactive messages to you if your profile’s privacy is set to Employers or Community. For more information on privacy settings on Handshake, refer to Profile Privacy on Handshake.

To help you identify which promotional campaigns and recruiting messages are most relevant to you, we display a “Top match” badge on the message preview.

Note: the “Top match” badge is only displayed if you’re among the top 15% of potential candidates. This indicator can serve as a motivation for you to pursue job opportunities when employers reach out to you.

Premium Employer Partners

Some employers on Handshake are Premium Partners. These employers have paid for enhanced Handshake usage and have undergone additional vetting by our team. They also have access to exclusive tools that help them connect with students in a more targeted and meaningful way.

Segments

Premium Partners can create Segments — subsets of students or alumni who may be a good fit for their open roles. These segments are based on specific criteria, such as qualifications, interests, or representation and diversity goals.

When Premium Partners use segment filters, they cannot view student names or profiles. However, they may be able to make general inferences about student associations based on the segment filters they apply.

Segment filters can include data from student profiles, such as:

  • Education details
  • Work experience
  • Involvement in organizations or extracurriculars
  • Gender and pronouns
  • Achievements and accolades
  • Interests, including Industry, Job Type, Role, or Location For more information on gender identity and pronouns, check out our blog post Student Gender Identity and Pronouns on Handshake.

Premium Partners who filter by student organizations can also select Underrepresented Groups Organizations as an additional filter. However, this filter must be used alongside another filter and cannot be selected alone.

Request an Appointment with your Career Center

If your school uses appointment scheduling in Handshake, you can request an appointment with a career counselor through either the desktop or mobile app.

Click on the expandable headers below for step-by-step instructions.

Desktop

  1. Click Career Center on the left navigation menu, then select Appointments under your school’s name.

  2. Click the button Request appointment.

Note: All past and upcoming appointments here if you need access to them!

  1. Choose a category, then select your desired appointment type.

Note: If you’re unsure which type to choose, contact your school’s Career Center. If your school hasn’t configured appointment categories, you’ll be prompted to select an appointment type.

  1. Choose your appointment type associated with category that was selected.

  2. The calendar displays available dates and times based on the appointment category and type you selected. Unavailable dates are grayed out. Select a date to view the available appointment times, or select Skip to next available on the right to jump to the next available appointment.

Tip: Use the filters in the upper-right corner to narrow your search. Search by staff member by selecting a name from the drop-down, or filter by appointment format, such as virtual or in-person. Once a filter is selected, only dates and times that match your search criteria will be shown. If no appointments match your search, click Clear filters to try a different search, or check back later.

  1. After selecting a date and time, describe the purpose of your appointment and select the appointment format: virtual or in-person.

Depending on the appointment, you may have only one format available or be able to choose between both. Select the appropriate radio button to confirm how you’d like the appointment to be held.

If you select in-person, you may also need to confirm the appointment location.

If an intake survey is included with your appointment request, you’ll be prompted to complete it before submitting your request.

  1. Click Request to submit your appointment request. A confirmation message will appear indicating that your request has been submitted to your career center. Your school will review and confirm the appointment.

Depending on your notification preferences in your user settings, you’ll receive updates about your appointment request, such as approvals or declines, reminders, cancellations, and comments.

To make sure you receive the updates you want, review your notification settings in Managing Your Notification Preferences.

If your notification preferences are set to email, you’ll receive an email titled “You have a new notification on Handshake.”

  • Approved: The email will include your appointment details, including the appointment type, staff member, date and time, and meeting format or location.
  • Declined: The email will indicate that your appointment request was declined. The appointment details page in Handshake will also be updated to show the status of your appointment. Approved appointments display a green status tag, while declined appointments display a red status tag.

From the appointment details page, you can manage your appointment and share information with your career center:

  • Add the appointment to your calendar
  • Cancel the appointment
  • Add comments for the staff member to review before your appointment When appointment reminders are enabled, you’ll receive reminder emails 24 hours and 1 hour before your appointment.

If you self-cancel an appointment, you may receive a confirmation email or in-app confirmation, depending on your notification settings.

For information about joining a virtual appointment on Handshake, check out Attending Virtual Appointments on Handshake!

Mobile

1 - Tap your Account icon in the upper-left corner of the screen.

  1. Tap Career Center, then tap Appointments on your Career Center page.

  2. Tap Request appointment.

  3. Select the desired category, then select the appointment type. Available appointment dates will be displayed based on your selections.

Tip: You can use the filters to find specific staff members or appointment formats, such as virtual or in-person.

  1. Tap an available date on the calendar to view and select a time.

Note: If an appointment category or type is not available on a certain date, the date will not be clickable. Only dates with available appointment times can be selected.

  1. Review the appointment details, then tap Request.

A confirmation message will appear indicating that your request has been submitted to your Career Center. Your school will review and confirm the appointment.

Once your appointment is confirmed, you’ll receive a confirmation email titled “You have a new notification on Handshake.” The email will include your appointment details, including the appointment type, staff member, date and time, and meeting format or location.

💡Note: if you need to reschedule an appointment, contact your Career Center or cancel the appointment and request a new appointment. To cancel an appointment, click the button Cancel on the appointment’s details page.

Missing the Career Center option on the left navigation bar?

Here are a few possible reasons:

  • School not linked: If you’ve requested to connect with a school, check your status by clicking your profile icon, then School Connections. If it says “Pending,” your school still needs to approve your request.
  • No school on account: If you registered without selecting a school, features like the Career Center won’t be available. To connect, click your profile icon, then School Connections. Find your school and request to join.
  • School not on Handshake (yet!): If your school isn’t a partner, encourage your career center to join so you can access more features.

Student Q&A (Question & Answer) in Handshake

Q&A is a way for students to ask career-related questions and receive responses from other students or alumni on Handshake.

Q&A is the most effective format to deliver a personalized and engaging experience at scale — through Q&A, you can network and build relationships with peers outside your school by sharing knowledge, advice, and experiences with one another.

Click on the expandable headers to learn more!

Accessing Q&A

You can locate Handshake’s Q&A via the Student community by clicking the following link: app.joinhandshake.com

From the community link, you have access to all questions submitted by peers on Handshake.

Use the search bar at the upper-middle of the page to locate topics regarding advice, interviews, job titles, companies, etc.

Click the tab:

  • My Questions to access any questions you’ve asked the community.
  • My Answers to access all questions you’ve responded to. Posting a Question

To post a question, locate the Ask your own question section, on the right side of the page of the community page.

Start typing your question in the text box, then click the blue button Submit Question when complete!

After your question is submitted, it’ll be moderated by our team before it is published to ensure all questions meet our community guidelines.

Click the blue button See My Questions after the question is submitted, or the tab My Questions to review the status of your questions:

  • Pending - the question is being reviewed.
  • Approved - the question met the guidelines, and was approved.
    • Note: you’ll receive an email when the question is approved and live on Handshake! Responding to Question

If you would like to provide insight to a question, and respond with an answer, click directly on the question to open the thread.

Scroll to the bottom and type your answer in the available text box.

Before submitting your response, choose your identity:

  • Fully visible: display full name, photo, school, school year and major
  • Semi-anonymous: hide full name and photo, but display school, school year and major Click the blue button Submit once complete!

After your question is submitted, it’ll be moderated by our team before it is published to ensure all questions meet our community guidelines.

Click the blue button See My Answers after the question is submitted, or the tab My Answers to review the status of your response:

  • Pending - the response is being reviewed.
  • Approved - the response met the guidelines, and was approved.
    • Note: you’ll receive an email when the response is approved and live on Handshake! Community Guidelines

All questions and answers that are submitted through the Q&A feature are moderated by our team before publication to ensure all questions meet our community guidelines:

  • Respect privacy: don’t post personal information
  • Be constructive: don’t ask questions or answers that are unhelpful or unrelated to helping other students advance their careers
  • Be honest, but don’t get personal: don’t ask questions or submit answers that contain negative comments about individuals
  • Be professional: don’t post profane, vulgar, discriminatory, hurtful, or illegal content
  • Respect confidentiality: don’t post information violating intellectual property or confidentiality
  • Stay on topic: don’t post spam Privacy Information

Anyone using Handshake will be able to access your published questions or answers on the platform.

Your published questions or answers won’t be visible to employers or students as a part of your profile.

Your published questions or answers may appear without your name in Google searches (and other search engines). The information that will be shared is your school year and most recent work experience.

Update Your Career Interests

When setting up your Handshake account, you’re prompted to include your career interests within the “What are you looking for?” section of your onboarding.

These interests determine the specific kinds of opportunities you are searching for, which consist of job roles, industries, and locations. By filling out this section, you’ll receive more personalized job recommendations tailored to you.

If your goals change and you’d like to update the selected interests, you can do so at any time!

You can update your interests from the “Looking for” section of your profile, or via the Career Interests page - Click on the expandable headers below for outlined instructions.

💡Note: if your profile is visible on Handshake and set to either Community or Employers, interests are displayed on your profile to the corresponding audience. If your profile is set to private, your interests will not be visible to other users on Handshake since they will not be able to access your profile.

From your profile

Click on your name in the upper-right corner of the screen, then click My profile from the dropdown.

From your profile, click the pencil icon, located to the right of Looking for — then fill in the desired information within the pop-up.

  • What are you looking for right now? (Select one)
    • Full-time job
    • Part-time job
    • Internship
    • Campus job
  • Roles (click in the search bar and begin typing to produce results in the dropdown)
  • Industries (click in the search bar and begin typing to produce results in the dropdown)
  • Locations (click in the search bar and begin typing to produce results in the dropdown) You must have at least one of the prompts filled out for the “Looking for” section to be displayed on your profile.

If no information is included in the “Looking for” section, or everything is removed, you’ll receive a prompt that states, “Answer this to make the”Looking for” section visible on your profile.”

Once everything is added and updated, click the button Save to save!

From the Career Interests page

  1. Click on your icon, located in the upper-right corner of the screen, then click Career Interests.

  2. Select (or deselect) the checkboxes as desired in each section:

  • What type of job are you looking for?
    • Full-Time Job
    • Internship
    • Part-Time
    • On-Campus Job
  • How can Handshake help you?
    • I want a job
    • I want an internship
    • I’m interested in grad school
    • I want to find out about career center events (faits, info sessions, appointments)
    • I want to build my network
    • I’m not sure / just checking it out
  • What options are you considering after graduation?
    • Working
    • Graduate School
    • Gap Year
    • Military Service
    • Volunteering
    • Fellowship
    • Not Sure
  • What job roles are you interested in? (Type in the box to add one or multiple roles)
  • Where are you interested in living? (Type in the box to add one or multiple cities)
  • Join the career community you are most interested in. To learn more, click here: [LINK TO YOUR SCHOOL INTEREST PAGE IF AVAILABLE]
  • Which industries interest you? (Check all the boxes that apply)
  • Which kinds of job, or job functions, interest you? (Check all the boxes that apply)
  • When do you expect to graduate? (Click the dropdown) Click the green button Save My Career Interest to update your selections!

Troubleshooting tip: if the changes aren’t saving, try clearing your browser cache and cookies! If that doesn’t work, we recommend trying another browser. Refer to Handshake Supported Browser for more information.

Company Profile Management

Company Profile Merges and How They Work

Handshake is designed to have a single company profile for each brand. Each company or organization should have only one company profile on Handshake.

The existence of multiple company profiles representing the same company, even if they are for regional or divisional recruiting purposes, can cause confusion for career service offices and may result in unnecessary flags. Furthermore, it can add confusion to students as they seek out your opportunities.

  • A company profile merge may take place if there are duplicate company profiles found in Handshake.

  • A merge may also occur if separate company profiles exist in Handshake as divisions but should all be under one parent company profile. After merging company profiles, the company profile owner can add divisions to the profile. Learn more about How to Add Divisions to Your Company.

  • Divisions currently exist for job postings and in-person career fair registrations. Separate company descriptions, branding images, websites, etc. will not be able to added in a division. Important: Merges are non-reversible and can not be undone once completed.

To request a company merge, contact Support.

Merge process

A merge will:

  • Take up to 7 days to process. A warning will be issued to the affected employers, giving them one week to respond.
  • Combine any duplicate company profiles into one centralized profile, allowing the company profile owner (or admin) to create divisions within that profile.
  • Merge historical data, including job postings, events, interviews, and career fairs, into the selected parent company profile.
  • Deactivate all teammate accounts from the company profile being merged, for security reasons.
    • The teammates of the merged-to company profile will not be impacted.
    • The company profile owner (or admin) will be able to review the status of each teammate and reactivate accounts as needed.
  • Combine approved schools from both company profiles.
  • Override other statuses (pending/declined) with school approvals from either company profile.
    • For example, if one company profile was denied at a school but the other was approved, the final merged company profile will be approved at that school.
  • Retain only the kiosk responses and check-ins of the “to” employer (the company profile being merged into) if both companies attended the same event.
    • To preserve specific check-in data from the other company profile before the merge, download a CSV file of this event information in advance. A merge will not:
  • Alter user login credentials (each user retains their own user account), job postings, school approvals, and historical data.
  • Reset any school approvals. However, the merge will reset each user’s Favorite schools list.
    • To add schools to your Favorite list, refer to Add or Remove Schools from Your Favorites.

Company Settings: Global Settings

Handshake allows employers to configure company-wide settings to help streamline processes across their organization.

Note: Only account Owners on Basic, Plus, and Pro plans, and Owners or Admins on Essentials and Enterprise (formerly TES) plans, can view and change these settings.

Access your global settings

  1. Click on your name in the upper-right corner of any page, then select Company Settings from the dropdown.

  2. From the menu on the left of the page, click Global Settings.

Configure your global settings

Employers can review and configure a range of settings that can be applied company-wide.

New teammate access

The options below allow employers to control how new teammates are added to their company profile and what access they are granted by default.

The settings that are available and visible on this page depend on your employer account type.

Allow Recruiters to create new teammates

When enabled, users with the Recruiter (Sourcer) or Recruiter (Advanced) role can add new teammates. Owners always retain this permission.

Note: For employers on Basic, Plus, and Pro plans, this setting is enabled by default and cannot be changed.

Auto-approve new users who sign up with a valid email that matches your company domain

When enabled, users signing up with a matching email domain (e.g., @yourcompany.com) are automatically approved. This option is available only if your domain is associated with a single company profile in Handshake.

Note: For employers on Basic, Plus, and Pro plans, this setting is enabled by default and cannot be changed.

Default new teammates to Representative

When checked, new teammates are assigned the Representative role by default. If left unchecked, they are assigned the Recruiter (Standard) role instead.

Note: This setting is available only to Essentials and TES customers. The Representative role is not available for Basic employers.

Company-wide feature access

Disable “Apply on Handshake” option for all jobs

Available to all employers regardless of account plan, this setting directs students to apply in your Applicant Tracking System (ATS) for all newly created jobs.

Note: This setting is disabled by default.

If enabled, the job form will not show the “On Handshake” option under “How will candidates submit applications?”

Messaging preferences

Allow candidates without Handshake profiles to reply to employee email addresses

Available to all employers regardless of account plan, this setting allows teammates to send messages to candidates who do not have a public Handshake profile but have RSVPed to or checked in at events or career fairs.

Candidates receive the message as an email and can respond directly. Learn more about Messaging Candidates without Handshake Profiles.

To learn more about receiving messages from students, and what guidelines to follow, refer to Receiving Messages from Students in Handshake.

School permissions

Only schools that have approved your company profile can be selected and granted permissions. These schools appear in the available dropdown menus.

  • If you are an on campus employer, permissions cannot be removed for the school where you’re based.
  • If the listed school is incorrect, update it in the Details section. For instructions, refer to How to Edit Your Company Profile Settings.
Select which schools can manage your profile.
  • Use the dropdown menu to select a school, or type to search.
  • To remove a school, click the X next to the school name.
Select which schools can post and edit jobs on your behalf.
  • Use the dropdown menu to select a school, or type to search.
  • To remove a school, click the X next to the school name.
  • Schools selected in this section will have permission to post and edit jobs on your behalf. Applicant Tracking Systems
Allow users to change default “External Apply” URLs

Available to all employers regardless of account plan, this setting allows teammates to manage job postings and edit the default “External Apply” URLs used for external applications.

Read more about How to Use Direct ATS.

Other Preferences

Allow Public Pages - SEO

Available to all employers regardless of account plan, this setting allows your Handshake company profile to appear in relevant search engine results. People who are not signed in to Handshake will be able to view a summarized version of your company profile.

The public view will include

  • Company name, logo, banner image, and About section
  • Location, type, size, industry
  • Reviews
  • Questions & Answers for your company
  • A list of Related Employers (other employers within the same industry) Learn more about Publicly Searchable Pages.

How Multiple Business Units Work on Handshake

Handshake’s division model allows multiple business units or teams to operate independently while using the same platform.

Divisions help you organize users, job postings, and career fair registrations, ensuring that teams can collaborate effectively without overlapping or interfering with one another’s recruiting efforts.

Features available to Premium partners only are indicated by an asterisk (*). For more information, please check out this resource.

Teams can scale their recruiting efforts using divisions across different areas of the platform, as outlined below.

Jobs

Companies with multiple divisions can streamline job postings by assigning each job to the appropriate division.

  • Learn how to add a division when posting a job by referring to How to Post a Job. Teammates can also filter the Jobs page to view only jobs within their division, ensuring clarity and reducing overlap between teams

  • Learn more about Navigating the Jobs Page. Career fairs

When registering for a career fair, you can register a specific division of your company instead of the entire organization.

On the registration form, navigate to the Basic Information section, then select the division from the Which division of the organization are you registering? dropdown.

  • Delve into the specifics for Registering for a Fair (Employers). *School lists

School lists allow you to keep teams and outreach efforts separate by targeting specific schools or geographic regions.

Each division can create customized lists to target candidates based on various criteria, such as:

  • Named school lists: Teams can target candidates from specific schools that align with their divisions recruiting goals.

  • Geographic regions: Divisions can recruit from schools in certain locations to meet local hiring needs.

  • Minority Serving Institutions (HBCUs, HSIs, MSIs): Separate lists can be created to focus outreach on these institutions, ensuring targeted engagement with diverse candidate pools. This approach helps divisions manage their outreach independently, avoiding overlap with other teams and improving the efficiency of recruiting efforts.

  • Learn more about Creating and Managing School Lists. Outreach

To provide a seamless candidate experience, teams should use templates that specify both the division and recruiting team.

When candidates may be contacted by multiple teams, it’s essential to clearly state the roles being hired for and the division represented to ensure clear and professional communication.

  • Find out more about Creating and Managing Templates.
  • Discover How to Send a Student a Message.

*Using exclusions to avoid over-messaging candidates

To avoid unintentionally sending multiple messages to the same candidate, campaign exclusions can be applied to your messaging campaigns.

This is particularly helpful for large teams who do not have the opportunity to communicate with each other regularly.

  • Unlock more information about Campaigns: Exclusions. *Insights

One of the key benefits of Handshake is the valuable data that can be extracted both from the platform and through our partnership with the Insights team.

The Applicants tab on the Analytics page is designed to help teams understand the ROI from campaigns and their impact on job applications, career fair RSVPs, and event registrations.

  • Dive deeper into Talent Analytics: Applicants.

Additional resources

  • Ready to optimize your recruiting efforts with company divisions? Learn How to Add Divisions to Your Company.

How to Add Divisions to Your Company

On Handshake, you can add divisions to your company profile and associate them with any job posting or in-person career fair registration.

Divisions currently exist only as names in the system. There is not a way to add separate branding (website, logo, etc.) to a division.

There must be at least 2 divisions in a company profile in order for divisions to appear. If you do not have a second division available, we recommend adding a filler division, which you could name (for example) “filler” or “extra”.

Note: This is an action that can only be performed by the Owner or Admin of a company profile.

Topics:

  • Add a division
  • Manage your division
    • Edit a division
    • Delete a division
  • Select a division
    • Job
    • Career fair

Add a division

  1. Click on your name in the upper-right corner of any page in Handshake, then select Company settings from the dropdown.

  2. In the left menu, select Divisions. On the Divisions page, enter your division’s name and code in the respective text fields, then click the blue button Add.

Note: The division code is not required and does not appear in job postings or career fair registrations.

Manage your division

Edit a division

  1. Click the three-line icon to the far right of the division name, and then select Edit Division Name.

  2. In the pop-up modal, enter the new division name or code, then click the blue button Save.

  3. Once saved, the name and code of the division will automatically be updated.

Delete a division

  1. Click the three-line icon to the right of the division name, then select Delete Division.

  2. Once clicked, the division will be automatically deleted. Deleted divisions cannot be retrieved.

Note: Divisions that are associated with a job posting or career fair registration cannot be deleted.

Divisions that cannot be deleted will display the error message “Cannot delete record because dependent jobs exist or”Cannot delete record because dependent registrations exist”

Select a division

Once you add a division, you can easily associate the division to any job or in-person career fair registration.

Job

To associate a specific division with a job, click the Company division field in the Your hiring team section of the job form, then select the desired division. For additional guidance, refer to How to Post a Job.

Career fair registration

To associate a specific division with an in-person career fair registration, navigate to the Basic Information section of the registration form, then select the division below the field Which division of the organization are you registering? Read more in Registering for a Fair (Employers).

Note: While the field is included in the registration form for a virtual career fair, the functionality is not currently supported.

How to Edit Your Company Profile Settings

Easily update your company settings on Handshake to keep your information accurate and showcase your brand.

Edit your company settings

Only the Owner or an Admin of your company profile can update company settings.

To get started, click your name in the upper right corner of any page in Handshake, then select Company settings from the dropdown.

From this page, you can use the menu on the left to edit your company details, as outlined below.

Details

The Details page lets employers update most company profile information directly in Handshake.

Fields marked with an asterisk (*) are required.

Fields you can edit directly

The fields listed below can be edited by employers:

  • Aliases
  • Other names your company may be known by.
  • Industry*
    • For a full list of industries in Handshake, refer to Employer Industry Name List.
  • Website*
    • Website URL must include http:// or https://.
  • Description*
    • A short summary or mission statement for your company.
  • Primary location
    • Your company’s main office or headquarters.
    • The address must include a full street address with a street number.
  • Locations
    • Additional offices or sites where your company operates.
    • The address can be a full street address or a city and state.
  • Employer size
  • Employer type*
  • On-campus employer
    • Check this box if you are an on-campus employer.
      • To confirm your eligibility and set yourself up as an on-campus employer, refer to Identifying as an On-Campus Employer on Handshake.
  • Auto-approve Staff
    • Automatically approves new staff members who join your company using an email address from your company’s domain.
    • This option will appear only if there is one company profile tied to your email domain in Handshake.
  • Public email (only visible to Handshake partner schools)
  • Public phone number (visible on the company’s profile)
  • Private phone number
  • Duns number
  • Time zone
  • LinkedIn profile URL
  • Facebook profile URL
  • Glassdoor profile URL
  • Instagram profile URL
  • Tiktok profile URL
  • X (formerly Twitter) profile URL
  • Logo
    • Must be at least 150 x 150 pixels.
  • Banner
    • At least 1400 x 400 pixels. Decorative only. Avoid including text.
    • Tip: After uploading your logo and banner, wait 30 seconds before clicking the Update employer button. Fields that require Support assistance

Employers cannot edit the following fields:

  • Name*
  • Employer Identification Number (EIN)* Contact support to update these fields, as they cannot be edited by employers.

Manage Your Promotion Settings

To ensure promotions are used consistently and within budget, you can set company-level controls for spend limits, default duration, and user access.

By default, only the company Owner can update promotion settings. Owners can also grant this access to Admins.

Haven’t created a job promotion yet? Start with Create a Job Promotion.

Access Promotion settings

From your name dropdown
  • Click your name in the upper right corner of Handshake, then select Company Settings from the dropdown.
  • From the left menu, click Promotion Settings.
From the Promotions page
  • Click Manage settings in the upper right corner of the Promotions page.

Review your budget overview

At the top of the Promotion settings page, you can review your Promotions budget for the current contract term, including:

  • Contract term dates
  • Total budget
    • The full amount available for the duration of your contract, including your base annual budget plus any bonus credits.
  • Spent budget
    • The amount of your total budget that has already been used.
  • Remaining budget
    • The portion of your total budget that is still available to spend for your contract duration.
  • Budget utilization
    • The percentage of your total budget that has been spent so far, displayed as a progress bar and percent spent for the current contract term.

Set default budget and duration

These settings apply company wide and help reduce manual oversight while maintaining budget guardrails.

Default budget

The default budget is the prefilled amount shown when creating a promotion. Team members can adjust this amount during setup.

Max budget

The max budget is the highest amount allowed when creating or editing an individual promotion.

Default duration

The default duration is the number of days automatically populated when setting up a promotion, and team members can adjust it when creating the promotion.

Manage role permissions

Access to Promotions is managed in Configure Roles under Company Settings.

From the Configure Roles page, you can control which roles have permission to:

  • Manage promotions
    • View, create and edit promotions
  • Manage promotion budget
    • Edit individual promotion budgets
  • Manage promotions settings
    • Edit default budget, overall budget and other promotions settings Limiting access to specific permissions can help maintain budget oversight while still enabling recruiters to support priority hiring needs.

To configure these permissions for your teammates, refer to How to Configure Role Level Permissions.

Publicly Searchable Pages

Handshake includes a company setting that allows employers to manage whether their company profile can appear on public pages.

Note: Only the owner or an admin on a company profile can manage whether public pages are allowed for their company.

Turning this setting on does not guarantee that a company page will appear publicly in search engine results. Public visibility depends on additional product conditions, and availability may vary by employer.

If you have questions about whether your company has a public page on Handshake, contact Support.

Background

To support access to career information, Handshake offers settings that affect whether company profile content may be available outside Handshake.

To protect students’ privacy, student profile photos, names, and schools are hidden on external pages. Only limited student information may be shown outside Handshake.

Manage your company’s SEO settings

  1. Click on your name in the upper-right corner of any page, then select Company Settings from the dropdown.

  2. In the left menu, select Global Settings, then uncheck the option for Allow public pages (SEO) in the Other preferences section.

  3. When you are finished, click the black Save button.

Public pages

Below, we provide an example of how your company profile will display as a public searchable page.

Who Is the Owner or Admin of My Company Profile?

If you need to find out who owns or manages your Handshake company account, follow the steps below.

The Owner or Admin is the teammate with the highest level of access to your company profile. This person may also be referred to as the company owner, company admin, or account administrator.

Before you begin

You must be connected to your company profile to view teammates and role assignments.

  • If your connection request is pending, you cannot see the Owner or Admin.
  • Approval typically takes 1 to 5 business days.
  • If your request has been pending for more than 5 business days, contact Support.

What is the difference between Owner and Admin?

Role availability depends on your account type:

  • On-campus employers and Basic, Plus, and Pro accounts include only the Owner role.
  • Essentials and Enterprise (formerly TES) accounts include both Owner and Admin roles. Some teams use the term “admin” interchangeably with “owner.” If only the Owner role appears in Handshake, that person is the highest level administrator for the company profile.

Locate your company’s owner or admin

  1. Click your name in the upper-right corner of any page, then select Teammates from the dropdown.

  2. The Teammates page displays the following information for each person connected to your company profile:

  • Name
  • Email address
  • Role
  • Visibility
  • Status
  1. In the left sidebar, locate the Role filter, then check the box for the role you want to view.
  • Accounts with Owner only will display a single role.
  • Accounts with Owner and Admin will display both.
  1. The teammates who match the selected role filter will appear in the results. Their name, email address, and role will display in the table.

Add or Remove Schools from Your Favorites

Note: Adding a school to your Favorites does not change your connection status.

Which schools can be added to Favorites

You can add a school to your Favorites list if the school is:

Add schools to your Favorites

Add a school you have not yet requested

Add a school you are approved by

Remove schools from your Favorites

  2. Filter your list to show only Favorites:

  • Essentials and Enterprise (formerly TES) customers: Click the white Lists button above the school list.
