Checking Your Permissions with a School

When a school approves your connection request on Handshake, they may grant a specific set of permissions. These permissions determine what your company can do with that school, such as posting jobs, creating events, or requesting interview schedules.

If a school does not appear as an option when you try to create an event, post a work-study job, or request an interview, the school may not have granted you the necessary permissions.

Note: You must have an approved connection with a school before you can review your permissions.

Check your permissions

  1. From the left navigation bar, select Schools.

  2. At the top of the page, click the gray My Network button to display schools you are currently connected with.

  3. Locate the school you want to review permissions for, then click the school’s name to open its profile.

Tip: Use the search bar to quickly locate the school by name.

  1. In the Account information panel on the right side of the school’s profile, review your permissions:
  • Granted permissions are displayed as badges under the Permissions section (e.g., Post jobs, Post interview schedules, Post work study jobs).
  • The Auto approvals section indicates whether your jobs and interviews are auto-approved or require school approval.
    • A green badge means auto-approval is enabled
    • A red badge means the school must manually approve.
  • If a permission such as Post work-study jobs is not listed under Permissions, the school has not granted that permission.

If you need additional permissions

Only the school can update employer permissions. If you need additional access, please contact the school’s Career Services department directly to learn about their approval process.

To find a school’s contact information, refer How to Contact a School.

Connecting with Schools on Handshake

To recruit on Handshake, your company must connect with schools where you would like to hire students and alumni.

This article explains how employers can request connections with schools.

Ways to connect with schools

You can connect with schools in two ways:

  • Post a job
  • When you post a job and select schools to share it with, a connection request is automatically sent to those schools. Learn How to Post a Job.
  • Request to join a school’s network
  • If you don’t have a job to post yet, you can send a connection request directly to schools you’re interested in recruiting from. Learn more about How to Request Approval from Schools. Note: You can search for and register for career fairs without being connected to a school or posting a job.

After you send a request

Once you’ve submitted a request, the school will review it based on its recruiting policies and standards.

  • Each school individually decides whether to approve or decline your request.
  • Review times vary, but most schools respond within a few business days. To learn how the approval process works and what to expect next, refer to Understanding School Approvals.

Explorer (tab)

Tip: Select Exclude schools you’re not approved at to focus on schools your company is already connected with.

Declined by a School

On Handshake, schools are responsible for approving or declining employer requests to connect, and each has different guidelines when choosing which jobs and employers to approve.

This article explains what happens when a school declines your connection request or job posting, how you are notified, and how to follow up.

Overview of declined requests

If a school declines your job posting, request to connect, or previously approved company, they are prompted to select a reason for the decline.

This reason is added as a comment to the school’s profile in Handshake so you can learn specifically why your job posting or company was declined.

Note: The reason is visible to both the school’s team and your company’s connected teammates.

Some schools may invite you to resubmit a job that has been declined. If you’ve been invited to resubmit a job posting, refer to Resubmit your Job for Approval.

What happens after a school declines your company

If your company was initially approved and later declined by a school, the following is impacted:

  • Search
    • You can no longer search for students from that school.
  • Messaging
    • You cannot send new messages to students from that school. If you have active message threads at the time of the decline, you may continue those conversations.
  • Jobs
    • Jobs posted to the school that were approved, pending, or in progress will be updated to declined. Any jobs that were closed remain closed. Existing jobs that were Handshake+ or self-service subscription will have that subscription canceled or downgraded.
  • Fairs
    • Approved or pending registrations for career fairs hosted by that school will be canceled. Registrants and associated contacts will be notified.
  • Events
    • Approved or pending event requests that have not yet taken place will be declined. Registrants and attendees will be notified.
  • Interview schedules
    • Approved or pending interview schedules at that school will be declined. Registrants will be notified.
  • Applications
    • Existing applications remain available to you, and you can still view documents submitted by those applicants.
    • Note: Students are not notified when employers or jobs they applied to are declined by schools.

How you are notified of a decline

When a school declines your request, an automated Handshake notification and email are sent to the teammate who posted the job, based on their notification preferences. Review your Default Notification Preferences (Employers).

In Handshake

  1. Click the globe icon in the upper-right corner of any page in Handshake.

  2. Click the Notification type button and select Schools from the dropdown, then click Apply to filter notifications by school.

  3. Locate the notification by school name. The notification will indicate either that a specific job was declined or that the school has declined to show your jobs and events.

  4. Click the school name to view additional details.

Via email

Note: Email notifications are only sent when your company is declined, not when an individual job is declined.

  1. Email notifications are sent to the requestor’s email address (connected to the Handshake user account).

The email will read:

Sent from: “handshake@notifications.joinhandshake.com”

Subject: “[SCHOOL NAME] has declined to show your jobs and events”

Body:

SCHOOL NAME has declined to show your jobs and events

Hello NAME,

[SCHOOL NAME] has declined to show your jobs and events for the following reason(s)

[REASON]

Comment: VARIES–CUSTOM COMMENT TEXT FROM SCHOOL

[View Decline Details] button.

For more information about the school approval process, visit our help center.”

  1. Click the red View Decline Details button to login to Handshake and view the details.

Following up with a school

To learn more about the decline, contact the Career Services department at the school directly. This may also be referred to as being rejected, denied, or not approved by a school.

To locate a school’s contact information in Handshake, refer to How to Contact a School.

How Can I Get Approved By Schools?

To recruit on Handshake, your company must first be approved by each school you want to connect with. Each school manages its own approval process and decides which employers and jobs to accept based on their unique recruiting policies.

This article explains the main factors schools consider when reviewing connection requests and offers practical tips to help you increase your chances of approval.

To learn how to request approval and connect with schools, refer to Connecting with Schools on Handshake.

What schools look for during approval

Schools review approval requests to ensure that employers meet their recruiting standards and provide safe, legitimate opportunities for students. While criteria differ, approval decisions often consider:

  • A complete and professional employer profile with a logo, website, and accurate company details
  • A legitimate business email domain (for example, yourcompany.com instead of Gmail or Yahoo)
  • Clear, detailed job postings that accurately describe roles and qualifications
  • A positive reputation or established track record
  • Transparency about the organization’s business model, roles, and compensation Tip: Schools are more likely to approve employers that provide clear, credible information about their organization and job opportunities.

If your company is new to Handshake or has limited recruiting history, ensure your profile and job postings are complete before submitting requests. This helps schools make informed approval decisions.

To strengthen your company’s profile and improve your chances of approval, refer to Create a High Quality Employer Profile.

If your request is delayed or declined

Approval timelines vary by school, but most decisions are made within 1–5 business days. If your request remains pending for several days, consider contacting the school’s Career Services department for an update.

If your request is declined, review your company profile and job postings for completeness or clarity. You can also reach out to the school directly to learn more about their approval criteria.

Note: Handshake cannot override or change a school’s approval decision.

To view and understand your connection request status, refer to Understanding Your School Connection Status.

How to Connect with Handshake Open Network

The Handshake open network includes students from accredited 4-year institutions and community colleges in the United States that are not yet Handshake partner schools.

These students can create Handshake accounts to explore employer profiles, apply to jobs, and use many of the same career features available to students at partner schools.

Posting jobs to the open network

All employers can reach open network students by posting a job to all schools on Handshake.

When creating a job post, select the option to share your job with all schools:

  • Auto-select schools: Visible to Basic, Plus, and Pro employers.
  • Post to full network: Visible to Essentials and Enterprise (formerly TES) customers. This automatically shares your job with all schools in your network and with students in the open network.

Jobs must meet the standard Handshake posting criteria:

  • Approved by at least one school
  • Paid position
  • Not an on-campus, co-op, or federal work-study role
  • Not located at a residential address

Additional ways to connect

Essentials and Enterprise (formerly TES) customers have additional tools to build connections with students in the open network.

Search and message

Search for and message open network students directly to build new connections. Learn more in A Guide to Talent List.

Events

Invite open network students to virtual or off-campus events by sharing the public event link.

  • Students with a Handshake account can sign in and register.
  • Students without an account can register as guests and choose to create a profile later. Learn more about Sharing an Event with Students.

Segments and campaigns

Include open network students in segments and use them in campaigns to promote jobs, events, or employer brand initiatives.

Learn How to Build a Segment.

How to Contact a School

Employers may contact a school on Handshake to request information about their approval status, review permissions, or seek additional guidance.

To view or respond to a comment left by a school on a job posting, refer to How to View Comments on a Job Posting.

Reach out to career services

  1. At the upper-left of any page in Handshake, enter the full name of the school in the search bar, then click on it.
  • If the school does not appear, it is likely not partnered with Handshake.
  • Tip: Search for the school by its full name. Abbreviations or short forms may not return results.

  1. The school’s profile will load. On the Overview tab, locate the School contact information card on the right side of the page. Contact information may include a phone number, an email address, or both.

  2. Call or email the school directly, depending on the information provided.

Note: Response times depend on each school’s operating hours and staff availability.

Access schools

    • My network to view schools that have approved your company

Actions you can take with schools

View and add notes

  • Personal Note to keep the note private and visible only to you

  1. Optionally, set a Reminder date and time for the note.

Add a comment

Understanding School Approvals

Each school partnered with Handshake manages its own approval process for employers and job postings.

Approval decisions are guided by the school’s recruiting policies and may differ based on the types of jobs you post, your company’s reputation, and how established your organization is.

This article explains how the approval process is managed, how schools make their decisions, and what to expect once your request has been reviewed.

How schools review employer requests

When your company requests to connect with a school or posts a job, the request is sent to that school for review. Each school evaluates connection and job requests according to its own recruiting policies and criteria.

While every school’s process is unique, approvals are typically based on factors such as:

  • The types of jobs your company posts
  • Your company’s recruiting history or prior relationship with the school
  • The completeness and legitimacy of your employer profile Your request will remain in pending status until the school takes action. Most schools review requests within 1–5 business days, but timelines vary by school.

To view and understand your connection request status, refer to Understanding Your School Connection Status.

Approval notifications

Once a school reviews your request, you will receive a notification in Handshake about the outcome:

  • If the school approves your company or job posting, you will receive a notification in Handshake.
  • If the school declines your request, you will receive both a notification in Handshake and an email notification.

After your company is approved

When a school approves your connection request, you can begin recruiting with that school.

Approval may grant your company additional permissions, such as the ability to:

  • Post work-study jobs
  • Post events
  • Post interview schedules To learn how to view your granted permissions, refer to Checking Your Permissions with a School.

If your request is declined

If a school declines your request, the decision is based on its internal approval criteria and recruiting standards.

Note: Handshake cannot modify or override a school’s decision.

If your request was declined:

  • Review your employer profile and job postings to ensure they’re complete and transparent.
  • Confirm that your job opportunities align with the school’s recruiting policies.
  • Consider contacting the school’s Career Services department to learn more about its approval criteria. For guidance on improving your company’s chances of approval, refer to How Can I Get Approved By Schools?.

Understanding Your School Connection Status

On Handshake, every school connection request and job posting has a status that reflects where your company stands in the school’s approval process.

Knowing your connection status helps you understand what actions you can take with each school and when to follow up.

View your connection status

You can view your connection status with each school in Handshake.

  1. Click Schools from the left navigation bar.

  2. At the top of the page, click the white Filters button at the top of the page.

In the Status section of the filters panel, check one or more boxes:

  • Approved
  • Pending
  • Not connected
  • Declined
  1. The table will update to display schools that match your selected statuses.

Connection status types

Approved

The school has approved your connection. You can now post jobs, request interviews, and engage with students.

To review the permissions granted by the school, refer to Checking Your Permissions with a School.

Pending

The school has received your request but has not yet made a decision. Most schools review employer and job requests within 1–5 business days, though timelines can vary. If your request remains pending after several business days, consider reaching out to the school’s Career Services department for an update.

While your status is pending, you will not be able to:

  • Message students at that school
  • Post events
  • Request interview schedules Not Connected

You have not yet requested to connect or post a job to this school.

To request approval, refer to How Can I Get Approved By Schools?.

Declined

The school chose not to approve your request. If you’d like more information, contact the school’s Career Services department directly.

Additional resources

  • To find a school’s contact information, refer to How to Contact a School.

You can view your company’s connection status for each school on the far right side of the school’s name.

  • Favorite and request: You are not connected. Click the white button Favorite and request to add the school to your Favorites list and submit a request to join their network.
  • In favorites: You are connected, and the school is already in your Favorites list.
  • Add to favorites: You are connected but have not added the school to your Favorites list. Click the white button Add to Favorites to add it.

Take bulk actions

To take action on multiple schools at once:

  1. Check the box next to the name of each desired school.

  2. Once selected, the following bulk actions will appear:

  • Start Segment with these schools
    • Learn How to Build a Segment.
  • Add to list
  • More
    • New List from selected
    • New Job from selected
    • New Event from selected
      • Learn more about Creating and Managing School Lists.

Using School Lists in Handshake

After creating your school lists, you can use them to streamline outreach by targeting schools for job postings, events, and segments.

This helps you efficiently manage engagement and strengthen relationships within your network.

Not sure how to create or manage school lists? Refer to how to Creating and Managing School Lists.

This feature is available only to Essentials and Enterprise (formerly TES) customers. For more information, please check out this resource.

Topics:

  • Post a job to a school list
    • New job
    • Existing job
  • Promote an event to a school list
  • Add a school list to a segment

Post a job to a school list

New job
  1. In the Choose schools section of the job form, you can either Post to full network (which includes all schools in your school lists) or select specific schools.
  • To limit the posting to schools in your lists, select Post to specific schools or use a school list.

  1. Click the white button Lists, then select the desired school list(s).

  2. Schools in the school list(s) selected will appear below the Choose schools field.

  • To remove a single school from the school list selected, click the X to the right of the school name.
  • To remove all schools from the school list, click the X to the right of the school list name.
  1. After selecting the school list(s), click the button Continue in the lower-left corner of the page and complete the job posting.
Existing job

  1. Click Jobs from the left navigation bar, select the relevant job, then click the Schools tab.

  2. On the Schools tab, navigate to the Post to more schools section, then click the white button Lists.

  3. Select the preferred school list(s).

  4. Schools in the school list(s) selected will appear below the search bar.

  • To remove a single school from the school list selected, click the X to the right of the school name.
  • To remove all schools from the school list click the X to the right of the school list name.

  1. ‌Once the school list(s) is selected, click the black button Post in the upper-right corner of the section.

  2. The message “Jobs sent to schools. Your Requested schools list will update shortly” will display in a banner at the top of the page, and schools will display in the schools table in the Requested schools section.

Promote an event to a school list

  1. On the new event form, click the hyperlinked text Add School List below the field Invite schools to promote your event, then select the preferred school list(s).

Note: School lists can only be added to events hosted off-campus or virtually.

  1. Schools in the selected school list(s) will automatically appear in the field.

  2. Edit the remaining details, then click the blue button Save in the lower-right corner of the page to create your event.

Add a school list to a segment

  1. On the Segments page, locate the segment to which you want to add a school list, then click the pencil icon.
  • To add a school list to a new segment, click the black button Create segment in the upper right corner. Learn more about How to Build a Segment.

  1. Click the hyperlinked text Add School List below the field +Add Schools in the Academics & Extracurriculars section, then select the preferred school list(s).

  2. Edit the remaining details as desired, then click the blue button Save Segment in the upper-right corner of the page.

What is a career center?

In Handshake, schools may have multiple career centers, which employers can choose from when requesting on-campus events or interviews.

What is a career center?

A career center, also known as a college career center or career services office, is a dedicated department or resource within a university or college campus that provides a wide range of support, guidance, and resources to help students and alumni in their career development and job search efforts.

Select a career center

Events

If an on-campus event is requested, choose the career center that is hosting it from Which career center is hosting? dropdown. Learn more about How to Create an Event.

Interview schedules

When requesting an interview schedule, select the career center you want to schedule an interview with from the Career Center dropdown. Discover How to Request an Interview Schedule at a School.

Contact career services

To locate a school’s contact information in Handshake, refer to How to Contact a School.

Contacts

Add a Contact

The contacts section is a place for you to manage all of your employer relationships, even with employers that may not yet have a Handshake account.

There are three ways to add contacts to your database in Handshake:

  • Create a contact from the user’s profile
  • Create new contact details manually
  • Import Employer Contacts - best if adding contacts in bulk, most relevant during implementation

Create a contact from the user’s profile

Navigate to the user’s profile in Handshake. On the left of the profile toward the bottom, locate the Actions menu list, then click the blue button Create Contact for User.

You’ll be able to update some fields as needed on the page that loads, then click Create Contact in the lower-right of the page to save the new entry.

Note: the edits made on this page are only reflected in your contact entry, not on the user’s profile!

Once you have a contact added for the user, the profile option will update to “View Contact Details”.

Create new contact details manually

  1. Click Contacts in the left navigation bar, and click Add Contact in the upper-right corner of the page.

  2. Enter the information about this new contact in Handshake. Enter the information for the contact entry. The following fields are available for the new contact, and fields with an asterisk (*) are required:

  • Assigned to: (select an existing university staff member from the dropdown)
  • *Email address
  • *First name
  • Last name
  • Title
  • Employer
  • *Location
  • Phone (this is a free text field, format as desired)
  • Cell phone (this is a free text field, format as desired)
  • Fax
  • Description
  • Alum graduation year
  • Recruiting interests *Fields marked with an asterisk are required.

Once the required fields are completed, click on the green button Create Contact in the lower-right corner of the page.

After creating the contact, you can invite an employer to join Handshake one of two ways, either the Standard Invite Process or a Custom Invite Process.

Until they create an account, you can use their contact information to keep them up to date on university information and recruiting calendars.

Archive or Delete a Contact

If an employer contact is no longer active at their company, you may want to either archive or delete their contact entry from your Contacts list. This will remove the contacts or archive the contacts for your school’s instance on Handshake.

Contacts that are archived won’t appear as options where contacts are normally selected. They will still appear historically (e.g. Analytics reporting, past job postings/career fairs/recipients of emails, etc.).

Note: Contacts are automatically archived when the company they are connected to is either deactivated or suspended. If the company is reactivated, the contacts will be unarchived.

  • Archiving a Contact (Current Workflows)
    • Bulk Archiving Contacts
      • Bulk Unarchiving Contacts
    • Archiving Individual Contacts
      • Unarchiving Individual Contacts
  • Deleting a Contact (Current Workflow)
  • Archiving a Contact (Historical Workflow)

Archiving a Contact (Current Workflows)

Previously there wasn’t a setting to archive a contact, so we recommended career services use labels in order to archive contacts. We are leaving this workflow at the bottom of this article for reference. Please scroll down to Archiving a Contact (Historical Workflow) for more information.

First, navigate to Contacts located under Relationships in the left navigation bar.

You’ll be directed to the Contacts page. It’s important to note that there are three tabs located in the top left; Active, Archived, and All. Active will display all active, non-archived contacts. Archived will provide all archived contacts, All will display all contacts, regardless of status association.

We will be working through the Active tab for this article, except when unarchiving a contact.

Bulk archiving or unarchiving actions for contacts

Bulk Archiving Contacts

You can select all contacts by clicking the box in the top left of the page, above the list of contacts

Note: This will automatically select every contact for your school. You can deselect contacts by clicking on the box next to the contact name.

If you deselect one contact, the total selection number will decrease to 24. This indicates that only the contacts on the first page have been selected.

After you’ve selected the contacts you wish to archive, select the More button above the contacts list and select Archive.

A pop up box will display, asking if you want to confirm archiving this many contacts. You can either click Cancel to cancel the action or the Archive button to proceed with archiving the contacts:

After archiving the contacts, a message will appear at the top of the screen:

Contacts are being archived. It may take a few minutes for your contacts to update.

Refresh the page after a few minutes, and you will notice that the contacts you selected have been moved to the Archive tab.

Bulk Unarchiving Contacts

To unarchive multiple contacts at once, navigate to the Archived tab. Select the contacts you want to unarchive. Then select the More button above the contacts and select Unarchive.

A pop up box will display, asking if you want to confirm unarchiving this many contacts. You can either click Cancel to cancel the action or the Unarchive button to proceed with archiving the contacts:

After unarchiving the contacts, a message will appear at the top of the screen:

Contacts are being unarchived. It may take a few minutes for your contacts to update.

Refresh the page after a few minutes, and you will notice that the contacts you selected have been moved to the Active tab.

Archiving or unarchiving individual contacts

Archiving Individual Contacts

To archive individual contacts, start on the Active tab. Click on any contact that you’d like to archive. This will direct you to that contact’s information page.

Scroll down and on the left hand of the screen, under Actions there will be a red button to Archive contact. Click this to instantly archive the contact.

Unarchiving individual contacts

If you wish to unarchive the contact, scroll down to the Actions section of the page and click Unarchive contact.

Deleting a Contact (Current Workflow)

If you prefer to fully delete a contact entry instead, this may be done at any time. Deleted contacts may not be reinstated later, and after Analytics updates later that same day, the contact’s details will be excluded from relevant reporting moving forward.

This will only remove the contact from your institution’s Contact list. It will not impact any contact entries at other institutions in Handshake, and if the employer has a Handshake user account, their account will remain intact and unimpacted.

  • If an employer’s user account needs to be deactivated instead, this must be done by the company’s Owner or Admin – you’re welcome to share the following article with them for steps How to Deactivate or Reinstate Teammate Accounts.

  1. Click Contacts in the left navigation bar, and type the employers name that would like to delete as a contact into the search bar, then click Search.

  2. Once the contact is located, click the three lines menu to the far right in the contact entry’s row, then click Edit.

  3. Scroll to the bottom of the page and click the red button Delete, located in the lower-left corner.

Archiving a Contact (Historical Workflow)

This is the historical workflow that uses labels

Using labels ensures that the contact entry remains intact and in place on any historical content (i.e. fair registrations, events, etc.), maintaining the integrity of related reporting.

  • This workflow only impacts your institution’s contact entry, not the employer’s user account.
    • If an employer’s user account needs to be deactivated instead, this must be done by the company’s Owner or Admin – you’re welcome to share the following article with them for steps How to Deactivate or Reinstate Teammate Accounts. If you’d like to implement and use this workflow, your Career Services team should do the following:
  1. Create a dedicated label

Decide on the desired label name that you’ll use to identify “archived” contacts, then create a new Normal label in your school settings. For steps to add a label, check out School Settings: Labels.

  1. Add the label to appropriate contacts

Once the label is created, it can be added to existing contacts at any time from the Contacts page.

  • Locate the contact(s), check the box to the left of the contact name, then click on the Manage labels button above the list of contacts to proceed.
  • In the popup that appears, select the appropriate label name your team created from the dropdown menu. If many are listed, use the keyword search to narrow the displayed options. You can create a new label or choose one that already exists. Click Apply label.
  • A message will appear at the top of the screen, indicating that the label has been applied: Successfully added label to items. It may take a few minutes for your labels to update.
  1. Hide or exclude archived contact entries

After adding the label to appropriate contacts, your staff can use the filter Not Labels to hide the “archived” contact entries from view on the Contacts page or to exclude relevant contact entries from a Targeted Email.

Note: Each Career Services user using this workflow would need to perform the same steps – these filtered searches do not impact other Career Services staff members.

On the Contacts page:

  • Click on All Filters, located in the top of the page, above the Contacts list.

  • Click below Not Labels in the sidesheet to search for the label you would like to not appear in the Contacts list.

  • Once selected, click Apply and the list will auto-refresh to only display contacts without the designated label.

    • Tip: if there’s a view that your staff uses frequently, create a Saved Search with pre-set filters to save time later! For the steps, check out Create a Saved Search.

  • From here, your staff can proceed with other filters and activities as normal! In a Targeted Email:

  • In a Targeted Email draft, Step 3: Select Recipients, click on Contacts as normal, then scroll down the list of filters on the left of the page to Not Labels, and check the box next to the relevant label name.

    • If it’s not appearing in the list, use the +Add Not Labels text box for a keyword search.

  • Once selected, the recipients list will auto-refresh to only display contacts without the designated label.

    • Note: the recipient list is dynamic, so if the email is scheduled to be sent another date/time, the recipients list will include contacts that meet the selected criteria at the time the email is actually sent.

Connecting Employer Users With Their Company

Your school may have a number of employer contacts who aren’t yet using the Handshake platform, or aren’t connected to their company. Follow the steps below to learn how to ensure that employer users get connected to their companies.

To learn more about the difference between Handshake Contacts and Users, refer to Contacts vs. Users.

Inviting Employer Contacts

  • You have two options for inviting employer contacts to connect with your school
    • Use the invite link from the Contact page (recommended). Refer to Inviting Contacts to Become Users: Standard Employer Invite Process for information on this option.
    • Copy the employer invitation link from the school settings page Once you have sent this out to your contacts they will receive an email asking them to join Handshake and connect with or create their company profile
  • Using option (1) above will generate invitation emails from Handshake
  • Using option (2) will allow you to create your own employer contact invitation emails If you are inviting a small number of contacts to join the system we recommend leaving a note with a reminder for about a week in the future to check and see if the contact was able to get connected with their company

Adding a Note and a Reminder

  • Navigate to the Contacts page from the left hand navigation bar, and locate one of the contacts you have invited to join Handshake either from the list, or by searching using their name or email address. Click this to be taken to their Contact page.
  • Scroll down, and locate the blue button View & Add Notes from the left hand side of the page, under Actions.
  • Now you are able to type a note reminding yourself to check back on the contact’s user status in about one week and can also add a reminder date at the bottom to ensure that you receive a notification in Handshake when the time comes!
  • On your set date, simply navigate back to the Contacts page, locate the contact(s) you invited and filter by User Status using the list of filters across the upper part of the screen. This will allow you to see if your contact has a pending, active or has no user status. You will want to reach out in different ways depending on the user status of the contact.
  • Refer to Employer Contact User Status for more on the statuses of employer user accounts.

Contacts vs. Users

All employer related individuals with information in Handshake fall into one of two categories: Contacts or Users. Understanding the difference between a Contact and a User is important, and this article will help.

As it relates to employers, all employer users are considered staff members, so these terms are used interchangeably.

Please note: A Company Profile may or may not have staff members connected. A school can create a Company Profile, so there may be no staff members. Likewise, an employer may leave a Company Profile, leaving the profile without any staff members.

Contacts

  • Contacts are added to Handshake via one of three methods:
    • a bulk upload
    • manually added by a Career Services Staff Member
    • automatically added through user account interaction with your school on Handshake (attending a career fair, posting a job, connecting with your school)
  • Contacts can be thought of as a virtual address book. They may be employers, community partners, career service, etc.
  • Contacts are accessed using the Left Hand Navigation Bar (Relationships → Contacts).
  • Each contact must have (at least) a first name, last name, and email address. A wide variety of other information, including notes and labels, can also be added to a contact.
  • A contact (unless they are also a user) does not have the ability to log on to, use, or have direct interaction with the Handshake platform. Although the contact does not use the platform directly, content from Handshake can be sent to contacts via email.
    • For example, an employer contact (who does not have his own Handshake user account) can be listed on a job and then receive applications to that job via email.
  • Contacts can be archived by your school.
  • A contact can also be a user. The two profiles will be linked in Handshake as long as the same email address is used for both their contact record and their user account.
  • The contact source identifies the initial creation or interaction the contact had with your school. For more information on the contact source, please refer to FAQs About Contacts. Here is an example of a contact profile:

Users

  • A contact can also be a user.
  • A user can have multiple contact entries in Handshake – one at each of the schools they work with.
  • All Handshake users have a username (email address) and password. Users may be students, alumni, employers (staff members), or Career Services Center staff members.
  • Handshake users are able to actively use the platform. Employer and Career Services users may have limited access based on roles (permissions) assigned.
  • All users can access their Profile using the left-hand navigation bar.
  • Career Services Center staff are able to see Handshake activity from all users.
  • Career Services Center staff cannot archive user accounts. Only the company itself can archive user accounts. Here is an example of a user profile:

To learn about how to invite a Contact to become a User, read Inviting Contacts to Become Users (Employer Invite Process)

Employer Contact User Status

If you would like to know the status of an employer users account, this article will assist in that!

Note: all employers in Handshake are considered a contact, but some employers are considered users if they’ve created an account and have a profile. For more information on employer contacts vs. users, refer to Contacts vs. Users.

Topics:

  • User statuses in Handshake
  • Filtering by status

User Statuses in Handshake

  • Active: the contact has an active Handshake employer user profile.
    • When you open the contact and click View User Profile you will be directed to their user profile.
    • You can reach out to them directly with a message in Handshake!
  • None: the contact does not have an employer user profile in Handshake associated with the email currently listed within your contact list.
    • When you open the contact, you will not have the option to View User Profile, as Contacts that have this status have not yet started the Handshake registration process.
    • To invite a contact to become a user, refer to Inviting Contacts to Become Users: Standard Employer Invite Process.
    • If it has been a few weeks since you invited this contact to join Handshake you may want to reach out again with an invitation email.
  • Pending: the contact has created a profile, but has not confirmed their email address or has not been approved with their company.
    • If the user has not confirmed their email, the Email Status on their profile will state Not confirmed Yet.
    • If the user has confirmed their email, but has not requested to join a Company, the Company Status on their user profile will state No Request Exists, while the Email Status reflects they are Confirmed/Active.
    • If the user has confirmed their email, and is currently awaiting to be approved by the Companies page owner, the Company Status on the users profile will state Pending Staff Member Approval At (Company Name). To help connect a user to their company, refer to Supporting Your Employers: Helping Employer Users Connect with a Company Profile.
  • Archived: this contact’s user account has been archived and they no longer have access to login (this may be due to them leaving their company).

List Contacts by Status

You can also filter your contacts by their User Status in Handshake. This tool is helpful if you want to invite your Contacts to create user profiles in Handshake!

Click Contacts on the left navigation bar. On the top left of the next page, three tabs will be available for use; Active, Archived, and All.

Click on any of the respective tabs to display a list of contacts with that status. The All tab will display all contacts.

FAQs About Contacts

If you are interested in learning more about Contacts in Handshake, we’ve created this resource to help address many of the questions you may have!

  • How do I know which companies do not have a contact at my institution?
    • Use this report link below to analyze which employers are approved but do not have a contact linked to your institution: app.joinhandshake.com
  • How do I make a user a contact at my institution?
    • Navigate to that user’s account and click the blue Create Contact for User button, located under the Actions section. For additional information, refer to Add a Contact.
  • Can I invite a contact to become a user?
    • Yes! If you would like to invite a contact to create an employer profile, refer to Inviting Contacts to Become Users: Standard Employer Invite Process or Inviting Contacts to Become Users: Custom Employer Invite Process.
  • Is a contact created for the employer that posts a job to our school?
    • Yes, although, this depends on how the employer posts the job to your school. If the employer selects your school specifically to post the job to, a contact will be created for the person that posted the job, provided that there isn’t a contact created for them already. However, if the employer posts the job to all schools in their network, a contact will not be created for them. We want to keep information streamlined and easy to track, and this is a step towards that. You’re more than welcome to create a contact for them if you’d wish to!
  • How does the source field get populated?
    • Blank: This contact was imported with a CSV upload.
    • Requested Approval: These contacts have requested to be an approved employer at your school. All of the contacts at an employer will not be created when that employer requests approval, only the specific user who requests connection.
    • Alum: This contact has identified themselves as an alum of your school during creation of their user account.
    • Attended Career Fair: This contact was added to a career fair registration at your school.
    • Posted Event: This contact has posted an event to which you were invited.
    • Posted Interview: This contact was listed as a requestor on an interview schedule at your school.
    • Posted Job: This contact was listed as a contact on a job that was posted at your school.
    • Attended Interview: This contact was listed as a contact on an interview schedule at your school.
  • Can I filter contacts by the source field?
    • Yes you can! Click All Filters on the Contacts list page and use the Source section to filter based on how the contact was populated on Handshake.
  • If the contact has completed more than one of the source actions, how will it be displayed?
    • The source will be the first way in which this contact has interacted with your school within Handshake.
  • What is the difference between Source = Alumni and filtering on Other “Alumni Contacts”?
    • When an employer signs up for Handshake and selects your school as their Alma Mater, they are automatically added to your contact list with the Source populated as Alumni. If your school happens to create/import a contact for this individual prior to them creating an account, and you indicate that they are an Alum during that creation process, that is what populates the “Alumni contacts” filter, located in All Filters.
  • Can I filter contacts based on employer labels?
    • Yes you can! Click All Filters on the Contacts list page and use the Employer labels section to filter based on labels applied to the employer’s company profile. For more information, refer to Filter Contacts: Employer Labels.
  • Can I email contacts in Handshake?
    • Yes! Refer to How to Email Contacts in Handshake for more information.

Filter Contacts: Employer Labels

Handshake is excited to announce the ability to filter Contacts based on labels applied to the employer’s company profile!

Note: If you’re using a certain Employer Label to indicate archived contacts, there is an updated workflow for archiving contacts. Please refer to Archive or Delete a Contact for more information.

To filter these contacts, click Filters

Then search for the label you’d like to filter on by clicking on the box below Employer Label and selecting Apply.

FAQs

  • I filtered on the Employer Label name and opened the contact, but I’m not seeing the Employer Label appear.
    • This is expected; the only label names that will appear on the contact entry are the labels your school has applied to that particular contact. You’ll need to open the employers company profile to manage applied Employer Labels.
  • Can I apply a label to the employer’s company profile from the contacts page?
    • No, you will only be able to filter on labels that are already applied to the company profile.

Filter Contacts: Last Login Date

We’ve added an option to filter contacts on their last login date. The feature will apply to contacts that are connected to user accounts. If you’d like to read more about the difference between Contacts and User accounts, please review the following article: Contacts vs. Users.

Topics:

  • Filtering on Last Login Date
  • Alternative workflow: All Filters

Filtering on Last Login Date

  • Navigate to contacts using the left navigation bar. Note: There is a new column on this page which indicates the Last Login date, you can use this column to identify when the contact last logged in.

  • Select the filter at the top of the page titled “Last Login”

  • Select the dropdown menu to choose from the following options:

  • Never logged in

  • In past 2 weeks

  • In past month

  • In past 3 months

  • In past 6 months

  • In past 12 months

  • More than 12 months ago

  • After choosing the filter, choose the blue button Apply Filters:

  • You’ll be provided a list of contacts with user accounts that have logged in within the selected time period.

Alternative workflow: All Filters

Alternatively, you can select All Filters and choose the login range there, before selecting the blue button Apply Filters.

Filter Contacts: Third Party Recruiters

When an employer registers for Handshake, they need to specify whether they are a Third Party Recruiter or not. Career Services users have the ability to view and filter on this status in the Contacts list. This can help you make sure you are targeting the correct contacts in your employer outreach.

  • Note: if the employer individual isn’t listed as a contact at your school, they will not be included in this list. For more information on how to add a contact, refer to Add a Contact.

  1. Click Contacts from the left navigation bar in Handshake for a full list of contacts.

  2. Click All Filters.

  3. This will bring up the filters side sheet. Choose Third Party Recruiters and click the blue button Apply Filters to filter on Third Party Recruiter contacts.

This will return a list of all your school’s contacts in Handshake who have identified themselves as third party recruiters during the Handshake registration process.

  • Note: if someone should be registered as a third party recruiter and they are not, they can reach out to our Support Team. They’ll be prompted to agree to our Third Party Recruiter Guidelines, and upon doing so, our Support Team will update their account to indicate they are a Third Party Recruiter. For more information and our guidelines, refer to Third Party Recruiters in Handshake.

How to Email Contacts in Handshake

With Handshake, it’s easy to keep in touch with your contacts via Targeted Emails.

You can select contacts as recipients via two methods:

  • after composing a new Targeted Email, when selecting recipients
    • described in Targeted Emails: Creating and Sending
  • from the Contacts page
    • described in this article Note: If you’d like to initiate an email to job creators or contacts specifically, refer to How to Send an Email to Job Contacts.

How to Email Contacts in Handshake from the Contacts page

  1. Click Contacts from the left navigation bar, under the “Relationships” heading.

  2. Put a check next to the desired contacts listed on this page. Use the filters or All filters above the contacts list to narrow down the displayed results.

  3. Select More above the contacts list and then select Draft Targeted Email.

  4. A confirmation will pop up with the number of selected contacts. Click the blue button Go to Targeted Emails to proceed.

  5. This will open a new Targeted Email draft. Proceed through the steps of creating and sending a Targeted Email, as described in Targeted Emails: Creating and Sending.

Note: if you add an Event or Career Fair that’s listed as “hidden” or “invite-only” via the Handshake Content option, this will allow students and employers to bypass those settings and view/register as if they had the public preview link.

  1. The recipients tab will display the preselected contact email addresses–click Next to finalise the details and send.

Learn more about tracking recipient activities (like opens and clicks) in Targeted Email: Performance Overview.

Inviting Contacts to Become Users: Custom Employer Invite Process

This resource outlines how to send a customized invite email followup to your employer contacts.

Most institutions will:

  • Send a “heads up” email about the upcoming switch to Handshake to their employers, typically in an external email or via prior system
    • We have some sample language available in Implementation: Invite Email Examples.
  • Send a bulk invite as outlined in Inviting Contacts to Become Users: Standard Employer Invite Process. If you would like to follow up the standard invite with additional custom invite instructions, follow the steps below.

1. Copy the Unique Employer Approval Request URL

​1. Click your name in the upper-right corner of Handshake, then click School Settings.

  1. The Details page will load by default–scroll down toward the bottom of the page, and copy the Employer Approval Request URL.

This link will provide employers with a direct link to connect with your institution when they register.

2. Embed the URL in an email to contacts

Follow the steps in How to Email Contacts in Handshake to generate and send the email to your contacts.

Tip: use a call to action Button in your email to share your employer approval link!

You might want to use content similar to that outlined below:

Example Language for Inviting Employer Contacts :

Greetings!

On behalf of [Institution Name] I am excited to invite you to join Handshake - a powerful, modern platform that enables employers to search for and manage relationships with top talent at institutions across the country.

By using the registration link below, we will help you connect with your organization and begin using Handshake for your recruiting at [Institution Name] and other institutions.

[LINK COPIED FROM THE SCHOOL SETTINGS]

Thanks, and welcome to Handshake!

[Institution Name / Sign off]

Reference these articles to learn more about the Employer invite and approval process during implementation:

  • Best Practices for Employer Approvals

  • Implementation Invite Email Examples To assist any employers who are having difficulties signing up or connecting to their company, please reference this article:

Inviting Contacts to Become Users: Standard Employer Invite Process

Individuals who are included in Handshake as Contacts, but not Users, cannot engage with your students, post jobs or request interviews, until they have an account on Handshake AND get approved by your institution.

To learn more about the differences between Handshake Contacts and Users, refer to Contacts vs. Users.

Inviting your employer contacts to become Handshake users is the fastest way to proactively get employers to connect with your institution and maximise the benefits of your student-employer relationships.

Note: If the invited contact has a user profile attached to it, and the user is approved by a company, the employer invite will automatically approve them at that institution. If the contact does NOT have a user profile attached to it, they will be prompted to sign up for Handshake and connect or create their company. From there, they will have to find the institution and request to recruit there.

Inviting Contacts

  1. Click Contacts on the left-hand navigation bar. This will bring up the list of all your contacts.
  • At this point you can invite ALL your contacts, or select individual checkboxes or use filters to narrow down who you’re inviting. You can even invite one user if you’d like.

  1. Once you’ve selected the desired contacts, select More and then select Invite employer contacts from the dropdown.

  2. A pop-up will appear summarising the total number of contacts invited. Click Invite employer contacts if you are satisfied with the count of invites to be sent.

Note: If you have not set your institution’s default employer approval setting when you created your institution profile, you will receive a pop-up notification reminding you to do so before sending out your bulk email invite. By taking this proactive step, all contacts, when they create an account in Handshake, will automatically send an approval request to connect with you. If approved, they will be granted the default permissions (roles) at your university. To learn more about how to set your institution’s default employer approval settings, refer to Institution Settings: Default Employer Approval Preferences.

  1. Once you’ve confirmed, you’ll be taken to a page that displays a summary (including a demographic breakdown) of your bulk invite.

  2. Click the blue button Send under Actions in the lower left corner of the screen. This will bring you to a page showing updated invitation demographics and employer actions taken.

After sending the invitation, one of three things will occur for each contact:

  1. Contacts without a Handshake account will receive an email invite to create an account on Handshake and to join your institution.

  2. Contacts with an account on Handshake, but not associated with your institution, will automatically be approved at your institution and granted your default permissions.

  3. Contacts with an account on Handshake who are connected with your institution will not get an email at all.

Pro-tip: Apply a label to invited contacts

A good way to keep track of which contacts have been previously invited is to apply a label to those contacts. You can create a label for the invite date, i.e. “invited 10/18/19”, then apply it to contacts invited on that day.

You can use this label as a filter on the Manage Contacts page as well as in the Contacts Explore in Insights.

Viewing past Bulk Invites

To view your bulk invites at anytime, click on your name in the upper-right corner of your screen, then click on Institution Settings. From the menu on the left of this page, click Bulk Invites.

From this page, you can open up the invites to view employer actions taken, including how many employers were approved.

Contact Invite Emails

The same basic content is included in all invite emails, however, the text on the button will change depending on the status of the user in Handshake.

  • If Handshake does not recognise the user’s email, we will ask them to create an account.
  • If Handshake recognises the user’s email and sees that they are connected to a company, the invite will automatically add your institution to the employer’s list of institutions and approve the company (if it has not already been approved).

Linking Contacts and Users

When an employer user updates the following fields on their profile, they will also be updated on any associated contact record that exists:

  • First Name
  • Last Name
  • Email Address
  • Title
  • Employer name
  • Bio (Description on the contact)

Managing Notes on Contacts

To help keep track of information regarding different contacts, we offer the Notes feature on Handshake. You can use notes to notify other staff members, keep notes for yourself, set reminders for later dates, and more.

Add a note to a contact

  1. Click Contacts on the left hand navigation bar

  2. Select the contact you’d like to add notes to

  3. Click the black button View & Add Notes under the Actions section

  4. In the pop up, you can enter a message for the note. You can also Set a Reminder and select a date from the calendar pop up. Click the Add Note button, to add the note to this contact.

Note: if you’d like to tag a staff member directly, you can add a “+” sign, followed by their email address to tag them. Example: +ted.brown@sol.edu

You can also use the Share with Staff button to select whether this note is accessible for other staff members, just yourself, or for a specific career center at your school.

Editing or Deleting a Note

  1. After you’ve added a note, in the same pop up, you can click the pencil icon to edit or delete the note

  2. If you’ve made changes, click the Update button on the right hand side to update the note. If you wish to delete the note, click the red trash bin icon in the upper-right corner.

Importing Notes

Refer to Importing Notes to learn more about bulk importing notes.

Create & Edit Job Postings

About Job Roles and Job Role Groups (Employers)

Handshake provides more than 380 Job Role groups, identified by our team using data such as career interests, majors, user research, and job details.

One of the strongest predictors of whether a student will apply for a job is their preferred job role. In Handshake, students can choose which role groups they are interested in, and relevant job postings are highlighted for them.

We can help students find the jobs that best match their interests and make sure the right students view your jobs by automatically identifying the most appropriate roles for your jobs.

Tip: Download the attachment at the bottom of this article to view the complete list of job role groups and their mapping.

Automated job role tagging

Handshake automatically adds the appropriate job role group to your job posting based on your job description and title.

  • To learn how to add or remove job roles from your job posting, refer to How to Post a Job.

Job role groups

For a complete list of job role groups, download the attachment on this article. The first tab in the file contains the names of the job role groups. In the second tab, each group name is mapped to over 8,600 job roles.

The job roles taxonomy is based on the Bureau of Labor Statistics’ (BLS’) Standard Occupation Classification (SOC). Almost all of our job role groups map to one or a few of the SOC’s occupations.

A few changes have been made to the SOC’s taxonomy to meet the needs of our student base. For example, we added the “Product Managers” role group.

If a specific job role group is not available, contact Support.

On-campus employment best practices

We’ve received feedback regarding how these roles align with on-campus opportunities, so we’ve put together some examples that may help on-campus employers better identify some common positions:

  • For office assistant, data entry, or any other clerical type positions: Office and Administrative Support Workers
  • For “Fundraising & Event Management” related positions: Fundraisers or Meeting, Convention, and Event Planners
  • For any research-related roles: University Student Researchers

Add an Attachment to a Job

You can attach documents to a job posting after it’s been created to give applicants more context before they apply.

Your ability to add or edit attachments depends on your employer account type and whether you created the job.

  • Basic employers: Owners and Recruiters can only add attachments to jobs they have personally created. Jobs posted by teammates will appear as view-only and cannot be modified.
    • To add attachments to jobs you did not create, you must upgrade to an eligible paid plan.
  • On-campus employers, Plus, Pro, Essentials and TES customers: All users, except Representatives, can add attachments to any job posting, whether created by themselves or a teammate, provided they have the appropriate permissions. If you have not yet posted a job, and would like to, refer to How to Post a Job.

Add an attachment

  1. Click Jobs from the left navigation bar, then select the job you want to add an attachment to.

  2. The job posting page will load–click the Job details tab, in the upper-middle section of the page.

  3. Click the white button Edit attachments in the Attachments section to the right of the page.

  4. Click the New Attachment tab in the upper-right corner of the page.

  5. Enter the name of the file in the Name field, then click the gray button Choose file to upload the desired file.

  6. Once the file is uploaded, click the green button Create Attachment.

  7. The message “Attachment was successfully created” will display in a green banner at the top of the page.

  8. The attachment will begin to process, and display the message “Attachment processing (refresh for updates).

  • Refresh the webpage. If the file is processed, it will display on the page as it was uploaded.
  • Teammates may click the blue button Download to download the file.
  • To edit the file while it’s uploaded, click the white button Edit and repeat the steps above.

Can I Pause or Put a Job Posting on Hold?

Handshake does not currently support pausing or putting a job posting on hold.

To temporarily stop receiving applications, you can close the job posting. When you’re ready to accept applications again, you may update the close date to reopen it.

  • Closed jobs can be reopened for up to 30 days after closing.
  • When reopened, the job is resubmitted for approval by each school where it was originally posted.
  • Applications submitted before the job was closed remain accessible on the posting.
    • Basic employers: Applicant data remains visible for 30 days after a job is closed. To view applicant data beyond this period, you must upgrade to an eligible paid plan.
    • On-campus employers, Plus, Pro, Essentials and TES customers: All users, except Representatives, retain unlimited access to view and manage applicants. Have questions about closing a job? Read more about how to Close a Job Posting.

Can I Remove Schools from a Job Posting?

After posting a job on Handshake, you may realize you have selected more schools than intended.

While there is not a way to remove individual schools from a job posting, you can still refine where your job is posted.

To ensure your job reaches the right schools, follow the steps below in the order provided.

If you need to edit other details of your job posting, refer to How to Edit a Job Posting.

Access job posting

Click Jobs from the left navigation bar, then select the job you want to remove a school(s) from.

Close job

  1. On the job posting page, click the three-dot menu icon in the upper-right corner, then select Close job from the dropdown.

Note: Because jobs cannot be removed from individual schools, you’ll need to close the job before making any changes.

  1. In the pop-up modal, click the black button Close job to confirm that you want to close the job at all schools.

  2. After closing the job, you will be redirected to the Overview tab on the job posting page.

Note: If the page does not display a closed date, refresh the page.

Duplicate job

On the job posting page, click the three-dot menu icon in the upper right corner of the page, then select Duplicate job from the dropdown.

Tip: Before posting the new job posting, double-check your school selections to avoid extra steps.

To complete the process, refer to the steps in How to Duplicate a Job Posting.

Access applicants

After closing a job posting, you can still access all applicant information. The job post will remain available, allowing you to review applications as needed.

Learn more about Reviewing Applications in Handshake.

Definitions: Job Position Types

On Handshake, you can select from various position types to enhance clarity, attract the right candidates, and streamline the recruitment process.

While we are aware that employers or schools use job types in different ways, these are our overall Handshake definitions for most use cases.

Discover How to Post a Job.

Position types

Job

Paid employment, typically long-term or permanent.

Internship

A professional learning experience that offers practical work related to career interest, typically for a limited time.

On campus student employment

A job or internship that takes place at an institution.

Cooperative Education

A partnership with an institution that provides students with work experience to complement their in-class training.

Experiential learning

Also known as an externship, a partnership with an institution that provides students with work experience typically for academic credit.

Fellowship

A funded, short-term opportunity focused on professional or academic development.

Graduate school

Advanced learning opportunity beyond a bachelor’s degree.

Volunteer

Unpaid work toward a mission or cause.

Federal Work- Study (could apply to multiple job types)

A federally funded part-time job or internship for eligible students.

Delete an Attachment on a Job

You can remove attachments from a job posting at any time to ensure applicants only see the most relevant and up-to-date information.

Your ability to delete attachments depends on your employer account type and whether you created the job.

  • Basic employers: Owners and Recruiters can delete attachments only from job postings they have personally created. Jobs created by teammates are view-only and cannot be modified.
    • To delete attachments from jobs you did not create, you must upgrade to an eligible paid plan.
  • On-campus employers, Plus, Pro, Essentials and TES customers: All users, except Representatives, can delete attachments from any job posting, whether created by themselves or a teammate, provided they have the appropriate permissions. To learn how to add a new attachment instead, refer to Add an Attachment to a Job.

Delete an attachment

  1. Click Jobs from the left navigation bar, then select the job you want to delete an attachment from.

  2. The job posting page will load–click the Job details tab, in the upper-middle section of the page.

  3. Click the white button Edit attachments in the Attachments section to the right of the page.

  4. Locate the attachment you want to delete, then click the white button Edit to the right of the attachment.

  5. On the attachment page, click the red button Delete below the Document field.

  • Make sure that you are editing the correct document before you click to delete.
  • Deleted attachments cannot be retrieved. We recommend saving the file to your computer if you need a copy.
  1. Once deleted, the message “Attachment was successfully destroyed” will appear in a green banner at the top of the page.

How to Duplicate a Job Posting

You can duplicate a job posting to quickly create a new version that carries over all the original details and settings. Previous applicants and school approvals will not be included in the duplicate.

Your ability to duplicate a job depends on your employer account type and whether you created the original posting.

  • Basic employers: Owners and Recruiters can only duplicate jobs they have personally created. Jobs posted by teammates will appear as view-only and cannot be duplicated.
    • To duplicate jobs you did not create, you must upgrade to an eligible paid plan.
    • On-campus employers, Plus, Pro, Essentials and TES customers: All users, except Representatives, can duplicate any job posting, including those created by teammates, provided they have the appropriate permissions. To learn how to close an existing job instead, refer to Close a Job Posting.

When a job can be duplicated

A job can be duplicated under any of the following conditions:

  • The job is closed.
  • The job is still open, and its opening date is within the past year, but the closing date is more than a year after the opening date.
  • The job is still open, and its opening date is over a year ago, while the closing date is more than a year after the opening date.

Duplicate a job posting

  1. Click Jobs from the left navigation bar.

  2. Locate the job posting you want to duplicate and click the three-dot menu icon at the end of the job posting row.

Tip: Use the Status or Division filter to quickly find jobs by posting status or team.

Note: If the original job was connected to an interview schedule, that link will not be preserved. To link an interview schedule to the new job, you’ll need to request a new schedule.

  1. Select Duplicate from the dropdown.
  • Alternatively, you may click the three-dot menu icon in the upper-right corner of the job posting page, then select Duplicate job.
  1. You will be redirected to the job form.
  • All original job details will be pre-filled.
  1. We strongly recommend reviewing all of the sections before you post the job.

Some key areas to review are:

  • Job title: To avoid confusion with the original, consider updating the title.
  • Schools: Add only the schools you want to post this job to.
    • Not ready to post yet? Click Save as draft in the upper-right corner to return to it later
  • Application open & close date: Review and update the default dates as needed.

  1. Once you are ready, click the black button Post job in the lower-right corner of the page.

  2. Your request will be sent to the selected schools for review. Read more in Understanding Job Posting Approvals.

Applicants

When you duplicate a job posting, the duplicate is treated as a new job posting. All eligible students can apply.

This includes students who applied to the original posting unless you adjust the qualifications or choose different schools for the new version.

How to Edit a Job Posting

You can edit a job post after it has been created, including fields like the application open and close dates to tailor the post to your specific needs.

Your ability to edit a job posting also depends on your employer account type and whether you created the job.

  • Basic employers: Owners and Recruiters can only edit jobs they have personally created. Jobs posted by other teammates will appear in your job list as view-only and cannot be edited.

    • To edit jobs you did not create, you must upgrade to an eligible paid plan.

  • On-campus employers, Plus, Pro, Essentials and TES customers: All users, except Representatives, can edit both their own job postings and those created by teammates, provided they have the appropriate permissions. The Job details tab will not be editable if:

  • The job closed more than 30 days ago, or

  • The job has been open for more than 365 days In these cases, you will need to duplicate the job to create a new, editable version.

  • How to Duplicate a Job Posting

  • Close a Job Posting

Edit the job details

The Job details tab contains the job form where you can edit fields such as title, description, qualifications, and application details.

  1. Click Jobs from the left navigation bar, then locate the job posting you want to edit.

  2. Click the More options menu (three dots) to the right of the job posting, then select Edit from the dropdown.

  3. On the Job details tab, click the pencil icon to the far right of the section(s) you want to edit.

  • Edits made to a job will be reflected at all schools where it is posted.

  • Fields that cannot be edited will appear grayed out and disabled. Editable fields include:

  • Job description

  • Job title

  • Position type

  • Location type

  • Schedule

  • Employment duration

  • Expected pay

  • Additional compensation

  • Benefits

  • Perks

  • Additional benefits

  • Job role groups

  • Work authorization

  • Skills

  • Degree level

  • School year

  • Latest graduation date

  • Major groups

  • Minimum GPA

  • Application open range

  • Number of hires

  • How will candidates submit applications?

  • Additional required documents on Handshake

  • Company division

  • Job owner

    • Note: Only on-campus employers and Premium partners can update the job owner. Fields that cannot be edited include:

  • Screening questions, if the job has already received applicants

  • Application duration

    • Basic employers cannot edit the default application duration range
    • On-campus employers and Premium Partners cannot edit:
      • Application open date, if the date is in the past
      • Application close date, if the new date extends the posting beyond one year from the application open date. If you need to change a restricted field, you will need to duplicate the job posting and create a new one. Learn more about How to Duplicate a Job Posting.
  1. After the changes are made, click the black button Save in the upper-right corner of the page.

5.The message ‘Job saved’ will display in a banner at the top of the page.

Edit the schools a job is posted to

The Schools section specifies the schools where a job posting is visible to students. The process for editing schools differs depending on whether the job was posted manually or through an XML feed.

  • Manually posted jobs: Employers may add a job to additional schools after it has been created. Learn How to Post a Job to Additional Schools.
  • XML feed jobs: Jobs posted via XML are sent only to schools where the employer is auto-approved. Employers cannot currently select or customize the list of schools.
    • These jobs may also be subject to school-specific criteria and may require additional approval.
    • For an overview of the Handshake XML job feed, refer to A Guide to Handshake XML Job Feed. Once a job has been created, schools cannot be removed from the posting, regardless of whether the job was posted manually or through an XML feed. For additional details, refer to Can I Remove Schools from a Job Posting?.

How to Request to Add a New Job Role Group

When creating a job, job roles are added to categorize your job, which helps surface it to the right candidates.

If the category you are looking for is not available, contact our Support team to request that it be added.

Note: Before requesting a new role, review About Job Roles and Job Role Groups (Employers). The article includes a job role group mapping at the bottom of the page. Review the file to confirm that the job role group does not already exist.

Request a new job role group

  1. Start a chatbot conversation from this article’s page:

  • Click Contact Support in the black header at the top of the page

  • Or

  • Click the green message bubble icon in the lower-right corner Once the chatbot opens:

  • Select your primary user type:

    • “An employer”, or
    • “In career services or IT” (if you work for one of our partner schools)

  1. In the chat window, type the phrase “New Job Role Group Request”, then press Enter or Return on your keyboard to send the message.

  2. You will be prompted to provide additional details about your request, including the specific job role(s) you want to add, as well as the job title and description.

Tip: Providing more context will help our Product team review your request more effectively.

  1. After you respond, the chatbot will prompt you to contact support. To create a support ticket, type “yes.” A new ticket will be created for our Support team, and you’ll receive a copy of your chat transcript by email.

Job role request status

Each request will be reviewed, and final decisions will be made by our Product team. If new job role groups are added, they will be highlighted in our Updates.

Manage your Job Drafts

You can return to incomplete job postings at any time to review, complete, and publish them when you’re ready.

Your ability to view and edit draft job postings depends on your employer account type and whether you created the job.

  • Basic employers: Owners and Recruiters can only view and complete drafts they have personally created. Drafts created by teammates will appear in your job list as view-only and cannot be edited.
    • To manage drafts created by teammates, you must upgrade to an eligible paid plan.
  • On-campus employers, Plus, Pro, Essentials and TES customers: All users, except Representatives, can access and complete drafts created by themselves or teammates, provided they have the appropriate permissions. To check the status of all your job postings, including drafts, refer Navigating the Jobs Page.

Topics:

  • Access your job drafts
  • Manage your job drafts
    • View drafts

Access your job drafts

Click Jobs from the left navigation bar, then click the white button View drafts.

  • Only job postings that were saved as a draft are listed.
  • If the draft is not listed, more than likely, the job was not saved properly.

Manage your job drafts

View drafts

On the Drafts page, you can view job postings created by you or your teammates.

Click the white button Job owner, then select:

Delete a draft
