Posting Personal, Babysitter, Household, or Caretaker Jobs

On Handshake, employers can post personal-type jobs. These roles typically include babysitting, caretaking, tutoring, and similar opportunities.

Personal jobs are well suited for students seeking supplemental income with flexible schedules that fit around other commitments.

To post a personal job, create an employer account using a personal or generic email address. Read more about Registering for an Employer Account with a Generic Email Address.

Guidelines

Employers must meet the following requirements to post a personal job on Handshake:

  • Register your employer account using a generic or personal email address.
  • If you are already connected to a company on Handshake, you may create a secondary employer account to post personal jobs. Learn How to Create a New Company Profile.
  • Personal jobs may not be posted under an existing company page, including the company where you are currently employed.
  • List a personal Facebook or LinkedIn profile as your company website.
  • A college website may be used only if instructed by the school where the job will be posted.
  • Use “LASTNAME Family” or a similar format as your company profile name. Note: Even when posting personal jobs, employers must complete the standard verification process. This includes providing a business registration number, such as an EIN, TIN, or local equivalent, and uploading a photo of a government-issued ID.

If you do not have a business registration number, contact Support. Learn more about our Employer Validation

Best practices

  • Review the recruiting policies of each school before posting a personal job to ensure the role meets the school’s guidelines and expectations.
  • If recruiting policies are not available or clarification is needed, contact the school’s career services office by phone or email.
  • Keep in mind that each school independently approves or declines employer connection requests and may use different criteria when reviewing personal job postings.
  • Fully complete the company profile to improve trust and visibility. Learn how to Create a High Quality Employer Profile.

Updating Job Posting Closing Dates

To extend or renew a job posting in Handshake, the job must have an open and close date within one year of each other. Use this article to extend or renew a job posting so you can continue connecting with candidates.

Who can update closing dates

Your ability to update a closing date depends on your account type and whether you created the job:

  • Basic employers: You can only update closing dates for jobs you personally created. Jobs created by teammates are view-only. To update closing dates for jobs created by teammates, upgrade to an eligible paid plan.
  • On-campus employers, Plus, Pro, Essentials, and Enterprise (formerly TES) customers: All users except Representatives can update closing dates on their own postings and those created by teammates, provided they have the appropriate permissions. How to extend an active job posting

  1. Click Jobs from the left navigation bar, then select the job you want to extend.

  2. Click the Job details tab and navigate to the Application process section.

  3. Click the gray Edit button to the right of the Application process section.

  4. Choose your extension option based on your account type:

  • Basic employers: Click 30 days to extend the posting by 30 days. Basic employers can only extend in 30-day increments. Repeat until the one-year limit from the original open date is reached. Once the limit is reached, duplicate the posting instead.
  • On-campus employers, Plus, Pro, Essentials, and Enterprise customers: Click 30 days to extend by 30 days, or click Custom to set a specific close date.
    • If using Custom, click the calendar icon in Close date field, select a date, then click Apply. The close date can only be extended up to one year from the original open date.
  1. Click the black Save button in the upper-right corner. The posting will immediately update with the new close date.

Note: Job postings automatically close at 11:59 PM in your time zone on the date you select.

How to renew a closed job posting

Jobs can only be renewed if less than one year has passed since the original open date.

The following conditions also apply to all account types before renewing a closed posting:

  • The job must have been closed within the last 30 days. If more than 30 days have passed, you cannot renew the posting; instead, duplicate it to create a new one. Learn How to Duplicate a Job Posting.
  • The posting must not have been open for more than one year from the original open date. If the one-year limit has been reached, duplicate the posting instead.
To renew a closed posting:

  1. Click Jobs from the left navigation bar, then use the Status filter to select Closed.

  2. Select the job you want to renew.

  3. On the job’s overview page, click the white Edit close date button.

  4. Navigate to the Application process section and click the gray Edit button.

  5. Choose your renewal option based on your account type:

  • Basic employers: Click 30 days to renew the posting by 30 days. Repeat in 30-day increments until the one-year limit is reached.
  • On-campus employers, Plus, Pro, Essentials, and Enterprise customers: Click 30 days to renew by 30 days, or click Custom to set a specific close date.
    • If using Custom, click the calendar icon in the Close date field, select a date, then click Apply.

  1. Click the black Save button in the upper-right corner.

  2. The job posting will be resubmitted for approval. Refer to Understanding Job Posting Approvals.

Note: Job postings automatically close at 11:59 PM in your time zone on the date you select.

Create & Manage Fair Registrations

Adding a Representative to an Existing Career Fair Registration

You can add representatives to an existing career fair registration as long as the registration period is still open.

Important limitations:

  • You cannot change the total number of representatives included in the registration.
  • If you need to increase the representative count, contact the Career Fair Point of Contact.
  • This process is not supported for virtual fairs. Virtual fairs automatically include up to 100 representatives.

Add a representative to an existing fair registration

1.Click Fairs from the left navigation bar, then locate the registration you want to add a representative to.

To access your registration, refer to How to View/Edit a Career Fair Registration.

  1. Navigate to the Representatives section on the Edit tab of the registration form.

Note: If the registration period has closed, you will not be able to make edits. Contact the Career Fair Point of Contact for assistance.

  1. In the Names of Representatives Attending this Session field, click into the search bar and select the user you want to add from the list of available users.

Tip: Type in the name of the teammate(s) in the search bar to quickly locate the teammate you’d like to add.

If Representative does not appear in search

  1. If the teammate you want to add does not appear in the list, click Create it here below the search bar.

  2. In the pop up modal, enter the user’s details and click the blue Create Contact button.

The following fields are required:

  • Email
  • First name Once the contact is created, search for the new contact in the search bar and add them as a representative.

Update registration

When finished, click the blue Update Registration button in the lower-right corner of the registration form.

Error messages

If the error message “The number of contacts must not be greater than the requested representative count” appears, the registration already includes the maximum number of representatives allowed. Contact the Career Fair Point of Contact to request an increase.

Canceling a Career Fair Registration

If you need to cancel your registration for a career fair, you’ll need to reach out directly to the school hosting the event.

While cancellations can’t be managed in Handshake, each career fair includes a point of contact provided by the school.

Cancel a registration

  1. In Handshake, click Fairs from the left navigation bar, then locate the fair you want to cancel.

Tip: Use the Show Registered Only filter to quickly find fairs you’ve already registered for.

  1. On the fair’s Details page, scroll to the Contact person section.

  2. Use the listed name and email address to reach out to the school’s point of contact and request cancellation.

How to Pay for a Career Fair Registration

This resource will provide the steps on how to pay for an invoice you have received for a career fair registration.

Before you can pay for a career fair

To submit a payment for a career fair registration, the following must be true:

  • The registration payment status must be Invoiced.
  • You must have a role other than Representative.
    • If you do not have access, contact your company’s Owner or Admin to request a role or permission update.
    • Not sure who the owner is? Refer to Who Is the Owner or Admin of My Company Profile?.

Ways to access the career fair registration

Payments are submitted from the career fair registration page in Handshake. You can access the registration in one of the following ways:

  • An invoice sent via email
  • Manual search

Invoice via email

When a school sends an invoice for a career fair, the registrant receives an email notification.

  • The email includes a Pay Here link at the bottom, which directs you to the career fair registration page in Handshake.
  • Click the Pay Here link in the email to proceed with payment by credit card. If you experience technical issues with the link, navigate directly to Handshake and access the registration manually.

If the registration was submitted with a manual payment option, the email will not include a Pay Here link. In this case, follow the payment instructions provided by the school or contact the career fair point of contact.

The email will read:

From: Handshake <handshake@notifications.joinhandshake.com

Subject: “Invoice for [EMPLOYER NAME]: Registration for [CAREER FAIR NAME] at [SCHOOL NAME]”

Heading: “Your invoice has arrived!”

Body: “Hello [CAREER FAIR REGISTRANT FIRST NAME],

Invoice #[NUMBER] for [EMPLOYER NAME]:

Your invoice has arrived! [SCHOOL NAME] has invoiced you for your [CAREER FAIR NAME] career fair registration. Your total comes to [COST].

Download Invoice [LINK]

You can view more details about your registration [LINK] at any time on Handshake.

Registration Date: [DATE]

Employer: [NAME]

Registrant: [REGISTRANT NAME]

Date Attending:

[MONTH, DATE] [TIME]

You can Pay Here [LINK] using a credit card.

or..

[SCHOOL NAME] has indicated they’ll be able to take payments manually for this career fair.

Thank you,

[SCHOOL NAME]”

Manual search

  1. Click Fairs from the left navigation bar.

  2. Select the career fair you want to submit payment for.

For help locating the registration, refer to How to View/Edit a Career Fair Registration.

Pay for the registration

  1. On the registration page, locate the Payment Status section on the left side.

  2. Click the green Pay Now button.

  3. Enter your credit card information in the pop up window, then click the Pay amount button to submit your payment.

Note: Handshake does not collect, store, or process credit card information for career fair payments.

If the Pay Now button is not available, the registration was submitted with a manual payment option. Follow the instructions provided by the school or contact the career fair point of contact.

Payment issues and declined cards

If you receive a message that your card was declined:

  • Double check your credit card details.
  • Contact your card issuer to confirm payments to Stripe are authorized. If payments continue to fail, the Stripe account linked to the hosting school may be blocking your payment method. Stripe may also block a card if there was an issue with a previous transaction.

To resolve this, contact the career fair’s point of contact for assistance.

How to Register Multiple Divisions for a Career Fair

If your organization has multiple divisions that want to attend the same in-person career fair, you can register each one individually.

Handshake allows you to submit separate registrations so each division has its own representatives, details, and approval status.

Register another division

  1. Click Fairs from the left navigation bar, then select the fair you want to register additional divisions for.

Tip: Use the Show Registered Only filter to quickly view fairs your company has already registered for.

  1. On the fair’s Overview page, click the More options menu (three-dot icon) next to the Save button, then select Register another division.

  2. Complete and submit the New Registration form for each division you want to register. For step by step guidance, refer to Registering for a Fair (Employers).

  3. The host school will review and approve each division’s registration individually.

Have questions about the approval process? Learn more in Understanding Career Fair Registration Approval.

How to View a Career Fair Invoice

If you’ve registered for a career fair on Handshake, you can easily access and download the associated invoice.

Note: Handshake does not have the ability to generate or provide receipts. Please reach out directly to the Career Fair’s Point of Contact (found on the Career Fair’s Details page) to request a receipt.

Locate fair

  1. Click Fairs from the left navigation bar, then select the fair for which you want to view the invoice.

Tip: Check the boxes for “Show Registered Only” and “Include Past Fairs (if applicable) to narrow your search results.

  1. Once the fair is located, click directly on its name to be taken to its Details page.

View and download invoice

  1. Click the More options menu (the three dots), then select View registration from the dropdown.

  2. On the Registration page, scroll to the Current Invoice section (near the bottom), then click the blue Download button to the far right of the invoice.

Note: The invoice download link is active for 6 months. For invoices older than 6 months, contact the Career Fair’s Point of Contact.

  1. The invoice will automatically download as a PDF file to your computer.

How to View/Edit a Career Fair Registration

Career fair registrations are available in Handshake at any time and can be edited while the registration period is open.

All user roles except Representatives can view and manage career fair registrations.

If your company is connected to an Essentials or TES account and you cannot view or edit a registration, one of the following applies:

  • Your role is set to Representative, or
  • The required career fair permissions are not enabled for your role. Contact your company profile owner or an admin to request a role change or to have the correct permissions enabled.

Topics:

  • View a career fair registration
  • Edit ‌career fair registration

View a career fair registration

  1. Click Fairs from the left navigation bar.

  2. In the lower-right corner of the page, check the box labeled Show Registered Only.

  • To view registrations for past career fairs, also check the box labeled Include Past Fairs.
  • Note: This view displays all upcoming fairs your company is registered for, including any that are still pending approval from the school.

  1. Click on the name of the career fair you want to view the registration(s) for.

  2. On the Details page, click the More options menu (the three dots), then select View registration from the dropdown.

  • If multiple divisions were registered, select the specific registration in the pop-up modal.
  1. The Overview page displays all the information submitted during registration. The page also displays the following information:
  • Payments (status)
  • Registration Packages
  • Survey responses (if any)
  • Invoice(s)
  • Payment History
  • Public Activity and Comments
  • School contact information If you need to pay for a career fair, refer to How to Pay for a Career Fair Registration.

Edit career fair registration

  1. Click on the Edit tab located in the upper-right corner of the Career Fair’s Overview page.

Note: If this tab is missing, the registration period has closed and no further edits can be made. For assistance, contact the career fair’s point of contact. Their information is available on the fair’s Details page.

  1. The following fields can be edited:
  • Representatives
    • Names of Representatives Attending this Session
  • Basic Information
    • Employer Description
    • Schedule Owner
  • Open Roles
    • Are the role(s) you want to fill posted on Handshake?
    • Jobs on Handshake/Job Titles
    • Do any of the positions that you are hiring for require U.S. work authorization?
    • Would you sponsor a work visa for the right candidate?
    • Are you willing to hire candidates that are temporarily authorized to work for a defined period in their field of study? (e.g. for a job / internship under OPT/CPT)
  • Looking For
    • Employment Types
    • Job Types
    • School Years
    • Major Groups Note: Any field you are unable to edit must be updated by the school hosting the fair. For assistance, contact the career fair’s point of contact. Their information is available on the fair’s Details page.
  1. Click the blue Update Registration button in the lower-right corner of the page to save your changes. You’ll be redirected to the Overview page, where a confirmation message will appear stating: “Registration was successfully updated.”

Resolving Issues Registering for a Career Fair

If you’re unable to register for a career fair in Handshake, it usually means one or more required conditions are not met.

Before you register

To register for a career fair as an employer, all of the following must be true:

  • Your employer account must be validated by Trust & Safety and cannot be under review or suspended.
  • The career fair is visible and open for employer registration
  • Your company profile has not been declined by the school
  • Your user account is an employer account, not a student account
  • For Essentials and Enterprise customers, teammates can only register if the ‘Manage Fairs’ permission is enabled for their role by a company profile Owner or Admin. If you’re unable to register, it may be due to one of the reasons outlined below. Review each section to identify and resolve the issue.

Check your account type

Students can register for career fairs as attendees, but employer registration uses a separate process.

If a colleague shares an employer registration link and you open it while logged into a student account, you will receive a permission error. This does not mean the fair is closed or restricted. It means the link requires an employer account.

How to resolve it
  • Log out and log back in using your employer account
  • If you do not yet have an employer account, create one using your work email.
    • Learn How to Create an Employer Account on Handshake.

Eligible roles and permissions

Employer registration for career fairs requires both an eligible role and the Manage Fairs permission.

Representative roles

Representative seats are available on Plus, Pro, Essentials, and Enterprise (formerly TES) plans.

If your account is assigned the Representative role:

  • You cannot register for career fairs
  • The Manage Fairs permission is not available for this role
  • This permission cannot be enabled, regardless of plan If you need to register for career fairs, you must be assigned a non-Representative role.
Other employer roles

For all non-Representative employer roles:

  • Career fair registration is allowed
  • The Manage Fairs permission must be enabled
What to do if you cannot register
  • If your role is Representative, request a different role from your Admin or Owner
  • If your role is eligible but lacks the Manage Fairs permission, ask the company profile Owner or Admin to enable the permission. To identify the Owner or Admin of your company profile, refer to Who Is the Owner or Admin of My Company Profile?.

Fair visibility and registration dates

Career fair visibility and registration windows are controlled by the school.

The fair does not appear in search

If you cannot find the fair after applying filters, the school may have hidden it from employers. Contact the school’s career center to request an invitation link.

Registration is closed

If the employer registration window has ended, the Register button will display Registration is closed. Only the school can advise on exceptions.

No Register button and no message

If you are on the fair page and there is no Register button and no message indicating registration is closed, continue to the next section Connection status with the school.

Connection status with the school

If a school has declined your company, employer registration for that school’s career fairs is not available.

How to check your connection status
  • At the top of the page, click in the search bar in the upper-left corner of Handshake.
  • Type the name of the school and select the school’s name from the dropdown list. This opens the school’s profile page.
  • Scroll down the page until you find the School Approval section.
What the status means
  • If the status displays Declined in a red oval, your company cannot register for that school’s career fairs. Learn more about being Declined by a School.
  • If the status displays anything other than Declined, your company is eligible to register, and you can continue troubleshooting.

Understanding Career Fair Registration Approval

After you submit a registration for a career fair, the next step is approval by the host school.

Each school’s career services office reviews employer registrations to confirm details before participation is finalized.

Approval process

After submission, your registration enters a Pending status. The host school will review your registration. If you registered multiple divisions, each submission is reviewed separately.

Once approved, your registration status updates to Approved on both the Fairs page and the individual registration page.

Note: Approval timelines vary by school.

Multiple division registrations

If you registered multiple divisions, each division’s registration will display its own approval status.

To confirm the status for each division, review the registration individually. Learn How to View/Edit a Career Fair Registration.

Notifications

If email notifications are enabled, the registrant will receive an email when the registration is approved.

Notification preferences can be managed in your Default Notification Preferences (Employers).

Payment after approval

You will not be able to submit payment until your registration is approved.

Once your registration is approved, you can choose from the payment options provided by the host school. Learn How to Pay for a Career Fair Registration.

Virtual fair schedule

A schedule for a virtual schedule can only be set once registration has been approved.

The registrant will will be notified upon approval and may then proceed to set the schedule. Learn more about Creating a Schedule for Virtual Fairs.

Creating & Editing Events

Canceling or Deleting an Event

If you need to cancel or delete an event on Handshake, the available options will depend on the event’s RSVP status and format.

  • Events without RSVPs can be canceled by adjusting the event’s date and time to a point in the past.

  • Events with RSVPs cannot be edited. In this case, notify the registered students, then contact Handshake Support to request cancellation.

  • Deletion options vary depending on whether the event is hosted on-campus, off-campus, or virtually. Topics:

  • Canceling an event with no RSVPs

  • Canceling an event with RSVPs

  • Deleting an event

Canceling an event with no RSVPs

  1. Click Events from the left navigation bar in Handshake, then select the event you want to edit from the table.

Tip: Click the white button Include past events in the header and uncheck the box to the left of “Include past events” to filter out past events.

  1. Click the More options menu (three-dot icon) in the top-right corner of the page, then select Edit event.

  2. On the event edit page, scroll to the Date and Time section.

  • Set the start date and time to a past date (e.g., yesterday).
  • Set the end date and time to an earlier time than the start (e.g., one hour earlier).
  1. Scroll to the bottom and click the blue button Save to apply your changes.

The event will now be treated as past and will no longer appear as an upcoming event to students.

Canceling an event with RSVPs

If students have already registered for your event, the date and time cannot be edited. In this case:

  • You are encouraged to send a message to all registered students letting them know the event has been canceled. Learn How to Send a Student a Message.
  • Contact the Support team with the event name and a request to cancel it.

Deleting an event

Off-campus and virtual events

Employers and host schools cannot delete off-campus or virtual events. To request deletion, contact our Support team.

On-campus events

To delete an on-campus event, contact the host school directly. For assistance, refer to How to Contact a School.

Creating a Shell Event for Tracking Attendance at Non-Handshake Events

On Handshake, employers can use a shell event to track attendance at events not hosted directly on the platform.

Features available only to Premium partners are indicated by an asterisk (*). For more information, please check out this resource.

A shell event can be used for the following event types:

  • Are not hosted at a partner school
  • Are hosted in partnership with a non-partner school
  • Have no school affiliation (e.g., conferences or career expos)

Create a shell event

  1. Click Events from the left navigation bar, then click the black button Create Event in the upper-right corner of the page.

  2. Complete the form below, paying special attention to the fields below:

  • Where is your event being held?
    • Off-campus
    • Virtually
      • *Handshake Video (only available to Premium partners with the Events Module)
      • External video platform (enter your video platform details (Zoom, Youtube, Webex, etc.)
  • *Attendee check-in (only available for events with Handshake hosted video)
    • Check this box to enable automatic check-in when candidates join a virtual event hosted via Handshake Video.
  • Invite schools to promote your event
    • Don’t select any schools in this field.
    • Note: Excluding schools makes the event private and invisible to students, allowing it to function solely as a check-in tool for tracking attendance.

Once your event is created, you’ll be directed to the event overview page, which displays key event information such as the date, time, location, and format.

At the top of the page, the RSVPs section summarizes your attendance activity:

  • Your check-ins: Candidates who have checked in
  • Your evaluations: The number of candidates your team has submitted evaluations for Learn more about Accessing Event and Fair RSVPs.

How to Create an Event

Approved employers on Handshake can create and post events to schools that have proactively approved their company.

Events can be hosted on campus, off-site, or virtually, and are a way to connect with students and alumni, share career opportunities, and provide career resources.

Not yet approved by a school? Refer to How Can I Get Approved By Schools?.

Features requiring a paid plan are indicated by an asterisk (*). For more information, please check out this resource!

Create an event

  2. Complete the fields in the Create a new event form:

      • Hiring and recruiting
      • About your company
      • Guidance
      • Networking
      • Career fairs
      • Conferences and more.

  • Contact: The contact person is the primary point of contact for event-related questions.
    • The contact must have an active Handshake user account and the role to manage events.
    • If their name does not appear in the dropdown, visit How to Create an External Contact.
    • Check the box for The contact person can accept messages from attendees to allow attendees to message the contact directly.

Off-campus

Virtually

To view and manage your event, visit Managing Your Event.

How to Duplicate an Event

Duplicating a previous event prefills a new event form with existing details, which expedites setup when planning a similar event.

Who can duplicate an event?

An event can be duplicated under the following conditions:

  • Your company has the Handshake Events package.
  • You have the “Manage events” permission within your organization. The Handshake Events package is part of the Premium offering. For more information, check out this resource.

How do I duplicate an event?

  1. Click Events from the left navigation bar, then select the event you want to duplicate from the table.

  2. Click the More options menu (three dots) in the top right corner of the page, then select Duplicate event from the dropdown.

  3. A new event form opens in a new tab, with certain fields pre-filled based on the original event.

  4. Review and update the event form, then click the Save button in the lower-right corner to complete the duplication.

Which fields carry over from the original event?

  • Event categories
  • Contact and contact message preferences
  • Event location preferences
    • On-campus: Host school and Career Center (if originally filled out)
    • Off-campus
  • Handshake video preferences, including the option to record
  • Registration limit
  • Invited schools
  • Description
  • Highlighted guests
  • Event thumbnail

Which fields need to be reviewed after duplicating?

  • Title: The duplicated event has “Copy of” added to the beginning. Edit this as needed.
  • Date and Time: The start date, end date, and time zone are blank, so enter the correct details.
  • External Links: Fields such as the external video link and external registration link are blank, so provide the updated links.

How to Edit an Event

You can edit event details in Handshake to update information such as the date, time, description, or registration limit.

Editing permissions

By event format

  • Off-campus and virtual events: These can only be edited by the employer.

  • On-campus events: These can be edited by both the employer and the host school. By employer account type and permissions

  • Basic employers: Owners and Recruiters can edit only the events they have personally created. Events created by other teammates will appear on your list but are view-only.

    • To edit events created by teammates, you must upgrade to an eligible paid plan.

  • On-campus employers, Plus, Pro, Essentials and TES customers: All users, except Representatives, can edit events created by themselves or by teammates, provided they have the appropriate permissions. Need to cancel or delete your event? Learn more about Canceling or Deleting an Event.

Editing an event

  1. Click Events from the left navigation bar in Handshake, then select the event you want to edit from the table.

Tip: Click the white button Include past events in the header and uncheck the box to the left of “Include past events” to filter out past events.

  1. Click the More options menu (three-dot icon) in the top-right corner of the page, then select Edit event.

  2. On the edit page, make desired changes as allowed. Fields that cannot be edited will be disabled and appear grayed out.

  • For on-campus or off-campus events that have already been approved, changing the event type, date, time, or registration limit will require the event to be re-approved. Note: The event format (i.e., where the event is being held) cannot be changed once students have RSVP’d.

Understanding Event Formats in Handshake

On Handshake, you can create three types of events to connect with early talent in ways that align with your recruiting strategy.

Need help creating a new event? Read more about How to Create an Event.

Features available to Premium partners only are indicated by an asterisk (*). For more information, please check out this resource.

Event formats in Handshake

On-Campus

An on-campus event takes place at a school’s campus and requires coordination with the school to secure a venue. Common examples include information sessions and panel discussions.

Because these events are hosted at a single school, you must select that school as the host when creating the event. After you submit the event request, it is sent to the school for approval.

Once approved, students can view and RSVP to the event. Learn more about Accessing Event and Fair RSVPs.

Off-Campus

An off-campus event is hosted by your organization at a location outside of a school’s campus, such as an office or recreational facility.

Basic, Plus, and Pro employers can promote one off-campus event per school and must create separate events to request the same event at multiple schools.

*Essentials and TES customers can select multiple schools or use a school list when hosting an event for a group of schools, such as HBCUs. Learn more about Creating and Managing School Lists.

Virtual

A virtual event is hosted online rather than in person, allowing attendees to join from multiple locations. Examples include webinars, online workshops, and virtual information sessions.

Check out Handshake’s Guide to Hosting Virtual Recruiting Events.

Emails

About Mail Merge Fields

Handshake wants to enable you to reach your students and contacts in ways that are time efficient and effective! Mail merge fields enable you to create emails that are specifically tailored to students or contacts, adding that extra touch of personalization that will lead to higher open rates. Use the mail merge fields as detailed below–this automatically adds the student or contact information as shown on the profile or contact entry.

While composing the email text, you can use the Insert Variables dropdown to select a pre-formatted mail merge field. If using a mail merge field in the subject field, you will need to type in the variable you’d like to use.

For example, if you are emailing multiple recipients, and you want the subject to contain something like “Join our event, [first name]” such that the [first name] portion of the email autofills for each recipient, you must use the exact text written below.

Variable you are including in email

Exact text to copy into your email

Recipient’s username

%recipient.username%

Recipient’s full name

%recipient.name%

Recipient’s first name

Creating and Sending Targeted Emails

Follow the instructions below to create and send a new Targeted Email. For an overview of the Targeted Email tool and resources, checkout An Overview of Using Targeted Emails.

  1. Click Emails from the left navigation bar, then click Create Email in the upper-right corner of the page.

  2. Enter an Email Name. This name is not visible to recipients, but it will be visible to other Career Services users.

  3. Choose a Layout, a Previous Email or a Handshake Template, then click Next. You’ll be able to customize this email in the next step.

  • Layouts contain placeholders for your own content, with all basic building blocks pre-formatted–allowing you to “fill in the blanks”.
  • Previous Emails allow you to copy email content from emails either previously sent or drafted.
  • Handshake Templates are ready-to-use content branded for you. Check out our gallery of Handshake Templates.
  1. Edit the content of the email.
  • New feature highlight! You can rearrange email content sections via drag and drop.
    • To rearrange email content, hover your mouse pointer over the specific section until the section highlights with a light pink dotted line border, as shown in the example below around the Call to Action button.
    • Click and hold on the section, then drag it up or down as desired. Release the section to place it. The different content elements are included below. After customizing the message, you can use Send Test Email in the upper-right corner of the email editor to send yourself a test email to preview.

Since May 2022: Our EDU Product Team has updated the UI for Handshake Content to improve functionality and provide a better user experience!

  • Primary Color: this will set the button and Handshake Content icon color in your email
    • Tip: use your school hex code here to create consistency!
  • Basic Content
    • Text: use the text to add verbiage to the email
      • Tip: add mail merge fields to the email to make it personal, via the Insert variable drop-down. Preferred Name will use a student’s preferred name or first name if they don’t have a preferred name set.
  • Heading: enter Header Text for the top of the email or a section. You can adjust Size (Primary/Secondary) and Alignment (Left/Center) as well.
  • Image: drag and drop a photo or choose an image to upload. Add alt-text below the upload, select the photo’s maximum width, and choose the image alignment.
    • Tip: use the cropping tool when adding a banner to change the height of the image!
  • Button: enter Text to display on the button, then add the desired URL.
    • Tip: this feature is great for surveys!
  • Spacer/Divider: add space between content sections
  • Handshake Content
    • Career Fair: select an approved career fair, and Handshake will add the following fields to the email:
      • Fair Name
      • Date
      • brief highlight for employers participating Note: if a fair is included within a targeted email, regardless of whether it’s invite-only or hidden, all recipients are invited to the fair automatically. The content option included within the email will allow students and employers to bypass those settings and view/register as if they had the public preview link. If the recipient is a student at another school, and the fair isn’t a public or multi school fair, the student will be blocked from receiving the email.
  • Event: Select an approved event and Handshake will add the following event fields to the email:
    • Name
    • Date
    • *Company name of participating employer, if applicable Note: if an event is included within a targeted email, regardless of whether it’s invite-only, all recipients are invited to the event automatically. The content option included within the email will allow students and employers to bypass those settings and view/register as if they had the public preview link.
  • Job Role: Select a job role and Handshake will add a description of the job role and a link to “Learn more” about that role in Handshake:
    • Job: Select an approved job and Handshake will add the following job details to the email:
      • Title
      • Employer name
      • Job Type
      • Employment Type
      • Location
      • Expiration Date (apply by)
  • Employer Collection: Select an employer collection and Handshake will add a description for the Employer Collection to the email:
  • Attachments: Files that’ll be attached to the email, most file types will be accepted, but we recommend that you attach PDFs.
  1. When you’re ready to proceed, click Next, in the lower-right corner of the screen, then choose your recipients: Student or Contact.

At least one filter must be selected on this page, unless you’ve pre-selected recipients from another page in Handshake.

Note: if the targeted email includes 65,000 recipients or more, the recipients information will not be available in Handshake. Click Download Recipients in the center of the page to download and view the recipients list.

Tip: to avoid delays in sending the email, we recommend keeping the emails targeted and scoped with 10,000 recipients or fewer.

Example of selecting 65,000 or fewer Student recipients:

Example of selecting 65,000 or fewer Contact recipients:

  1. Click Next to proceed and finalize email details.
  • Subject*
    • Tip: use students or contacts first name to increase open rates! (exact formatting required - refer to About Mail Merge Fields for more details)
  • Sender Name*
  • Reply To Email*
    • Note: The Sender Name and Reply to Email fields will need to be filled out for each email unless the Targeted Email Configuration is set up in your institution’s School Settings. Learn more about this process here: School Settings: Targeted Email Configuration
  • Carbon Copy Emails
    • Note: this will only send one copy of the email to CCs listed.
  • Campaign Name*
  • Send Now or Send Later
    • If you choose to send later, select a date and time to send the email.
      • Note: unless your recipients are pre-selected based on email address (i.e. the email is created via Contacts or Manage Students), recipients will be identified at the time the email is scheduled to be sent. For example, if you select recipients based on Major, on the scheduled send date/time, the recipients are identified based on the Major selected on their profile at that date/time (which may differ from when the email was originally created). Note: Any field with an asterisk (*) must be filled out before successfully saving the targeted email on this step.
  1. Click Save Details to save your email draft. When you’re ready to send the email, click Send (if sending now) or Schedule for DATE (if sending later) to queue the email.

Once the email is sent, you can review the campaign’s Performance Details.

Email Security

Handshake users interested in email security may want to know if we support using Sender Policy Framework (SPF) and/or DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM) to identify messages that are legitimately sent by Handshake.

All emails sent by Handshake (such as notifications, job digests, etc.) use SPF / DKIM and DMARC for enforcement to validate that they are legitimate Handshake emails.

  • Note: DMARC records for Handshake emails are published under DNS records and can be confirmed for free using tools like Valimail. Our email sending domains are currently:

  • joinhandshake.com

  • notifications.joinhandshake.com

  • mail.joinhandshake.com

  • m.joinhandshake.com

  • g.joinhandshake.com

  • cm.joinhandshake.com

  • m.ai.joinhandshake.com These servers send emails using TLS encryption protocol. In the event that sendings fail with TLS it may attempt to send emails using other protocols such as SSL.

How can I edit a scheduled email?

If you need to edit a scheduled email in Handshake, you can do so up until 5 minutes before the email is scheduled to go out. To make an edit, follow the steps below:

  1. Click Emails on the left navigation bar.

  2. Click on the name of the scheduled email you’d like to edit.

  3. Click the gray button Unschedule Email in the upper-right corner.

Note: if the Unschedule Email button is no longer there, this means your edit window has passed. You will not be able to make any edits.

  1. Make the desired changes, then proceed through the re-scheduling process.

Note: if you’re editing a scheduled email close to the send time, and you finish edits within 5 minutes of the scheduled send time, the edits will be saved, but you will not be able to adjust the send time.

An Overview of Using Targeted Emails

Targeted Emails, Handshake’s internal email tool, offer a way for institutions to email students and contacts with relevant, timely, and useful information.

1. Save time by setting up a default sender name and email address for your institution.

Adding these defaults can help save time later when composing emails. Each email is still customizable, so you’re welcome to adjust the sender name and/or email address per individual email.

For instructions, check out School Settings: Targeted Email Configuration.

2. Create consistent emails that drive clear actions from students and contacts.

The Targeted Email tool empowers you with the following options for content:

  • Duplicate a sent email or email draft
    • easily reuse a favorite layout or format
  • Use a pre-configured Handshake Template
    • check out our gallery in Handshake Templates
  • Customize a new email with:
    • Basic Content (building blocks): Text, Heading, Image, Button (call to action - customizable text on button and hyperlink), Spacer/Divider
    • Handshake Content: Career Fair, Event, Job Role, Job Learn more about: Creating and Sending Targeted Emails, how to edit a scheduled email, and Targeted Email Statuses.

3. Once your email is sent, track campaign performance and recipient engagement.

Quickly track opens, clicks, account activations, event/fair registrations, and more, all within Handshake. For details, check out Targeted Emails Performance Overview.

To more quickly locate previously composed emails by you and your team, use our Targeted Emails Search.

Re-Subscribe to Handshake Emails

Are you missing a test email? Missing notifications or other expected Handshake emails? If these emails aren’t being filtered out to a different folder (such as junk/spam), then it’s likely your email has been unsubscribed from Handshake emails.

To resume receiving these emails, you will need to reach out to our Support Team to request that the suppression be removed from the account.

You are welcome to contact us on behalf of a student that’s unsubscribed as well. When you are reaching out on behalf of a student, you will need to include their express permission along with your request in order for the suppression to be removed.

*Not sure how you were unsubscribed from our emails? Typically, we see this happen if you have forwarded a Handshake email to someone else, and a recipient of that message clicks on “Unsubscribe”. Since the original message was sent to ‘you’, the unsubscribe links to your email address, not the forwarding recipient.

School Settings: Targeted Email Configuration

To set up your institution’s Targeted Email default from name and email follow these instructions:

  2. Enter the Default from name (name) and Default reply to (email address), then click Update email preferences to save your changes.

Note: If your institution does not set up the Targeted Email Configuration under School Settings, you will need to manually add the Sender Name and the Reply to Email fields for future Targeted Emails.

When you send a new targeted email, the values entered will appear in the From and Reply to fields (unless otherwise changed within the specific targeted email).

Targeted Email Statuses

This resource defines Targeted Email statuses after finalizing an email and can help confirm if a message has been sent successfully.

To learn more about the targeted email tool, check out An Overview of Using Targeted Emails.

Scheduled

If the email is set to be sent at a future date/time, the status will be “Scheduled” until the scheduled date/time arrives.

Sending

A status of “Sending” means that the email is in the process of being sent. The status will not change to “Sent” until all recipients have received the email.

Sent

When the status changes to “Sent”, this confirms that an email has been sent successfully to all designated recipients.

For additional information on delivery and engagement rates for your campaign, refer to Targeted Emails: Performance Details.

Targeted Emails Performance Overview

After a Targeted Email has been sent, performance details are tracked and viewable directly in Handshake. Results can take up to an hour to fully update after the initial send, and data is updated continuously as more actions occur.

To access these tabs, click Emails from the left navigation bar, then click the desired sent email from To Students or To Contacts.

  • If your team sent emails via our legacy tool, you can access historical engagement data. For details, refer to View Legacy Emails Engagement Data! While viewing the email, performance details can be viewed via two tabs:

  • Email

    • Delivered
    • Open rate
    • Click rate
    • Unique URL clicks
      • A breakdown of each unique URL click (if applicable)
    • Handshake Activation Rate
    • All actions

  • Recipients

    • Search by name or keyword
    • Filters
    • Excluded recipients

Email

The Email tab displays high-level performance (open rate and click rate) and the actions that were taken on the Handshake components included in the email.

Note: In some cases, you may notice that the open rate is much higher than click rate. This is likely because your school’s email security gateway have bots that analyze each link that’s emailed for potential malware. These bots open the email and drive up the open rate. We are looking into possible methods of omitting the bot activity in open rate, but for now we recommend utilizing click rate for the most accurate data.

Delivered
  • The amount of emails that were successfully sent to students (delivered emails are calculated by the recipients minus recipients that had previously unsubscribed from Handshake emails minus any bounced emails) If the recipient didn’t receive the email due to a “bounce” or if they chose to unsubscribe from receiving Handshake emails, they will not be included in the equation. Only emails that are successfully delivered are included in these statistics.
Open rate
  • The count of students that opened this email (Open percentage is calculated by the unique number of opens divided by the number of emails successfully delivered) If a recipient received an email and forwards it to someone else, and that person opens the email, then that open will only count once as the original recipient. This is why it’s considered “unique” and not total.

In order to track opens, we attach an image “sensor” that is basically hidden to the email recipient. This “sensor” is at the very bottom of the sent email, which can impact the open rate in Targeted Emails:

  • If students don’t scroll to the bottom of the email, it could result in the open sensor not being triggered
  • If you have content in excess of 100kb, it can result in the message being clipped from some mail providers, which can also reduce the open rate
  • If an individual blocks images on their email client, then the image “sensor” is never loaded, so the open will never be counted
Unique URL clicks
  • The count of unique recipients that clicked one or more links from the email. This number will display the total number of unique clicks across all links in the email
  • The percentage will represent the rate that recipients have clicked on each individual URL link (unique click percentage is calculated by the number of students that clicked the link(s) divided by the number of emails successfully delivered) Similar to unique opens, if a recipient received an email and forwarded it to someone else, and that person clicked a link within the email, then that click will only count once as the original recipient.

All links that had unique clicks within the email will show on the results page. If a link does not show, it is likely the link didn’t have any clicks.

Handshake account activations
  • The count of students that activated their Handshake accounts after clicking a link in this email (Handshake account activation percentage is calculated by the number of students that activated divided by the number of emails successfully delivered) Note: this requires that the student activate their account via the link that was clicked in the email. For example, if the student clicks the link, closes the tab, then pulls up Handshake by navigating to the site and activates, this will not count as an activation.
All actions

  • Actions on the Handshake Content that was added to the Targeted Email (percentages are all calculated by dividing the number of students who took an action by the number of emails successfully delivered) Actions can be:

  • Event Registrations

  • Career Fair Registrations

  • Job Applications

Recipients

The Recipients tab provides details about the students or contacts who were sent the selected email.

  • Recipient names and email addresses are listed in table format on the page. Student recipients will also display their designated Major(s) and School Year.
  • Search by name or keyword on the left of the page to identify specific recipients.
  • Click Download Recipients to download a .csv file with activity details per recipient.
  • Filters applied to the selected email’s recipient list are listed on the left of the page, below the Download Recipients button.
Excluded recipients

Students that are unsubscribed from Targeted Emails will be listed as “Excluded”. In the recipients list, a red oval to the far right in the row will indicate Excluded.

Use the filter “Show excluded only”, on the left of the page, to identify all recipients that are unsubscribed.

For more information on re-subscribing to Handshake emails, refer to Re-Subscribe to Handshake Emails.

Note: emails are sent from the domain “mail.joinhandshake.com”. If recipients are not unsubscribed from this domain but still not receiving Targeted Emails, it’s possible Handshake email domains need to be unblocked. For more information, refer to Email Delivery: Unblocking Handshake Email.

Targeted Emails Search

In the tabs “To Students”, “To Contacts”, and “Drafts by Others”, you may search by subject, name, or created by.

In the “Your Drafts” tab, you may search by subject or name.

Note: this search does not include email content.

Acting on Behalf of Employers: Creating a Company Profile

There may be situations where an employer is required for a feature on Handshake but the employer hasn’t signed up for a Handshake account yet. These situations might include needing to add an employer to an event, career fair registration, job posting, or interview schedule. For these circumstances, careers services users can create company profiles on behalf of the employers.

Before proceeding with creating an employer, ensure that you have the Manage Employers role for your account. You can learn more about this role in School Settings: Career Services Staff Roles and Permissions

To create an employer, please follow the steps below:

  1. Click on Employers under Relationships in the left navigation bar.

  2. Click on the button Create Employer in the upper-right corner of the page:

  3. Complete the fields for the employer.

  • Every text field is required: Except for those listed as (optional).
  • For Employers that do not have a dedicated website: A LinkedIn/Yelp/Facebook/social media page dedicated to their business will suffice for this field.
  • For Employers that do not have a corporate domain and are using a generic email address: Enter the business name followed by .com (for example, xyzcompany.com). If you experience any issues with this field, contact Support.
  • When adding the Location: Select the best address option from the list of suggestions. If the exact street address isn’t available, you’re welcome to just use the city and state!
  • On-campus employer: Select this only if the account you’re creating is an On-campus employer account. Learn more here: On-Campus Employment Options in Handshake Note: You can add an EIN when creating a company profile; however, it cannot be edited later. To update an employer’s EIN, contact support.
  1. When you’re finished, click Create Employer in the lower right corner.

Note: Once the company has been created successfully, you’ll need to set the desired permissions and approve the company profile at your school. To learn more about this, refer to Employers Page Overview

Alumni Hub

Alumni Hub helps you build, track, and nurture relationships with your most important alumni contacts. Centralizing key data about employer users who attended your institution, the hub acts as a jumping off point for engaging your alumni and unlocking unique opportunities for your students.

To access Alumni Hub, click on Alumni in the left navigation bar, in the Relationships section.

Alumni Hub provides a directory of all employer users in Handshake that have listed your institution as their alma mater. Contacts without an account in Handshake will not be included on this page. Learn more about Contacts vs Users.

Use the filters at the top of the page to narrow down the results displayed in the table:

  • Status

  • Labels

    • These are labels applied to the Contact entry. Use Employer Label to filter on labels on the company profile instead.

  • Employer Select Filters to display additional options on the right side of the screen:

  • Keywords

  • [Employer Status]

    • Approved
    • Pending
    • Declined

    • Not Yet Connected

  • Labels

  • Employer

  • Last Login Start Date - Last Login End Date

  • [Recruiting Activity]

    • Posted Job
    • Posted Event
    • Registered for Fair
    • Posted Interview

  • Access Level

  • Collections There are five columns in the table, which display the following information:

  • Name - User’s name with role below

  • Employer and Title - The company they are connected to in Handshake and their job title

    • Best Practice: look for employers that are currently pending or haven’t yet connected with your institution!

Best Practices: Add a Comment on Job and Employer Approvals

When processing Job Postings or Job Postings from New Employers and either:

  • Don’t feel like you have enough information to approve
  • Want to ensure that you’re communicating your employer guidelines efficiently You can always use the comment feature to notify the employer or request more information. This option exists on both an individual job posting and on the company profile page.

This article will outline how to add a comment and a few example canned responses you can send.

How to add a comment

Note: if declining an employer or job, you’ll be prompted for a decline reason, which will be added as a comment as well. More information is available in Processing Employer Approval Requests using Job Based Approvals and Using Job Decline Reasons.

  1. Navigate to the Job or Employer list view by clicking Jobs or Employers from the left navigation bar in Handshake, then select the posting or company.

  2. Review the details (and add a note) if you determine that you:

  • Need more more information about the employer
  • Want to share your employer guidelines
  • Want to provide reasoning why you’re declining
  1. After typing your comment, click the Add button to save. This will send a notification to the employer who requested approval to connect or post a job.

The comment will then display in the activity log, along with any responses or followups from the employer.

Note: In order to receive updates when an employer comments back on this approval page, you will have to set the visibility options for a Career Services staff member. This staff member will then receive updates that come through the notifications queue at the top of the page.

Viewing Employer Comments on Job and Employer Approvals

If you receive notification that an employer has commented on a job or employer approval, you can click on the link in the notification to pull up that specific job posting or company profile page.

On the employer page, select Activity. This will display any comments that have been made for this employer.

Example “Canned” Comments

Keep in mind, these are only templates - tailor this copy to the needs and high priority workflows of your institution.

Approved + acknowledgement of posting guidelines

Thank you for your interest in recruiting our top talent at {insert school name} We look forward to connecting with you! We value your campus partnership, and have provisioned your company with the following roles:

{default approval roles here}

Please keep the following guidelines in mind as you engage with {insert school name} students and alumni {insert posting guidelines here}

Let us know if you have any additional questions

Thank you,

{Employer Relations team contact}

Missing profile information

Thank you for your interest in recruiting our top talent at the {insert school name} We require a few things before approving a company registration in Handshake at {school name}.

  • An email address associated with your employer/organization website domain (no Gmail, Yahoo, Hotmail, etc). Individual contact names and email addresses should match whenever appropriate.
  • A functioning website that clearly relates to your employer/organization and contains helpful information about your company for the potential applicant; website should not be in a pre-launch/beta phase nor contain “coming soon” language.
  • Social media websites (Facebook pages, blogs, Twitter feeds, LinkedIn pages, etc.) should not take the place of a company website.
  • An employer/organization address that is easily identifiable as a place of business When you are able to provide each of these, we’re happy to revisit your registration in Handshake @ {school name}

Thank you,

{Employer Relations team contact}

Does not align with institution posting guidelines

Thank you for your interest in recruiting our top talent at the {insert school name}.

Given our mission to {insert mission here (help students find meaningful careers) ,etc} our office can only approve postings that adhere to {include employer/institutional job posting guidelines or link here} and cannot approve your posting/company at this time.

Let us know if you have any additional questions,

Thank you,

{Employer Relations team contact}

Didn’t have a chance to approve job before posting expired

Typically you’ll want to get to Employer approvals within ~1 week, and should absolutely approve postings before your student launch date. However, even with all of that, the employer volume can be quite high during the first few weeks after your employer launch. Use this template to buy time without damaging any new employer relationships:

Hi there!

We’re so glad that you requested to connect and post your position @ {school name}

We haven’t had a chance to approve your posting yet because we’re focusing much of our efforts on student launch date on {student launch date here} We want to ensure that students have the best possible experience on Handshake, and are confident this will in turn drive application rates to your future positions.

For now, we are going to decline this expired position while we work through our queue of pending postings, but please keep us in mind for your next open posting.

Let us know if you have any additional questions,

Thank you,

{Employer Relations team contact}

Other Ideas?

Do you have different canned responses that you use to build employer relationships? Share and leverage tips from 500+ university partners in our Handshake Community!

Best Practices: Employer Approvals

Engaging with your Employer partners is vital to building long-term campus recruiting connections. Upon making the switch to Handshake, most schools typically see a 2-3X increase in employer engagement due to the ease of use.

With this increase in volume, it’s important to identify strategy up front to help you build those long-term employer connections!

Pre-invite Checklist:

If you’re in implementation, run through this checklist to ensure you’re ready to send the invite:

  • Import your employer contact file (Importing Employer Contacts)
  • Send your employers a “heads up” email (Implementation: Invite Email Examples) (optional)
  • Determine if you’ll targeting a select group of Employers (on campus, “white glove” partners, etc) and how you will identify them (How to Bulk Add Labels)
  • Determine which team member is “sending” the invite in Handshake (Inviting Contacts to Become Users: Standard Employer Invite Process)
  • When you’re ready, send the invite! If you’re in implementation, once you’re live, you should start to see quite a few employers trickling in. This is a great time to nail down a vetting and approval process that works for your office.

Employer Approval Best Practices

Once you’re live and working through a queue of employer approvals, use these tips to build and efficient workflow, tailored to your team’s needs.

Set aside time to approve incoming New Employer job postings

Why: This empowers your office to vet relevant postings, it ensures high quality, engaging network for students, and puts you in a position to strengthens and build employer relationships

Strategy:

  • Configure default approval settings (School Settings: Default Employer Approval Preferences)
  • Add labels to track white glove or high-touch employer partners (School Settings: Labels)
  • Setup saved searches for job postings or employer approvals (Create a Saved Search)
  • Configure your automatic job approvals to streamline the approval process (Job Automatic Approval Configuration)
  • Leverage the Handshake Community for insights and tips
Vet job postings and companies from New Employers thoroughly

Why: Employers can post jobs to your school in order to be approved by your school. Once your school approves a New Employers’ job posting, all staff who are connected to the account can request to post another position.

The time that you invest in vetting the company now, allows you to quickly scan and approve postings down the road.

The up-front approval process helps you curate an engaging network that aligns with your university’s brand.

Strategy:

Use ALL of these factors to determine if the company is a good fit:

  • Staff Member email addresses (align with company contact?)
  • Company contact information + social pages
  • Ensure that the “about” details align
Confirming employer information
  • When vetting employers, know that employers who have a residential address or an industry size of 1-10 are likely just getting started, so this is not usually a cause for concern.
    • Tip: instead of simply Googling an address, try searching the company name and the address together, and this can help you validate if the address is registered to the company!
  • Please account for human error! If you see an error that may just be an oversight, such as a website that ends in “.ocm” instead of “.com”, chances are, this is not a reason to be suspicious, and probably just a typo.
  • Communicate directly with the employer about your concern/observation by adding a comment on the company profile, in the Employer Approval box, or on the job posting. The employer will receive a notification about your comment and have a chance to make the needed changes or otherwise address your concern directly.
Industry best practices:

In addition to confirming employer information you should also note the email address attached to the staff members at the company requesting approval. Our “extra details” (yellow triangle) will help you answer these questions:

  • Does the domain match that of the email address?

  • Is the email domain a generic one (gmail, hotmail, outlook, etc.)?

  • Is the email domain one that nearly matches the company name, but may have an extra word in it (for example, @mcdonaldsmail.com instead of @mcdonalds.com)? Another tipoff that a company may not be legitimate is the company details:

  • Are you able to locate more information on the company via a web search? Are there reviews of the company on peer review sites?

  • Does the website actually work?

    • Sometimes sites can be set up to redirect to another site–if the website loads successfully, does the address in the web address bar match what’s in Handshake? Using this information can help you make an informed choice when approving or declining an employer.
Scan + approve jobs/employers

Why: We recommend approving jobs from a variety of employers and industries (even if they don’t typically align with your traditional relationships) as this give students the ability to explore meaningful careers beyond their major.

However, your office does have the final say on job approvals and can curate the network based on your institutional guidelines. This also gives you a chance to vet postings your students will access.

Reminder: Employers will be approved when you approve their job posting. Refer to Processing Employer Approval Requests for more information.

Strategy:

  • Setup saved searches to build a variety of job posting queues (Create a Saved Search)
  • Add comments (and develop canned responses) when you decline a job posting to notify the employer as to why (Best Practices: Add a Comment on Job and Employer Approvals)
  • Check the description, pay, and other details for unrealistic or suspicious information
  • Leverage Handshake Community for insights and tips across the network
