Managing Employer Requested Events

Employers can request to host an event at your school at any time (provided they’re approved at the school and granted the role of “Post Events”).

These events may be hosted on-campus, off-site, or virtually. For more information on the creation process from the employer perspective, refer to How to Create an Event.

Note: employer-requested events cannot be duplicated. Only events created by your career services office can be duplicated.

Some images in this article display the beta version of the new event page. This images are subject to change and the overall instructions will still be relevant to the current version of Events.

Topics:

  • Approving Event Requests
  • Editing Employer Events

Approving Event Requests

  1. Click Events on the left navigation bar to review pending requests.

  2. All future events that are pending and approved will be displayed — this includes events requested by employers, and those being hosted by your institution.

Use the search and filters at the top of the page to narrow down the displayed results. Filters include:

  • Type
  • Include past events
  • Status
  • Filters
    • Type
    • Include past events
    • Approved
    • Cancelled
    • Declined
    • Pending
    • Location
    • Earliest date
    • Latest Date
    • Format
    • Host
    • Organizer
    • Career center
      • Tip: if your institution has configured career centers, employer-hosted on-campus events must be linked to a career center.
      • Employer host industry
        • Tip: since employer-hosted virtual events cannot be linked to a career center, use this filter to narrow down results relevant to your career center!
    • Collections
    • Labels
    • Not Labels
  • Include declined events — check this box to include declined events as well as the pending or approved events listed on the page by default.
  • Invite-only events — check this box to display events that are set up to only be joinable through invitation. Note: you can Reset to pending/Approve/Decline event requests directly from this page by clicking the three dots on the right side of the event column. Below is an example of an approved event and the options to Reset to pending or Decline the event.
  1. Click on the name of the event you’d like to review, and load the Event page. Make modifications to the event by selecting the pencil icon next to the status. The example screenshot shows an approved event, which has an option to be Reset to pending.

Note: Approved events can be set to pending, from pending, an event can be set to approved or declined. From declined, an event can be set to approved or pending.

Editing Employer Events

Events hosted by employers can be edited by your career center only if the event is hosted on-campus. If the event is hosted off-campus or virtually, you won’t be able to make edits to the event. For more details, scroll down to the Off-campus and Virtual events section below.

Note: employer-requested events cannot be deleted by a Career Services user or the employer. If an employer-requested event needs to be deleted, please reach out to our Support Team for assistance.

The event Host/Creator cannot be changed once the event has been created.

  • If an employer user creates and requests the event, the employer’s company will be listed as the host.
  • If a career services user creates an event on behalf of the employer, the institution will be listed as the host.
On-campus Events

When an event is hosted on campus, there’s an Edit tab in the upper-right corner of the page. Click on the Edit tab to make changes to the event.

You’ll be taken to the Events creation page. Make the updates needed, go through the steps, then click the Save button in the lower-right corner of the last page to save!

Note: if you make changes to the event, we recommend looping the employer in on the changes made to ensure alignment!

Off-campus and Virtual Events

When an event is Off-campus or Virtual and created be an employer, you won’t have the option to click edit — only the employer will be able to edit these events.

If you find that edits need to be made to the Event, you can follow up with the employer directly — just keep in mind that comments posted on the Event are viewable by other Career Services staff, the employer, and students (if the event is approved).

The event location is identified either with an address for off-campus, or with the link provided for the virtual events.

  • An example of an Off-campus event with the event’s address displayed:
  • An example of a Virtual Event link:

Virtual and Off-Campus Events

When Premium employer partners create a virtual or off-campus event in Handshake, they must select a school to post the event to under the Invite a school to promote your event field.

Employers can include the URL to the event in Campaigns (emails to students within Handshake), and Campaign recipients will be able to access and register for the event directly via the URL.

The employer needs to request the event to be approved by schools in order for it to be discoverable by students in general, and once the event is approved by the requested school, students will be able to discover the event, just like a normal event.

Note: if the employer shares an event link with students, but the event has not been requested at your institution, the event will not display for career services users using the link.

For more information on the employer process for creating and requesting and event, refer to How to Create an Event.

Events

Activating the Kiosk for a Virtual Event

You can reactivate a previously deactivated check-in kiosk to collect student information for virtual events.

This feature is available to Premium partners with the Events module enabled. For more information, please check out this resource.

Activate the kiosk

  1. Click Events from the left navigation bar, then select the event you want to activate the kiosk for.

  2. On the event page, click the Kiosk setup tab, then click the text Activate check-in to the right of the Save button.

  3. Choose an existing template or create a new one.

  • To use an existing template, refer to Reusing Check-in Kiosk Templates.
  • To create a new kiosk, click the button Create kiosk. Learn how to Create and Launch a Check-in Kiosk.

Virtual event check-in process

For virtual events with an active kiosk, the kiosk will be shown to students when they click the Join Video button.

  • This kiosk will be set live for students to check in automatically 30 minutes before the event’s start time.
  • The check-in kiosk will remain live throughout the duration of the event up to 30 minutes after its end time.
  • Students will be sent to the Web Host URL after checking in. To access and review your RSVPs, refer to Accessing Event and Fair RSVPs.

Adding Custom Questions to Your Check-in Kiosk

Adding custom questions to a check-in kiosk allows you to gather more detailed information from attendees participating in an in-person event, career fair, or virtual event.

In addition to our standard list of check-in questions, custom prompts can be configured to align with your hiring needs.

  • To create and launch a check-in kiosk for an in-person event or fair, refer to Create and Launch a Check-in Kiosk.
  • To reactivate a check-in kiosk for a virtual event, refer to Activating the Kiosk for a Virtual Event. This feature is available to Premium partners with the Events module enabled. For more information, please check out this resource!

Adding custom questions

  1. Navigate to the event or fair you want to add custom questions for, then click the Kiosk setup tab.

  2. Navigate to the Custom questions section at the bottom of the page, then click the white button + Add question.

  3. In the text box that appears, enter your custom question.

Note: You are responsible for ensuring custom questions comply with Handshake’s terms of service.

  1. From the dropdown, select the desired answer type to specify how you want attendees to respond to your questions:
  • Short free text
  • Single-select
    • Add your own prompts for attendees to select from
  • Multi-select
    • Add your own prompts for attendees to select from
  • To add an additional question(s), click the white button + Add question.
    • Note: You can add as many custom questions as desired.
  • To make a question required, check the box for Required.
  • To remove a question, click the bin icon located on the far right side of the textbox.
  1. Once all custom questions have been added, click the black button Save in the lower-right corner of the page.

Connecting Your Jobs to Your Events

Connect your job postings to events in Handshake to increase visibility and drive more engagement from qualified student candidates.

Highlighting open roles on your event page helps students discover your opportunities, come prepared to engage, and apply directly to positions you’re actively recruiting for.

Create an event

You can only connect jobs to an event after the event has been created.

If you have not created your event yet, start by creating one. For step-by-step instructions, refer to How to Create an Event.

Access event

Click Events from the left navigation bar, then select the event you want to connect a job(s) to.

Tip: Click the white button Include past events in the header and uncheck the box to view only upcoming events.

Connect your job(s)

  • On the main event page, scroll to the Connect jobs section near the bottom, then click the black button Connect jobs.
  1. In the pop-up modal, use the Search jobs field to find and select the jobs you want to connect.

Note: You can connect to up to 15 active jobs in total.

  1. Selected jobs will appear as tags below the search bar.
  • To remove a job, click the X next to the job title.
  1. When you’re done, click the black button Connect jobs to save your selections.

Disconnect job

Scroll to the Connect jobs section, click the More options menu (three dots) next to the job title, then select Disconnect job from the dropdown.

Creating a Check-in Kiosk

Create and customize a check-in kiosk to collect student information at your on-campus, off-campus, or virtual event.

Need to reactivate a kiosk for a virtual event? Refer to Activating the Kiosk for a Virtual Event.

This feature is available to Premium partners with the Events module enabled. For more information, please check out this resource.

Create a check-in kiosk

  1. Navigate to the event or fair you want to set up a check-in kiosk for, then click the Kiosk setup tab.

  2. Click the black button Create kiosk in the upper-right corner of the Set up a check-in kiosk section.

  • To use an existing template, refer to Reusing Check-in Kiosk Templates.
  1. Enter a welcome message, if desired. This message displays to students on the kiosk when they scan the check-in QR code.

Note: The character limit is 500.

  1. In the setup form, choose the information you want to collect from students by toggling the button to the right. To make a field required, check the “Required” box located to the right of the field.

You may collect the following information:

Basic info

The Basic info section contains optional fields for Major category, School, and Graduation date.

Note: A student’s first and last name, as well as their email address, are always required.

Job aspirations

The Job aspirations section contains optional fields for Job locations, US work authorization, Type(s) of employment, Areas of interest, and relevant job opportunities.

You can customize the responses that candidates can select from for job locations, areas of interest, and relevant job opportunities.

  • Type in each respective search bar to configure responses. Select Include relevant job opportunities to allow candidates to express interest in relevant jobs posted by your employer on Handshake. Enter the title of the job(s) you want to showcase in the search bar to help refine your results. Each job will feature a unique job ID # to help identify the job(s) selected.
Competencies

The Competencies section allows candidates to select skills they want to add.

Custom questions

The Custom questions section allows you to collect additional details from your attendees.

  • Learn more about Adding Custom Questions to your Check-in Kiosk. Ready to launch your kiosk? Learn more in Launching a Check-In Kiosk.

Creating Check-in Kiosk Templates

You can create and save your kiosk question sets as templates, making it easy to reuse them across multiple events, saving both time and effort.

To reuse an existing check-in template for an event or fair, refer to Reusing Check-in Kiosk Templates.

This feature is available to Premium partners with the Events module enabled. For more information, please check out this resource.

  1. Navigate to the event or fair you want to create a check-in kiosk template for, then click the Kiosk setup tab.
  • If you do not have any templates, the message “You do not have any templates yet. When you create a kiosk and save it as a template you will be able to see them here.” displays on the page.
  1. In the Set up a check-in kiosk section, click the black button Create kiosk in the upper-right corner of the page.
  • To reuse an existing template, refer to Reusing Check-in Kiosk Templates.

  1. Select the information you want to collect from students, then click the black button Save. For additional details on each section, refer to Create and Launch a Check-in Kiosk.

  2. Click the three-dot menu icon in the upper-right corner of the page, then select Make it a template from the dropdown.

Note: The “Launch” button is displayed on the page if the event or fair is held in person.

  1. In the pop-up modal, enter the name of the template so that you can reuse the questions from this kiosk at any time, then click the black button Create template.

  2. Once created, the message “Template created successfully” appears in the lower-center of the page. You can now use this event template for any event or fair that you host or register for.

To learn how to manage your existing templates, refer to Managing Check-in Kiosk Templates.

Day-of Checklist for Events and Career Fairs (Events)

Use this checklist to help your team prepare for in-person or hybrid events and career fairs hosted on Handshake.

Follow these key steps before and during the event to ensure a smooth, successful experience for staff and attendees.

Before the event

Access the event on Handshake

  • Make sure you can access the event and navigate the Handshake platform either through the Events app or a desktop browser.
    • iOS users: Download the Handshake Events app from the App Store
    • Web users: Log in at app.joinhandshake.com If you’re new to the Handshake Events app, take a few minutes to explore its layout and functionality before the day of the event.

Confirm QR codes are printed

Your event lead should provide printed QR codes for attendee check-in. Bring them with you and display them clearly at the event.

Need a full pre-event checklist? Review Preparing for the Day-of an Event.

Day of the event

Set up check-in stations

  • Place printed QR codes in a visible location at the entrance of your booth.

  • Optional: Provide a tablet or laptop on a stand for attendees who prefer not to use their phone or do not have one. Launch the kiosk

  • Launch the kiosk while connected to a reliable internet connection, ideally before arriving at the event. Need help launching your kiosk? Refer to Launching a Check-In Kiosk.

  • Once launched, the kiosk will stay active throughout the event, even if your device temporarily loses its internet connection. To understand how offline mode and QR code check-in work, see How QR Code and Offline Check-In Work in Handshake.

Greet and prompt attendees to check in

  • Encourage attendees to scan the QR code or check in via the tablet or laptop station. Troubleshoot check-In issues

Experiencing connectivity problems or check-in errors? There are steps you can take to keep check-ins running smoothly, even without internet access.

For detailed troubleshooting steps and offline check-in tips, refer to:

  • Troubleshooting Errors with the Handshake Events App
  • Checking in Attendees at Events with Unstable WiFi

During the event

Find and open the event in Handshake

  • Open the Handshake Events app, or log in at app.joinhandshake.com
  • Locate and open the event or fair you want to manage Evaluate attendees

You can evaluate attendees using either the Handshake Events app or the web version. Evaluations can include a thumbs up/down rating, notes, and labels to help your team track and engage with candidates after the event.

  • For the web version, navigate to the event or fair page and click the Candidates tab. Attendees will appear in real time as they check in. Refresh the page periodically to view the most recent check-ins.
  • For the app, tap Check-ins within the event to view attendees who have checked in and require evaluation. Curious about how to rate candidates or add notes during the event? Read more about Managing RSVPs with Evaluations, Notes, & Labels.

Report any issues or feedback to your event lead

  • Share anything that went well or could be improved for future events.

Download an Event or Fair Booth QR Code (Events)

For each event or fair session you’re registered for, you can download a QR code to streamline student check-ins and accurately track attendance.

QR codes help create a seamless candidate experience, even during peak times or in areas with limited connectivity. You can download them as ready-to-print PDFs or images for use in posters or presentations.

This feature is available to Premium partners with the Events module enabled. For more information, please check out this resource.

Key benefits of using QR codes:

  • Seamless candidate check-in: Create a smooth check-in experience at your booth and avoid losing interested, qualified candidates due to long lines.
  • Offline check-in mode: If your booth lacks reliable WiFi, check-in data will be stored locally and automatically synced once you’re reconnected.
  • Capture attendee info without wifi: Collect candidate details even in low or no WiFi environments to avoid missing valuable connections.

Access event or fair

To download a booth QR code, navigate to the event or fair you want to download it for.

Events

Click Events from the left navigation bar, then select the event for which you want to download the QR code.

Tip: Uncheck the box labeled Include past events to filter out past events.

Fairs

Click Fairs from the left navigation bar, then select the fair you want to download a booth QR code for.

Tip: Check the box labeled Show Registered Only to limit results to fairs your company is registered for.

Download QR code

Event

On the event page, click the More options menu (the three dots) in the upper-right corner, then select Print booth QR code.

Fair

On the fair page, click the More options menu (the three dots) to the right of the Save button, then select Print booth QR code.

If you are registered for multiple sessions, a pop-up modal will appear displaying each session. Select the session for which you want to download a QR code, then choose to download it as a PDF or PNG.

Using the QR code for candidate check-in

Once generated, the QR code will open in a new browser tab, displaying the following information:

  • Your company name

  • The event or fair name

  • The date and time You can:

  • Print the QR code directly from your browser

  • Display it on a device for students to scan during the event Fairs only: You can also download the QR code as a PDF or PNG.

  • PDF files are ready to print

  • PNG files can be added to promotional materials like posters or slides

  • You can also access the QR code from your email. Click the Print QR code button in the notification email you receive.

Candidate check-in process

To check in:

  • The candidate opens the Handshake mobile app or logs into their account via a mobile browser.
  • They scan the QR code using their phone’s camera.
  • The check-in form opens automatically, allowing them to complete the process. Offline mode supported:

If a candidate is using the app in offline mode, the form will still load. Their submission will be stored and synced once an internet connection is restored. Learn more about Checking in Attendees at Events with Unstable WiFi.

After the fair

Following the event:

  • An email summary will be sent to both:

    • The attending representative(s)
    • The user who registered the employer

  • This summary includes the number of candidate check-ins at your booth You can also download detailed attendee information from Handshake, including:

  • Public resumes (if shared)

  • Student profile data Learn more about Accessing Event and Fair RSVPs.

Handshake’s Guide to Hosting Virtual Recruiting Events

Virtual events are a powerful way to enhance your early talent strategy. They help you reach a wider audience while reducing travel-related costs.

Use these guidelines to create, host, and follow up on engaging virtual events.

Features available to Premium partners only are indicated by an asterisk (*). For more information, please check out this resource.

Create an event

For detailed steps, refer to How to Create an Event.

Edit an event

To edit an event, refer to How to Edit an Event.

Handshake Video

*Handshake Video is only available to Premium partners with the Event Manager module.

You can choose between hosting an interactive event or a large event:

  • Interactive events
    • Support up to 100 registrants.
    • Participants can independently unmute themselves and turn on their cameras.
  • Large events
    • Support up to 1,000 registrants.
    • Participants cannot unmute themselves or enable their cameras independently. When creating the event, you can set the total number of hosts and assign teammates as co-hosts afterward.

Note: Only teammates designated as event co-hosts will be able to launch the event.

On the event overview page, click the button Select hosts in the yellow banner located mid-page to add teammates as hosts.

In the pop-up modal, select the teammate to add, then click the button Save.

If you use Handshake Video, you will be able to launch your event video up to 60 minutes early to test audio and video connections.

For assistance with video requirements and troubleshooting, refer to Handshake Video Requirements & Troubleshooting.

Click each headline below to learn best practices for creating and hosting engaging virtual events.

Before the event

  1. Plan your event
  • Set goals: Define your objectives, such as increasing brand awareness or driving applications.
  • Find the right host: Select relatable speakers, like recent grads, for a stronger connection with students.
  • Promote effectively: Tailor outreach to specific roles or groups. Learn how to personalize recruiting outreach for Gen Z.
  1. Choose an event type
  • Office Tours: Show day-to-day life through pre-recorded videos.
  • AMA (Ask Me Anything): Let students ask questions about culture, hiring, and career growth.
  • Employee Panels: Feature relatable alumni and employees to share their career journeys.
  • ERGs (Employee Resource Groups): Highlight inclusivity and support within your organization.
  1. Select a platform

Handshake supports external links for live-streaming. Popular platforms include Zoom, WebEx, YouTube Live, and Facebook Live.

  1. Target your audience

Use Handshake’s segmentation tools to invite priority student groups. Aim for a higher RSVP count than your attendance goal (e.g., target 85 RSVPs for 50 attendees).

During the event

Test audio and video

  • Test audio and video: Login 20 minutes early to test connections and troubleshoot issues. You may take our Handshake Video Test.
  • Track attendance: Use RSVP lists or download attendee data from your streaming platform. Learn more about Accessing Event and Fair RSVPs.
  • Monitor engagement: Assign a moderator to manage chat questions and facilitate discussions. After the event
  1. Follow Up
  • For attendees: Recap key content and share next steps, like applying for open roles.
  • For no-shows: Send a “sorry we missed you” message with your main call to action.
    • Learn more about Messaging Event and Fair RSVPs.
  1. Measure Success

  • Track attendees through your hiring funnel using source codes. This data helps demonstrate ROI to leadership. Pro-tips

  • Timing: Host events on Tuesdays to Thursdays, considering time zones (3–6 pm ET works well nationally).

  • Duration: Keep sessions concise—45 minutes of content plus 15 minutes for Q&A.

  • Authenticity: Foster genuine connections by using casual, unscripted conversations. Looking for the highlights? Download a snapshot of these virtual event takeaways for easy reference.

How QR Code and Offline Check-In Work in Handshake

Students can check in to your event either by using a shared kiosk device, such as a tablet or laptop, or by scanning a QR code with the Handshake mobile app.

This article describes how QR code check-ins function, outlines offline mode capabilities, and highlights key limitations, particularly when custom questions are included.

For instructions on launching the kiosk for your event, refer to Launching a Check-In Kiosk.

Overview of check-in methods

Handshake supports two primary check-in options for in-person events:

  • Kiosk device: Students check in using a shared device provided by your team (e.g., a tablet or laptop).
  • QR code: Students scan a printed QR code using the Handshake mobile app on their personal device. Both options allow attendees to record their check-in and complete any required fields configured in your kiosk setup.

QR code check-in requirements

To successfully check in using a QR code:

  • The student must have the Handshake mobile app installed.
  • Their device must be connected to the internet to fully load the check-in interface and display any custom questions. Students without the app or internet access may not be able to complete check-in via QR code.

Offline mode in kiosks

Handshake kiosks support offline mode, allowing check-ins even when internet access is unavailable. The process is as follows:

  • The kiosk must be launched online before it can operate offline.
  • After launch, check-ins are stored locally on the device.
  • When the device reconnects to the internet, the check-in data automatically syncs to Handshake.
  • If the device is shut down before syncing, reopen the kiosk on the same device to upload the saved data.

Limitations with offline QR code check-in

QR code check-in behavior depends on the student’s mobile device, not the kiosk. If a student scans a QR code without an internet connection, the following may occur:

  • If the Handshake app is installed, the student’s profile data (e.g., name and email) may still pre-fill.
  • Custom questions (e.g., competencies, areas of interest, job preferences):
    • Will not appear if the app cannot load the kiosk configuration due to a lack of internet.
    • If the questions are loaded before losing connection, the student can still complete them.
    • Any questions that fail to load will not be displayed or saved.

How to Pay for an Event

This resource will provide the steps on how to pay for an invoice you have received for an on-campus event.

To pay for an on-campus event:

  • The Payment Status on the registration must be “Invoiced”.

  • You must have a role other than Representative. If you do not have access, reach out to your company’s Owner or Admin to request a role change or permission. For more information, refer to Who is the Owner of My Company’s Profile? Payments can be made from the Event overview page on Handshake. There are two ways to access the event overview page:

  • An invoice sent via email

  • Manual search

Invoice via email

When a school sends an invoice for an on-campus event, the registrant will receive an email in their inbox. The invoice will contain a link to view the event, and another to download the invoice.

Click the View Event link to be directed to the Event overview page in Handshake.

  • If you experience any technical issues, navigate directly to Handshake to view the registration.
  • To proceed with a manual payment, you’ll need to follow the school’s provided instructions, or connect with the career fair’s point of contact. The email will read:

From: Handshake <handshake@notifications.joinhandshake.com

Subject: “Invoice for Attending event [EVENT NAME]”

Heading: “Your invoice has arrived!”

Body: “Hello [EVENT REGISTRANT FIRST NAME],

Invoice #[NUMBER]

Your invoice has arrived! [SCHOOL NAME] has invoiced you for the [EVENT NAME] career fair registration. Your total comes to [COST].

View Event [LINK]

Host: [SCHOOL NAME]

Event Date: [DATE OF EVENT]

Payment Instructions: [AS PROVIDED BY SCHOOL]

Refund Policy: [AS PROVIDED BY SCHOOL]

Please contact [SCHOOL NAME] for any questions.

Download Invoice [LINK]

Thank you,

[SCHOOL NAME]”

Manual search

  1. Click Events from the left navigation bar in Handshake, then select the event you want to pay for.

Tip: Click the white button Include past events in the header and uncheck the box to the left of “Include past events” to filter out past events.

  1. Once the event is selected, click the black button Pay Now in the upper-right corner of the page.
  • If the Pay Now button is not available, the school has not yet created an invoice for the event.
  1. Follow the prompts to complete your payment.

Launching a Check-in Kiosk

Once your kiosk has been created and configured, you’re ready to launch it for use at your in-person or hybrid event.

Haven’t set up your kiosk yet? Start by Creating a Check-In Kiosk.

This feature is available to Premium partners with the Events module enabled. For more information, please check out this resource.

Launch the kiosk

Click the black button Launch in the upper-right corner of the Kiosk setup tab on the event page.

A pop-up modal will appear to provide information about weak connections and offline mode. Click the black button Okay to proceed.

  • We offer offline check-ins for locations that have limited or no internet connectivity.
  • QR code check-ins are dependent on the student’s mobile connection.
  • If a student is offline, their check-ins will be logged once they regain an internet connection.

After the kiosk is launched

  • Students with a Handshake profile will see their basic information pre-filled.

  • They will be prompted to complete any additional fields configured by your team (e.g., graduation date, competencies, areas of interest).

  • Students without a Handshake account will be prompted to register as a guest and complete the check-in form. Students can check in using:

  • A shared kiosk device (tablet or laptop)

  • Their own device by scanning the event’s printed QR code (if available) Learn more about How QR Code and Offline Check-In Work in Handshake.

To access and review your RSVPs, refer to Accessing Event and Fair RSVPs.

Who can create or manage events based on my account type?

Personalizing an RSVP Confirmation Email for Events

To increase student engagement and attendance at your events, you can add a personalized note to the automated RSVP confirmation email sent to students upon registration.

Adding a custom message allows you to reinforce key details, provide clear expectations, and create a more engaging experience for students.

This feature is available to Premium partners with the Handshake Events module. For more information, please check out this resource.

Access event

  1. Click Events from the left navigation bar, then select the event where you want to add a personalized note.

  2. On the event page, click the Communications tab.

The Communications tab provides an overview of all automated messages sent to students, including RSVP confirmation emails.

Here, you can:

  • Preview transactional messages.
  • Check the status of messages.
  • Add a personalized note to RSVP confirmation emails to provide additional information for students.

Add a personalized note

  1. Locate the RSVP confirmation message in the Message column.

  2. Click the RSVPs button in the Audience column to the right of that message.

  3. In the window that opens, enter your personalized note in the text box below the heading ‘Notes from the host (optional)’. You may use the formatting toolbar at the bottom of the text box to customize your message or include links.

  4. When you are finished, click the black button Confirm to save your note.

  5. Your message will be automatically included in the RSVP confirmation email sent to registrants.

  • To return to the previous page, click the black button Close.

Preview or edit note

  1. To preview or edit your note after adding it, navigate to the event where the note was added.

  2. Click the three-dot menu icon to the right of the RSVP confirmation email status, then select Preview from the dropdown.

  3. On the preview page, you can take the following actions:

  • To preview only: Review the message, then click Close to exit without making changes.
  • To edit: Click Edit note.
  • To delete: Click the red trash bin icon to permanently remove the note.

View email status

To check the status of the RSVP confirmation email, navigate to the Status column on the event page.

  • Ready to send: The email is prepared and waiting to be sent to registrants.
  • Sent: The email has been successfully sent to registrants. To create a custom automated follow-up message for evaluated candidates, refer to Creating Automated Follow-Up Messages for Evaluated Event Attendees.

Preparing for the Day-of an Event

To ensure a smooth and successful event experience, it’s important to prepare your team in advance.

This article outlines key actions to take in the 1–2 weeks leading up to your event to help your team feel confident and ready to engage with attendees.

Follow these best practices to create a seamless experience for both your team and attendees.

1. Confirm team access to Handshake

All teammates participating in the event should have individual, active Handshake accounts connected to the correct company profile.

Before the event:

  • Ensure each rep is connected to your company’s Handshake profile.
  • Verify that new teammates have been approved by a company owner or admin.
  • If a teammate joined the wrong profile, direct them to Leaving a Company in Handshake. Need help managing team access? Refer to How to Approve Teammates at a Company.

2. Review attendee RSVPs

Familiarize yourself with the students who plan to attend. Reviewing the RSVP list ahead of time allows you to tailor conversations, identify potential candidates, and prepare your team accordingly.

To preview your attendee list before the event, refer to Accessing Event and Fair RSVPs.

3. Set up the check-in kiosk (Premium partners only)

Premium partners with the Events module and create and customize a check-in kiosk to collect student information.

Haven’t set up your kiosk yet? Start by Creating a Check-In Kiosk

4. Print QR codes and materials

Prepare signage or printed materials, including:

  • Event QR codes (for students to check in via mobile)
  • Role-specific talking points, company collateral, or swag (if applicable) Need to download a QR code for your event booth? Refer to Download an Event or Fair Booth QR Code

5. Confirm device setup

Ensure you have the necessary hardware for check-in and engagement:

  • A tablet or laptop for the kiosk (if applicable)
  • Reliable Wi-Fi or a hotspot if the venue’s connection is limited
  • Chargers or battery packs for kiosk devices

6. Align with your team

Hold a brief team prep meeting before the event to confirm:

  • Who will be managing check-in
  • Who is responsible for follow-up with students
  • Talking points or roles during the event
