Registration per division is supported (multiple registrations per company)

Creating a New Virtual Fair

A virtual fair is a great way to engage students and employers in a remote environment. In Handshake, we provide flexibility in creating and hosting virtual fairs, either hosted in Handshake or externally, while tracking registrations and data for reporting purposes.

If your institution is planning to host both in-person and virtual fairs, check out our resource, Best Practices: Hybrid Fairs!

  1. Click Fairs on the left navigation bar to get started. You’ll be taken to the Fairs overview page where fairs your school has already created or been invited to are listed.

  2. Click the New Career Fair tab in the upper-right corner of the page.

Basic Information

- Career Fair Name
- Career Fair Logo (for our image size guide, refer to [Handshake Image Size Guide](https://support.joinhandshake.com/hc/en-us/articles/219132827))
- *Career center (this will only appear if you have more than one career center configured for fairs)
- Point of Contact for Students (select from an existing contact or create a new one)
- Status
    - Published: visible to students and employers
    - Drafting: only visible to career service users

Location

The fair must be set to Virtual and facilitated in Handshake for employers to be able to set schedules.

  • Is this career fair in-person or virtual?
    • In-Person
    • Virtual (select Virtual)
  • Is this career fair facilitated on Handshake? (select one)
    • Yes
    • No (if no, “This virtual career fair is facilitated on another site, but students and employers can discover and RSVP through Handshake.”)
      • Student Registration Link (add link to textbox if fair is not facilitated on Handshake)
  • Location (inactive field — this is for in-person fairs only)
  • Currency: Select either USD, GBD, or EUR. Dates and Times

Virtual fairs are each limited to one session (date and time) and six hours to reduce scheduling complexity.

If you would like to run a multi day fair, you can use the duplicate option to quickly create multiple fairs.

  • Time Zone (confirm the time zone from the dropdown)

  • Student RSVP Limit (inactive field — this is for in-person fairs only)

  • Start Time & End Time (click the calendar icon to the right of the box to choose. Virtual fairs cannot exceed 6 hours — you’ll receive an error message if you select more than 6 hours)

    • Tip: we recommend a 3 hour fair!

  • Focus Area (if you plan to host multiple virtual fairs with specific focus areas for each – for example: Engineering Students, Companies Hiring Designers, etc.)

  • Industry focus (select employer industries that you’d like to be represented at the fair, if you aren’t sure, select All)

  • 1:1 session duration (Select one or multiple. These cannot be changed after an employer has built out their schedule and selected sessions.)

    • 10 minutes
    • 15 minutes
    • 20 minutes
    • 30 minutes
    • 45 minutes
    • 60 minutes

  • Group session duration (Select one or multiple. These cannot be changed after an employer has built out their schedule and selected sessions.)

    • 10 minutes
    • 15 minutes
    • 20 minutes
    • 30 minutes
    • 45 minutes
    • 60 minutes

  • Booth Map (inactive field — this is for in-person fairs only)

  • Add new date and time (not selectable for virtual fairs facilitated in Handshake)

    • If you create or edit a fair that has both a Virtual fair type and the Facilitated in Handshake = No selected, the “Add new date and time” button will be available. Student Information

  • Career fair is invite-only (check the box if only invited students should attend)

  • Student registration start and end dates and times(click the calendar icon to the right of the box to choose)

  • Estimated student attendance(enter the number of students that you expect to register for this career fair)

  • Student registration survey (add a survey from the dropdown you’d like students to complete as part of registration. If you aren’t able to locate the survey you want to include, create it by clicking the link.)

  • Make available to ALL non-Handshake schools (check the box to allow any student on Handshake with a non-partnered school, and/or community members, to view and register for this fair) Employer Information

  • Hide this career fair from employers (check the box to hide the fair)

    • Note: if the fair is hidden, employers won’t be able to discover the career fair unless you share the employer preview link with them.

  • Employer registration start and end dates and times (click the calendar icon to the right of the box to choose)

  • Estimated employer registrations (enter the number of employers you expect to register for this fair)

  • Employer instructions (enter any instructions that should be displayed to employers on the registration page, not visible to students)

  • Employer payment methods (select one or both)

    • Credit Card (payments have to be enabled at your school to select Credit Card)
    • Other

  • Payment Instructions (enter any payment instructions. These are sent to the employer within the invoice notification email and will also appear on the employer invoice if you allow “Other” as a payment method)

  • Approve Employers before invoicing (check the box if required)

  • Employer refund policy (enter the refund policy for the fair. These instructions are sent in the invoice notification email and are on the invoice if you allow manual payments.)

  • Company description limit (enter the maximum character length of the company description–the default is 750 characters)

  • Allow all majors (check this if you want employers to specify that they accept all majors on registration)

  • Choose majors (click the Choose Majors button if you want to restrict the majors employers can select from)

  • Employer registration survey (select a survey you’d like employers to complete as part of registration, or create a new survey if needed.)

  • Survey title (this title appears as the heading for your employer registration survey. If you leave this field blank, the title will default to “Extra Questions.”) Messaging

  • Student description (enter the career fair description that’s shown to students)

  • Student welcome message (enter a message that’s emailed to students after they register for this career fair)

  • Employer description (enter the career fair description that’s shown to employers)

  • Employer welcome message (enter a message that’s emailed to employers after you approve their career fair registration)

  • Default invoice message (enter a message to invoice a registered employer — you’ll be able to add a custom message when sending the invoice as well) Additional Information

The fields for Name tag printing and Name tag XML are inactive for virtual fairs.

Click the green Create Career Fair button in the lower-right corner of your page to save your setup!

Next Steps: Configure Details

You’ve now created the basic structure of your career fair — now it’s time to configure additional details for your fair!

When the fair has been created, you’ll be taken to a page where you can edit the basics you just created and add more details. The default view will be on the Details tab, and you can use the boxes on the left side of the page to navigate:

  • Create Registration Types
  • Add Extra Item Options
  • Create (and Apply) Discounts
  • Set Student Qualifications
  • Add Invited Schools

Transitioning a Physical Fair to Virtual

Note: in-person fairs cannot transition to virtual if it is within 3 weeks of the fair date.

  • Make sure that your fair is only one session and within 6 hours from start to end
  • Change the Location type to Virtual
  • Change the facilitation type to Handshake Learn more in Change an Existing Fair to a Virtual Fair.

FAQs

We are hearing that employers will be more likely to participate in a virtual event if it is on a smaller more targeted scale. Is this true?

  • Handshake does recommend smaller, industry-focused events. In addition, we have heard from employers that they are interested in these types of interaction as well. Can we support graduate school events, volunteer opportunities, and student organization events through your virtual fair feature?

  • If these types of organizations have Handshake profiles and job postings, then yes, you can support these types of events in Handshake.

  • Note: the language in the product will be oriented to fairs, and we won’t be creating specific fair types for graduate school, volunteer, or student organizations.

  • Also, please keep in mind that non-career related fairs might make your video usage exceed typical fair use. If you plan on supporting non-career center fairs, please let your Relationship Manager know. How many virtual fairs or events can a school run at the same time?

  • Handshake supports hosting multiple fairs at the same time. There’s no capacity limit of fairs per day. I received an error about too many virtual sessions or too long of a limit, but I’m not ready to adjust those yet. What can I do?

  • Change the fair type to facilitated outside of Handshake so you can save other updates. Then, when you’re ready to adjust your sessions, you can switch the host type back to virtual. Is there an end date timeline for employer registrants to consider? i.e. two weeks in advance of the date to allow time for booth set up, etc.?

  • Since employers will need to setup a schedule we recommend that you close employer registration 3 weeks prior to the career fair.

Fairs

Best Practices: Representing Divisions at Virtual Fairs

Virtual fairs on Handshake allow employers to host consecutive sessions throughout the event and support up to 100 company representatives per registration.

If your company has multiple divisions participating, follow these best practices to help students clearly understand and engage with each one.

Update your title in Handshake

Update your title to reflect the specific division you represent. This helps students identify which team you’re part of when scheduling 1:1 sessions.

To update your profile, refer to Employer Account: Update My Profile.

Example: How your title appears to students when scheduling 1:1 or group sessions:

Include division names in group session titles

When creating or editing group sessions, include the division name in the title and provide relevant context in the description to help students select the right session.

Example: How division names appear to students in group session listings:

Claiming a Virtual Fair Schedule

To meet with students during a virtual career fair on Handshake, you must first claim your schedule. Claiming ensures that students can see your availability and sign up for sessions.

In addition to claiming your own schedule, you can also claim a schedule on behalf of a teammate.

Note: An employer user account is required to claim a schedule. Not set up yet? Learn How to Create an Employer Account on Handshake.

Topics:

  • Claim your schedule via email
  • Claim your schedule on Handshake
  • Claim your teammate’s schedule on their behalf

Claim your schedule via email

If your organization sets up a schedule for you, you’ll receive an email invitation with fair details:

The email will read:

From: Handshake <handshake@m.joinhandshake.com

Subject: “You have been invited to a career fair”

Body:

Fair details

[NAME OF FAIR]

Time

Invited by:

Please review and claim your spot at this fair as soon as possible. Students will not be able to sign up to meet with you until you have completed this.

More info about virtual fairs (hyperlinked)

[Review and claim schedule] button.”

Click the black button Review and claim schedule to log in and confirm your spot. Students won’t be able to sign up for your sessions until this is completed.

💡 Missing the email? You can also claim your schedule directly in Handshake.

Claim your schedule on Handshake

  1. Click Fairs from the left navigation bar, then select the fair you want to claim your schedule for.

Tip: Check the Show Registered Only box to view only the fairs you’ve registered for.

  1. On the career fair overview page, click the Schedule tab, then click the white button Manage.

  2. In the pop-up modal, click the blue button Claim schedule.

  • If the pop-up modal does not appear, you can also click the blue button Claim Schedule on the Schedule tab.

Claim your teammate’s schedule on their behalf

In the Schedule tab, locate their name from the Name dropdown, then click the blue button Claim Schedule.

  • Ensure your teammate is available on the day of the fair.
  • Teammates will not be notified when their schedule is claimed for them. Once a schedule has been claimed, you can edit or manage it as needed. Learn more about Managing Schedules for Virtual Fairs.

Connecting Your Jobs to Your Fair Registrations

Connect your job postings to your fair registrations in Handshake to increase visibility and encourages engagement from qualified student candidates.

You can only connect jobs to a fair after submitting your registration for that specific career fair. If you have not registered yet, start by registering for the fair first. Learn more about Registering for a Fair (Employers).

Access your fair registration

  • Click Fairs in the left navigation bar.
  • Select the fair whose registration you want to connect a job to. Tip: On the Fair page, check the box labeled Show Registered Only. This filters the list to display all upcoming fairs your company is registered for, including any pending school approval.

Connect a job to your fair registration

  1. Click the Jobs tab on the career fair page.

  2. Click the white Add job button in the middle of the page, or in the upper-right corner.

  3. In the pop-up modal, choose the job you want to connect from the dropdown, then click the black Done button.

Note: Only approved jobs can be added to a fair. If you cannot find a job, it may still be awaiting school approval.

  • If you haven’t created the job yet, click the white Create a job button in the pop-up.

Connect jobs to multiple fair registrations

If you have multiple divisions registered for the same fair, use the registration dropdown to choose the division you want to connect a job to, then click the white Add job button.

Note: Jobs must be added to each registration individually.

Remove a job from your fair registration

  1. Click the More options menu (the three dots) to the right of the job, then select Remove job from the fair.

  2. In the pop-up modal, click the red Yes, remove button to confirm.

Note: Removing a job from a fair hides it from that fair’s participants, but the job itself remains active on Handshake. Students, including fair participants, can still find and apply to it.

Creating a Schedule for Virtual Fairs

After your company’s fair registration is approved, the schedule owner can create the initial schedule in Handshake.

The schedule can include group sessions, 1:1 sessions, or a combination of both, based on your company’s goals for connecting with students.

Note: Only the Schedule Owner can create the initial schedule. If another team member should manage this, refer to Managing Schedules for Virtual Fairs.

After your company’s fair registration is approved, the schedule owner will receive an email notification to add the schedule. If the email is not received, navigate to the fair in Handshake.

Add a schedule

  1. Click on the black button Add Schedule in the email, or on the Schedule tab from the fair overview page.

Email

Career fair overview page

  1. Click the black button Setup to access the Create Schedule form, which is divided into four sections:
  • Add team members
  • Add group sessions
  • Add 1:1 sessions
  • Review schedule

Add team members

In the Add team members section, check the box next to each team member who will represent your company at the fair, then click the blue button Add team in the lower-right corner of the page.

To find a specific teammate, use the search field to narrow down the displayed list.

Note: There is a limit of 100 team members per virtual fair registration.

  • All team members must have an active Handshake account to launch a Handshake video session.
  • Team members listed without a role and marked as ‘Unclaimed Account’ had accounts created on their behalf but have not yet claimed them (i.e., confirmed the account and set a password).
  • If a teammate doesn’t appear on the list, they likely don’t have a Handshake account yet or aren’t connected to your company.
    • Recruiters can manually add teammates or invite colleagues to join their company on Handshake, if this setting is enabled by the company profile owner or admin.
      • If enabled, recruiters will have two options to invite a teammate who is not yet on Handshake.
        • Copy Invite Link: Click this button to copy a link to share with your colleague. This allows them to create their own account and connect directly to your company profile once their account is confirmed.
        • Add Teammate Manually: Click this button to create an account for your colleague. They will receive an email prompting them to confirm their account and set a password. Once the account is claimed, you’ll be able to add them to group or 1:1 sessions.

Add group sessions

Group session durations, ranging from 10 to 60 minutes, are determined by the school hosting the fair. Employers can schedule as many group sessions as needed using either Handshake Video or an external provider.

Note: Employers cannot set qualifications for group sessions.

  1. Is your organization planning to have group sessions with students? (select Yes/No)
  • If No, click the blue button Confirm sessions in the lower-right corner to proceed.
  • If Yes, provide a response to the following questions:
    • Are you using Handshake Video or another video tool? (select one)
      • Handshake video session
        • *Would you like to record these sessions? (Select Yes/No)
          • Note: this feature is only available to Premium partners.
        • Title
        • Description
        • How many people from your team will host this event?
          • Note: When using Handshake Video, please note that there’s a maximum limit of 100 attendees at a time, including team members. Any restrictions for external providers are set by the provider you select.
        • Duration
        • Time
      • External video platform
        • Note: If you prefer to use an external video provider for 1:1 sessions, you can update each session individually after the schedule is created.
        • Title
        • Description
        • Video URL
        • URLs should begin with http:// or https://.
        • Duration
        • Time To add another session, click the blue hyperlinked text +Add Another Session, then follow the same steps to enter the session details.
  1. Once you’ve added all the desired sessions, click the blue button Confirm sessions to continue.

3.Select the team members leading the group session(s). Multiple team members can host group sessions.

  • You can add up to the specified number of team members per group session. If you try to add more than the allowed number, you will not be able to proceed.
  1. Once you’ve added the team members leading the group session(s), click the blue button Assign team to continue.

Add 1:1 sessions

1:1 session durations, ranging from 10 to 60 minutes, are determined by the school hosting the fair.

These sessions allow your team members to meet individually with qualified students for video conversations.

  1. To add a 1:1 session for yourself or a team member, click the hyperlinked text Add 1:1 session.
  • If 1:1 sessions are not being held, click the blue button Assign team. Tip: If teammates from multiple divisions are hosting 1:1 sessions, we recommend they add their division name to their title in their Employer Account User Settings. This helps students easily identify who they are meeting, especially if they’ve signed up for multiple 1:1 sessions.
  1. Select the duration of the 1:1 session and indicate if you want to add any student qualification requirements.
  • If you want to add qualification requirements, click the blue button Add requirements.
  • If you prefer not to add qualification requirements, click the blue button Schedule sessions. Adding requirements
  1. On the Student Qualification Requirements form, choose your preferred qualifications, then click the blue button Add and schedule sessions.
  • Qualifications can be changed up until the fair starts. After the fair begins, the only option will be to clear all qualifications.
  • By selecting qualifications, you limit student sign-ups to only those who meet the criteria. Students who do not meet the selected qualifications will be unable to sign up for 1:1 sessions.
    • To help fill any empty 1:1 sessions, we offer an automated feature that pauses your session qualifications 48 hours before the fair.
      • To opt out of this feature, select No, keep my qualifications in place the whole time.
      • If you opt into the feature, you will receive a reminder email 72 hours before the fair, allowing you to opt out at that time if desired.
  1. Once you are finished, click the blue button Add and schedule sessions in the lower-right corner.
  • This will return you to the 1:1 sessions page, where you can add additional sessions for other team members. Repeat the steps above for each team member as needed.
  1. Once you have added all the 1:1 sessions, click the blue button Assign team to proceed.

Review schedule

Review the group and 1:1 sessions to confirm the session details, then click the blue button Confirm schedule and invite team to generate an email for team members to claim their schedules.

Once the initial schedule is created, any team member, regardless of role, can add new group sessions, 1:1 schedules, and take other actions as outlined in Managing Schedules for Virtual Fairs.

Day-of Checklist for Events and Career Fairs (Fairs)

Use this checklist to help your team prepare for in-person or hybrid events and career fairs hosted on Handshake.

Follow these key steps before and during the event to ensure a smooth, successful experience for staff and attendees.

Before the event

Access the event on Handshake

  • Make sure you can access the event and navigate the Handshake platform either through the Events app or a desktop browser.
    • iOS users: Download the Handshake Events app from the App Store
    • Web users: Log in at app.joinhandshake.com If you’re new to the Handshake Events app, take a few minutes to explore its layout and functionality before the day of the event.

Confirm QR codes are printed

Your event lead should provide printed QR codes for attendee check-in. Bring them with you and display them clearly at the event.

Need a full pre-event checklist? Review Preparing for the Day-of an Event.

Day of the event

Set up check-in stations

  • Place printed QR codes in a visible location at the entrance of your booth.

  • Optional: Provide a tablet or laptop on a stand for attendees who prefer not to use their phone or do not have one. Launch the kiosk

  • Launch the kiosk while connected to a reliable internet connection, ideally before arriving at the event. Need help launching your kiosk? Refer to Launching a Check-In Kiosk.

  • Once launched, the kiosk will stay active throughout the event, even if your device temporarily loses its internet connection. To understand how offline mode and QR code check-in work, see How QR Code and Offline Check-In Work in Handshake.

Greet and prompt attendees to check in

  • Encourage attendees to scan the QR code or check in via the tablet or laptop station. Troubleshoot check-In issues

Experiencing connectivity problems or check-in errors? There are steps you can take to keep check-ins running smoothly, even without internet access.

For detailed troubleshooting steps and offline check-in tips, refer to:

  • Troubleshooting Errors with the Handshake Events App
  • Checking in Attendees at Events with Unstable WiFi

During the event

Find and open the event in Handshake

  • Open the Handshake Events app, or log in at app.joinhandshake.com
  • Locate and open the event or fair you want to manage Evaluate attendees

You can evaluate attendees using either the Handshake Events app or the web version. Evaluations can include a thumbs up/down rating, notes, and labels to help your team track and engage with candidates after the event.

  • For the web version, navigate to the event or fair page and click the Candidates tab. Attendees will appear in real time as they check in. Refresh the page periodically to view the most recent check-ins.
  • For the app, tap Check-ins within the event to view attendees who have checked in and require evaluation. Curious about how to rate candidates or add notes during the event? Read more about Managing RSVPs with Evaluations, Notes, & Labels.

Report any issues or feedback to your event lead

  • Share anything that went well or could be improved for future events.

Download an Event or Fair Booth QR Code (Fairs)

For each event or fair session you’re registered for, you can download a QR code to streamline student check-ins and accurately track attendance.

QR codes help create a seamless candidate experience, even during peak times or in areas with limited connectivity. You can download them as ready-to-print PDFs or images for use in posters or presentations.

This feature is available to Premium partners with the Events module enabled. For more information, please check out this resource.

Key benefits of using QR codes:

  • Seamless candidate check-in: Create a smooth check-in experience at your booth and avoid losing interested, qualified candidates due to long lines.
  • Offline check-in mode: If your booth lacks reliable WiFi, check-in data will be stored locally and automatically synced once you’re reconnected.
  • Capture attendee info without wifi: Collect candidate details even in low or no WiFi environments to avoid missing valuable connections.

Access event or fair

To download a booth QR code, navigate to the event or fair you want to download it for.

Events

Click Events from the left navigation bar, then select the event for which you want to download the QR code.

Tip: Uncheck the box labeled Include past events to filter out past events.

Fairs

Click Fairs from the left navigation bar, then select the fair you want to download a booth QR code for.

Tip: Check the box labeled Show Registered Only to limit results to fairs your company is registered for.

Download QR code

Event

On the event page, click the More options menu (the three dots) in the upper-right corner, then select Print booth QR code.

Fair

On the fair page, click the More options menu (the three dots) to the right of the Save button, then select Print booth QR code.

If you are registered for multiple sessions, a pop-up modal will appear displaying each session. Select the session for which you want to download a QR code, then choose to download it as a PDF or PNG.

Using the QR code for candidate check-in

Once generated, the QR code will open in a new browser tab, displaying the following information:

  • Your company name

  • The event or fair name

  • The date and time You can:

  • Print the QR code directly from your browser

  • Display it on a device for students to scan during the event Fairs only: You can also download the QR code as a PDF or PNG.

  • PDF files are ready to print

  • PNG files can be added to promotional materials like posters or slides

  • You can also access the QR code from your email. Click the Print QR code button in the notification email you receive.

Candidate check-in process

To check in:

  • The candidate opens the Handshake mobile app or logs into their account via a mobile browser.
  • They scan the QR code using their phone’s camera.
  • The check-in form opens automatically, allowing them to complete the process. Offline mode supported:

If a candidate is using the app in offline mode, the form will still load. Their submission will be stored and synced once an internet connection is restored. Learn more about Checking in Attendees at Events with Unstable WiFi.

After the fair

Following the event:

  • An email summary will be sent to both:

    • The attending representative(s)
    • The user who registered the employer

  • This summary includes the number of candidate check-ins at your booth You can also download detailed attendee information from Handshake, including:

  • Public resumes (if shared)

  • Student profile data Learn more about Accessing Event and Fair RSVPs.

Following Up After a Fair

With Handshake, you can easily manage and follow up with your participants after your in-person or virtual sessions are finished.

Communicate directly with candidates, add evaluations and labels to track progress and preferences, and seamlessly download resumes to review qualifications and further your recruitment goals.

Access fair

  1. Click Fairs from the left navigation bar.

  2. On the Career Fairs page, use the following filters to narrow your search:

  • Include Past Fairs
  • Show Registered Only 💡 You can also use keyword search, filter by school, location type, or set a date range to find a specific fair.
  1. Select the relevant fair from the list of results.

Follow-up with RSVPs

  1. On the career fair page, click the Candidates tab. Learn more about Accessing Event and Fair RSVPs.

  2. The candidate table displays a list of students who have RSVP’d or checked in to your sessions.

Use the filters at the top of the table to refine your view.

Note: Filters marked with an asterisk (*) are available to Premium partners only.

Available filters include:

  • Keyword search: Search by name, school, or other attributes.
  • *Status: Shows whether a student checked in, RSVP’d, or received an evaluation.
  • *Evaluation: Indicates if an evaluation has been submitted for a candidate.
  • School: Filter by the student’s institution. To access more filters, click the Filters button. A side panel will appear with additional options.
  1. From the Candidates tab, you can:
  • Add evaluations, notes, and labels. Read more in Managing RSVPs with Evaluations, Notes, & Labels.
  • Send messages to RSVPs and attendees. Learn more about Messaging Event and Fair RSVPs.
  • Download public resumes of students who checked in. Find out more about Downloading Public Resumes.

Hosting Virtual Fair Sessions

Handshake supports both integrated video through our partnership with Daily and externally hosted sessions.

Employers can host their virtual fair sessions using Handshake video or an external video provider. This article explains how to launch your sessions and outlines when and how students can join during the fair.

To prepare for the best possible experience, we recommend reviewing this resource ahead of the fair Preparing for the Day-of a Virtual Fair.

On the day of the fair

You can launch a session up to 60 minutes before the scheduled start time. Students can join up to 5 minutes before the session begins to test their connection, so you may notice students entering slightly early.

Launch your session on Handshake

  1. From the left navigation bar, click Fairs. Locate your fair, then click the Schedule tab.

  2. On the far right of the session name, click the blue Launch video button to start your session.

Note: The Launch video button is only available for sessions that have at least one student signed up.

  1. On the launch screen, review and adjust your audio and video settings. To enter the session, click the Join button. Learn more about Hosting via Video on Handshake.

Hosting a session with an external video provider

If a session is hosted externally, Handshake displays the external link so students can access it at the scheduled time.

For externally hosted sessions:

  • Students are presented with a Join external video button on the session page
  • This button becomes available 5 minutes before the scheduled start time.
  • Clicking the Join external video button directs students to the external platform you provided.
  • Students are able to access the external link even if you are not logged into Handshake. Tip: We recommend checking your external link before the fair begins to ensure a smooth experience.

How to Search for a Career Fair

Use this article to find upcoming career fairs on Handshake, locate fairs your company has attended, and find fairs you previously saved.

How do I search for a career fair?

  1. Click Fairs in the left navigation bar.

  2. Use the filters and search bar on the left side of the page to narrow your results:

  • Keyword search: Search by school name or fair title.
  • Show Favorite Schools Only: View fairs hosted by your favorite schools.
  • Show Followed Only: View fairs you saved.
  • Location: Filter by geographic location and adjust the mile radius.
  • School: Filter by a specific school.
    • Tip: To view career fairs hosted by specific schools only, use the School filter by itself and avoid combining it with Location or Location Type filters.
  • Location Type: Choose between in-person or virtual fairs.
  • Include Past Fairs: Show fairs your company registered for previously.
  • Show Registered Only: Show only fairs your company is already registered for.
  • Show Open for Registration: Show fairs that are currently open for registration.
  • Date: Filter by a specific date range. Note: Fairs your company has already registered for display a status such as Approved Registration or Pending Registration next to the fair’s name.

What other ways can I search for a career fair?

  1. Go to the school’s homepage on Handshake.

  2. Scroll to the Upcoming Career Fairs section.

  3. Click a fair’s name for more information about that fair, or click View All Upcoming Career Fairs to view every upcoming fair posted by that school.

How do I find a career fair I saved or bookmarked?

  1. On the Fairs page, set the Show Followed Only filter to Yes.

  2. Fairs you saved will appear in the results.

Managing Schedules for Virtual Fairs

After creating your company’s initial schedule, you can continue managing it as needed.

All teammates in Handshake can manage the schedule, regardless of their role. However, there are a few exceptions:

  • Only Recruiters, Owners, or Admins can change the schedule owner while employer registration is open.
  • Only the schedule owner can cancel group sessions.
  • Representatives cannot launch or manage group sessions, including editing or canceling them. To watch a guided tutorial, check out our course on Events and career fairs on Handshake.

Access fair

  1. Click Fairs from the left navigation bar, then select the fair you want to manage.

Tip: Check the box for “Show Registered Only” to narrow your search results.

  1. On the overview page, click the Schedule tab, then click the white button Manage.
  • Sessions will display the number of open and booked sessions.
  • Group and 1:1 sessions are listed in the order of their start time, for each teammate.
  1. If you’re included in the schedule, your sessions will be displayed by default.
  • To view another teammate’s schedule, select their name from the Name dropdown.

Manage schedule

Change schedule owner

You can change the schedule owner on your fair registration as long as the employer registration window is still open.

  • If the registration window has closed and the edit button is no longer visible, please contact the Career Services office for assistance in changing the owner. Find How to Contact a School.

  1. On the overview page, click the gray button Registered button in the upper-right corner of the page, then select View registration.

  2. Click the Edit tab in the upper-right corner of the registration page.

  3. Scroll to the Basic Information section, click into the Schedule Owner dropdown, then select the teammate that should be the new schedule owner. The dropdown will list all active teammates at your company.

Note: The schedule owner must have the role of Recruiter, Owner, or Admin to set the schedule for a fair.

  1. Click the blue button Update Registration in the lower-right corner to save your changes.

Note: The teammate will not be notified of the change, so please communicate with them once you have updated the registration.

Create a new group session

  1. On the Schedule tab, click the white button Manage.

  2. Click the white button Manage Sessions, then select Create new from the dropdown.

  3. In the pop-up modal, select what type of session you want to create. Click Group session.

  4. The pop-up modal will expand to include fields to complete.

  • Are you using Handshake Video or another video tool? (select one)
    • Handshake video session
    • External video platform
      • If External video platform is selected, enter the URL in the Video URL text field.
  • Title
  • Description

Ensure team has active accounts

  • After teammates register for their account and connect to the company profile, they can be added to virtual fair sessions.

Virtual career fairs

Fellowship Expectations

Fellowship work authorization eligibility

To join Handshake AI as a US person (US citizen, resident, or as otherwise defined by the IRS), you must:

  • Have a Social Security Number (SSN) or Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN); and
  • Have a valid US work authorization that can be supported by Handshake. For International Fellows: Participation is currently invite-only, however, if you haven’t yet received an invitation, you’re welcome to create and maintain an active profile. Not sure if your invite is legitimate? Review tips to recognize legitimate communications.

SSN or ITIN

A SSN or ITIN is required to complete onboarding and receive payment. If you do not yet have an SSN or ITIN, you must wait until you’ve received one to complete your application and onboarding steps.

Supported work authorizations

  • US Citizens and Lawful Permanent Residents
  • F-1 Visa Holders
    • CPT (Curricular Practical Training)
    • OPT (Optional Practical Training)
  • Other Supported Work Authorizations
US citizens and lawful permanent residents

US Citizens and lawful permanent residents (green card holders) are eligible to participate in Handshake AI.

F-1 visa holders

F-1 students may be eligible to participate in Handshake AI through either CPT (Curricular Practical Training) or Optional Practical Training (OPT). CPT/OPT supervision may not be available for every project, especially ones that are not domain-specific.

Participation in these programs also must be approved by your Designated School Official (DSO). If applicable, we can provide you with an offer letter that can be the basis for the DSO approval. If your school requires a CPT course, Handshake AI may not meet your school’s requirements. If you require CPT/OPT work authorization, please do not accept a project invitation or sign a project contract before your work authorization has been approved by your DSO or USCIS.

Please note that there are minimum or maximum hour requirements under these programs. Compliance with these requirements is your responsibility.

Work with your DSO to ensure your eligibility and consult the federal government for more information on these programs.

Other supported work authorizations

Persons with the following status and valid work authorization are also eligible for Handshake AI:

  • H-4 dependent spouse with an Employment Authorization Document (EAD)
  • L-2 dependent spouse
  • Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA)
  • Refugee
  • Asylum seeker or grantee
  • Temporary Protected Status (TPS)

Unsupported work authorizations

  • F-1 Visa Holders: STEM OPT Extension
  • J-1 Visa Holders
  • H-1B Visa Holders
  • TN Visa Holders
  • H-4 dependent spouse without an Employment Authorization Document (EAD) We cannot support these visas or work authorizations at Handshake AI. Most of these require an employer-employee relationship. Handshake AI operates under a contractor model and not an employer-employee relationship.

FAQs

I’m not ready to provide documents before starting—can I still apply?
  • If you’re still waiting on documents (such as a visa or green card), you’re welcome to apply once you’re ready!
  • Already applied and now have your documents ready? Just reach out and let us know—we’ll be happy to revisit your application.
  • If your CPT eligibility changes and you need to pause participation, feel free to contact us. We’re happy to reconnect once you’re eligible again.
Can I get a DSO offer letter before I’m assigned to a project?
  • We’re only able to provide DSO letters once you’ve been invited to an eligible project. When the project invitation appears on your Handshake AI dashboard, contact Support to confirm eligibility and request your letter.

Handshake AI Fellowship expectations

As a Handshake AI Fellow, you’re joining a community of contributors helping to shape the next generation of AI. The expectations below apply throughout your time in the program and across every project you participate in. They’re designed to help you understand how the program operates and what’s expected of you along the way.

Projects are completed independently. All work is done on your own time, letting you choose when and how much to contribute. We recommend jumping into a project as soon as you’re allocated to one, as availability can change quickly.

Project and task availability is subject to change. Projects may start, pause, or end based on our partner labs’ needs, sometimes with short notice. We’ll share updates as early and clearly as possible, but some changes may be unavoidable.

Quality standards are high and project-specific. This work requires careful judgment and attention to detail — your contributions directly improve real AI systems. Each project has its own requirements, workflows, and quality standards, which will be clearly communicated in project details and training materials. These standards may evolve as our partner labs’ research needs change. Fellows may be removed from a project if expectations aren’t met.

Assessments may be required. Some projects require passing an assessment to confirm readiness or maintain quality. New assessments may be introduced as project needs evolve, and continued participation may depend on meeting them.

Fraud and community guidelines are taken seriously. Violations may result in removal from a project or from Handshake AI entirely. Work completed in violation of these guidelines may not be paid.

Handshake AI Fellowship support guide

As a Handshake AI Fellow, you’ll use a few different tools and platforms as you move through onboarding, training, and project work. We know questions come up, so we’ve put together a simple guide to help you figure out the fastest way to get support.

Before submitting a ticket, check your project materials, onboarding guides, and FAQs. Most common questions are answered there, and you’ll often get a faster answer than waiting for a response from the team.

When to contact Handshake AI Support

Reach out to the Handshake AI Fellow Experience team for help with:

  • Onboarding questions
  • Trouble accessing practice tasks or viewing assigned projects
  • Issues with the Handshake annotation platform
  • Project invites, timelines, or questions about which project you’re staffed to
  • Time tracking
  • Missing or delayed payments after hours are logged
  • Eligibility questions How to contact support

Make sure you’re logged into Handshake before reaching out so your account information is accessible to the team.

  • Open the support chat. Click your profile picture in the upper-right corner of any Handshake page, then select Contact Support from the dropdown. The Handshake Digital Assistant window will open directly in Handshake.

  • Start your conversation. Your email and user type are pre-filled — click Submit, then type your question. The more specific you are, the more accurate the chatbot’s response will be. For tips on getting the most out of the chatbot, see Best Practices: Leveraging the Help Center Chatbot.

  • Escalate if needed. If the suggested articles don’t resolve your issue, you’ll be asked whether you’d like to connect with a specialist. If you confirm, a support ticket is automatically generated and your chat transcript is sent to the team. You’ll receive a copy of the transcript via email once your ticket is submitted. For more on how tickets are handled, see Handshake Support Ticket Urgency and Classification. Tips for faster resolutions

  • Be specific when describing your issue — include relevant details like your project name, the action you were trying to take, and any error messages you saw.

  • For guidance on writing support tickets that get resolved quickly, see How to Get Support Tickets Resolved ASAP.

  • To track the status of your submitted tickets, visit the Handshake Requests page.

  • To get notified about planned maintenance or system issues, subscribe to updates on the Handshake Status page.

Support interaction policy

Handshake strives to provide the safest environment for our users and employees while engaging in any conversation on our platform or vendor tools we use to service our customers. We require consensuality when interacting with our team members, meaning that conversations must remain professionally relevant and contribute to our community in a constructive manner.

We require that every user be civil and respectful as they interact with our team. If any of our employees wish to terminate the consensual conversation due to abusive behavior, they may do without penalty or fear of retribution.

Handshake does not tolerate abuse of its employees: We do not allow profanity, bullying, harassment, unwanted advances, threats, violence, intimidation, prejudice, retaliation, discriminating, dehumanizing, or hateful language/action against individuals working for or on behalf of Handshake.

How to identify fraud and scams

Scammers sometimes target students & fellows by pretending to be Handshake in order to steal personal information, money, or account access.

Knowing what to look for can protect you. Use this guide to quickly spot red flags and stay safe!

What scammers are after

Scammers typically want:

  • Sensitive personal information (Social Security Number, bank details, credit card numbers, passwords)
  • Account access through fake links or login pages
  • Money (wire transfers, gift cards, cryptocurrency) Important: Handshake and its partners will never ask for sensitive information via text, in-app messages, email, phone, social media or WhatsApp.

The only times you’ll provide sensitive information are through:

  • Persona (identity verification during account creation)
  • Stripe (payment processing, taxes) Handshake provides you with access to all of the tools and sites related to the Handshake AI Fellowship. Steps for setting up Stripe along with screenshots of what to expect are available in How to Set Up Stripe.

Important: If you’re being prompted to share any sensitive personal information through another site, or if the experience does not match the screenshots in our articles, do not enter any information or proceed further - contact Support to verify!

Learn more about Handshake AI Payments Processing.

Common red flags

Be cautious if a message includes any of the following:

  • Requests for sensitive information
    • Requests for your passwords or other account information
    • Requests for your SSN, bank account details, or credit card numbers
    • Requests to share any of this information via messages, email, WhatsApp, phone, or Google form
  • Suspicious links or attachments
    • Links that look unusual, shortened, or don’t clearly belong to a real company
    • Unexpected attachments or login requests
  • Urgent or fear-based language
    • Messages that pressure you to act immediately, such as:
      • “Your account will be suspended if you don’t click now.”
      • “Immediate action required.” Scammers often create urgency so you don’t stop to verify.

Common scam types

Fake job or project offers on Handshake: Someone may contact you with an “opportunity” outside the Handshake platform

Red flags:

  • Asking to move off Handshake to apply or provide PII (via email, WhatsApp, phone, Google Form)
  • Does not ask for your credentials or verify your identity
  • Requests for personal or financial information outside the Handshake onboarding process
  • Poor grammar or overly casual tone
Impersonation on Handshake: Scammers may create accounts or profiles pretending to be official organizations (Handshake, Schools, Employers)

Red flags:

  • Urgent messages (“Act now or lose access”)
  • Suspicious profiles or accounts
  • Messages claiming to be “Handshake Support”
  • “Student” accounts offering support
Impersonation off Handshake: Scammers may pretend to be a Handshake employee reaching out with invitations or followups

Red flags:

  • Misspelled or fake domains (e.g., joinhandhsake.com, joinhandshake-careers.com)
  • Generic, valid email addresses (e.g. handshake.helixprojectlead@gmail.com, handshakeprojectlead@gmail.com)
  • Requests to complete a Google Form as part of validation or verification (e.g. provide either your Handshake Code or your Handshake Password)
  • Urgent requests to avoid delays or disqualification

Quick Reference: Red flags vs. legitimate communications

A full list of official email domains and additional tips are available in How to Recognize Legitimate vs. Fraudulent Communications.

If you receive a suspicious message: contact Support to confirm email address validity or report any suspicious interactions.

If your account or information has been shared or compromised: as soon as possible, take the recommended steps in Safety: Protecting Your Personal Information.

How to recognize legitimate vs. fraudulent communications

Being able to identify legitimate Handshake emails and messages is critical to avoid scammers.

Official Handshake emails and texts

Handshake emails are sent from addresses ending in:

  • joinhandshake.com

  • notifications.joinhandshake.com

  • mail.joinhandshake.com

  • m.joinhandshake.com

  • g.joinhandshake.com

  • cm.joinhandshake.com

  • m.ai.joinhandshake.com

  • ai.joinhandshake.com April 22, 2026 update: our team rolled out a domain change, so ticket responses will only be sent from addresses ending in “ai.joinhandshake.com” or “joinhandshake.com”.

  • If you requested a support ticket prior to April 22nd, past email responses may have been sent from an address ending in joinhandshakeai.zendesk.com – this was the only distinctly different and valid domain Handshake used. May 4, 2026 update: we’ve rolled out optional SMS updates, however, Handshake will only send text updates if you have opted in to receiving texts from us.

  • If you have not yet opted in to receiving Handshake text updates, then you will not receive informational or promotional text updates from us.

Handshake on other platforms

Handshake has a limited number of official accounts, all registered as employer accounts.

  • LinkedIn: linkedin.com
  • Wellfound: wellfound.com
  • Facebook: facebook.com
  • Instagram: instagram.com
  • TikTok: tiktok.com
  • X: x.com
  • Youtube: youtube.com
  • Glassdoor: glassdoor.com
  • Indeed: indeed.com Postings on other sites should always direct you back to our official site joinhandshake.com, considered the source of truth.

Other types of communication

Any email, message, account, or post claiming to be from “Handshake Support” or “the Handshake Team” outside of the official channels outlined above should be treated as fraudulent.

  • Handshake does not use in-app messages or feed posts to share important account information.
  • Handshake does not send voice notes, Whatsapp messages or any other SMS-based communication to your personal phone. Learn more about common red flags and scam types in How to Identify Fraud and Scams.

How to protect yourself

  • Don’t click suspicious links or download unexpected files
  • Never share sensitive information through messages or email
  • Don’t respond to any emails or messages, or complete any forms
  • If something feels off, pause and double-check, look at the email domain carefully. Scammers like to use emails that can at first glance look legitimate, like joinhandhsake.com, joinhandshake.net, or joinhandshake-careers.com
    • The joinhandshake.com domain may appear on it’s own or as variable.joinhandshake.com, but should always follow this format and match one of the recognized domains listed above! If you receive a suspicious message: contact Support to confirm email address validity or report any suspicious interactions.

If your account or information has been shared or compromised: as soon as possible, take the recommended steps in Safety: Protecting Your Personal Information.

How to showcase your Handshake AI Fellowship experience

Adding your Handshake AI Fellowship experience to your LinkedIn, Handshake profile, or resume/CV is a great way to showcase your expertise, build your professional brand, and highlight your contributions to impactful AI projects.

You’re encouraged to share your role, responsibilities, and the value of your work. However, please do not include the name of the partner company or AI lab, as these projects are confidential.

Example template

Job Title: AI Trainer – [Domain] Expert

Employment Type: Contract

Company: Handshake AI Fellowship

Location: Remote

Dates: [Month, Year] – [Month, Year]

Description:

  • Developed and evaluated domain-specific prompts to assess the performance of large language models (LLMs) in [domain]
  • Analyzed LLM outputs for scientific accuracy, clarity, and depth in specialized subfields
  • Contributed to improving AI understanding of complex [insert topic] through expert review and feedback
  • Conducted independent research to support prompt development and evaluation tasks
Helpful tips
  • Customize your domain – Adjust your title and description to reflect your area of expertise (e.g., biology, finance, law, philosophy).
  • Keep it professional – Focus on what you did and the skills you used or developed.
  • Respect confidentiality – Do not mention the name of the company, AI lab, or share internal materials. If you’re ever unsure what to include, feel free to reach out to the Handshake AI Fellowship team for clarification. We’re here to help!

Project Removal

Fellows may be removed from a project for a variety of reasons, including violations of our Terms of Service or Code of Conduct. If you’d like your case reviewed by our support team, request an appeal and our team will review your situation and follow up via email.

Referring someone to the Handshake AI Fellowship

Know someone with the expertise to contribute to cutting-edge AI projects? Refer them to Handshake AI and earn as they work — while helping them find meaningful opportunities to put their skills to use. Our referral program is currently available for Fellows based in the United States of America, India, and Canada.

How the referral program works

Referring someone is simple. Share your referral link, they sign up and get matched to a project, and you start earning for every hour they contribute. Referral earnings are paid out as part of your weekly pay cycle.

There are two ways to share your link:

  • Use the Copy referral link button at the top of your Referrals page to share a general link.
  • Select a specific role under “Earn as your referral earns” to generate a link tailored to a particular expertise area. The roles you see in your Referrals page are the ones available within your country.

Tips for a successful referral

  • Share your link before they sign up — referrals can’t be applied retroactively.
  • Use a role-specific link when referring someone you know is a strong fit for a particular expertise area.
  • Encourage your referral to stay active in their first 6 months — the more they work, the more you both earn.
  • Track your referrals’ progress from your Referrals page to stay on top of where each one stands.
  • If you have questions about a referral not showing within your referrals dashboard, contact Support.

Referral bonus earning structure

For every hour your referral works, you earn 10% of their first production project’s rate. Here’s what you need to know:

  • Payouts unlock at 10 hours — your referral must complete at least 10 hours of production work before your earnings are released.
  • Earnings are capped at 40 hours per referral.
  • There’s a 6-months earning window from when your referral joins. Once the window closes, no further earnings can be accrued from that referral.
  • Your earnings are based on your referral’s localized hourly rate on their first production project.
  • Maximum earnings per referral depend on where your referral is based.
  • All projects are eligible — you earn no matter which project your referral works on.
  • All referral earnings are calculated and paid in USD.

Referring someone in another country

You can refer someone in any country where the Handshake AI Fellowship is available — your referral doesn’t need to be based in the same country as you.

Your earnings are always based on your referral’s first project rate, not your own. For example, if you’re based in India or Canada and refer someone based in the US, you’ll earn 10% of their US project rate. Maximum earnings per referral also follow your referral’s country, so the amount you earn may differ from the amounts shown on your Referrals page.

Understanding referral statuses

Every referral’s status is tracked on your Referrals page. Here’s what each status means:

  • Account created: Your referral has successfully signed up and created an account.
  • Tasking: Your referral is active within their 6-month window and contributing to projects.
    • If you see a lock icon next to your earnings for this referral, it means they haven’t hit the 10-hour minimum yet and your payout hasn’t unlocked.
  • Term ended: The 6-month window has closed.
    • If your referral met the 10-hour minimum, your earned amount will be paid out.
    • If they didn’t reach 10 hours, no earnings will be generated from this referral.
  • Completed: Your referral has hit the maximum earnings cap. You’ve earned the most you can from this referral. Tip: if an expected referral is missing from your Referrals page, and your referral confirms they signed up, it’s possible they weren’t using your referral link when their account was created. Referrals will only be listed if your shared referral link is used to sign up!

Why a referral may be missing from your dashboard

Referrals are only tracked if your link is used at the time the account is created. Attribution is set automatically during signup. If an expected referral isn’t appearing in your dashboard, the most common reasons are:

  • The referral link wasn’t used when signing up
  • The account was created before clicking the link
  • A different link or session was used during signup Because of how this tracking works, we’re unable to change the original source of an account or manually add a referral after signup. For future referrals, the best way to make sure everything tracks correctly is to share your referral link before they sign up and have them use that link when creating their account. Once they sign up through your link, you’ll be able to track their progress and earnings directly from your Referrals page.

Referrals pending review or on hold

Occasionally, referral payouts may be delayed while our team works through and reviews submitted referrals. If your referral earnings are pending or on hold, no action is required on your part.

Impact on existing referrals

Our new referral program structure may impact existing referrals. We’ve outlined possible scenarios and what this means for you below.

Referrals moved to the new program:
  • If your referral is less than 6 months old and your referred friend has completed project onboarding but has worked fewer than 10 hours
    • Your referral has been moved to the new program. Once your friend crosses 10 hours of production work, payouts will begin. Your original 6-month expiration window continues.
  • If your referral is less than 6 months old and your referred person has not yet completed project onboarding
    • Your referral has been moved to the new program as active. Your referral rate will lock in once they complete onboarding on their first project.
Referrals not moved to the new program:
  • If your referral was created more than 6 months ago and was never paid out
    • Your referral has expired and is no longer eligible for a payout under the new program.
  • If your referred friend worked 10+ hours but you never received a payout because they weren’t on a referral incentive-eligible project
    • Your referral has expired and is no longer eligible for a payout under the new program.
  • If you already received a referral payout for this person
    • Your referral is marked complete. No additional payouts will be generated. For full details on eligibility and program terms, refer to our Handshake AI Fellowship Referral Program Terms of Service.

Updating your Handshake AI email address

Keeping your account email up to date helps you receive important updates and access your Handshake AI work.

For security reasons, our team cannot directly change the email address on your Handshake account.

Use the steps below to update it based on your specific circumstances.

If you can still log in with your current email address

If you can still sign in with the email currently associated with your Handshake account, follow the steps below:

  • Log in to Handshake using the email address and password already linked to your account.
  • Update your email address by following the steps in Update Your Primary Email Address in Handshake. Once your changes are saved, your new email address will automatically sync to your Handshake AI account. No additional steps are required. This is the fastest and most secure way to update your email address.

If you can no longer log in with your current email address

If you have permanently lost access to the email associated with your Handshake account (for example, if your school email has been archived), follow the steps below:

  • Create a new Handshake account using your new email address. Go to Handshake account registration and follow the prompts to create a new student account.
  • Wait to be added back to projects. After your new account is created, you will be added back to the standard queue for Handshake AI project allocation. Note: project matching and timing depend on your eligibility and current project availability.

Because we cannot verify your identity without access to your original email address, creating a new account is the only secure option if you no longer have access to that email.

If you’ve been assigned to a project and are looking for your Handshake AI alias email, refer to Getting Started on a project.

Working as an AI Trainer with frontier labs through Handshake AI

Curious what it’s actually like to work as an AI trainer through Handshake AI? Whether you’re exploring flexible work, curious about how AI models are trained, or already part of the Handshake AI community, here’s a straightforward breakdown of what to expect grounded in how the work actually operates.

Do I have to be a student to do this?

No. While Handshake is widely known for connecting students and early talent with opportunities, Handshake AI trainer roles are open to people at all stages of their careers.

What matters most is your ability to apply your knowledge, professional skills, or domain expertise while following detailed guidelines to produce high-quality work.

Our AI trainer program includes:

  • Current undergrad students
  • Recent graduates from universities and community colleges
  • Researchers and PhDs
  • Working professionals There’s no single “right” background.

What does an AI trainer actually do?

AI trainers help improve and advance AI models by completing specific tasks designed by known frontier labs. There are several leading organizations building and researching cutting-edge AI models who want, and need, human intelligence and expertise to make AI smarter and more reliable.

Depending on the project, your work might include:

  • Writing or evaluating responses to prompts
  • Reviewing AI-generated outputs for accuracy or reasoning capabilities
  • Challenging and stumping the model on specific tasks
  • Labeling or categorizing data
  • Providing detailed feedback that helps models improve This is detail-oriented work. Your judgment and reasoning directly influence how models behave in real-world scenarios.

What to expect day-to-day: Your experience will vary depending on the project you’re on, but in general you can expect to log in, review your available tasks, and work through them at your own pace. Some projects move quickly, while others are longer-running.

Room to grow: Fellows who consistently deliver high-quality work may have the opportunity to take on additional responsibilities, such as reviewer or specialist roles. If you’re interested in advancing within a project, that’s a conversation worth having with your project lead.

Is this a full time job?

Handshake AI is not a full-time employment opportunity. It is a flexible, project-based fellowship program designed to fit around your existing commitments — whether that’s school, a full-time job, or other responsibilities.

Work on Handshake AI is contract-based and varies in availability depending on the projects you’re matched to. There are no guaranteed hours, and task availability fluctuates based on the needs of our partner labs. Some fellows contribute consistently over time, while others work more sporadically depending on what’s available.

This structure works well for people who want:

  • Flexible, remote work that fits around their work, school, and life schedule
  • Supplemental income
  • Exposure to real AI development without committing to a traditional role

Is work always available?

This is one of the most important things to understand up front: AI trainer work fluctuates over time.

Projects can ramp up quickly and they can wind down just as fast. In some cases, availability can change within a matter of days. While Handshake AI works to give advance notice when projects are ending, there’s no guarantee of continuous work week to week.

Our top priority is being as transparent as possible with our AI trainer community. As soon as we’re aware of changes to project availability and are able to share details, we communicate those updates directly while continuing to build strong, trusted partnerships that make this work possible.

Because of this, we encourage AI trainers to:

  • Work more when projects are active, if their schedule allows
  • Treat the role as flexible or supplemental rather than relying on it as a sole source of income When a project ends, AI trainers may be considered for other opportunities, but timing and availability can be difficult to predict.

Is there training or support?

Yes! Every project includes structured onboarding and ongoing support, led by a project lead. Training is primarily asynchronous, with documentation, examples, and tools designed to help you get answers as you work. Some projects also offer live office hours or additional support sessions depending on the scope and need. Many AI trainers join without prior AI experience, and our Learning and Training team and project leads are there to provide guidance throughout the lifecycle of each project.

Each project includes:

  • Clear instructions and task guidelines
  • Examples of high-quality work You’re not expected to be an AI expert on day one. The goal is to help you succeed within each project’s specific scope and expectations.

How do people get offered new projects?

New projects are offered based on a combination of performance, fit, and project needs. Each project is scoped to specific domains, degree backgrounds, or skill sets, so having the right academic or professional background matters when matching fellows to new work.

Your performance on past projects plays a major role in:

  • Whether you’re prioritized for future opportunities
  • How quickly you’re invited when new projects launch Most projects also require project-specific screening or assessments, since each Frontier Lab has its own goals, standards, and task types. Even experienced Handshake AI trainers may need to complete new evaluations to join different projects. This helps ensure the right fit and maintains high quality across every collaboration.

Who tends to do well as an AI trainer?

This work is a strong fit for people who:

  • Enjoy independent, focused work
  • Pay close attention to detail
  • Are comfortable with ambiguity and change
  • Want flexible, remote opportunities
  • Are curious about how AI systems are built and improved If you adapt quickly and care about doing high-quality work, most projects feel engaging and rewarding.

What’s the big picture?

Working as an AI trainer through Handshake AI means contributing to frontier AI development—while maintaining autonomy over your schedule.

It isn’t always predictable. It isn’t always steady. But for many Handshake AI Fellows, it’s a meaningful way to:

  • Apply expertise to real AI systems
  • Build experience in an emerging field
  • Earn income with flexibility
  • Stay connected to leading AI labs shaping the future
