Accelerating Your Job Search: How to Land the Best Role and Company for You

Finding the right job can feel like a daunting task, but with the right strategy, you can make the process more efficient and effective. Whether you’re just starting your job search or you’re in the middle of exploring different options, it’s important to leverage all the resources available to you.

In this guide, we’ve gathered some key strategies to help you accelerate your job search, connect with the right people, and find the company that fits your career goals and values.

🚀Tip: Before jumping into your job search, take a moment to consider what you really want in a role. Beyond just the job responsibilities, consider the benefits that matter the most to you. Equally important is identifying the type of company culture where you’ll thrive. Reflecting on these factors early can help you focus your search on opportunities that align with your values and long-term goals.

1. Leverage the feed on Handshake

One way to discover new opportunities is by exploring the feed. It’s not just for browsing content posted by peers and career experts, but also a valuable tool for discovering companies.

Use the feed to learn more about companies, what others are saying about their experiences, and get updates from companies you’re interested in.

🚀Tip: follow companies of interest. This will keep you up-to-date on the latest posts, events, and opportunities related to those companies.

To learn more about following companies and users on the feed, check out Following Users on Handshake.

To learn more about following employers on Handshake, refer to Following an Employer in Handshake.

2. Connect with employees & alumni

The power of networking is undeniable, and reaching out to employees or alumni at companies you’re interested in can improve your chances of landing a job. Networking can happen through direct messages on the platform, events, or career fairs.

Messaging on Handshake

When you reach out, make it clear why you’re interested in connecting. Keep it professional and respectful of their time. Mention specific things that drew you to their company and express your interest in learning more about their experience.

🚀Tip: Ask Insightful Questions. Use this opportunity to learn more about their role, the company culture, and any advice they might have for you as you search for your next opportunity.

Learn more about finding peers to connect with and sending messages on Handshake in Peer Messaging in Handshake.

Learn more about finding employers at companies of interest and messaging them in Access Employer User Profiles on Handshake and Messaging Employers in Handshake.

Find events and fairs to attend

Attending events and fairs on Handshake is a great way to connect with employers, learn about open roles, and gain insights into companies. These events let you make direct connections with recruiters and stand out in the hiring process, giving you an edge in your job search.

Learn more about searching for events and fairs in Discover Events & Fairs in Handshake.

3. Research companies on Handshake

Before applying for any role, it’s essential to understand the company’s culture. Check out the company’s brand page to get an inside look at what it’s really like to work there. Do they align with your values? Do they offer benefits you’re interested in? Reading the testimonials (if available) can give you a good sense of whether the company’s environment is a good fit for you.

To learn more about finding employers on Handshake and navigating their brand page, check out Navigating the Employer Brand Page on Handshake.

4. Keep Your Profile Updated

One of the most important things you can do in your job search is to keep your profile up to date. An outdated profile means potential employers or recruiters might not find you, or they could pass over your application because your profiles doesn’t show everything that makes you unique!

Make sure to:

  • Add your latest experiences: Include any internships, projects, or part-time work you’ve done recently.
  • Update your skills: If you’ve learned something new or completed relevant coursework, make sure it’s reflected in your profile.
  • Highlight your strengths: Make sure your key accomplishments and skills stand out to recruiters who might be looking for someone like you. A well-maintained profile will not only help you show up in search results but also attract the attention of the right employers who are looking for candidates with your specific qualifications.

💡Note: You have full control over your profile’s privacy settings. If you choose the Community or Employers option, only include information you’re comfortable sharing. To learn more about your profile privacy settings in Handshake, refer to Profile Privacy Options in Handshake.

For detailed guidance on updating your profile, check out Completing your Profile in Handshake.

Reminder: Avoid adding sensitive information such as phone numbers or addresses to your profile.

5. Don’t Let Job Rejections Get You Down

Job hunting can be tough, and rejections are a part of the process. It’s easy to get discouraged, but remember that rejection isn’t a reflection of your worth.

For tips on handling rejection, check out How to Handle a Job Rejection: Turning Setbacks Into Growth

🚀Tip: Meeting with a career advisor at your school (if available) is a great way to get advice, support, and valuable connections! To learn more about scheduling an appointment at your school, refer to Request an Appointment with your Career Center.

By combining these strategies—you can greatly improve your chances of landing a role at a company that’s right for you

Remember, your job search is a journey, and every step you take is bringing you closer to the perfect opportunity. Handshake is here to help you along the journey, so make the most of all the resources at your disposal!

To learn more about searching for jobs in Handshake or available work-study positions, check out Searching for Jobs and Internships.

To find available on-campus positions at your school, refer to Search for On-Campus Positions in Handshake.

AI Assistant on Jobs

The AI assistant helps you understand how well your experience aligns with a specific job and offers suggestions to strengthen your Handshake profile or application materials for that role.

It’s an optional tool designed to provide guidance, not a guarantee of a job or interview.

The AI assistant isn’t available on every job in Handshake. It’s currently enabled on select postings where it can provide more targeted suggestions.

What the AI assistant does

When you start the AI assistant from a job, it:

  • Uses details from the job description and your Handshake profile (and, when available, your resume) to understand what the employer is looking for.

  • Asks you short questions about your skills, experience, and interests related to that job.

  • Suggests specific updates you can make to your Handshake profile or other application materials to better reflect your fit for the role. The assistant is designed to:

  • Help you determine how your experience connects to a particular job.

  • Give you practical suggestions (for example, skills to highlight, projects to add, or ways to describe your experience). You stay in control the entire time — you decide what to add, edit, or ignore.

By using this feature, you acknowledge that while this conversation is governed by the Handshake Privacy Policy, the information you share will be transmitted to and processed by a third-party large language model (“LLM”) to generate profile-improvement suggestions. Do not include sensitive information (e.g., Social Security numbers, financial or health data), and note that outputs are automated and for guidance only—you remain responsible for reviewing and deciding to apply any changes.

Where to find AI assistant on a job

If a job includes the AI assistant, it will appear under the “What they’re looking for” section on the job’s detail page.

If the AI assistant option isn’t listed, it means the feature isn’t available for that particular job.

To learn more more about searching for jobs and internships on Handshake, refer to Searching for Jobs and Internships.

How to use AI assistant

  1. On the job details page, click Get help refining profile.

If prompted, review and accept the AI terms and privacy notice to continue.

  1. Depending on your device and configuration, you may be able to:

  • Speak to the assistant and have it transcribe what you say (this is the most common option)

  • Type your responses as text (this option is not available for all users) If this is your first time using the feature, your browser may ask for microphone permission. Choose one of the following:

  • Allow while visiting the site

  • Allow this time

  • Never allow If you select Never allow, you may not be able to use this feature if typing is not available on your device or configuration. To update your browser’s site permissions, click the two-line icon next to the URL and allow microphone access.

  1. The assistant may ask about:
  • Relevant classes, projects, or internships
  • Skills you’ve used (technical or soft skills)
  • Work or volunteer experience that connects to the job Be as specific and honest as possible—this helps the AI provide more accurate and useful suggestions. You can communicate with the assistant using voice or text. When you’re ready, click the up arrow to send your message.
  1. The assistant may recommend:
  • New sections or details to add to your profile
  • Skills or keywords to highlight
  • Ways to describe your experience so it better matches what the employer is asking for Follow the on-screen prompts to accept, edit, or skip individual suggestions. You don’t need to accept every recommendation.

When you’re finished, make sure your changes are saved. Then review the job posting again and decide whether you’d like to submit an application

Tips for getting better suggestions

  • Focus on one job at a time: Use the AI assistant while you have a specific job open, so it can tailor feedback to that role’s requirements.
  • Highlight real examples: Mention actual classes, projects, part-time jobs, or activities — not just buzzwords. The more detail you share, the better it is for the AI to help you surface the right information.
  • Use it as guidance, not a script: Treat suggestions as starting points. Edit the recommendations so it accurately reflects you and your experience.

Application Submitted: Email Confirmation

Once you have successfully submitted a job application on Handshake, you will receive an email confirmation sent to your primary email address.

This confirmation serves as a reminder that your application has been successfully received and includes important details about your submission.

Confirmation email details

From: Handshake (handshake@notifications.joinhandshake.com)

Subject: “Application submitted to [COMPANY NAME]”

Content:

“Just applied? Keep your search going

Nice work. You successfully applied to [JOB TITLE] at [COMPANY NAME] on [DATE] at [TIME] [TIMEZONE].

Good luck!”

The email also includes a summary card with the company name, industry, job title, pay, location, and job type, along with a View application link.

💡Note: Some employers may send customized responses to applicants based on their application status. These emails are sent from Handshake (handshake@notifications.joinhandshake.com), but the employer fully controls both the subject line and the message content. To confirm that the email was written by the employer, look for the line “Sent from [COMPANY NAME]” directly below the custom message.

Received a confirmation but did not apply?

If you receive an email confirmation but did not apply for the job, it is likely because:

  • A Career Services staff member at your school manually added you as an applicant to the job posting.
  • The employer reviewed your Handshake profile and added you as an applicant to an on-campus interview schedule that is linked to the job posting. Handshake sends application confirmation emails only when an application is successfully submitted to an active job posting.

However, if you are added as an applicant to an expired posting and the employer has set up custom responses, you may still receive an email based on their settings.

Apply for a Job in Handshake

Ready to apply for a job or internship in Handshake? Follow the steps below to submit your application!

If you want to browse available opportunities, check out Searching for Jobs and Internships. This article offers tips on navigating the job search page and using filters to find the most relevant opportunities for you!

Apply for a job

  1. Access the job you’d like to apply for. Click Jobs on the left navigation menu—The jobs overview page will display by default.

To view any previously saved jobs, click Saved in the upper-left corner of the page.

  1. View the Job Details. Click on the job to load its full details page, which includes key information about the role.

  2. Click on Apply, Apply Externally, or Quick Apply as applicable for that particular job.

  • Apply appears if one or more of the following are true:
    • You don’t meet all employer preferences
    • One or more documents are required, and you don’t have them uploaded
    • More than one document is required
    • You’re accessing a job via “Saved Jobs” that leads to an external application
  • Apply Externally indicates the employer is using an external site to collect applications. Additional steps outside of Handshake are required to complete your application. Learn more about the next steps in Jobs: Apply Externally.
  • Quick Apply indicates you meet all employer preferences and either:
    • No documents are required
    • Only one document (a resume) is required, and you have at least one approved or pending resume uploaded. Learn more about this in Jobs: Quick Apply in Handshake. Note: There is a daily limit of 300 applications. If you exceed this limit, your account will be automatically blocked. You’ll receive a notification explaining the reason, and your account will remain blocked until it is reviewed and cleared by our Trust & Safety team.
  1. Upload your documents and submit the application. Select your resume or other document(s), complete any additional required actions, and Submit Application.

Once you click Apply, a pop-up will appear with details about the application.

If a document is required, you can:

  • Choose from your existing documents by selecting the dropdown menu
  • Select one of your two most recently added documents
  • Upload a new document by clicking the blue button Upload New If a document isn’t required, the popup will confirm no additional documents are needed, and you can submit the application by clicking the green button Submit Application, located in the lower-right corner of the popup.
  1. Confirm Submission. After you apply, a green confirmation banner will appear at the top of the job details page stating “You applied on [DATE].” You’ll also receive a confirmation email in your inbox.

If you don’t receive the email, you may have unsubscribed from Handshake notifications. To confirm your application, click your account icon in the upper-right corner and select My Jobs from the dropdown—any roles you’ve applied to will be listed there. If you’d like help verifying if your email has any unsubscribes associated with it, contact Handshake Support.

For more information regarding this confirmation email, check out Application Submitted: Email Confirmation.

If your school requires document feedback, your application won’t be submitted until your Career Services center reviews your documents. For more information on this, refer Document Status in Handshake.

Career Center Collections at your School

Your school’s career services department may choose to spotlight specific jobs, employers, events, and career fairs using curated categories known as Career Center Collections on Handshake.

These collections are thoughtfully designed to help you explore opportunities that align with your unique career goals and interests.

Use the expandable sections below to learn how to explore, search, and identify Career Center Collections at your school.

Explore Career Center Collections

Interested in discovering jobs, employers, events, and fairs curated by your school? Here’s how to access Career Center Collections on both desktop and mobile:

On Desktop

Click Career Center on the left navigation menu, then locate your school’s Career Center Collections section. Alternatively, click Explore on the left navigation menu, then scroll to the bottom of the page to locate Career Center Collections.

You can either:

  • Click on a specific collection that interests you to view relevant opportunities.
  • Click the link View all collections to browse all curated categories.
    • On the Career Center Collections page, you’ll find category tiles. Use the filters at the top of the page to narrow your search and click on any tile to explore that collection in detail. Once you’re on a specific category page, you’ll have access to two tabs at the top: Jobs and Employers. If your career services department has added any events or fairs, those tabs will also be available.

Click on any tab to explore the curated content within the category.

Each item—whether a job, employer, event, or fair—is displayed as a tile. Here’s what happens when you click on each:

  • Jobs: the job posting in Handshake, which includes the description, application instructions, and deadlines.
  • Employers: the employer’s profile to view available opportunities and learn more about the company.
  • Events & Fairs: the details page, which includes registration links, and related resources. To return to the main Career Center Collections page, click Back to collections in the upper-left corner.

Tip: Want to stay updated on an employer’s activity? Click Follow on their Handshake profile. For more details, check out our guide on Following an Employer in Handshake.

On Mobile app

Tap on your icon in the upper-left corner of the screen, then tap Career Center.

Tap Career Center Collections from the menu, then scroll to choose a category of interest from the list.

Once you’re on a specific category page, you’ll have access to two tabs at the top: Jobs and Employers. If your career services department has added any events or fairs, those tabs will also be available.

Click on any tab to explore the curated content within the category.

Each item—whether a job, employer, event, or fair—is displayed as a tile. Here’s what happens when you click on each:

  • Jobs: the job posting in Handshake, which includes the description, application instructions, and deadlines.
  • Employers: the employer’s profile to view available opportunities and learn more about the company.
  • Events & Fairs: the details page, which includes registration links, and related resources. To return to the main Career Center Collections page, click Back to collections in the upper-left corner.

Search Jobs via Career Center Collections

Looking for jobs or internships curated by your school? You can easily filter your job search by Career Center Collections to discover opportunities aligned with your interests!

Note: The list of categories available directly from the job search page may be limited. To view the full list of collections your career center has created, visit the Career Center Collections page.

On Desktop

There are two ways to access your school’s collections from the Jobs page. Start by clicking Jobs in the left navigation menu, then choose one of the following:

  • The white button [SCHOOL] collections, located to the right of the search bar. Click in the text box to select a specific category via the dropdown, then click the black button Apply.
  • The All filters option, located at the far right of the header bar. Within side sheet, scroll down to locate the [SCHOOL] collections section and click in the text box to select a specific category via the dropdown, then click the black button Apply. Once filtered, jobs that match your selected collection(s) will appear as a list on the left side of the page.

To learn more about the jobs details page, and apply for a job, refer to Apply for a Job in Handshake.

On Mobile app

  • Tap Jobs at the bottom center of the screen.
  • Tap the More filters icon just below the search bar.
  • Scroll to find [SCHOOL] Collections.
  • Tap Add Collections for the category to be listed under your [SCHOOL] Collections.
  • Once all categories have been added, click the back button then tap Show jobs. Follow a Collection and set up job alerts

Following a Career Center Collection is a great way to stay aligned with your career goals—by doing so, you’ll get quick access to curated jobs, events, and fairs your career center has handpicked just for you.

To follow a collection, click the black Follow button in the upper-right corner of the categories page.

After following, a job alert is automatically set for you as a proactive way to stay in the loop, save time in your job search, and receive updates and alerts for new opportunities that match your interests within the category.

Search Events and Fairs via Career Center Collections

Click Events on the left navigation menu, then click the [SCHOOL NAME] Collections filter located below the search bar. From the dropdown, select the categories you’re interested.

Note: if there’s zero search results, the view results button will appear grayed out.

Once you’ve selected your categories, click the blue button View results to explore the curated events and fairs.

All the curated events and fairs are displayed as tiles—clicking the tile will take you to the event or fair page, where you can find event details, registration links, and any additional resources.

Identify Jobs And Employers Within A Career Center Collection

Career Center collections at your school can be identified by a gray badge. You’ll find these in Handshake across several areas, including the job list during your search, the jobs details page, and employer profiles.

  • Job list: The badges appear below the job title, for easy recognition.
  • Job details page: The badges are displayed midway down the page, under the section “About the employer” section. 💡Note: up to three badges may be displayed at a time. If the employer or job is a part of more than three school collections, a plus sign badge is present. Hover over the plus sign badge to discover other collections the employer is a part of!

Finding Remote Jobs in Handshake

Use Handshake’s job filters to find remote work-from-home opportunities that fit your schedule and lifestyle.

To learn more about searching for jobs and internships, visit Searching for Jobs and Internships.

Find remote jobs

  1. Click Jobs from the left navigation bar.

  2. Click the Filters button in the header bar to open the filters panel.

  3. Under Onsite/remote, select Remote (Work from home).

How Job Collections are Generated

Handshake offers students a range of curated job collections on the new Explore page. This page organizes resources to help you easily discover career opportunities and access content that aligns with your interests and goals. Below is an overview of the key collections available on the Explore page.

Not all collections may appear on your Explore page, so you might not have access to every collection listed below.

Jobs Collection

The Jobs Collection curates a selection of job and internship opportunities based on your profile information, interests, and activities. These collections include:

  • Job Role Group (Major Group): Discover jobs and internships that are relevant to your declared major or job role group. These listings are tailored to your field of study.
  • Location-Based Jobs: Find jobs and internships available in your specified location.
  • Popular Jobs: View the most popular job listings among students within your major group. These roles are highly sought after by your peers, making them a great place to start your job search.
  • On-Campus Jobs: Check out job opportunities available right on your campus. This collection includes part-time jobs, internships, and other roles specifically on your school grounds.

Events Collection

Stay informed about important career events that can help you network, learn, and grow your professional skills. The Events Collection includes:

  • Upcoming Career Fairs: Find information about upcoming career fairs hosted by your school or other organizations. These events provide great opportunities to connect directly with employers and explore job openings.
  • Employer Events: Learn about events hosted by employers that align with your career interests. This may include webinars, information sessions, or networking events.
  • Guidance Events: Access events organized by your school’s career center for additional guidance, including resume workshops, interview prep, or career counseling.

Employer Collection

The Employer Collection gives you insights into companies that are actively recruiting students like you. The key sections include:

  • Employers Hiring: Discover employers that are currently hiring for roles relevant to your major group and location. This collection features companies looking for candidates with skills similar to yours.
  • Popular Employers: See which employers are popular among students in your major group. These companies often offer roles that are highly sought after by students in your field

Career Center Collection

Your Career Center plays an essential role in supporting your job search and career development. This section of the Explore page includes:

  • Career Center Collections: Access curated collections from your school’s career center. Learn more about career center collections in Career Center Collections at your School.

How to Handle a Job Rejection: Turning Setbacks Into Growth

It’s tough when you put in the effort, write a stellar application, nail the interview, and then… you don’t get the job. You might be feeling discouraged, frustrated, or even questioning your abilities. But know this; A rejection is not a reflection of your worth or potential. It’s simply a part of the journey—one that nearly every professional, at every level, has faced.

Whether you’re just starting your job search or trying to figure out your next move after an opportunity didn’t work out. Let’s take a look at how to cope with rejection, stay motivated, and continue moving forward with confidence.

1. Acknowledge your feelings

It’s okay to feel disappointed. Job rejections can sting, especially when you’ve invested time, energy, and hope into a role that seemed like the perfect fit. Allow yourself to feel what you’re feeling. Whether you’re sad, frustrated, or confused, your emotions are valid. Try not to rush to move past them. Take a moment to reflect on how you feel before you take the next step.

Remember, it’s normal to have a period of emotional processing after any setback. You’ve been working toward something, and it’s okay to give yourself the time you need to recalibrate.

2. Don’t take it personally

A job rejection doesn’t define you or your abilities. While you’re a great candidate, sometimes companies have a certain criteria or experience they’re looking for.

Think of rejection as an opportunity for growth—not a judgment on your potential. Every “no” is a step closer to a “yes” in the right place. Take comfort in knowing that the right opportunity for you is out there.

3. Ask for Feedback (if you can)

If possible, consider reaching out to the employer for constructive feedback. While not all employers can provide this, many are willing to offer insight into what they were looking for or how you could improve. Constructive feedback helps you better understand how you can make your next application or interview even stronger.

Feedback is a valuable tool, and it can help you refine your approach for future applications.

4. Refocus and Keep Moving Forward

After a job rejection, it’s easy to get stuck in a negative cycle of overthinking or doubting yourself. But remember: resilience is about getting back up after a setback and continuing to move forward. Take some time to reset, refocus, and remind yourself why you’re looking for work in the first place.

Tips to help you regain momentum:

  • Revisit your goals: What kind of work excites you? What skills are you looking to grow? Reaffirm your “why” so that you can continue your job search with clarity and energy.
  • Update your resume and Handshake profile: Is there something you could refine or update? Small adjustments can help you stand out more in your next application. To learn more about updating your Handshake profile, refer to Completing your Profile in Handshake.
  • Reach out to your network: You might be feeling isolated right now, but you’re not alone. Reach out to people who have been through the process or who can offer advice and encouragement.
  • Keep applying: The job search process is often about persistence. Don’t let one rejection discourage you. Continue applying to new opportunities that align with your passions and goals. To learn more about searching for jobs on Handshake, check out Searching for Jobs and Internships.

5. Remember: Rejection isn’t forever

One of the most empowering things to remember is that rejection is temporary. It’s part of your journey toward finding the right fit, and with every rejection, you’re learning, growing, and becoming even more prepared for the opportunity that’s waiting for you.

The right employer is out there, one that will recognize your strengths and the potential you bring to the table. Sometimes, all it takes is one “yes” to turn everything around.

Stay Positive, Keep Going

Job searching can be a long and winding road, but every step, even the rejections, are shaping you into a stronger, more capable professional. You have a community of people rooting for you—and we at Handshake are here to help you stay motivated and equipped for success!

Job Application Status in Handshake

Use the My jobs section in Handshake to track the status of any job application, including applications connected to on-campus interview schedules.

Topics:

  • Access My jobs
  • Filter and search your applications
  • Application statuses definitions

Access My jobs

  1. Click your account icon in the upper-right corner of Handshake.

  2. Select My jobs from the dropdown menu.

On the My jobs page, all the jobs you have applied to will be displayed, including the employer, job title, location, date applied, and current application status.

Filter and search your applications

Use the search bar and filters at the top of the My jobs page to sort and refine your view:

You can use the search bar and filters at the top of the page to sort and refine your view:

  • Application type
    • Job applications
    • Applications to interview (Applications tied to on-campus interview schedules)
  • Status
    • Applied
    • Hired
    • Declined
    • Primary (for on-campus interviews)
    • Alternate (for on-campus interviews)
  • Filters
    • Applied after
    • Applied before

Application status definitions

  • Applied: Your application has been submitted. This is the initial status for all applications.
  • Declined: The employer reviewed your application but chose not to move forward.
  • Hired: You have been selected for the position.
  • Primary: You have been selected as a primary candidate for an interview schedule.
  • Alternate: You have been selected as an alternate candidate for an interview schedule. If you want to follow up on your application status, reach out directly to the employer or your career services center for updates.

Jobs Digests and Recommendations

Handshakes offers students personalized job recommendations based on their interests, activity, and engagement on the platform. These recommendations aim to help you discover opportunities that align with your career goals. As a student, you have full control over how you receive these notifications—whether through email or mobile push notifications.

For more information on managing your notification preferences, refer to Managing Your Notification Preferences.

Job Digest Emails

If you’ve listed at least one career interest in your Handshake profile, you’ll automatically receive a weekly job digest email. This email is sent every Tuesday and includes 5–10 job recommendations based on the interests you’ve selected within your career interests. The recommendations may include roles you haven’t yet viewed or applied to, but they could be relevant to your career goals.

Key Details:

  • The jobs included in the digest may not be brand-new listings, but rather ones you haven’t yet explored.
  • The recommendations are personalized based on your profile and the activity you’ve had on Handshake (e.g., job views, searches, etc.).
  • If you no longer wish to receive the weekly digest emails, click the Manage email preferences link within the email. This will direct you to Handshake, where you can adjust your notification preferences.

Job Recommendations Emails

For students actively engaging with job listings on Handshake (i.e., those who have viewed at least one job), you’ll receive Job Recommendations Emails. These are sent the following day after your activity, containing 5–10 tailored job recommendations.

Key Details:

  • The frequency of these emails will not exceed once per day.
  • The email will include job recommendations that reflect your recent searches and views, designed to help you find the best-fit opportunities.
  • If you no longer wish to receive the job recommendation emails, click the Manage email preferences link within the email. This will direct you to Handshake, where you can adjust your notification preferences.

Jobs: Apply Externally

Some employers may choose to collect applications in their internal tracking system rather than Handshake. If this is the case, the job posting will have a button to Apply Externally.

To submit an application externally, follow the process outlined below.

Part 1

On the job details page, click Apply Externally to start your application.

You’ll need to submit the application on the external site to fully apply for the position!

Part 2

If a popup appears in Handshake, after clicking Apply Externally, this indicates the employer has added an additional step in the application process.

If no popup appears in Handshake, proceed to the external site and follow the instructions under Part 3 of this article.

Within the popup, there are 3 possible actions that may be required for Step 1. These options are detailed below:

  • Review Employer Instructions
    • “[COMPANY NAME] has provided the following instructions for applying externally: [CUSTOM MESSAGE FROM EMPLOYER]”
  • Submit Documents on Handshake
    • Details on required Document(s) are provided in this space. Select your document via one of the following:
      • Click the dropdown menu to select from all uploaded documents.
      • Click the blue button Upload New to choose a new file from your computer.
      • Click on the name of one of the two most recent document uploads to your account, displayed below “Recently Added”.
  • Complete Pre-Application Questions
    • CUSTOM QUESTIONS FROM EMPLOYER (if questions are listed, enter your responses in the provided text field within the popup) Once complete, click the green button Step 2: External Application, and continue with Part 3.

Part 3

A new browser window or tab will open with the designated application link. You’ll need to follow the instructions on this site to fully submit your application.

For any questions related to this application, you’ll need to reach out to the employer directly, as Handshake does not have access to the external site.

Tip: if the link does not open, check if your browser has a popup blocker enabled. If so, allow popups from the site, then go back to the job in Handshake and click the link View application to try again. This link appears in place of the Apply Externally button since the Apply Externally button was already clicked.

Part 4

When you return to Handshake, the job posting will automatically be added to the “My Jobs” section (accessible from the Account Icon menu), with the application status of Pending. However, since Handshake cannot track your activity on the external site, you’ll need to confirm if you’ve finished your application.

The job posting will prompt you to answer, “Did you apply to this job?” — Click the button for YES / NO as appropriate.

  • If No, the button Apply Externally will reappear on the posting, and the job will be removed from the “My Jobs” section
  • If Yes, the text will change to “You applied on [DATE]” To withdraw an application that has been submitted externally, refer to Withdraw an Application in Handshake.

Jobs: Quick Apply in Handshake

Quick Apply streamlines the application process, making it faster and easier for you to apply for jobs. It is available on both the web and the mobile app.

Quick Apply is available only if all of the following conditions are met:

  • You meet all of the employer’s specified candidate preferences for the job.
  • The application requires no documents, or only one required document (a resume).
    • If a resume is required, you must have an approved or pending resume. To learn more about other application methods on the platform, check out Apply for a Job in Handshake and Jobs: Apply Externally.

To find jobs to apply for on Handshake, refer to Searching for Jobs and Internships.

Quick Apply

Once you’ve found a job of interest that has ‘Quick Apply’ as an option, click the button Quick Apply on the jobs details page.

If there are no required documents, a message at the bottom of the screen will confirm no additional documents are required. Click Submit Application to proceed.

If a resume is required, your most recently uploaded resume with an Approved or Pending status is selected automatically. To review it, click Preview document below the document name.

If you’d like to use a different resume, click the X next to the selected document, then choose one of the following options:

  • Click the search bar to view all uploaded resumes with an Approved or Pending status.
  • Click Upload new document to upload a different resume. When you’re ready, click Submit Application to complete your application.

After the application is successfully submitted, a confirmation will appear at the bottom of the screen stating “Application submitted!” A green banner at the top of the job will also be displayed showing the date you applied.

You’ll also receive an email confirmation letting you know that you submitted your application successfully. For more information on this email, check out Application Submitted: Email Confirmation.

Additional considerations

Preferences

Employer’s can select candidate preferences per job, and preference matching is based on information in your Handshake profile. If you should match the qualifications set for a job, learn how to make the necessary updates to your profile:

  • How to Edit Education Information on Your Profile
  • Student Work Authorization Information
Documents

Some schools that partner with Handshake choose to review uploaded resumes. Depending on your school’s preferences, documents that aren’t approved may prevent the application from being fully submitted.

Document feedback and review preferences are customizable per school. If your document on an application states “Pending”, we recommend you contact your career center to learn more about the selected preferences.

For more information on document statuses in Handshake, check out Document Status in Handshake.

Navigating the Job Details Page in Handshake

The purpose of the job details page is to provide comprehensive information on job opportunities. This includes key details such as the job description, qualifications, company benefits, and other relevant information. The goal is to help you identify and evaluate job opportunities that align with your interests.

Click on the expandable headers below to learn more about each of the sections included on the job details page!

💡Note: some of the sections listed below may not apply to the job or employer. For example, if an employer is not part of a Career Center collection or doesn’t have an upcoming event, those sections will not appear on the job’s details page.

Want to share a job you found? Learn how in Sharing a Job on Handshake.

At a glance

This section provides an overview of the job. It also includes key details such as the salary, location, salary range, job type, position overview, and more. This allows you to quickly assess if the job aligns with your career goals and preferences.

Note: if the employer includes a pay, it’ll be presented as an exact number or a range. For jobs that are posted in the following states must include a pay amount: California, Colorado, Hawaii, Illinois, Maryland, Massachusetts, Minnesota, New York, Vermont, and Washington.

What they’re looking for

This section provides specific information about the qualifications and skills that the employer is seeking in potential candidates for the job. This could include:

  • School Year: the classification of the academic year you are currently in. This can include levels such as Freshman, Sophomore, Junior, Senior, or other specific categories for specialized programs.
  • Skills: specific skills that the employer is looking for. These could be technical skills (like proficiency in a certain software) or soft skills (like communication or leadership abilities).
  • Major: any specific studies/majors preferred for the job. Tip: remember, these are the qualifications that the employer is looking for, but don’t be discouraged if you don’t meet all of them. Many employers are willing to consider transferable skills and potential, so if you think you could be a good fit for the role, consider applying and highlighting your relevant skills and experiences in your application.

What this job offers

This section provides the transparency of Company Benefits/Perks. This could include dental and medical coverage, 401k plans, and more. This information can play a crucial role in your decision-making process.

Ask the hiring team

This section allows you to communicate directly with the hiring team of the company. It provides an opportunity to ask questions or seek clarifications about the job role, company culture, application process, or any other relevant details.

This feature is designed to promote transparency and open communication between you and the employer, making the job search process more interactive and informative. It’s a great way to get a better understanding of the job and the company, and for employers to engage with potential applicants.

Note: the availability and functionality of this feature may vary depending on the settings chosen by the employer.

Upcoming Events

This section includes any events that the employer has scheduled that are relevant to the job or the company.

If the employer is attending a career fair or hosting an event at your school, the details will be displayed. Click on the name of the event to be directed to the registration page.

For more information about registering for an in-person career fair or virtual fair, refer to Registering for an In-Person Career Fair (Students) and Signing Up for & Managing Virtual Fair Sessions.

Learn more about registering for an employer-hosted event in Registering for an Event.

About the employer

This section provides information about the company offering the job. This could include:

  • Company Overview: a brief description of the company, its mission, and its values. This can give you an idea of what the company does and what it stands for.
  • Company Size: information about the size of the company, such as the number of employees - Giving you an idea of the scale of the company’s operations.
  • Industry: the industry or industries in which the company operates.
  • Location: the location of the company’s headquarters or main offices, and other significant locations.
  • Company Culture: some information about the company’s culture, such as its approach to work-life balance, diversity, inclusion, employee development, and more.
  • Career Center Collection: if the employer or job is part of a custom category created by your school, a badge will identify it. For more information on this, refer to Career Center Collections at Your School. Tip: click the button Follow to follow the employer, or the link Learn more to be directed to the employer’s profile.

Similar jobs

This section is designed to provide you with additional job opportunities that are closely related to the job you’re currently viewing. Similar jobs are typically determined based on factors such as job title, industry, skills required, and location.

This feature is beneficial for your job search as it provides you with more opportunities that align with their interests and qualifications.

Connect with alumni

This feature is designed to help you connect with alumni from your school.

  • If there are alumni who are employed by the company, you’ll have access to a list of peers under the section “alumni at this employer”
  • If there aren’t enough alumni from your school, you’ll have access to a list of peers under the section “alumni in similar roles” Tip: click the button Follow to follow the user, or their name to check out their profile in Handshake!

Additionally, it encourages students to reach out and message these alumni for insights and advice, thereby promoting networking and informed decision-making during their job search.

To learn more about searching for a job or internship on Handshake, refer to Searching for Jobs and Internships.

For more information about applying for job on Handshake, check out Apply for a Job in Handshake.

You can easily create a Job Search query on Handshake to save a search based on the criteria that matter most to you!

Save a Job Search

Saving a job search on Handshake allows you to create a query with the specific criteria you’re interested in.

  1. Click Jobs on the left navigation bar.

  1. Enable Job Alerts: Once you’ve applied your filters, a purple banner above the search results will state, “Notify me about new jobs like this.” Slide the toggle to the right to save your search and activate job alerts.

Job Alerts

Job alerts are created when you save a job search. You’ll receive email notifications whenever a new job matches your search criteria.

The Jobs page

    • Weekly Once you’re done, click the Save button to apply your changes.

Your Notification Preferences

Click on your account icon, located in the upper-right corner of the screen, then click Notification preferences from the dropdown.

All saved search queries are listed at the top of the page, under Job Alerts. Click on Edit button to the right of the job search query you want to update notifications for.

In the pop-up window, you can edit the following settings:

  • Search Title: Enter a name for your job search query.
  • Get Notified: select how you want to be notified by clicking the dropdown and checking/unchecking the boxes:
    • Email
    • In app
    • Push (mobile)
  • Receive Alert: Choose how frequently you want to receive alter:
    • Daily
    • Weekly Once you’re done, click the Save button to apply your changes.

To delete the job alert, simply click the Delete button.

Important: Email notifications will include a maximum of 25 job postings. To view all available jobs, we recommend logging into Handshake and accessing your job alert through your Notification Preferences.

Searching for Jobs and Internships

Handshake connects you with thousands of employers, making it a powerful tool for your internship and job search. When you understand how Handshake’s search features work, you can find opportunities that fit your interests. This article outlines strategies and tips to help you refine your search and find relevant roles.

To start browsing, click Jobs in the left navigation menu to open the Jobs page. The jobs listed are influenced by your career interests and information on your Handshake profile.

💡Note: If you’re connected to a school on Handshake, you’ll have access to jobs and collections targeted specifically to your institution. If you registered without selecting a school, you’ll only have access to jobs posted to the broader network. Some jobs are limited to certain schools or require that you meet specific qualifications, so you may not be able to view or apply to every posting.

If you signed up without affiliating with a school, your access to Handshake’s features is more limited. To connect to your school, click your account icon in the upper-right corner and select School Connections from the dropdown menu.

If your job preferences are out of date, a pop-up may prompt you to update them. You can also update your preferences any time from your profile by editing your job interests. To do this, refer to Update Your Career Interests.

Search Methods in Handshake

Use the jobs list on the left side of the page to review roles that interest you, or use the options below to narrow your search and surface the most relevant jobs:

  • Search bar: Search using keywords, job titles, job IDs, or employer names—or describe what you’re looking for in natural language. As you type, Handshake’s type-ahead feature suggests options based on job roles, industries, and employers, ranked by the number of relevant postings available at your school.
  • Handshake Collections: Use your school’s curated collections to find jobs grouped into categories chosen by your career services team. Not all collections appear directly on the Jobs page; for full details, refer to Career Center Collections At Your School.
  • Location: Filter for jobs in a specific city, state, or ZIP code. The location filter defaults to a 50-mile radius—use the slider to decrease or increase the radius around your chosen location.
  • Job type buttons: Quickly focus on Full-time job, Internship, or Part-time roles. As you apply these filters, matching results update immediately in the jobs list on the left side of the page.

🚀Tip: If you’re not interested in a job or it’s not relevant to your search, you can hide it so it won’t appear again. To learn more, refer to Hide a Job on Handshake.

Sharing a Job on Handshake

Sharing jobs helps fellow students discover opportunities they might not have found on their own, strengthens your network, and sharing works both ways. Your peers may return the favor and share great opportunities with you.

This article explains how to share a job posting on Handshake with other students and alumni.

To learn more about searching for jobs and internships, check out Searching for Jobs and Internships.

Share a job

  1. Click on the job to open the full posting.

  2. Click the Share button at the top of the page, next to the Save button.

  3. From the dropdown, select one of the following options:

  • Copy link
  • Share to…
  • Send job to…

Copy link

Selecting Copy link copies the job link directly to your clipboard. A “Link copied!” confirmation will appear in the lower-left corner of the page. You can then paste the link anywhere you choose.

Share to

Selecting Share to… opens your device’s share sheet, where you can share the job link via apps such as Mail, Messages, or AirDrop.

Send job to

Selecting Send job to… sends the job directly to another student or alumni through the Handshake Inbox.

  1. Begin typing the name of the person you want to share the job with, then check the box next to their name. You can also select from the list of suggested contacts.

Note: You can only share job postings with other students at your institution.

  1. Add a personal note about why you are sharing the job (optional).

  2. Review your message and recipient, then click Send.

The recipient will receive the job posting in their Handshake Inbox as a private message, including your name, any personalized message you wrote, and a direct link to the job posting.

Tags Displayed on Jobs

Tags are added to job postings on Handshake to help you quickly identify information about a job or employer.

These tags are designed to enhance your job search experience on the platform. They offer additional context to help you prioritize particular job postings and improve your understanding of why certain jobs are showing up in your search outcomes.

Available tags in Handshake

  • Top Match: Highlights jobs that you are most suited for, based on your qualifications. This tag is only shown to the top 15% of candidates. It is intended to help you identify jobs that match your skills and qualifications.
  • Recommended for You: Draws attention to jobs that align with your interests. This tag personalizes your job search experience by highlighting opportunities that match your career goals and interests.
  • Be an early applicant: Highlights jobs that you would be among the first to apply. This tag serves as a direct call to action, emphasizing the advantage of being early in the application process.
  • Responsive Employer: Means the employer responds to messages within 48 hours and has responded to at least 10 messages in the past. This tag lets you know the employer is actively engaged on the platform and will likely reply to any questions or inquiries you may have!
  • Job Closes Soon: Alerts you that the job will close within 7 days, ensuring you don’t miss out on opportunities that are about to expire.
  • Promoted: Indicates that the job has been given extra visibility in your search results. Employers who are actively hiring for a position may choose to promote a job. Promoted jobs are selected based on both their relevance to you and how other students are interacting with them (for example, viewing, saving, or applying). As a result, you may occasionally find a promoted job that doesn’t match every filter you’ve set, but is still likely to be a strong match based on your profile and activity on Handshake.
  • Career Center Collections: Highlights certain jobs and employers that your school’s career services department has chosen to feature. The tags displayed are custom categories created by your school. For more information about Career Center collections, refer to Career Center Collections at your School. To learn more on how to search for jobs and internships on Handshake, check out Searching for Jobs and Internships!

Withdraw an Application in Handshake

This article explains how to withdraw a job application on Handshake, including applications submitted directly through Handshake, externally, or through Greenhouse.

General requirements for withdrawing an application

To withdraw an application in Handshake, the following conditions must be met:

  • The job posting must still be active (not expired).
  • Your application status must be Pending. Note: You can only withdraw applications that were submitted directly through Handshake. If you applied externally, such as through an employer’s website or a system like Greenhouse, you will not be able to withdraw the application through Handshake.

Select the scenario below that applies to your application:

Application submitted externally

If you clicked Apply Externally on a job posting, you were redirected to the employer’s application site, such as their website or an external platform. After applying, Handshake will display a prompt asking: “Did you apply for this job?”

  • Selecting No will withdraw the application from Handshake entirely.
  • Selecting Yes will update the posting to show: “You applied on [DATE].” Withdrawing your application in Handshake does not affect any application you submitted on an external site. Only the employer can remove or withdraw your application from their system.

If you need assistance removing your Handshake application record, contact your school’s Career Center. Include the job title and a direct link to the posting.

The Career Services team can review the employer’s application preferences and may be able to remove the application on your behalf.

If not, they may advise you to contact the employer directly to withdraw your application.

Application submitted through Greenhouse Integration

Some employers use Greenhouse to manage their application process. When applying for a job posted through Greenhouse, you will receive a prompt before clicking the Submit Application button that says:

“Employer is using Greenhouse to track applications. To withdraw this application after submission, you will need to contact Employer.”

Applications submitted via Greenhouse cannot be withdrawn through Handshake. Only the employer can remove your application from Greenhouse.

If you need to withdraw, contact the employer directly.

Application submitted in Handshake

If you applied directly in Handshake (not externally or via Greenhouse), you can withdraw your application as long as its status is Pending.

Once the employer has reviewed your application, contact your Career Center to request a withdrawal.

  1. Click your account icon in the upper-right corner of Handshake, then select My jobs from the dropdown menu.

  2. Locate the job you want to withdraw from, then click the job title to open the job’s overview page.

Tip: Use the filters at the top of the page to narrow down your list of applications.

  1. On the job overview page, click the white Withdraw Application button.

  2. In the confirmation pop-up, click the red Withdraw button to confirm that you want to remove your application and cancel any associated interview schedules.

Application attached to an Interview Schedule in Handshake

If your application is linked to an interview schedule in Handshake, such as for an on-campus interview, you can still withdraw your application as long as its status is Pending.

Once the employer has reviewed your application, contact your Career Center to withdraw.

To remove your application from an interview schedule:

  1. Click your account icon in the upper-right corner of Handshake, then select Meetings from the dropdown menu.

  2. In the upper-left of the page, click the On-Campus Interviews tab.

  3. Locate the relevant interview schedule, then click on it to remove your application.

Re-applying after withdrawing

If the employer re-opens a job that was previously posted on Handshake and you were declined at that time, contact your school’s Career Center to withdraw your application so you can re-apply.

To find your school’s contact information, refer to How to Locate your School’s Contact Information in Handshake.

You can re-apply to a job at any time as long as the job posting is still active (not expired/closed).

For more information on applying for jobs in Handshake, refer to Apply for a Job in Handshake.

Create a New First Destination Survey

A First Destination Survey allows you to gain valuable insights into where your graduates are going after graduation. This data can be used to track trends in the job market, and identify emerging career opportunities.

To learn best practices for FDS use, check out Handshake’s Guide to Using the First Destination Survey.

To access Handshake’s First Destination tool, click First Destination on the left navigation bar, then click the blue button Create First Destination Survey in the upper-right corner of the page.

Click on the expandable headers to learn more about each step!

  1. Survey Setup

This section includes adding Key Dates and Details for the survey.

Key Dates

On the Key Dates tab, fill in the following fields, then click Next in the lower-right corner to move on:

  • Report Year: The year that you will be reporting on
  • Survey Name: Make sure your first destination survey has a descriptive name that you can refer back to when analyzing.
    • Note: you’ll be able to set a different name for students to view on the next tab.
  • Graduation Groups: These are the different sets of graduating students that you will be sending the survey to. Refer to First Destination Graduation Groups for additional information.
    • Example: send two different invitation and reminder emails to spring undergraduates and graduate students.

Survey Details

The Survey Details tab is next to complete. Fill in the following fields:

  • Survey Name: How this survey appears to students in emails and questionnaires. This is helpful if they are added to multiple first destination surveys.
  • Survey Type: Choose from one of the four dropdown selections (click the link below to see standard questions for each type):
    • Standard (NACE)
    • MBA CSEA - Full Time
    • MBA CSEA - Part Time
    • MBA CSEA - Specialty Masters
  • Is this survey mandatory? (Check the box if mandatory) This is only used for reporting purposes and will not be reflected in the student experience. This field will help track how making a survey mandatory impacts response rates.
  • Salary Information Required (Check the box if required) Leave the box unchecked to allow students to submit responses without salary and pay schedule information.
  • Disable Handshake Email Content? (Check the box to disable Handshake’s content and enable fully-custom email content, with no Handshake default content besides a ‘Take Survey Now’ button.)
  • Send Recipient Emails? (Check the box to enable Handshake reminder emails) If unchecked, all invitation and reminder emails will be disabled.
  • Minimum Graph data points: Students will see data compared to their classmates for their type of work and salary information, this will be the minimum responses necessary for students to see the information.
  • Sender Info: Invitations and reminder emails will appear to be sent from this person. Sender info can be further customized for each email.
  • Custom Questions: If you would like to ask additional questions on your first destination survey you can do so in a survey that you can attach here. You can also create a survey from this page if you have not yet added your additional questions in the surveys section.
    • Set Skip Logic based on outcome by clicking on “Use Skip Logic”. Refer to Use Skip Logic in Your Additional Questions for FDS for additional information.
      • Note: to avoid lengthy load times for students, it is recommended that your custom survey does not exceed 125 questions.
  • Advanced Options - Customize emails for each graduation group: If you are interested in setting custom invitation and reminder messages for each graduation group that you have setup please review the instructions in Send Custom Invitation and Reminder Emails to Each Graduation Group. Once you’re ready to proceed, click the blue button Next.
  1. Timeline & Emails

This section includes finalizing a timeline for the survey to be sent, and adding custom messages to your emails.

Timeline

Review the Timeline and Emails section of the First Destination setup. Make sure to check each graduation group email invite and reminder dates using the drop-down.

If you would like to change the dates of any of the emails, click Customize Timeline, then fill in the dates for each email.

Once you’re ready to proceed, click the blue button Next.

Emails

Enter in your custom message for the Invitation Email, and then choose your default sender, or enter a custom one.

Repeat this step for each of the following reminder emails:

  • Reminder #1
  • Reminder #2
  • Reminder #3
  • Reminder #4
  • Final Reminder (Still Seeking)
  • Final Reminder (Unsubmitted) Note: if you would like to view the email, click the gray button Send Test Email, located in the lower-left corner of the page.

If you choose to enable Handshake content, refer to First Destination Student Email Previews.

When you’ve finished customizing the emails as necessary for each graduation group, click Update in the lower-right corner.

  1. Recipients

This section includes adding students to your FDS (and to appropriate Graduation Groups).

Click the Add Students button located in the upper-right corner of the Recipients section.

In the pop-up, choose a Graduation Group from the dropdown, then add the students email in the text box, located below Student emails - You can either type the emails individually or copy/paste them.

Note: you may also add students to the FDS via the Manage Students page. To do this, use the filters accordingly to narrow down your results (Example: Seniors or Graduation Date Range = May 1, 2023 - May 31, 2023), then put a check next to the students name. Click on the bulk action “More”, and click on “Add to First Destination Survey”. You’ll need to select a survey and a graduation group, then confirm the addition.

Once all sections have been added to your survey, click the blue button Publish Survey in the upper-right corner of the page.

Important: once your survey is published, you cannot unpublish it.

After publishing, we recommend testing and confirming the functionality of the setup. For more information on testing your survey, refer to First Destination Survey (FDS) Testing Guide.

Once you are done with any testing, if you’ve selected to send recipient emails, you can simply wait for your invite and reminder emails to kick off for the graduation groups that you have added!

FAQs: First Destination Survey

If you are thinking about using the First Destination Tool in Handshake, we’ve created this resource to help address many of the questions you may have!

Is FDS an additional cost to my Handshake contract?

No, Handshake’s First Destination Tool is included in your Handshake contract.

Is it NACE compliant?

Yes, Handshake’s First Destination is NACE and NUBS compliant and offers a one click NACE download for easy reporting of results. You must have education level and major data added to students when you add them to the survey in order for Handshake to generate NACE compliant reports. As long as students have degree level and major on their profiles at the time they are added to the survey this will work as expected. Attached Example Report (scroll down to the bottom of this article to download)

What are the standard FDS questions?

We have outlined all standard questions in this article: First Destination Survey (FDS) Standard Questions.

Can we change the standard FDS questions?

These cannot be changed, but if you do need to include additional questions, you can include additional survey questions for each student pathway.

How do I download all FDS responses?

You can download the responses to all FDS responses, not just the NACE report, from a First Destination Survey. If you go to the Recipients tab, select one student, then choose “Select All ____”, you will be able to use the Download CSV action under the More dropdown.

Can users submit multiple responses on the FDS? How does reporting work for that?

Yes, users can submit multiple responses to Handshake’s First Destination Survey. We only count a student’s most recent response in reporting, but you can always access the previous response by searching for the student.

Can I remove a student’s response from a FDS?

Yes, if you remove a recipient, any responses are still associated with the student. If you add the student back to the FDS the system retains their responses and they are visible on the FDS.

Note: if there were any changes to the student’s profile (i.e school year, major, etc.), these changes will not be reflected in the student’s recipient data. You will need to manually add this back in if the student is re-added.

Can I import legacy outcome data into Handshake?

We can import data from many sources, but we will want to take a look at the format of your data and make sure it will match what is in Handshake. Refer to Importing Historical FDS Responses for more information.

Can I submit responses as a career service staff member for a student?

Yes, you can enter a response for a student and mark it as a Response Answer or a Knowledge Answer. Enter a FDS Response for a Student (Knowledge Response)

Can we add additional questions that are specific to our institution?

Yes, you can add a survey to your Handshake First Destination Survey that will be presented to students after the general Handshake questions. This survey can be created in the Survey section of Handshake or you can simply select the ‘Create Survey’ button under Create New questions.

Can we use skip logic in the additional questions that we add?

Yes, you can use skip logic based on Handshake’s first question “What are you primarily doing after graduation?” In the additional questions themselves, you can use skip logic for each question you would like.

Can we report based on College?

Yes, we offer advanced reporting on many student filters.

How do I increase the response rate of my First Destination Survey?

Since the survey will be located in Handshake which many of your students have already connected to, you may see higher results than normal. Other universities use techniques like asking students to enter their responses when they pick up their cap and gowns or offering gift cards (Amazon) when a student fills out the survey. Refer to Improve FDS Response Rates with the FDS Kiosk for more information.

How do you add students to FDS?

You can add students to the FDS directly in Handshake from the Manage Students section. You can also add students by copying and pasting their email addresses in the Add Students section of the Student Tracking page.

When they have access to what other students are doing, how does that impact their decisions?

In the research done here at Handshake we found that this was motivating for students and they continued to fill out the survey to get more information about how their first destination related to their peers.

Can the FDS be taken on a mobile device?

Students can access the FDS through a link provided in one of the reminder emails. This will open the FDS in their mobile browser window.

How do you indicate that you are looking for students that are still looking to continue education?

You can search for students that have submitted a certain response type in the Student Tracking section and reach out to them directly with an email or a request that they submit their most recent work experience.

Can you delete a First Destination Survey?

Yes, career services staff can delete First Destination Surveys. It is unlikely that you would need to delete one unless it is a test. You should always use extreme caution when deleting a First Destination Survey.

Is FDS ready to go or do I have to customize it?

You can use the pre-built surveys (NACE standard or MBA CSEA).

With the gamification of showing students what other students are doing, how does that impact their decisions?

In the research done here at Handshake we found that this was motivating for students and they continued to fill out the survey to get more information about how their first destination related to their peers. This is customizable and you can remove this gamification if you desire.

Can students access FDS without logging in?

Yes, we have released a “logged out link” to help prevent blockers with students needing to log in.

For other FAQ articles regarding specific areas in Handshake, check out the below links:

First Destination Survey Reminders Emails FAQs

First Destination Survey Student Submissions FAQs

FAQs: First Destination Survey Notifications

We send two notifications to career services users if First Destination Survey reminder email campaigns need attention.

24 hour reminder: “Your scheduled email will not be sent”

This email is sent 24 hours before a scheduled email will not be sent because the survey has not been published. For this email to be sent you will need to publish the survey or edit the email timeline by clicking on the links provided.

Email not sent: “Email for [Survey Name] was not sent

This email is sent after a scheduled email is not sent. For this email to be sent you will need to visit the survey timeline and click the link to send this email.

FAQs: First Destination Survey Reminder Emails

The purpose of this article is to provide answers to any inquiries you may have about First Destination Emails in Handshake.

Click on the expandable headers to learn more about each of the inquiries!

Can I change the subject of the reminder emails?

Yes! If you select the Custom Sender option above the Name, Title, and Subject entry, you can customize both the Name (sent from) and Subject line for each reminder email.

Who gets the invitation email?

All recipients added to your survey. You can find these recipients on the Student Tracking page in your survey.

If a student has a primary and additional email address associated with their account, which email address receives the FDS emails?

The primary email address associated with the student’s account receives the FDS emails.

Who gets each reminder email?

  • Reminder 1 - 4: students who have not yet responded to the first destination survey.
  • Final reminder: students who have not yet responded and students that responded that they are still seeking employment. Who do the invite and reminder emails come from?

In a students inbox, the emails will appear from the custom sender you set up in creation.

How did you pick two weeks as the default for invitation emails?

We did a lot of research on the most effective way to increase response rates. We found that reminder emails were the most effective when paired with an incentive and sent around 10:00am during the week. Additionally, we saw a 15% increase in response rates with each reminder email we sent, which is why we have built this into the product.

Will invitations and reminders go out to students on drafting surveys?

No, survey responses are only accepted on Published surveys. You can still report on any responses that exist on a drafting survey.

Will invite and reminder emails be sent after the survey close date?

No - after the survey close date, the invite and reminder emails will no longer be sent to students.

If I add a student to the FDS after the first invitation has already been sent, what happens?

The newly added student will receive the invitation email once added to the survey, then they will receive the subsequent reminder emails.

Will archived students receive invitations and reminder emails?

No, any archived students will not be able to submit responses on First Destination Surveys. This means they won’t receive any email communication and will not have access to the dashboard card either.

Can I set invitation and reminder email dates in the past?

Invitation and reminder email dates must be in the future. Emails can be disabled by unchecking the Send Recipient Emails checkbox.

Can I change the top section of the email to students?

To keep the First Destination invitation and request message consistent for students, you will not be able to edit the standard Handshake sections of the emails.

Can I send custom messages and reminders to students that are added to the survey?

Yes, you can use the bulk action Send Email to Surveyees.

- Tip: copy the link in the Survey Setup Details section to direct students to this survey.
- Note: The survey link will only appear if the survey is published and there are recipients on the survey. Students will need to login to Handshake to submit a response if they are using this link.

Is there a recommended size for the image included within the FDS email?

We accept any ratio but recommend any image ratio that is under 450x450 pixels for best results!

FAQs: First Destination Survey Student Submission

  • What is a unique link for a Handshake First Destination Survey?
    • A unique link is a specific URL that is generated for each student when they are added to a First Destination survey. This is unique for each student and allows them to respond to the survey without being logged into Handshake! These links are only connected to invitations and reminders sent through Handshake’s campaign tools.
  • Can I send the students their unique links from a mass email or an external email tool?
    • No, the unique link is only generated by using the Send Invitation/Reminder Email option in the Student Tracking section of the Survey.
    • You can send students an email with the Survey Link (image below) but this link will require that each student logs into Handshake to complete their response.
  • What does the First Destination survey look like for students that are not logged into Handshake?
  • What does the First Destination survey look like for students that are logged in to Handshake?
  • What if the student has already responded to the first destination survey and they try to use the unique link that was sent to them in an invitation/reminder?
    • The student will need to login to Handshake to submit an additional response to the survey. They will be directed to the first page of the survey immediately after logging in.
  • If the student partially completes a response can they use the unique link again and be taken back to where they left off?
    • No, if the student clicks Begin on the survey the unique link will be expired. The next time the student uses the link they will need to login to complete their response or submit an additional response.
  • If the student exits the first page of the survey without clicking Begin will they will be able to use the unique link again?
    • Yes, if the student does not click Begin then they will be able to use the unique link in their email again.
  • What if the student wants to login to complete the survey but they don’t know their password?
    • They can use the reset password link on the login screen
    • Will they be directed to the survey if they have to reset their password first?
      • No, they will need to use the link on the left navigation bar or the dashboard card to get to the first destination survey
  • Will a student have to go through new student onboarding if they haven’t logged in?
    • No, they will bypass the onboarding step and be taken directly to the first destination survey.
  • What if the student has the survey open in two windows or tabs? Can they complete both?
    • No, the student will see a message that they need to log in when they try to Begin the survey in a second window, tab or browser.
    • We are updating these error messages to be more descriptive.
  • Does the unique first destination survey link expire?
    • Yes, after the student starts the survey (clicks Begin on the first page) they will have 24 hours to complete their response - this is to protect students who leave the link open. After 24 hours if they click the link again or try to continue the survey they will be asked to log in.
  • Do the links sent ever expire for students who do not click on them?
    • Yes, one year after the unique links are sent they will no longer function.

In addition, if you choose to send a test email, please be aware that the “Take Survey” button will not load the FDS for you, as it will not contain the token for FDS recipients. When the email is sent to the surveyees, the “Take Survey” button will include a unique token that will load FDS for the email recipient.

Below are the changes to FDS in Spring 2020 - click on the link to jump to that section within the article.
