Optional Reminder Emails

This change introduces the ability to select between three possible email configurations for your FDS:

  • Send reminder emails and include Handshake content
  • Disable Handshake Content from reminder emails
  • Do not send any automated emails to recipients for the FDS If you would like to send reminder emails with custom content, you should check the “Disable Handshake Email Content”

If you would like to completely disable automated invitation and reminder emails, you should uncheck the box for “Send Recipient Emails” in the Survey Details tab.

Optional Salary

If you would like students to be able to submit their response without requiring salary information, you should uncheck the box for “Salary Information Required” on the Survey Details tab.

Skip logic based on profile data

When creating a new survey, you’ll be able to choose the audience for specific pages based on profile data: Majors and/or Schools.

To add an audience, put a check next to Audience, then select a Major Group or School from the dropdown, or begin typing to filter results. The choices you can select from are mapped in your School Settings in the Major Groups section and Colleges section.

Please note: Only major groups that have majors mapped to them at your school will display in the dropdown menu. If you are missing a major group, we’d recommend to double-check that you have at least one major mapped to the group.

General survey link that doesn’t require login for response submission

We’ve added a new link to the Details page that allows students to complete the FDS while logged out, as long as they have been added to the FDS. In order to complete the FDS via this link, students will need to have an account in Handshake, however, they do not have to be activated in order to complete the survey.

This link will not be provided automatically; students will need to have the link shared with them.

The FDS Responses tab

On the FDS Responses page, you’ll have quick access to information and data relevant to each FDS. You can also take actions for individual or multiple responses at once. Learn more about the FDS Responses page below!

  • Navigating to the FDS Responses tab
  • The FDS Responses page

Navigating to the FDS Responses tab

  1. Select First Destination under the Students category in the left navigation bar.

  2. Choose a survey.

  3. Select the Responses tab. You will be directed to the FDS Responses page.

The FDS Responses page

On the FDS Responses page, you can utilize the search bar to find a specific student’s survey response. You can also select All Filters to narrow down the responses on this page.

Outcomes: This graph provides a visual for the outcomes that students chose in their FDS response (Working, Volunteering, Continuing Education, Military, Still Looking, Not Seeking).

Top employers: The top 3 employers that students have listed as current employers in their FDS response.

Download report: Process the data from the FDS responses through a quick download.

Students’ responses will be listed below, you can click on the three ellipsis (more options) button on the right hand side of an individual response to open a menu of options:

  • Edit response: Select this to open a new page where you can edit the student’s response.

  • Add labels: A pop up will appear with an option to add a new or existing label.

  • Remove labels: A pop up will appear with an option to remove a label.

  • Edit student data: This will open a new page where you can change the student’s information that is attached to their response.

  • Submit new response: Create a new response to overwrite the student’s most current response.

  • View profile: Select this to be redirected to the student’s profile in Handshake. You can also use the checkboxes to select more than one response and choose a bulk action. After selecting a checkbox, the following options appear:

  • Edit employer: A pop up will appear allowing you to change the employer/organization for the responses selected.

  • Add labels: A pop up will appear allowing you add a new or existing label for the responses selected.

  • Remove labels: A pop up will appear allowing you to remove an existing label for the responses selected.

  • Download: Selecting this will download the responses into a spreadsheet. A “download in progress” message will appear in the center of the page, and once the download is complete, the message will change to “Download complete”.

FDS Sourced Outcomes

To help streamline the knowledge response process in First Destination Surveys, we’ve introduced sourced outcomes!

Here are some important key facts about sourced outcomes:

  • The data is sourced from LinkedIn (via Coresignal) and from the Work Experiences and Education sections of the recipient’s Handshake profile.
  • Sourced outcomes rely on graduation groups. Ensure that your FDS has accurate grad group information when setting up your FDS.
  • To establish accuracy, data for sourced outcomes must meet the criteria of being about 6 months prior to, and 6 months after, the graduation date listed in the FDS grad group.
  • Sourced outcomes are currently only provided for NACE surveys.

How to display sourced outcomes

  • Select First Destination Surveys in the left navigation menu and choose a NACE FDS.
  • Head over to the Recipients tab. The filters at the top of the table will help with identifying which responses have sourced outcomes. Select Has sourced outcomes.

  1. You can select any recipient from the list to display their primary response, if applicable, and their sourced outcome as well. Note that in the image, the sourced outcome is from the student’s LinkedIn.

  2. (suggestion) It’s possible that the data shared in sourced outcomes may be incomplete or doesn’t exactly align with the most recent work experience. This may be due to LinkedIn profile visibility settings or limitations with matching Handshake data with LinkedIn data. Select the hyperlinked LinkedIn button to open up the LinkedIn profile in another tab and verify that the information is accurate.

The sourced outcome for this recipient has already been saved, check out the section below to learn how to save sourced outcomes as responses!

Save a sourced outcome as a response

  • For this workflow, we’ll use the filters at the top of the page to display responses that have a sourced outcome but also require action. Use the Needs attention (students that have not yet responded or have responded that they are still seeking) and Has sourced outcomes filters.
  • Select a recipient. It’s recommended that you verify the information with the source so that everything is accurate for your records.
  • If you’d like to save the sourced outcome as the primary knowledge response, you can select Save as response.
  • A message will pop-up in the bottom right corner of the screen verifying that the response has been saved. The sourced outcome response will then appear as the primary response.

Ignore a sourced outcome

If you don’t want to save a sourced outcome as a primary response, you can ignore it.

  • Use the Needs attention and Has sourced outcomes filters once again.
  • Select a recipient.
  • Click Ignore for the sourced outcome.
  • The sourced outcome will fade and there will no longer be an option to save the response. If you wish to undo this, select Undo ignore.
Are there scenarios where information may not match what’s available in LinkedIn?

There are possibilities of technical delays or other conditions that create data discrepancy between LinkedIn and the sourced outcome. It’s important to double-check all sourced outcomes to ensure that the information is accurate. If the information is not accurate, it’s best to edit the response so that it has accurate information. Here are some examples of sourced outcomes not matching what’s in LinkedIn, and why:

  • A sourced outcome shows a LinkedIn profile as the source but after clicking the link, no profile appears. This student likely had a LinkedIn profile but either deleted it or changed their settings to hide it.
  • The sourced outcome seems to be outdated and the LinkedIn profile has more up-to-date information. The student may have chosen to set the specific section of the profile/experience to be hidden - Coresignal cannot bring over information that is hidden. Another possibility is a delay in our system between identifying the sourced outcome and then bringing that information over to Handshake. If a student updates their LinkedIn during that period of time, the sourced outcome may be outdated.

First Destination Graduation Groups

Graduation groups are a way for you to define different sets of graduates within one First Destination Survey. These graduation groups are completely customizable by your institution, and will influence the reminder email campaigns that are set on your First Destination Survey.

For more information on sending reminder emails for graduation groups, refer to Send Custom Invitation and Reminder Emails to Each Graduation Group.

To create a First Destination survey in Handshake, refer to Create a New First Destination Survey.

Graduation Groups

There are different ways to name graduation groups in Handshake. We recommend connecting with your schools career services team and identifying the best way to identify the groups at your Institution.

Note: graduation groups must be different from one another, and you can create as many graduation groups as needed!

Format Suggestions for graduation groups:

  • Month, year (May 2025, December 2025)
  • Month, year, major (May 2025 - Engineering, May 2025 - Business, May 2025 - Nursing)
  • Month, year, education level (May 2025 - Undergraduate, May 2025 - Graduate)
  • Importing groups from the past: If you need to create a graduation group for a past year for an import, select a future date for the group while using the name field to indicate the real year. Example: 2029-10-01 / May 2019 To view students associated within a particular graduation group, click the Recipients tab on the First Destination Survey overview page, then click on the desired graduation group.

Students are listed below the Knowledge rate and Survey response rate analytics, on the left side of the page.

If you need to move a student to another Graduation group within the same First Destination group, you can do so! Add a check to the left of the students name/s you’d like to move, then click More in the upper-right corner of the header bar. From the dropdown, click Move between Grad Groups.

Within the popup, select the graduation group from the dropdown, then click the blue button Confirm.

First Destination Survey (FDS) Standard Questions

A First Destination Survey is used to capture information regarding how new college graduates fare in their careers within six months of graduation. The initiative is to provide clear, concise, and consistent data on the outcomes associated with a college education on a national scale. All questions are compliant with NACE.

First Destination Survey (FDS) Testing Guide

If you’ve recently created a First Destination Survey in Handshake, and would like to preview it before sending out to students, we recommend testing the functionality!

To efficiently test the FDS, you’ll need:

  • A student account in Handshake
    • If you don’t have one already, refer to Create a Student Account Associated with Your Career Services Account.
  • A published FDS to test
    • Make sure that no actual students have been invited before testing.
    • If you need to create a FDS, refer to Create a New First Destination Survey. For more information regarding First Destination Survey’s, refer to FAQs: First Destination Survey.

Testing a First Destination Survey that I created

Once the FDS has been created and published, follow the steps below to test the functionality, prior to adding graduating students.

  1. Locate the FDS that you would like to test, then click the gray button Add Students, located on the right side of the screen, or at the bottom-center of the screen.

  2. Within the pop-up:

  • Select the Graduation Group from the dropdown
  • Add your student email address (that’s linked to your Handshake account) into the text field Once entered, click the blue button Add Emails in the lower-right corner — your student account will be listed in the Recipients List.

  1. Now it’s time to test! You’ll need to switch to your students account — click on your name in the upper-right corner of Handshake, then click Switch Users.

  2. Click Switch to Students Account.

  3. Select Career Center from the left menu.

  4. Select First Destination to be directed to your First Destination Survey.

  5. Click the blue button Next in the lower-right corner to explore the FDS! Keep in mind that you can go back and change your answers (or submit multiple responses) to consider how different outcomes (and custom questions/skip logic) appear.

If you attached a custom survey to the FDS, you won’t want to submit your responses to the survey questions, as those can’t be edited or deleted.

  1. After identifying anything you may want to adjust or change, switch back to your Career Services account. Make your changes to the survey, switch users, and test again!

  2. When you’re done testing, you’ll need to remove yourself as a recipient from the survey.

  3. To remove yourself as a recipient, go back to the Recipients page, find yourself as a recipient and select the three dots, then choose Remove. You will be asked to confirm removal, select Yes, and you will remove your student account and response from the FDS.

Now, you’re ready to launch! Add your graduating students to the appropriate graduation group(s), then let the Survey Invite email and reminder emails kick off.

Handshake’s Guide to Using the First Destination Survey

This guide provides industry best practices, as well as how other institutions leverage the tools available for successful response rates and FDS management.

Consider the set-up that will provide the outcome you need

Before creating a new survey, consider which setup you’d like to proceed with that will help you accomplish your institution’s goals.

  • You can use out-of-the-box preset industry-formatted survey questions (based on NACE/MBA CSEA).
    • First Destination Survey (FDS) Standard Questions
    • First Destination Survey (FDS) MBA CSEA Questions - Part Time
    • First Destination Survey (FDS) MBA CSEA Questions - Full Time
    • First Destination Survey (FDS) MBA CSEA Questions - Specialty Masters
  • You can customize the survey tool to fit the needs of your institution.
  • Add in additional custom questions to the preset industry standard questions.
  • You can build out skip logic to direct your students to specific subsets of questions that you want to collect information on.
    • Skip based on outcome, major or college Ready to Create a New First Destination Survey?

Ready to launch? Test your survey first!

Once you’ve set up a new FDS, check out our resource here: First Destination Survey (FDS) Testing Guide for full instructions on testing the FDS, as well as demo-ing the FDS with other campus stakeholders!

How to increase response answers

Using Handshake for FDS allows you to capitalize on students’ built-in familiarity with the platform (for those who have been engaging with it over time).

  • Launch FDS kiosks at any on campus event to collect responses easily and on the spot.
    • Improve FDS Response Rates with the FDS Kiosk
    • Launch the FDS Kiosk
  • Utilize on-campus events/kiosk/pre-graduation events.
    • Princeton requires their students to complete FDS to get their caps and gowns, resulting in a 98% response rate!
  • Send reminder emails and off-cycle emails
    • Send Off-Cycle FDS Reminder Emails Note: We have discontinued the FDS incentive program that was built into Handshake in Spring 2024. Please utilize one of the above options instead to increase response rates!
Handshake has invite and reminder emails set up and ready to use out of the box.
You can use as is or turn off the Handshake email content completely to create a fully customizable experience for your institution.

If you’d like to use Handshake default content, here are some examples of what that looks like: First Destination Student Email Previews

You can also choose to turn off invite and reminder emails altogether and market these as you choose.

On top of allowing the automation of emails to send, you can send off cycle emails to your students through our targeted email feature!

Leverage connections across campus by providing the logged out link to other stakeholders (marketing materials, websites, give to faculty) to incentivize students to take the survey.

Students will need to have an existing account in Handshake that’s associated with the FDS to take the survey, but they don’t have to have an activated or “claimed” account.

Note: the logged out link won’t be displayed until recipients have been added to the FDS.

Enter knowledge answers directly into survey

The FDS tool offers a one-page form to submit responses on behalf of students (located at the bottom of the submission form). You can read more about this process in Enter a FDS Response for a Student (Knowledge Response).

Keep your data timely and up to date

NACE suggests collecting data for 6 months after graduation; before closing the survey — you can stop at 5 months and use the 1 month to review/clean up data.

Tip: download the non-industry formatted report - CSV file to review.

Download Standard NACE Undergrad or MBA CSEA Report Data From Your FDS

Bulk Download All FDS Responses (Not NACE formatted)

Reporting on “In Progress” FDS Responses

Following up with students who reported “still seeking”

Utilize student advising teams, executive director emails and hot jobs newsletters to keep them engaged and increase response when the time comes.

How to Use the First Destination Survey Recipients Page

The Recipients page will give you insight into how your First Destination Survey is performing!

Knowledge rate

The knowledge rate provides your overall progress towards collecting a known outcome for each student, regardless of response type.

Survey response rate

The survey response rate provides feedback on how well your survey collection efforts are performing. This provides the percentage of students that have submitted a response to your survey. If a student responded to the survey, but a knowledge response has replaced their Primary response, the student’s survey response will still count towards the survey response rate.

Note: If you are displaying “All graduation groups” the denominator in the above formulas would instead be Total number of students in all graduation groups.

Filters

The filters at the top of the table include the following:

  • Needs attention: This will return all recipients that have not yet submitted a response, or have responded with “Still looking”

  • Status: Choose between submitted and unsubmitted responses

  • Major If you select the Filters button, there are more options to choose from. The following are commonly used filters for First Destination Surveys:

  • Outcomes:

    • Working
    • Continuing Education
    • Volunteering
    • Military FAQs

  • How do I add students?

    • To add students you can use the Add Students button which is now located in the top right corner of the page.

  • Where is the option to download all First Destination Data?

    • If you check the boxes next to the students’ names using the table, you can use the More option to locate the Download button to download the data for the selected students.

  • Why can’t I view email data for “All graduation groups”?

    • Email campaigns are unique to each graduation group. Select a graduation group to view the specific outreach schedule.

  • Why is there missing data before May 10th, 2018?

    • Handshake started tracking this data after May 10th so you will see limited date for open rates and click through rates before then. We are sorry about the inconvenience.

  • When I choose a graduation group does it update the list of students shown?

    • Yes, the list of students is only for the selected Graduation Group, select All Students if you would like to see all students.

Improve FDS Response Rates with the FDS Kiosk

First destination data helps students navigate the workplace and proves the impact of Career

Services. Handshake’s FDS tool is user-friendly and increases response rates by up to 3x.

One method that has proven tried and true to increase First Destination Response rates, is to leverage on-going events with graduation seniors. With the recent addition of the FDS kiosk, you can use on-campus events to increase response rates without students needing to log into their Handshake accounts!

Make the Most of Graduation

Campus Events

Campus is bustling with end of year parties, concerts, and celebrations. Make sure the Career Center and FDS is part of the fun! Contact the organizer to see if you can station near the entry point with iPads for survey completion or put a link on their website.

Buzz in High Traffic Areas

Set up a table with iPads and posters in high traffic areas like the student union, cafeteria or the quad and ask students to complete the survey in exchange for candy, popsicles, or a cold beverage.

Free Coffee

If there’s a popular coffee spot on campus, promote free coffee for those who complete survey for 1-2 hours over the course of a week. This will recreate buzz, awareness, and increased traffic each day, which benefits students, coffee shops and the Career Center. This tactic is more expensive, but definitely effective.

Buddy Up with Professors

Ask professors to promote the FDS survey in their class. Again, reminding them of the benefit to students.

Tie FDS to key milestones.

Before students graduate, catch them at opportune times…
Cap & Gown

Set up a table where students pick up their cap and gown. While they’re waiting in line, collect their responses.

Commencement Rehearsal

Commencement rehearsals have been very successful for our customers.

Graduation Events

Graduation events like Senior Sendoff is another great opportunity.

Book Returns

Post up by the bookstore to engage students returning books. Give out candy, popsicles or other giveaways to students who complete the survey. “What are you doing Next?” and invite them to share.

Did you know…

Princeton requires their students to complete FDS in order to get their caps and gowns, resulting in a 98% response rate!

Learn how to Launch the FDS Kiosk next!

Launch the FDS Kiosk

If you’re interested in launching a Kiosk for your First Destination Survey, follow the instructions outlined in this article!

Before launching the Kiosk, you’ll need to ensure:

  • The survey is in Published status
    • You won’t be able to launch the kiosk if your survey is in drafting status.
  • Students have been added to the survey
    • Only students added to the survey will be able to submit responses via the Kiosk. For more information on creating a FDS, adding students, and publishing the survey, refer to Create a New First Destination Survey.

Launch Kiosk

  1. From the Details page of the First Destination Survey, click the Kiosk Mode tab.

  2. Enter a Custom Kiosk Message in the provided space — this message will be displayed to students taking the survey in Kiosk Mode.

Example: “Please fill in your first destination survey and then show a staff member the confirmation page to pick up your cap and gown.”

  1. Click the blue button Open Kiosk Mode to launch the Kiosk, or the blue button Save Message to store your custom message for another time.

Note: we don’t recommend checking the Keep me logged in option if students will be submitting their own responses.

If you need to launch multiple Kiosks for separate First Destination Surveys, you’ll need to open them in separate browsers, OR one in a regular browser window and the other in a private or incognito window.

Once the Kiosk is launched, you’ll be directed to the check-in screen — students can now check into the Kiosk and submit their responses!

Reporting on “In Progress” FDS Responses

If your FDS close date is soon approaching, and you notice that a few students have just a few unanswered questions (for example, if they stopped answering at the salary question), you can manually update the response to submitted. This way the existing data will be included in the NACE reporting download - we’ll walk through the steps here!

How complete are students’ “in progress” results?

You can find this data in the quick download on the Students and Stats page.

  • Filter to your in progress students
  • click the checkbox to the left of the student name
  • select the bulk action More, then select Download CSV from the list This spreadsheet will highlight the student FDS responses - explore the different columns and categories to understand how complete any in progress response might be.

How can I manually update a student response to “Submitted”?

Navigate to the Recipients tab on your FDS, choose the individual student whose response you need to update, and then click the Create Response button to manually enter the first response for this student:

From the following page, fill out the survey accordingly:

If you do fill in answers, please make sure to update the response type to Knowledge answer. Once the fields are completed, you’ll want to update the Status field on any individual responses from In Progress to Submitted:

**Please be aware that this process is for the standard FDS setup. If your school has additional Custom Questions, you will have to submit this status change as a Knowledge Response to bypass the Custom Questions.

Send Custom Invitation and Reminder Emails to Each Graduation Group

  • Navigate to your First Destination Survey
  • Within the Survey Setup go to the Details page
  • Under Advanced Options check the box to Customize emails for each graduation group
  • Navigate to the Timeline & Emails section of setup you will now see a Graduation Group selection
  • Select the correct Graduation Group and customize that message
    • Do this for each email that you want to customize per graduation group

Send Off-Cycle FDS Reminder Emails

In mid-March 2018, Handshake released a new FDS setup interface that includes the ability to pre-schedule four reminder emails that are sent to students who haven’t yet submitted a response. You can learn more about that new feature here.

If you’d like to send more emails to your survey recipients, you can use the following process…

  • Pull up the Students & Stats tab of your First Destination Survey.
  • Apply any labels or filters necessary to get down to the list of students you want to email. For example, you might just want to email students with an “Unsubmitted” response status, or you could be targeting students in a certain major.
  • Use the checkboxes next to students’ names to select the students you want to email. The checkbox at the very top of the box will allow you to select everyone at once.
  • Once you’ve selected your students, you’ll see a blue More dropdown bulk option show up at the top of your list of students. Click on it and select Send Email to Surveyees.
  • This will take the your selected list of students into the Targeted Email flow in Handshake. Proceed through the flow to create your content and schedule your email.
  • You’ll want to include a link to the first destination survey in your email so that you can redirect your email recipients to it. You can find the external link on the Details page of the Survey Setup tab. You can choose to use either the standard link or the logged out link.
  • Once you complete the email flow and schedule your email to go out, you’ll have sent an off-cycle FDS reminder email!

Use Skip Logic in Your Additional Questions for FDS

Creating a “skip logic” survey allows you to direct respondents to the appropriate questions based on their previous answers, making the user experience better.

Get insight into students’ interests and preferences after graduation by creating a “skip logic” survey in Handshake and attaching it to your FDS!

Tip: we recommend planning your survey questions and responses beforehand to make the process easier. For example, if you plan to ask “What are you primarily doing after graduation?”, you’ll need to plan the options you’d like students to choose from. From there, you can create additional questions based on their responses.

Once you have your survey planned, you’ll need to create a survey in Handshake’s survey section, then attach the survey to the corresponding FDS.

Create a new survey

To create your own survey, refer to Creating and Testing Surveys for outlined instructions.

To use the First Destination Template in Handshake, follow the steps below.

  1. Click Surveys on the left navigation bar, then click New Survey From Template.

  2. Click First Destination Survey Additional Questions from the list.

  3. On the Setup tab, enter the survey setup details:

  • Title - enter the title, which will be displayed to survey recipients
  • Description - provide a description as desired
  • Required for Students? - check this box if this survey is required for students. If marked, this will display a message under the student’s survey section in Handshake. Please refer to How to Take a Survey in Handshake for the student’s perspective of this message.
    • Tip: don’t check this box if this is a survey you plan to attach to a form or appointment
  • Available to employers? - check this box if you’d like employers to find and take this survey
  • Completion Label - if selected, the label will be applied to any users who complete this survey
    • Tip: if you plan to use a completion label, but the desired label has not been created, open your School Settings in a new tab or window (via right click, open in new tab/window), and create the label. When you come back to the survey creation, the new label should be listed in the dropdown.
    • For more details, refer to About Survey Completion Labels. When you’re ready to proceed, click the blue button Next in the bottom-middle of the screen.
  1. On the Pages tab, all working options for students to choose from are listed:
  • Working
  • Volunteering
  • Continuing Education
  • Military
  • Still Looking
  • Not Seeking Note: once a student chooses a response from the list, they’ll be directed to additional questions that build on their response. These questions are created on the next step.

To edit a response, click Edit to the right of the option.

To add a response, click the blue button Add Page, located in the lower-left corner of the page.

To rearrange the order, click on the page and drag it to the desired location.

When you’re ready to proceed, click the blue button Next in the bottom-middle of the screen.

  1. On the Questions tab, all questions for each of the responses will be displayed. Use the left menu to review questions for each response option.

To edit a question, click Edit to the right of the question.

To delete a question, click Edit to the right of the question, then click the red button Delete.

To add a question, click the blue button Add Question, located in the lower-left corner of the page.

When you’re ready to proceed, click the blue button Next in the bottom-middle of the screen.

  1. On the Review tab, confirm that all the information on the survey is correct and ready to go! If so, click the blue button Save Changes in the lower-left corner of the page, then click the green button Create.

Note: surveys cannot be edited after responses have been submitted. Please make sure this survey is finalized before sending to students or employers.

Tip: if you test the survey, do not submit your response.

Attach the survey to your FDS

Open the First Destination Survey you’d like to attach your skip logic survey to, then click the Survey Setup tab.

Review the information for the FDS, then click the blue button Next.

Scroll towards the bottom of the Details page and locate the Custom Questions section. Click the dropdown to choose the corresponding survey.

Once the survey has been added click the blue button next in the lower-right corner of the page and proceed with the survey FDS setup. Your custom survey questions will be added to your FDS!
