If you believe you don’t have access to school-specific offerings on Handshake, your account may not be connected to your school’s Handshake instance.

To unlock your school’s full range of content and services on Handshake, your account must be linked to your school.

After confirming your email address, if you only have access to sections like Feed, Events, and Profile—but not Career Center—this likely means your account isn’t connected to a school or was created without selecting one

School Not Linked

If you requested to connect with a school, you can check the status of your request by clicking your account icon in the upper-right corner of the page, then selecting School Connections from the dropdown. If your request is still pending, you’ll have the message:

“Request sent! Hang tight while the school reviews it.”

To follow up, click the Email the school link under Having issues?

If no contact information is listed, you can either reach out to your school’s Career Services (You can typically find contact info on the school website) or by contacting our Support team.

Tip: while waiting to be connected, you can begin filling out your profile on Handshake! To learn how, check out Completing your Profile in Handshake.

Create a Saved Search

Users can perform searches in different areas of Handshake and save their search criteria, making future searches easier to retrieve and reuse.

For example, your staff may have to perform repeated searches, such as searching for juniors with a GPA above 2.5 who have scheduled a career services advising appointment.

Topics:

- Saved search overview
- My saved filters
- Set saved search as default or delete a saved search

Saved search overview

There are many areas in Handshake where Career Services staff can create and save filtered or saved searches, including Manage students, Experiences, Job Reviews, Resource Library, Events, Career Fairs, Appointments, Job Postings, Interviews, Employers, Contacts, and Analytics.

Although the search criteria will vary in each of these pages, the steps you will follow to create and save a search will be similar.

Note: when saving a search, you are saving your search criteria, not your search results. Searches are always performed using real-time data, so your results will likely change if you rerun the search later.

My Saved Filters

We will use the Employer page as an example below.

To create a saved filter, you will need to first create your search criteria.

  1. From any screen, click Employers located on the left navigation bar, then select [your school]’s network.

Note: When you visit a page that allows for saved searches, also referred to as saved filters, you will view the option to save these filters. This can be displayed either in the filter sidebar or in the upper-middle section of the screen.

  1. Use the Favorites, Collections, Assigned to, or the Filter button at the top of the page to select the criteria for your search. As you adjust your search criteria by adding or removing options and selecting Apply, the list of employers displayed in the results table will change.

  2. After selecting your search criteria, you can save your filters by clicking Save search located in the upper-right corner of the page.

  3. A pop-up window will appear on the screen and prompt you to enter a Name and Description for your saved search. You can also select Make this my default landing experience, so whenever

  4. Once you have entered this information, click the “Save search” button in the lower-right corner of the pop-up window.

  5. Once saved, the message “The saved search has been created” displays in a banner in the lower-right corner of the screen.

  6. After saving your filters, you can select the dropdown arrow on the right of the Save search button to display your current saved searches.

Choose from the list of saved searches and click “Apply search” to use those set of filters.

Note: When multiple filters are applied in the same saved search, you will notice that there is AND logic across different filters (i.e., Status = Approved AND Type = Public) and OR logic within the same filter (i.e., Employer Industries = Retail Stores OR Manufacturing). For more information on the reporting and filtering logic, refer to the custom reporting section in Analytics: Using ‘AND’ Filtering in Custom Reports.

Set saved search as default or delete a saved search

To set your saved search as your default set of criteria or delete a saved search, click the dropdown arrow to the right of Save search. Then, click the ellipsis to the right of the saved search and select either “Set as Default” or “Delete saved search”

A message appears in the bottom right corner of the page to confirm whether the saved search is set as a default filter set up or if the saved search was deleted.

Create a Student Account Associated with Your Career Services Account

We recommend creating a student account associated with your career services account, in order to test different functionalities in Handshake from a student perspective.

To link your Career Services account with the Student account, you must use the same email address that is connected to your Career Services account.

First, find out whether or not you already have a Student account. While logged into your Career Services account, click on your name in the upper-right corner of the Handshake screen, then click on Switch Users. If Switch Users isn’t listed, or if you click on Switch Users and you don’t have Switch to Student Account on the following screen, you will need to create your student account.

Best Practice: If you are not actually a student, we strongly recommend setting your account visibility to Private, so that employers don’t accidentally source you instead of your students when looking for candidates. For more information on how to do this, refer to How to Change Your Student Profile Privacy Setting.

To create your student account

  1. Click Manage from the left navigation bar in Handshake.

  2. Click the tab New Student in the upper-right corner of the page.

  3. Enter the information for your student account:

  • Email address (Make sure you use the same email address that your career services account uses so you can switch between these accounts)
  • *Username (Username is used in student imports to identify a student. It must be unique.)
  • Auth identifier (This should be the username users sign in to your Single Sign On system)
  • Card
  • *First name
  • Preferred name
  • Middle name
  • Last name
  • School year
  • Visa status
  • Campus
  • Assigned To
  • Work study eligible
  • Exclude From Automatic Syncs (Checking this box will make sure that this user is not updated by any automatic student syncs you have setup in Handshake.)
  • Archive This Profile (do not check this box)
  • Status (select the radio button for active)
  • Mobile (Format: +15556667777)
  • Message
  1. Click Create User in the lower-right corner of the page. When you choose to Switch Users, you should now have the option to Switch to Students Account.

Best Practice: Handshake recommends that you create a label for all career services student accounts so they do not throw off any reports that you run. Example: cs students.

Once your student account is created, check out Switching User Views for more information!

If you are interested in creating an employer account as well, refer to Create an Employer Account Associated with Your Career Services Account.

Create an Employer Account Associated with Your Career Services Account

This article explains how to create an employer account using the same email address as your career services account.

If you want to create a student account using the same email address, refer to Create a Student Account Associated with Your Career Services Account.

Before you begin

Keep the following in mind before creating your employer account:

  • Sign out of your career services account before you begin creating your employer account.
  • Using an incognito or private browsing window can help prevent your browser from automatically signing you back in to your career services account during registration.

Single single on (SSO)

To connect both your career services account and employer account to the same email address, you’ll need to create Handshake login credentials. Employer accounts do not use Single Sign-On (SSO) to access the platform.

Note: Your Handshake login credentials are separate from your school’s SSO login. Your Handshake password is unique to the platform and is not linked to your school’s SSO login.

Create an employer account

  1. Go to app.joinhandshake.com.

  2. Enter your first name, last name, email address, and the password associated with your career services account.

  3. Review the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy, then click the black Create account button.

  4. A yellow banner will appear below the email address field with a message that your email already exists in Handshake and is associated with an career services account. This is expected.

  • If you forgot your password, click Reset it in the yellow banner, then return to app.joinhandshake.com to complete registration.

  1. Confirm that the email address, first name, last name, and password match your existing account, then click Create account again.

  2. Check your inbox for a confirmation email from Handshake with the following details:

From: handshake@notifications.joinhandshake.com

Subject: Confirm your email address on Handshake

Body: “Welcome to Handshake! Please confirm your email address to get started.”

Confirm email [button]

If this is a mistake or you didn’t initiate this request, contact Handshake support.

Click the Confirm email button in the email.

  1. After confirming your email address, Handshake redirects you to complete your employer profile.

For the remaining registration steps, refer to How to Create an Employer Account on Handshake.

After you create your employer account

After you sign in, you can switch between your career services account and employer account from the menu under your name. For more information, refer to Switching User Views.

Creating an Account and Logging In to Handshake

This guide walks you through the different ways you can log in or create an account, whether your school is partnered with Handshake or not.

Topics:

  • Registering an Account with a School affiliation
  • Registering without a School
  • How to Log In After Creating Your Account
  • Logging in with Apple or Google: FAQ’s

Registering an Account with a School affiliation

If your school is partnered with Handshake, you can log in using your school’s credentials or create your own Handshake credentials using your .edu email address.

  1. Join Through the Invitation Email (for School Partners)

If your school partners with Handshake, you’ll receive an invitation email from your Career Services Center with a link to claim your account. Click the link to log in and complete your account setup.

If you didn’t receive the email or want to log in directly, go to the Handshake login page and enter your email address.

  1. Select Your School

From the dropdown menu, select your school. Schools are listed alphabetically.

Note: Only the first 25 schools appear in the dropdown. If your school isn’t listed, search for it by name. If it still doesn’t show, your school may be in the process of integrating with Handshake. For more details, check out School Not Found on Handshake.

  1. Log In/Create Handshake Credentials

Once your school is selected, you’ll receive the following options:

  • School’s Single Sign-On (SSO): Log in with your school credentials.
    • Tip: If you don’t remember your school login details, try using the same username and password you use for other school systems, like your student portal.
  • .edu Email Address: Set a unique password for Handshake. If your school hasn’t created an account for you yet, you’ll be prompted to set up and verify your own. To begin, select “I’m a Student or Alumni” to start the account creation process.

If you’re not receiving the confirmation email, refer to Troubleshooting Missing Confirmation Email.

To learn more about verifying your phone number, refer to Phone Number Verification for Students on Handshake.

After your account is verified, you’ll be guided through an onboarding experience. For more information learn more about this, check out The Student Onboarding Experience.

Important: If you created your own account to connect with a school, you’ll either be automatically approved based on your email domain, or need to wait for a manual approval by your Career Services center. If you have any questions about your pending connection, you’ll need to reach out to your school’s Career Center.

Registering without a School

If your school isn’t partnered with Handshake, you can still create an account and use Handshake’s features.

  1. Create an Account Without School Affiliation

Go to go to the Handshake login page and enter your email, then click the “Continue without a school” link, located below the Next button to proceed with the registration process.

Note: If you choose this option, you will not have access to all the features available to students affiliated with a school, such as school-specific job postings and events.

  1. Enter your First and Last name and choose your login method

You can sign up using one of the following methods:

  • Continue with Email: Create a password to log in with your email.
    • Note: Password must be between 8 and 50 characters and contain at least 2 of the following categories: letters, numbers, and special characters.
  • Sign in with Google or Apple: Skip the email/password setup by logging in with your Google or Apple account. Click the Sign in with Google or Sign in with Apple button on the registration page, follow the prompts, and your account will be automatically created. By continuing, you agree to our Terms of Service and Privacy Policy, and you’ll start getting emails from us. Unsubscribe any time.
  1. Verify Your Email

Check your inbox for a confirmation email. Click the “Confirm Email” link to verify your address. If you’re not receiving the confirmation email, refer to Troubleshooting Missing Confirmation Email.

  1. Verify Your Phone Number

To keep our community safe, Handshake requires phone verification. For more details on this process, refer to Phone Number Verification for Students on Handshake.

After your account is verified, you’ll be guided through an onboarding experience. For more information learn more about this, check out The Student Onboarding Experience.

How to Log In After Creating Your Account

Once your account is set up, you can log in at: app.joinhandshake.com

You’ll have the option to log in using one of the following methods:

  • If you registered with your school: You can log in using your your school’s Single Sign-On (SSO), your Handshake credentials, your Apple/Google login, or a one-time password sent to your email.
    • Note: Your school’s SSO is different from Handshake credentials. If you’ve been logging in via SSO or no longer have access to it, you can create a Handshake-specific password. For instructions, refer to How to Set Up Handshake Login Credentials (if you’re unable to use Single Sign On)
  • If you registered without your school: You can log in using your Handshake credentials, Apple/Google login, or a one-time password sent to your email. Handshake Password: If you’ve created a password and need to reset it, refer to Reset the Password for a Student Account in Handshake.

Apple or Google Login: To use Apple or Google login, the email associated with that account must match the email on your Handshake profile.

One-time password: Signing in with a one-time password allows you to securely access Handshake without entering your regular password. When you choose this option on the login page and your email is verified, Handshake sends a unique, single-use link or passcode to your email. Clicking the link or entering the passcode will log you in without needing a password.

Note: The single-use link and passcode expire after a short time to help keep your account secure.

Logging in with Apple or Google: FAQ’s

  • Social login methods (Apple and Google) both require an email address to connect or authenticate to an existing account. Apple must share your email unless it’s already been linked. Google always shares your email by default.
  • If your Apple ID is tied to an outdated or inaccessible email address, you may not be able to complete sign-up or log in. You’ll need to use a current, accessible email.
  • If Apple does not resend name or email data—both required to complete sign-up—the process may fail.
  • Handshake requires users to share their email when signing up with Apple. The “Hide My Email” option is not supported, as we need the email to create and link your account.
  • You can remove Sign in with Apple from your Handshake account by going to your Apple ID settings, selecting Sign in with Apple, finding Handshake, and choosing to stop using your Apple ID with the app. This must be done through your Apple ID settings, as disconnection is not currently managed within Handshake. For step-by-step instructions, check out Apple’s Support page.
  • To manage your Google account connection, you can refer to Google’s Support article.

Filter Logic in Handshake

Understanding the way filter logic works throughout Handshake will help you isolate information more efficiently while getting the most accurate results possible.

Across Manage Students, Manage Employers, Manage Jobs, Emails, Insights, and more, the filter logic operates the same (with ONE exception: the “Other” sections in Manage Students/Employers/Targeted Emails Recipients, addressed at the end of this article).

Within a Single Filter:

When you select a single filter, say for example School Year, and you choose more than one option within that filter, the logic is “OR”. This means the results will pull in any users or items that match either of the options selected.

In this example for School Year, I’ve selected Freshman and Sophomore on the Manage Students page, so any student that is listed as a Freshman OR Sophomore will appear in the results.

You can see next to each school year name the total count of students that meet that criteria, and in the list of students, there is a total count of results:

Across Multiple Filters:

When you select criteria from 2 or more filters, the logic is “AND”.

If we continue the example from above, I’ve left the School Year filters selected, and I add on the filter for Industry Interest.

Now, the results will only show students that are listed as either Freshman OR Sophomore AND have selected the Industry Interest “Movies, TV, Music, Gaming”.

We see the total count of students in the Industry Interest filter, with a breakdown of students by School Year:

The One Exception - Other

The only exception that exists at this time is in the section “Other” for Manage Students/Employers/Targeted Emails Recipients. You can find this filter under the Filters button.

These sections could be mistaken for one category, but in truth, each filter is a stand-alone filter, meaning that “AND” logic will apply across each of these options.

In this example from the Manage Students page, students will be selected that both have a mobile login AND are identified as an Athlete:

Getting Started with Handshake

Welcome to Handshake! Whether you’re a student, recent graduate, early career professional, or exploring new career opportunities, we’re excited to have you here. In just a few steps, you’ll gain access to job opportunities, career resources, and more!

Click on the expandable sections below for a guide to get started.

Step 1 - Login/Create your Handshake account

Login

If your school has partnered with Handshake, you should have received an invitation email from your Career Services Center. Use the link in the email to log in and claim your account.

If you don’t have an invitation email from your school, go to the Handshake login page and select your school from the dropdown menu to proceed.

To learn more about creating an account and logging in, refer to Creating an Account and Logging In to Handshake.

To learn more about student accounts on Handshake, check out An Overview of Student and Alumni Accounts in Handshake.

Step 2 - Upload documents

By uploading resumes, cover letters, transcripts, and other relevant documents, you can apply for jobs directly through Handshake. This streamlines the application process and ensures that all necessary documents are readily available to potential employers you apply to!

To learn more about how to upload a document, refer to How to Upload a New Document.

Step 3 - Fill out your Profile

Filling out your profile includes many benefits! For example, you’ll receive personalized job recommendations, proactive employer outreach, and the opportunity to showcase your skills and experience.

Note: you are in control over who has access to your profile. To learn more about your privacy options, refer to Profile Privacy Options in Handshake.

For more information on filling out your profile, refer to Completing your Profile in Handshake.

If there are already details in your profile, this means your school partners with Handshake and has pre-loaded your information, usually based on data from the school registrar. Check to be sure all pre-loaded information is correct, especially your major and GPA (if included); if you find any errors, contact your school’s Career Services Center to correct it, as Handshake is unable to change any of your profile data.

Step 4 - Explore Handshake

Use your home page, and other tools available on Handshake to look for companies, events, and jobs you’re interested in learning more about or applying to!

To learn more about your home page, check out Navigating the Student Homepage.

To find jobs of interest, refer to Searching for Jobs and Internships.

To find events and fairs to sign up for, check out Discover Events & Fairs in Handshake.

Tip: you can always save your searches in Handshake by clicking the bookmark icon. This makes finding relevant employers and jobs easy to access later. To do this, refer to Saved Job Searches and Alerts.

Step 5 - Follow jobs and employers you’re interested in

When you follow an employer or a job, you’ll receive alerts when a job application window is closing or when an employer is attending an event or fair at your school.

Learn more about following employers in Following an Employer in Handshake.

By following these five steps, you will be well on your way to utilizing Handshake to effectively and efficiently kickstart your career!

Handshake Career Services Best Practices

Here are some tips for career centers on managing Handshake with ease. Follow these and you’ll be a Handshake expert in no time.

When you come across a problem on Handshake, follow these steps for help!

Find an expert in your office:

Have a Subject Matter Expert for different areas or modules of the Handshake platform and celebrate them by making them known throughout the office. Print our our template attached and fill in the relevant Handshake experts for your office so you know who to turn to for advice:

  • Importer ________________
  • Employer/Contact Management ________________
  • Student Approvals ________________
  • School Settings ________________
  • Experiences ________________
  • Appointments _______________
  • Labels ________________ Utilize Training Resources:

Handshake offers a wide variety of helpful resources for different types of learners. Whether you like to read through step-by-step articles, attend webinars, or watch interactive videos, our resources are here to help!

Training Courses ● Help Center ● Webinars ● Support Office Hours

Access these resources at support.joinhandshake.com.

Office Training Sessions

We understand that everyone learns differently and that you know how to best teach your office teammates new skills. Take advantage of that and schedule 1:1 or group training sessions to teach key features of Handshake! Some examples of trainings include:

  • Live demos with Power Point materials
  • Circulating summarized information from webinars and support office hours to the rest of your team
  • Creation of in-office training materials specialized for your team’s needs
  • 1:1 sessions with new employees during onboarding Eyes on the Prize

Handshake can be overwhelming to learn, but don’t worry! Here is some advice from some Handshake veterans:

  • “The key to success is communicating how Handshake helps each student/employer in a unique way” – Texas Tech University, Rawls College of Business
  • “Enable conversations to be more about the work and less about the tech functionality if you keep a human involved” – Biola University

How Faculty Can Use Handshake

Many schools encourage faculty and staff to use Handshake in order to promote student log-ins and activations. This can:

  • Lead to increased student engagement on Handshake
  • Help associate the brand & impact of the larger Handshake network with individual departments or programs There is not specific “faculty” account type, so you can use this article to understand the tradeoffs associated with each of the 3 current account types in Handshake. However, the Career Services account may commonly be referred to as a faculty account type by our users.

For more information on how to introduce Handshake to campus parters (faculty and staff) refer to Best Practices: How to Introduce Handshake to Faculty (Campus Partners)

  • Student accounts (Recommended Approach)
    • Pros:
      • They can see exactly what students can see
      • They can find jobs that are relevant to their students
      • They can’t change any settings at the school level
    • Considerations:
      • They could apply to jobs / RSVP for events when they shouldn’t be able to
  • Employer accounts connected to the university employer profile
    • Pros:
      • Faculty can post on campus jobs and interact with students like an employer would
      • Faculty manage their own profiles
    • Considerations:
      • Faculty won’t be able to manage students and perform other admin roles
      • The experience is different than what a student may experience, which will make it hard for them to show students what Handshake is like, and why they should use it
  • Admin / Career Services accounts
    • Pros:
      • Faculty have access to any roles you would like them to have: manage experiences, manage students, view jobs posted , create appointments with students
      • They can curate content (e.g. apply labels to job postings to share with their students)
      • They can send emails
    • Considerations:
      • You will have to manage a large number of staff in the staff management page, and the product currently doesn’t provide a way to quickly organize or filter staff accounts
      • They will have read / write access which means they could have access to data and account settings that shouldn’t be edited

How to Log into Handshake Mobile

Handshake’s mobile app is a great way to find and apply for jobs, sign up for events, engage on the feed, and more!

The mobile app is free to download and use on iOS and Android devices!

To start, search Handshake in the app store on your mobile device and download it!

Logging into Handshake via the mobile app

  1. Open the app on your device and enter your school to get started — Tap in the search box to type in the name of your school, then select it from the dropdown.

  2. Enter your email address that’s connected to your Handshake account, then tap Continue.

  3. Check your email for a unique code sent to your inbox.

Subject: “Here’s your sign-in link”

From: Handshake handshake@m.joinhandshake.com

Body: “Finish signing into Handshake from your mobile device by tapping below. This link can only be used once and expires after 30 minutes.

[Finish signing in button]

Having trouble with the link? Copy this code into the Handshake app to log in.

[CODE]

Pro tip ☝️ Protect your privacy — don’t share this link with anyone else!”

  1. Copy the code provided within the email, then click the button Finish signing in.

  2. Paste the code into the provided field within the app, then tap Continue.

If you haven’t logged into Handshake before, you’ll be taken through the on-boarding process before accessing your Handshake account.

To log out of the mobile app, tap your account icon in the upper-left corner of the screen. Select Account Settings from the menu, then tap Log Out. Confirm by tapping Log Out again to exit your Handshake account on the app.

If You Accidentally Requested to Connect with Wrong School

Each school manages its own student and alumni approvals in Handshake. If you requested a connection to the wrong school, use the steps below depending on your situation.

If you request hasn’t been approved

If the school you requested to connect with hasn’t approved your request, you can update it by following these steps:

  • Click your account icon in the upper-right corner of the page, then select School connections.

  • If your request shows as Pending, click Cancel request and confirm when prompted. After canceling the request:

  • Use the Find your school search bar to locate the correct school.

  • Select your school, then enter your email address and any additional required information.

  • Verify your email address to complete the connection.

If your request was approved by the wrong school

  • Contact the career services center at your correct school.

  • Let them know you were added to the wrong school in Handshake. Be sure to include:

  • Your full name

  • The email address you use for Handshake Your school’s career services team can then reach out to Handshake to have your account moved to the correct school.

Tip: You can usually find your school’s career services contact information on its official website.

Login to Handshake as a Career Services Staff Member

Refer to this article when logging into Handshake for the first time!

If you do not have a Career Services staff account yet, you’ll need to work with your institution’s POC or someone with the access and permission to create new staff accounts.

  • Career Services staff accounts may only be created by either your institution’s Handshake POC or someone with the Staff Management permission. The step-by-step process to create a staff account is available in Creating New Staff Accounts. There are two ways to login to Handshake as a Career Services Staff Member. The one-time passcode grants you access into Handshake immediately. The alternative method requires you to set a password the first time you attempt it.

How to login to Handshake as a Career Services Staff Member using a one-time passcode

  • Go to the Handshake login page
  • Type your university email address into the Enter email section and select Next

  1. Select Send one-time code to receive a temporary login code via email

  2. An email is sent to your inbox with a code from handshake@m.joinhandshake.com with the subject line “Here’s your one time password”. Enter that code to log in to Handshake and select Verify to log in. Select Resend code to receive another code to login

How to login to Handshake for the first time as a Career Services Staff Member by setting your password

  1. Set your password by going to the password reset link (https://app.joinhandshake.com/password_resets/new) and enter your email address, then select Reset password

Note: If you ever need to reset your password, you can use the same link provided in step 1

  1. Open the email and select the Set my password hyperlink

  2. You will be asked to enter a new password and confirm the password

  3. You will be redirected to enter your email on the login page again. This time, you can choose to type in a password instead of selecting the one-time code. Choose Continue with password to login.

An Overview of Student and Alumni Accounts in Handshake

Both current students and alumni can access Handshake with a Student account. However, some features that are specific to the school may only be available to those who are attending the current school year.

The features available to your account will depend on:

  • Your account’s connection with a school instance
    • You may need to be approved by the school to access all of their offerings.
  • Your school’s partnership status with Handshake
    • A school is considered a Handshake partner if the Career Services Center has chosen to manage your school’s instance and use Handshake for additional features, such as managing Appointments, internships (via Experiences), First Destination Surveys, and more.
    • Schools that haven’t yet partnered with us may still have a school instance as part of the Handshake Open Network. Read more about our goals for Expanding Our Efforts to Help All Students Find Opportunity. To use Handshake as a current student or alum, you’ll need a Student account. For more information on creating a student account, check out Getting Started with Handshake!

Click on the expandable headers to learn more!

Not connected to a school in Handshake?

If your account isn’t connected to a school instance yet, you won’t have access to all of their offerings until you are. Until then, you can manage your profile and access public career fairs on Handshake. This is typical if you have created a new account and your school request is pending.

For more information on how to get connected with a school, check out If You Can Only Access Profile and Fairs.

If you attend a Handshake-partner school

Once you’re connected to a Handshake-partner school, you can access your school’s career center via the left navigation menu.

Click Career Center to access your career services staff, schedule appointments, complete a First Destination Survey, take a survey, or check out additional resources your career center has created for you!

If you attend a school that hasn’t yet partnered with Handshake

If you’re connected to a school that hasn’t yet partnered with Handshake, you can:

  • Manage your profile
  • Access fairs and events hosted by Handshake-partner schools that are public
  • Apply to jobs posted by a subset of trusted employers One way to determine if your school is a Handshake partner is by checking for the Career Center option in the left navigation menu.

If there’s no Career Center available to you, and your request to connect isn’t pending, this means your school is not a Handshake partner yet.

If you’re enjoying your experience with Handshake, feel free to encourage your career center to formally partner with us and we can unlock additional benefits for you and your school!

Performing Bulk Actions

This article provides streamlined process to take bulk actions. We will be using the Manage students and Contacts list pages as examples.

If you are on the Manage students page, simply check one box on the left of a student’s name to have access to the bulk actions. You also have the option to Select all, without manually checking each box. You will have options appear to take actions, including a More dropdown button, which gives you additional options to choose from.

The Contacts page is another location where you can utilize bulk actions. In this screenshot, we selected the top most box on the far left side of the screen to select all contacts. You will have options appear to take actions, including a More dropdown button, which gives you additional options to choose from.

Note: If you use the email options (Send Email to Users/Draft targeted email) on either the Manage students or Contacts page, you will be be able to send to a maximum of 50,000 recipients. If you’d like to message more than 50,000 recipients, refer to our targeted email article Creating and Sending Targeted Emails.

Phone Number Verification for Students on Handshake

To keep Handshake a secure and trustworthy platform for students and early talent, phone number verification is required during sign-up for accounts not created by a school. This applies to both the web and mobile app.

If your school hasn’t created an account for you, you’ll need to verify your account via text message during sign-up.

Phone verification helps us:

  • Prevent fake and duplicate accounts
  • Build a trusted space for job seekers and employers alike To learn more about creating an account on Handshake, refer to Getting Started with Handshake.

How the Verification Process Works

When creating your Handshake account, you’ll be prompted to verify your email address first. After that, you’ll be asked to enter your mobile phone number. The country code will be pre-selected based on your location.

The following message is displayed:

“We use phone verification to keep our community safe. By continuing, you agree to get a one-time SMS. Rates may apply.”

Note: Not all country codes are supported at this time. You must be able to verify a phone number with a supported country code to access Handshake.

Step 1: Enter your mobile number

Input your phone number when prompted during sign-up then click Continue.

Step 2: Receive a verification code

You’ll receive a one-time verification code via SMS. If you don’t receive it right away, you can request it again after 60 seconds.

Step 3: Enter the code

Type the code into the verification screen to complete the process.

Once verified, your number is securely stored and used only to confirm your identity and prevent misuse (such as creating multiple fake accounts). It will never be used for marketing and will not be visible to employers or other users.

Additional Information

  • Unsupported numbers: If your number can’t be verified (e.g., VoIP or toll-free numbers), you’ll be prompted to try again with a valid mobile number.
  • Accounts created before verification was required: If your account was created before phone verification became mandatory and you’re not affiliated with a school, you’ll be asked to verify your number the next time you log in.
  • Changing or updating phone number: phone numbers cannot be edited, even by Handshake admins
  • Disconnecting a phone number from one account to use with another account: Phone numbers cannot be edited; the only way to remove a phone number from an account is to delete that account altogether.
  • Phone number is associated with another account: If you’re unable to identify which account your phone number is linked to, contact Support for further investigation and provide the phone number you’re attempting to use.

Troubleshooting tips

Didn’t receive a verification code?

This is usually caused by rate limiting, carrier filtering, or blocked messages. Try the following:

  • Wait 30 minutes before requesting another code. Requesting multiple codes in a short period can temporarily pause code delivery as a security measure. After 30 minutes, request a new code only once. Keep in mind that codes can arrive late. If a delayed code arrives, it may have already expired, so use the most recent code you receive.
  • Make sure your phone can receive SMS messages from U.S. numbers. Verification codes are sent from a U.S. phone number. Some carriers and prepaid plans block international SMS by default, so confirm that international SMS is enabled with your carrier.
  • Check for blocked numbers or spam filtering.
    • Android: Open the Messages app → tap the three-dot menu → Spam & blocked → unblock any unfamiliar numbers.
    • iPhone: Go to Settings → Apps → Messages → Blocked Contacts, and check your Unknown Senders or Junk messages if applicable.
  • Check your Focus or Do Not Disturb settings. Make sure notifications or messages aren’t being silenced.
  • Use a standard mobile number. Virtual or VoIP numbers (such as Google Voice or TextNow) often cannot receive verification codes.
  • Perform a few quick device checks. Confirm that you entered the correct phone number and country code, ensure you have cellular service, and try toggling Airplane Mode on and off or restarting your phone.

School not Found on Handshake

If you’ve tried to sign up for a Handshake account, and couldn’t find your school, it’s possible:

  • You’re using an email address other than your school-provided one
    • You’ll need to sign up with your .edu email address to connect you with the proper school. We recommend double-checking the email you’re signing up with.
  • Your school is currently in implementation, and hidden at the moment
  • Your school isn’t partnered with Handshake To confirm your school’s status, we recommend reaching out to your Career Services Center. You can find their contact details by visiting your school’s website or doing a quick search online.

You’re using an email address other than your school-provided one

In order to be linked with your school through Handshake, you’ll need to register using your .edu email. By using your school-provided email address, the system can help connect you to your school instance. We recommend double-checking the email you’re signing up with.

Your school is currently in implementation, and hidden at the moment

If your school is partnered with us and in implementation, you’ll need to wait until they are completely setup and live on the platform before creating your Handshake account. Your Career Services center will typically send out an invite once they are ready!

Your school isn’t partnered with Handshake

Some schools may not be a Handshake partner. If you’re signing up with your school email, and you’re still not finding your school on the list, click the link Continue without a school to start the registration process without being affiliated with a school.

💡Note: If you do not connect with a school instance, you will not have access to all the features Handshake has to offer.

Handshake is currently available only in the United States, United Kingdom, Germany, and France. If your school is outside these countries, you won’t be able to create an account at this time.

The Student Onboarding Experience

Handshake’s onboarding experience sets you up for success with a few impactful questions. From the start, we help clarify your career goals, personalize your job search, and build your professional network—so you can discover relevant opportunities and make meaningful connections from day one.

Note: You can update your interests and preferences on the platform anytime if they change after setup.

Additionally, every 6 months, you’ll be prompted to complete a quick re-onboarding process. This helps you review and update your selections to ensure you’re getting the most relevant job recommendations.

Don’t worry—re-onboarding does NOT mean your profile has been deleted. It’s simply a prompt to ensure you’re getting the most relevant job recommendations.

To update your career interests, refer to Update Your Career Interests. To update your information, refer to Update Personal Information on Your Profile.

Confirm your information

Add or review the following information for your account:

  • First name
  • Last name
  • Education level
  • Graduation month
  • Graduation year
  • Major
  • Add a personal email — Use this email to access Handshake after you graduate. If you’re prompted to re-onboard, you’ll have the opportunity to review and update your information as needed.

What kind of jobs are you open to?

Choose from the following:

Which jobs sound interesting?

Select from the available options or use the search bar to add your own.

Which industries are you curious about?

Select from the available options or use the search bar to add your own.

Where are you open to working?

Select from the available options or use the search bar to add your own.

Choose Your Profile Visibility

Your profile helps people, employers, and opportunities find you. By default, your profile visibility is set to Community, which means other students, alumni, and employers on Handshake can view your profile, message you, and follow you. You can also post to the feed!

To change your profile visibility, click Change, then select your preferred setting in the pop-up window. For a detailed explanation of each option, refer to Profile Privacy Options in Handshake.

If you choose the Community option, you’ll also have the option to make your profile shareable outside of Handshake. To do so, check out How to Make Your Handshake Profile Public and Share Your Profile Link.

Important: When you select the option for employers to find and view your profile, you’re consenting to the section of our Terms of Service and claiming your own account. By doing so, you take ownership of the FERPA data and choose to share it. That information is no longer protected by your school’s FERPA responsibility and is now owned by you.

Build Your Network

Follow suggested users to jumpstart your community and enhance your feed experience. Click Follow & finish up to follow all suggested users, uncheck any you don’t want to follow, or select Maybe later to skip this step for now.

Once you’re done, you’re all set to start exploring Handshake! Click Start exploring to dive into jobs and connect with the community.

Switching User Views (Getting Started in Handshake)

Handshake users can create multiple account types using the same email address, such as Career Services, Employer, and Student accounts.

If you have more than one account type linked to the same email address, you can switch between them without logging out.

To switch between account views, each account must be created using the same email address.

Each linked account must also have a confirmed email address before you can switch between account views.

You may need to switch account views if:

  • you are in the wrong account view
  • you cannot access certain features, such as teammate management
  • you need to complete an action that is only available to a specific account type

Switching users from a career services account

  • Click your name in the upper right corner of the Handshake screen.
  • Select Switch Users from the dropdown menu.
  • All connected accounts will be listed. Select Switch to Students Account or Switch to Employers Account, depending on which account you would like to access.

Switching users from an employer account

  • Click your name in the upper-right corner of the Handshake screen.
  • Select Switch Users from the dropdown menu.
  • All connected accounts will be listed. Select Switch to Career Services Account or Switch to Student Account, depending on which account you want to access.

Switching users from a student account

  1. Click your account icon in the upper-right corner of the Handshake screen. This may appear as your first initial or a small photo if you have a profile picture.

  2. Select Switch Users from the dropdown menu.

  3. All connected accounts will be listed. Select Switch to Career Services Account or Switch to Employers Account, depending on which account you would like to access.

If an expected account does not appear

If an expected account type does not appear in the list, or Switch Users is unavailable, confirm that each account was created with the same email address.

If your accounts use different email addresses or different email domains, Handshake treats them as separate accounts and they will not be linked for switching.

Errors when switching accounts

If you receive an error message while switching accounts, review the sections below.

Email verification required

If you receive a message indicating that you need to verify your email address, you must verify the email associated with your Handshake account.

Click the verification link in the message to receive a verification email. Then open the email and follow the instructions to complete verification.

Common reasons you may receive this message include:

  • Support manually added your account upon request
  • Support assisted with a sync and your account was not fully verified Note: Each account created in Handshake must be verified before use.
Email confirmation required

If you receive a message stating that you have not confirmed your email address, you will need to confirm the email associated with your account.

Click the link in the message to resend the confirmation email, then follow the instructions provided.

If you are not receiving the confirmation email, refer to Troubleshooting a Missing Confirmation Email.

Troubleshooting a Missing Confirmation Email

The confirmation email sent during account creation is important for security and for accessing your Handshake account. If you haven’t received it, use the steps below to troubleshoot and resend the email.

Troubleshooting steps

Step 1: Check your email address
  • Make sure the email you used during sign-up is spelled correctly.
  • Look in your junk or spam folder.
  • Search your inbox for “Email Confirmation.”
  • If you encounter the message “Couldn’t find that account” when trying to log in, your email may have been entered incorrectly during sign up. In that case, you will need to create a new account.

Step 2: Review your email client settings

Sometimes filters or security settings route emails away from your main inbox.

Tip: Review any rules, filters, or spam settings that may prevent delivery.

For client specific guidance, choose your provider below:

  • Gmail
  • Outlook
  • Yahoo

Step 3: Add Handshake to your contacts and resend the email

  • Add handshake@m.joinhandshake.com to your contacts.
  • Log in to Handshake. You will be redirected to a page indicating your email hasn’t been confirmed.
  • Click the Resend confirmation email button on the page to resend the confirmation email. The message should arrive right away, but it can take up to 10 minutes.

Step 4: Contact your IT department

If you still haven’t received the email, reach out to your company or institution’s IT team. Ask them to confirm that Handshake messages aren’t being blocked and request that they add our domain to their allow list.

Note: Some organizations use a 24 hour quarantine period for new vendors or rely on antivirus tools or firewalls that may delay or block email delivery.

Step 5: Wait and resend

After IT has reviewed the issue, log in to Handshake and resend your confirmation email. If your institution or organization uses a 24 hour quarantine period, wait the full day before trying again.

If you’ve completed the steps above and still cannot receive the email, contact Support.

Using Notes in Handshake

This resource will help you understand how to use the Notes tool as well as how Note privacy works.

Within Handshake, you can add Notes to certain items. These include:

  • Students
  • Events
  • Contacts
  • Jobs
  • Appointments
  • Interviews
  • Employers

Creation

When creating notes, please be aware that only career services staff will see the note; it can never be visible to employers or students, unless they also have a career services staff account at your school with the necessary permission.

  1. Click the blue button View & Add Notes on the desired item (job posting, event, etc.).

  2. A pop up will appear with the information listed below.

Notes are private and will not be seen by anyone except you and your staff. If you select ‘Personal Note’ the note will only be visible to you. To mention a co-worker, type ‘+’ and their email address.

Note: Mentioned coworkers will only receive the notification if they have the appropriate notifications enabled. Please refer to Career Services User Settings: Manage Your Notifications for more information. Mentioning yourself won’t send a notification to yourself.

Enter the following:

  • Note content in the Add a Note… text box.
  • Attachment: click Choose File to add a file.
  • Set a Reminder if you’d like a notification from Handshake to remind you of the note
  • Select desired note privacy with the blue button Share with Staff (read more about options in the section below)
  1. Click the blue Add Note button when you’re ready to save the note.

Once a note has been created, only the original creator will be able to edit the note content.

Privacy

When creating a note, you are able to select who is allowed to view the note:

  • Personal/Private: only you, the creator, will see the note. The note will not be included in any reporting (Analytics or Quick Downloads).
  • Share with Staff: this will share the note with all Career Services staff that have the “Show Private Notes By Staff” permission, and the note data (creation date and time plus content) can be included in reporting.
  • Share with “Career Center Name”: only other users connected to your career center will be able to access the note. This option will only appear if your school has more than one career center configured.
    • Note: You must be connected to the career center in order to select the career center or view related notes. You can adjust your career center connections in User Settings > Personal Information > Career Centers.
      • Learn more about connecting in Career Services User Settings: Personal Information (Profile).

Reporting on notes

You can report on notes by creating a custom report in Analytics. Notes are provided in certain report templates such as the Employers and Appointments.

What Happens If I Misspelled My Email When Signing Up?

It’s possible that your email address was accidentally mistyped when you registered for your new Handshake account—no worries, it happens to the best of us!

If you remember the misspelled email address, please let us know and we can delete that account for you. In the meantime, feel free to start over using the correct email address.

If you don’t remember the misspelled email address, you can simply start over and register again with the correct one.

What if I signed up for the wrong account type?

If you accidentally created an employer account but you’re actually a student or alum, this can be fixed.

Option 1: Create your student/alumni account

You can still create a student/alumni account using the same email address you used for your employer account.

  • Log out of Handshake (if you’re signed in).
  • Go to the student sign-up page: app.joinhandshake.com
  • Enter the same email address and follow the prompts to create your student/alumni account. Tip: If you get a message that your email is already in use, open an incognito/private browsing window and try signing up again.

For detailed steps, refer to Getting Started with Handshake

Option 2: Remove an employer account you don’t need

If you do not need the employer account at all, you can request that it be removed. Let us know the email address you used for the employer account.

We can help remove the unnecessary employer account so you can just use your student/alumni account going forward.

Why can’t I access my career services account in Handshake?

Below are common reasons you may have trouble logging into Handshake, and what to do in each case.

1. You may not have an account

If you receive the error message:

“Hmmm… Looks like there is no account on file for EMAIL.”

it means there’s no account associated with your email.

If you are a career services staff member and need a Handshake account:

  • Contact a colleague or supervisor who already has a career services Handshake account.
  • Ask them to create a staff account for you using your work email address. Note: The staff member must have the appropriate permissions to create staff accounts. For more information about required permissions and how to set up staff accounts, refer to School Settings: Career Services Staff Roles and Permissions.

2. You may have entered the wrong email address

If you receive the error message:

“Hmmm… Looks like there is no account on file for EMAIL.”

it can also appear if the email you entered does not match the email on your existing Handshake account.

Common reasons:

  • Your Handshake account is associated with a different email address (for example, if you have multiple work emails).

  • Your organization uses email aliases, and you are entering an alias instead of the primary email. Handshake treats aliases as separate email addresses.

  • Your email address was misspelled when the account was created. To troubleshoot:

  • Try logging in again using the exact email address used when your account was created.

  • If you are not sure which email was used, try any other work emails you have.

  • If none of your emails work, ask your career services Handshake admin to confirm which email is on your account.

3. You may need to clear your browser cache

If you have logged into Handshake before but now cannot log in, even though you are sure you are entering the correct email and password:

  • Your browser’s cache or stored data may be causing issues. To try resolving this:

  • Clear your browser’s cache and cookies.

  • Close all browser windows.

  • Open a new window and try logging into Handshake again.

  • If possible, also try a different browser (for example, Chrome, Firefox, or Edge).

4. You may have entered the wrong password

If you receive the error message:

“You entered an invalid password. Don’t have an account yet?”

either:

  • The password you entered is incorrect, or

  • There is no Handshake account associated with the email you used. To reset your password:

  • On the login page, select Reset Password?

  • Enter your email address and click Reset Password.

  • You’ll be prompted with a message:

  • “Almost there! Please check your email to set your password.”

  • Check your inbox for an email from handshake@m.joinhandshake.com.

  • Open the email and click Reset My Password.

  • You will be taken back to Handshake. Enter and confirm your new password, then click Reset.

  • After the reset is successful, log in with your new password. Important notes:

  • If you do not have an account with the email address you entered, you will not be able to complete the reset flow. In that case, refer back to the “You may not have an account” section above.

  • If you do not receive the reset email, confirm that you entered the correct email and check your spam or junk folder.

5. Your account may be deactivated

If your account is deactivated, you will receive the message:

“Account Deactivated. If you would like your account reactivated, please contact Handshake Support.”

In this case: Someone at your school or organization has deactivated your account. To reactivate your account, reach out to your school’s admin and let them know you’d like your account active again.

6. You may be experiencing SSO login issues

If your school or organization uses SSO (single sign-on ) and you receive a specific SSO error message when trying to log in:

  • Refer to the SSO troubleshooting article: SSO Setup Guides: Login Error Codes by SSO Type
  • Follow the steps listed for the error you are receiving. If you still cannot access your account after following these steps, reach out for further assistance.

Getting Started With Handshake

About AI Powered Features in Handshake for Employers

At Handshake, we are committed to making the hiring process easier, more efficient, and more effective for employers.To support this mission, we use artificial intelligence (AI) in various features within the Handshake platform.

This article provides a detailed overview of how these AI-powered features function, what they are designed to do, and how they benefit you as an employer using Handshake.

Our use of AI is governed by a commitment to transparency, fairness, and responsible innovation. We follow these principles:

  • We never make hiring decisions on behalf of the employer. We keep a “human in the loop” and do not use AI for automated decision making.
  • We do not share data with third parties for AI training purposes. We do not export employer data to third party AI vendors for training purposes, nor do we ingest employer data from ATS or other systems for training purposes.
  • Governance and control: We maintain oversight of all AI models through internal governance frameworks and ensure compliance with applicable privacy and regulatory requirements. We use observability tools and follow a quality assurance process to monitor performance. Where appropriate, we also conduct independent AI bias audits.
    • The latest summary of results conducted by independent auditor Holistic AI can be found here.

Which Handshake features use AI?

1. AI-Powered Autofill

Handshake uses AI to reduce manual work for recruiters by extracting data from job posting text to pre-populate fields in Handshake.

  • Job Form Autofill
  • How the AI use case is triggered: Job form autofill is primarily triggered by employers through the Handshake application when they start posting a job. Employers have the option to use AI to break down their job posting text into the required Handshake job fields. The autofill option is selected by default, but employers can choose to de-select it. Job form autofill is also used to fill out fields for publicly posted jobs that are imported into Handshake.
  • Employer control: Employers retain full control, with the ability to edit or disregard AI-generated suggestions.
  1. Campaign Segment Autofill
  • How the AI use-case is triggered: When an employer starts creating a campaign and attaches a job post, Campaign Segment Autofill pre-populates suggested targeting filters based on the job requirements. Employers can review, edit, or add to these filters before finalizing the campaign.
  • Employer control: Employers retain full control, with the ability to edit or disregard AI-generated suggestions.
  • Data and privacy: These features do not access or rely on any personal data. Only job details are processed. Note: In the future, we plan to extend AI-powered autofill capabilities across other areas of the product, following similar model & data use and privacy considerations above.
2. AI-Assisted Draft Messaging

Handshake offers AI-powered features to assist employers in crafting messages to reduce manual work in message creation and improve personalization of messages:

  1. AI-Assisted Direct Messaging
  • How the AI use-case is triggered: When an employer opens the message composer to draft a message to a single candidate from a relevant product area, such as Matches or Applicants, Handshake offers an AI-generated draft personalized to the candidate and job.
  • Employer control: Employers retain full control, with the ability to edit or disregard AI-generated suggestions.
  1. Automated Message Generation for Automated Job Promotions (AJPs)
  • How the AI use-case is triggered: When Handshake Plus employers create an Automated Job Promotion, Handshake offers an AI-generated draft message personalized to the candidate and job.
  • Employer control: Employers retain full control, with the ability to edit or disregard AI-generated suggestions.
  • Data and privacy: We obtain applicable consents from educational institutions and students to share student information with employers. Sensitive demographic information such as race or gender is not used to generate messages. Note: In the future, we plan to extend AI-assisted messaging capabilities across other areas of the product, following similar model & data use and privacy considerations above.
3. AI-Powered Audience Selection

Handshake provides AI-powered features to select student audiences most relevant for employer campaigns and other promotions:

  1. Campaign Relevance
  • How the AI use-case is triggered: When an employer initiates a campaign, AI is used to select the student audience most likely to find it relevant
  1. Dynamic Targeting in Campaigns
  • How the AI use-case is triggered: When an employer initiates a job campaign, they have the option to further optimize campaign delivery by delivering outreach in batches to students with the highest predicted likelihood to apply.
  • Employer control: Campaign Relevance is used across all campaigns, but employers have the option to choose whether to use Dynamic Targeting.
  • Data and privacy: Employer and job details, and candidates’ interest and activity patterns (e.g., previous job clicks or applications) are used to surface opportunities to a relevant student audience. Data is pseudonymized before being ingested into the applicable underlying AI models powering Campaign Relevance and Dynamic Targeting, meaning it cannot be traced to the individual. Note: In the future, we plan to extend AI-powered audience selection across other product areas where promoted opportunities are surfaced.
4. AI-Powered Relevance

Handshake uses AI to surface the most relevant candidates to employers across the product including:

  1. Job Matches
  • How the AI use-case is triggered: When an employer views candidates on Job Matches, candidates are sorted based on Best Match by default.
  • Employer control: Employers can change the sorting to alternative criteria like name and recent activity.
  1. Talent List
  • How the AI use-case is triggered: When an employer views candidates on Talent List, candidates are sorted by an evaluation of the candidate’s relative qualifications and interest in the employer’s job. For example, we consider whether the candidate has engaged with the employer in the past through messaging, following, or applying, and whether their profile matches any active jobs the employer has posted
  • Employer control: Employers can view alternative lists of candidates by viewing saved searches or filtering by segments or other candidate criteria.
  1. Applicant Management (available to Plus and Pro)
  • How the AI use-case is triggered: When an employer views applicants on the Applicants tab, they can define which criteria to use to rank those applicants.
  • Employer control: Employers can choose to sort applicants by application date or name instead.
Data and privacy (applies to Job Matches, Talent List, and Applicant Management)

Employer and job details, and candidates’ interest and activity patterns (e.g., previous job clicks or applications) are used to present the most relevant profiles. No protected categories (e.g. race or gender) are used to determine a candidate’s relevance.

Note: In the future, we plan to extend AI-powered relevance across other areas of the product, following similar model & data use and privacy considerations above.

Employer Validation

Handshake partners with Persona to verify that employers on the platform are legitimate and authorized to hire.

Handshake also uses proprietary fraud detection technology to add additional layers of security during verification and continuously monitors for fraudulent activity after verification to help keep all platform activity and user interactions secure.

Note: Only the employer user who creates the company profile must complete the validation process. Other users who join the company profile do not need to complete validation. If the profile creator is inactive, contact Support.

Haven’t created an employer account yet? Refer to How to Create an Employer Account on Handshake.

Submitting your government-issued ID

When you create a new company profile, a modal appears prompting you to verify your company and identity.

  1. Click the black button Get started to begin.

  2. On the Let’s get down to business screen, review the auto-populated company details (legal name, business registration number, DBA if applicable, website) and update them if needed. Click Save and continue.

Note: One of the most common reasons employer verifications fail is due to incorrect or mismatched business registration information. To avoid delays, ensure you provide the correct Employer Identification Number (EIN or TIN) and the legal business name exactly as registered with the IRS.

If your company operates under a “doing business as” (DBA) name or any other variation, it will not pass verification. Only the official legal name associated with your EIN/TIN should be submitted.

  1. On the next screen, select the country that issued your government ID, then choose the appropriate type of ID (driver’s license, passport, or other available option).

  2. Upload a clear, legible photo or scan of your identification document.

  • You will be prompted to upload photos of the front and back of your ID.
  • If your images cannot be verified, tips will be provided to help you confirm your identity. After reviewing the tips, click the Retry button to upload your photos again.
  1. Persona will process the submission. Upon successful completion, the confirmation message displays:

“Congratulations, you’re done! Thanks for verifying your identity. Click the Done button to finalize the process.

  • If Persona cannot process your ID on the first attempt (e.g., due to blurriness, expiration, etc.), you will have four additional attempts.
  • After the fifth attempt, no further attempts will be available, and Persona will use your final submission to verify your identity. After you submit your ID, your company account automatically enters the company verification stage.

Canceling an employer verification request

Verification requests that have entered the verification stage cannot be canceled directly in Handshake.

If you have already reached the verification stage and want to cancel the request, contact Support.

Company verification process

Once your information has been submitted, Handshake begins verifying your company account.

During this time, the following message will be displayed: “Almost there! Verifying your company account… This should only take a moment.”

Once your company profile is verified, you will receive an email notification and gain access to Handshake.

The email will read:

From: Handshake employers@g.joinhandshake.com

Subject: “Your company profile has been validated”

Body:

“You now have access to Handshake!

Your company profile has been validated. Log in to update your company profile, post jobs, attend or create events, and engage with students.

[Log in to Handshake] button.

Need help getting started? Here are a few helpful insights and tips that will jumpstart your recruiting efforts for early talent.”

Further review required

If your company requires additional review by our Trust and Safety team, the following message will be displayed:

“Hang tight—your company requires further review.

Your job is not posted yet.

After new employer verification, your account needs further review by our Trust and Safety team. We’ll email you as soon as your account is ready, usually within 1 business day. If you have additional questions, contact us.”

Access to the platform will be restricted during this period and will only be granted after the review is complete.

Account could not be verified

If your company cannot be verified, the following message will be displayed:

“Your company could not be verified, and your job was not posted.

Your company didn’t pass our verification check. Please reach out as soon as possible.”

Click the Contact us button on the screen to connect with our Trust and Safety team for assistance.

You will also receive an email notifying you that your account couldn’t be verified, along with the next steps to take.

The email will read:

From: Handshake handshake@notifications.joinhandshake.com

Subject: “Contact us-your account couldn’t be verified”

Body:

“Contact us-your account couldn’t be verified. Looks like your company didn’t pass our verification check. Please reach out Handshake as soon as possible.

[Contact us] button.”

Temporary suspension during or after verification

If a potential risk is detected during verification or subsequent account activity, your company account may be temporarily suspended.

When this occurs, the following message will be displayed:

“Your company is temporarily suspended.

Your job is not posted yet.

{Company name} account has been suspended by our Trust and Safety team for a potential violation of our Terms of Service. If you have additional questions – Contact us.”

An email will also be sent to the address associated with the account, explaining the reason for the suspension and providing next steps, including a direct link to contact our Trust and Safety team.

Trust and Safety review

The Trust and Safety team may review your account if company verification cannot be completed automatically, if additional manual review is required, or if your account is suspended.

To complete this process, verifiable and supporting documentation may be required.

Examples include:

  • An endorsement from a university partner
  • Proof of personal identity (e.g., driver’s license, passport)
  • Proof of company affiliation (e.g., business license) To restore access to your Handshake account, contact Support. After the review is complete and no safety concerns are found, your access will be restored and you will receive an email confirming that your account is active.

Multi-factor authentication

As an additional security measure, you may be required to complete multi-factor authentication when logging in.

  • A 6-digit code will be sent to your registered email address.
  • Enter the code within 15 minutes to access your account.
  • If the code is not received, click Re-send code to generate a new one. To ensure email deliverability, refer to How can I ensure deliverability for Handshake emails?.

On-campus employers and employer accounts created by career services

To reduce platform risk, most employer accounts are required to complete the employer verification process. However, the review experience differs depending on how the account is created.

Employer accounts created by Career Services staff

  • When a Career Services user creates an employer account from their Career Services profile using their institution email address, the account automatically bypasses employer verification.
  • If a Career Services user creates an employer account with a personal or non-institutional email address, the account will follow the standard employer verification process. On-campus employer accounts

On-campus employer accounts follow the standard verification process. During this review, our Trust and Safety team identifies eligible on-campus employers and approves those accounts accordingly.

Account monitoring, fraud detection, and review

All employer activity on Handshake is continuously monitored for potential fraud or other high-risk behavior.

If an account is identified as high risk, it may be submitted for review, and access will be granted or revoked based on the Trust and Safety team’s assessment.

The Handshake EMEA Migration: What You Need to Know (Employers)

Handshake has consolidated its EMEA platform into a single global platform. Unlike student and alumni accounts, EMEA employer accounts were not migrated and are not automatically part of the global network.

If you previously recruited on Handshake’s EMEA platform, you’ll need to re-create your employer account on the global platform to continue using Handshake.

What’s different for employers

Moving to the global platform requires a few additional setup steps. We understand this may take a little extra time, but once you’re set up, you’ll have access to a broader network of talent and the same hiring tools on the global platform.

  • Create a new employer company profile: If your company doesn’t already have a company profile on the global platform, you’ll need to create one. For step-by-step instructions, refer to How to Create a New Company Profile.
  • Create your employer user account: If you need to create a user account and connect it to your new employer account, check out How to Create an Employer Account on Handshake.
  • Historical activity: Job postings, candidate messages, saved candidates, and other activity from your previous EMEA account won’t be carried over to the new global account.
  • Access to a global talent pool: Once your account is set up, you can post jobs and connect with students and alumni across Handshake’s global network, expanding your reach beyond the former EMEA platform. Learn how to post a job in How to Post a Job.
    • Note: Your new global account gives you access to more candidates and universities. To target specific schools, select “Post to specific schools or use a school list” when posting a job. You can choose schools individually or create and use a preferred school list. Learn more in Creating and Managing School Lists.
  • Your data continues to be protected under the same privacy standards outlined in Handshake Infrastructure & Data Update.

Handshake Supported Browsers (for Employers)

Employers should use a desktop browser for the best and most seamless experience across the Handshake platform.

Please note that our site format and usability may be impacted on tablets or mobile devices.

For the best experience on Handshake, we recommend using Google Chrome, which supports all platform features, including integrated video with blurred backgrounds.

If Chrome is not your default browser or is otherwise inconvenient to use, Handshake also supports most features on the latest versions of the following browsers:

  • Firefox
  • Safari
  • Microsoft Edge Note: We no longer support any version of Internet Explorer.

Outdated browsers

If you are using an outdated browser version, the following error message may appear:

“It looks like your browser is out of date and not fully supported. This may cause Handshake to work improperly. We recommend updating your browser for a better experience and improved security.”

You should be able to use Handshake features with most modern browsers released within the last rolling 6 months. However, there may be certain limitations or behaviors specific to the browser used.

It is recommended that you update your browser whenever there is a new version available, as these updates often include performance and security improvements.

Troubleshooting tips

If you encounter unexpected errors or unusual behavior while using Handshake such as “SyntaxError Unexpected token ‘u’”upstream c” is not valid JSON”, open Handshake in Chrome and try again.

  • If you’re already using Chrome, or if the issue occurs in multiple browsers, clear your browser’s cache and cookies. For additional guidance, refer to Refresh your Cache.
  • If you cannot clear your cache immediately, you can use an incognito or private browsing window:
    • PC (Windows 7/8/10/11):
      • Chrome: Press Ctrl + Shift + N.
      • Firefox/Edge: Press Ctrl + Shift + P.
    • Mac (OS X):
      • Chrome/Safari: Press Command + Shift + N.
      • Firefox: Press Command + Shift + P. If the issue persists after these steps, contact Support.
