  • The job will be submitted for review and approval. For additional details, refer to Understanding Job Posting Approvals. To post your job to recommended schools, check out How to Post a Job to Additional Schools.

How to Post a Job to Additional Schools

To post a job to additional schools in Handshake, the job must be active and meet Handshake’s standard posting criteria.

Who can post to additional schools

Your ability to post to additional schools depends on your account type and whether you created the job:

  • Basic employers: You can post to additional schools only for jobs you personally created. Jobs created by teammates are view-only. To post jobs created by teammates, upgrade to an eligible paid plan.
  • On-campus employers, Plus, Pro, Essentials, and Enterprise (formerly TES) customers: All users except Representatives can post to additional schools, whether the job was created by themselves or a teammate. If the posting is saved but not yet posted, refer to How do I post a ‘not posted’ job to a school?.

When a job cannot be posted to additional schools:

  • The opening date is within the past year, but the closing date is more than a year after the opening date. To resolve this, update the closing date to fall within 365 days of the opening date.
  • The opening date is over a year ago and the closing date is more than a year after the opening date.
  • Your company has been declined by the school..

Select job

  1. Click Jobs from the left navigation bar, then select the job you want to post to additional schools.

  2. On the job posting page, click the Schools tab.

How to post to a specific school

  1. In the Post to more schools section, click into the search field and type a school’s name or location. Avoid abbreviations for best results – for example, type “Massachusetts Institute of Technology” instead of “MIT.”

  2. Select the correct school from the results. Repeat to add more schools. To remove a school, click the X next to its name.

  3. Click the black Post button to the right of the section title.

How to post to a school list

  1. Click the Lists button to the right of the search field.

  2. Select the list you want to use. All schools in that list will be added to your posting.

Available lists depend on your account type:

  • Basic, Plus, and Pro employers: Only your Favorites list is available.
  • Essentials and Enterprise customers: Your Favorites list and any lists created by you or your teammates are available.

How to post to all available schools or the full network

Depending on your account type, different options are displayed:

  • Basic, Plus, and Pro employers: Option to auto-select schools, which includes all schools you are approved to connect with.
  • Essentials and Enterprise customers: The full network option is only available for jobs that meet Handshake’s standard posting criteria. The button will not appear for on-campus, co-op, or federal work-study roles, unpaid positions, or jobs listed at a residential address. For full posting criteria, visit How to Connect with Handshake Open Network.
To post to all available schools or the full network:

  1. Check the box labeled Post to all available schools or Post to full network above the search field.

  2. Click the black Post button to the right of the section title.

  3. A confirmation banner will appear: “Jobs sent to schools. Your Requested schools list will update shortly.”

How to post to recommended schools

  1. In the Recommended schools section, click Post job here now within the school card you want to post to.

  2. In the pop-up, review the application open and close dates, then click Post Job to submit for approval.

Note: Any additional schools selected will adhere to the original open and close dates.

  1. A confirmation message will appear within each school card you posted to.
  • Track approval status in the Status column of the Requested schools section.

Why is a school missing from search results?

If a school does not appear, does not show up, or cannot be found in your search results, one of the following applies:

  • The school is not partnered with Handshake.
  • Your company was declined by the school.
  • Your company is approved, but your connection does not include permission to post jobs to that school.

How to View Comments on a Job Posting

Employers can view and respond to comments left by schools on job postings while the posting is active.

To set up or adjust your job notification preferences, refer to Default Notification Preferences (Employers).

Note: Comments on closed job postings remain accessible for 30 days after the job is closed.

View comments

  1. Click the globe icon in the upper-right corner of any page in Handshake to open your notifications.

  2. Click the Notification type dropdown, select Comments, then click the black Apply button.

  3. Locate the relevant job in your notifications and click the job title to open the posting.

  4. On the job posting page, click the Schools tab, then navigate to the Requested schools section.

Tip: The Comments column shows the number of comments left by each school, so you can quickly identify which schools have left comments without clicking into each one.

  1. Click the More actions icon (three horizontal lines) to the far right of the school name.

Tip: Use the Search for a school field to quickly find the relevant school by name.

  1. Select View Details from the dropdown.

  2. In the pop-up window, review the comment(s) left by the school.

To respond:

  • Enter your message in the Comments and Activity text box.
  • Click Add Comment to submit your reply.
  • Click Close to exit the window

Resubmit your Job for Approval

If a school has declined your job posting, they may invite you to submit a second approval request after reviewing the reason for the decline.

This article explains how decline notifications work and how to resubmit your job if the option is available.

For background on how job postings are approved, refer to Understanding Job Posting Approvals.

Note: Employers can only be invited to resubmit a job for approval once.

Topics:

  • How job declines work
  • Decline notifications
  • Submit a second approval request

How job declines work

When a school declines a job posting, they are prompted to select a reason for the decline and decide whether to allow a second approval request.

The decline reason is added as a comment on the job posting and can be accessed from the Requested Schools section in the Schools tab of the posting.

The comment is visible to both the school’s team and any teammates connected to your company profile.

To access decline comments, refer to How to View Comments on a Job Posting.

Decline notifications

When a posting is declined, Handshake automatically sends a notification to the teammate who posted the job, based on their notification preferences.

To adjust your preferences, refer to Default Notification Preferences (Employers).

In Handshake:

  • Click the globe icon in the upper-right corner of any page, to the left of your name.

  • Select School from the left sidebar, then locate the notification by school name. The notification reads: “A staff member at [SCHOOL NAME] has declined the job [TITLE] at [SCHOOL NAME].”

  • Click directly on the job title to view the decline details.

Via email

Decline notifications are sent to the email address associated with the Handshake account of the teammate who posted the job.

  • Sent from: handshake@notifications.joinhandshake.com
  • Subject: “Your job [TITLE] has been declined at a school.”
  • Body:
  • Your job [TITLE] is declined at [SCHOOL NAME]
  • Hello [NAME],
  • [SCHOOL NAME] declined your job [TITLE] for the following reason(s):
  • [REASON]
  • Comment: [CUSTOM COMMENT FROM SCHOOL]
  • [View Decline Details]
  • For more information about the job decline process, visit our help center. Click View Decline Details to log in to Handshake and view the decline.

Submit a second approval request

If the school has opted to allow a second request, follow these steps to resubmit your job.

  1. In the pop-up, review the decline reason and any comments provided by the school.

  2. To respond before resubmitting, enter your reply in the text box in the Comments & Activity section, then click the gray Add Comment button.

Tip: Address the school’s concerns and respond to any comments before resubmitting.

  1. Click the blue Request approval again button, then click Close in the lower-right corner.

Note: If the Request approval again button is not visible, the school has not opted to allow a second request.

Understanding Job Posting Approvals

When you post a job on Handshake, each school you select must approve your posting before it becomes visible to students.

This article explains how the approval process works, what each posting status means, and how edits affect your posting’s approval.

If you have not yet posted a job, refer to How to Post a Job.

Job posting approval process

It typically takes 1–5 business days for a school to approve a job posting. If there is no status change within that time frame, you can leave a comment on the posting or contact the school directly for more information.

  • Learn How to View Comments on a Job Posting.
  • Find How to Contact a School.

Job posting statuses

Active postings are jobs that have not yet closed and have one of the following statuses:

  • Pending: The posting has been successfully requested at the school and has not yet been processed.

  • Approved: The posting is visible to students at the approving school, based on the job’s open date.

  • Declined: The posting has been reviewed and declined by the school. Declined jobs are not visible to students at that school. Inactive postings have one of the following statuses:

  • Closed: The posting was previously approved, and the close date has passed.

  • Not Posted: The job was created and saved but has never been submitted to a school.

How edits affect your posting

You can edit a job at any time, but the outcome depends on the posting’s current status.

  • Pending: Edits do not affect the status or request date. The posting remains pending until the school processes it.
  • Approved: If you change the application open or close dates, the posting will return to pending and the school will need to approve it again. All other edits are saved and appear immediately at approved schools without changing the approval status.
  • Closed: Renewing a closed posting resubmits it to the schools it was originally posted to for approval.

Jobs

About Job Roles (EDU Partners)

This article explains how Handshake uses job roles to connect students with relevant opportunities and how career services staff can apply this knowledge to support students in their job search.

  • For information on how students interact with job roles, visit Job Roles (Students).
  • For information on how employers use job roles, visit About Job Roles and Job Role Groups (Employers).

How Handshake assigns job roles to postings

When a new job posting is saved on Handshake, the system automatically tags up to three job roles on the posting based on the job title and description. A student’s preferred job role is one of the strongest predictors of whether they will apply to a particular job. By automatically assigning the most relevant roles to job postings, Handshake helps students find jobs that match their interests and ensures the right students are surfaced for each opportunity.

Job role groups were identified using resources such as career interests, user research, majors, and data coverage of job details. A complete list of 380+ role group names and a mapping of each group name to over 8,600 job roles is available in the attached spreadsheet at the bottom of this article.

On-campus employment best practices

The following examples can help on-campus employers identify the most appropriate job roles for common positions:

  • For office assistant, data entry, or other clerical positions: General and Miscellaneous Office Clerks and Administrative Support Workers
  • For fundraising and event management positions: Fundraisers or Meeting, Convention, and Event Planners
  • For research-related positions: University Student Researchers For positions not listed above, download the attached spreadsheet to find the full job role group list and mapping.

About the Apply Start Date

Every job posting in Handshake has an Apply start date, which is the date students can begin applying for an approved position.

This date is determined by one of the following:

  • A custom date set by the job posting creator
  • The job posting approval date at your institution, if no Apply start date is specified
  • The Apply start date of an interview schedule attached to the posting Note: If a job posting is approved but the Apply start date is set to a future date, students can access the posting but will not be able to apply.

Locate the Apply start date

The Apply start date is available in several places in Handshake:

  1. Filters

On the job postings page, click the white Filters button to open the filters side sheet. Under the Dates section, enter a date range using the Apply start date min and Apply start date max fields. For more information, visit Job Postings Page Overview.

  1. Posting side sheet

Click on a job posting to open the details in a side sheet. The Apply start date is listed in the Open for applications field, which displays the full application date range.

  1. Job details page

From the side sheet, click the ellipsis icon in the upper-right corner, then select View job details to open the job details page in a new tab.

The Apply start date is listed under the Global Apply Start Date field at the top of the page.

  1. Job creation

When creating a new job, the Application open date field is located in the Application process section. This is where the Apply start date is set.

Acting on Behalf of Employers: Editing a Job Posting

This article explains how Career Services users can edit job postings for on-campus and non-campus employers in Handshake.

Note: You can only edit job postings for on-campus employers who have selected your school as their associated school, and employers who have granted your school permission to post and edit jobs on their behalf.

Find the employer

  1. From the left navigation bar, click Employers under Relationships.

  2. Click the [Your School’s] Network tab.

  3. Click Filters to open the filter panel.

  • If searching for an on-campus employer, check On-campus employer under the Other section.
  • If searching for a non-campus employer, select the relevant filters for your search.

  1. Click the black Apply button in the lower right corner. The table will update to show the employers that match your selected filters.

  2. Click the name of the employer whose job posting you want to edit.

Locate the job posting

  1. On the employer’s profile page, click the Jobs tab.

  2. In the jobs table, click the name of the job posting you want to edit. The job posting will open in a new tab.

Edit the job posting

  1. On the job posting page, click the Edit button to the right of the section you want to update. The available sections include:
  • Basic information
  • Position details
  • Location requirements
  • Time requirements
  • Compensation and benefits
  • Categorize your job
  • Candidate qualifications
  • Additional qualifications
  • Application process
  • Your hiring team

  1. Make your changes within the section, then click the black Save button.

  2. A confirmation banner will appear at the top of the page indicating the job was saved successfully.

Repeat these steps for each section you need to update.

Acting on Behalf of Employers: Posting a Job

Career services staff can post job listings directly on Handshake on behalf of employers at their institution.

Use this guide to ensure you have the necessary permissions and information before posting.

Topics:

  • Before posting a job
  • Post a job on behalf of an employer
  • After posting a job
  • What to do if you cannot get permissions

Before posting a job

Check if the employer is approved by your institution

Navigate to Employers from the left navigation bar and select the [School name]’s network tab to confirm the employer is approved by your institution and has the necessary roles to post jobs at your school.

Verify you have permission to post on the employer’s behalf

Before posting, confirm with the employer that they want you to post a job on their behalf. Some employers prefer to maintain consistency across their job postings and may not want career services staff to post on their behalf.

If the employer approves, discuss the following details before posting:

  • Application deadline
  • Which students will be able to apply
  • Any other relevant details about the job posting Next, confirm that the employer has granted your institution permission to post jobs on their behalf.

Employers can do this by navigating to their Global Settings and selecting your school under Select which schools can post and edit jobs on your behalf.

If you cannot find the employer when posting the job, it is likely they have not granted your institution this permission. For more information on employer global settings, visit Company Settings: Global Settings.

Post a job on behalf of an employer

  1. Click Job postings under Jobs from the left navigation bar.

  2. Click the + icon in the upper-right corner of the page. The job form will open in a new tab.

  3. On the Basic information page, search for and select the employer you are posting on behalf of in the Employer field.

  4. Complete the remaining fields in the job form. For guided steps, refer to How to Post a Job.

  5. On the Additional qualifications page, you can optionally complete the following fields:

  • Colleges: Add specific colleges affiliated with your institution where students would be a good fit for the role. Students outside of the selected college will still be able to apply.
  • Labels: Add labels to restrict applications to only students with those labels. Note: This page is only visible to career services users and is not part of the employer job posting form.

After posting a job

Once the job has been posted, inform the employer and ask them to review the posting to confirm all details are correct. You may also want to:

  • Discuss with the employer whether they would like to promote the job through your institution’s Handshake instance.
  • Check the job posting regularly to stay up to date on applicants.

What to do if you cannot get permissions

If the owner of the company profile is unavailable to grant posting permissions, you can instead post the job from your own employer account.

To help students and staff easily recognize these postings:

  • Update your company profile name to a clear, recognizable name, such as The [X] University Network or Friends and Alumni of [X] University. Contact Support to request this change.
  • Include the employer name in the job title, such as “Sprinkle Dreams: Brand Ambassador.”
  • Add the job posting to collections to highlight it to students.

EDU: Jobs Imported into Handshake from External Sites

Handshake imports externally posted jobs to ensure students have access to a comprehensive set of opportunities without leaving the platform.

Imported jobs come from LinkedIn and company websites, and are only imported for employers that already exist in Handshake and have completed the verification and validation process.

Note: Imported jobs are currently available only for Basic employers.

For information on the employer experience with imported jobs, visit Imported Jobs on Handshake.

Imported job criteria and behavior

  • Jobs must meet your institution’s auto-approval criteria to be posted to your school. For more information on your auto-approval criteria, refer to Job Automatic Approval Configuration.
  • Imported jobs that meet your auto-approval criteria are posted automatically and do not require manual approval from you or your staff. You will not receive an influx of pending job postings from this process.
  • As with other approved jobs, you may decline an imported job after it passes through automatic approval.
  • Imported jobs function as external-apply job postings on Handshake. When a student clicks Apply, they will be directed to the employer’s external application flow.
  • Students cannot tell that a job has been imported. Employers, however, will have a visual indicator confirming the job was imported by Handshake.
  • Imported jobs do not have an assigned owner by default. Any user connected to the employer account, with the exception of representatives, may claim ownership to manage and review applicants for that job.

How to Filter for Interview Status on Job Posting Page

In Handshake, you can filter approved job postings by interview status to identify whether an employer has indicated interest in interviewing for a position or has scheduled an interview.

Filter by interview status

  1. Click Job postings in the left navigation panel.

  2. On the job postings page, click the white Filters button to open the filters side sheet.

  3. In the filters side sheet, scroll to the Posting status section, then locate the Interview status field. Click the search field to display the available options and select one of the following:

  • Scheduled: The employer has created an interview schedule with this job attached. The interview schedule can be found in the Interviews tab in the left navigation panel.
  • Interested: The employer has indicated they are interested in conducting on-campus interviews for this position. This does not create an interview schedule.
  • None: No interview status has been indicated for this position.

How to Send an Email to Job Contacts

In Handshake, you can send an email to job contacts or creators directly from the Jobs postings overview page.

For information on how to email other contacts outside of job postings, visit How to Send an Email to Job Contacts.

Send an email to job contacts

  2. The Pending tab loads by default. Select the relevant status tab as needed: Pending, In progress, Approved, Declined, or Expired.

  3. Select the job or jobs you want to include in the email using one of the following methods:

  • Individual job: Click the ellipsis icon on the job row, then select Email creators.

  • Creators

  1. A new email will be generated. For more information on composing and sending emails in Handshake, visit Creating and Sending Targeted Emails.

How to Use Bulk Actions on Jobs

Bulk actions provide a quick way to complete a task or action for several job postings. Options for Jobs will appear when you have at least one posting checked from the table view on a single Status tab. For more information on Status tabs, refer to Job Postings Page Overview.

Note: bulk actions may only be completed per status tab. All selected postings must be on the same tab in order to be included.

Bulk actions are available on all job posting Status tabs. To complete a bulk action, take these steps:

  1. Click Jobs from the left navigation bar and select the relevant status tab as needed to view jobs: Approved, In Progress, Pending, Declined, or Expired.

  2. Use the filters to narrow down displayed results, then put a check to the left of each of the job titles desired.

  3. Choose the desired bulk action:

  • Select all
    • This will select all job posting on this page.
  • Approve/Decline
    • You will see approve or decline depending on the status tab that you are using.
    • For more information about approving and declining employers through job postings, refer to Processing Employer Approval Requests using Job Based Approvals
  • More (dropdown menu):
    • Set to “In Progress”
    • Manage job labels
      • If the label being removed is greater than 100, we recommend removing it in sections of 100 or less each time.
    • Email to Students
      • You can choose up to 30 jobs to promote in the email.
    • Email contacts or creators
    • Decline employers
      • Employers can be declined on the jobs page. Please refer to Processing Employer Approval Requests using Job Based Approvals for more information.
  1. You’ll be prompted to confirm the action on selected items. Double-check the summary of your action, then click the blue button in the lower-right corner of the popup to proceed with the action.
  • For emailing students, you’ll need to create and send the email via Handshake’s Targeted email tool Learn more about this process in Creating and Sending Targeted Emails.
  • For emailing contacts/creators, you’ll need to put a check next to the desired recipients, then confirm.
    • Here is an example of how the jobs will appear in your email template:
  • To bulk approve or decline jobs, refer to these instructions in Processing Job Posting Requests. Tip: If you have a group of postings that you would like to open for applications on a certain date, you can label those positions, then on the date that you would like them to be active, filter by your label name and bulk approve the postings.

Job Automatic Approval Configuration

In Handshake, all jobs posted to your school must be approved by career services before students can apply.

The Job Automatic Approval setting lets you automatically approve jobs that do not meet specific criteria you define, allowing your staff to focus on positions that require closer review.

For manual approval options, refer to Processing Job Posting Requests.

Before you begin

Before modifying Job Automatic Approval settings, confirm the following:

  • You have the Manage Job Automatic Approval permission on your account.
    • Any staff member with the Manage Staff permission can grant this. For more information, visit School Settings: Career Services Staff Roles and Permissions.
  • Job Automatic Approval settings do not override auto-approve permissions previously set for a specific employer.
    • If an employer is already configured to have their jobs automatically approved, your settings will not prevent their jobs from being auto-approved. For more information, review Employers and Jobs System Setup and Managing Employers.

Configure Job Automatic Approval settings

  1. In the left navigation panel, click Jobs.

  2. Click the white Auto-approval settings button in the upper-right corner of the Jobs page.

  3. In the modal, enable the Automatically approve jobs toggle to configure your settings.

Note: The criteria you configure in these settings represent exceptions to automatic approval. Jobs that meet any selected criteria will be withheld from auto-approval and will require manual review.

Available exception criteria include:

  • Job is posted by a new employer (employers with no previously approved jobs at your school)
  • Job is located at a residential address
  • Employer tag
  • Compensation
    • Job is unpaid
    • Job does not include exact amount (e.g. $50K/yr)
    • Job does not include range (e.g. $40-$60K/yr)
    • Note: If you select all three compensation options, any jobs where the employer opted out of sharing salary information will be sent to your school’s pending tab.
  • On-campus, Work-Study, and co-op jobs
  • Job type
  • Job duration
  • Employer industry
  • Employment type
  • Employer label
  • Work authorization requirements undisclosed or not required
  • School year
  • Degree level
  • Location type
  • States
    • Jobs located in states not listed will require manual approval; jobs located in listed states will be automatically approved
  • Jobs outside of the United States
  • Employer outside of the United States
  • Job role
  1. Click the black Apply Settings button to save your selections.
  • These criteria will apply to all future jobs posted to your school until you update them.
  • Any jobs currently in a pending state must be manually approved or declined.
  1. In the confirmation modal, click the black Confirm button to apply the changes to your institution.

Jobs that do not meet any of the criteria configured in these settings will now be automatically approved.

Filter for automatically approved jobs

To view jobs that were approved through Job Automatic Approval:

  1. In the left navigation panel, click Jobs.

  2. Click the Approved tab to view jobs your school has approved.

  3. Select the Jobs automatically approved filter from the All filters section. This filter displays all jobs that were automatically approved, whether through the Job Automatic Approval settings or through settings configured for individual employers.

For more information on the All filters option, refer to Job Postings Page Overview.

Job Details Page

The Job Details page provides information and actions you can take related to a specific job posting. You can make edits to the job information fields for jobs that are posted to your school only, so the posting best represents information that you’d like to get across to your students. We will explore the different aspects of the Job Details page in this article.

  • Lefthand Fields
    • Employer, Expiration, Applicants
    • Social Media
    • Label
    • Preview Link
    • Actions
    • Attachments
  • Center Fields
    • Approval status, Apply Start, and Expiration Date
    • Job information fields
      • Exceptions for schools
        • Federal Work Study
        • Hiring Team

  1. Select Jobs from the left navigation bar.

  2. Select either the Approved, In progress, Pending, Declined, or Expired tab.

  3. Select a job posting, and click on the job posting title in the sidebar. You will be directed to the job details page.

Lefthand Fields

This section will explain all of the fields and sections related to the left side of the page.

Employer, Expiration, Applicants:

  • Employer: The name of the Employer. Click this to be directed to the Employer’s page in Handshake

  • Expiration: The expiration date and time for the job posting

  • Applicants: The number of students that have applied to this job in Handshake Social Media:

  • Like or Share on Facebook, X, LinkedIn or via Email: Clicking one of the icons will open a new window to complete the process. Label:

Labels in this field are used for organization and management purposes. Adding a label here does not set qualifications that students need to meet in order to apply to this job. To set labels for qualification purposes, use the Additional Qualifications section of this page.

  • Select a Label: Choose a previously created label from the dropdown menu
  • Create New Label: Create a new label in the pop up box that appears. To learn more about creating labels, please refer to School Settings: Labels Preview Link:

This is a link to the job posting for any student that might not have a Handshake account or is not currently signed in. The student won’t be able to apply using this link, but they can access the general job posting information.

Actions:

  • Add an Applicant: Add an applicant to this job posting. Note: An applicant added this way might override the qualifications set for the job posting

  • View & Add Notes: View and Add Notes that can be accessible by other Career Services members from your school

  • Browse Applicants: Directs you to manage applicants on the job posting

  • Create Interview for this Job: Begins the process of creating an interview schedule. Learn more in the help center article Building an Interview Schedule in Handshake

  • Duplicate this Job: Create a copy of this job posting

  • Expire Posting Now: Only available on approved job postings that are posted to your school only. You must have permissions from the employer to manage their job postings. This will immediately expire the job posting.

  • Flag this Employer: Refer to Handshake’s Flagging System for more information about flagging employers Attachments:

  • New Attachment: Use the pop up box to attach a file to the job posting. Note: You can select the word Attachments to access all the attachments currently used for this posting and delete them if necessary.

Center Fields

This section will explain all of the fields and sections related to the center of the job posting page. In order to make changes to any of these fields, you will need to click the Edit button in the top right corner of the section.

Approval status:

The approval status can be updated by anyone at your school with the To learn about the Approval status field, please refer to the From the job posting’s overview page section of this article: Processing Job Posting Requests.

Apply Start and Expiration Dates:

The Apply Start and Expiration Dates will be listed. You can identify the information here, and scroll down to make changes to these dates under the Application Process section.

Note: The Apply Start Date and Expiration Date cannot have more than 365 days between them. Expiration dates can be updated if the job is posted to your school, and your school only.

Job information fields:

Job information fields pertain to specific information about the job posting. These fields can be editable by your school. You can select the Edit button with the pencil icon on the right of any section to make modifications to the job details. These edits will only be reflected at your school.

The following Employer article provides in-depth information about these fields. You can click on each of the headers up to Your Hiring Team for information about the fields: How to Post a Job.

Exceptions for schools:

Sometimes there are exceptions as to what schools can edit on jobs. This section will cover those topics.

Federal Work Study:

In some cases, you will be able to indicate whether a job is a Federal Work Study program or not. If you are unable to make this change, it is because the employer does not have permissions to post work study jobs at one or more schools that they posted the job to.

Hiring Team:

As a school, you can add or edit unlimited additional Hiring Team members. These can be contacts, they do not need to be users only. To learn more about the difference between contacts and users, please refer to Contacts vs. Users

Add applicants after the Expiration date:

You can add applicants after an expiration date for a job posting has passed. This ensures that students are given a fair opportunity to apply to job applications on Handshake in cases where they weren’t able to apply on time.

Job Postings Page Overview

The Job Postings page in Handshake highlights key information relevant to the job posting status to speed up your workflow. Statuses are broken down into tabs with search filters and table columns.

Topics:

  • Job Posting Status Tabs
  • Job Posting Side Sheet
  • Search Filters
    • All Filters
  • Create a Saved Search

Job Posting Status Tabs

Job postings are organized into five tabs based on possible statuses: Approved, In Progress, Pending, Declined, and Expired.

For increased posting review and processing speed, the default status tab is the Pending tab. However, if you are on another tab and leave the page, then come back later, the tab you were on will reload.

There are 50 Postings listed per page. Postings are displayed in a table with unique column headers per approval status to ensure the most high-impact information is readily available. For example, the count of saves is included on the Approved tab.

You can approve or decline postings from the table view in the Pending or In Progress tabs.

After approving 4 consecutive postings from the same company in the table view, Handshake will prompt you to enable auto-approve jobs for that employer. Intuitive Approvals may only be triggered from this table view (not from an individual posting itself).

For a breakdown of the approvals workflow, refer to Processing Job Posting Requests.

When you select at least one job posting from a non-Expired tab, bulk actions will appear in the column headers row. For more information, check out How to Use Bulk Actions on Jobs.

Individual Actions for a Job Posting

The Job Postings page will include actions for each individual job posting.

Note: The following example is taken from the Pending and In Progress tabs.

  • Approve job: Indicated by a checkmark. This action will approve the job instantly.
    • If the employer is a New Employer, you will be asked to set permissions for them. Learn more about this process in Processing Employer Approval Requests using Job Based Approvals.
  • Decline job: Indicated by a circle with a line through it. This action will decline the job instantly.
  • View job details: Indicated by an arrow exiting a box. This action will open Job details in a separate tab.
  • Additional actions: Indicated by the ellipsis. This action will provide a dropdown menu; depending on the status tab, you will be provided some of the following options
    • Set to “In progress”
    • Copy job preview link
    • Manage job labels
    • Manage employer labels
    • Email contacts or creators
    • Decline employer

Job Posting Side Sheet

The Job Posting Side Sheet allows you to access job posting and employer information all in one location without needing to navigate away from the postings list page. To open this side sheet, click on any job on the postings list page and the side sheet will appear on the left side of the screen.

The following information will be available for your review:

Job Posting

  • Job title

  • Location

    • Remote - This will only appear if the job is available for remote workers

  • The job post ID number

  • Additional actions: Select the 3 ellipsis button for more actions

    • View job details
    • Set to “In progress”
    • Add label to job
    • Remove label from job
    • Email to students
    • Email contacts or creators
    • Add to favorite jobs

  • Job description

  • Employment type and duration

  • Hiring team (contact)

  • Posted on date

  • Apply start - Expiration date

  • Candidate qualifications

  • Job roles Employer Information

  • Employer name

  • Employer location

  • Employer description

  • Employer industry

  • Employer size

  • Employer type

  • Website

  • Employer contact: phone number and email address

  • Account owner

  • Additional actions: Select the 3 ellipsis button for more actions

    • View employer profile
    • Add label to employer
    • Remove label from employer
    • Edit employer collections

  • Employer tags (if applicable, for more information on employer tags visit: Employer Tags)

Create a Saved Search

Handshake makes it easy to save search criteria so the search can be run again in the future. If you would like to setup a saved search, please review the Create a Saved Search article to enable and apply saved search filters. Once created, a new filter called My Saved Filters will appear below Save These Filters on the left column of the Jobs page.

Processing Job Posting Requests

Job postings must be approved in order to be discoverable by your students. Employers can request to post jobs to your institution in Handshake.

Note: If you’d like to approve an employer after they’ve posted a job to your institution, please refer to Processing Employer Approval Requests using Job Based Approvals

To review job posting requests pending at your institution, click Jobs from the left navigation bar, then click on the Pending tab.

Note: you can also access Pending jobs via the Home tab on the left navigation bar. Pending jobs will be displayed on the right side of the page under Job Postings.

  • Pending jobs from the Jobs tab reflects currently pending jobs.

  • Pending jobs from the Home tab reflects all pending jobs, which includes jobs employers posted that expire within the same day. So the result may be jobs pending and expired. Job posting requests can be processed in the following ways:

  • individually:

    • from the list of pending or in progress jobs
    • from the job posting’s overview page

  • in bulk from the list of pending or in progress jobs

  • automatically approved by the system

    • intuitively prompted
    • via Employer Permissions

  • Second Request postings

Process pending jobs individually

From the list of pending jobs

To approve an individual posting from the list of pending jobs, in the column to the far right titled “Actions” click Approve or Decline in the corresponding job’s row to approve or decline that posting.

Note: if you decline a job, you’ll be prompted for more information. For more info on this prompt, check out Using Job Decline Reasons!

From the job posting’s overview page
  1. From the list of jobs, click directly on the job title to open the job side sheet. From here, you can click the ellipsis in the top right corner and choose View job details to open the job overview page, which displays all of the posting details. Scroll down the page to review job posting information.
  • If you’d like more information from the employer prior to approving, we recommend to use the In Progress status and add a comment to the job to request the desired clarification. Type your comment in the text field, then click Add Comment to save.
  1. To process the posting, in the Status row, click the button for Approved, In Progress, or Declined, then click the Save or Save and View Next (to review the next pending posting).
  • Approved: Save will turn green and update to “Save Approved” or “Save Approved & View Next”
  • In Progress: the buttons will remain blue and read “Save” or “Save & View Next”
  • Declined: Save will turn red and update to “Save Declined” or “Save Declined & View Next”
    • Note: if you decline a job, you’ll be prompted for more information. For more info on this prompt, check out Using Job Decline Reasons!

Process pending jobs in bulk

  1. From the list of jobs, click to check the box to the immediate left of the job posting’s title––check as many as is desired, or click Select All in the column header row to select all listed postings.

  2. To process the postings, in the column header row, click:

  • Approve to make the posting live to students
    • Note: if the Apply Start date is in the future, the posting will be viewable to students, but they will not be able to apply till the specified start date. For the best experience, we recommend not approving jobs with an Apply Start date in the future and instead, leave them as “Pending” or “In Progress” till the specified date.
  • Decline to prevent the posting from being accessible to your students
    • Note: if you decline a job, you’ll be prompted for more information. For more info on this prompt, check out Using Job Decline Reasons!
  • The ellipsis button to select from more options:
    • Set to In Progress to indicate the posting is under review or consideration.
    • Tip: If you plan to approve at a later date, such as with the example for a future Apply Start date, you can also add a label to quickly identify the postings at that time!
    • Add label to job to add a label to the job.
    • Remove label from job to remove a label from the job.
    • Email contacts or creators to open a targeted email draft so that you can contact the owner of the job posting with questions.
  1. After approving, declining, or setting the job to in progress, the page will automatically refresh and save the changes.

Configure automatic job approvals

Best Practice: Start Small; allow auto-approval for only your most trusted employers at first which may include: Alumni, Employers that attended your career fair, Fortune 500, or local/recruiters you have worked with in the past.

Intuitive Approvals

When you’ve approved 4 consecutive job postings from the same company and click to approve the 5th, a notice will appear immediately after approval, asking if you want to enable auto-approval for the employer.

Click the option to Turn On Auto-Approval to enable automatic job approvals for future job posting requests.

A confirmation will pop-up in the lower-right corner of the screen indicating that job postings from that company will now be auto-approved.

Note: if there are any other pending jobs from that employer, those jobs still must be manually processed. Only job postings requested after auto-approval is turned on will be auto-approved.

Employer Permissions

When employer requests are being processed, after selecting the permission (role) “Post Jobs”, you can also select “Auto-Approve Jobs”. This will auto-approve all future job posting requests from this employer. For more information, review Processing Employer Approval Requests.

Likewise, you can setup default employer approval preferences as described in School Settings: Default Employer Approval Preferences.

Second request postings

Second request postings are postings that were previously declined, and the employer was allowed the employer to submit the job for reconsideration.

You can locate Second request postings by clicking on All filters and scrolling to the bottom of the side sheet. The filter will be titled Second requests and you can choose to Show only second requests.

Processing second requests is functionally the same as a new posting request, however, we recommend to process second requests individually, via the job’s overview page.

From the Pending list, click the Job Title to access the job details side sheet. Then click the ellipsis button and choose View job details.

On the Job Details page, scroll down to access the status and comments for this posting. The prior decline, decline reason, and actions taken by the employer are displayed in the comment experience.

You can update the posting status and comment as described in the section above, from the job posting’s overview page.

For more info on how to allow second requests, check out Using Job Decline Reasons!

Searching for Jobs in Handshake (Career Services)

In Handshake, jobs have two IDs that serve different purposes:

  • Job ID: Connected to the job itself, allowing it to be shared across Handshake.
  • Posting ID: Connects the job to a specific school. Your school approves a posting (posting ID) that is linked to the job (job ID).

Search for a job posting by ID

You can search for a job posting by ID using one of three methods:

  • Search for a job from the Jobs page
  • Global search
  • URL search Note: Enter the job ID number only. Including the # symbol will yield no results.
Search for a job from the Jobs page

  1. Click Jobs in the left navigation panel, then select the approval status tab that reflects the current status of the job: Pending, In Progress, Approved, Declined, or Expired.

  2. Type the job ID into the search bar.

Global search

  1. Type the job ID into the general search bar at the top of the page.

  2. Select the job from the results.

Note: Global search only returns active, approved job postings. Expired or pending jobs will not appear in the results.

URL search

If you know the job ID, you can enter it directly into the URL using the following format:

app.joinhandshake.com ID]

For example: app.joinhandshake.com

Using Job Decline Reasons

When processing job posting requests, if you choose to decline a posting, a popup appears to gather more information:

  • select a reason for the decline. These job decline reasons make it easier for employers to understand why their job was declined at a specific school.
    • The selection chosen will be added as a comment to the job’s comment history. Employers are able to review the decline reason and comment added.
  • choose to share your name with the employer.
  • choose to allow employers to initiate a second request for approval after being declined once. Note: Declining a job does not decline the employer. If you wish to decline the employer, please refer to Processing Employer Approval Requests using Job Based Approvals.

In the prompt that appears, check the appropriate box(es) that represent the reason for the decline; you may add comments in the text box if you’d like.

Check at least one of the boxes listed:

  • Pay structure
    • This job is being declined due to its pay structure
  • Job requires upfront cost
    • This job is being declined for requiring an upfront cost
  • Not aligned with my institution’s offerings
    • Note: We do not recommend declining jobs based on academic/degree fit. Handshake will only recommend this job to students who we think may be interested in it.
  • Employer is a third party recruiter or staffing agency
    • This job is being declined because it is from a third party recruiter or staffing agency
  • Location doesn’t make sense for my students
    • This job is an international position or its location does not make sense for my students
  • Job is located at a residential address
    • This job is located at a residential address, and your institution chooses not to approve jobs located at residential addresses
  • Job description needs more information (please explain below)
    • This job description requires more information
  • Other (please explain below)
    • This job is being declined for a reason other than those listed above Note: If the reason isn’t listed, check the last box, “Decline reason not listed”, and add the accurate reason in the text box: Please tell us more about this decision…
  • Share my name with employer (Yes / No)
    • If you select this option, your name will be displayed with the comment.
  • Would you like to invite this employer to submit this job for approval again after changes or discussion? (Yes / No)
    • If you select this option, employers will be able to submit the job for approval one more time, after describing the actions taken. Refer to Processing Job Posting Requests for details on second requests. If you’d like to review decline reasons for jobs, you may access the decline reason and comment via the specific job overview page–click the arrow to dropdown the comment box.

You can also report on these fields in Analytics via the Jobs template. We’ve added “decline_reasons” and “decline_comment” to the Postings section.

Keep in mind that any updates made “today” will be processed “tonight” and reflected in Analytics reporting “tomorrow”!

Kiosk Setup & Usage

Check-in Kiosk Hardware Recommendations

This resource includes our recommendations for hardware related to the Check-in Kiosk for standard check-ins and card swipe check-ins.

Topics:

  • Check-in Device
  • Card Reader

Check-in Device:

Any laptop or device that has USB output will work with Handshake; it should not matter what brand or type you use. Many of our schools use iPads, PCs, etc.

Note: while a check-in kiosk may be utilized on a tablet/iPad, name tag printing is only supported on a desktop/laptop, as specific software is required to be installed by Dymo.

For more information on name tag printing, refer to our Name Tag Printing Configuration Guide.

Card Reader:

Any USB card reader that has keyboard emulation will work with Handshake. The only required specs are that the device must:

  • Connect via USB

  • Use keyboard emulation

  • Output plain text to the keyboard

  • Contain the number you consider uniquely identifying a student and that number must be on the student’s “card_id” field in their student sync If your kiosk is using an iPad, you will need to also purchase:

  • Lightening to USB adapter We recommend the MagTek 21073062 Dynamag Magnesafe Triple Track Magnetic Stripe Swipe Reader - only because most of our schools use this reader and have success in setting it up!

Note: There is no software required for the card reader. For more information, refer to How to Enable Card Swipe Check In for Students.

Card Reader Types

There are two type of card readers that can be used:

  • Magnetic stripe reader

  • BarCode reader If you decide to use a BarCode reader, it must have:

  • Keyboard output

  • Student ID or unique identifier to be contained in the outputted string More information on BarCode readers can be found on the TALtech website.

Check out our Handshake User Community in order to see specific hardware recommendation from 500+ Career Services professionals!

How to Enable Card Swipe Check-in for Students

Card swipe check-in allows students to checkin for appointments, interviews, and in-person fairs and events using their student ID cards.

1. Acquire and set up a card reader.

The card reader must meet the specifications referenced in Check-in Kiosk Hardware Recommendations.

  • Once you have acquired a card reader, you’ll need to plug it in, open any program that accepts keyboard input (e.g., the Handshake check-in kiosk), and swipe a card. The card reader needs to be functioning normally in order to produce the data needed for our team to set up the kiosk.

2. Make sure your student sync file includes the card_id field.

This links their card ID to their profile and connects card swiping to each student. Ensure card ID has been uploaded in Importing Student Data.

  • Note: if you’re experiencing issues with the leading 0’s of card ID, check out Importer: Student Card IDs and Leading Zeros.
  1. Identify the output and exact input of the card swipe.

Along with the output you receive from the card reader, we will need to know which part of the input is actually the card id.

  • For example, a card reader could give us “;X2934010923-AD402020222A,” but the card id is only the “293401” portion of the input.
    • In some cases, the card reader may only give us the card id portion, so the full output may not be necessary.

4. Submit a kiosk setup request via this form.

After confirming your card reader works correctly, card_id is imported successfully to Handshake, and identifying the output and input, complete the linked form in this step.

This form generates a ticket for our Tech Support Team, who will be able to get this up and running for you. You’ll receive a confirmation once the setup is complete.

Kiosks: Launch a Kiosk for One Session of a Career Fair

In order to make it easy to track attendance for each session of your career fair we have added kiosks per session. Follow the instructions below to launch a kiosk for a particular session of a career fair.

Note: Kiosks will not be available for virtual fairs; when students launch a session, Handshake will record that as a check-in for reporting purposes.

  • Open the career fair

    • Make sure this fair has multiple sessions

  • Click Open Check-In Kiosk from the Actions section on the left side of the screen

  • De-select Allow All Sessions

  • Note: If you don’t check the Keep me logged in box and you have other tabs open, it may effect your cookies and cause your kiosk session to log out unexpectedly. For the best experience, ensure that other tabs are closed before proceeding.

  • Select the session that you would like to open the kiosk for

  • Note: You can still open the kiosk for all sessions which will ask students to select the session they are there for

  • Click Launch Kiosk in the bottom right corner of the window What does the kiosk look like if I launch it for all sessions?

  • Students will be asked to pick the session that they are checking in for, in the example below the career fair had two sessions

Launch a Check-in Kiosk

Handshake provides a convenient link per feature to launch the applicable Check-in Kiosk. The kiosk can be launched as a general kiosk directly from the Appointments and Events overview page, or from the specific Career Fair or Interview Schedule.

Once the kiosk is open, students check in via one of the methods below:

  • entering their username or email address
  • swiping their card
    • Note: if your institution hasn’t enabled card swipe and is interested, check out How to Enable Card Swipe Check-in for Students. To learn more about Check-in Kiosks, refer to An Overview of Check-in Kiosks.

Note: kiosks are not available for virtual fairs; when students launch a session, this will be recorded as a checkin for reporting purposes.

Topics:

  • Launch a General Check-in Kiosk
  • Launch a Check-in Kiosk for a specific:
    • Career Fair
    • Event
    • Interview Schedule
  • Test a student check-in

Launch a General Check-in Kiosk

  1. From the device you’re using as a kiosk, login to Handshake.

  2. Click either Events or Appointments on the left navigation bar (both will open a general Check-in Kiosk).

  3. Click the Check-in Kiosk tab in the upper-right corner of the page. This tab is in the same location from both Events and Appointments.

  4. From the popup that appears on the screen, select from the following settings, then click Launch Kiosk:

  • Choose an Office Location (dropdown menu)
    • Note: If an office location is not selected, appointments across all locations will become available.
  • Choose a Career Center (dropdown menu)
  • Keep me logged in (checkbox)
    • Note: It is strongly recommended that you do not stay logged in, because doing so will allow anyone using the Kiosk full access to your account.
  • Allow Drop-In Appointments (checkbox)
    • If checked, appointments marked as drop-in will display when students check in.
  • Appointment-Only Kiosk (checkbox)
    • If checked, students will only be able to check into appointments through this kiosk.

Launch a Check-in Kiosk for a specific Career Fair

  1. From the device you’re using as a kiosk, login to Handshake.

  2. Click Fairs on the left navigation bar, then click the name of the relevant fair.

  3. Click the Open Check-In Kiosk button, under Actions on the left of the page.

  4. From the popup that appears on the screen, select from the following options, then click Launch Kiosk:

  • Allow All Sessions (checkbox)
  • Keep me logged in (checkbox)
    • If unchecked, your account will be put into a limited access mode when the kiosk is launched to prevent unintended access to your account.
    • If you’d like to keep your account in full access mode, you may choose the Keep me logged in option. Keep in mind that anyone using the kiosk will have full access to Handshake via your account if you remain logged in.

Launch a Check-in Kiosk for a specific Event

  1. From the device you’re using as a kiosk, login to Handshake.

  2. Click Events on the left navigation bar, then click the name of the relevant event.

  3. Click the Open Check-In Kiosk button, under Actions on the left of the page.

  4. In the popup that appears, choose where to stay logged in or not, then click Launch Kiosk:

  • Keep me logged in (checkbox)
    • If unchecked, your account will be put into a limited access mode when the kiosk is launched to prevent unintended access to your account.
    • If you’d like to keep your account in full access mode, you may choose the Keep me logged in option. Keep in mind that anyone using the kiosk will have full access to Handshake via your account if you remain logged in. Note: if an event is invite only, students will still be able to check into the event via the Kiosk. They’ll receive the following message after they’ve checked in — “You have successfully checked in but there are additional steps needed. Please speak with the event organizer. You were not invited to this event.”

Launch a Check-in Kiosk for a specific Interview Schedule

  1. From the device you’re using as a kiosk, login to Handshake.

  2. Click Interviews on the left navigation bar, then click the name of the interview schedule from the list.

  3. Click the Open Check-In Kiosk button, under Actions on the left of the page.

  4. In the popup that appears, choose where to stay logged in or not, then click Launch Kiosk:

  • Keep me logged in (checkbox)
    • If unchecked, your account will be put into a limited access mode when the kiosk is launched to prevent unintended access to your account.
    • If you’d like to keep your account in full access mode, you may choose the Keep me logged in option. Keep in mind that anyone using the kiosk will have full access to Handshake via your account if you remain logged in.

Test a student check-in

  1. Launch either a general Check-in Kiosk, or a Check-in Kiosk for a specific career fair or interview schedule.

  2. Enter a test student email or swipe a student ID card to check-in (if your institution has enabled card swipe), then click Go.

  3. Once checked in, a green popup notification will appear in the lower-right corner of the page, which states “You have successfully checked in!”.

Confirm the check-in

To confirm the student check-in went through successfully for an in-person fair or event:

Events:

  1. From the event overview page, click the Attendees tab in the upper-right corner of the page.

  2. All registered and checked-in students will show on the left side of the page. Ensure that the test student used to confirm the Check-in Kiosk is marked as checked-in.

  3. If you’d like to remove attendees to preserve accurate reporting, follow the steps in Removing Event and Fair Attendees.

Fair:

  1. From the fair overview page, locate the Students section at the upper-middle of the page, and click View Registered Students.

  2. Click the fair session link from the popup that appears on the screen.

  3. All registered and checked-in students will be listed on the left of the page. Ensure that the test student used to confirm the Check-in Kiosk is marked as checked-in.

Note: If you’d like to remove attendees to preserve accurate reporting, follow the steps in Removing Event and Fair Attendees.

Name Tag Printing Configuration Guide

Check-in kiosks with name tag printing can be used for in-person career fairs and events setup in Handshake. This guide will take you through the necessary steps to set up name tag printing.

1. Acquire a name tag printer and install the software as described in Name Tag Printing System Requirements.

Install the software on the computer you’ll be using for name tag printing with this specific printer.

  • Note: only one DYMO LabelWriter printer should be added to local printers in the settings. Make sure to remove others that won’t be used. Using more than one name tag printer? Make sure to track which printers are set up per computer. The printer connected at the time of software installation will also need to be connected to that same computer the day of the event or fair.

2. Configure the name tag printing XML.

The XML is the method of formatting the name tag information, such as name, major, etc, according to your label size. For the steps to customize your own XML, refer to Name Tag XML Formatting.

3. Add your Dymo XML to the in-person fair or event in Handshake.

Make sure name tag printing is enabled on the event or fair, then paste in the XML and save your changes.

Name tags will not print if:

  • the XML is saved in the event or fair, but name tag printing isn’t enabled (box isn’t checked)
  • name tag printing is enabled, but the XML isn’t saved in the text box For specific steps, check out Name Tag XML Formatting.

After configuring name tag printing, test your setup! Check out our recommendations in Testing Name Tag Printing.

Name Tag Printing System Requirements

Name tag printing is supported for in-person fairs and events in Handshake, with the following requirements for hardware, software, and settings.

Check-in Device

Name tag printing via Handshake’s check-in kiosk requires a desktop/laptop computer with the printer connected via USB, as Dymo requires specific software be installed on the computer.

The desktop/laptop must use a Windows or MacOS operating system for the DYMO software installation. Other operating systems like ChromeOS (Chromebooks), Linux] aren’t supported.

The printer connected to the computer at the time of software installation will need to be connected to that same computer the day of the event or fair.

Tip: if you will be using multiple computers for name tag printing, make sure to track/map which printers are set up per computer!

While the check-in kiosk is usable on tablets/iPads, name tag printing will not function.

Name Tag Printer

Handshake supports either a Dymo 450, Dymo 450 Turbo, Dymo 550, Dymo 550 Turbo or Dymo® LabelWriter® Wireless printer. If you do not already have one of these supported printers, explore this link (a third-party site) to review those options.

Note: only a Dymo 450, Dymo 450 Turbo, Dymo 550, Dymo 550 Turbo, or Dymo® LabelWriter® Wireless printer are supported by Handshake. Other printers will not work when printing name tags through Handshake.

If you plan to use a Dymo® LabelWriter® Wireless Printer, we recommend having your IT team help you set it up. This requires connection with your Wi-FI network, you’ll want to make sure it’s properly connected and working before the fair or event!

Corresponding Dymo Label Software

Once you have acquired one of the supported printers, you will need to download and install the Dymo software that corresponds with your printer.

  1. Refer to the Dymo Compatibility Chart for the correct software download.

  2. Scroll down to the All Software Versions table, then select the most recent version of DYMO Label Software or Connect.

Note: If using LabelWriter 550, the most recent version of DYMO Connect is required (v1.4.3). LabelWriter 550 isn’t compatible with DYMO Label Software.

  1. When installing the software, keep the printer unplugged from the computer. The instructions will tell you exactly when to connect it!

Additional considerations:

  • If you’re currently using DYMO Label Software on a 450 or 450 Turbo, and you’d like to upgrade to DYMO Connect, you’ll need to fully uninstall DYMO Label Service and its corresponding web service before reinstalling the software.
  • Only one DYMO LabelWriter printer should be added to local printers in the settings. Make sure to remove others that won’t be used.
  • When installing 550 on a Mac, a terminal window will pop up and ask for your Password to be input — this is the password for your user login to your computer. This is necessary for the web service to be trusted. You may also need to enable the extension via security settings.
  • If DYMO Connect isn’t installing on a Mac, confirm that the web service is connected. Click the DYMO.WebApi icon in the top navigation bar, then click Diagnose. The DYMO Connect service will begin running.
    • If you receive an error connecting, click Reset.
    • If you receive a trust certificate error, make sure ‘Always Trust’ is selected for each of the Trust settings. To check, locate your Keychain Access, then double-click Localhost. After installing the software, learn about Name Tag XML Formatting.

Name Tag XML Formatting

Handshake’s name tag printing uses XML (short for Extensible Markup Language) to transport data from student profiles via our check-in kiosk, then format that information on their printed name tag.

As XML relies on customization, you’ll need to ensure the XML you use meets your needs, is compatible with the student profile fields, and is formatted according to the name tag label size you’ll be using.

You can create your own custom XML, or we have some preconfigured XML that we know works well, if you’d prefer to use that to start with (or test with)!

Note: DYMO Connect is now supported for 450, 450 Turbo, and 550 printers! However, any XML created within Dymo Connect will not be compatible, instead you can use one of the examples below. If you are using the original DYMO Label Software, you can continue using it or upgrade to the most recent version. For additional details, refer to Name Tag Printing System Requirements.

Topics:

  • Supported fields for name tags
  • Format name tag XML
  • Add XML to an event or fair
  • Example XMLs
    • Label size 1 1/8 x 3 1/2
    • Label size 2 1/4 x 4

Supported fields for name tags

Handshake supports the following fields from the student profile for name tags:

  • FirstName
    • The FirstName field will pull the student’s preferred name if they have one associated with their account.
  • LastName
  • Name
  • Major
  • GradDate
  • MajorGradDate The fields Major, GradDate, and MajorGradDate all pull data from the student’s Education section on their profile. If your institution imports student data, this information should be included in the import.

When printing name tags, if any of this information is missing or inaccurate, we recommend to first double-check the student profile to ensure it’s reflected correctly in Handshake.

Format name tag XML

To customize your XML, open the Dymo software on your computer and follow the steps below.

Note: At this time, only the Dymo Label Writer has the options listed below for customization. If you have Dymo Connect instead, we recommend using one of the below examples and editing the Font Family and Alignment sections directly to adjust the label formatting.

  1. You will need to format your label based on the size of your label and the fields you would like to include. To do this, create a text box on your label as shown in the example below:

  2. Double click on the text box and select the Advanced tab.

  3. In the Reference Name text field, add one of the following supported fields:

  • FirstName
  • LastName
  • Name
  • Major
  • GradDate
  • MajorGradDate
  1. Repeat steps 1-3 until your label is formatted with the information that you would like, then save your label format in a .label file, as you will need this when you add label printing to your event or fair.

You will need to open the .label file with a text editor in order to copy the XML code for Handshake.

Add XML to an event or fair

  1. Navigate to the fair or event in Handshake, then click the Edit tab in the upper-right corner of the page.

  2. Scroll to the bottom of the page and ensure Name tag printing is checked, then paste the XML in the text box below, Name tag label XML.

    • Tip: expand the Name tag label XML text box by clicking, holding, and dragging downward in the lower-right corner of the box, on the diagonal lines.

  3. Make sure to save your updates after pasting!
