Creating and Managing Templates

Leverage templates to craft your outreach messages and share messaging best practices across teams.

Learn more about Using Templates in Messages.

Topics:

  • Access templates
  • Template search filters
  • Create a template
  • Edit template
  • Duplicate template
  • Archive template
  • Restore an archived template

Access templates

Click on your name in the upper-right corner of the page, then select Templates from the dropdown.

Template search filters

You can filter templates by the following criteria:

  • Keyword search
    • Search template by name
  • Created by
    • Created by anyone
    • Created by you
  • Status
    • Active
    • Archived
  • Sort by
    • Sort by newest
    • Sort by oldest
    • Sort by last update
    • Sort alphabetical

Create a template

On the Templates page, click the Create button to the far right of the page to create a new message template.

In the pop-up modal, enter the following details:

  • Template name (maximum 50 characters)
  • Subject line (optional)
  • Message When you’re finished, click the Save button in the bottom-right corner.

Once saved, the message “Template created successfully” displays in the lower-right corner of the page.

At this time, you cannot star commonly used templates. However, we recommend prefixing them with [Evergreen] or wording of your choice to make them easily searchable.

Edit template

Select the message you want to edit, then click the Edit button to the far right of the template message name.

Edit the message and the subject line as needed, then click the Save button in the upper-right corner.

Once saved, the message “Template updated successfully” displays in the lower-right corner of the page.

Duplicate template

Select the message you want to duplicate, then click the duplicate icon (two overlapping squares) to the far right.

In the pop-up modal, enter the following details:

  • Template name (maximum 50 characters)
    • The template name will contain “Copy [name of original template]
    • Edit the name as needed.
  • Subject line (optional)
  • Message When you’re finished, click the black Save button in the bottom-right corner.

Once saved, the message “Template created successfully” displays in the lower-right corner of the page.

Archive template

Select the template you want to archive, then click the bin icon to the far right of the page.

  • Templates cannot be deleted.
  • The company profile owner or admin can archive templates created by teammates. Once archived, the message “Template archived successfully” displays in the lower-right corner of the page.

Restore an archived template

In the Status filter, select Archived. Then, select the message you want to restore and click the Restore button.

Once the message is restored, the message “Template restored successfully. You can now view it as an active template.” displays in the lower-right corner of the page.

How Do I Access My Messages?

On Handshake, you can access your sent, archived, and received messages in just a few simple steps.

  1. To begin, click on the chat bubble icon in the upper-right corner of the screen to access your messages. The number displayed on the icon represents the number of unread messages since your last visit.

  2. From the inbox toolbar, click on the respective button for the folder you want to view messages for.

Note: all messages are sorted by the timestamp of the last message received. The newest will be displayed at the top and the oldest at the bottom.

  • Inbox: contains all the new and received messages that have not been moved to another folder.
  • Sent: contains all the messages sent.
  • Archive: contains messages that you have removed from your main folder.
  • Unread: contains messages that have not yet been read.
  • Starred: contains messages that have been starred.
  1. To search for messages associated with a campaign, or to filter messages by the school a student attends, click Campaign or School respectively.

Tip: to easily find a message within any folder, enter any identifying information into the search bar, such as the sender’s name.

  1. From any folder, select a conversation to read the message in its entirety and take action.

The side sheet on the right of the message will provide direct access to a student’s profile if it’s visible in Handshake. Click the white button View profile to view the student’s complete profile in a new tab.

Learn more about How to Reply to Handshake Messages via Your Email Client.

How to Reply to Handshake Messages via Your Email Client

Employers can reply directly to student messages from their email client without logging into Handshake.

Key details

  • This feature is available for all messages and role types.
  • Responses sent via email will be automatically stored in your Handshake inbox within 5 minutes.
  • Signatures are included, but certain elements are not supported (details below).

Replying to messages

When a student messages you, an email notification is sent to your registered email address.

  • Open the notification email.
  • Click the red button View the Message and Reply in the email.
  • Compose and send your response from your email client. Note: If you reply via email, your email address remains hidden from the student.

Unsupported features (when replying)

The following items are not supported:

  • Hyperlinks: URLs can be included but will not be formatted as clickable links.
  • Handshake templates: Templates cannot be used when replying by email.
  • Automated replies: Out-of-office or other automated replies are not supported.
  • CC’ing additional users: You cannot CC others on your email reply.
  • Attachments or images: These cannot be added to email replies.
  • Generating new messages: This feature is for responding only.

Notification email

The notification email will read:

From: “Handshake handshake@notifications.joinhandshake.com”

Subject: You have a new notification

Body:

Hello YOUR NAME,

You have a new message from STUDENT NAME.

Student’s full message displayed

View the Message and Reply (RED BUTTON)

You can also reply directly from this email

Respond to this message by simply replying to this email any time within 6 months of receiving it.

Note: Candidates will receive a plain text version of your response. For security purposes any images, links, fonts, and other such formatting will be removed.

Thank you,

The Handshake Team”

Note: If you reply via email, your email address won’t be visible to the student.

Enable message notifications

To receive student messages in your email client, ensure that new message notifications are enabled in your Handshake account. Learn more about Default Notification Preferences (Employers).

  1. Click on your name in the upper-right corner of the page.

  2. Select User settings, then click Notification Preferences.

  3. Scroll down to the Messages section and confirm that “I am sent a new message” is checked.

How to Send a Student a Message

Employers can message students on Handshake when certain recruiting requirements are met.

Where you can send a message, and whether you’re eligible to, depends on your account type and the part of Handshake you’re using.

Where can employers send messages to students?

  • Source candidates tab
    • Message students who appear in the Source candidates tab of a job posting. Learn more in How to Source Candidates.
  • Candidates tab
    • Message students directly from the Candidates tab of an event or fair page after they RSVP. Read more about Messaging Event and Fair RSVPs.
  • Talent page
    • View and message students from the Talent page or directly from their profile. Read A Guide to Talent List.

What are the messaging requirements for partner schools?

  • Basic and Pro employers must have at least one approved or closed job posting at the school where the student attends. Learn more in Understanding Job Posting Approvals.
  • Essentials and Enterprise employers can message students at partner schools without posting a job.

What are the messaging requirements for Handshake Open?

  • Basic and Pro employers must have at least one approved or closed job posting at any partner school to connect with students and alumni in the Open Network. Learn How to Connect with Handshake Open Network.
  • Essentials and Enterprise employers can message students in the Open Network without posting a job.

What other requirements apply before messaging a student?

  • If no job posting exists, the school must proactively approve the company.
  • The student must have an activated profile with visibility set to Community or Employers. Profiles set to Private cannot be messaged.
  • Employers must stay within their account’s message limits. Learn more about your Message Limits in Handshake.

Managing your Inbox

On Handshake, you can easily mark messages as unread, archive messages, and star conversations, and more. With these easy actions, you can save time and help keep your inbox organized.

Features available only to Premium partners are indicated by an asterisk (*). For more information, please check out this resource.

Manage your messages

By managing your messages individually, you can keep your inbox organized and access the information you need.

To begin, navigate to your inbox. For guidance, refer to How Do I Access My Messages?.

Inbox folders

Your inbox contains the following folders, including your main folder:

  • Sent: contains all messages you’ve sent, excluding campaign messages, if you are a Premium partner.
    • Note: student replies to campaigns can be accessed within your inbox.
  • Archive: contains messages that you’ve removed from your main folder.

Actions you can take

Apply and remove labels

To search for unread or starred messages in any folder, you can apply the following labels:

  • Unread
    • Note: unread messages can also be identified in bold text.
  • Starred

Apply the label Unread

To apply the label Unread, check the box to the left of each message you want to add the label to, or check the box in the upper-left corner of the page to select all messages, then click the white button Mark as unread.

Tip: to revisit your inbox with specific labels applied, click the star icon on the right side of the address bar, then bookmark the page. The page URL will include the name of the labels applied, and can be accessed after logging in.

Apply the label Starred

To apply the label Starred, click the star icon to the left of the student’s name for each message you want to star.

Labels applied

When a label(s) is applied, the button is highlighted in blue, and it will filter your inbox to show only messages that match the label(s).

Removing labels

To remove a label(s), simply click on the respective button. When the label is successfully removed, the button will be highlighted in white, and your inbox will once again display all messages.

Star a message

Star conversations in your inbox to help you quickly identify important conversations that need your attention.

  1. Click the star icon to the left of each message you want to star, or check the gray box in the header to select all messages, then click the white button Star.

  2. The message(s) will move immediately to your Starred folder and remain accessible from your main folder as well.

Unstar a message

  1. Locate the message in either your main or Starred folder.

  2. Click on the star icon. The message will be removed from your Starred folder and will remain in your main folder.

Mark a message as unread or read

Mark a message as unread or read so that you can easily return to them later when you have time to respond.

Mark a message(s) as unread

From main inbox

Check the box to the left of each message you want to mark as unread, or check the gray box in the header to select all messages, then click the white button Mark unread.

From within message

Click the white button Mark unread, located in the upper-right corner of the message.

The message(s) will be marked as unread and will remain in your main folder.

Mark a message(s) as read

Check the box to the left of each message you want to mark as read, or check the gray box in the header to select all messages, then click the white button Mark read.

Archive a message

From main inbox

  1. Check the box to the left of each message you want to archive, or check the box, located to the left of Inbox to select all messages, then click the white button Archive.

From within message

  1. Click the white button Archive, located in the upper-right corner of the message.

The message will move immediately to the Archived folder, where it will be stored for future reference, if needed.

Unarchive a message

  1. Navigate to your Archive folder, then click on the relevant message you want to unarchive.

  2. Click on the white button Unarchive, located in the upper-right corner of the message.

The message will move immediately to your main folder, where it will be stored indefinitely.

Note: messages cannot be deleted. They can only be archived.

*Filter by campaign

Premium partners can filter their inbox to view replies by individual or multiple campaigns sent.

Note: the campaign filter is only visible to users who can send campaign messages and have sent 1 or more campaigns.

To view student replies to a specific campaign sent, click the Campaign button, then select the campaign(s) from the dropdown. The campaign filter displays both completed and in-progress campaigns.

Once the campaign is selected, click the blue button Done in the lower-right corner of the dropdown.

If a campaign filter is applied with no replies, the message “Student replies to your messages and campaigns will show up here” displays.

Filter by school

All employers can filter their inbox to show messages from students at selected school(s), so they can prioritize and focus their time, making it easier to engage with students.

To view replies by students from a specific school, click the School button, then select the school(s) from the dropdown.

Note: schools are sorted by alphabetical order.

Once the school(s) is selected, click the blue button Done in the lower-right corner of the dropdown.

Explore our Messaging Best Practices.

Messaging Best Practices

To message students and alumni effectively on Handshake, use a personalized, strategic approach.

Steps to write an effective message

  1. Write a strong subject line

The subject line appears in the candidate’s email, Handshake inbox, and mobile notification, so it has a major effect on open rates. Include your company name for higher engagement.

The default subject line format, “[Recruiter name] at [Company] has sent you a message on Handshake,” performs well. Customizing the subject line with your brand voice can improve open rates further, especially when it includes a clear action word like “apply.” Keep subject lines between 80 and 110 characters.

  1. Personalize the message

Open with a line that shows why you are reaching out to this specific student, such as referencing their major or a relevant skill. Personalized openers increase response rates. Sign off with a real name rather than a generic company address. Candidates respond better to a message from an individual recruiter than from a company account.

  1. Make the call to action clear

Make the call to action stand out using bold text, underline, or color, and hyperlink it directly. Phrases like “Apply to this job” or “RSVP to this event” work well. Include an application deadline or event date to create urgency. Direct candidates to apply through Handshake so their engagement can be tracked.

  1. Link to your brand

Link to your Handshake Brand Page or a marketing video in your message so candidates can learn more about your company culture before applying. This gives candidates a reason to research your company further.

Additional resources

  • Learn How to write a recruiting message to students (plus 7 templates).
  • Uncover the 4 steps to a winning message that engages college talent.
  • Discover the 8 dos and don’ts of messaging underrepresented students.

Messaging Candidates without Handshake Profiles

Essentials and Enterprise employers can message students who do not have a Handshake account after they register as a guest for a publicly shared event.

Premium features are for Handshake Premium accounts only. For more information, please check out this resource.

How do I identify a candidate without a Handshake profile?

Candidates without a Handshake profile, sometimes called guest registrants or candidates without an account, are marked with a human icon showing an X and the text “No Handshake profile” below their name.

To view only these candidates:

  • Click Filters above the candidate list. A sidebar opens with additional filter options.
  • In the Handshake profile section of the sidebar, check the No profile box.
  • Click Apply.

How do I message a candidate without a Handshake profile?

To send a candidate without a Handshake profile a message, refer to Messaging Event and Fair RSVPs.

A candidate without a Handshake profile receives your message at the email address they used to register for the event.

Can a candidate without a Handshake profile reply to my message?

Not through Handshake. However, you can allow candidates without Handshake profiles to reply directly to your employee email addresses.

Turn this on in Company Settings under Global Settings. For instructions, refer to Company Settings: Global Settings.

Receiving Messages from Students in Handshake

Students can message you in Handshake either by replying to a message you sent them or by initiating contact when certain conditions are met.

How students can message employers

Students can initiate a message to an employer when any of the following apply:

  • You have already sent them a message
  • You appear in the People section of your company’s Brand page
  • You hosted a 1:1 session with them
  • You were introduced as a teammate in a message
  • You are attached to a campaign as a point of contact or Advocate

Manage who appears on your Brand Page

Owners and admins can control which teammates appear in the People section. Learn more about Customizing your Brand Page.

Note: This feature is available to customers on Essentials and Enterprise plans.

Reduce unexpected messages from students

To limit student-initiated contact for a specific teammate, avoid the following:

  • Messaging students
  • Hosting a 1:1 session unless direct follow-up is expected
  • Introducing a teammate in a message unless they should be contactable
  • Attaching a teammate to a campaign as a point of contact or Advocate unless they should receive student outreach
  • Leaving the Brand page People section on automatic fill if tighter control over visibility is needed.

Using Suggested Responses in Your Inbox

Suggested responses in your inbox help you reply faster to candidates who respond to Automated Outreach messages, which Handshake sends automatically based on criteria you set for a job posting.

Who can use suggested responses?

  • Suggested responses are available to all employers using Automated Outreach, except on-campus employers.
  • Suggested responses only apply to replies to Automated Outreach messages.

How do I review a suggested response?

Handshake may draft a response based on the associated job posting, but it does not send anything automatically. You review the draft first.

  1. Open your Inbox.

  2. Find a conversation labeled Suggested response.

Tip: Use the Automated Outreach filter to narrow your inbox and locate these conversations faster.

  1. Open the conversation.

  2. Read the suggested response.

  3. Choose one action:

  • Accept to send the response as written.
  • Edit to open a textbox where you can revise the wording, then click Send when ready.
  • Reject to dismiss the suggestion.

Why doesn’t every conversation have a suggested response?

Handshake does not generate a suggestion for every candidate reply. A suggestion may be withheld when:

  • The reply does not require an answer.
  • The reply requires information Handshake cannot access.
  • The reply involves a safety concern.
  • The job posting does not contain enough detail to answer reliably.

Using Templates in Messages

Message templates in Handshake help your team communicate efficiently and keep outreach consistent.

Use templates when composing individual messages, bulk messages, or campaign messages to save time and apply pre-approved messaging created by yourself or your teammates

To create and manage your message templates, refer to Creating and Managing Templates.

Insert a template

  1. In the message composer, click the three dots (more options) icon at the bottom of the message box.

  2. From the menu, click Templates.

  3. Click the button that matches where you’re sending the message:

  • Individual or bulk messages: click Use template.
  • Campaigns (job, event, fair, or other): click Choose template.
  1. In the Use template pop-up, select the Your templates or Team templates tab, then select the template you want to use.

Tip: Enter the template’s name in the search box to locate it quickly.

  1. The message preview appears on the right. Click the black Apply button.

  2. Once applied, the template will appear in the message box. Review and refine your message before sending.

Why can’t I message students?

If you’re not able to message students in Handshake, it’s most likely due to your current recruiting activity status at schools you’re connected with.

Partner Schools

To proactively message students, Basic and Handshake Plus employers must have at least one approved or closed job posting at the student’s current or former school.

  • For additional details, refer to How to Send a Student a Message. Handshake Open

To connect with students and alumni in the Open Network, Basic and Handshake Plus employers must have at least one approved or closed job posting at any partner school on Handshake.

  • Learn How to Connect with Handshake Open Network. Note: Premium partners can send messages to students without creating a job posting. Premium features are for Handshake Premium accounts only. For more information, please check out this resource!

Additional resources

  • You can message applicants on your postings, regardless of your recruiting activity. For more information, refer to Messaging Applicants.
  • If you’re receiving a message that says “Message limit reached”, refer to Why does Handshake say “message limit reached”?.

Why does Handshake say “message limit reached”?

In Handshake, Message limit reached displays when you’ve met your company’s set messaging limit.

Message limits are set based on recruiting seasons and message types, as well as your company’s partnership status with Handshake. For more details, refer to Messaging Limits in Handshake.

Messages & Campaigns

AI-Assisted Direct Messaging

AI-Assisted Direct Messaging helps you connect with top candidates faster by generating personalized draft messages for 1:1 outreach.

Whether you’re inviting a student to apply for a job or encouraging an applicant to interview, the AI creates a tailored draft based on the candidate’s resume, Handshake profile, and your job description.

AI-Assisted Direct Messaging is available to Pro, Essentials, and Enterprise (formerly TES) customers. For more information, please check out this resource!

This tool does not influence employment decisions. The AI-generated message is always optional — messages are never sent automatically.

Using AI-assisted direct messaging

To access AI message drafts, you must send a message from the Matches or Applicants tabs of an active job. AI-generated drafts are only available when messaging one candidate at a time.

Note: If you select multiple candidates, the AI draft will not appear.

To compose a message using AI:

  1. Navigate to the job posting you want to send messages for.

  2. Click either the Matches or Applicants tab.

  3. Click to send a candidate a message. The message composer will open with an AI-suggested message pre-filled.

The AI-generated message is based on:

  • The candidate’s Handshake profile
  • Your job description, including requirements and qualifications Note: Candidates will not be notified that AI was used.

Customizing the AI-suggested message

You have full control over the message before sending. Use the options below to tailor the message to your needs.

Edit and format the message

Use the toolbar at the bottom of the message composer to edit and format your message before sending.

  • Rewrite message: Generate a new AI-suggested draft. You can rewrite the message up to 99 times per job match or candidate.
  • Text formatting (Aa): Opens a formatting toolbar where you can apply Bold, Italic, or Underline to selected text, or add a list.

Message Limits in Handshake

To promote more meaningful, intentional interactions with students, Handshake enforces limits on employer messaging.

What types of message limits does Handshake have?

There are two types of limits:

  • Time-based limits
  • Per-send limits These limits apply to all employer messages. The exact thresholds vary by account type. For Essentials and Enterprise (formerly TES) customers, limits are further based on the partnership your company has with Handshake.

What is a time-based limit?

A time-based limit is the number of messages allocated within a single monthly period. This limit is shared collectively by all teammates connected to your company profile and applies to all message types, including individual messages, bulk messages, and campaigns.

You can use your organization’s messages all at once or spread throughout the month.

What is a per-send limit?

A per-send limit is the number of recipients you can select for a single bulk message or campaign.

  • Bulk messages
    • Basic accounts are limited to 10 messages per month total, so that monthly limit applies instead of a per-send limit.
    • Essentials and Enterprise (formerly TES) customers can send bulk messages to up to 500 recipients at a time.
  • Campaigns
    • Only Essentials and Enterprise (formerly TES) customers can send campaigns. All campaigns can reach a maximum audience of 5,000 recipients.

What are the messaging limits by plan?

Messaging limits vary by both your package and role type. All message limits refresh on the 1st of the month at midnight PST.

Basic (free)

Limit: 10 messages per month, shared across all users in the account.

Plus

Limit: 10 messages per month, shared across all users in the account.

Pro

Limit: 200 messages per month, shared across all users in the account.

Essentials

Premium (paid) roles: Owner, Admin, Recruiter-Sourcer, Recruiter-Advanced, Advocate

  • 200 messages per month per premium seat (not shared)

  • 1 campaign per month (refreshes monthly)

  • Campaign reach: up to 5,000 candidates Basic (unpaid) roles: Representative, Recruiter-Standard

  • 25 messages per month shared across the employer account To upgrade Basic (unpaid) users for full messaging access, contact your account team.

Enterprise (formerly TES)

Premium (paid) roles: Owner, Admin, Recruiter-Sourcer, Recruiter-Advanced, Advocate

  • Message limits vary by plan and are customized to your organization’s hiring needs. Basic (unpaid) roles: Representative, Recruiter-Standard

  • 25 messages per month shared across the employer account To upgrade Basic (unpaid) users for full messaging access, please contact your account team.

What counts toward my message limit?

The following message types count toward your monthly limit:

  • Campaign messages
  • Campaign follow-up messages.
  • A message sent to a student from their student profile page.
  • A direct message sent from the employer inbox.
  • A single or multi-recipient message sent from the Talent list.
  • A single or multi-recipient message sent from the Source candidates list.

What does not count toward my message limit?

Messages do not count toward your limit if the student:

  • Applied to one of your job postings, has a scheduled interview with your organization, or has a scheduled meeting with your organization.
    • This exemption never expires and applies account-wide.
  • RSVP’d to one of your events or career fairs.
    • This exemption lasts for one year from the RSVP date. After one year, messages to that student count toward the limit again unless another qualifying relationship exists, such as a job application or a scheduled interview or meeting.
  • Initiated the conversation, or replied to a message you sent.
    • Once a student has messaged a specific employer user, all future messages in that same conversation are exempt from the limit, regardless of how much time has passed.
    • This exemption applies at the individual employer user level, not the employer account level. If a different employer user contacts the same student, that is treated as a new conversation and counts toward the limit unless another exemption applies.
  • Deleted their Handshake account after receiving your message.
    • The message credit is returned and available to reuse within the same month.

How will I know when I’m approaching my limit? (Enterprise)

Enterprise (formerly TES) customers get proactive updates as their team’s monthly messaging usage grows.

Note: This feature is currently available to Enterprise customers only.

  • Handshake sends automatic email notifications to your team as usage approaches key milestones toward the monthly limit.
  • Once the monthly limit is reached, an in-product notice appears for users reflecting this.
  • Reaching the monthly limit blocks the creation of new campaigns until the limit refreshes.

Messaging Students: Attach a Teammate

Enterprise (formerly TES) customers on Handshake can introduce a teammate to a candidate via direct messaging.

Discover How to Send a Student a Message.

Premium features are for Handshake Premium accounts only. For more information, please check out this resource.

Permissions

To use this feature, your account must have one of the following roles:

  • Recruiter (Advanced)
  • Recruiter (Sourcer)
  • Owner
  • Administrator If you lack access, contact your company’s Owner or Admin to request a role change or additional permissions. For more information, refer to Who Is the Owner or Admin of My Company Profile?.

Teammate requirements

  • Must have one of these roles: Advocate, Recruiter (Sourcer), Recruiter (Advanced), or Admin.
  • Must be enabled to send and receive messages from candidates, even without a Handshake profile.

Attach (introduce) a teammate

  1. Click Talent from the left navigation bar. A teammate can be introduced in either a 1:1 or bulk message.
  • To introduce a teammate to many students, check the box to the left of Candidate in the header bar, then click the white Message button above the header.
  • To introduce a teammate to a specific student, click the white Message button located on the far right of their row.
  1. The message text box will appear. Draft your message, then click the Handshake icon in the lower-left corner of the message box, and select Teammate.
  • At the bottom of the message box, you can find options to format your message, insert web links, and access additional tools like templates and variables to personalize and enhance your communication.

  1. In the pop-up modal, choose a teammate from the dropdown menu and click the black Attach button. The teammate will appear as an attachment below the message text box

  2. Review your message carefully. When ready, click the black button Send.

  3. Students will receive the message and can choose to respond to either you or your teammate.

Receiving a Campaign Introduction

If you’ve been introduced as a contact in a campaign message by a teammate, messages received in response to the campaign will provide additional context, which allows you to enhance your relationship-building efforts and create a more personalized and meaningful candidate experience.

If you’d like to introduce a teammate in a campaign, refer to Messaging Students: Attach a Team Member.

Premium features are for Handshake Premium accounts only. For more information, please check out this resource.

Access your messages

To access and view messages received, refer to How Do I Access My Messages?.

Review messages

Messages will include the original campaign message, the associated job or event, if applicable, and a summary of the student’s prior engagement with the company.

Campaign message

The message includes the original campaign message, and the name of the recruiter who introduced you.

To view the profile of the recruiter who introduced you, click directly on their name below the message body.

You will be directed to their profile page, where you can learn more about their role, as well as their contact information.

To read the message in its entirety, click More and review the message as needed.

To efficiently manage your messages, refer to Managing your Inbox.

Campaign type

The message may feature job and event postings to attract potential candidates and attendees.

Jobs and events attached to the campaign are displayed in card format. To view additional details, click the link within the card.

The level of job and event details you view will vary based on your user role. Explore A Guide to Employer Role Types in Handshake.

Student profiles

The side sheet on the right of the message will provide direct access to a student’s profile if it’s visible in Handshake. The side sheet contains details, such as their education, skills, and experience. Additionally, it includes information on any previous engagements they may have had with your company.

To view a specific engagement in further detail, click on the hyperlinked name or title.

To view the student’s complete profile in a new tab, click the hyperlinked text View profile in the upper-right corner of the page.

Implementation Team Structure

As you get started in Handshake, one of the first objectives is to assemble an implementation team. This article outlines the recommended structure.

If you’re working with several stakeholders across a distributed campus, explore this article to learn implementation best practices for distributed campuses.

We strongly recommend the following steps in order to ensure visibility and clear ownership of tasks as your institution works to implement Handshake:

  • Identify Career Services POC Identify your school’s go-to contact(s) in Career Services for all things Handshake. This POC will lead the implementation project, understand and prioritize key workflows, and become an expert in the product.This is a critical step in your implementation and future success on Handshake!
  • Identify IT POC: This person will serve as the point-person for the IT required to set up Handshake and will set up tasks that are linked in Phase 0 of this guide. Depending on your IT structure, this could be one to three people. We recommend that you keep your implementation team small to allow for streamlined decision making and more efficient knowledge sharing.
  • Add IT POC to Handshake: Invite a Staff Member to Manage SSO
  • Build a Project Plan Task List: Find a comprehensive project task list here. Please save a copy of this and edit it to distribute to the POCs and key stakeholders on your implementation team.

Implementation: Kiosk Configuration

Kiosks are configured in Handshake using the information that you provide in this form. With that information, our team produces a regex string and substring. The regex string defines the card output formatting that’s being used, while the substring defines the actual student’s card ID found within the raw output.

Example:

Card output: !9234708294300==124;

Regex string: ^!==;$

Student’s card ID: 347082

Regex substring: ^!()==;$

Glossary of Regex terms:

  • “^” = What every regex string will start with
  • “ = the numbers you are wanting to convert in a card output. If there are 4 concurrent numbers in the output, then the regex would be “
  • “” = the letters you are wanting to convert in a card output. If there are 5 concurrent letters in an output, then the regex would be “

Rules of Thumb

  • Card_id on student record MUST be contained within the Card’s output
  • We can always shave off information from the output (i.e. if a student’s correct card_id is “1234123”, an output of “;001234123400;:” can be submitted without issue, truncating to a card_id of “1234123”)
  • We can’t add information to the output of a card to make it match the card_id of a student (i.e. if a student’s correct card_id is “0012341234”, an output of “;1234123400;” will not submit successfully. The card_id will require an update to “12341234”)

What if we have multiple card formats?

Handshake only supports one card format, so you’ll need to partner with your team to determine which makes the most sense to add to Handshake for your events, fairs, appointments, interviews, etc.

If you’d like us to configure your kiosks, please fill out the following form: forms.gle

  • Note: we recommend filling out this form at least a week before your first event. This will give your team enough time to test it and allow for any troubleshooting as needed.

What if we want to configure our own kiosks?

Provided you have the correct permissions, you may go into your school settings and click “Kiosk Preferences” on the left menu, then fill out the open fields.

Does Handshake support barcode readers?

It’s not officially supported, but if the barcode reader outputs keyboard (USB Output) and the student ID or a unique identifier is contained in the outputted string, then we should be able to support your barcode reader.

Setting up Custom Terms of Service for Students or Employers

If you need to have students or employers agree to a unique terms of service for using Handshake at your school, here are examples of what schools currently do:

For Students:

  1. Build a custom survey with the Terms of Service (TOS) that students need to acknowledge.
  • Marking the survey as “required” for all students, which will prompt the student to complete once they’ve completed the onboarding process.
  • Ensure that the survey has a completion label - so any student that takes this survey will have a specific label added to their profile. This way you can see who has acknowledged.
  1. If you need to restrict student access to feature on Handshake based on the TOS acknowledgement, you can then use this completion label to restrict certain features like appointments and interview schedules.

For Employers:

Typically schools will post any Employer Community Guidelines on their website. Then, once you’ve vetted and approved an employer, you can comment on the employer approval with a link to those terms or employer guidelines. Additionally, we recommend exploring our Handshake Community for advice and best practices from our other partner schools.

Transitioning from Handshake Open to Handshake Partner

Background on Opening Handshake

Handshake’s mission has always been to ensure that all students are able to find meaningful jobs, regardless of where they’re from or where they go to school. This year, more students across the country will have that chance.

As of August 20th 2019, any undergraduate student with a “.edu” email address from a four-year college or university can sign up for Handshake, where they will get access to some of the job search and community features we offer our Partner school students today. You can read more about the decision to open up access here. You can also review our VP of Higher Education and Student Success Christine Cruzvergara’s blog post about opening up access here.

Transitioning from Handshake Open to Being a Handshake Partner School

For schools that join the Handshake network post-August 2019, your school will be transitioned from a “Handshake Open” instance to a “Handshake Partner” instance on the platform. This functionally means that you will be starting from the advantageous position of already having interested students using the Handshake platform and employers who already want to recruit them.

Here are some key things to know about this transition:

  • Jobs: Approved Handshake employers are able to post jobs to the Handshake Open Network before a school joins as a partner. This means that you may see approved jobs when you log into Handshake for the first time.
  • Contacts: Approved Handshake employers who have posted a job to the Handshake Open Network or have identified themselves as an Alum at an institution are automatically added to a school’s Contacts list. This means that you may see contacts when you log in for the first time. All of the employers that are pre-approved are vetted by our validation process and will expand the opportunities available to their students.
  • Students: Students are able to access Handshake as a part of Handshake Open before a school joins as a partner. These students’ data will be updated once the school (your Career Services team) starts running a student data upload.This means that you will see active student profiles when you log in for the first time.

How will my student data upload impact information that my students have put in their profiles?

School year, major and GPA are the three fields that will be overridden for the students once the school does their first student data upload. We will notify the student that their information has changed once your school starts importing education information.

What do I need to do in order to transition my school from Open to Partnered?

Nothing. Your Relationship Manager will ensure this transition happens when you sign on to partner with Handshake!

What if I want to work on my transition but leave my students in the open network?

We can set your instance so that students can access the platform without seeing any of the career services features. We can enable this setting at any time, so if you’d like to do this, reach out to us support.joinhandshake.com and cc your Relationship Manager on the request.

What this means for your students:

  • With this setting, students with an email address ending in your school domain will automatically be approved when they request an account. You will not need to approve any requests.

  • Students will be able to access the job network and community aspects of the platform, but they will not see any information about your career services-specific features (career fairs, appointments, on-campus interviews, career center contact information, experiences, surveys, etc.)

  • Students will be able to apply for jobs that are part of the Handshake Open network. Those jobs are only posted by employers that have been validated and approved by at least 10 schools)

  • Students will be able to register for and attend public events and Career Fairs hosted by other schools. What this means for employers who wish to connect with you:

  • Employers will not be able to connect with your school or post jobs directly to your school until you choose to launch to them.

  • Employers will not be able to interact with your career center either, including requesting interviews, requesting events, or viewing your contact information for any related issues. What this means for you and your colleagues in Career Services:

  • You will not be able to view your school’s profile (you’ll get a permissions error - if you need to see the profile to review changes we could always send you a screenshot)

  • You will not be able to stop students from connecting to your school

  • You will be able to remove students from your school if necessary

  • You will be able to manage students’ profiles, and archive or delete their accounts

  • You will still be able to manage and test employer-related features if needed, such as Career Fairs and events, as you can create these from your end without real employers needing to see them

  • You will still be able to manage and test student-related features such as surveys, experiences, interview schedules, and appointments

Where should I go if I have other questions?

Reach out to your Relationship Manager via email or contact our Support team.

New to Handshake

Best Practices: Leveraging the Help Center Chatbot (New to Handshake)

Handshake Digital Assistant, our Help Center-based chatbot, provides an improved conversational experience on-demand with 24/7 availability.

  • Each response synthesizes information across relevant articles to quickly unblock next steps, enable key workflows, or share ways to optimize tools.
  • We’ve also created a more seamless handoff to Support for certain processes and issues best handled by a specialist, reducing friction during ticket creation. We’re always looking for opportunities to improve our user experience, which includes surfacing tips to engage effectively with this resource!

Select the appropriate user type

Choosing the right user type is the first step to ensuring you have the best experience possible. Our chatbot uses Help Center content in combination with customized instructions and guidance, which varies based on the user type selected.

When opening the chatbot, choose your user type based on your primary role in Handshake.

  • Student or alumnus - you’re a current student or alum using Handshake to look for internships or jobs, connect with employers, participate in fairs and events, or engage with your school’s Career Center
  • Employer - you work for a company that is hiring or will be hiring and are using Handshake to post internships or jobs, register and participate in school-hosted career fairs, or create and promote events for students/alumni
    • If you’re an employer, always only select “Employer”!
      • Selecting An EDU Partner will prioritize our EDU partner content first in responses, which may not be relevant or accurately describe steps you should take.
      • Selecting Student or alumnus will scope results to only the student user perspective, which won’t include details on employer features or workflows.
  • An EDU Partner - you work directly for a Handshake partner school (college, university, or higher education institution) and are using Handshake to facilitate Career Center or campus workflows, i.e. FDS, student syncs via Importer, appointments, creating and managing career fairs, events, or on-campus interviews, etc.
    • If you’re an EDU partner, select this option, even if you’re helping a student or employer!
      • We include content for each user type in your experience, but prioritize Career Services-based results first. This accounts for your unique workflows while still supporting you as you help your students and employers, too!

Have a conversation

When asking a new question, write your message the way you would explain it to a colleague or our Support team! Use sentences or descriptive phrases, include any error messages encountered, share the steps you’ve taken already, etc.

Note: the chatbot cannot read images or other media types, so please only upload attachments you wish to include in any tickets created.

Tips bulleted below are accompanied by screenshots of real conversations demonstrating the behavior outlined.

  • Providing more details improves accuracy in each response generated. By describing specific circumstances, our model better understands the goal or outcome desired, then identifies the most relevant content to create a response from.
    • Example conversation:
  • If a response provided doesn’t quite address the question or issue at hand, try rephrasing the message or providing more context, such as clarifying what you want to do.
    • Example conversation part 1 - the first response isn’t quite what was needed:
  • Each message and response plays an important role in how the conversation progresses, building on logic used to refine scope, provide guidance, or redirect as needed.
    • Example conversation part 2 - rephrasing the question provided more clarity on the goal, resulting in an accurate response:
  • When reading a chatbot response, don’t hesitate to ask followup questions or dig into the details! This applies the same logic as the tip above, building on conversation history to refine and elaborate.
    • Example conversation - this EDU workflow addressing major mapping leads up to questions about results from a recent job in Importer:
  • In the event the chatbot doesn’t have the information necessary to respond, you’ll be able to connect with our Support team directly.
    • Example conversation - this is a later portion of the above example, showing specific followup questions about Importer errors, along with an offer to handoff to Support: If you choose to proceed with contacting support, the conversation transcript is included in the ticket created – our Support team members read these transcripts first, and having more information available upfront can help expedite the resolution or next steps needed!

Community: Guidelines

Handshake Community is a space created for career services users to connect, and share best practices and strategic iniatives. The goal of this space is to empower one another in a supportive and relevant environment!

Click on the collapsible headers to learn more!

Guidelines

Content

At Handshake, we recognize sharing among peers can drive learning, scale workflows, and help support our valued partners to leverage all parts of the platform.

We encourage you to connect with other schools by initating questions, and offering solutions or guidance based on on best practices and/or strategic knowledge sharing.

Questions posted to Handshake Community may include:

“What appointment types do other schools have?”

“What are some successful ways of marketing Handshake to students?”

“Tips for creating engaging resource articles”

If you have any product-specific questions or need help troubleshooting an issue, we recommend referring to our Help Center or contacting our Support Team.

Note: Handshake will lightly moderate the community, but not comment on every post.

Privacy

When posting in the Community, other career services users will only have access to your name. If you feel it may be relevant to add your institution, job title, or anything else to help engage with the Community better, feel free to add the information within your posts and responses!

Joining Handshake Community

All career services users in Handshake have access to the community! To acces, click Help in the upper-right corner of your Handshake screen, then click Community from the dropdown.

Tip: set your notification preferences to manage which discussion boards you receive emails about!

When viewing a discussion board you’d like to be notified for, click the button Follow, located in the upper-left corner of the page, then select all new posts or all new posts and comments from the dropdown.

Posting in Handshake Community

To post an inquiry, click the button New Post, located in the upper-right corner of the Handshake Community homepage.

On the form that loads, enter the following information:

  • Title: an overview of your inquiry
  • Details (optional): any additional information that supports your inquiry
    • Tip: format your information to emphazie any points, or add images and hyperlinks
  • Topic
    • select a relevant topic from the dropdown for your inquiry to be posted under
      • Alumni in Handshake
      • Appointments
      • Career Fairs, Kiosks, & Payments
      • Community College Partners
      • East Coast Partners
      • Events
      • Experiences
      • Handshake Announcements
      • Handshake Implementation
      • IT and Technology (SSO, Importer, AutoSync, RSS, API)
      • Jobs Best Practices & Assisting Employers
      • Marketing & Communication
      • Midwest Partners
      • On Campus Interviews
      • Reporting and Analytics
      • Southern Partners
      • Student Employment
      • Surveys & First Destination Surveys
      • Tips, Tricks, & Miscellaneous
      • UK Partners
      • West Coast Partners Once everything is entered, click Submit to complete!

Responding to a Post

To respond to a post in the community, click in the text box, located below the Comments section of the page, and to the left of your icon.

Note: you can format your content in the text box to emphasize any points or include images and hyperlinks.

How to Submit Product Feedback

About Handshake’s Product Feedback process:

Here’s a visual overview of our process:

If you have an idea about how a feature could be improved, we welcome your feedback!

Please note that submitting this does not guarantee any changes, but our liaison reviews all submissions and triages the feedback appropriately for review by our University Product Team.

When reading through feedback, we’re primarily evaluating the level of impact that an update could have on all of our users. The larger the impacted audience = the more likely that feedback would be prioritized.

When feedback comes in that doesn’t have quite as much immediate impact but could definitely help improve our platform, we’ll track that feedback in a workspace created by our Product Team. As more feedback comes in with similar themes, those tickets are grouped together to demonstrate the growing impact of investing in that area.

Our Success, Support, and Product Teams each have designated points of contact that meet biweekly to discuss prioritization of submitted feedback and trends that we are seeing.

A great example of the results of this process is Handshake’s Targeted Emails tool. We received over 90 product feedback tickets offering suggestions on how we could improve our old Mass Emails tool. These tickets were an important driver in our Product Team’s decision to invest in building the a new tool - they helped to shape many of the key features of Targeted Emails!

What does a strong Product Feedback submission look like?

  • clearly outlines either the current perceived deficiency within Handshake OR what the ultimate goal is (not sure what would solve it, but you know your goals aren’t met currently)
  • defines the impact of that deficiency (how many users are affected and how so?)
  • provides all additional context around why this change would be helpful (ex. how will it improve your daily workflow?)
  • solution focused, as much as possible! We don’t expect you to know all the answers, but feel free to get creative with what you think would work!

How to submit Product Feedback:

  1. Click on the Help menu in the upper-right corner of the Handshake window.

  2. Click on the last option, Product Feedback.

  3. You’ll be taken to the submission page, where you’ll need to enter the following information:

  • Your email address
  • Subject
  • Product Category (optional)
  • Description
  • Attachments (optional)
  1. Click Submit when you are finished.
