How to Take Ownership of an Imported Job Posting

If you’re connected to a Basic employer account, you can take ownership of a job posting that was imported into Handshake without an assigned owner.

Imported jobs do not have an owner by default. Any user connected to the employer account, except representatives, can claim an unowned or unclaimed job to manage it and review its applicants.

Note: This feature is currently only available for Basic employers.

How do I find imported jobs that don’t have an owner?

  1. Click Jobs from the left navigation bar in Handshake.

  2. On the Jobs page, click the Owner filter.

  3. From the dropdown menu, select Jobs without owners, then click the black Apply button.

  4. The job list updates to show only jobs without an assigned owner. These jobs display “No owner” in the Job owner column.

  5. Select the job you want to take ownership of.

How do I claim ownership of a job?

  1. At the top of the job posting page, a banner displays the message “This job has no owner. To manage and review applicants, take ownership of this job.”

  2. Click the black Take ownership button.

  3. A confirmation message appears in the lower-right corner of the page: “Ownership claimed. You are now the owner of this job.”

Once confirmed, you are the job owner and can manage the posting and review its applicants.

How to Use Direct ATS

In Handshake, you can direct candidates to apply through your applicant tracking system to streamline the application process.

If you haven’t created a job on Handshake yet, refer to How to Post a Job.

Find or create the job you want to update

  1. Click Jobs from the left navigation bar.

  2. Locate the job:

  • If the job is a new job, click the black Create job button in the upper-right corner of the page.
  • If the job was saved as a draft, click the View drafts button and select the job.
  • If the job exists but isn’t posted yet, select the status Not Posted from the Status dropdown and select the job.

Set up Direct ATS on the job

  1. In the Application process section of the job form, answer the question “How will candidates submit applications?” by selecting On a separate website.

  2. Complete the following fields:

  • External URL: Enter the full link to your external application. The URL must begin with http:// or https://.
  • Instructions for applicants (optional): Add brief notes to guide candidates, for example “Complete the full application” or “Attach a cover letter.” Exceptions for Workday and Greenhouse

Workday

The External URL field is pre-filled. It is only editable if the global setting for Applicant Tracking Systems is enabled to “Allow users to change default ‘External Apply’ URLs.”

  • To make changes to your global settings, refer to Company Settings: Global Settings. Greenhouse

For Greenhouse-integrated jobs, both the External URL field and the Instructions for applicants textbox are visible on the job form.

The External URL field is pre-filled and greyed out, so it cannot be edited, because Handshake automatically populates it through the Greenhouse integration. The Instructions for applicants field remains editable.

How the application process works

If your job posting has any required documents checked, applicants will first be prompted to upload those documents in Handshake before being redirected to your external application (ATS).

Note: Some students may upload their documents and click through to your external site but may not complete the application process.

The Applicants tab in Handshake shows all students who clicked to apply, regardless of whether they submitted the full application through your ATS.

  • If you’d prefer that students go directly to your ATS without uploading documents in Handshake, uncheck any required documents in the Application process section of your job posting.
  • Include clear instructions in your job description so students understand they must complete their application on your external site. Need help managing applicants? Learn more about Reviewing Applications in Handshake.

Imported Jobs on Handshake

Handshake imports high-quality roles from publicly available sources such as job boards and employer career sites. This helps students discover more relevant opportunities on Handshake without needing to search elsewhere.

The goal is to fill gaps in job availability by providing accessible roles for students while enabling employers to extend their reach on Handshake.

Note: At this time, imported jobs are limited to Basic employers.

Which jobs are imported?

  • Prioritized roles: Imported roles focus on early-career opportunities that are valuable to students but less common on Handshake. These roles align with student interests and qualifications and are matched to employers who already have a Handshake presence.
  • Quality standards: Only jobs where all required details can be reliably parsed from the public posting are imported. If an imported job looks suspicious or out of place, contact Support.

Where are imported jobs posted?

Imported jobs are only posted at schools where the role meets job auto-approval criteria.

How to find and take ownership of imported jobs

Imported jobs appear directly on the Jobs page in Handshake. By default, they do not have an assigned owner.

Any user connected to the company profile can take ownership by setting themselves as the job owner.

Taking ownership allows your team to manage, edit, and oversee the posting. For more information, refer to How to Take Ownership of an Imported Job Posting.

How to view imported job details

All job details can be reviewed on the Jobs page in Handshake. From your jobs list, open a posting to view the imported information exactly as students will.

How are employers notified of imported jobs?

Handshake does not send notifications when jobs are imported. Imported jobs will always appear on the Jobs page, where you can review, manage, or close them at any time.

How do candidates apply to imported jobs?

Candidates can view full job details on Handshake, but applications are always completed externally on the employer’s career site.

The application link in Handshake directs students to the original posting, ensuring they apply through the most accurate and up-to-date source.

How to manage imported jobs

Once a teammate claims ownership, the job can be edited, updated, or closed at any time.

  • For more information on editing, refer to How to Edit a Job Posting.
  • For more information on closing a posting, refer to Close a Job Posting.

Invite Students to Apply to a Job Posting

Expand your reach by messaging students directly in Handshake about jobs that align with their skills and qualifications.

  • Basic employers: Can invite students to apply only from the Jobs page.
  • On-campus employers, Pro, Essentials, and Enterprise customers: Can invite students to apply from the Jobs page and the Talent page.

Jobs

  1. Click Jobs from the left navigation bar and select the job you want to invite students to apply for.

  2. Click the Source candidates tab. Handshake uses your job description to generate hiring criteria and surface a curated list of strong-fit candidates. For more information, refer to How to Source Candidates.

  3. Click a candidate card to load their profile in the right panel, then click Message [Name].

  4. A message composer opens with an AI-generated message personalized based on your hiring criteria. To write your own message, remove the AI-generated message and type your own. To restore an AI-generated message, click Add AI Messaging.

  5. Click Send when ready.

Note: Bulk messaging to sourced candidates is not currently supported.

*Talent

Note: The Talent page is available only to on-campus employers and Pro, Essentials, and Enterprise (formerly TES) customers.

  1. Click Talent from the left navigation bar, then select the student(s) you want to invite to apply.

  • To invite a specific student, click the white Message button to the far right of their name.

  • To select multiple students, check the boxes next to their names, then click Message in the header. To select all students on the page, check the box next to Candidate at the top of the table, then click Message in the header.

  • To select all students across all pages, click Select all 10,000 in the header.

  1. In the message window, draft your message, then click the Handshake icon in the lower-left corner of the text box and select Job.

  2. In the pop-up modal, select the job from the dropdown, then click Attach. The attachment will appear at the bottom of your message.

Note: Employers can also attach a teammate to messages for added personalization. For more information, visit Messaging Students: Attach a Teammate.

  1. Review your message and click the black Send button. A confirmation banner will appear at the top of the page.

Upon receiving the message, students can choose to apply for the job if it aligns with their interests.

Job Applicant Notification Preferences

Adjust email notification preferences for each job posting to stay updated on candidate applications, including a summary once the job closes.

To manage other types of job notifications, visit Default Notification Preferences (Employers).

Access by employer type

Basic employers

  • Owners and Recruiters can only manage notification preferences for jobs they personally created.

  • Notification preferences for jobs posted by other teammates cannot be changed.

  • To gain full access to manage notifications for all jobs, you must upgrade to an eligible paid plan. Plus, Pro, Essentials, Enterprise, and on-campus employers

  • All users, except Representatives, can manage notification preferences for both their own jobs and those posted by teammates, provided they have the appropriate permissions.

  • On-campus employers: You must be designated as an on-campus employer in your profile settings to manage notifications for jobs created by yourself and teammates. This designation is enabled by the owner of the company profile. For more information, visit Identifying as an On-Campus Employer on Handshake.

Manage job-level notifications

Each job posting allows the job owner and hiring team members to select their own email preferences.

  1. From the Jobs page, select the job you want to manage email preferences for, then click the Job details tab.

  2. Scroll to the Your hiring team section, then click the pencil icon to edit.

  3. In the Job owner or Hiring team members section, check or uncheck the boxes under Email settings to choose your notifications:

  • Send summary email once application period closes
  • Send email when a candidate applies
  • Send email when a candidate who meets qualifications applies
  1. Once your notifications are selected, click the black button Save.

Learn more about Receiving Applicant Package Emails.

Job Posting Overview Tab

The Overview tab provides aggregate performance data for applications, job views, and reach, as well as recommendations to improve your job’s performance.

Features available only to Premium partners are indicated by an asterisk (*). For more information, please check out this resource.

Access the job posting overview tab

  1. Click Jobs from the left navigation bar, then select the job you want to review.

  2. The Overview tab loads by default.

Explore the Overview tab

The Overview tab is available for all postings, for all employers. The data is divided into three sections: Applicants, *Job Views, and Reach.

Applicants

The Applicants section displays insight for your posting’s applicants. A recommendation to improve posting performance may appear on the right side of the section. Click the linked text in the modal to take action.

Below the Applicants heading are three tiles with counts for Total, Matching, and Invited to apply. Click a tile to review the relevant applicants.

The graph below the tiles shows the number of applications received over the past 30 days: green for total applicants, blue for matching applicants, and purple for invited applicants.

  • Hover over the graph to review application counts per day.
  • Click View table data below the graph to view the data in list format.
  • If no one has applied yet, this section displays “No applicants yet.” You can take action by clicking one of the options listed:
    • Invite your matches to apply
    • View recommended schools to add to this job *Job Views

Job Views is available to the following users:

  • Employers on an Essentials or Enterprise (formerly TES) account with the role of Advocate, Recruiter (Advanced), Recruiter (Sourcer), Admin, or Owner
  • Pro employers who have promoted a job
    • Note: Job views will be available for promoted jobs only. The Job Views section displays two tiles: Total (all time) and Invited to apply.

Below the tiles is a graph of job views per day for the last 30 days.

  • Hover over a day to see total views (in green) and views from invites (in purple).
  • Click View table data below the graph to view the data in list format. If no one has viewed the job yet, this section displays “No views yet.” Click Try Inviting Matches to apply to help increase job views. Learn more about Job Matches.

Reach

Reach provides the total count and percentage of students on Handshake who have access to your posting, broken down by Total and Matching.

Below the heading are tiles for Total and Matching. Click the Matching tile to access the Matches tab.

Below the tiles is a donut graph showing total reach and matching reach.

  • Total: The total number of early talent with Handshake accounts at schools where this job is approved.
    • Click View all schools you posted to to review schools or post the job to additional schools.
  • Matching: The total number of early talent in your total reach who also match all qualifications.
    • Click View matches to review your matches.

Manage Your Job Promotion

Edit a promotion to better fit your hiring needs, or stop a promotion if you no longer want to promote the job.

Haven’t created a job promotion yet? Start with Create a Job Promotion.

This article is for Essentials and Enterprise employers. Basic and Pro employers manage promoted jobs through a different workflow. For more information, Basic and Pro employers should refer to Manage Your Promoted Jobs.

Promotions is currently available only for Essentials and Enterprise customers. For more information, please check out this resource!

How to access your job promotion

  1. Click Promotions from the left navigation bar.

  2. Locate the promotion you want to manage.

Tip: Use the filters above the Promotions table to quickly find the promotion you want to manage.

  1. Click the three-dot menu on the far right of the promotion row.

  2. From the menu, you can choose Edit promotion or Stop promotion.

Note: Only Owners, Admins, and Recruiters (Sourcers) can edit or stop promotions.

Edit a promotion

You can edit an active promotion to update its duration or budget.

To edit a promotion:

  1. Select Edit promotion from the dropdown.

  2. Update one or both of the following:

  • Duration
  • Budget
  1. Click the black Save changes button.

Stop a promotion

You can stop an active promotion if you no longer want to promote the job.

To stop a promotion:

  1. Select Stop promotion from the dropdown.

  2. A confirmation message appears explaining that the job will no longer be promoted, any remaining budget will not be spent, and you must create a new promotion if you want to promote the job again.

  3. Click the black Continue button.

Manage Your Promoted Jobs

Once a job is promoted a job, Basic and Pro employers can view, stop, or restart that promotion from the Plan & Billing page.

Haven’t created a promotion yet? Learn how to Promote a Job.

Topics:

  • View your promoted jobs
  • Stop a promotion
  • Restart a promotion
  • What happens next

How do I view my promoted jobs?

  1. Click your name in the upper right corner, then select Plan & Billing from the dropdown.

  2. The Plan & Billing page displays your plan details, upcoming charges, and payment method at the top of the page.

  3. Select the Promoted jobs tab to view all active job promotions, including:

  • Job title and creator
  • Daily promotion rate
  • Promotion end date
  • Billing period and accrued charges
  • Payment method on file
  1. Select the Past promotions tab to view jobs that are no longer being promoted.

How do I stop a promotion?

You can stop a promotion at any time. You’re billed through the current day only, with no charges starting the following day. Stopping a promotion does not close your job. Your job remains active and visible to candidates at standard visibility.

  1. On the Plan & Billing page, locate the job you want to stop promoting and click Manage promotion.

  2. On the Manage promotion page, review your current plan (Standard or Premium), then click Stop promotion.

  3. A window titled Stop promoting this job? appears. It lists the promotion benefits you’ll lose, such as featured placement in search, inbox, and email, reach to more qualified applicants, applicant screening, AI-powered applicant recommendations, and AI-assisted direct messaging.

This window also confirms that you’re billed for today only, with no charges starting tomorrow, and that you can restart the promotion within up to one hour if you change your mind.

  1. Click Stop promotion to continue, or Keep promoting to cancel and keep the promotion active.

  2. You may be offered a limited-time discount to continue promoting the job for another month. This offer, if shown, is subject to change. Click Stop promotion to decline the offer and continue stopping the promotion, or Keep promoting to accept the offer and keep the promotion active.

  3. If this is the last job you’re actively promoting, a Before you go survey page appears. Rate your experience with promoted jobs using the star rating.

  • The star rating is required before the Stop promotion button becomes clickable.
  • You can optionally select a reason for ending the promotion and add feedback in the text box. If you still have other active job promotions, this survey does not appear and the promotion stops immediately.
  1. Click Stop promotion to confirm. You will be redirected to the Plan & Billing page, and the job returns to standard visibility.

Restart a promotion

You cannot restart a stopped promotion until one hour has passed. The Restart promotion button remains greyed out until the cooldown period ends.

Note: You can only restart a promotion if the job is still active and you have Owner, Admin, or Recruiter-Sourcer permissions.

  1. On the Plan & Billing page, locate the job you want to restart and click Restart promotion.

  2. A confirmation message appears in the lower left corner of the page: Promotion restarted. This job’s promotion has been restarted successfully.

What happens next

  • Stopped promotions return the job to standard visibility immediately.
  • Restarted promotions become active immediately and billing resumes.

Basic employers

Access the Jobs page

Top opportunities

The Top opportunities section provides insight-driven guidance to help improve job applications for open roles.

Jobs that would benefit from an action are highlighted at the top of the page, and their cards display specific calls to action based on the employer’s account type and the user’s role.

Note: The yellow, oval-shaped button indicates that the job posting has 5 or fewer applications.

Job filters

A set of filters is located at the top of the Jobs table, allowing you to refine your search and locate jobs across all statuses.

You can filter jobs by the following criteria:

  • Keyword search
    • Search by ID number or title
  • Owner
    • Jobs owned by you

    • Note: This option is only displayed if the company owner has set up divisions.
  • Status
    • Active
      • Jobs that are pending or approved.
      • Note: This filter is selected by default. To view all jobs, including those with a future apply start date, deselect this option.
    • Not Posted
      • Jobs whose job form has been completed but not yet posted to any schools.
    • Closed
      • Jobs that have been previously approved at a school and the closing date has passed.

Job specifics

The Jobs table shows the following information for jobs with an Active, Not Posted, or Closed status:

  • Job title
  • Job ID (located below the title)

  • Job owner (who the job was created by)
  • Open date (date job was created)
  • Close date (date job closes)
  • Applications (count)
  • Matches (count)
  • Schools (count)
    • *The Matches tab is replaced with Campaigns (count) for Essentials and TES customers.

Job management

Posting a Job to Recommended Schools

Recommended schools are schools with the highest number of candidates who meet your job’s location and qualification criteria.

You can review, customize, and post jobs directly to these schools to reach the most relevant candidates.

Features available only to Premium partners are indicated by an asterisk (*). For more information, please check out this resource.

Access recommended schools

  1. Click Jobs from the left navigation bar, then select the relevant job.

  2. On the job posting page, click the Schools tab.

  3. The page displays a Recommended schools section at the top, with a Customize recommendations button in the upper-right corner.

Each recommended school is displayed as a card and includes:

  • School name and location
  • Number of qualified candidates based on the job’s criteria
  • A Post job here now button To view additional recommendations, click Load more to view up to 25 schools.

If no schools can be recommended based on your current qualifications or job location, a banner appears. From the banner, you can take any of the following actions:

  • Click Edit locations to update the job’s location.
  • Click Edit qualifications to update candidate qualification criteria.
  • Click Customize recommendations to manually adjust recommendation filters.

How schools are recommended

Employers are matched with schools based on the following criteria:

  • Location: Schools within 250 miles of the job’s primary location.
    • If a job includes multiple locations, the first listed location is used by default. You can change this by customizing your recommendations.
    • If “various locations” is listed instead of a specific location, no geographic filter is applied.
  • Candidate qualifications:
    • Work authorization
    • School year
    • Graduation date
    • Major groups

Customize your school recommendations

By default, recommendations are based on your job’s existing candidate preferences and primary location.

  1. Click Customize recommendations in the upper-right of the Recommended schools section.

  2. A panel will appear on the right side of the page with available filters.

All employers can customize recommendations based on the following:

  • Candidates meet your job’s qualifications: Your current preferences are displayed. To edit, click Edit qualifications.

  • Their school is near your job location(s): The selected locations are listed with a range of 250 miles. If this option is unavailable, the job’s location type is set to remote. *Essentials and Enterprise (formerly TES) customers can also customize recommendations based on the following:

  • *They want to work near your job’s location: Students who have expressed interest in jobs close to your posting’s location(s). Select from a radius of 5, 15, 30, 50, 75, 100, or 250 miles. When a posting lists multiple locations, any student who has expressed interest in at least one of those locations is counted as a match.

  • *They’re interested in roles like this one: Students who have indicated interest in the job role(s) associated with your posting. For more information on job roles, refer to Job Roles and Job Role Groups.

  • *They’re interested in your industry: Students who have expressed interest in your industry. Confirm or update your industry in your company settings. To view all industries in Handshake, access the Employer Industry Name List.

Post a job to a recommended school

  1. Click the Post job here now button on the school card for the school you want to post to.

Note: Schools that have declined your company approval will not appear in the Recommended schools section.

  1. In the pop-up, choose the application’s open and close date, then click Post Job.

  2. Once posted, a confirmation banner will appear within the school card.

  3. The posting will appear in the Requested Schools section of the Schools tab with a Pending status until reviewed by the school. For more information, refer to Understanding Job Posting Approvals.

Promote a Job

Promoting a job post helps you reach more qualified applicants faster. This article covers how Basic and Pro employers can promote a job, either while creating a new posting or on an existing one at any time.

Essentials and Enterprise (formerly TES) employers can also promote jobs in-app, but through a separate workflow. For step-by-step instructions, refer to Create a Job Promotion.

What promotion tiers are available?

Three tiers are available when you post or promote a job:

  • Basic Post (free): Listed in search results, with limited visibility. This option does not include promotion.
  • Standard ($34/day): Best for everyday hiring. Includes:
    • Priority placement before 95% of other jobs
    • Increased visibility across search, inbox, and email
    • Access to more qualified applicants where they’re looking
    • Applicant screening as they apply
  • Premium ($59/day): Best for competitive and urgent hiring. Includes:
    • All Standard features
    • 35% more reach with qualified candidates
    • Up to 40% more applicants than Standard

How do I promote a job while posting it?

  1. While completing your job posting form, you will reach the Promote your job post page.

  2. Compare Basic Post, Standard, and Premium and review the features included with each tier.

  3. Select Standard or Premium, then click the black Promote job button.

  • To post without promoting, select Basic Post instead, then click Post without promoting. You can always add a promotion later.

  1. On the Confirm your promotion page, review the tier you selected, its daily rate, and included features.

  2. In the Payment details section, enter your email address.

  • If Handshake recognizes saved payment information linked to that email, you can verify your identity by entering the code sent to your phone, or click “Send code to email instead” to receive the code by email instead. If no saved information is found, enter your payment details directly.

  1. Choose a payment method: Card, Direct debit, or Google Pay.

  2. Review the total charged today and the billing terms, then check the box agreeing to Handshake’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.

Promotion is billed weekly based on the daily rate and the number of days your job stays active, and a one-time authorization hold matching one day’s rate is placed when you confirm. You can cancel the promotion at any time.

  1. Click the black Promote job button to confirm payment.

  2. After payment is confirmed, you will reach the Review job details page. A “Payment accepted” message appears briefly, and a Promoted job panel shows your selected tier, its features, and the total charged today.

  • To change your tier, click Change in the Promoted job panel. This returns you to the Confirm your promotion flow so you can choose a different tier and complete payment again.

  1. Review your job posting details and click Edit next to any section you want to change.

  2. Click the black Post job button in the top-right corner to finalize your posting.

How do I promote a job post that’s already live?

  1. Click Jobs in the left navigation bar, then select the job you want to promote.

  2. On the job detail page, click the Promote job button in the upper-right corner.

  3. Compare the Standard ($34/day) and Premium ($59/day) options and the combined “What you get” feature list, then select a tier and click Promote job.

  4. On the Confirm your promotion page, review the tier you selected, its daily rate, and included features.

  • If you have promoted a job before, your saved payment method and the total charged today are displayed automatically.
    • To use a different payment method, click Update next to Payment method.
  • If you do not have a saved payment method, enter your email address in the Payment details section.
    • If Handshake recognizes saved payment information linked to that email, verify your identity by entering the code sent to your phone, or click “Send code to email instead” to receive the code by email instead.
    • If no saved information is found, enter your payment details directly, then choose a payment method: Card, Direct debit, or Google Pay.
  1. Review the total charged today and the billing terms, then check the box agreeing to Handshake’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.

Promotion is billed weekly based on the daily rate and the number of days your job stays active, and a one-time authorization hold matching one day’s rate is placed when you confirm. You can cancel the promotion at any time.

  1. Click the black Promote job button to activate your promotion.

What happens after I promote a job?

Once your promotion is confirmed, a window displays “Your promoted job is live.” This window explains that Handshake will automatically send invitation messages to qualified candidates on your behalf. From this window, you can turn on either or both of the following:

  • Automatically invite qualified candidates to apply: When turned on, this displays the date and time of the next automated message and an editable message template. You can customize the message with details about the role and your organization. The template includes placeholders, such as the candidate’s first name, that personalize each message.
  • Automatically book interviews with top candidates: When turned on, this lets qualified candidates skip the application step and book an interview with you directly. You must share your calendar for candidates to book time directly. Select the options you want and click the black Save changes button.

If you turned on automated invitations, a follow-up confirmation displays: “Your automated outreach is in progress.”

Share a Job Posting URL

Expanding the visibility of your job postings is key to attracting qualified student applicants. To help you reach more students, you can share a direct link to your job post in just a few steps.

All role types except Representatives can view and manage job postings, unless their permissions are configured otherwise.

If you’re unable to view or manage a job posting, reach out to your company’s owner or admin to request the necessary permissions. To identify the owner of your company’s profile, refer to Who is the Owner of my Company’s Profile?.

Copy and share a job posting URL

  2. On the job posting page, copy the full URL from your browser’s address bar.

  • The link will begin with: app.joinhandshake.com (followed by a unique job ID number).
  • Students can view job postings using this link, even though it includes “emp” in the URL.
  1. After copying the job posting URL, paste it into the communication channel you’re using to promote the opportunity.

Students will be able to view the job posting only if they:

  • Are logged into their Handshake account
  • Attend a school where the job has been approved If a student does not meet these criteria, they will be redirected to the Handshake login or sign-up page.

Note: If you share the URL with someone outside of your company (e.g., another agency or partner), they must have a Handshake account and be connected to your company profile to view the full details of the job posting.

To boost engagement and reach more qualified applicants, refer to Invite Students to Apply to a Job Posting.

Source Tag URL for External Applicant Tracking Systems

Source tags enable your ATS to recognize Handshake as the source of your candidates.

Since Handshake can only identify an applicant who clicks to apply once they have been redirected from the site, it’s essential to track the source in your ATS to identify which candidates were sourced from Handshake.

Topics:

  • Source tags
  • Configure your source tag
  • Add a source tag to a new job

Source tags

A source tag is a string of text appended to a URL that contains instructions for the ATS on how to track the referral source. Although ATS systems use different names for these tools, the purpose remains the same. Among these names are “tracking links”, “source tracking”, “tracking codes”, and “source code”.

For the ATS to automatically identify Handshake-referred applicants, source tags must be configured correctly.

Source tags are typically structured as a URL parameter. URL parameters (sometimes called query strings) are the part of the weblink that follows a single question mark. Multiple parameters can be appended to a single URL separated by ampersands.

  • The following is an example of an ATS source tag: www.companyname.com/careers/jobID12345/source=Handshake Note: The actual URL will be different for each employer and their respective ATS service, but they will all end with “source=Handshake”.

Configure your source tag

To configure your source tag, refer to the support documents provided by your ATS partner. They should all have resources available to help you retrieve your source tags.

These resources should contain the following information:

  • ATS name
  • Name of concept: how the ATS refers to source tag
  • Example URL: a sample job link URL with the source tag component bolded
  • Source tag structure: a generic example of the source tag
  • Cross-session Attribution: does the ATS support auto-tracking if the candidate leaves the site and then returns? Typically true if the source tag adds a browser cookie.
  • Configuration: if the ATS requires each source to be configured before it can accept a new source for Handshake, a rough guide will be provided with a link to the exact instructions from the ATS provider Note: If you are currently posting manually on job boards like Indeed, LinkedIn, or Glassdoor, this is likely the same process you’ve done before if you’re tracking those sites as candidate sources in your ATS.

If you need help configuring your source tag, contact the ATS support team for guidance on locating the correct URL.

Add a source tag to a new job

Now that you have successfully configured your source tag, you can apply it to a new job in Handshake.

  1. Click Jobs from the left navigation bar, then click the black Create Job button in the upper-right corner of the page.
  • To add your source tag to a job post that was saved as a draft, click the white button View drafts, then select the job.
  • To add your source tag to a job that isn’t posted, select the status Not Posted from the Status dropdown, then select the job.
  1. In the Application process section, add the source tag URL in the External URL field, then click the blue Save button in the upper-right corner of the section.

Understanding Colorado’s Job Application Fairness Act: A Resource for Colorado Employers on Handshake

As of July 1, 2024, Colorado enacted the Job Application Fairness Act (JAFA), which restricts the collection of age-related data from job applicants.

This article offers guidance to help employers on Handshake remain compliant while continuing to connect with potential candidates.

What is the Job Application Fairness Act?

JAFA prohibits employers from inquiring about a job applicant’s age during the hiring process. Specifically, employers cannot ask about:

  • The applicant’s age
  • Date of birth
  • Dates of attendance at or graduation from an educational institution If application materials such as transcripts or graduation certificates are requested, inform applicants of their right to redact any information that could reveal their age, date of birth, or dates of school attendance or graduation. These restrictions apply only at the time of an initial employment application.

Under certain conditions, JAFA allows employers to require verification of age for:

  • Positions where age is a necessary qualification for public or occupational safety
  • Compliance with federal law or regulation
  • Compliance with state or local law or regulation based on a required occupational qualification In these instances, employers may ask if an applicant meets a minimum age requirement but cannot ask for specific dates that would disclose the applicant’s age.

How does JAFA affect employers on Handshake?

Handshake does not collect information about a student’s age or date of birth. While employers can request graduation years or dates of attendance as part of job qualifications, collecting this information is optional and not required when creating a job posting.

To ensure compliance with JAFA on Handshake:

  • When posting a job: Avoid requiring students to submit age-related information such as school year or graduation date in the Candidate qualifications section. Focus on skill-based qualifications relevant to the job.
  • Compliance responsibility: Employers are responsible for ensuring their use of Handshake and other recruitment tools complies with JAFA and other applicable laws. Consult with legal counsel for specific guidance.

Posts & The Feed

EDU: Posting and Accessing Content on the Home Feed

Handshake’s Post Composer grants you the ability to share content with your students through the feed! You can provide inspiring messages, updates, videos, opportunities, share Handshake content and more using our posting feature.

To learn more about Handshake’s Feed, please refer to Handshake Feed and Post Composer Overview.

Posting Content to Handshake’s Feed

To get started, select Posts from the left navigation bar.

Then click Share something with students…

Posting an image or video

In the pop-up, select Choose file to upload an image or video. You can also drag and drop an image or video into this box to upload it. We support JPG and PNG files for images.

Note: When you record videos in HDR, Cloudflare automatically converts them to SDR for compatibility, which can make colors look less vibrant. To keep your video looking its best, export it directly to SDR in your video editing app before uploading, so you can avoid Cloudflare’s automatic conversion.

Adding alternative text

After you’ve chosen an image file you can add alt text to help describe your image to other Handshake users.

Add the text in the next window and select the Save button to return to your draft. You can then Post your content.

Audio Description

After uploading a video file, you may add a secondary audio descriptor track. This track can be utilized to explain the contents of the video.

Select the menu at the upper left of the video and choose Add audio description

Another file selection window will appear. Choose the audio track (e.g. MP3 file) that describes what’s happening in the video and select Post when you’re ready to publish this to the feed!

Creating a text post

If you’d like to write a text post, when you create a post, select text post under the “Write a text post instead” message.

Note: the text character limit is 3,000 characters and the video upload limit is 30 GB. For more information about dimension recommendations, refer to Handshake Image Size Guide

Tip: inspire students and alumni through your content by guiding and educating them with your posts!

  • If you wish to modify the author of your post, click on the dropdown arrow to the right of your name, then choose the desired author. Once text content has been added, click the button Post to share it to the feed!

Access Content Posted to Handshake’s Feed

To review content you’ve posted to the feed, click Posts on the left navigation bar.

Note: currently, you only have access to posts made by yourself. Soon you’ll have access to all posts by your institution!

Posts are listed below the text box to add new content in chronological order with the newest at the top and oldest at the bottom.

Tip: You can “like” a post by clicking the heart in the lower left corner of the post!

  • If any students and alumni have reacted to your post on the feed, the number of likes will be present in the bottom-right corner of the post.
  • When you click on a post, the number of impressions will appear. This is how many individual students have viewed this post on the feed.

Delete a post

You can delete your own posts.

To delete a post, click the three dots menu, located to the right of the post, then click Delete from the dropdown.

You’ll be asked to confirm deletion of the post. Select the red button Delete to remove the post.

Handshake Home Feed and Post Composer Overview

The Handshake feed and Post Composer on Handshake are powerful tools designed to enhance the career exploration journey for students.

In this article, we’ll explore who has access to the feed, how content is uploaded via Post Composer, feed engagement at your institution, and the future of the Handshake feed!

Handshake Feed

The Handshake feed is an access point or entrance for how content is discovered and consumed by students.

It serves as a discoverability tool that exposes students to various elements of the job search, including:

  • Career-related content posted by your institution
  • Career-related content posted by employers
    • Only by approved employers at your institution
  • Available jobs
    • Jobs posted by premium partners or those that are upgraded with Handshake Plus, if they employer chooses to post them to the Handshake feed.
  • Upcoming events and fairs
  • Appointment opportunities If a student does not meet all the specific qualifications or permissions to access any of the above elements, they will not be available on their feed.

The range of content posted to the feed can extend from a text post, link, or video.

Note: all students have access to the Handshake feed via their homepage. Eventually, content in the feed will surface within other areas of Handshake. For example, an uploaded video may appear in the feed and a job posting for students.

Content displayed on the feed is unique to each student as it is based on a relevance ranking system on the backend. The relevance of the content is determined by a variety of factors such as the student’s major, career interests, location, and graduation year.

Important: only students and alumni have access to the feed.

  • To learn more about the student experience using the Handshake feed, check out Handshake Feed: Overview & Interactions.
  • To review Handshake’s content policy, refer to Handshake’s Content Policy.
  • To learn more about how Handshake moderates content on the feed, check out How Handshake Moderates Content on the Handshake Feed.

Who has access to Posts?

Students have access to posts from their institutions and employers through the feed. Institutions and employers currently have access to posts that they have created themselves.

To maintain a fresh and captivating feed, Handshake intends to surface the following information in the future:

  • 1:1 and Group Sessions with employers
  • Employers to follow
  • Saved jobs and event reminders
  • Peer students to reach out ot
  • Your team’s resources
  • Employer collections

Post Composer

Post Composer is a tool that allows users to post content to the feed. Ultimately, this is a part of Handshake’s vision to scale content across the platform.

Note: to access Posts, you need the Post Content role with “Access” permission. To learn more about your roles and permissions, refer to School Settings: Career Services Staff Roles and Permissions.

To learn more about how to post content to the Handshake feed, refer to EDU: Posting and Accessing Content on the Handshake Feed.

Engagement at your institution

Note: to review the Handshake feed dashboard, you need the Data role with “Access” permission. To learn more about your roles and permissions, refer to School Settings: Career Services Staff Roles and Permissions.

To review the content included in the Handshake feed dashboard, refer to Dashboard: Handshake Feed engagement.

The future of the Handshake feed

This is an evolving feature release and will consist of many layers over time.

The end goal is to have all users posting user-generated content to the feed via post composer - this includes career services, employers, and students!

Privacy & Safety

Blocking A User on Handshake

Handshake is designed to be a professional and respectful community. If you’d prefer not to interact with another user, you have the option to block them directly from their profile.

Note: Blocking is only available for individual user profiles, not employer profiles. If you’re receiving messages from a company you’re not interested in, you can temporarily pause their outreach. To learn more about muting employer campaign messages, refer to Mute Employer Campaign Messages.

What Happens When You Block a User

Blocking a user will:

  • Prevent them from messaging you
    • If the user is an employer, this also includes bulk messages and campaigns sent by that employer
  • Hide your profile and activity from them
  • Remove any past messages between you
  • Hide them from your view in:
    • People search
    • Event attendee lists
    • Job pages (e.g., “Alumni who worked at this job”)
    • Your feed and other shared views Important: Blocking a user is currently a permanent action. If you need to unblock someone, contact us.

How to Block a User

  • Go to the user’s profile. You can do this by clicking their name anywhere you find them on the platform.
  • Click the three dots menu located in the upper-right corner of the page (to the left of Message), then click Block.
  1. In the pop-up the following message is displayed:

“Are you sure you want to block [NAME]? Blocking this user will prevent them from messaging you and will hide your profile and activity from them. You will no longer see their activity on Handshake, and they will no longer see yours.

If you wish to report this user for violating our terms of service, let us know [LINK].”

Confirm you want to block the user by clicking the black button Yes, block or Cancel to cancel.

Once confirmed, a message will appear in the lower-right corner letting you know the user has been blocked successfully

Confirmation that Handshake Does Not Sell Student Data

Handshake does not and will never sell any identifiable student data. We are committed to protecting your privacy and ensuring that your information is used only in accordance with our Privacy Policy.

Data Ownership in Handshake

Students retain ownership of the data they upload to Handshake. We only use your data as outlined in our Privacy Policy and Terms of Service, and if your school has partnered with Handshake, in accordance with the agreement we have with your school.

Your data rights and how to exercise them:

Controlling what you share: profile and account settings

Handshake gives you control over what information you share, who can see it, and how you interact on the platform. Whether you’re setting up your account for the first time or updating your preferences later, you can manage your privacy in the following areas:

  • Profile visibility: Choose who can view your Handshake profile. Learn more in. Learn more in How to Change Your Student Profile Privacy Setting.
  • Public profile and profile link: Make your profile publicly accessible outside of Handshake or share a direct link to your profile. Learn more in. Learn more in How to Make Your Profile Public and Share Your Profile Link.

Employer Interactions with Students

This article details how employers can interact with students on Handshake once students activate their Handshake account. Employers may initiate interactions with students, depending on the profile privacy option the student has selected. For more information on this, refer to Profile Privacy Options in Handshake.

Employer Trust & Safety Requirements

We work hard to make sure employers contact students in a safe and secure manner. Handshake now vets new employers for legitimacy and monitors for fraud on an ongoing basis. This new validation process is backed by an industry leading fraud-prevention platform technology, and helps us maintain a credible network of employers without the trust score.

If there’s an employer in violation of our Terms of Service, our Trust & Safety team will review the employer’s account and suspend access if needed.

In order for employers to directly interact with students at your school, the school must approve the employer.

  • If your school has partnered with Handshake, the Career Services team is responsible for reviewing each employer request. For more information on this process, refer to How do employers get approved at my school?
  • If your school has not yet partnered with Handshake, and you’re part of the Handshake Open Network, any employer that’s vetted via the fraud-prevention platform and has past activity on Handshake can interact with the Open Network. If you encounter any suspicious activity from an employer, refer to Safety: Flagging an Employer on Handshake so that our Trust & Safety team may review and take appropriate action.

Employer Outreach Activities

Every type of activity an employer might take on Handshake has a prerequisite that helps strengthen the Trust & Safety on our network. These prerequisites are listed below:

  • Post jobs
    • Employer must be approved at the school or for Open Network.
    • If a job posting is requested at a Handshake partner school, that school is responsible for reviewing and processing the job posting requests..
      • For more information on how employers connect with students from the open network, refer to How to Connect with Handshake Open Network.
  • Message students
    • Employer must be approved at the school or for Handshake’s Open Network.
    • Employer must have an approved or expired job posting at your school, or on the platform for Handshake’s Open Network.
      • Note: Some schools block student messaging.
    • Student must have interacted with the employer (via applying for a job, signing up for virtual fair sessions, or RSVPing for an event).
  • Download resumes
    • Employer must be approved at school or for Open Network.
    • Student must have interacted with the employer (via applying for a job, signing up for virtual fair sessions, or RSVPing for an event).
      • Note: there are a very small number of employers that have been individually vetted by our Trust & Safety and provided access to download public resumes without the above.
  • Host events
    • Employer must be approved at school or for Open Network.
    • To host an event in partnership with a school, employers must be approved at the school, and the school must approve the event to be hosted for it to be discoverable.
  • Host virtual fair sessions
    • Employer must have an approved fair registration with the school, and students have signed up for the fair session(s).
    • Employers that have been declined at a school won’t be able to register for a fair or host sessions.
  • Career Fairs - Employers with an approved fair registration with the school, will have the option to attend the fair. - Note: employers can’t view the registered student attendees list for a career fair.
  • Interviews
    • Employer must be approved at the school, and the school must have approved the interview schedule requested.
    • Interviews can’t be posted to the Handshake Open Network. Employers may also use a combination of these methods in interaction — for example, an employer may message students in Handshake inviting them to an event or apply for a job, or download a student’s public resume after the student registers for an employer event or signs up for a session at a virtual fair.

How Employers Search for Students

To find students to message and/or download resumes from, an employer can use the following filters at schools the employer is approved at:

  • School
  • School year
  • Graduation date
  • GPA
  • Labels (added by employers)
  • College
  • Department GPA
  • Students that have a public resume (limitations exist on which employers can download) Premium Employer Partners

Some employers on Handshake are considered Premium partners — these employers have paid for Handshake usage and have been through additional vetting by our team. They have access to additional filters and tools to help them connect with students in a more meaningful way.

For more information on Handshake Premium product and features, please refer to Handshake’s Premium Employer Offering.

Our Premium partners have the additional filters below to search for students at approved schools:

  • Location Interests

  • Major Category

  • Institution Type

  • Diversity and Inclusion Focused Organizations

  • Majors

  • Past Companies

  • Past Job Titles

  • Organizations/Extracurriculars

  • Skills Premium partners can also create Segments (groups of anonymized, aggregated students and/or alumni at approved schools) based on filters that include:

  • School, Profile keywords, Major keywords/group/category

  • New grads/recent grads/interns

  • student interests (Job Role, Industry, Job Type)

  • GPA, Work Authorization, Organizations/Extracurriculars

  • Achievements and Accolades

  • Location Preference, Current Location

  • Skills/Coursework/ work experience (job title or company)

  • Underrepresented Groups (based on Organizations, Gender, or institution types)

    • Note: Employers aren’t able to only select an Underrepresented Groups Organizations filter — this filter must be selected in conjunction with another filter. When Premium partners use these Segment filters, they won’t be able to view a list of student names that meet these criteria; however, these students will be able to be messaged, and student association with a particular segment filter may be inferred if the student responds to that employer’s message.

For more information, refer to How Employers Use Messaging with Students.

Information Employers have access to

Students are in full control of whether an employer can view their profile.

If a student selects Private, no other students or employers can view their profile — only career services staff.

If a student has selected the Employers or Community profile privacy option, then employers that are approved at their school will be able to view their profile. Employers will have access to the following information:

  • Education information
    • School name, school year, graduation date, major, minor, college, GPA*
    • Student GPA is never public unless the student expressly opts-in to make it public. If a student does choose to make their GPA public, this information is visible to employers only. Other students or alumni won’t be able to view other students’ GPA’s, even if the GPA’s are visible by employers.
  • Work experience details
  • Skills
  • Organizations / Extracurriculars
  • Projects
  • Pronouns*
    • When a student opts into specifying their pronouns, they’ll be able to choose to share their pronouns with employers, other students, or both.
    • For more information, refer to our blog post Student Gender Identity and Pronouns on Handshake.

Handshake Age Requirements for Students

Handshake has different minimum age requirements depending on the type of account you’re creating. Use the table below to find the requirement that applies to you.

Student account affiliated with a school (Age 16+)

To create a student account on Handshake, you must be at least 16 years old.

If you are under 16, a parent or legal guardian must complete Handshake’s consent form and submit it by reaching out to our Support team.

Individual account not affiliated with a school (Age 18+)

An individual student account is for users who are not affiliated with a school on Handshake (i.e., you’re not signing up as a current student or alum through a school partnership).

To create an Individual account, you must be at least 18 years old. There is no consent form option for individual student accounts not affiliated with a school — users under 18 are not eligible to create this account type.

For more information about this, refer to our Terms of Service.

Handshake Infrastructure & Data Update (Privacy & Safety)

Migration from EU to US Infrastructure

We’re excited to share that Handshake consolidated into a global platform July 4, 2026. This news means that the network and opportunities are growing for both students and employers! With this, there will be some changes to data storage, as outlined below.

What is changing for EU users?

Handshake transitioned from EU-based data storage to a US-based environment, supported by Handshake’s primary US infrastructure (our global platform). As part of this, EU/UK platform data migrated from Google’s EU region to Google’s US region.

This is primarily a hosting-location change; purposes and legal bases for processing generally remain unchanged, as do data categories, access controls, and security measures on the platform. Note that both Handshake and Google participate in the EU–US Data Privacy Framework. Our Privacy Policy is updated and key details will be communicated if and as required.

Why is Handshake making this shift?

To ensure long-term product stability, higher performance, and alignment with Handshake’s global platform architecture. Centralising infrastructure allows us to:

  • Scale innovation more quickly
  • Maintain a single global codebase
  • Improve reliability, uptime, and security
  • Accelerate AI-powered product development
Is this move compliant with GDPR?

Handshake remains fully committed to GDPR/UK GDPR compliance. Specifically, we will:

  • Rely on approved transfer mechanisms for cross-boarder transfers: EU–US Data Privacy Framework (DPF) participation for certified entities and Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) where required;
  • Maintain lawful bases: Processing purposes, categories, and retention do not change; existing legal bases (e.g., contract/legitimate interests) continue to apply;
  • Apply appropriate technical and organisational measures: Encryption in transit/at rest, access controls, logging/monitoring, and vendor due diligence equivalent to (or stronger than) the current EU setup;
  • Preserve data subject rights: Data subject rights such as access, erasure, etc. remain available via existing channels, and are not impacted by hosting location.
Will this change affect our service or data access?

No service disruption is expected. The transition is designed to be seamless for all partners, with no functional changes to your Handshake instance. Data access and security controls remain unchanged.

Should you have any additional questions or concerns, please contact Support.

Handshake Privacy Policy and TOS Highlights (Students)

Since our founding, Handshake has aimed to incorporate privacy into our platform in a manner that upholds the rights of students, meets the responsibilities of universities, and fulfills the needs of employers.

Our Terms of Service and Privacy Policy are written to enhance the protection of student privacy and to ensure that Handshake remains a valuable platform for all users.

  • Video on Handshake requires employers to inform and obtain consent from job seekers before initiating any type of video recording.

  • To protect the privacy of job seekers, third party recruiters may only use candidate data to market employment opportunities which those candidates have already applied to.

  • We aim for Handshake to be a welcoming platform for everyone, so we expanded our definition of spam to also include messages with a low response rate. As a reminder, these very basic privacy principles guide all of our policies and practices:

  • Students are in control of when they make their profile private

    • Student profiles are set to public by default but can be switched to private by the student at any time.

  • Education partners choose the student data they share with Handshake

    • We value students’ rights to their personal data and are proud to collaborate with our education partners to enhance the value of their career center without compromising student privacy.

  • Handshake will never sell personal student data

    • We have never done it and we never will! Our business model is based on offering valuable tools for our student and employer users that enhance the career discovery process. Your email address and personal data will never be sold to any third party. Please be aware that if you live in the EU or any other regions outside the US and are using the US platform, any information collected through our Service will be transferred and processed in the US or other countries.

While Handshake participates in the EU/US Privacy Shield program, these locations may not have the same data protection laws as the country in which you initially used our services. By using our services, you consent to any transfer and processing in accordance with this Policy.

Handshake SMS & RCS Terms of Service

By opting in to receive text messages from Handshake, you agree to these SMS & RCS Terms of Service (“SMS Terms”). These SMS & RCS Terms supplement, and should be read together with the Handshake Privacy Policy.

Programs you may enroll in

Handshake offers two separate messaging programs. You are only enrolled in a program if you have affirmatively opted in to it. Enrolling in one program does not enroll you in the other.

  • Informational (Transactional) messages: Account and activity-related texts, such as projects seeking your participation, application status updates, interview or event reminders, account alerts, security/verification codes and other messages related to your use of Handshake.
  • Promotional (Marketing) messages: Marketing texts, such as product announcements, new feature updates, surveys and other promotional offers from Handshake.

Message frequency and rates

Message frequency varies depending on your activity and the program(s) you’re enrolled in. Message & data rates may apply.

How to opt out

You can stop receiving text messages from Handshake at any time. Text STOP to the number you received messages from. After you send STOP, we will send you a confirmation message, and you will no longer receive SMS messages from that program. If you are enrolled in both the Informational and Promotional programs, you may need to text STOP separately for each, or as instructed in the confirmation message, since opting out of one program does not automatically opt you out of the other.

Getting help

Text HELP to the number you received messages from for assistance. To contact the Handshake Support team, refer to Contacting Handshake Support.

Changes to these Terms

Handshake may update these SMS Terms from time to time. Continued participation in an SMS program after changes take effect constitutes acceptance of the updated SMS Terms.

Handshake’s Content Policy (Privacy & Safety)

Handshake is committed to keeping our platform safe for all users. Content that falls into the categories below is strictly prohibited and may result in enforcement action.

Important: These policies may evolve over time as our platform grows and as our team’s moderation capabilities expand.

This policy applies to all text, images, audio, and video posted, uploaded, or messages on Handshake, including user profiles, résumés, job postings, video descriptions, comments, reviews, peer messages, and external links (both clickable URLs and references shared verbally in content).

Community Standards

Handshake is a platform for career-related discussion and opportunities. Content should contribute to users’ professional journeys, encourage authentic discourse, and remain respectful.

  • Content not broadly career-related, or lacking context to be informative, may be removed.
  • While political and social issue discussions are prohibited, job postings or discussions about jobs related to political campaigns, elections, or candidates are allowed.
  • Threats or harassment against individuals, groups, or Handshake staff are strictly prohibited—both on and off the platform.

Prohibited Content

The following are broad categories of content that may be removed if we determine they apply, even if not explicitly listed here.

Violent Content

  • Depictions or promotion of physical harm, injury, or violence against individuals, groups, or animals.

  • Content that glorifies or threatens violence. Harassment and Bullying

  • Repeated, harmful, or intentional behavior meant to intimidate, harass, or cause distress.

  • Insults, slurs, or degrading language targeting another person or group.

  • Impersonating someone with the intent to harass, deceive, or harm. Hate Speech

  • Content that discriminates against, degrades, or incites violence or prejudice toward individuals or groups based on protected attributes (race, ethnicity, nationality, religion, gender, sexual orientation, disability, or similar characteristics). Self-Harm

  • Content that promotes, encourages, or depicts self-harm or behaviors that put an individual’s physical or mental well-being at risk, including eating disorders. Sexually Explicit Content

  • Content that explicitly depicts or describes sexual activity, genitalia, or intimate body parts. Harm to Civil Discourse

  • Behaviors or content that disrupt healthy, respectful discussion and undermine a safe community environment.

  • Derailing discussions by posting off-topic, unrelated, or repetitive content that interferes with healthy, respectful conversation. Illegal or Regulated Activities

  • Promotion, facilitation, or engagement in unlawful actions or activities restricted by applicable laws or regulations. Misinformation

  • The spread of false, misleading, or inaccurate information that could cause harm or confusion. Fraud, Scams, and Spam

  • Phishing attempts, malicious links, malware, or other deceptive tactics.

  • Repetitive or irrelevant content, including automated/bot-generated content.

  • Content designed to disrupt discussions or overwhelm the platform.

  • Recruitment content from non-employer accounts may be treated as fraud. Learn How to Spot and Report Scams on Handshake.

Other Restricted Content

Jobs from Unapproved Employers or Recruiters

  • Job postings, internships, or other opportunities from employers or recruiters not verified by Handshake. All employers on Handshake go through a verification process. Learn more about How to Create an Employer Account on Handshake.

Commercial Content

  • Buying or selling of products or services, including fundraisers, ads, or attempts to move users off-platform for transactions.

  • “Get rich quick” schemes or similar solicitations. Content Posted in Bad Faith

  • Content created with the intent to mislead, deceive, or circumvent Handshake policies.

  • Irrelevant or off-topic content unrelated to career development.

Authenticity

We expect users to be truthful about who they are and what they share. Fake or misleading information undermines trust on Handshake and will be removed.

  • You may not use or attempt to use another person’s Handshake account, create a profile for someone else, or share your account credentials.
  • Any attempt to buy or sell Handshake accounts will be reported to relevant law enforcement agencies.
  • Custom URLs must represent you or your business. We may revoke URLs that belong to registered trademarks.
  • You may not post or share false or misleading information, including fabricated credentials, achievements, or job opportunities.
  • You may not impersonate another individual, business, or organization, or misrepresent your affiliation with them.

Enforcement

If your content violates this policy or our Terms of Service, it may be removed. You will be notified by email, and in some cases, your school or employer partners may also be informed.

Consequences for violations may include:

  • Warnings

  • Account limitations

  • Temporary suspension

  • Permanent removal from the platform For certain types of violations, Handshake may restrict your account for the duration of an investigation. In these cases, your account will remain restricted until the investigation is complete and a final decision is reached. Some investigations may also require user action prior to accounts being reinstated. User action may include:

  • Email responses to Trust & Safety outreach

  • Supplemental account verification through Persona or phone

Reporting

If you come across content that violates this policy, please report it to our team by flagging the content in Handshake.

For more on how to flag content and details on how we moderate, refer to How Handshake Moderates Content on the Home Feed.

How do employers get approved at my school?

Employer approval depends on your school’s partnership with Handshake. Partnered schools manage their own employer approval processes based on their institutional policies and settings, while non‑partnered schools follow Handshake’s Open Network safeguards and validation requirements.

Check out the expandable headers below for more information!

If your school has partnered with Handshake

Schools that have partnered with Handshake manage their own approval processes. Your career services office may handle individual employer approvals, use job-based approvals, and/or apply optional auto-approval settings. The specific approval procedures vary by school.

For more information on how your school approves employers, we recommend reaching out to your Career Services office.

Additionally, your school may choose to feature approved employers (along with jobs, events, and career fairs) in curated categories called Career Center Collections. To learn more about these, refer to Career Center Collections at your School.

If your school has not yet partnered with Handshake

If your school has not yet partnered with Handshake and you’re part of the Handshake Open Network, employers are first validated by Handshake before they can recruit. We use a combination of automated fraud‑prevention technology and manual review by our Trust & Safety team to confirm that employers meet our platform standards. Employers that pass this validation and meet activity requirements can connect with students in the Handshake Open Network.

Once employers are approved to connect with your school or the Handshake Open Network, they can engage with you in various ways on the platform. To learn more about this, refer to Employer Interactions with Students.

These interactions depend on your privacy settings and your engagement with the employer (e.g., applying for a posted job). For more information on privacy settings, refer to Profile Privacy Options in Handshake.

While approval to recruit at your school or on the Handshake Open Network allows an employer to connect with students, it does not guarantee the employer’s legitimacy. We strongly encourage you to remain cautious and vigilant throughout your career exploration process. For tips on staying safe, check out Safety: Best Practices for Job Searches.

How Handshake Moderates Content on the Feed

The Handshake home feed offers a welcoming and engaging platform for individuals wanting to gain knowledge about various job opportunities, career options, networking, and other prospects. Our goal is to provide you with a source of joy and amusement while navigating your academic and professional journeys.

💡Note: as we continue to build the Handshake home feed, it is essential to establish guidelines. These guidelines will aid our team in being responsive on the platform and allow our users to concentrate on their main goal with Handshake - advancing in their professional journey.

To learn more about Handshake’s Content Policy, prohibited content, and the actions taken if content is violated, refer to Handshake’s Content Policy.

Topics:

  • How content on Handshake is moderated
  • What happens to flagged content?
  • How users can flag content
  • Is there an appeal process for those that violate the policy?

How content on Handshake is moderated

Handshake uses both content moderation technology and human moderators to monitor all content posted to the home feed. Content is assessed for compliance with our Content Policy and Terms of Service. Any content determined to violate our Policy and Terms will be removed.

What happens to flagged content?

When content is flagged, it is sent to our Trust & Safety team to review. Once the review is completed, Handshake may choose to remove the content or take other disciplinary action against the offender, including issuing a warning, an account limitation, suspension, or a user’s permanent removal from the platform.

How users can flag content

Users can flag content they believe to be inappropriate or in violation of our Content Policy or Terms of Service. Our Trust & Safety team will review the flagged content.

Content may be flagged directly from your web browser or mobile app.

To flag content, click the three dots located in the upper-right corner of the post, then click Report this… from the dropdown.

In the pop-up that appears, choose the most relevant reason as to why you’re reporting the content:

  • It’s spam or a scam
  • It’s inappropriate
  • It’s abusive or threatening
  • Something else Once a selection is made on your mobile device, the flag is sent to our team. To submit your flag via your web browser, click the black button Submit.

Is there an appeal process for those that violate the policy?

If you believe your content was mistakenly removed, please respond to the removal email and someone from our Trust & Safety team will get back to you.
