How to Spot and Report Scams on Handshake

Your safety is our top priority. While we work hard to keep Handshake secure, scammers may still attempt to contact students or employers. Below are tips to help you identify common scams and steps to report them to our Trust & Safety team.

How to Recognize Common Types of Scams

The goal of most scams is to extract money, sensitive information, or credentials from people. The methods used to do this vary but here are some of the most common types of scams.

Fake Job Leads

Typical format: A scammer may contact you claiming their company is hiring and ask you to email them if interested. These messages may even use the name of a real company. They may set up a fake interview or phone call, followed by a request to complete a fraudulent job application or share personal information. Some scammers may also contact you outside of Handshake, claiming they found your profile even though you didn’t apply to their company.

How to identify:

  • Attempts or requests to move the conversation off Handshake – asking you to share your resume or other personal information via email, URL link, WhatsApp, or phone (text or call).
  • Too good to be true offers – promises of jobs or interviews offering unusually high pay for little work, or attempts to bypass a formal job application process.
  • Spelling errors, grammatical errors, or the use of informal language - reputable businesses create messages that have been edited for spelling and grammatical errors and generally do not include emojis.
  • Requests for sensitive information - legitimate employers will never ask for your Social Security Number, bank account details, credit card numbers, or password via messages, email, URL links, WhatApp or phone.

Impersonations

Typical format: Scammers may impersonate Handshake, a school, or an employer. These messages often claim that you must take urgent action on your account and provide a link to click. The link will then attempt to collect personal or financial information.

How to identify:

  • Suspicious links – links that don’t match Handshake’s official domain, look unusual, or are shortened (e.g., “low-priority.com” instead of a valid Handshake URL). Some may ask you to copy and paste the link into your browser.
  • Spelling errors, grammatical errors, or the use of informal language - when asking you to take an account action, reputable schools and businesses create messages that have been edited for spelling and grammatical errors and generally do not include emojis.
  • Handshake student accounts - Handshake has a limited number of official accounts, all registered as employer accounts. Any other message, account, or post claiming to be from “Handshake Support” or “the Handshake Team” should be considered fraudulent and reported. Handshake does not use in-app messages or feed posts to share important account information—we will always contact you by email from an official joinhandshake.com address. Handshake does not send text messages, voice notes, Whatsapp message or any other communications to your personal phone number.
  • Urgent or fear-based language – messages pressuring you to act immediately (“Your account will be suspended if you don’t click now”).
  • Requests for sensitive information – legitimate employers, career services, and Handshake staff will never ask for your Social Security Number, bank account details, credit card numbers, or passwords via messages, email, URL links, WhatsApp, or phone.

What to Do If You Suspect a Scam

  • Do not click links or share personal information.
  • Report it to our Trust & Safety team by using the “Report” button directly within your message inbox. To learn more about this process, refer to Safety: Report a Message. If something feels off—pause before clicking, sharing, or replying. It’s always better to double-check than to risk exposing your personal information.

How We Protect You

  • We actively monitor and remove scam accounts.
  • Our detection systems flag suspicious activity to help protect students and employers.
  • Reported scams are investigated by our Trust & Safety team, and action is taken quickly.
  • We analyze scam content and behavior patterns to continuously improve our detection systems.

Opt-out of Sharing Data in Handshake

To prevent your data from being shared with employers, you can set your profile to “private” in Handshake. To learn more about how to change your privacy settings as well as your privacy options, check out Profile Privacy Option in Handshake.

You may also contact your school’s Career Center and opt out of sharing your Directory Information. Many of our partner schools sync this information to help students get started and keep data up to date. Read more on opting-out and its impact in Opting Out of Directory Information and the Impact to Handshake.

If you are no longer a student, we can deactivate your account upon request. But note that this will prevent employers from contacting you about future job opportunities.

If you prefer to fully delete your account, reach out to your Career Center to ensure your information will not be re-uploaded during future student data syncs. Either your Career Center or our Support Team can assist you with the account deletion.

Opting Out of Directory Information and the Impact to Handshake

I opted out of Directory Information sharing with my school. How does this impact my use of Handshake?

We respect your decision to opt out of directory information sharing. Our system is designed to support students who prefer not to share their basic information with others

As an administrative platform for career center partners, Handshake receives certain information from your school to help your career center perform its functions. Rest assured, we do not share this information with third parties, including employers, unless you give us explicit permission to do so. You can learn more about Profile Privacy Options in Handshake in Profile Privacy Options in Handshake.

You will still be able to use Handshake to schedule appointments and sign up for career fairs. However, employers and recruiters will not be able to view your profile or contact you when searching for candidates.

Please note, when you apply for jobs through Handshake, employers will have access to any information you provide in your resume or application

Profile Privacy Options in Handshake

Handshake provides three profile privacy options for student accounts: Community, Employers, and Private.

If your institution is partnered with Handshake and created you an account on your behalf, the account privacy is automatically set to Private, meaning it is not visible to any employers or peers.

If you have created your own account, or when you activate an account created for you, you have the option to update your privacy settings and choose if you want to make it public when you first log in.

To learn more about public profiles on Handshake, check out How to Make Your Handshake Profile Public and Share Your Profile Link.

To change your privacy settings in Handshake, check out How to Change Your Student Profile Privacy Setting.

Regardless of who created your account, if your institution is partnered with Handshake, members of your institution’s career services team (with a Handshake account) can view your profile, even if it’s set to private. However, they cannot change your privacy settings—only you have the ability to update them.

Topics:

  • What does each profile privacy option allow me to do?
    • Community
    • Employers
    • Private

What does each profile privacy option allow me to do?

Most features on Handshake—such as applying to jobs, registering for in-person events or career fairs, and scheduling appointments—are available regardless of your profile visibility settings.

However, some features require selecting either the Employers or Community visibility option. These include participating in virtual 1:1 or group sessions, attending virtual events, posting on the feed and connecting with peers through campus profiles and messaging.

If you choose Community or Employers, we recommend completing your profile to get the most out of your experience. A well-filled-out profile supports more meaningful and relevant interactions!

💡Note: your GPA is never visible to other student or alumni accounts, and your GPA will only be visible to employers if you expressly opt in to sharing. You can adjust this setting in the Education section of your profile. For step-by-step instructions, refer to How to Edit Education Information on Your Profile.

Community

The Community option is the most comprehensive privacy setting in Handshake, providing access to all available features and interactions. If you select this option, you won’t be prompted to change your privacy settings when taking any action on the platform.

With the Community option enabled, you can:

  • Post to the feed
  • Message students and alumni
  • Receive messages from employers about job opportunities
  • Browse jobs and other resources from Handshake and your institution
  • Make your profile visible to employers, students, and alumni across all Handshake institutions
  • Share a public link to your profile so others can view it outside of the platform Virtual Events & Fairs

Virtual events and group sessions within virtual fairs require the Community setting, since they involve interaction with both employers and other students.

These events are designed to mirror the in-person experience, with features such as participant lists, chat functionality, and visible speakers (either employer hosts or students using video/audio).

If your profile is already set to Community, you can register for virtual events and fairs without any additional changes. However, if your privacy setting is set to Employers or Private, you’ll be prompted to update it to Community before signing up for a virtual event or group session.

Employers

With the Employers option enabled:

  • You can’t post to the feed
  • You cannot message students or alumni
  • You can receive messages from potential employers about job opportunities
  • You can browse jobs and other resources from Handshake and your institution
  • Your profile is visible to employers only If you prefer not to have your profile visible to other students or alumni, the Employers privacy setting is a good choice. This option allows employers to discover your profile, message you, and invite you to apply for jobs.

Virtual Events & Fairs

You can register for virtual events hosted outside of Handshake (e.g., on Zoom or another platform). You can also sign up for 1:1 sessions with employers during virtual fairs hosted in Handshake (one recruiter and one student)

However, if you’d like to attend group sessions or register for virtual events hosted within Handshake, you’ll be prompted to switch your privacy setting to Community to proceed.

Private

With the Private option enabled:

  • You can’t post to the feed
  • You cannot message students and alumni
  • You cannot receive messages about job opportunities from potential employers
  • You can browse jobs and other resources from Handshake or your institution
  • Your profile will not be visible to the employers you apply for jobs to If you choose to keep your profile Private, you can search for and apply for jobs, register for in-person events and fairs, and explore career paths. If your institution is partnered with Handshake, you can interact with your Career Center via appointments, experiences, surveys, First Destination Surveys, and institution posted resources.

Prompts to Update Your Privacy Setting in Handshake

During onboarding: As part of the onboarding process, you’ll be prompted to select your profile visibility setting. Each privacy option is explained in detail, so you can make an informed choice about how your profile is shared on Handshake

Virtual fair session signup: When signing up for a virtual fair session that requires a privacy setting change, Handshake will prompt you to update your visibility.

The message will read:“In order to participate in a virtual career fair on Handshake, you will need to change your visibility.”

The prompt will show your current profile visibility and outline the required setting based on the type of session:

  • Community – Required to participate in group sessions
  • Employers – Required to participate in 1-on-1 sessions with employers This ensures you’re set up to fully engage in the virtual fair experience.

Virtual event registration prompt: When registering for a virtual event in Handshake, you may be prompted to update your profile visibility depending on how the event is hosted:

  • Events hosted outside of Handshake (e.g., via Zoom):
  • The minimum required privacy setting is Employers.
    • If your profile is set to Private, you’ll be prompted to update it.
    • If you’re already set to Employers or Community, you can register as usual.
  • Events hosted within Handshake (using Handshake’s video platform):
  • The required privacy setting is Community.
    • If your profile is set to Private or Employers, you’ll be prompted to update it.
    • If you’re already set to Community, you can register without making changes. The prompt you’ll receive includes the following message: “In order to participate in a virtual event on Handshake, you will need to change your visibility.”

It will also display your current privacy setting along with the required option and its purpose:

  • Community – Required for virtual sessions hosted on Handshake
  • Employers – Required for virtual sessions hosted externally with employer participation

Safety: Best Practices for Job Searches

When searching for a new job or internship, following the best practices outlined below can help you identify the best opportunities for you!

Before you apply to a job or internship posting

  1. Research the Company and Recruiter. Start by visiting the company’s website to learn about their culture, values, and business model to ensure they align with your goals. If the website lists staff members, try to identify the recruiter mentioned in the job posting.

  2. Review the Job Posting Details. Knowing the details is key. For example, where is the job’s location? Does it match the company’s address or operations? Are the responsibilities clearly outlined, and do the requirements align with your skills? If the salary is listed, does it match industry standards for the role?

If you happen to view any jobs posted on Handshake that are sub-standard, or if the salary is much higher than the average known salary for that role, feel free to flag it so our Trust & Safety team can validate the posting. For more information on flagging an employer, refer to Safety: Flagging an Employer on Handshake.

  1. Update your resume and write a cover letter. Ensure your resume is up to date and tailored to the job you’re applying for. For tips, check out our student blog How to Create a Student or New Grad Resume. For personalized advice, we recommend connecting with your school’s Career Center.

Before you accept an offer

  1. Interview with the employer. A legitimate employer will typically require one or more interviews. Be sure to speak with a trusted person about your experience with the company and keep copies of all communication. Never accept a job offer without an interview, especially if the employer is pressuring you to accept quickly or offering a role you didn’t apply for.

  2. Clarify salary and pay frequency. Make sure the employer confirms your salary and the frequency of payments. You should not be asked to deposit or cash a company check before you start working.

  3. Understand the role and expectations. Ensure the employer has clearly outlined your job responsibilities, work schedule, and expected time commitment. It’s important to know exactly what to expect when you start the role.

Red flags to watch out for

Pay attention not only to the job description but also to how the employer interacts with you. Here are some red flags to be aware of:

  • Untraceable Contact Information: The employer calls you from a blocked number or one that can’t be returned.
  • Suspicious Email Offers: The employer contacts you directly by email offering a job you didn’t apply for or inviting you to apply for a job that isn’t posted on a reputable site.
    • Tip: Check the sender’s email address for unusual domains, such as @live.com or other domains not affiliated with the company.
  • Request to Cash or Deposit Checks: You’re asked to cash or deposit a check on behalf of someone else, return a portion of the money, and keep the remainder.

Additional Resources

  • Common Scams & Frauds:usa.gov
  • Report Scams & Frauds:usa.gov
  • Handshake’s Student Blog - Top 100 companies hiring students on Handshake right now
    • Free Resume Template for Students and New Grads
    • Free Cover Letter Template for Students and New Grads

Safety: Flagging an Employer on Handshake

If you come across an employer that raises concerns, you can notify our Trust and Safety team by flagging or reporting the employer in Handshake using your web browser (on desktop or mobile) or the Handshake mobile app.

Employers will not be notified when a flag is submitted for review. If a job or user is suspended following the review, the employer will receive a notification detailing the suspension and the specific Terms of Service violation that led to it.

Flagging an employer

On web, employers can be flagged via two ways on Handshake:

  • The Employer’s Company Profile by clicking Flag this Employer for abuse, located in the lower-left corner of the page.
  • The employer’s Job Posting by clicking the three dots menu, located to the right of the Apply button, then clicking Flag or report employer. On the Handshake mobile app, employers can be flagged via the Job Posting, by clicking the three dots menu in the upper-right corner, then clicking Report employer.

In the popup that appears, choose all the reasons that apply:

  • Fake or fraudulent employer
    • Ex: this employer or job is fake or misrepresenting itself
  • Scam, phishing, or malware
    • Ex: this employer or job is a scam, asking for private personal information or posting suspicious links
  • Advertising or promotional content
    • Ex: this employer or job is for something other than hiring
  • Discriminatory practices
    • Ex: this employer is discriminating against me
  • Offensive, abusive, or harmful conduct
    • Ex: this employer offers a negative hiring experience, abusive work environment or is harassing students
  • Exploitative, unethical, or illegal practices
    • Ex: this employer is operating in an illegal or unethical manner
  • Adult content
    • Ex: this employer or job post promotes nudity, sexual scenes and/or adult language Once selected, describe the situation in the text box. Include all relevant details when submitting a flag to our Trust and Safety team.

Click the button Submit feedback in the lower-right corner to send the flag to our Trust and Safety team.

Review and moderation process

Once a flag is submitted, our Trust and Safety team will begin the review within one hour, with a maximum time frame of 1-2 business days. The exact duration may vary depending on the severity of the issue and whether the flag is submitted during our business hours (5am - 5pm PST).

Safety: Protecting Your Personal Information

While searching for a job, it’s crucial to safeguard your personal information from potential scams and fraudulent employers, and even more important to know what steps to take if your information has been compromised.

If you’ve accidentally given personal information to a fraudulent contact or suspect your personal information has been compromised, it’s important to act quickly.

Here are the steps you should take right away:

  • Contact your bank or credit card company. If you’ve shared any financial details or sent money to a fraudulent employer. They can help protect your accounts and dispute any unauthorized transactions.
  • Secure your accounts. Change passwords on any accounts that may have been compromised, and double-check that account settings and payment details look as expected.
  • Flag the employer. If they’re on Handshake, flagging the employer automatically alerts our Trust & Safety team so they can investigate and take appropriate action. For more information, refer to Safety: Flagging an Employer on Handshake.
  • File a report with the Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3). If you’ve encountered a scam involving our business or been a victim of online fraud, report it to the FBI’s Internet Crime Complaint Center at ic3.gov by clicking “File a Complaint” and providing your contact details, a description of the scam, any financial losses, and supporting evidence (screenshots, emails, links). Be sure to note if the scammer impersonated our name, logo, or website.

Safety: Report a Message

Handshake’s top priority is ensuring students’ safety on the platform. When you receive messages, you have the option to report any employer messages that violate our guidelines, such as spam or messages that appear fake or fraudulent.

Reporting a message allows our Trust and Safety team to proactively review the issue and take appropriate action if needed.

Keep in mind that this safety feature is only available within Handshake—if messages are exchanged outside the platform, this protection is lost. We recommend using Handshake’s messaging feature to build secure relationships with employers!

Report a message

  1. From the message in your inbox, click the three dots menu in the upper-right corner of the messaging window, then click Report Message from the dropdown.

  2. Choose why you are reporting the message by selecting the radio button, located to the left of the reason:

  • This employer appears to be fake or fraudulent
    • if selected, please describe the situation by typing in the provided text box.
  • This employer is spamming me
  1. Click the blue button Submit to send your report to our Trust and Safety team for review.

Reporting a message will stop the other person from messaging you. The conversation will then be reviewed and moderated by Handshake. Your school may also be looped in if appropriate.

Understanding Cloudflare Security Checks on Handshake (Privacy & Safety)

To help protect the Handshake platform from bots and malicious activity, Handshake uses Cloudflare, a trusted security service that detects suspicious behavior.

This added protection helps ensure a safe and reliable experience for all users, including students, employers, and career services staff.

Why does Handshake use Cloudflare?

Cloudflare helps Handshake:

  • Prevent the creation of fake or automated accounts
  • Block bots from misusing the app or website These measures are part of ongoing efforts to keep the platform safe for real users.

What you might experience

Most users will not notice any change. However, in rare cases, you may encounter a brief Cloudflare verification screen when:

  • Creating a new Handshake account
  • Logging in or using the Handshake mobile app The screen typically disappears within a few seconds, and no action is required.

If you receive a checkbox confirming you’re a human, check the box and you will be redirected back to Handshake automatically.

If the check does not complete, or the page does not recognize your action, you’ll remain on the Cloudflare page instead of being returned to Handshake.

Troubleshooting steps

If the verification screen does not go away or seems to repeat:

  • Refresh your browser or restart the app.
  • Ensure your browser is up to date and that JavaScript is enabled.
  • Disable any browser extensions, such as ad blockers, or try using an incognito or private browsing window. For more troubleshooting help, refer to Cloudfare Docs: Challenge solve issues.

Understanding Document Visibility

Handshake allows you to upload multiple documents to support your job search, such as resumes, cover letters, and transcripts. While you may have several documents in your account, only one document can be designated as public at a time. Understanding how document visibility works will help you control what employers can access and when.

For steps on how to upload a document in Handshake, check out How to Upload a New Document.

Visibile to employers

A document is considered public when its visibility is selected as Visible to employers in Handshake. You can select this option during the upload process, when applying for a job, or update it later within the document’s Action settings.

Public documents are visible to employers in the following situations:

  • When you apply for a job with them

  • When you sign up for a virtual fair session they are hosting

  • When you register for an event hosted by them Public documents may also be included when employers download resumes from:

  • Virtual fair RSVP lists

  • Bulk resume downloads Public documents are not displayed directly on your profile for general browsing. Employers and other users cannot view your resume simply by visiting your profile. Access is limited to the specific interactions listed above.

Additionally, Career Services staff at your institution, with the appropriate permissions, can view all documents in your account regardless of their visibility settings.

Private documents

Private documents are those that are not marked as Visible to employers.

These documents:

  • Can only be attached to specific job applications
  • Are visible only to the employer receiving that application and your school’s Career Services Center
  • Are not accessible to other employers or users on Handshake

Update document visibility

To change a document’s visibility:

  • Click your account icon in the upper-right corner of Handshake
  • Select Documents from the dropdown menu
  • Click the document you want to update
  • Click Actions in the upper-right corner, then select Edit from the dropdown menu
  • Check the box next to Visible to employers to make the document public, or uncheck it to make it private
  • Click the button Save to update Note: If you are registered for a virtual fair, Handshake will prompt you to confirm which document you want to make visible to employers when you sign up for your first employer session. Employers can only download resumes from RSVP lists if the document is marked as visible to employers.

Why am I getting an error “You do not have permission to do that”? (for Students)

If you encounter an error that says “You do not have permission to do that”, this indicates you do not have the necessary permission to access the particular page or complete the task in Handshake.

For students, this error could appear if you’re:

  • Using a link for an event or fair that is invite-only, and you’ve not been invited
  • Trying to load a job posting that hasn’t been approved at your school
  • Trying to load a job posting that was approved at your school, but has expired Note: These are the most common reasons for this error, but other situations may also result in the error. In all cases, the item is restricted from your view.

What to do if you encounter this message

If your school has partnered with Handshake: reach out to your Career Center for more information about the error. To find your school’s contact details, refer to How to Locate your School’s Contact Information in Handshake.

If your school has not yet partnered with Handshake: contact our Support team for assistance.

Privacy & Security

Handshake Infrastructure & Data Update (Privacy & Security)

Migration from EU to US Infrastructure

We’re excited to share that Handshake consolidated into a global platform July 4, 2026. This news means that the network and opportunities are growing for both students and employers! With this, there will be some changes to data storage, as outlined below.

What is changing for EU users?

Handshake transitioned from EU-based data storage to a US-based environment, supported by Handshake’s primary US infrastructure (our global platform). As part of this, EU/UK platform data migrated from Google’s EU region to Google’s US region.

This is primarily a hosting-location change; purposes and legal bases for processing generally remain unchanged, as do data categories, access controls, and security measures on the platform. Note that both Handshake and Google participate in the EU–US Data Privacy Framework. Our Privacy Policy is updated and key details will be communicated if and as required.

Why is Handshake making this shift?

To ensure long-term product stability, higher performance, and alignment with Handshake’s global platform architecture. Centralising infrastructure allows us to:

  • Scale innovation more quickly
  • Maintain a single global codebase
  • Improve reliability, uptime, and security
  • Accelerate AI-powered product development
Is this move compliant with GDPR?

Handshake remains fully committed to GDPR/UK GDPR compliance. Specifically, we will:

  • Rely on approved transfer mechanisms for cross-boarder transfers: EU–US Data Privacy Framework (DPF) participation for certified entities and Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) where required;
  • Maintain lawful bases: Processing purposes, categories, and retention do not change; existing legal bases (e.g., contract/legitimate interests) continue to apply;
  • Apply appropriate technical and organisational measures: Encryption in transit/at rest, access controls, logging/monitoring, and vendor due diligence equivalent to (or stronger than) the current EU setup;
  • Preserve data subject rights: Data subject rights such as access, erasure, etc. remain available via existing channels, and are not impacted by hosting location.
Will this change affect our service or data access?

No service disruption is expected. The transition is designed to be seamless for all partners, with no functional changes to your Handshake instance. Data access and security controls remain unchanged.

Should you have any additional questions or concerns, please contact Support.

Handshake Privacy Policy and TOS Highlights (Employers)

Since our founding, Handshake has aimed to incorporate privacy into our platform in a manner that upholds the rights of students, meets the responsibilities of universities, and fulfills the needs of employers.

Our Terms of Service and Privacy Policy are written to enhance the protection of student privacy and to ensure that Handshake remains a valuable platform for all users.

  • Video on Handshake requires employers to inform and obtain consent from job seekers before initiating any type of video recording.

  • To protect the privacy of job seekers, third party recruiters may only use candidate data to market employment opportunities which those candidates have already applied to.

  • We aim for Handshake to be a welcoming platform for everyone, so we expanded our definition of spam to also include messages with a low response rate. As a reminder, these very basic privacy principles guide all of our policies and practices:

  • Students are in control of when they make their profile private

    • Student profiles are set to public by default but can be switched to private by the student at any time.

  • Education partners choose the student data they share with Handshake

    • We value students’ rights to their personal data and are proud to collaborate with our education partners to enhance the value of their career center without compromising student privacy.

  • Handshake will never sell personal student data

    • We have never done it and we never will! Our business model is based on offering valuable tools for our student and employer users that enhance the career discovery process. Your email address and personal data will never be sold to any third party. Please be aware that if you live in the EU or any other regions outside the US and are using the US platform, any information collected through our Service will be transferred and processed in the US or other countries.

While Handshake participates in the EU/US Privacy Shield program, these locations may not have the same data protection laws as the country in which you initially used our services. By using our services, you consent to any transfer and processing in accordance with this Policy.

Reporting Duplicate, Spam, or Suspicious Activity in your Employer Account

As an employer account owner, you may occasionally notice suspicious activity in your company profile. This could include duplicate job postings, spam job or event creations, or activity from users who should not have access.

Types of activity to watch for

  • Duplicate job postings
  • The same job may appear more than once if a connected teammate also created it.
  • Spam job or event creations
  • Examples include:
    • Jobs or events that don’t represent your company
    • Irrelevant or inappropriate content (e.g., scam jobs, non-career-related events)
    • Jobs or events created by teammates without your prior approval
  • Malicious or unauthorized users
  • A user appears to be posting jobs or events on behalf of your company without approval.

Deciding what action to take

  • If you know the teammate and the posting is intentional, no action is needed.
  • If the posting looks suspicious, irrelevant, or was not created by your team, you should report it to Handshake Support. Tip: If you’re unsure whether a job or event was created by your team, check with your teammates first. If no one recognizes it, contact Support.

What you should do

  • If you are a Basic employer Owner
  • Basic Owners cannot close jobs or cancel events created by other teammates, or deactivate teammates directly. If you notice suspicious activity, contact Support.
  • If you are on another employer account type (On-campus employer, Essentials, Enterprise)
  • Teammates with the appropriate permissions can take direct actions such as closing jobs or canceling events, while only Owners and Admins can deactivate teammates. Report any suspicious activity to Support so the team can investigate and ensure your account remains secure.

Staying informed

To stay informed about activity in your employer account, owners can keep their notification settings turned on.

Notifications include alerts when:

  • A new teammate needs approval
  • A teammate posts a job to a school where you recruit
  • A teammate creates an event at one of your favorite schools Review your Default Notification Preferences (Employers).

Safety: Login From a New Device Notification

Your safety on Handshake is our highest priority. To protect your account, we will notify you of any unusual login attempts.

We monitor your IP address, device, operating system, and browser version each time you log in. If any of these details change during your next login, such as a different device, browser, or IP address, we will send an email alert to your registered email address.

The email will read:

Subject: New Handshake Sign-In Detected

Body:

“Hi [name],

We detected an unfamiliar sign-in to your Handshake account near [location - city, country].

If this was you, no action is needed.

If you don’t recognize the sign-in and believe someone else may have accessed your account, please change your password now [link].

Thanks,

Handshake Trust and Safety

Handshake will never ask for sign-in credentials or personal payment through email. If you receive an email requesting these or containing unusual phrases, spelling, or grammar, please don’t click on any links or reply. Forward any suspicious emails to phishing@joinhandshake.com.”

What happens if I’m tagged or flagged?

Our educational partners may tag or flag employers on Handshake if they do not align with a school’s moral, ethical, or legal standards.

Each school sets its own criteria for tagging or flagging employers. These criteria may vary based on factors such as the employer’s industry, business practices, or violations of Handshake’s Terms of Service or policies.

Are you new to Handshake? Learn more about our Employer Validation.

Employer tags

Employer tags are a community-driven resource that help our educational partners identify and filter employers that do not align with their institution’s standards or policies.

  • Tags are only visible to institutions and are not displayed to students or employers.
  • Tags are reviewed by Handshake’s Trust and Safety team, who confirm or deny them based on the school’s submission.

Employer flags

Employer flags allow schools and students to report potential fraud, abuse, or violations involving a company, user, or job posting on Handshake.

Flags remain in a pending status while reviewed by the Trust and Safety team. If needed, employers may be asked to provide additional information or documentation.

  • If confirmed, the flag will be applied, and users impacted by the flagged activity will be notified.
  • If dismissed, the flag will not affect the employer, and no action will be taken. Employers who violate Handshake’s Terms of Service may face the suspension of their company account, or specific users or job postings may be suspended.

Support

If your company is notified of a tag that you believe is incorrect, contact Support.

Why am I getting an error “You do not have permission to do that”? (for Employers)

This error occurs when your role, permissions, or account type in Handshake restricts access to a specific page or task.

Check your role and access level

Roles such as Advocate, Recruiter, or Admin determine your permissions in Handshake. Ensure your role is appropriate for the action you’re trying to complete.

For more information on role-specific access, refer to our Guide to Employer Role Types in Handshake.

Confirm your permissions are enabled

Even if your role is correct, certain permissions may not be enabled for your account. Contact your company’s Owner in Handshake to request the necessary access.

For help identifying your company profile Owner, visit Who Is the Owner or Admin of My Company Profile?.

Ensure you’re using the correct account type

Another possible cause of this error is registering with the wrong account type. If you accidentally signed up as a student instead of an employer, you will need to create a new account using the employer registration process.

For guided steps, visit How to Create an Employer Account on Handshake.

Verify which company profile you’re connected with

If you are connected with a company profile in Handshake, you can only view content and activity for that specific company. You will not be able to access or view information from other company profiles, such as their posted jobs, created events, or fair registrations.

To confirm which company profile you are connected with, click Brand page from the left navigation bar. The Brand page will display the name of your connected company, including its location.

If you need to disconnect from your current company profile and connect to a different one, visit Leaving a Company in Handshake.

On-campus employer designation

If you are an on-campus employer and are receiving this error when trying to manage jobs, review applicants, or download applicant data created by teammates, you may not have been designated as an on-campus employer by your company profile Owner.

This designation is required to manage jobs and other content created by yourself and teammates on Handshake. Contact your company profile Owner to request the designation.

For more information, visit Identifying as an On-Campus Employer on Handshake.

Profile

Build Profile from Resume

Because of the student profile changes on Handshake, our team will be refocusing on this feature in the future.

As a result, the option to “Build profile from resume” has been removed.

Completing your Profile in Handshake

Filling out your Handshake profile—especially getting it to 100% complete—is one of the most important steps you can take in your job search. A complete profile helps Handshake tailor job and internship recommendations to your interests, skills, and experience so you receive more relevant opportunities. It also makes you more visible and appealing to employers, increasing the chances they’ll reach out with job offers, interview requests, or invitations to events that match your background and goals.

Employers can view your profile only if you’ve set your profile visibility to “Community” or “Employers.” Students and alumni can only view your profile if you’ve set your profile to “Community.” To learn more about your profile privacy options, refer to Profile Privacy Options in Handshake.

To fully complete your profile in Handshake, you’ll want to add the following information:

  • Looking for
  • Summary
  • Skills
  • Work experience
  • Education
  • Courses
  • Organizations
  • Projects
  • Languages
  • Profile Picture
  • General information To update this info, click on your icon in the upper-right corner then select My Profile.

For more details on profile insights, refer to Profile Insights: Track Views and Engagement.

Looking for

The “Looking for” section on your profile is designed to help specify what types of opportunities you are seeking.

This can include job roles, industries, locations, and other preferences. By filling out this section, you can receive more personalized job recommendations and increase your visibility to employers who are looking for candidates with specific interests and qualifications.

💡Note: depending on your profile visibility, this section is displayed on your profile if at least one prompt is filled out.

Click the pencil icon, located to the right of Looking for — then fill in the desired information within the pop-up.

  • What are you looking for right now? (Select one)
    • Full-time job
    • Part-time job
    • Internship
    • Campus job
    • Networking and inspiration
  • Roles (click in the search bar and begin typing to produce results in the dropdown)
  • Industries (click in the search bar and begin typing to produce results in the dropdown)
  • Locations (click in the search bar and begin typing to produce results in the dropdown) Once everything is added, click the button Save to update!

Summary

This section offers you the opportunity to add a personal bio to your profile.

Click the + icon, located to the right of Summary — then type your bio in the pop-up that appears.

💡Note: there’s a 300 character limit.

🚀Tip: if you’re not sure what to include, we recommend topics such as what you’re passionate about, what you’re looking for on Handshake, and any experiences or skills you want to highlight!

Once the information is added, click the button Save to update or the button Cancel to cancel!

Skills

Add technical skills (like SQL) along with soft skills (like communication). The more skills you list, the better your chances are of showing up in an employer search!

Click the + icon, located to the right of Skills.

In the pop-up that appears, type in a skill you would like to add to your profile in the search box. The dropdown will produce results based on your search — click on the skill to add it. We recommend 10 or less.

💡Note: when you click in the search box, the results will display up to 25 available skills to add — These are listed in alphabetical order. To find a certain skill, continue typing in the search box to produce the desired result.

Once all of your skills are added, click the button Save to add or the button Cancel to cancel!

Work experience

Have you had a part-time job, internship, work study, research position, or volunteered? If so, employers like to know that you’ve taken on the responsibility, and value these experiences as they’ve helped you develop skills!

Click the + icon, located to the right of Work experience.

Within the pop-up, enter the following details:

  • Employer name
  • Job title
  • Job type (select)
    • Full-time
    • Part-time
    • Internship
    • On-campus
    • Fellowship
    • Co-op
    • Other
  • Current working here (check box if you’re still in the role)
  • Time Period
    • Start Date (Months and Year)
    • End Date (Month and year)
  • Location
  • Description
  • Did you use Handshake to get this job? Show it off! (check box) Click the button Save to add the information to your profile or the button Cancel to cancel!

To add more work experiences, continue clicking the + icon and following the steps above!

Education

The Education section is intended to reflect the school you’re currently affiliated with, along with other schools you may have attended in the past.

  • If your school has pre-created a profile for you, your Education will already be added to your profile.
  • If you created an account yourself, your Education will be pre-filled with the school you associated yourself with during the creation process. To change or update your major, refer to If Your Major (or Minor) is Missing or Incorrect.

To update your Primary Education, refer to Managing Primary Education.

Courses

Add courses you’ve taken to your profile to express the skills developed throughout your learnings.

Click on the + icon, located to the right of Courses.

In the pop-up that appears, enter the Course Name and Code (if applicable) - Check the box if you are/were a TA or Course reader, then click the button Save to add to your profile or the button Cancel to cancel.

To remove a course, click the trashcan icon, located to the right of the course.

To add more courses, continue clicking the + icon and following the steps above!

Organizations

These signal your specific interests, affinity groups, and participation and involvement on campus.

Click on the + icon, located to the right of Organizations.

Within the pop-up, enter the following details:

  • Organization
  • Position (check box if you’re still in the role)
  • Time Period
    • Start Date (Month and Year)
    • End Date (Month and Year)
  • Location
  • Description Click the button Save to add the information to your profile, or the button Cancel to cancel!

To add more organizations, continue clicking the + icon and following the steps above!

Projects

Adding projects to your profile may include a wide variety of work, such as publications, photos, presentations, pitch decks, websites, and more!

Click on the + icon, located to the right of Projects.

Within the pop-up, enter the following details:

  • Project title
  • Role (check box if you’re still working on the project)
  • Time Period
    • Start Date (Month and Year)
    • End Date (Month and Year)
  • URL
  • Description Click the button Save to add the information to your profile, or the button Cancel to cancel!

To add more projects, continue clicking the + icon and following the steps above!

Languages

Let employers know the language/s you are fluent in!

  1. Click the + icon, located to the right of Languages.

  2. Within the pop-up, click on the search box Select Language and type the desired language you want to add — A list will populate based on what you type. Select the option from the dropdown to add.

Note: there is the option to include Sign Language in various languages across the globe.

  1. Once a language is added, click on the search box Select proficiency and choose your expertise from the dropdown:
  • Elementary proficiency
  • Limited working proficiency
  • Professional working proficiency
  • Full professional proficiency
  • Native or bilingual proficiency
  1. Once added, click the button Save to update or Cancel to cancel!

To remove a language, click the trashcan icon, located to the right of the language.

To add more languages, continue clicking the + icon and following the steps above!

Profile Picture

Add a picture to connect your school’s career services and fellow students — or to help your profile stand out to employers!

Click on the image avatar to add your photo, located on the left side of the page.

Within the pop-up, click the button Upload photo, then choose an image from your computer to upload.

Note: If you can’t upload your image, it may be because your picture is too big. The max image size is 20 megabytes. If larger than 20 megabytes, you’ll need to crop the photo to a smaller size, and then re-upload it.

Once the image is uploaded, use the - sign to zoom out and the + sign to zoom in, then click the button Save to save!

General information

Your personal information includes details such as your name, pronouns, location, and any links you’d like to feature on your profile.

During the account setup process, you’re prompted to provide details. If you previously skipped this step or want to update any of this information, follow the steps below to make changes!

  1. Click your account icon in the upper-right corner of Handshake, then click My Profile from the dropdown.

  2. From your profile, click the button Edit located on the left side of the page.

Missing the Share button located to the left of Edit? This means your profile isn’t set to public and cannot be discovered outside of Handshake. To learn more about making your profile public and sharing it, check out How to Make Your Profile Public and Share Your Profile Link.

  1. Within the pop-up that appears, you can add/edit the following fields:
  • First name (Type in the box)
  • Last name (Type in the box)
  • Headline (Optional—Type in the box)
  • Pronouns (Type in the box to add one or multiple responses, or add your own)
    • She/her
    • He/him
    • They/them
  • Location (Type in the box, then choose from the dropdown)
  • Custom profile link (Learn more about custom profile links in Create a Custom Profile URL on Handshake)
  • Links (optional — add up to 5 links)
    • Title
    • URL (Must start with https://)
    • Description
    • Only include links to projects or portfolios you wish to showcase—links to other profile pages will not be accepted.
    • Important: The links added here are only visible to people who access your profile through a direct profile link (for example, if your profile is set to public and viewed by someone who is not on Handshake). If you want employers on Handshake to have access to your links when they view your profile, be sure to include them in the Summary or Projects section instead.
  1. Once the updates have been made, click the button Save to save or Cancel to cancel.

Create a Custom Profile URL on Handshake

One of the best ways to stand out to employers and make your Handshake profile more shareable is by claiming a custom URL for your profile. This personalized link can be added to your résumé, email signature, or social profiles, making it simpler for recruiters and peers to find your professional profile.

This guide will walk you through how to unlock, set, and manage your custom Handshake URL!

What Is a Custom Profile URL?

A custom profile URL is a unique web address that links directly to your Handshake profile (e.g., joinhandshake.com/yourname). You can choose this URL—subject to availability—so it aligns with your personal brand, making it easy to share and access.

How to Unlock Your Custom URL

To claim your custom URL, follow these steps:

  • Complete at least 70% of your Handshake profile
  • Fill out key sections such as Education, Work & Volunteer Experience, Skills, and Interests to get closer to profile completion. For more tips, check out Completing your Profile in Handshake.
  • Have a Community profile with visibility set to Public
  • Your profile must be set to “Public” in order for others to view your profile and share your link. Learn more about your profile visibility options in Profile Privacy Options in Handshake. Once you meet these requirements, the option to set your custom URL will be available on both the web and mobile versions of Handshake.

How to Create Your Custom Profile URL

  • After reaching 70% profile completion, you’ll receive a notification in-app. You’ll also be prompted with banners guiding you to unlock your custom URL.

  • Alternatively, you can click your profile icon in the upper-right corner, then select My Profile from the dropdown. Next, Click the Customize Profile Link button.

  • In the pop-up that appears, scroll to the “Custom Profile Link” section. Remove the auto-generated URL and enter your desired URL. You’ll receive instant feedback if your chosen URL is already taken. Try variations that reflect your personal brand.

  • Note: If this option is grayed out and unclickable, it means you’re not yet eligible for a custom URL. Complete your profile to unlock this feature.

  • Once you’re happy with your URL, click Save. Edit Limits and Restrictions

  • Update Frequency: You can change your custom URL once every 30 days. If you need to update it, wait until the 30-day period has passed.

  • Restricted Words: Certain terms, like the names of the top 500 employers, cannot be used in your URL.

  • Community Guidelines: URLs that violate Handshake’s community guidelines may be reported by other users.

Additional Information

  • Once set, your URL is yours to keep, even if you later remove content from your profile or change your profile’s privacy setting. Just know, if you change your profile’s privacy setting, other will not be able to view your profile through your custom link.
  • Setup banners and notifications only appear if you’re eligible and haven’t already claimed a custom URL. If you dismiss a banner, it will no longer appear in the app. You’ll need to claim your custom link within your profile settings. To do this, refer to Update Personal Information on Your Profile. Ready to share your custom URL or add it as an email signature? Check out out Locating the Link to Your Handshake Profile.

How to Add Work Study Eligibility to Your Profile

If you believe you’re eligible for work-study jobs, you’ll need to contact your school’s Career Services Center to update your work-study eligibility status in Handshake.

Once your status is updated, you’ll be able to view and apply for work-study jobs!

To locate your school’s contact information, refer to How to Locate your School’s Contact Information in Handshake.

How to Edit Education Information on Your Profile

As a student, you may need to change your major, GPA, school year, or other education information within Handshake.

While some schools allow students to update these fields directly in the system, others don’t.

To determine if you are able to change your Education Information in Handshake, follow the steps below.

If you need to change your Primary Education (the school you are connected to on Handshake), refer to Managing Primary Education.

  2. Scroll down to the Education section of your profile, then click on the pencil icon, located to the right of the school that you need to update the corresponding information with.

  3. Within the pop-up, a list of fields will be available for you to update.

If any of the fields are grayed out — this means the field is locked and you won’t be able to edit the information. You’ll need to notify your career services department of the change you’d like to make. If you need assistance finding your career center’s contact information, refer to How to Locate your School’s Contact Information in Handshake.

  • School
  • Education Level (drop-down list)
    • High School
    • Associates
    • Certificate
    • Advanced Certificate
    • Bachelors
    • Masters
    • Doctorate
    • Postdoctoral Studies
    • Non-Degree Seeking
    • Technical Diploma
    • Master’s of Business Administration
    • Community / Technical college
    • Accelerated master’s
  • College (drop-down list)
  • School Year (drop-down list)
  • Time Period
    • Start Date (Month and Year)

      • Note: the end date field is only available if you’re not currently attending the institution

  • Major (type to search)
    • Note: only majors associated with your institution are available via the dropdown
  • Minor (type to search)
    • Note: only majors associated with your institution are available via the dropdown
  • Cumulative GPA

  • Department GPA
    • Check the box to hide from employers. Your GPA will never be shown to employers unless you choose for it to be shown.
  • Description (type your response in the box, up to 500 characters)
  1. Once the updates are complete, click Save and close in the lower right corner.

How to Edit the Summary on Your Profile

The Summary section offers you the opportunity to highlight your skills and include any additional information that you’d like to share with employers and/or peers!

If you’ve never added a Summary to your profile, refer to Completing your Profile in Handshake.

How to Make Your Profile Public and Share Your Profile Link

Your Handshake profile serves as a key component of your digital identity, showcasing your skills, experiences, and interests. With the new Public Profiles feature, you can share your profile with potential employers, recruiters, mentors, and peers—whether they’re on Handshake or not.

What is a Public Profile?

A Public Profile is a version of your Handshake profile that can be viewed by anyone, even if they don’t have a Handshake account. This feature is designed to help you:

  • Connect with employers and recruiters through email or other external channels.
  • Get advice from mentors, alumni, or professionals who may not be on Handshake.
  • Showcase your work experience and interests by displaying your projects and organizations in a rich, multimedia format.
  • Diversify your digital presence, providing you with more visibility and networking opportunities. Once you’ve made your profile public and shareable, you can distribute it via email, messages, or social media to broaden your reach.

Note: The public version of your profile is a condensed version. Certain sensitive details, such as your GPA or other private information, will not be visible to the public. Your public profile will showcase the following sections you’ve filled out on your profile: Summary, Skills, Work experience, Education, Organizations, Projects, and Languages.

Make your profile public

To make your Handshake profile public, follow the below steps:

  • Log in to your Handshake account.
  • Click on your profile icon in the upper-right corner of the page, then select Settings from the dropdown menu.
  • Select Privacy.
  • Click the radio button next to the desired option: Community (public), then click the box next to “Make profile public and shareable outside of Handshake”.
  • Once selected, click the Save changes button to update! To learn more about your profile privacy settings on Handshake, check out Profile Privacy Options in Handshake.

Sharing your public profile link

Once you’ve opted into making your profile public, you can share it a few ways by copying the link to your profile!

To find your link, go to your profile in Handshake, then click the button Share, located on the left side of the page. From the dropdown, click the option to Copy profile link. Your unique public profile URL is now copied to your clipboard, ready to be shared.

For more information on how to find your profile link, check out Locating the Link to Your Handshake Profile.

Ways to share your profile

Now that you have your public profile link, there are several ways you can share it to boost your visibility and connect with others:

  • Email: Paste your profile link directly into the body of an email. This is a great way to share your profile with recruiters, potential mentors, or anyone you’d like to connect with professionally.
  • Social Media: Post your public profile link on LinkedIn, Twitter, Instagram, or any other platform where you engage with your network. It’s a way to showcase your skills and experience to a broader audience.
  • Resume or Portfolio: Include your Handshake profile link on your resume or portfolio. This makes it easy for hiring managers, potential employers, or collaborators to view your profile and learn more about your accomplishments.
  • Networking events: Whether you’re attending in-person or virtual events, sharing your profile link can help others learn more about you. For in-person events, can include it on your resume or a business card. Tip: For more visibility to your profile, generate an email signature with a link to your profile. The link will include a preview of your profile directly from your signature! For more information on how to generate an email signature from your profile link, refer to Locating the Link to Your Handshake Profile.

If Your Major (or Minor) is Missing or Incorrect

Having your major added to your profile is an important component of Handshake! Employers often use majors to connect with students of interest to offer job opportunities as well as event invites. Career services users may also use majors as a requirement to attend appointments, events, or fairs.

Your major is added to our profile via one of the following ways:

  • Uploaded by your school
    • If your school pre-created an account for you, your major and minor are uploaded to your profile for you. This is usually added from data provided by your school registrar.
  • Added by yourself
    • If you created an account yourself, you received the option to add a major for yourself during the account creation process.

Update or add major

🚀Tip: If you’re a current student at a partner school and you’re changing your major, we recommend you contact your school’s Career Center to correct it on their end. This will ensure that the data your school has on file is accurate, and that your information doesn’t revert in Handshake.

  1. Click your account icon in the upper-right corner of the screen, then click My profile from the dropdown.

  2. Scroll down to the Education section of your profile, then click on the pencil icon located to the right of the school that you need to update the corresponding major to.

  3. Within the pop-up scroll to find the major section, then click inside the text box and start typing to find your major. Only majors associated with your institution are available via the dropdown.

To add a second major, click inside the box and start typing the major’s name. Majors will appear in the order you enter them. To change the order, remove the majors and re-add them in your preferred sequence. To remove a major, click the X next to its name..

If the major field is grayed out with a lock icon, this means your school has locked the field and you cannot edit the information. You’ll need to notify your career services department of the change you’d like to make. To find your school’s contact information, refer to How to Locate your School’s Contact Information in Handshake.

  1. Once the major is updated, click the black button Save and close to save!

For more information on updating your profile in Handshake, follow the steps in How to Edit Education Information on Your Profile.

Locating the Link to Your Handshake Profile

You may want to share your Handshake profile with your school, a mentor, or an employer.

The ability to share your profile depends on your privacy preferences on Handshake and the users connection with the platform.

  • If you’ve chosen the Community option in your profile settings and have selected to make your profile public and shareable, you have the option to share your profile link with anyone you choose.
  • If your profile is set to Employer or Community in your profile settings and you did not choose to make it public, you’ll need to ensure the individual you are sharing your profile link with has a Handshake account and is approved at your school. To obtain your profile link, follow the steps below based on whether your profile is set to public and shareable or not.

For more information about your profile privacy options, refer to Profile Privacy Options in Handshake.

To learn more about public profiles on Handshake, check out How to Make Your Handshake Profile Public and Share Your Profile Link.

To create a custom profile link, refer to Create a Custom Profile URL on Handshake.

Public profile

If you’ve chosen to make your profile public and shareable, Handshake offers a convenient way to generate a link for you to share!

  1. Log in to your student account on Handshake.

  2. Click on your account icon in the upper-right corner of Handshake, then click My Profile from the dropdown.

  3. Click the button Share, located on the left side of your profile.

  4. From the dropdown, choose from one of the following options:

  • Copy profile link: Copies your profile link to your clipboard so you can paste it wherever you want to share it!
  • Share via email: Launches the email feature on your device, allowing you to copy and paste content into the body of an email for sending.
  • Create email signature: Provides a custom email signature with a link to your Handshake profile. Your Handshake signature includes your profile image, primary education, end date, and major (if added to your profile).
    • Tip: paste the link directly into your email signature settings. Not sure how to update your email signature? Check out these help articles for Gmail and Outlook.

Non-public profile

If you have opted out of making your profile public and shareable, you’ll need to locate and copy the URL to your profile.

  1. Log in to your student account on Handshake.

  2. Click on your account icon in the upper-right corner of Handshake, then click My Profile from the dropdown.

  3. The link to your profile is the URL that is displayed within the address bar (above the profile page) — Copy and paste the link to share with the desired audience!

Important: If you have opted out of making your profile public and shareable, the individual you are sharing your profile link with will need to have a Handshake account and be approved at your school. Additionally, you’ll need to ensure your profile privacy settings are set to Community or Employer. For more information about your profile privacy options, refer to Profile Privacy Options in Handshake.

Managing Primary Education

Your Primary Education is intended to represent the school you’re currently affiliated with. This is the school that you can schedule appointments with, attend fairs and fairs at, view approved jobs, etc.

You can add as many schools to your Handshake profile as needed, but can only have one Primary Education.

On the new student profile in Handshake, your Primary Education is identified with a gray badge that states Primary.

If you need to update your Primary Education on your profile, you’ll need to contact Handshake’s Support team. This is because the school will need to approve your affiliation before being added.

To update the Education information on your profile (GPA, major, minor, etc.), refer to How to Edit Education Information on Your Profile.

To add or edit the summary/bio on your profile, refer to How to Edit the Summary on Your Profile.

To update your personal information (name, pronouns, location) within the header of your profile, refer to Update Personal Information on Your Profile.

Profile Insights: Track Views and Engagement

Profile Insights reveals how many times your profile has been viewed—and on the web, even who viewed it. Whether you’re job hunting, networking, or just getting started, these insights keep you informed and improve your chances of connecting with the right people and opportunities.

Profile Insights can help you:

  • Recognize employer interest – Know when your background is attracting attention.
  • Stay proactive – Use this insight as a signal to update and improve your profile.
  • Stay motivated – Engagement can be a great push to continue building connections. Maintaining a complete and up-to-date profile makes it easier for the right opportunities to find you.

Learn how to update and finish your profile in Completing your Profile in Handshake.

How to Access Profile Insights

On Web:

  • Log into your Handshake account.

  • Click your profile icon in the upper-right corner.

  • From the dropdown, select My Profile.

  • On your profile page, click the Profile Viewers tab (located to the right of Posts). On iOS:

  • Open the Handshake app and click your profile icon in the upper-left corner.

  • Tap on your name.

  • On your profile page, tap the Insights tab (located to the right of Posts).

What You’ll Find in Profile Insights

On the web, you’ll have access to a list of users who have viewed your profile in the past 90 days. This includes employers, peers, and other members of the Handshake community. The total number of views is displayed in the bottom left corner of the page. If a user has a private profile, they will be listed as “private profile”.

On iOS, you’ll have access to the total number of profile views over the past 90 days, along with a graph showing view activity over time.

Tips to boost engagement directly from iOS:

  • Leave a comment on a post
  • Attend an event
  • Follow peers or employers directly from the page You’ll also have access to a profile completion bar—click it to track your progress and update your profile!

Note: On both web and iOS, profile views are updated once daily (not in real time) and appear in order from most recent to oldest.

Privacy Settings

To allow others to view your profile, your visibility must be set to Community. If you haven’t updated your settings yet, you can do so directly from the Profile Insights tab by clicking the Visibility link—it will take you to your settings page to make changes.

If you switch your privacy setting to Employer or Private, you’ll still be able to access profile views collected while your profile was set to Community.

To learn more about privacy options on Handshake, check out Profile Privacy Options in Handshake.

Public Labels on Profile

Public labels in Handshake are tags that your school’s career services staff can apply to your profile.

Only you and the career services staff at your school have access to these labels. They are not visible to anyone else.

The “Public Labels” section on your profile displays the specific labels applied to your profile.

These labels can be used to categorize, arrange, and increase exposure to specific things, such as jobs, interview schedules, employers, or events.

If you have questions about the labels added to your profile, we recommend you reach out to your career center for more information. To find your career center contact information, refer to How to Locate your School’s Contact Information in Handshake.

Student Work Authorization Information

We collect work authorization information directly from you to improve your application process and ensure your time is well-spent applying and interviewing.

The work authorization information provided by you determines if you are considered qualified or not qualified for employer preferences on job postings and requirements on virtual fair 1:1 sessions.

💡Note: if your school is partnered with Handshake, your career services office may choose to import a field called “visa status” primarily for reporting purposes. This field is not visible to you on your profile.

The only instance in which this field is used to determine your qualification on job postings is if both of the following circumstances are true:

    - (1) you have not ever answered these questions AND
    - (2) a Career Services user is submitting an application on the your behalf

Click on the expandable headers to learn more!

Work Authorization - Set and Update Your Information

How to Set or Update Your Information

You can update your work authorization info anytime:

  • Click your account icon located in the upper-right corner of the screen, then click Settings from the dropdown menu.

  • Select Work Authorization.

  • Choose your answers and click Save changes. Handshake work authorization information consists of 2 questions—you must either answer both questions or opt out of sharing. After you’ve answered the questions once, you will not be prompted to answer again.

  • Select Yes/No for both questions:

    • Are you legally authorized to work in the United States?
    • Will you now or in the future require visa sponsorship?

  • Select the checkbox for Prefer not to answer these questions.

    • There is a tooltip to the right of this option with a “i” icon—click the icon to display the following tooltip:
      • If you check this box, you may be sent or recommended irrelevant jobs, because employers won’t know if you meet work authorization requirements.
      • Employers will see your work authorization status listed as “unknown.”
      • If you have DACA and don’t know how to answer, here’s a resource on how to answer these questions: www.informedimmigrant.com/guides/daca/#employment-rights-daca If you haven’t already provided this information in your Settings, you’ll be prompted to select your work authorization when you apply to your first job—or, if you haven’t applied to any jobs yet, when you register for a virtual fair.

Note: if you check the option “Prefer not to answer these questions”, you will be FULLY QUALIFIED for all posting preferences or virtual fair sessions with work authorization requirements.

Job Search Filter

You can filter job searches by work authorization requirements by clicking All filters on the job search page.

Scroll to the Work authorization section – there are two checkboxes that correspond with the questions both employers and students answer. Select your preference(s), then click Show Results:

  • Open to US visa sponsorship
  • Open to Optional Practical Training (OPT)
  • Open to Curricular Practical Training (CPT)
  • No US work authorization required
  • Unknown Work Authorization Qualifications

Note: if you check the option “Prefer not to answer these questions”, you will be FULLY QUALIFIED for all posting preferences or virtual fair sessions with work authorization requirements.

Virtual fair 1:1 session qualifications

For virtual fair 1:1 sessions, if the employer has set work authorization qualifications and your selections do not meet their qualifications, you will not be able to view or sign up for their 1:1 sessions.

Job posting preferences

When viewing a job posting, the work authorization selected by the employer is shown under the “At a Glance” section.

If you’re interested in how your qualification status displays to employers, refer to the examples in our employer-facing article.

Update Personal Information on Your Profile

Your personal information within your settings includes details such as your name and demographic details.

During the account setup process, you’re prompted to provide details. If you previously skipped this step or want to update any of this information, follow the steps below to make changes!

If you want to update your profile information, such as your bio, skills, and education information, check out Completing your Profile in Handshake.

  1. Click your account icon in the upper-right corner of Handshake, then click Settings from the dropdown

  2. Within your settings, click Personal info

  3. Add or edit the following fields:

  • First name (Type in the box)

  • Language (Choose one)
    • English (US)
    • English (UK)
    • Français
    • Deutsch

    • Gender (Optional)
    • Race and Ethnicity (Optional)
