Project Participation

Access the Handshake AI Slack workspace

The Handshake AI Slack workspace is where all project updates, instructions, and time-sensitive updates are shared. Slack access is only granted after you complete all onboarding steps and pass applicable project assessments in your Handshake AI dashboard.

You will not be able to access Slack if you’re currently onboarding to a project or have not yet completed and passed any project-related assessments.

Slack access and setup

Quick tips to get started

  • Slack invites are sent automatically once you’ve fully onboarded and passed applicable project assessments. Please allow 24 hours for updates to process and invites to be sent.
  • From your dashboard, click View Project, then click Message on Slack to launch the sign in page.
  • Use the email address associated with your Handshake AI account when signing into Slack.
  • Download the Slack desktop app (Mac or Windows) or the mobile app (iOS or Android).

How to navigate the Handshake AI Slack workspace

Find your way around

  • Workspace switcher (top left): switch between workspaces if you belong to more than one.
  • Sidebar: access your channels, direct messages, and apps.
  • Search bar: the fastest way to find past answers and pinned posts. Understand your channels

You’ll be added to relevant project channels based on your project role and the channels created. Always refer to your project training for guidance on available channels and where to post.

Each project has two primary channels:

  • #projectname-announcements: where the Handshake AI team posts important updates. You will not be able to post in this channel.

  • #projectname-tasking: where the project team shares day-to-day work information and task updates. You can post and ask questions in this channel on designated threads. Post in a way that keeps channels organized

  • Search the channel before posting to check if your question has already been answered.

  • To reply in a thread, hover over a message and select Reply in thread. On mobile, long-press the message and choose Reply in thread.

  • React with ✅ when your question is resolved so others can see it has been addressed.

Common issues and fixes

  • Issue: You used a different email for Slack than your Handshake AI email
    • Resolution: Slack access is tied to the email on your Handshake AI account, so you’ll need to use that email address to sign in (not an alias). Sign out of any other accounts, and sign in with your Handshake AI account email.
  • Issue: You are in Slack but do not see the channels you expected
    • Resolution: Contact Support. Channel access is based on your project role. If channels are missing, contact Support so the team can verify your role and channel setup.

Assessments on Handshake AI

Assessments are evaluations used to confirm that you have the knowledge and skills needed to contribute to a project. They are a required part of onboarding for many projects and may also appear during a project if quality standards need to be re-verified.

Assessments are project-specific, and the format, length, and passing criteria will vary depending on the partner lab and the type of work involved. Details about any required assessments will be communicated as part of your project onboarding materials.

What to expect

Before you begin tasking on a project, you may be asked to complete one or more of the following:

  • A knowledge quiz based on your onboarding training materials
  • A practice task or sample submission reviewed by the Handshake AI team
  • A written or skills-based evaluation relevant to your project domain Take your time and review all training materials thoroughly before attempting an assessment. Assessments are designed to reflect the real work you’ll be doing on the project, so your onboarding materials are the best preparation.

What happens if my assessment is under review?

After submitting your assessment, there may be a processing period before you receive results. This is normal. During this time, your submission is being evaluated by the Handshake AI team or your project reviewers. You do not need to resubmit. You will be notified once a decision has been made.

What happens if I encounter an error during my assessment?

If you experience a technical issue, such as the assessment not loading, a submission error, or being locked out — do not attempt to restart or resubmit on your own, as this may affect your results. Contact Support and describe the issue in as much detail as possible, including any error messages you received.

What happens if I fail an assessment?

Failing an assessment means you did not meet the minimum score or quality threshold required for that project. In most cases, retakes are not available. If retakes are not permitted, you will not be able to continue onboarding for that specific project.

This does not disqualify you from the Handshake AI Fellowship altogether. Your profile remains active and you’ll still be considered for other projects that match your qualifications.

Can I request a retake?

Retake availability is determined on a per-project basis and is not guaranteed. Retake requests are reviewed case by case, and approval is not guaranteed.

Note: simply wanting to improve your score is not typically grounds for a retake. Retake requests are generally only considered when there is a documented error or technical issue.

Tips for success

  • Complete all training modules and onboarding materials before starting your assessment
  • Set aside uninterrupted time — do not rush through the assessment
  • Follow all instructions carefully; each project’s standards are specific
  • If something seems unclear, review your onboarding materials again before submitting

Getting started on a project

Once you’ve completed onboarding and are ready to begin work, this guide will help you hit the ground running. For a comprehensive overview of the journey leading up to this point—including your invitation email, onboarding checklist, and training materials, refer to From application to first project: your complete Handshake AI Fellowship journey.

How to prepare before starting a project

Taking a little time to set yourself up before diving in will help you hit the ground running.

  • Read everything first. Go through all onboarding materials thoroughly before starting any tasks — task guidelines, quality standards, and any example submissions. Missing a detail early can affect the quality of your work throughout.
  • Set up any required tools. Some projects require specific platforms or software. Make sure everything is installed and working before you begin so a technical issue doesn’t hold you up mid-task.
  • Understand the quality bar. Every project has its own definition of high-quality work. Study any example tasks or reference materials closely so you have a clear sense of what a strong submission looks like.
  • Ask questions early. If anything is unclear after reviewing the onboarding materials, don’t wait until you’re mid-task to ask. Reaching out to the project team or support channels early is always better than guessing.
Finding your Handshake AI alias email

Some projects provide a Handshake AI alias email for project-specific communications and platform access. Your onboarding materials will typically include instructions for locating it.

You can also find your alias email in your project dashboard. From your Handshake AI dashboard, open your project, then check the left sidebar under Credentials, alongside the other project resources. If your project includes an alias email, it will be listed there.

Tasking on a project

Each project has its own detailed instructions, deadlines, tasking expectations, and platform. Pay close attention during onboarding so you’re set up for success when you’re ready to begin. These instructions are always accessible from your project dashboard.

Common mistakes to avoid on your first project

  • Skipping or skimming the instructions. This is the most common mistake new fellows make. Read everything carefully before you begin.
  • Prioritizing speed over quality. A smaller number of strong submissions is always better than a high volume of weak ones.
  • Starting a task you can’t finish. If you don’t have enough time to complete a task properly, wait until you do. Submitting incomplete work or abandoning a task mid-way can negatively affect your standing on a project.
  • Ignoring feedback. If you receive feedback on early submissions, act on it. Repeating the same mistakes signals to reviewers that you’re not engaging with the project’s standards. To learn about Tasks, check out Tasks on Handshake AI.

Navigating your Handshake AI dashboard

Your Handshake AI dashboard is the source of truth for everything related to your account and projects. It updates in real time and shows the latest available info on opportunities, assignments, earnings, and account standing.

Your dashboard is organized into three main tabs: Projects, Payments, and Referrals.

Projects Tab

The Projects tab is your home base for all project activity.

  • Your Projects: Displays all projects you’re currently enrolled in or have previously worked on. Toggle between Current (active projects) and Past (paused or ended projects).
    • Tip: Select a project to view its details, including your assigned tasks. Additional project resources, such as the project terms and other project-specific information—are available in the left-side panel.
  • Invited To: Projects you’ve been personally invited to apply to based on your background and experience.
  • Open Opportunities: All projects currently accepting fellow interest. Each project tile includes the project name and description, required tools or specializations, work type, current pay rate, number of fellows earning on the project, and a Submit Interest button.
Projects Sidebar

The sidebar on the right side of the Projects tab provides a quick overview of your activity and account.

  • Awaiting payout — earnings approved and queued for your next payout (may not yet reflect all earnings)
  • Total paid — all amounts paid and currently processing
  • Tasks this week — number of tasks completed in the current week
  • Hours this week — approved hours eligible for payment
  • Update your profile — keep your skills, experience, and resume current so your project matches stay relevant. To learn more about updating your profile, check out Completing your Profile in Handshake.
  • Spot suspicious activity — a reminder to watch for fraud or scam accounts impersonating Handshake; select “Learn more” for guidance on staying safe

Payments Tab

The Payments tab provides a visual overview of your earnings over time. Use the filters at the top of the page to view earnings by specific projects or time periods, including All Time, Week, Month, and Year. The earnings graph updates instantly based on your selected filters, making it easy to track your payment history and earnings trends.

Payments Sidebar

The right sidebar of the Payments tab includes the same activity summary as the Projects tab, plus a few additional options specific to payments and tax:

  • Payment method — set up your payment method if you have not done so already, or verify that payments are being sent to the correct account
  • W-8/W-9 form — download your W-8/W-9 form
  • Update tax form — update your tax information on file

Referrals Tab

The Referrals tab is where you can find your personal referral link to share with others who may be interested in joining the Handshake AI Fellowship. For full details on how the referral program works, eligibility, and earnings, check out Referring someone to the Handshake AI Fellowship.

Dashboard Updates

Your dashboard surfaces real-time updates for: project and task availability, current assigned projects, account updates and status. Email notifications are sent automatically at the time of certain activity, updates, or changes in the annotation platform.

Notice a difference between an email and your dashboard? Check when the email was sent, consider the information shared, and double-check what’s different! Because projects can change quickly based on research needs, project priorities, quality requirements, timelines, and platform demand, the information shared in emails—including invitations, announcements, and pay-rate notifications—may become outdated.

Your dashboard reflects the most accurate information currently available and able to be displayed. Additional resources to check if something is still unclear:

  • Project Terms: includes expectations for pay rate and structure, time commitment, location requirements, and other project rules.
  • Project Instructions: information needed to complete tasks
  • Slack: real-time announcements, updates, and other information If the information isn’t found or you have additional questions, contact Support!

Offboarding from a project or the Handshake AI Fellowship

If you’re ready to step away from a Handshake AI project or the Fellowship entirely, we’re here to make the process straightforward.

Offboarding options

To begin the offboarding process, please reach out to us and let us know which of the following applies to you:

Leave your current project only

You’ll stop working on your current project but remain part of the Fellowship. You may still be considered for future opportunities based on project availability, your experience, and overall performance.

Leave the Handshake AI Fellowship entirely

You’ll no longer be eligible for Handshake AI project opportunities, and your access to the Handshake AI dashboard will be removed after offboarding. Your regular Handshake account — including access to jobs, events, and networking, will remain active and unaffected.

Before you go

If you’re stepping away from a specific project (rather than the entire fellowship), you may still be eligible for future opportunities. Be sure to include your domain expertise in your annotation platform preferences so we can keep you in mind for future opportunities that may be a better fit.

Thanks again for being part of the Handshake AI Fellowship! Your contributions are deeply valued, and we hope to collaborate again in the future.

Projects on Handshake AI

A project is a body of work provided by one of our partner AI labs. Each project has a defined start and end date and includes details such as:

  • The type of tasks you’ll complete
  • The pay structure (hourly or per task)
  • Any required qualifications or experience Projects are not self-serve and are not available immediately after applying. Handshake AI matches fellows to projects based on their qualifications, experience, and profile.

To learn more about onboarding a project, check out Getting started on a project.

To learn more about the work you’ll complete within a project, refer to Understanding tasks on Handshake AI.

How to get matched to a project

Project matching is handled by the Handshake AI team. To maximize your chances of being matched to new opportunities, make sure your profile is fully completed and that you’ve finished any required assessments. This is the most important step you can take to become eligible for project invitations.

Can I work on more than one project at a time?

In some cases, yes — it depends on the specific projects involved. Some projects allow fellows to work on multiple projects concurrently, while others require exclusive focus. Any exclusivity requirements will be clearly communicated in the project details and onboarding materials. If you’re unsure, check with your project lead before accepting additional work.

If you’re balancing multiple projects, be mindful of your capacity. Each project has its own quality standards, and spreading yourself too thin can impact your performance across all projects. Consistently delivering excellent work on one project is better than delivering average work on several.

Accessing your projects

After onboarding, your active projects will appear in your Handshake AI dashboard under Your Projects. Task access is granted once all required onboarding steps have been completed, including assessments, training, and platform setup.

If a project you were expecting to show isn’t in your Handshake AI dashboard, there are a few possible explanations for this:

  • The project may have been paused or closed. If a project has disappeared from your dashboard, select Past under Your Projects to confirm whether it has been temporarily paused or completed. Projects may be paused or closed with little notice based on the needs of our partner labs. Be sure to check your email as well, as the Handshake AI team will communicate any project status updates there.
  • There may be a technical issue. Occasionally, dashboard display issues can be caused by a browser or account problem. Try refreshing the page, clearing your browser cache, or logging out and back in.
  • Check your Spam or Promotions folder. If you’re expecting an invite email related to your annotation work and haven’t seen it land in your inbox, it may have been filtered into your Spam or Promotions folder instead.

Tasks on Handshake AI

A task is an individual unit of work within a project. Each task has its own instructions, expectations, and submission requirements. Tasks are the primary way fellows contribute to a project.

Before you start a task

Each task will include instructions and an indication of the expected time commitment before you begin. Take a moment to review what’s involved before starting. Avoid beginning a task if you don’t have enough time to complete it thoughtfully. Rushed work often falls short of quality standards and may need to be revised or redone.

A few things to keep in mind:

  • Follow the task instructions. Each project has its own quality standards, and requirements can vary from task to task.
  • Only work on one task at a time. If you open another task while one is in progress, the platform will automatically pause the current task’s timer.
  • Time tracking matters. All paid work is tied to accurate time tracking. Make sure the task timer is running while you work and paused when you step away. For more details on time tracking, refer to Time tracking for Handshake AI Fellowship projects and Time tracking standards.

How long tasks typically take

Task length varies depending on the project and type of work involved. Some tasks can be completed in a few minutes, while others, particularly those requiring deeper reasoning or specialized expertise may take significantly longer.

Why tasks aren’t always available

Task availability is driven by the needs of our partner AI labs and can fluctuate. Projects may ramp up quickly, slow down, pause, or end altogether depending on where a lab is in their research and development process. This is a normal part of how AI project work operates.

There may be periods where tasks are limited or unavailable, even if you’re actively matched to a project. These gaps aren’t a reflection of your standing as a fellow. When tasks do become available, we recommend jumping in promptly, as availability can change quickly and with little notice.

What it means if a task is paused or closed

From time to time, tasks or entire projects may be paused or closed. This is a normal part of working on AI projects and is driven by the needs of our partner labs — not your performance as a fellow.

Paused tasks: A paused task means work has temporarily stopped. This can happen for a variety of reasons, such as a lab may be reviewing progress, adjusting requirements, or shifting priorities. When a project resumes, you’ll be notified by email and the tasks will reappear in your dashboard.

Closed tasks: A closed task or project means the work has ended. Projects can close suddenly and with little notice depending on where a lab is in their development process.

If a task or project is paused or closed, no action is required on your end. The Handshake AI team will communicate updates as early as possible — keep an eye on your inbox and dashboard so you’re ready when new tasks open up.

Time tracking for Handshake AI Fellowship projects

To ensure accurate time tracking, we use an automated time tracking system directly within our annotation platform—no manual submissions! You can work on tasks at your own pace, even over multiple days, as long as you stay within the time cap and meet project goals.

If your project is hosted on the AI labs’s platform, you’ll report your hours using either Hubstaff or a Google Form. Your project lead will provide detailed instructions, and our team will handle the processing of your reported time.

Important Timer Information:

  • Your Responsibility: You are responsible for accurately managing and reporting your work time with this timer. Start, pause, and track your time.
  • Taking Breaks: Remember to pause the time whenever you need to step away from the task.
  • Timer Persistence: An unpaused timer continues running even when the browser tab is closed or you navigate away.
  • Time Calculation: Your task time is calculated based on active periods when the timer is running.
  • Time Limit: Stay within the time cap assigned for your task. Anything beyond the limit won’t be paid.

Starting your timer

When you begin a new task, a confirmation window will explain how the timer works. To start tracking time, click the Start Timer button.

Pausing your timer

Your timer is located at the top-center of the screen and displays your time spent compared to your task’s time limit. To pause the timer, click the pause icon.

Submitting a task

When you submit a task, the timer will automatically stop, and a confirmation pop-up will display the total time you spent on the task. You’ll also have access to how much time remains before reaching your cap, along with a breakdown of active vs. inactive time.

Time caps are based on analysis of similar tasks and reflect the average time needed to complete them. They help ensure efficiency and fairness across all Fellows. If you reach the time cap, you’ll still need to submit the task for review. Any required revisions after the cap must also be resubmitted.

You’ll have the opportunity to review this for accuracy. If something looks off or is incorrect, click the blue Edit time link to make adjustments.

By clicking confirm time, you agree this accurately reflects your work contributions for this task. You also authorize Handshake to use this as your formal submission for this task, which will determine your hourly compensation on this project.

Adjust your time spent

In the pop-up, your session time is automatically recorded. If needed, update the hours, minutes, or seconds to reflect the correct time for your pay. Then click Update to save the changes or Cancel to discard them.

Once you’ve made your changes, the updated time will be applied and ready for you to submit your task.

Note: There may occasionally be discrepancies between what you see in the platform, our communications, and your payments dashboard, due to processing delays. If you ever have questions or concerns about your logged time or compensation, don’t hesitate to reach out—we’re happy to help clarify or resolve any issues

To learn more about using the annotation platform, check out Using the Annotation Platform: FAQs and Troubleshooting.

Using the annotation platform: FAQs and troubleshooting

The annotation platform is where you’ll complete most practice and project tasks. Below is a guide to help you navigate the platform, understand how tasks work, and resolve common issues.

Depending on the project, you may work on Handshake’s internal platform or directly within the partnering AI lab’s platform. You’ll always receive clear instructions on where to go and how to access your task dashboard before beginning projects.

The “annotation platform” is how we refer to our site, ai.joinhandshake.com (also known as your dashboard). Once you’re assigned to a project, you’ll be able to access the project dashboard from this page.

To learn more about the invite process to Handshake’s annotation platform, check out Getting started on a project.

Project overview and expectations

If you’re accepted into the program, refer to your Handshake AI dashboard and Slack for detailed project updates and training sessions.

In general, your tasks will include:

  • Creating prompts in your field of expertise. You will not be asked to write prompts outside your domain.
  • Evaluating the model’s responses, identifying inaccuracies, and adding relevant citations or research to help improve model performance.
  • Participating in training sessions where the team will walk through expectations, examples, and prompt-writing best practices.

Prompt creation guidelines

  • Submit one question per prompt.
  • Prompts do not need to be long. If a clear, concise question plus a formula effectively challenges the model, that’s a great result.
  • After submission, the model will generate a response.
    • You are responsible for evaluating the response for correctness.
    • Do not use external AI tools to assist with evaluation. Doing so will result in removal from the program.

How is “success” or “failure” defined?

Each AI lab has its own evaluation criteria, but most follow a “wrongness threshold”. For example, if more than a certain percentage of the answer is incorrect, it’s considered a failure.

Common model failure types include:
  • Incomplete or incorrect citations
  • Faulty logic or broken mathematical reasoning
  • Inability to integrate knowledge across domains
  • Biased or insensitive content If you’re unsure about your specific project, we recommend reaching out to your project lead for clarification.

Handshake AI’s platform & access issues

The below section applies to tasks completed on Handshake’s annotation platform. If the AI lab you’re working with has chosen to use their own platform, connect directly with your project lead for support and instructions.

Not finding your assigned project on the platform? Contact Support so our team can take a look.

Seeing the wrong project or unable to start a task? Contact Support so our team can investigate your task access.

Trouble accessing the platform with your school email? Not a problem—contact Support to share a personal email address and we’ll update your account and resend the invite.

Having issues with model responses? If a model’s response is incorrect or buggy, click the Revert button to return to a previous version. This helps maintain accuracy and provides useful feedback to our engineering team.

Working on projects from outside the United States

This article explains where Handshake AI project work can be completed and who is eligible to participate. These guidelines are in place to protect fellows, ensure data security, and meet legal and compliance requirements. They apply to all Handshake AI contractors performing paid annotation, evaluation, or task-based work.

Can I work on a project while I am outside of the United States as a US person?

All work must be completed from within the United States and associated territories. If you plan to be outside the US for 14 or more consecutive days, you must receive written confirmation from your project lead before working during that time. Work completed outside the US without prior approval may not be accepted.

Can I work on a project if I’m not authorized to work in the United States?

At this time, non-US persons are eligible to join Handshake AI on an invitation-only basis. If you’ve received an invitation, follow the onboarding steps in your invitation email to sign up and get started. If you have not received an invitation, you are not currently eligible to participate.

Reporting

How to Convert Dates and Times in Handshake Reports

Would you like to convert the dates in a report that you have downloaded in Handshake? All dates that are pulled from Handshake are in UTC time which is Coordinated Universal Time.

If your download includes the text “UTC” at the end of your date/time cell, you will first have to remove that text from each cell. To do this, highlight the cells with your dates/times and utilize the Find and Replace feature within Excel to find the “UTC” text and replace it with nothing:

Next, format those cells in the Date / Time format of your choice:

Finally, use the Excel formulas listed below to converting your dates (ST = Standard Time / DT = Daylight Savings):

EST =CellName - (5/24)

EDT =CellName - (4/24)

CST =CellName - (6/24)

CDT =CellName - (5/24)

PST =CellName - (8/24)

PDT =CellName - (7/24)

MST =CellName - (7/24)

MDT =CellName - (6/24)

How to Use AI in Insights

Insights provides an optional AI assistant that you can use to create, summarize, and modify reports. The AI is located in a few different locations in Omni, we’ll discuss where and how this assistant can be helpful for your reporting needs.

If you do choose to use the AI Assistant, we highly recommend double checking the work to ensure that the information the assistant provides you is accurate. AI is always being improved and is not yet perfected. It requires human intervention and prompting to reach desired outcomes. If you ever feel unsure about the information or report provided by the AI Assistant, contact Support.

Note: Using the AI Assistant is not a requirement for Insights. You can opt out of using the AI Assistant by not engaging with it in Insights.

Topics:

  • Introduction to the AI Assistant
  • Creating a report from scratch using the AI Assistant
  • Updating a report using the AI Assistant
  • What else can the AI Assistant do?
    • Create a visualization of data
    • Answer questions you might have about Insights
    • Create an XLOOKUP function in an existing workbook
  • What is the AI Assistant unable to do?
  • Are there limits on AI Reporting Usage?
  • Additional Resources

Introduction to the AI Assistant

The AI Assistant has a few different names we may refer to it by:

  • AI Query Builder
  • AI Query Helper
  • AI Assistant
  • Omni Agent At the end of the day, the AI Assistant is here to help you with your task. Whether it’s creating a report, modifying one that’s already existed, answer questions that you might have about Omni, or creating a visualization for data, it can do pretty much anything!

Creating a query from scratch using the AI Assistant

  • Head over to Insights and select New in the top right corner of the screen.
  • From the list of starting point topics, select Ask AI
  • This will open a chat with the AI Assistant. You can ask it to do anything at this stage, create a new report, explain different features in Insights, or tell it what information you’re trying to report on and ask it to give suggestions. The screenshot below shows an example of asking the AI Assistant to run a query on job postings created on or after 2025, as well as how the AI Assistant decided to create the report. If you want to make modifications to a report created by the AI Assistant, select the Display fields & topics button in the top left corner of the page.
  • Continue modifying the report or ask the AI Assistant to update the report until you reach your desired outcome! Tip: Since AI is generative, your mileage my vary on the response you may receive, however, a good prompt to ask the AI Assistant is: “Show [who/what] in [timeframe], grouped by [how to breakdown/visualize], with [table/chart/calculation]”

For example: “Show approved jobs created in the last 90 days at my institution, grouped by employer and job type, with a bar chart of the top 20 employers”

Updating a report using the AI Assistant

  • Open any saved report and select Explore in the upper right corner of the screen to make modifications to the report.
  • Select the (Workbook Agent button) to open a chat with the AI Assistant
  • In the chat, request that the AI Assistant make a modification to the report. For example, “add a column for the student attendees’ school year” or “filter on only active students”.
  • Check the AI Assistant’s response and the report to ensure that your request was fulfilled.

What else can the AI Assistant do?

Create a visualization of data

Go into any query that’s already been created and ask the AI Assistant to create a visualization of the data. In this example, we asked for a pie chart on employers that were created within the last 3 years and each slice shows that total number of job postings for that employer.

Answer questions you might have about Insights

For example, you might see that there’s a way to create an XLOOKUP function, but you may not necessarily know what it is. You can just ask the AI Assistant and it will give an answer for that.

Create an XLOOKUP function in an existing workbook

If you’re feeling unsure about how to set up an XLOOKUP function, ask the AI Assistant! Using the example from the above screenshot, the AI Assistant was asked to create an XLOOKUP that bring average salary data based on major into another query that has students counts by major. The AI will show its work so you can verify whether the information is accurate. Example:

What is the AI Assistant unable to do?

  • The AI Assistant cannot set up a schedule to send a report or alert. You can set up a schedule yourself by following the steps in: Analytics: Scheduled Reports
  • The AI Assistant cannot create two separate visualization charts for two different queries. If you want to do this manually, refer to the following steps:
    • Save the query as a tile on a dashboard
    • Create a second query and save it as another tile
    • On the dashboard, click Edit to arrange them side by side

Are there limits on AI Reporting Usage?

As with any AI-powered feature, we’re monitoring overall usage to ensure the service remains reliable and sustainable. This data will inform whether we implement usage limits in the future. We’ll provide ample notice before introducing any limits and rest assured that they should not impact the vast majority of schools. In the meantime, if a school’s usage approaches unusually high levels, we’ll proactively reach out and work with you before taking any action.

To learn more about efficiently using AI in Insights, refer to Insights: AI Assistant Best Practices.

Insights: AI Assistant Best Practices

Curious about how to get the most out of the Omni’s AI Assistant? Use the tips below to generate more accurate results quickly and consistently!

Some notable topics include: reducing credit usage, using specificity in AI prompts, saving reports and dashboards for efficiency, and using the AI assistant for reporting related questions only.

Start new AI sessions wherever possible rather than going back to a past session in your history

  • Similar to the way it works with Claude, long sessions can consume more credits as the context accumulates.

  • Omni surfaces a little yellow dot to try to encourage users to start new sessions when the context window starts to get full. Be specific with your questions/prompts from the start

  • The more context you give, the better and faster the answer. Instead of asking “show me student data,” try “show me a breakdown of student sign-ups by major for the past 90 days, grouped by week.” Specificity reduces back-and-forth and gets you to a usable result in fewer exchanges. Ask for one thing at a time

  • It’s tempting to ask a multi-part question in one message, but breaking complex requests into sequential steps produces more accurate results and uses credits more efficiently. Build your analysis incrementally: get the base data first, then ask for visualizations. Save and create a template of your best reports and dashboards

  • When you produce the report you need, save it. Reusing and returning to a dashboard/workbook is faster than starting from scratch and produces consistent results. Use precise date ranges and filters upfront

  • Asking for data with open-ended time ranges (e.g. “all time”) pulls more data than necessary and can produce unfocused results. Always specify the time range, cohort, or segment you care about from the start. This narrows the analysis and reduces unnecessary processing. Iterate on an existing report rather than rebuilding

  • If you have a report you like, use the AI to modify or extend it rather than generating a new one from scratch. Know when Omni AI Assistant isn’t the right tool

  • Omni is best for exploratory analysis, one-off questions, and building new reports. For reports you run on a recurring weekly or monthly basis, it’s more credit-efficient to save and schedule them directly in Omni rather than re-prompting the AI each time. Build it once with AI help, then schedule it. Omni is a reporting tool, not a stand-in for ChatGPT or Claude

  • It does not scrape the web or other resources beyond your data and any additional context you give it. Additionally, it should not be used for questions unrelated to data analysis. Review before you iterate

  • Before sending a follow-up prompt, read the full response. Many users send a correction immediately after a response without fully reading it, only to find the AI already addressed their concern. A quick read before each follow-up avoids redundant exchanges. Be explicit about the output format

  • Tell the AI how you want the output presented: “as a table,” “as a bullet summary,” “as a chart,” or “in plain text.” Without this, the AI may produce a format you have to ask it to redo, costing an extra exchange.

Insights: Data Definitions

Handshake’s reporting tool, Insights, is powered by Omni. Before you start building or exploring reports, it helps to know the core terms Omni uses, as they show up throughout the interface and in Handshake’s help articles and Academy courses.

Note: You’ll need both Analytics: Access and Analytics: Manage permissions to view and/or build reports. If you don’t have these permissions, reach out to your institution’s Handshake administrator.

The building blocks of a report

Workbook: A workbook is the container for your report. Think of it as the whole document. A single workbook can hold multiple sheets (tiles), so related visualizations and tables can live together in one place.

Sheet / Tile: A sheet (sometimes called a tile) is one page or visualization within a workbook. A workbook can contain several tiles. For example, one tile with a data table and another with a chart built from the same query.

Topic: Topics are curated, pre-organized sets of data in Omni. Each topic groups together the fields (dimensions and measures) that are relevant to a particular subject area, so you’re only working with data that’s related to what you’re trying to report on.

Explore: An explore is where you build and interact with a query — adding fields, applying filters, and shaping your results. Opening an existing report and selecting Explore creates a duplicate you can modify without affecting the original.

Query: A query is the actual request for data. The combination of dimensions, measures, and filters you’ve selected. Running a query returns your results.

Fields: dimensions and measures

Dimension: A dimension answers the question “What data do I want?” Dimensions are the descriptive columns in your table — things like student major, employer name, or event date. They’re the attributes you use to group and segment your data.

Measure: A measure answers the question “What do I want to do with my data?” Measures are the math performed on top of your data — counts, sums, averages, and other calculations.

Custom fields: Custom fields let you create reusable dimensions and measures beyond what’s built in, using modeled objects like bins, groups, or filtered measures.

Table calculations: Table calculations are Excel-style, post-query formulas — used for things like percent of total, running totals, or period-over-period comparisons. These are applied after your query has already returned results.

Shaping your results

Results: Results are the data your query returns after you run it, based on the dimensions, measures, and filters you’ve selected.

Filters: Filters answer the question “How do I get the right data?” They let you narrow your results down to the specific records you’re interested in (for example, filtering to a specific graduation year or a location radius).

Pivots: Pivots let you reorganize your results by rotating a dimension into columns instead of rows. You can only pivot on a dimension if you also include a measure (such as a count) in your data.

Saving and sharing

My Documents: Saving a report to My Documents keeps it private to you and anyone specific you choose to share it with.

The Hub: Saving a report to the Hub shares it with everyone at your institution who has access to Omni Insights.

Spreadsheet tabs: Spreadsheet tabs bring an Excel-like environment directly into your workbook, letting you connect familiar spreadsheet formulas to live query data — no exporting or manual refreshing required.

Good to Know

  • Data refresh: Data in Insights refreshes at midnight.
  • Caching: Omni caches result sets to speed up performance; cached results are shared across users based on their own data access permissions.
  • Downloadable: Any results in Insights can be downloaded to Excel — if you can’t accomplish something directly in Insights, you can always export and continue working in a spreadsheet.
  • AI Assistant: Omni includes an AI Assistant for building reports using natural language prompts. It’s a reporting tool only — it doesn’t scrape the web and shouldn’t be used for anything outside of your Handshake data. Being specific in your prompts (e.g., “show sign-ups by major for the past 90 days, grouped by week”) gets you better results faster.

Related articles

  • Insights: The Art of Reporting
  • Insights: AI Assistant Best Practices
  • How to Use AI in Insights

Insights: Employer Engagement Tracker & Reporting

Handshake provides tools to help you measure how employers engage with your school, similar to the existing Student Engagement Tracker.

For information on tracking student engagement, refer to Insights: Student Engagement Tracker & Reporting.

What employer engagement reporting shows you

Employer engagement reports help answer questions such as:

  • Which areas of Handshake do employers use the most?
  • How can you increase employer job postings, applicants, or fair attendance?
  • Which employers are the most relevant to feature in collections for your students?

Get started with the Employer Engagement Dashboard

These resources are an early-stage starting point for employer engagement reporting and may change over time.

Download the Employer Engagement Reporting Dashboard 2026.xlsx file (600 KB) located at the bottom of the page. The file contains:

  • A Directions tab with setup steps
  • An Employer List tab, where you build your employer list and populate lookup formulas that pull in each employer’s activity counts
  • Six touchpoint tabs for pasting downloaded report results: Approved & Expired Postings, Job Applications, Career Fair Registrations, Events, Interview Schedules, and First Destination Responses Follow the Directions tab to populate the Employer List and touchpoint tabs. When downloading each report from Handshake, select “Download all possible results” to capture every record.

Build individual reports for these topics

You can also create individual reports in Insights to track employer engagement instead of using the full dashboard.

Each report below lists suggested fields and filters as a starting point. You can customize them to fit your needs:

  • Employer list: Include Employer Name, Employer ID, Industry Name, and Employer Approvals Response Date. Filter on Employers = approved.
  • Approved and expired postings: Include Employer ID and Postings Count. Filter on Postings Status is approved or expired, and Postings Responded on Date is any time.
  • Job applications: Include Employer ID and Applications Count. Filter on Applications Withdrawn? No, and Applications Created at Date is any time.
  • Career fair registrations: Include Employer ID and Registrations Count. Filter on Registration Status is approved, Career Fair Status is published, and Career Fair Dates and Times Start Date is any time.
  • Events data: Include Employer ID and Events Count. Filter on Event Status is approved, Employer ID is not null, Events Host Type is any value, and Events Start Date is any time.
  • Interview schedules: Include Employer ID and Interview Schedules Count. Filter on Interview Schedule Date is any time, and Interview Schedules Status is approved.
  • First Destination responses: Include Employer ID and First Destination Responses Count. Filter on First Destination Responses Status is submitted, First Destination Responses Latest Response? is Yes, First Destination Responses Updated at Date is any time, and Employer ID is not null.

Insights: Interpreting Gender and Ethnicity in Handshake

When incorporating ethnicity and gender data in reporting, there are unique considerations to take into account. This article provides an overview of how gender and ethnicity is added to Handshake and field visibility, recommendations for checking your school’s importing status, and reporting considerations.

Importing ethnicity and gender

Schools are able to import student gender and ethnicity as a part of the student file.

The field accepts custom text, so you can include any text that you wish to upload. For instructions on importing student ethnicity or gender, refer to Importing Student Data.

How can I tell if my school is already importing this data?

These reports will show whether the majority of your students in Handshake have these fields filled out. When reviewing the reports, compare the count of students with a reported gender or ethnicity to the total number of students you have in Handshake.

If the majority of your students do not have a gender or ethnicity field designation, we recommend connecting with your team’s main point of contact for using the importer.

For any reporting regarding gender or ethnicity in Handshake, we strongly recommend starting with the anchor reports listed under the Pulling gender and ethnicity data into reporting section.

Gender and ethnicity information visibility

Gender and ethnicity information is not visible to employers in Handshake via the student profile, regardless of how the data is managed.

School-managed data

When a Career Services user views the student profile, “Gender” and “Ethnicity” fields are displayed under the heading Demographic Info, in the Personal Information section on the right of the page. Both fields may be manually managed by Career Services users with the Manage Students role or imported by the school, then used for reporting in Analytics.

Students cannot view or edit the school-managed gender and ethnicity fields or information on their profile.

Self-reported data

Students can self-report their ethnicity, gender, and pronouns in fields separate from school-managed data. These fields and information entered are only visible to and managed by the student by logging into their account.

Career Services users are not able to view self-reported data from their Career Services user account or when viewing as the student, and this data is not reported in Analytics.

Pulling gender and ethnicity data into reporting

School-managed data is available in Insights and is displayed in Results as “Students Gender” and “Students Ethnicity”.

Here’s an example of school-managed information from our demo instance:

Before creating new reports with this field, we recommend taking the following steps:

  • Check your anchor report(s) to understand how many students currently have information filled
    • Gender Anchor Report: Fields: Students Gender and Students Count. Filters: School Year Name: Alumni, Colleges Name, Educations Primary (Yes/No): Yes, Students Archived (Yes/No): No, Students Status: Active, Majors Name, Students Gender, Students Ethnicity.
    • Ethnicity Anchor Report: Fields: Students Ethnicity, and Students Count. Filters: School Year Name: Alumni, Colleges Name, Educations Primary (Yes/No): Yes, Students Archived (Yes/No): No, Students Status: Active, Majors Name, Students Gender, Students Ethnicity.
  • Review the saved report blog post linked below
Saved reports

We have lists of saved reports that can be used as a starting point of student engagement data for gender and for ethnicity. We provide an overview of these reports in our blog post: DEI Report Templates to Drive Equitable Engagement.

Custom reports

If you’d like to include gender and/or ethnicity in custom reports you created, you can add the dimensions “Gender” and/or “Ethnicity” from the field picker on the left of the custom report’s page, under the Students section.

These dimensions are included in the following student-based templates:

  • Applications
  • Appointments
  • Career Fairs
  • Career Fair Session Attendees
  • Events
  • Experiences
  • First Destination Responses
  • Interview Reviews
  • Interview Schedules
  • Interview Schedule Applications
  • Job Reviews
  • Room Only Interview Schedules
  • Students For more information on creating a custom report, refer to Insights: How to Create a Custom Report and Dashboard.

Insights: Scheduled Reports

Scheduled Reports enable Career Services users to more easily share data with campus stakeholders and external platforms. Reports can be in a number of formats –– image, PDF, CSV –– to minimize the need for post-processing, and they can be sent on the frequency of your choosing. This means you can create a report and then “set and forget”—Handshake will deliver the report for you.

Note: you will need both Analytics: Access and Manage permissions in order to schedule reports to an email. To select SFTP or S3 as a destination for reports, you will need a role called Schedule Reports to File Storage. If you do not have these roles, please reach out to your team’s Handshake administrator to request access.

*For additional information about the Insights workflow, refer to Handshake Academy: Scheduled Reports.

Click the collapsible headers below to learn more about that topic.

Insights

Setting up a scheduled report

Open a report that has already been saved or create a new report and save the changes you made. You can learn more about creating a new report here: Insights: How to Create a Custom Report and Dashboard

Once you’ve opened the saved report, select the Dashboard button in the top right corner and then select File from the top left corner of the page and choose Document Settings.

Note: If you select File and don’t have the option for Document settings, you will need to verify that your workbook is saved and that you are viewing the Dashboard perspective.

By default the toggle for Schedule is not enabled. Enable this setting to gain access to schedule the report.

Select File once again and choose the new option that has now appeared, Deliveries & Alerts.

The New delivery sidesheet will appear on the left side of the page. Complete the fields to set up your first scheduled report!

Note: These steps highlight everything related to scheduling a report. For Alert, refer to the next section in this article.

  • Send: Choose between sending the entire dashboard or one query
  • Destination: Choose between Email, Amazon S3, SFTP, and Webhook.
  • Delivery name: Create a name that will help your team easily distinguish what this delivery entails
  • Schedule: Select the cadence that the schedule will be sent. If you select Now, the report will send one-time, after you’ve set it up. If you select Weekly or Monthly, the report will send on the settings that you choose under those options. Read more about the Custom cadence below.
    • Custom: Enter a Cron string to customize the cadence that the schedule will be sent. An example cron string is 00 09 ? * 2,3,4,5,6 . The first four numbers indicate the time (Military time format), the question mark separates the time from the days, the represents skipping that day of the week, and any individual number represents that number of day in a week (ex. 1 = Sunday, 2 = Monday, 3 = Tuesday, etc.). Timezones can also be set below the cron string. In this example, the report would send at 9:00 AM on Mondays, Tuesdays, Wednesdays, Thursdays, and Fridays.
  • Send on: Choose the days of the week that this report will send.
  • At: Use the dropdown menu to select the time the report will send. These times are set up at 15 minute increments, if you want to send this at other times outside of the 15 minute increments, use the custom schedule option.
  • Times are in: Use the dropdown menu to choose any timezone.
  • Test Now: Send yourself a test email of what the scheduled report might look like for recipients. If you do not receive your test email within an hour, try again or contact Support.
  • Send: Select this and the schedule will be created, the report will send at the allotted times and days. You can modify the schedule at any time. There are additional steps for the Dashboard and Email when setting up a schedule.
Dashboard
  • Format: Choose between PNG (Image), PDF, XLSX (Excel), CSVs (in ZIP file), Link back to dashboard. This is how the dashboard will show up for recipients of this scheduled report.
  • Expand tables: Selecting this will ensure that the tables in the dashboard are expanded to 1,000 rows.
  • Arrange dashboard tiles in a single column: Places multiple dashboard tiles into a horizontal column.
  • Hide title: Select this to hide the title of the saved report from above the report.
  • Include a link back to the dashboard:
  • Use cached results if available: If the recipient has received or viewed this dashboard before and their browser has cached data that matches the data in the dashboard, the results will load faster for them if this is enabled.
Email
  • File name (without extension): Provide a filename (e.g. query-dashboard) and the selected format will appear at the end as an extension (e.g. .png).
  • Recipients: Choose recipients to receive this email. Recipients do not need a Handshake account to receive the email.
  • Personalize content with recipient’s user attributes: If the recipient does have a Handshake account, they will see content specific to their account. For example, if they are missing permissions to access certain data, that data will not appear in the email.
  • Subject: Represents text that will appear in the subject line of the email.
  • Body: Represents text that will appear in the body of the email.
Final steps

After you’ve entered your settings and customized the scheduled report to your preferences, you can use the buttons at the bottom of the page to finalize your decision on saving this scheduled report.

  • Test Now: Send yourself a test email of what the scheduled report might look like for recipients. If you do not receive your test email within an hour, try again or contact Support.
  • Delete: This option only appears after saving the scheduled report. Selecting this will delete the schedule you’ve set up.
  • Save: Select this and the schedule will be created, the report will send at the allotted times and days. You can modify the schedule at any time.

Setting up a Scheduled Alert

Alerts send updates to recipients if a query has met a certain condition to trigger an alert. For example, you want your recipients to receive an alert whenever data on a dashboard has changed.

After opening the Deliveries & Alerts, select Alert as the delivery type. Most of the fields match the process for Setting up a scheduled report. However, there are some fields available specifically for alerts:

  • Results to check: Select the query that will be checked for the alert notification to send.
  • Condition: Choose between Results have changed, Results have stayed the same, No results are returned, Any results are returned. Our system will use this condition to determine whether the condition has occurred within the query selected. Check the dashboard and email tabs to verify that the settings meet your expectations.

Note: The schedule cadence for alerts are not determined on the schedule in these settings. Alerts are sent whenever the condition is met. That means if you set this alert on a weekly schedule, it will still only send when “Results have changed” on the query.

Select Save and you can hover over the bell icon on the next screen to verify what conditions are set for this alert. This example states Sends when “Query” returns results that have changed.

Note: Scheduled Reports to an SFTP or Amazon S3 will only be visible to the schedule creator.

FAQs

Q: What is SFTP and why would I use it? Can HS set it up for me?

A: SFTP stands for Secure File Transfer Protocol –– it’s essentially a secure location that can receive files from Handshake. Because the data may likely contain PII (Personally Identifiable Information), Handshake ensures the options for export remain private and secure. Your IT contact should be able to set up an SFTP location with access permissions. Handshake will not set up the SFTP server on behalf of our partners due to the inherent security considerations.

To learn more about set up, refer to the Looker Documentation. To receive SFTP deliveries from Handshake, be sure your network admin has added Looker’s IP addresses to your SFTP server’s IP allowlist or inbound traffic rules.

For Omni Insights, the necessary Public IP addresses to unblock are as follows:

  • 54.172.168.164
  • 52.205.119.255
  • 3.211.115.21
  • 44.199.154.198
  • 54.213.219.131
  • 52.33.167.28
  • 54.213.140.155
  • 34.215.77.3 Q: What time of day do reports arrive? Can it be changed?

A: You can select the time that you would like to receive the report!

Q: My report filenames don’t contain timestamps when they’re being delivered. Can users add a date/time stamp to filenames for scheduled SFTP reports in the Insights tool?

A: Yes. Although timestamps are not included by default, users can add {{currentDate}}{{currentTime}} to the filename setting when creating the delivery. For example: query-dashboard-{{currentDate}}{{currentTime}}. See the Omni documentation on dynamic date and time content for more information.

Q: Why can’t I email a report to someone else?

A: At this time, scheduled reports can only be sent to your own email address. Handshake may consider opening this up at a later date. The intent is to ensure data is not inadvertently sent to people who should not have access to it, so we are taking a conservative approach at this time.

Q: Is there a row limit on data pushed?

A: Handshake’s analytics service is backed by Looker (Google), which has placed some limits on the data that may be delivered to email / SFTP / Amazon S3 –– Read the details in Looker’s scheduling and sharing article. The summary is:

  • Email
    • CSV or JSON formats do not have row limits, but have a file size maximum of 15MB so your email client doesn’t reject it.
  • SFTP
    • CSV or JSON - No row limit Q: What about other destinations like Dropbox?

A: There are numerous locations that can serve as intermediary ‘destinations’ for exported data. Handshake started with SFTPs because of their low-cost and ubiquity. If there are specific destinations you’d like added, we plan on releasing more options in the future, so please let us know what serves you best.

Q: Who’s allowed to send reports to Email, SFTP, or Amazon S3?

A: Any user with Access and Manage Analytics permissions can schedule reports to be sent to their email address. There is a permission “Schedule Reports to File Storage” that needs to be granted for users to send reports to an SFTP or Amazon S3 destination.

Q: Would you recommend I use my own Handshake account to send reports, or should I set up a separate ‘system user’ account to manage the process?

A: This is up to you. The benefit of a system user is that it can remain untouched and a dedicated user account on which to run your automated exports. If your personal account becomes deactivated (if you leave the school, for example), having a separate account can be useful. However, be sure to control password and lock down permissions to ensure this doesn’t become a risk for improper access to student data.

Q: What happens to the scheduled report if the saved report changes?

A: If the original report is edited and changes saved, the scheduled report will reflect those changes. Therefore, be careful not to disrupt automated reporting. It is recommended that SFTP and 3rd-party system integrations use a saved report that is a dedicated ‘integration’ export report.

Tip: if you’d like to use another user’s saved report, we recommend to duplicate that report and save the duplicate as a dedicated schedule version, as described in Analytics: Using Saved Reports.

Q: Can we use AZURE SFTP to receive Scheduled Reports?

A: At this time our data partner, Looker, does not support the host_key algorithm used by Azure SFTP. Any attempts to send reports to Azure SFTP will result in this error:

“Connection failed. Upload to SFTP host ‘______________’ failed due to error: Net::SSH::Exception. Error: could not settle on host_key algorithm. Please check your credentials.”

Insights: Sharing Reports

In Insights, the Share button opens a window to determine which users you wish to share the report with. This Share button is only available after your query or dashboard has been saved. Sharing does not generate a URL, as direct URLs are not available for Insights.

Sharing Workbooks

Open a saved workbook and select the Share button.

As the owner of the workbook, you have the ability to share this with others at your institution. It’s important to note that only user accounts that have accessed Insights can have a workbook shared with them. That means even if someone has permissions to access or manage analytics, they still won’t appear as someone to share the workbook until they open Insights. Someone who has accessed Analytics is referred to as an embed user.

Select Share with users or groups to look up who you can send this workbook to.

Select Viewer to modify the permissions that the users can have:

  • Viewer: View dashboard (you can use the settings to allow them to view the workbook as well).
  • Editor: Edit dashboard & workbook
  • Manager: Edit dashboard & workbook & manage permissions. Select Settings on the bottom left of the box to open up additional settings. Each option is defined and explained here, select Access if you want to go back to your share options.
Copying a query tab to another workbook

It may be helpful to copy a query from one workbook to another. In order to do this, select the dropdown arrow in the lower-left side of the screen. Then choose Copy to…

A prompt will appear to Copy to existing workbook. You can either manually highlight and copy the query ID or you can select Copy Query ID to automatically copy the ID.

After you open another workbook, you can select Edit and Import Tab…

This open a prompt and you can paste the query ID, select Import. The tab will be added to this workbook.

For more foundational knowledge on Insights, please refer to Analytics: The Art of Reporting and for overall reporting guidance, Getting Started with Reporting on Handshake.

Note: you will need both Analytics: Access and Manage permissions in order to view, save, and share reports. If you do not have these permissions, please reach out to your team’s Handshake administrator to request access.

Insights: Student Engagement Tracker & Reporting

Handshake provides tools to help you measure how students engage with your school.

For information on tracking employer engagement, refer to Insights: Employer Engagement Tracker & Reporting.

What student engagement reporting shows you

Student engagement reports help answer questions such as:

  • How many students are taking advantage of the resources available on Handshake?
  • How many students are engaging directly with your career services office?

Understand how the Student Engagement Tracker works

The Student Engagement Tracker is an Excel spreadsheet that combines data from several Insights reports into one view.

Create each report listed below, download it, and paste the contents into the corresponding tab of the Master Data Tracker. The Data Wrap-Up tab automatically combines the data to show high-level trends in how students have interacted with your career office.

This spreadsheet supports up to 45,000 rows. If your institution has more students than that, extend the formulas in the Merge Master tab to cover the additional rows.

Get started with the Student Engagement Dashboard

These resources are an early-stage starting point for student engagement reporting and may change over time.

Download the dashboard that matches your institution. Both files are attached at the bottom of this article.

Build individual reports for these topics

You can create individual reports in Insights to track student engagement. Each report below lists suggested fields and filters as a starting point. You can customize them to fit your needs:

  • Student data: Include Student Email - Institution, Students First Name, Students Last Name, Students Username, School Year Name, Colleges Name, and Majors Name List. Filter on Students Archived (Yes/No) is No, Students Status is active, Assigned to Disabled? (Yes/No) is No, Note Created by (Career Service Staff) Disabled? (Yes/No) is No, and Educations Primary? (Yes/No) is Yes.
  • Login and notes data: Include Students Email - Institution and Notes Count. Filter on Students Archived? (Yes/No) is No, Students Status is active, Assigned to Disabled? (Yes/No) is No, and Note Created by (Career Service Staff) Disabled? (Yes/No) is No.
  • Appointments data: Include Student Email - Institution and Appointments Count. Pivot on Appointments Drop-In? (Yes/No). Filter on Students Archived (Yes/No) is No, Students Status is active, Staff Member Disabled? (Yes/No) is No, and Created by Disabled? (Yes/No) is No.
  • Job applications: Include Applicant (student) Email - Institution and Applications Count. Filter on Applicant (student) Archived? (Yes/No) is No, and Applicant (student) Status is active.
  • Interview student applications: Include Applicant (student) Email - Institution, Interview Schedule Applications Count, and Interview Schedules Count. Filter on Applicant (student) Archived? (Yes/No) is No, and Applicant (student) Status is active.
  • Events data: Include Student Attendees Email - Institution and Events Count. Filter on Student Attendees Archived? (Yes/No) is No, and Student Attendee Status is active.
  • Career fair data: Include Student Attendees Email - Institution and Student Attendees Count. Filter on Student Attendees Archived? (Yes/No) is No, and Student Attendee Status is active.

Insights: The Art of Reporting

Handshake Insights is a customizable reporting tool, powered by Omni, that helps career services teams explore and analyze their institution’s Handshake data.

Use Insights to build and refine reports with dimensions, measures, and filters, then save and share them with colleagues.

Before you begin

To complete the reporting tasks in this article, you need both of the following permissions:

  • Analytics: Access
  • Analytics: Manage If you do not have these permissions, contact your institution’s Handshake administrator.

Build and refine reports in Insights

Expand the headers below for guidance on reporting tools, results, filters, and best practices.

What are the main parts of the reporting page?

An Insights report is called a query. A query displays data within a workbook.

The reporting page includes the following components.

Data table

The data table displays the fields you add to the query.

By default:

  • Dimensions appear on the left in black text.
  • Measures appear on the right in green text.
Field picker

The field picker appears on the left side of the page. Use it to find and add dimensions and measures to your query.

Fields are organized into categories. Click a category to display its available dimensions and measures.

  • Dimensions are descriptive fields used to identify or group records, such as Student Name, Major Name, or Employer Name.
  • Measures are calculated values, such as a count, percentage, sum, or average.
Results, filters, and pivots

You can use dimensions and measures as results, filters, or pivots.

  • Results determine which fields appear in the data table. Click the name of a dimension or measure to add it as a result.
  • Filters limit the records included in the query. Point to a dimension or measure, move to the right, then click Filter.
  • Pivots display dimension values horizontally with their associated counts. Point to a dimension, move to the right, then click Pivot. To pivot on a dimension, include a measure, such as a count, in the data table.

What controls are available above the data table?

The controls above the data table are available in the Results, Chart, and Both views.

  • Options: Customize the query, including column height and width, totals, field display, and pivot options.
  • Natural language filter: Enter a request in plain language for the AI Assistant to configure filters.
  • Summarize results: Ask the AI Assistant to summarize the displayed results and identify key observations.
  • Download results: Select a file name and format, apply formatting, and choose whether to download all rows or only the rows allowed by the current limit.
  • Limits: Set the maximum number of rows returned by the query.
  • Run query: Refresh the query after changing its fields, filters, or other settings. How do dimensions work in Insights?

Dimensions describe attributes of the records included in a query. The following examples explain how to locate or interpret dimensions used in common reports.

  • Profile Completion: Profile completion counts and percentages are available in the Student Engagement Dashboard. To include profile completion information in a custom report, use the Students topic, then open the Profile Completion category in the field picker to access the available dimensions and measures.
  • Registered compared with Checked In: Registered means the student registered for the fair or event. Checked In = Yes means the student checked in at the fair or event. If the event date has passed and a student is registered but not checked in, Handshake records the student as not having attended. How do measures work in Insights?

Measures calculate or summarize values in a query. Some measures can also combine multiple values into one result.

  • Name List measures: Use a Name List measure when a student or other record can have more than one value and you want the record to appear only once.
    • For example, a student with two majors appears twice when Major Name is included as a result. If you use Major Name List instead, the student appears once and both majors are combined in a single cell. How do filters work in Insights?

Every dimension and measure within a topic can be used as a filter.

How do I select filter values?

When using is equal to or is not equal to, click the filter’s text field to display the available values.

How do I filter by institution label?

Institution labels are labels created and applied to records by your institution.

To include or exclude specific institution labels:

  • Add the institution_labels_name dimension as a filter.
  • Select is equal to to include specific labels or is not equal to to exclude them.
  • Select or enter the applicable label names.
  • Run the query.
How do AND and OR filters work?

Within a single filter containing multiple values, Insights uses OR logic.

For example:

Major Name is equal to Business Administration OR Business Analytics OR Economics.

Across two or more separate filters, Insights uses AND logic.

For example, if a query includes a Major Name filter and a School Year Name filter, a student must match:

  • One of the selected majors
  • One of the selected school years This is the default filter behavior.

Custom filters can apply different logic, but they are limited to dimensions and measures available in the selected topic. A custom filter cannot add data from another topic.

Custom filters can also be used with institution labels. Label values are treated similarly to major values.

For custom filter syntax, review Looker Expressions: Functions and Operators.

How do I exclude a value from a field that can repeat?

For a field that allows only one value per student, does not equal excludes the matching student record as expected.

For a field that can contain multiple values, such as Institution Label Name or Major Name, does not equal excludes only the matching value. The student may still appear because another value remains associated with the student.

For example, if a student has several institution labels, excluding one label does not automatically exclude the student’s other label records.

To exclude any student whose profile contains a specific value:

  • Add the List version of the field, such as Label Name List.
  • Add that field as a filter.
  • Select doesn’t contain.
  • Enter the value you want to exclude.
  • Run the query. Because the List field combines the student’s values, the filter evaluates all applicable values together.
Can I paste a large list of filter values?

You can copy values from one report and paste them into a filter in another report. There is no set limit to the number of values you can paste, but larger lists can reduce browser performance.

If you paste hundreds of values, the browser may ask whether you want to close the page or wait. You may need to select Wait more than once.

For better performance:

  • Divide the original report into smaller groups.
  • Copy fewer values at a time.
  • Paste each group into the applicable filter.
How do I filter by distance from a location?

Add the Lat_long dimension as a filter and use the following format:

100 miles from 41.8781136, -87.6297982

Replace the distance and coordinates with the values for your intended location.

What should I know about results in Insights?

Results are the fields selected for display in the data table. The following guidance explains how to sort, interpret, and combine report results.

Note: Insights can only report on data that already exists in Handshake.

  • Sort results: To sort results alphabetically or numerically, click a column header. Click the header again to switch between ascending and descending order.
  • Results with zero values: If a report returns zero values, confirm that you selected a topic containing the records you want to include. A topic can only return records that exist within its underlying dataset.
    • For example, to identify employers that have never posted a job, use the Employers topic instead of the Jobs topic. The Jobs topic starts with job records, so an employer without a job posting cannot appear in the results. In the Employers topic, filter the posting_count measure to values less than 1 to include employers without job postings.
  • Results with null values: Null values can appear for different reasons depending on the report.
    • Education records: If you report on student education records without filtering for primary education, the query may include secondary education records. If a student lists a high school as a secondary education record, fields that apply to a Handshake institution may return null for that record.
    • Employer approval date: The employer approval date may be null if the employer was not approved through the standard employer approval process. In this situation, Insights may not have a recognized approval date to return.
    • Document Reviewer ID: Insights may not provide a Document Reviewer ID for every reviewer. Use the available Document Review Staff fields instead.
  • Combine results from different topics: Handshake stores data under the feature area where it was created, so one topic may not contain every field required for a report.
    • For example, job types are stored in the Jobs topic, while on-campus interview data is stored in the Interview Schedules topic. To report on job types associated with on-campus interviews:
      • Create a query using the Jobs topic and include job_id as a result.
      • Create another query using the Interview Schedules topic and include job_id as a result.
      • Download both reports.
      • Merge the datasets in a spreadsheet by matching their job_id values with XLOOKUP or VLOOKUP.
    • The Insights AI Assistant can also help create an XLOOKUP in an existing workbook. Confirm that the lookup fields and returned values are correct before using the combined results. Learn more in How to Use AI in Insights. What options are available after I save a workbook?

After you save a workbook or dashboard, additional options appear at the top of the page.

When you modify a saved workbook, it enters Draft mode. Click Draft in the upper-left corner to access the following options:

  • Publish: Save and publish the changes made in Draft mode.
  • Explore: Create an unsaved copy that you can modify without changing the saved workbook.
  • Save as: Update the workbook’s title, description, or folder location. What are the reporting best practices?

Follow these practices when building reports:

  • Run one query at a time.
  • Start with a small, simple query and add fields or calculations gradually.
  • Aim for queries that return results within a few seconds.
  • If a query takes longer, remove unnecessary fields or simplify the query.
  • Add filters to reduce the number of records being processed.
  • Download the results to a spreadsheet when you need processing that Insights cannot perform directly. When does Insights data update?

Insights data updates nightly. Changes made in Handshake today, whether manually or through Importer, appear in Insights the next day. The nightly update begins around midnight Pacific time.
