Insights: Using Saved Reports

Saved reports are available via pre-built reports from Handshake’s Product Team as well as reports shared from your school’s colleagues and other schools on Handshake.

Using a saved report can significantly reduce your time spent building a new report in Insights or Analytics. Likewise, saving your favorite reports to share with colleagues or other schools can help others save time as well!

Note: This article features content related to Analytics. Analytics will only be accessible until August 17th, 2026.

Click the collapsible headers below to learn more about that topic.

Insights

  • Select Insights on the left navigation bar, then select a location where the report is saved. In this example, we’ll use the Hub to pull up legacy reports.
  • Choose Handshake - Legacy Reports.
  • Choose one of the folders, and then select a report.
  • If you want to build on any of these reports, select Explore in the upper right corner of the page to create a duplicate of this report.
  • Add the whichever fields and filters you wish to add to this query. The data should automatically update but if it doesn’t, select the Run Query button in the upper right corner of the screen.
  • After you’ve checked that the data matches your reporting goals, select File in the upper left corner of the page and Save this workbook. Note: If you save this report in My documents, it’s shared privately with you and others you wish to share it with. If you save this report in the Hub, it’ll be shared with everyone at your institution that has access to Omni.

Best Practices & Reminders

  • Run only one report at a time for the most efficiency

  • Start small and simple and work your way up to more complicated explores

  • The best explores are those that return within a few seconds, if it takes longer than that you should try removing fields and starting simpler

    • Also, more filters = less data

  • All data can be downloaded to excel –– if you can’t do something in Analytics or Insights, you can always download the results and transform there

  • Location searches - Filter on Lat_long and use syntax of: “100 miles from 41.8781136, -87.6297982”

  • Institution Labels are the labels created/apply to that item by your school. Within each view there are “dimensions” and “measures”:

  • Dimensions - What data do I want? Dimensions are the column descriptors of your table.

  • Measures - What do I want to do with my data. Measures are the math on top of your data. Within each dimension and measure there are “results”, “filters”, and “pivots”:

  • Filters - How do I get the right data? Choosing the data that you are interested in.

  • Pivots - What if I have 2 questions? Pivoting enables dimensions to be displayed horizontally. If you are having trouble pulling a report, you can always contact Support and share the report.

Reporting Updates

Career Services users will need to have Analytics “Access” and “Manage” in order to fully use Insights!

August 2026

We have officially removed Looker Analytics from Handshake. We will keep the historical updates in this article but moving forward, all of your reporting needs will be completed in Omni Insights. Check out the May 2026 updates for more information about Omni!

May 2026

Introducing Omni Insights

This is a major update! We added a new reporting tool to improve reporting capabilities to all of our EDU partners. Some new features include:

  • Create your own dashboards: In the past, we created dashboards that were available for use to anyone with specific permissions. Those dashboards will still remain available, but you can also turn any report you create into a dashboard and update it later as well!
  • Organize your reports in an embded folder database: Your institution will have their own unique folder system. Similar to saving a file on your computer, you can choose where to save reports and organize your work in a way that makes the most sense to you and your colleagues.
  • Optional AI assistance when building a report: You can ask AI to clarify certain terms and reporting functions. You can even ask AI to start building a report for you by sharing the dimensions and measures you would like to have included in the report. You can also choose not to use AI and just build a report out manually!
  • Manage multiple tabs in one workbook: Using Insights, you can create multiple queries (reports) in one central workbook. Using this feature gives you the chance to easily jump between multiple different topics and compare the data is a seamless flow.
  • Send reports and alerts on a scheduled basis: Similar to Analytics, reports can be sent by setting up a schedule and the formats for sending a report include Email, Amazon S3, SFTP, and Webhook. Omni also allows for alerts to be scheduled so recipients will be informed whenever a certain condition is met in regards to a query or dashboard. For example, if the results for a query have changed since the alert had been set up, recipients will be informed about that! For now, Analytics will still be available. If you have reports you wish to transfer over to New Analytics, now is the time to do so.

February 2021

The new Share button

This new addition provides a way to quickly generate a shareable URL, directing the recipient to the report viewable on-screen at that time, regardless of report status. This means the link can be used for an unsaved report (either an unsaved new report or existing report with unsaved changes) without requiring you to save the report.

For more information, refer to Analytics: Sharing Reports.

Scheduled Reports

Scheduled Reports enable Career Services users to more easily share data with campus stakeholders and external platforms. Reports can be sent to your email address or a secure cloud file storage on the frequency of your choosing. Reports can be in a number of formats –– image, PDF, CSV –– to minimize the need for post-processing. This means you can create a report and then “set and forget”—Handshake will deliver the report for you.

For more information, refer to Analytics: Scheduled Reports.

What are the similarities and differences between Insights and Analytics?

The first reporting tool that we introduced on Handshake was hosted by Looker. This created opportunities for your institution to report on data so you could easily view data on Handshake as it pertains to students, staff members, and others connected to your institution.

We’ve now introduced Omni’s reporting tool under Insights. To help get you acclimated to this new feature, we will walkthrough the similarities and differences between the two tools.

Note: This article features content related to Analytics. Analytics will only be accessible until August 17th, 2026.

Topics:

  • Similarities

  • Differences

  • Terminology Similarities

  • Both reporting tools use Handshake data to build out reports, data refreshes at midnight.

  • Permissions remain the same, you need Access Analytics permissions to view reports and Manage Analytics permissions to build custom reports.

  • While Insights will include some new fields, every field that was available in Analytics will be available in Insights.

  • The explores and topics are the same across Analytics and Insights.

  • Handshake created legacy reports from Analytics will be available in Insights under the Handshake - Legacy Reports folder. Differences

  • In Analytics, you created stand alone reports. In Insights, a workbook is created and there can be multiple queries that appear as tabs.

  • Upon creating a new report, Analytics sets default filters automatically. Insights no longer sets default filters, so you can build from zero.

  • Analytics provides shareable links. Insights uses a folder storage system, workbooks can be shared within the feature.

  • Analytics could only provide pre-built dashboards, but in Insights, you can create your own dashboards. Learn more in Insights: How to Create a Custom Report and Dashboard

  • Insights provides an AI Assistant to help answer questions, define terms, and build queries. Learn more in How to use AI in Insights

  • Functions such as XLOOKUP can be completed within Insights.

  • Insights has more customizable options available for reports. Terminology

Use this table for a quick glance of some similarities and differences between Looker and Omni!

Resource Library

Add or Edit a Resource in the Resource Library

The Resource Library is where you can share curated content with students at your Institution to explore. Here, students can find the latest news, articles, and even videos to help educate and inspire them.

To access the Resource Library in Handshake, click Resources under the Communicate Category in the left navigation panel.

1. Access the resource draft editor page

Resources are created and edited within the draft editor page–the only difference between creating and editing is how you access the draft editor page.

  • Create a new Resource: Click the blue button Create Resource in the upper-right corner of the page.
  • Edit a Resource: Select the Resource you’d like to edit from the list. On the next page, click the blue button Edit to begin editing the resource. Changes within the resource draft editor page are automatically saved, and will be accessible to students when you choose to publish the resource.

2. Add or change the cover photo and add alt text

Select Add cover photo (recommended) to provide an image accessible to students. You will be able to select any image with the appropriate image format type from your personal device. Please refer to Handshake Image Size Guide for more information about images, image size, and the format types accepted on Handshake

Click the expandable header below to learn about different editing options for the cover photo.

Make adjustments to your cover photo

After you’ve added your cover photo, click the three ellipsis next to the image and select edit image to make modifications to the image.

Drag image: You can pull the image into a different position. When you hover over the image, your cursor will become four directional arrows. Click and drag the image into a desired position.

Zoom in or out: The magnifying glass slider allows you to zoom in or zoom out on the image. The slider scale ranges from completely zoomed out (left) to completely zoomed in (right).

Add alternative text: Provide descriptive text for the image that can be read by a screen reader. (145 character limit)

Click Save to close the pop up box and continue to make edits to the Resource.

3. Add or update related resource details

The following options are available when adding or editing a resource:

  • Add Title: Click to add your own custom title for this resource.
  • Select an Author: The dropdown menu below the title allows you to select any active staff member as the author of the resource. You can also select your school as the author of the resource.
  • Note: Any archived staff members will not be selectable as authors.
  • Formatting bar: You can change the style of text by clicking dropdown bar titled “Normal Text”. You can choose from the options of Normal Text, Heading 1, and Heading 2.
    • Use the formatting bar to bold, italicize, and underline the text for your resource. You can also attach a hyperlink, create bullet point or number list, create a block of quoted text, and insert an image or media link.
    • Note: The media link option supports YouTube and Vimeo links only.
      • Insert Image: After uploading the image, you will have options to resize the image by dragging the boxes near the corners in or out, insert an image link using the button at the top, and enter a caption using the text at the bottom of the image.
  • Text box: Use the text box to write the information that will be shared as your resource.
  • Attach Files: Select this to attach a file to supplement the information in the resource. Click the blue button Continue to go to the next page.

4. Adding Qualifications (optional)

Any options chosen on this page will make this available to students that fit the qualification criteria selected. The number in the top right will update automatically to show how many students can access this content.

  • School year: Select school years from the dropdown menu. After you select one, it will appear below the dropdown menu with an “x” as an option to remove that school year. You can then select more school years.
  • Individual majors: Select each individual major from the dropdown menu. To add new majors, refer to School Settings: Majors and Minors
  • Majors groups: Click Add major groups to select boxes next to each major group you’d like to add as a qualification.
  • Colleges: Choose which colleges are qualified to access this content.
  • Required labels: Select labels that students need in order to access this content. To learn more about labels, refer to School Settings: Labels
  • Career Clusters: Select career clusters applicable to your school as qualifications for this template.
  • Require minimum cumulative GPA: Checking this box will create a new box where you can enter a minimum required GPA. Click the blue button Publish Resource to publish your Resource!

Note: If you’re planning to publish your resource later, you can exit this page and publish it at a later date by using the steps below.

Publishing a drafted resource

If you have a draft of a resource that has not been published yet, you can do so by clicking on Drafts and selecting the resource.

Choose the blue button Publish to make the resource available for students!

Note: You can always undo the publishing of the resource by clicking the unpublish button, located on the upper-left of the page

Now that your resource is live, learn how to set the view order for resources in Setting the Position Order for a Resource

Create and Manage a Resource Category

Resource categories are used to group certain resources together. Grouping the resources together into a category allows ease of access for yourself, your students, and your fellow school staff members! We offer a lot of customization options for resource categories, this article will go into more detail about these options.

  • How to Create a Resource Category
  • Managing resource categories on the Resource Library page
  • Managing individual resource categories To access the Resource Library in Handshake, click Resources under the Communicate Category in the left navigation panel.

How to Create a Resource Category

  • Click on the Categories tab or select Create Category at the upper-left of the page.
  • (optional) If you clicked the Categories tab, and this is the first time your school has created a resource category, you can click the blue button Create Category to make your first category.
  • The Add title and description page:
  • Title: (required) Create a title for this category. This is required before proceeding to the next page.
  • Description: Describe this category for ease of access for your students and school staff.
  • The Add Resources page:
  • Filters:
    • All states: This filter refers to whether the resource is published or in draft. Clicking this filter allows you to narrow the list of resources on this page to Drafts and Published.
    • All authors: At default, this filter will provide resources published by any of your school staff. Clicking the filter allows you to narrow the list of resources on this page to a specific staff member.
  • Use the box on the upper-left of the list or by each individual resource to select which resources you’d like to add to this category.
  • Once you’ve select your resources, click the blue button Create New Category in the lower-right of the screen to proceed with creating the category. Note: You don’t need to add resources to the category, you can just proceed with creating the category without selecting any resources.

After you’ve created the category, you will be taken to Resource Library Category tab. Here you can manage the different resource categories, which we will explain in the next section.

Managing resource categories on the Resource Library page

  • On the Resource Library Category tab, you can click the ellipsis listed on any of the Resource Category titles to access the options available to manage that category:

  • Move to first position: Arranges the category to be listed before all other categories.

  • Move one position up: Arranges the category one space up on the category list.

  • Move one position down: Arranges the category one space down on the category list.

  • Move to last position: Arranges the category to be listed after all other categories. Note: Any of the options to move the category influences the order of categories in the staff and student view!

  • Edit category: Redirects you to the title and description page to make edits to this category.

  • Get shareable link: Automatically copies a link to the category that can be provided to students or other staff members.

Managing individual resource categories

Select any category that you’ve already created to make changes to that category.

You can select the ellipsis in the top center-right of the page to edit or delete the overall category.

Click the Share button to copy a link to share the category with students or staff members.

Click the Add existing resources button in the upper-right corner of the page to pull up a list of existing resources that you can add to this category.

Select the ellipsis on the right of an individual resource to choose from the following options:

  • Edit resource: Redirects you to the resource editing page. Learn more about editing resources here: Add or Edit a Resource in the Resource Library
  • Get sharable link: Instantly copy a link that you can share with students or staff members for this individual resource.
  • Remove from category: Instantly removes the resource from this category.
  • Delete resource: Deletes the resource from Handshake.

How to Delete a Resources Article

If you have posted an article to students in your Resources that you would like to remove from the Resources Library, you can do this easily!

First go the Resource Library from the University main page, then select the article you would like to remove, and click Edit.

Then go to the lower left and select the tab by Cancel, to then see the option to delete the resource article.

Resource Article Not Displayed In Correct Order

If it appears that a resource article is out of order, there are four possible reasons this could be happening, based on the resource article display logic or the user account you’re viewing the resource from:

  • Resource articles are displayed based on 1 of 3 variables:
      1. the position order “weight”, OR
      1. the position in the library, OR
      1. if the position order “weight” is not greater than “0”, and the library position is in the default setting “0”, the displayed order is based on resource creation date
  • Note: if there is a position order “weight” greater than “0”, this adjustment will not impact the display order in your Career Services account view.
    • In order to confirm display order, you can switch to your student account to view the Resources page. Keep in mind that adding qualifications to a resource will potentially impact the display order for students, depending on who has access to the resource.

Articles positioned with the highest number will be given the highest priority and sit at the top of the Resources page for students. If more than one article is given the same position order “weight”, then the articles will be displayed at the top of the list and in order of creation date.

For the item that is displayed out of order, click on the name of the Resource article in the Resource Library

On the Resource page, make any desired change to the Set position in library field. Be sure to make this number greater than 0 (zero) to give this resource a higher priority. The change will automatically save.

To confirm the change in display order, switch to your student account view. In the example below, I have assigned the highest order number for How to Network, so it is listed at the top.

Setting the Position Order for a Resource

After you’ve created a resource, you can decide the order the resource will appear in the students’ perspective of the Resource Library. This article will explain how to set the position order for a resource.

To access the Resource Library in Handshake, click Resources under the Communicate Category in the left navigation panel.

Click on any published resource on the Resource Library page to set the position.

Setting the Position Order

On the right side of the screen, you can set the position order by clicking in the box next to Set position in library

Enter any number above 0. The higher the number, the higher priority/position this resource will have. For example, a resource with ‌position 2 will be located higher than the resource with ‌position 1.

Student Engagement Metrics in Resources

Student engagement metrics provide your career center data to identify the frequency in which your students engage with different resources in your Resource Library.

Topics:

  • View Count and Sorting
  • Download list of resources
  • Individual resource engagement statistics
  • FAQs To access the Resource Library in Handshake, click Resources under the Communicate Category in the left navigation panel.

View Count and Sorting

On your Resource Library page, you will have access to the number of views for each resource. The count provided here is the total number of views from the past year.

A new Sort by category will be selectable. Select Last updated to sort by either Last updated, Most Viewed, or Least Viewed.

Download list of resources

The Download list button in the top right corner of the list of resources will download the full list of resources in your Resource Library. A CSV file with the following fields will be provided:

  • Resource title
  • Author
  • Last updated date
  • Category list
  • Number of total views from past 30 days
  • Number of unique views from past 30 days
  • Number of total views from past 6 months
  • Number of unique views from past 6 months
  • Number of total views from the past year
  • Number of unique views from the past year

Individual resource engagement statistics

Select a resource from the Resource Library. On the center-right of the screen, the following information is provided:

  • Total views of the resource
  • Unique student views
  • Clicks on any links in the article
  • Downloads of any attachments
  • Plays on any embedded videos* The information is reflective of the student engagement in the last 365 days. If a resource was added less than 365 days ago, then the information will be reflective of student engagement since the resource was added.

*Student engagement on embedded videos has been captured since September 22, 2023. As a result, the data will be provided from that date forward.

FAQs

What are unique views?

The number of unique students viewing the article in a certain time frame.

What are total views?

The number of total views of this page by students only.

What happens if I unpublish and republish my resource, do they view and click counts reset? No, the engagement counts do not reset. If you unpublish a resource and move it to the draft state, you are still able to see engagement stats on the draft list page. You are also able to download stats for those articles as well.

Do the counts include views on mobile or only views from desktop?

Yes, both! The counts take into account engagement from mobile and on desktop.

Do the views and clicks include interactions from career services user accounts?

No. The data you see is only generated by student user engagement. We filter out any engagement taking place from career services accounts.

If I ‘view as’ a student and then view and click on items within a Resource, will that engagement be included in the statistics?

No. Any actions when you “view as” a student are not included in these statistics.

Is this data 100% accurate? What could potentially impact the view or click counts I’m seeing? This data you see should be taken as a general indicator of what content is viewed and clicked on by your students - not a perfect representation of exact clicks. A couple of factors may impact the counts you are seeing, including:

  • Certain ad blockers that students may have added to their browsers will not allow tracking of views or clicks.
  • If you have multiple occurrences of the exact same link in the article, you will see one combined count. (For example if you included www.example.com at the top of the article and again at the bottom of the article, you will see just one view count for that link rather than two separate counts.

Employer Role Types: Advocate

Employer Role Types: Representative

The Representative role is typically assigned to individuals outside the recruiting team who need to participate in their company’s virtual fairs and events.

This role is available exclusively to on-campus employers, Essentials customers, and TES customers, who can assign an unlimited number of Representative seats. For more information, please check out this resource!

The Representative role is not available to Basic employers. To assign Representatives, you must upgrade to an eligible paid plan.

Who the Representative role is best suited for

The Representative role is ideal for individuals who need to attend and support virtual recruiting experiences but do not manage core recruiting workflows.

This includes:

  • Employees outside the recruiting team who participate in virtual career fairs and events.
  • Team members who support student engagement by managing attendee check-in and participation during events.
  • Individuals who assist with 1:1 schedules and event logistics but do not post jobs or manage applicants. Representative access consists of default permissions and module based permissions, as outlined below.

How to Configure Role Level Permissions (Role Types (Details) )

In Handshake, you can configure role level permissions to control what actions teammates are allowed to perform.

This feature is available only to Essentials and Enterprise (formerly TES) customers. For more information, please check out this resource.

Configure role level permissions

Only Owners and Admins of a company profile can configure role level permissions.

  1. Click on your name in the upper-right corner of the page, then select Company Settings from the dropdown.

  2. Select Configure Roles from the left sidebar. The page displays each role type as a column, with a list of permissions per row.

  • Permissions are grouped by feature, with a small information circle icon located on the right side of each permission. For additional details on the permission, hover your mouse pointer over the circle icon.
  1. Check or uncheck permission boxes as desired for each role. Changes are saved automatically as they are made.
  • Default permissions are already checked.
  • Available permissions have an open checkbox.
  • A gray circle with a line through it indicates that permission is not available for that role type.
  • Checkboxes that are checked but not clickable represent required permissions for that role type.

RSVPs & Check-in

Accessing Event and Fair RSVPs

After hosting an event or fair, you can easily view and manage your RSVPs to gain insights, measure the success of your outreach, and follow up with participants.

Features available only to Premium partners are indicated by an asterisk (*). For more information, please check out this resource.

Access RSVPs

  1. Click Events or Fairs from the left navigation bar, then select the event or fair you want to view RSVPs for.

Tips:

  • For fairs, select Include Past Fairs and Show Registered Only to find the fair quickly.
  • For events, select Include Past Events to narrow your search results.

  1. On the event or fair page, click the Candidates tab, then select the number displayed below Your RSVPs.

  2. A table will display all candidates who have RSVPed or checked in to your session(s) or event. Use the filters at the top of the table to refine your list.

Note: Filters marked with an asterisk (*) are available only to Premium partners.

  • Keyword search
  • *Status (only available to Premium partners)
  • *Evaluation (only available to Premium partners)
  • School To further refine your search, click the button All filters. Once clicked, a side sheet with additional filters will appear.

Basic and Plus employers can filter by:

  • School year

  • Labels / Not labels

  • Major

  • Major category

  • Graduation date (start and end) Premium partners can also filter by:

  • Status

  • Evaluation

  • School

  • Basic info (major)

  • Graduation date (start and end)

  • Major category

  • School year

  • Handshake profile (public only)

  • Touchpoints

  • Labels / Not labels

  • Evaluated by

  • Outreach-sourced invitees (includes candidates registered through campaigns or bulk messages within the last six months)

  • Sessions (career fair sessions for which your company has registered) Premium partners with the Events module can also filter by:

  • Kiosk questions (responses to configurable check-in questions)

  • U.S. work authorization

  • Preferred job location

  • Type(s) of employment

  • Areas of interest

  • Job opportunities

  • Skills Candidates without a Handshake profile or with a private profile are labeled with a human icon and the text No Handshake Profile. You can view profiles of candidates who have made their profiles public.

View kiosk responses

If a check-in kiosk was set up for your event, you can view a student’s responses after they’ve checked in.

Notes:

  • Kiosk responses are only available on desktop and do not sync in real time with the Handshake Events app.
  • Employers must use the desktop version to view this data during or after the event.

  1. Click the student’s name whose responses you want to view.

  2. A side sheet will open displaying the candidate’s kiosk responses, including:

  • Basic information
  • Work aspirations
  • Competencies
  • Custom questions (if configured)
  • Labels (if any) Note: Optional questions will appear blank if left unanswered by the student.

To view the complete profile, click View profile next to their name. Learn more about Viewing Student Profiles.

Additional resources

  • Download resumes: Easily download resumes from candidates who registered for your event or checked in at your fair booth. Learn more about Downloading Public Resumes.
  • Message attendees: Connect and engage with candidates by messaging your event and fair RSVPs. Read more about Messaging Event and Fair RSVPs.
  • Manage your RSVPs: Use evaluations, notes, and labels to stay organized. Find out more in Managing RSVPs with Evaluations, Notes, & Labels.

Creating Automated Follow-Up Messages for Evaluated Event Attendees

Employers can set up automated messages to follow up with attendees who were evaluated during or after an event, helping streamline communication based on evaluation outcomes.

This feature is available to Premium partners with the Handshake Events module. For more information, please check out this resource.

Create an automated message

  1. Click Events from the left navigation bar, then select the event where you want to create an automated message.

  2. On the event page, click the Communications tab, then click the black button Create message in the upper-right corner.

Note: Automated messages can only be sent to attendees who have received an evaluation. Attendees without an evaluation will not receive the message.

Follow up with your attendees

On the message setup page, complete the following fields:

  • Who do you want to send this message to? (select one or more evaluation statuses)
    • Select attendees based on their evaluation outcome:
      • All evaluated as a…
        • Includes all evaluated attendees, regardless of specific rating.
      • Strong yes
      • Yes
      • No
      • Strong no
  • Time trigger
    • Choose when the message should be sent:
      • When event ends — Sends immediately after the event concludes.
      • A day after event — Sends 24 hours after the event ends.
  • Enter message
    • Write a tailored message relevant to the selected evaluation group.
    • Tip: Use this space to thank attendees, provide next steps, or invite them to future events or interview.
    • You can customize your message and include:
      • Attachments
        • Learn how to Attach a job to the message.
      • Formatting options
      • Links When you’re ready, click the button Create to schedule your message. Once created, Handshake will automatically send your message based on the selected evaluation group and timing.

Attach a job to the message

  1. To attach a job to your message, click the Handshake icon in the lower-left corner of the message composer.

  2. In the pop-up modal, click the search field and either type the job title or scroll through the list to find the job.

  3. Once you find the job, click to select it, then click the button Attach.

Preview or edit your message

In the Event communications table, click the three-dot menu icon next to the message you want to preview or edit, then select Preview or Edit.

On the message setup page:

  • To preview your message, review the content shown on the screen.
    • To return without making changes, click Close.
  • To update the message, click Edit message.
    • After editing the message, click Update.

Delete your message

  1. In the Event communications table, click the three-dot menu icon next to the message you want to delete then select Delete from the dropdown.

  2. In the pop-up modal, confirm that you want to delete the message, then click the button Delete message.

  3. The message will be deleted, and the page will refresh automatically.

Managing RSVPs with Evaluations, Notes, & Labels

On Handshake, you can manage your RSVPs with evaluations, notes, and labels to follow up more efficiently.

To manage your RSVPs, navigate to the specific event or fair. Learn more about Accessing Event and Fair RSVPs.

Features available to Premium partners only are indicated by an asterisk (*). For more information, please check out this resource.

*Add evaluations and notes

Evaluations and Notes is a feature in the Events module for Premium partners. It is available to all active teammates. The feature can be used for events, fairs, and employer-hosted schedules.

  1. Click on the text “Add Evaluation” located in the Evaluation column on the far right of the student’s name.

  2. Add an evaluation and/or notes in the pop-up modal.

Note: only one evaluation can be saved per student. If you have a colleague who also wants to rate the student, your colleague should add a note with their comments.

  • Recommendation
    • Would you recommend the student?
      • Select rating
        • Strong no
        • No
        • Yes
        • Strong Yes
  • Comments
    • Include any relevant comments related to the student in the textbox if applicable.
  • Photos
    • In this section, photos of the resume or notes uploaded through the Handshake events app will be displayed. Learn more about the Handshake Events App for Employers.

  1. Click the black button Submit to save your evaluation and/or notes.

  2. After submitting the evaluation, the message “Evaluation updated successfully” appears in a black banner at the bottom of the page.

  • The Status column displays the status ‘Evaluated’ and the Evaluation column displays the student’s rating.

Update evaluation and/or notes

To update a student’s evaluation or notes, locate the student in the table and click on the rating button.

In the pop-up modal, modify the rating and any notes that have been submitted as necessary, then click the black button Submit.

Download check-ins

To download evaluations, notes, or student information, click the white button Download in the upper-right corner of the page, then select All Check-ins.

The following information is included in this CSV:

  • First Name
  • Last Name
  • Email Address
  • Graduation Date
  • Majors
  • School
  • RSVP
  • Check-in
  • Labels
  • Notes
  • Job Preferences
    • Only included for in-person fairs with a check-in kiosk
  • Evaluation Rating
  • Evaluation Photos
    • Only available to employers who have the Events module Note: if you set up a check-in kiosk, the students’ responses to the kiosk questions will also be included.

Add or remove labels

Campaigns: Audience Size

If your estimated audience size is different from your actual audience size, or if there are no recipients, this is likely due to how the campaign is configured, or the default exclusions that apply to all campaign types.

Explore Campaigns: Exclusions.

Default exclusions

There is an automated 48-hour exclusion in place to safeguard multi-sends on the same day for any initial and follow-up campaigns. This excludes recipients who received a message from the campaign creator.

In addition to the automated 48-hour exclusion, recipients who are not seeking job opportunities are automatically excluded.

Campaign targeting

To better target qualified students, we remove students from your segment that are very unlikely to engage with your campaign, which can result in a lower audience size.

Estimated audience size

The estimated audience size is an estimate of the number of students a particular campaign can reach. It is based on the assumption that the job, event, or career fair will be approved at all the schools it was requested at. Then, it estimates how many students from those schools meet the segment criteria.

However, the total count of recipients may vary at the time the campaign is sent. It is dependent upon Handshake’s default exclusions, the optional exclusions set in place by the employer, and the status of the job, event or career fair promoted.

The audience size displayed on the campaign overview page will reflect the total count of recipients reached.

Troubleshooting

Below, we highlight common reasons that can cause a low audience and solutions you can apply.

Low or no estimated audience

There are various reasons the estimated audience is 0 or lower than expected.

Reasons include, but are not limited to:

  • The job, event or fair registration was not approved at all the schools it was posted to at the time the campaign was created.

  • Exclusions are set in place (exclusions apply regardless of campaign type)

  • Automated 48-hour exclusion.

  • Exclusions were removed too quickly.

  • Overlapping segment audience Solutions include, but are not limited to:

  • Prior to sending the campaign, confirm that all the schools in your segment have approved the job, event, or fair registration because if they are not, the campaign will exclude them and result in a smaller audience.

  • Be sure to review the exclusions applied, particularly the exclusion that prevents students from receiving a message from your company within a specific time frame, and modify as necessary.

    • For example, you create a campaign for a career fair or event, and then send a job campaign immediately after. This can cause students to be excluded from the job campaign due to the default 48-hour exclusion, and if the “Received a message from” exclusion is not disabled.

  • Do not send campaigns that utilize the same segment within 48 hours. The automated 48-hour exclusion will exclude students who have received a message from the user in the past 48 hours.

  • If multiple exclusions are to be removed, allow the audience size to load after removing each exclusion. This will allow Handshake time to process each removed exclusion and recalculate the estimated audience size.

  • Minimize the impact of overlapping audience segments by carefully reviewing and refining the segment criteria.

    • For example, instead of grouping cities together based on their physical proximity, consider other characteristics such as organizations, extracurricular activities, or job role interests to ensure that they are unique and distinct from each other.

Campaigns: Exclusions

Exclusions allow senders to further filter the audience of their campaigns beyond the set of filters applied to a segment.

Premium features are for Handshake Premium accounts only. For more information, please check out this resource!

Campaign exclusions

You can apply exclusions in the Define audience section of the campaign form.

The exclusions set in the form apply to both the initial campaign send and the follow-up campaign. Most exclusions are optional and can be combined in any way you prefer.

Types of campaigns exclusions

You can optionally apply various types of exclusions to your campaign. However, some Handshake exclusions are applied by default.

Default exclusions (applied to all campaigns by default)

  • Recently messaged
    • Excludes recipients who have received a message from the campaign creator in the last 48 hours, or who have muted you (cannot be opted out of).
  • Students who are not seeking job opportunities
    • Excludes recipients who are not seeking job opportunities (can be toggled). Optional exclusions
  • Applied to a job
    • Excludes recipients who have recently applied to a job posted by your company on Handshake. The time frame for this exclusion can be 1, 3, 6, or 12 months.
  • Received a message (from you or teammates)
    • Excludes recipients who have received a message from you (campaign creator) or any other teammate on Handshake. The time frame for this exclusion can be 1, 3, 6, or 12 months.
  • Employer labels
    • Excludes recipients that have any custom labels attached to their profile by your company on Handshake.

Follow-up campaign exclusions

You can apply exclusions to the follow-up message in the Write message section of the campaign form.

  • Exclude students who replied to this campaign (optional)
    • Excludes recipients who have already responded to the initial campaign message.
  • Exclude original job posting attachment (only displays in job form campaigns)
    • Prevents the job posting attachment from being included. If you’ve received an unexpected estimated audience size, refer to Campaigns: Audience Size.

Campaigns: Manage a Campaign

After creating and scheduling your campaign, you can manage it as needed.

Once your campaign has been sent and completed, review your Campaign: Results.

Premium features are for Handshake Premium accounts only. For more information, please check out this resource.

Topics:

  • Edit a campaign
  • Cancel a campaign
  • Archive a campaign

Edit a campaign

To edit a campaign that is in progress or scheduled, refer to Campaigns: Editing a Campaign.

Cancel a campaign

  1. Navigate to the Scheduled tab, select the campaign you want to cancel, then click the circle-backslash icon on the far right.

Notes:

  • Campaigns can only be canceled if they are scheduled or in progress.
  • Dynamic campaigns cannot be canceled or stopped once they are in progress.
  1. Confirm the action in the pop-up modal, then click the button OK to cancel the campaign.
  • If you prefer to keep the campaign, click the button Cancel.
  1. Once canceled, the message “Campaign was successfully cancelled” displays in a black banner at the bottom of the page.

Archive a campaign

Campaigns can only be archived if they are not scheduled.

Note: Campaigns cannot be deleted. They can only be archived.

  1. Navigate to the Drafts tab, select the campaign you want to archive, then click the bin icon on the far right.

  2. Once archived, the message “Campaign was successfully archived” displays in a black banner at the bottom of the page.

How to Build a Segment

A segment is a filtered group of students you can use to create a campaign or identify job matches.

Premium features are for Handshake Premium accounts only. For more information, please check out this resource.

Access segments

Click Segments from the left navigation bar. This page lists active segments created by you and your teammates, as well as archived segments.

Each segment in the table includes the following details:

  • Name: The name of the segment

  • Date Created: The date the segment was created

  • Count: The number of students in the segment

  • Schools: How many schools are included

  • Owner: The creator of the segment You can take the following actions on any segment using the icons in the table:

  • Envelope: Initiate a campaign directly from this segment

  • Pencil: Modify or update the segment details

  • Paper: Create a duplicate of the segment

  • Trash bin: Archive the segment to remove it from active use

Create a segment

  1. Click the Create Segment button in the upper-right corner of the Segments page.

  2. Select filters to identify the students you want to include. As you select filters, the results on the right update in real time. Adding more filters will generally reduce the number of students included.

Important things to know about filters:

  • Candidates are included based on all education details they have made available on their Handshake profiles.
  • If you filter for BA candidates who majored in Business, results may include candidates who completed that degree and are currently pursuing a higher degree, such as a Masters.
  • Segments are fluid. Students move in and out of segments as their profiles change. For example, if a student updates their major or graduation year, they may no longer match the segment criteria.

What filters are available when creating a segment?

Schools

  • Select individual schools or add a school list

  • Handshake Open Network (students at 4-year accredited U.S. institutions not directly partnered with Handshake)

  • Include or exclude Community and Technical Colleges Academic Profile

  • Profile Keyword

  • Major Group (consolidates majors across schools into a common taxonomy)

  • Major Keyword

  • Major Category: STEM, TEM Only, or Liberal Arts Graduation and Class Standing

  • New Grad Hires

  • Intern Hires

  • Recent Grad Hires

  • Custom graduation date range Work Authorization

  • Does not have work authorization (will need sponsorship)

  • Has work authorization (will not need sponsorship)

  • Status unknown GPA

Interests and Goals

  • Job Role Interests

  • Candidate Industry Interests

  • Candidate Job Seeking Interests: Full-Time or Part-Time Location

  • Student Location Preferences

  • Candidate Location Preferences

  • Current Location Language

  • Desired Language

  • Proficiency Level

  • Note: You must add at least one language proficiency level to save your segment. Skills and Experience

  • Desired Skills

  • Coursework

  • Work Experience Activities

  • Organizations/Extracurriculars

  • Achievements and Accolades Underrepresented Groups

  • Organizations (by type)

  • Institutions (by type)

  • Note: If you select an underrepresented group filter, you must also select at least one other filter. These filters cannot be used alone.

Save your segment

  1. Once you have selected your filters, enter a name for your segment in the upper-right corner of the page, then click Save Segment.

Segments: Coursework

Filtering potential candidates based on their coursework allows you to create targeted, personalized recruitment campaigns.

Premium features are for Handshake Premium accounts only. For more information, please check out this resource!

  • During onboarding, candidates enter their coursework details, which are considered trustworthy as Career Services reviews each profile.
  • Our proprietary Coursework Taxonomy, developed by our data science team and validated by external sources, maps individual courses to Subject Areas, allowing you to choose one Subject Area and view all candidates who have taken relevant courses without entering every possible keyword.

Using the coursework filter

  1. Select whether you want to search by Subject Area or by Specific Course.

  2. If Subject Area is selected, choose a Subject Area from the dropdown, or type to search.

Note: to view all Subject Areas, download and refer to the excel file attached below.

  1. Optionally, restrict your subject area to only candidates with “beyond introductory level” skills.

This means that candidates have taken a few courses in that area or have courses with specific keywords, such as “Advanced.”

If you have multiple subject areas selected, we’ll select candidates who have beyond introductory level skills in either subject area.

  1. If you choose to search by a Specific Course, enter your keyword normally.

We’ll search all candidates with a course containing that keyword.

Segments: Job Seeking Interests

Segments help you easily find and recruit candidates based on their job-seeking interests, creating a positive candidate experience.

Learn more about How to Build a Segment.

Premium features are for Handshake Premium accounts only. For more information, please check out this resource.

The candidate filter Candidate Job Seeking Interests indicates a candidate’s preferred employment type.

In Segments, the filter allows you to select either Full-Time, Part-Time, or both.

  • When using segment filters, the candidates included are determined by reviewing all of the education details that candidates have made available on their Handshake profiles.
    • For example, if you’re seeking BA candidates who majored in Business, the results may display candidates who have completed a B.A degree in that specific degree, and are in pursuit of a higher degree, e.g., Masters. As filters are added, a dynamic query will update with the number of candidates that meet the filters selected.

To target the right audience, a candidate’s employment preference is automatically matched to your campaign’s audience criteria.

  • Candidates who have indicated their disinterest in part-time work will be excluded from all job campaigns advertising part-time positions.
  • Candidates who have indicated that they are not interested in full-time work will be excluded from all job campaigns advertising full-time positions.
  • Candidates who didn’t state a preference will be included in all campaign advertisements for either full-time or part-time positions.

  • When using segment filters, the candidates included are determined by reviewing all of the education details that candidates have made available on their Handshake profiles.

You can further customize your segment by adding other filters, such as the candidate’s location preferences, or achievements and accolades.
  • The Location filter retrieves data from the candidate’s current work experience..

The candidate filter Graduation and Class Standing indicates a candidate’s class year, as well as degree type.

  • When using segment filters, the candidates included are determined by reviewing all of the education details that candidates have made available on their Handshake profiles.
    • For example, if you’re seeking BA candidates who majored in Business, the results may display candidates who have completed a B.A degree in that specific degree, and are in pursuit of a higher degree, e.g., Masters.

Select preferences

I’m looking for

In the section, select one of the following options:

  • New Grad Hires
  • Intern Hires
  • Recent Grad Hires
  • Custom
Class Of

Once selected, we’ll use our smart defaults to pre-select the corresponding class of to match your search. Although pre-selections for class of are made, you can adjust the filters at any time.

Note: if you choose “custom graduation date range”, the smart defaults aren’t available.

Custom graduation date (not required)

As filters are added, a dynamic query will update with the number of candidates that meet the filters selected.

Annual updates

We rotate ‘Class Of’ labels once per year (on July 1st), so they will always be updated for the current School Year.

Your existing segments will remain as is - the target audience may shift but the criteria will remain in place.

  • Class Of / Degree Types: all school years will be retained - they’ll just be updated to reflect the new Class Of / Degree Types.
  • Grad Date Range: all graduate date ranges will be migrated to maintain their graduation date range.
