Student Account Management

About Actions in the Student Profile

The Actions section within a student’s profile allows Career Services users to:

  • View as this student
  • Go to Documents
  • Schedule appointment
  • More actions
    • Send Message
  • View Appointments
  • Add note
  • Explore activity snapshot
  • View public profile
  • Review student documents
  • View calendar
  • View student record For more information on accessing a students profile, refer to How to View a Student’s Profile.

View as this student

If you would like to access Handshake from a particular students account, this action provides permission to do. For more information, refer to How to View as a Student.

Go to Documents

If a student has documents connected to their student profile, this action will direct you to their documents page.

Schedule An Appointment

If you would like to schedule an appointment on behalf of a student, this action will direct you to the Appointments page to create a new appointment for them.

Send Message

If you would like to send a student a personal message, or follow-up message from an appointment, this action will open a new message box directly from their profile.

View Appointments

This action opens all past appointments the student attended at your institution.

Add Note

Selecting this will open up the Add note prompt. At the top of the prompt you can use the Visibility options to share the note with staff, keep the note private so only you can view it, or share the note with specific career centers at your institution on Handshake. You can also use the Reminder (optional) field to set the date and time for when you’ll be notified about the note. The reminder depends on your notification preferences, refer to Career Services User Settings: Manage Your Notifications for more information.

After you select Add, a confirmation message will appear in the lower right corner of the screen.

Explore activity snapshot

This will direct you to a Dashboard that includes actions the student has taken in the system and other personal information such as:

  • Student Information
  • Last Login Date
  • Total Logins
  • Documents
    • loaded to the students profile
  • Notes
    • General (only shared notes can be accessed)
  • Appointments
  • Career Interests
  • Applications
  • Event & Career Fair Attendance
  • First Destination Responses
  • Reviews
  • Experiences
  • Room Only Checkins

View public profile

Career services users have access to more information on a students profile than employers. If you would like to confirm the information that employers can view, this action allows you to do so!

Review student documents

If a student has a Document loaded to be reviewed, this action will direct you to their document.

View calendar

Directs you to the present day on the student’s calendar. This will show their availability as listed on Handshake.

View student record

This action displays the student’s appointment record in Handshake thus far.

About Student On-boarding

Handshake has redesigned the on-boarding experience for new students to better set them up for success. This new experience not only looks brighter and cleaner, but it will also communicate to the student the value of showcasing their skills and experience to employers.

Claiming accounts in Handshake is how we allow students to decide to share their information publicly to employers and other students in the network. Whether a student decides to become public in Handshake is entirely their decision and is also a decision they can easily change later.

When they click that they want employers to be able to find and view their profile, they are consenting to the section of our terms of service and claiming their own account. By doing so, they are taking ownership of all of the data on that profile. That information no longer needs to be protected by the university’s GDPR responsibility and is owned by the students.

For an overview of how it works in the system, please refer to The Student On-boarding Experience.

Add an Existing Student Account to Your Institution

If a student has created a Handshake account, but they are not in your user requests, and not connected to a different school, or if you accidentally rejected the original request, you can still add them by following these steps:

  1. Click Manage on the left navigation bar to access the Manage Students overview page.

  2. Select the three dots in the top right of the page and choose Add existing user by email.

  3. This will bring up the Add existing pop up message. You can enter a student’s email address and select Add student to add them to your institution’s instance in Handshake. A message will appear confirming the success of adding the student.

Additional Email Addresses for Students

Students may add additional email addresses to Handshake and opt to use them to receive communications from your team and from Handshake.

Institutions may import multiple .edu email addresses, or personal email addresses (e.g. gmail.com), per student account. To import additional email addresses, refer to additional_email_addresses in Importing Student Data.

Topics:

  • Additional email addresses configuration
  • Student login and data imports
  • Check-In Kiosk and Importing attendees
  • Deleting an additional email address
  • Additional Resources

Additional email addresses configuration

Student email addresses will fall into one of these definitions below:

  • Primary email address: The email address where students receive all emails that your team sends via Targeted Emails, and all emails from Handshake.
  • Institution email address: The email address your team imports into Handshake.
  • Additional email address: Any other email addresses that a student shares with Handshake. These could be personal emails or alternative .edu emails. Students can enter as many additional email addresses as they wish. Note: when “viewing as” a student, you will be able to view the student’s institution provided email address, the designated primary email address (if they have added an additional email and marked it as Primary), and there will be no option to add another email.

In order to access the exact view students have, you will need to “switch users” to your student account. Read more on Switching User Views.

For the steps students take, refer to (and share!) our student-facing article: Update Your Primary Email Address in Handshake.

Student login and data imports

With the introduction of additional email address support for students, there are no changes to our login flow. If your institution uses single sign on (SSO), that’ll still be the login method that’s displayed most prominently for students.

As far as login is concerned, the update is focused on helping students continue to access Handshake after graduation if they lose access to their institution email or SSO.

The institution provided email address imported by your team will be the student’s default primary email address. If you import any additional .edu emails, or if the students choose to use an alternate email address as their primary email instead, the main institution provided email will still be:

  • associated with their student account
  • be connected to your student file imports
  • available for and included in reporting A student’s primary email address and institution email addresses in Handshake are viewable via user account settings. This means if a student updates their primary email address, you’ll be able to capture their new, preferred contact information.

Note: when reporting in Handshake, use the dimension “Email - Institution” for email addresses imported by your institution, and use “Email - Primary” to identify the email address the student uses to receive emails sent by Handshake and your institution. This matches the institution email by default but can be updated by the student.

Check-In Kiosk and importing attendees

When a student adds an additional email to their account, all confirmed emails will work to check them into a kiosk. This is the case for appointments, events, career fairs, and FDS kiosks. The additional email will also work as a “signed out” FDS link that might be distributed.

Note: if you are importing a student attendees file for a historic event or career fair, only the institutional email will work.

Deleting an additional email address

If a student adds an email themself, they have the option to remove the email at any time in Handshake. For the student workflow, refer to Update Your Primary Email Address in Handshake.

If a student would like to remove an email that’s been imported, they’ll need to contact their career services center. If a student does reach out, be sure to update any recurring Importer jobs that may have the student’s additional email address listed.

Important: you’ll need to reach out to the person that manages your student sync to ensure that the requested account is removed from the student syncs. This will prevent the account from being recreated in future imports.

Additional Resources

For more information about how this benefits students and your team, check out our blog post Supporting additional email addresses for students.

The Banner Message for Updating Students to Alumni

To streamline updating school years to alumni after the students have graduated, we added a banner that asks if you wish to update student accounts that have been listed as “Senior” in Handshake for over 3 years. This message appears at the top of the Handshake homepage when you log in, as well as the Manage students page. You must have the Manage School Profile, Manage Students, and Manage Analytics permissions in order to view this message. Learn more about roles and permissions here: School Settings: Career Services Staff Roles and Permissions

Select View students to download a .CSV file with a list of the students.

Select Update to alumni to change these students’ school years to Alumni. It may take up to an hour for the school years to change. This will remove the banner for all Career Services staff members at your institution until another student account is listed as a Senior for more than 3 years.

Select X to dismiss this message for your own account. The message will still appear for other Career Services staff members and the message will re-appear for you after 30 days.

Additional Resources

Importer: Updating Graduating Students to Alumni

School Year Options in Handshake

Best Practices: Non-Degree Seeking Students

If your school has some non-degree seeking students that you’d like to have access to Handshake, below are some tips for easily identifying these students and managing data.

These tips can help you ensure that your reporting on degree seeking students is as accurate as possible, while helping you target the right demographic for on-campus activities via qualifications/requirements.

To identify or exclude these students from impacting degree seeking data, you could:

  • Set them to alumni: if you do not include alumni in your reporting data, this is a good way to ensure that the numbers to not have an impact.
  • Apply a label: this provides the most flexibility in reporting and identifying students via filters
    • This also allows you a variety of options for setting requirements and qualifications via labels, as well as increased visibility into reporting data. To manage student data:
  • If the students are included in Importer, you can leave school year blank, you just need to keep header in the import file.
  • If you want to ensure these student aren’t impacted by Importer jobs, you can manually exclude relevant students from the sync.
    • to do this, you’ll need to visit their profile, click the Account tab, then check the box for Exclude from Automatic Syncs and save your changes.

Employer Attributes in Student On-boarding

During the on-boarding process, Handshake will now ask students what is important to them in a company.

This is what the selection will look like from a student perspective:

FAQ’s

How did you generate this list of attributes? We asked a diverse group of students from several different universities around the country what was important to them in an employer and used their own words to generate this list. We then asked questions around what type of companies exist to further expand on the individual sections. We also did a text analysis of reviews that had been submitted by students about employers to pull out the words most used by students to describe those employers.

How can this information be used by employers? Employers can search for students who have selected different attributes.

Why are the choices capped at five? We found limiting the number helped students to focus and figure out what was actually most important to them. Without the cap, students selected too many responses for it to be a useful signal in job recommendations.

Can students change their answers? At this time they cannot change their responses after on-boarding. This will be coming shortly.

Will this information be on the student profile? At this time the information will not be visible on the student profile.

What about students who have already on-boarded? We will ask them these same questions when they log in.

Guide to Managing Student & Alumni Connections

This article provides an overview of how to manage student connections at your institution with links to supporting resources.

Note: In order to manage a student’s account, they must be connected to your institution.

Topics:

  • How student accounts are created
  • Customize your institutions request message
  • How to approve a student request
  • How to manually connect a student with an existing account
  • How to create an account for a student
  • Duplicate student accounts

How student accounts are created

Students and alumni access Handshake via their user account, which is either imported by your institution or manually created by the student when they register on Handshake.

When student accounts are imported, they are automatically connected with your institution’s instance on Handshake.

This is the recommended workflow for creating multiple student accounts in the system. For additional information, refer to Importing Student Data.

Note: AWS autorun jobs cannot approve student requests due to the job requiring changes to identifier data. Manual Importer jobs can approve pending student connection requests.

A student or alum can manually create their own account and request to connect with your institution. To learn more about this, check out How Students & Alumni Can Request to Access Handshake.

Customize your institutions request message

When approving a student’s request to connect with your institution, verify that they are either an incoming student, active student, or alum.

To expedite this process, your institution may create a custom message for new student account requests. This message will appear when a student registers for a new account and chooses to connect with your institution.

Possible things to include within this message:

  • requirements to connect
  • specific instructions
  • any additional information needed to be approved For more information creating custom messages, refer to How to Customize a Student’s User Request.

How to manually approve a student request

If a student creates an account, they may not be connected to your institution automatically, depending on the school settings and the email address used during sign up. Student account requests have to be manually reviewed in Handshake if your institution:

  • has not selected to auto-approve student requests with their .edu address.
  • has opted in to auto-approve student requests, but the account is created with an email domain other than the specified .edu address Follow the steps in How to Process Student & Alumni Connection Requests to connect them.

If your institution is interested in the auto-approve setting, refer to School Settings: Details, specifically the Configuration section.

For information on student notifications during the request process, check out Notifications for Students Requesting to Join a School.

Note: Student requests that are pending can be approved by running a manual student import job. For more information, refer to the question “What happens if I try to import student data for a student that is currently pending approval to connect with our school on Handshake?” in this article: Importer: Implementation FAQs and Student Data Best Practices.

How to manually connect a student with an existing account

If a student has an account in Handshake already, but they are not connected to your institution, or if you previously rejected their request, you will need to manually add them. For more information on this workflow, refer to Add an Existing Student Account to Your Institution.

If a student has an account that is already connected to another institution, and they need to be transferred to yours, contact our Support team for further assistance.

Additional information on students with an existing account can be found in Managing Students Already in Handshake but Not Connected to Your School.

Note: Students can apply for jobs when they are not connected to an institution on Handshake. If the student’s existing account uses their personal email address, has data attached to it, and is a duplicate, then there are ways to manage this account. Check out Duplicate student accounts below for more information!

How to create an account for a student

In the event a students account hasn’t yet been created, and you have permission to create the account on their behalf, you can follow the process outlined in Create a Student Account Associated with Your Career Services Account.

Note: this is not an ideal process, and is only recommended for adding 1-2 students at a time as the process is time-intensive.

Duplicate student accounts

If you’ve imported student accounts into Handshake and the student then creates their own account with a different email address, follow the suggested steps in Managing and Merging Duplicate Student Accounts.

Archiving student accounts

There may be specific situations where you choose to archive student accounts.

If you still want to archive student accounts, you can do so through the importer as shown in the article Importer: Bulk Archiving Students.

Additional resources for once a student is connected:

  • Additional Email Addresses for Students

  • Update Student & Alumni Email Addresses Consider the following before archiving student accounts:

  • Archiving a student account is not the same as deleting a student account. The student can still log in to the account and have access as an unaffiliated user. Graduated students can still use Handshake if you’ve archived their account. Learn more about this in What Happens When I Archive a Student?

  • You do not need to archive a student account if they plan on using a new email address. If a student wants to change their email address, you can assist them with this process by providing this article: Update A Students Institution Email Address.

  • About Student On-boarding

  • Employer Attributes in Student On-boarding

How Students & Alumni Can Request to Access Handshake

To provide equal opportunity to Handshake, students and alumni are always able to create and request an account on either the main login page or your school-specific domain:

  • Handshake’s website
    • app.joinhandshake.com
  • Your institutions specific domain page
    • yourschooldomain.joinhandshake.com Note: both of these options have the same registration process.

  1. Students are then prompted to enter their school email address that ends in .edu

  2. Students are then required to add their school:

  • If the student has an email domain that matches your institutions settings in Handshake, the field will pre-populated with the matching school.
  • If the student has an email domain that does not match, they will need to select their school from the dropdown menu. If your institution has chosen to add an additional set of instructions specific to the approval process, these will also be displayed on the page.

For more information on creating custom request messages, refer to How to Configure Your Institutions Request Message.

  1. Once the school is confirmed, the student will need to create a unique password for their account and agree to Handshake’s Terms of Service.

  2. Students will then be prompted to fill in their information:

  • First name
  • Last name
  • Major
  • Graduation Month
  • Graduation Year
  1. Once the information is added, the account is created and a confirmation email is sent. The student must click the link in the email confirmation to confirm and use the account.

Depending on your school’s settings and the email address they used, the student will either be:

  • auto-approved to connect with your institution
    • refer to School Settings: Details for more information on this feature
  • in the Pending Requests waiting to be approved by a career services user
    • refer to Processing Student & Alumni Connection Requests for more information on approving student requests

How to Block a Student

Blocking a student is available in Handshake if you need to temporarily suspend a student’s access to Handshake due to misuse of the system or a late bill payment.

If you need to block a student, you can follow these steps:

  • Select Manage from the left side navigation bar
    • You will be then directed to the student’s main profile page
  • Select the Account tab at the upper-right of the page​
  • Scroll down to the Status section of the student and change the status of the student to blocked
  • Once you make this change, scroll down to the bottom of the page and click the green Update User button. The change will be effective immediately and the student will see the following message when they try to access their Handshake account.

How to Delete a Student Account

If a student created a duplicate account in Handshake, or if they are requesting their account to be deleted, you can delete their account from the system.

For more information about handling duplicate student accounts, refer to Managing Duplicate Student Accounts

Note: if your institution imports student data, you’ll need to reach out to the person that manages your student sync to ensure the deleted account is also removed from the student sync, so the account won’t be recreated.

Delete a student account

  1. Navigate to the student profile in Handshake.

  2. Click the Account tab in the upper center of the page.

  3. Click the red Delete button, located in the lower-left area below all the settings.

Note: If the student has any historical data connected to the account, such as: Appointments, Applications, Experiences, or First Destination Surveys, the system won’t allow you to delete the student. A pop-up will appear in the middle of the screen confirming the data the student is connected with in Handshake. Contact Support for more information.

  • If the student doesn’t have any historical data connected to their account, a pop-up will appear in the middle of the screen where you can confirm that you would like to delete the student’s account by typing their email address into the text box and then clicking the red Delete button.
    • This account will be permanently deleted and the Handshake team can’t recover the account. Note: students have the option to request an account deletion by reaching out to our Support Team. To learn more about the student process, refer to Request User Account Deletion.

How to Reactivate an Archived Student

If a student is archived by your institution in Handshake and wants to reconnect to your school, they can submit a Reactivation Request. This request will appear as a notification, and will need to be approved or declined by a career services user.

To approve or decline a students reactivation request via notification, follow the steps below.

  1. Click the person icon, located in the upper-right corner of the screen.

  2. Use the filters at the top of the page to locate the students request.

  3. Click Decision dropdown menu. Choose Approve or Reject to either accept or decline the student’s attempt to connect to your school.

  4. A popup will ask to you confirm your choice. Choose Yes, approve or Yes, reject to finalize your decision.

Once the student is reactivated, you’ll need to decide whether the student should be included in student syncs via the Importer or not.

  • If the student shouldn’t be included, follow the steps outlined in Importer: Excluding Students from Automatic Syncs to remove them.
  • If they should be included, make sure the box is unchecked for Exclude from Automatic Syncs. You may refer to Importer: Excluding Students from Automatic Syncs for steps to locate this setting.

Managing and Merging Duplicate Student Accounts

This article will provide you with best practices for managing duplicate student accounts. In some cases, a student may create an account independently and have a separate account that is already connected to your school.

Students that are not connected to your school can still apply for jobs on the open network. You can learn more about the student connected and unconnected experience in EDU: Understanding the Job Seeker Experience - Connected vs. Not Connected.

We have proactive and reactive suggestions for managing duplicate student accounts. It is recommended to try the proactive workflows before trying the reactive workflows, but as always, do what’s best and most relevant for your school! And if you have any additional questions on how to approach this, reach out to your Relationship Manager.

Topics:

  • Proactive: Lowering the amount of new Duplicate Accounts
    • Update alumni emails through the Importer
  • Reactive: Merge
  • Additional Resources
  • FAQ’s

Proactive: Lowering the amount of new Duplicate Accounts

We’ve added a banner to the student side of Handshake that encourages students to add their personal email address to their accounts. When students graduate, they may end up creating a duplicate account with their personal email address so they can still access Handshake as an alumni. This banner helps reduce the amount of duplicate accounts that will appear.

Update alumni emails through the Importer

The additional_email_addresses field provides the opportunity to add other .edu email addresses, alumni specific email addresses, aliases, etc. for individual students. When successfully updated, the student’s account will include the additional email addresses which should help prevent the creation of a duplicate account with that email address!

Additionally, if you have the student’s personal email address, you can update their institution email address to a personal or alumni email address as detailed in Importer: Updating Graduating Students to Alumni.

Reactive: Merge

Note: Merges should only be reserved for situations where you cannot delete the account successfully on your end. Attempt to delete the duplicate student account before requesting a merge.

If deletion is not possible, contact Support to request an account merge. A merge will bring over some of the data from one account into an existing institution created account.

It’s important to note that this is not a complete merge and not all data will be carried over. This merge exists specifically for removing unconnected student accounts that have job application data attached to them, and transferring that data into an established account that is connected to your school. Specifically the data transferring over will be the email address and applications, if applicable, any documents, a profile photo and their profile custom link will be carried over as well.

The following are the criteria that need to be met for the account that is not connected to your school, that you wish to remove from Handshake:

  • The duplicate account’s status is either pending or rejected by your school for connection

  • The duplicate account has accepted Handshake’s Terms of Service agreement

  • The duplicate account has confirmed their email address or authorized Single Sign On

  • The duplicate account is not blocked or disabled The following are the criteria that need to be met for the account that is already connected to your school that the duplicate accounts will be merged into:

  • The connected account has accepted Handshake’s Terms of Service agreement

  • The connected account is not blocked or disabled

  • This connected account has Handshake data in one of the following modules:

    • Fair/Event attendee data
    • Appointment data
    • Experience data
    • Job application data
    • FDS/Survey data Following a successful merge, the duplicate account will be removed and the job application data and email address (as well as any documents, profile photo, and/or profile custom link, if they exist) associated with the duplicate account will be transferred over to the connected account.

Additional Resources

  • If the account was created with a personal (not .edu) email, and they haven’t applied to any jobs with that account yet, the student can contact Support to request account deletion, then use one of the following options on the existing account:
    • Have the student add the email address as an additional email on their account as described in Update Your Primary Email Address in Handshake.
      • Learn more about this workflow’s impact to your team in Additional Email Addresses for Students.
  • If the student cannot access their .edu email to change the email themselves, you can change it for them per Career Services User Settings: Email Change Request Process - this will prompt a confirmation to the new email which the student will need to confirm within 24 hours.
  • Alternative: if the student account with the .edu email address doesn’t have any data associated with it, you can delete the account by following the steps in How to Delete a Student Account, then approve the pending request with the personal email and update the username and auth identifier fields as needed by accessing the account tab in their student record:

FAQ’s

“This email address is already connected to an existing user in Handshake.” shows when I try to change the email, but I am unable to locate an account with that email address. What do I do?

  • If this is the case, there’s already an existing account in Handshake with the email address that is not connected to the school. You will need to determine whether the student is connected to another institution or not. If you’re unsure, contact Support for verification.
    • If the student is not connected to another institution, you can add them manually by following the steps in How to Process Student & Alumni Connection Requests.
      • Note: you can use this workflow to determine whether a student is connected to another institution. If you are unable to add them this way, they are likely connected elsewhere.
    • If the student is connected to another institution, refer to Managing Students Already in Handshake but not Connected to Your School. Can I delete a student that is pending at my institution?
  • Yes, you can delete an account that is pending at your institution if there is no data associated with it (ex. an application). This is only suggested if you know that the student already has an existing active account connected to your institution. We suggest you email the student to let them know what account they should be using. Refer to How to Delete a Student Account for more information. Note: If the student has any historical data connected to the account, such as: Appointments, Applications, Experiences, or First Destination Surveys, the system won’t allow you to delete the student. A pop-up will appear in the middle of the screen confirming the data the student is connected with in Handshake. Contact Support for more information.

When is the student’s email changed?

  • When they confirm the change by entering the verification code that was sent to their updated email address. Can I update an email address to one that already exists in Handshake?

  • No, if the email address already exists in Handshake (even if it is tied to a different user type) you can’t use that email address. This is to make sure that students don’t get access to a career services user or employer account.

  • Note: If you are testing this process as a career services user, and you attempt to change the email to your student account, you will not be able to change it back to match your career services account email.

Managing Students Already in Handshake but Not Connected to Your Institution

There may be instances where a student has an account in Handshake, but they are not connected to your institution. This is due to:

  • the student creating an account and not requesting to connect
  • the student request to connect being rejected (denied) or left in pending by career services
  • the student being connected to another institution

Student has an account but they are not connected

When a student manually creates a new Handshake account, they can request to connect with your institution. If they are not connected, their profile remains active, but they can not explore your institutions offerings. To learn more about this process, refer to How Students & Alumni Can Request to Access Handshake.

If they are not connected to an institution, students can still access different parts of Handshake. To learn more about the access that students can have when they are not connected to an institution, refer to EDU: Understanding the Job Seeker Experience - Connected vs. Not Connected

If a student creates an account and requests to connect, and they are declined, this will not delete the account but leave them unconnected.

There are two possible indications a student already has an account in Handshake:

  • when you import the student’s information through the importer and they appear on the failed rows download with the error {“success”:false,“errors”:{“email_address”:[“has already been taken”]}

    • for more information on this, refer to Importer Error: Email Address Has Already Been Taken.

  • when you manually create a student account in Handshake and receive a message that the email address is already in use If the student is not already connected to another institution, there are two ways to resolve this and connect them:

  • manually add the student individually

  • reload the failed rows via the importer Note: If the student has an account that’s already connected to your institution and has another account that is not connected to your institution, they have a duplicate account. Refer to Managing and Merging Duplicate Student Accounts for more information on how to manage and possibly merge duplicate student accounts.

Manually add the student individually

You can add students to your institution directly by email address on the Manage Students page. This is only recommended when connecting less than 25 students at a time, as it can be a time consuming process. To do this, follow the steps outlined in Add an Existing Student Account to Your Institution.

Note: if the student’s account is connected to another institution, you will receive an error message when attempting this workflow. Skip to the section below, titled Student is connected to a different institution, for more information on this process.

Reload the failed rows into Importer

If you need to connect several students to your institution, we recommend re-uploading the failed rows file into Importer. For detailed information on why this error is occurring and how to resolve , refer to Importer Error: Email Address Has Already Been Taken.

Student is connected to a different institution

  • If their email address is the email domain for your institution:
    • Confirm that they want to switch to your institution and then contact Handshake Support with the email address, name, and institution this student wants to be switched to.
  • If their email address is the email domain for a different institution:
    • You will need to create a new student account for them with their current email address for your institution. The student will then have two email addresses and logins into Handshake, one for each institution they are connected to. Follow the steps outlined in Create a Student Account Associated with Your Career Services Account, using the student’s information.
  • If their email address is a generic (gmail, yahoo, etc.) address:
    • Confirm that they want to switch to your institution and then contact Handshake Support with the email address, name, and institution this student wants to be switched to.
    • Once they are connected to your institution, if they would like to update their email address, you can update their email address to their .edu address for your school. For information on this, refer to Career Services User Settings: Email Change Request Process.

Participation and Engagement Data on the Manage Students Page

On the Manage students page, you’ll notice the Participation and Engagement Data listed at the top of the page. Let’s take some time to review what this information is and how you can utilize filters to drill down on specific information.

To begin, select Manage from your left navigation bar, located under the Students section.

Participation

This section of data is split between two subsections:

  • Activated: if a student has accepted ToS

  • Completed profile: if the student has at least 70% of their account completed If you select the Participation filter, the following options appear:

  • Activation

    • Has activated
    • Has not activated

  • Profile

    • Completed profile
    • Not completed

Engagement

This section of data is a little more straight forward, it is split into four subsections:

  • Submitted an application: if a student has submitted an application through a job posting on Handshake

  • Attended fair: if a student attended a fair on Handshake

  • Attended appointment: if a student attended an appointment on Handshake

  • Attended event: if a student attended an event on Handshake If you select the Engagement filter, the following options appear:

  • Applications

    • Has submitted
    • Has not submitted

  • Appointments

    • Attended
    • Not attended

  • Fairs

    • Attended
    • Not attended

  • Events

    • Attended
    • Not attended

  • Within the last ___ months: You can modify this when you select one of the above engagement filters Note: the date range under the Engagement filter will not impact the Participation data. This is because participation always considers “all-time” data rather than a specific range of time.

Hide or Show Analytics

If you prefer to have a more compact viewing of the Manage students page, you can always choose to hide this data, by clicking Hide Analytics on the top-right corner of the Participation and Engagement data information.

Note: If you refresh the page or go to another section of Handshake and return back to the Manage students page, the analytics will revert back to being shown instead of hidden.

After hiding the data, to show the data again, click Show Analytics located in the same area.

Applying additional filters

You can apply any other filters to help narrow your search. The data will update in real-time. For example, I selected Freshman under the School Year filter and Accounting as a major under the Filters option. This returns different data results in the Participation and Engagement sections at the top of the Manage students page:

Try different filters to achieve different data results!

Remember, this isn’t the only data that you can find about your students’ activity and participation on Handshake. You’re welcome to use the Student Activity Dashboard to view more specific data for each student: About the Student Activity Dashboard. The Student Engagement Tracker is also a great place to track data: Analytics: Student Engagement Tracker & Reporting.

Processing Student & Alumni Connection Requests

When a student or alum creates a new Handshake account and submits a request to connect with your institution, a notification badge appears on the person icon in the blue navigation bar at the top of the screen.

Approving or Rejecting Individual Student Requests

  1. Click on User Requests (the person icon), located in the upper-right corner of the screen, to the left of Help.

  2. The default filter settings on this page show all student requests with a None Decision. This means that the requests haven’t been approved or declined yet. You can set the filter by selecting Decision. For now, we will discuss the workflow for any student requests that haven’t been responded to yet.

  3. To approve or decline a request, select the dropdown menu on the right titled None. The options to Approve or Reject will appear. Select one of these to either approve or decline the request.

  4. A box will appear asking you to confirm your decision. In this example, approving the request was selected so the box asks to confirm approval for this request. “This can’t be undone.” Select Yes, approve to confirm.

  5. The student will no longer appear in the table as they have been approved. If you approved the student, you can change the Decision filter to Approved to verify that the student has been approved. The same can be done if a student was rejected, using the Rejected filter.

The dropdown menu in the right-most column will be grayed out, as these request statuses cannot be changed once you set them to Approved or Rejected.

Note: if a student request is accidentally denied, you can add manually connect the student to your institution using the process outlined in Add an Existing Student Account to Your Institution.

Approving or Rejecting Multiple Student Requests

Simply select the checkbox to the left of the name to choose all student requests, or use the individual checkboxes next to each student name to select those students. Then choose to Approve requests or Reject requests.

Note: You will be asked to confirm your decision, which cannot be undone once confirmed.

Students received notifications when they request for a connection and when they are approved. For details on email notifications, check out Notifications for Students Requesting to Connect to a School.

What happens if I reject a student’s request?

The student will be able to use Handshake without connecting to your institution. If they would like to request to connect to your school again, they can log in, select their profile in the upper-right corner of the screen and choose School connections to request to connect to your school again.

Pull email addresses from the request page

Use the spreadsheet attached at the bottom of this article to copy and paste the rows from the request page (Name, Request date, Request type, Decision), and easily extract the email address using the formula in Column E.

Restricting Student Access with Permission Labels

In Handshake, permission-based labels may be configured to determine which students are eligible to use these features:

  • Appointments
  • Interviews
  • Experiences By using permission labels, Career Services can set parameters regarding which students are eligible to apply.

Follow the steps below to add a permission label:

  1. Click your school name on the upper right-hand corner of the screen, and click School Settings from the drop down menu.

  2. On the left of your screen you will see a list of school settings tabs. Select the category you’d like to add a permission label to.

Permission labels may be set on any of the following tabs - Appointment Preferences, Experience Preferences, or Interview Preferences. While the content within each of these tabs may be different, the steps for setting up permission labels will be identical.

Depending upon your selection, you will see a header called Instructions or Student Permission Label.

  1. Check the box next to Students to enable this feature.

  2. Select from the drop down menu whether the students MUST or MUST NOT be labeled the desired label name.

  • If a student MUST be labeled “label name”, then that means only students with the selected label will be able to use that particular feature.
  • If students MUST NOT be labeled “label name”, this means that only students without the specified label will be able to use the feature.
  1. Search or select from a drop down menu the label you’d like to use.
  • If you don’t see the label you’d like to use, you may click Create New Label and a new window will pop-up.
    • Note: Most schools have internal policies regarding label creation. Please check with your Handshake account owner if you’re unsure about whether or not you are empowered to generate a new label at your school. On the form fill out the following information:
  • Enter your label name.
  • From a drop down menu, select the area in Handshake where you’d like to use this label (i.e. job, employer, etc.), or select All to allow it to be used in any area.
  • From a drop down menu, select the label type. “Normal” labels are private, meaning only Career Services staff can see them. “Public” labels are visible by staff and students.
  • Click Create in the lower right hand corner.

  1. Next, you may enter a custom Permission Denied Message. This message will appear when a student attempts to apply for or participate in something that he/she is not qualified for based on your label selection.

  2. Click Save in the lower right-hand corner of the page to save your changes.

Troubleshooting: Student Data Discrepancies

This article will help you navigate issues related to inaccurate student data counts. We’ll outline the reasoning, and highlight next steps to reconcile what you’re seeing in Handshake with the data you find in your student information system.

Why is my data inaccurate?

If your data looks incorrect, this is most likely result of:

  • Out-of-date student data - you should be regularly refreshing your student data, especially at the end of each semester
  • Inaccurate data coming from your student information system - it’s important that you’re importing records that are the “source of truth” at your school
  • Duplicate student accounts - we do not recommend approving “pending” student accounts for students that have an existing, imported account. For more information refer to Managing and Merging Duplicate Student Accounts.

Things to keep in mind:

This information is coming from your student information system (SIS) so your IT team, Registrar, or data team are best equipped to assist. The Handshake Support team can outline the processes, confirm the required formatting, and help you update the data in Handshake - we just can’t reconcile the data from the source of truth.

A (throwback!) metaphor to help clarify:

You can think of the process like a VCR - where the Importer is the VCR, Handshake is the TV that displays what the VCR processes, and your data files are the VHS tapes that you feed into the VCR.

The TV (Handshake) will display whatever the VCR (Importer) processes. The VCR will only process the right kind of tapes (student data) to confirm everything is formatted correctly. That said, there’s no way for the VCR or the TV to know what exact film should be displayed - it relies on whoever is feeding the tape (student data) into the VCR to make the accurate “film” choice!

How to check if your student list is accurate in Handshake:

  • Generate an Insights report of your full student list - including school year name
  • Download the full report (using little gear icon in upper right hand corner) to an Excel file. Note: If the download exceeds 5,000 rows, you will need to contact our Support team to request access to download more than 5,000 rows.
  • Obtain a correct list of current students from your Registrar office (if the data going through the importer is correct, you may want to just download that importer file)
  • Compare the lists from your Registrar and from the Insights report to ensure they match up. You may want to use student email as the unique identifier or anchor point. You could also use the username or auth identifier.
  • Identify any gaps. If there are students that exist in the Handshake list and NOT in the registrar list they are likely either…
  • Alumni
  • Students who transferred / dropped out

Next steps to adjust:

For alumni, you will likely just want update their “school year” field to alumni. This article outlines the specific instructions for Importer: Updating Graduating Students to Alumni

For students who transferred or who did not complete their degree, you can archive their accounts by following the steps in Importer: Bulk Archiving Students and learn more about archiving student accounts in What Happens When I Archive a Student?

Note: Students will still be able to access Handshake if they are archived, they just won’t be connected to your institution after they attempt to log in. In some cases, you may want to block students from using Handshake while remaining connected to your institution. Refer to this article for more information: How to Block a Student

For any additional student groups, you might also consider Importing Labels. You can then use this labels to filter on your analytics moving forward.

For data discrepancies, use the attachment below to help identify and resolve data discrepancies.

If you’re still running into issues:

Additionally, you can connect with our Support team to confirm that you have followed the process outlined above and to provide specific details, such as:

  • Student lists/reports you’re exploring (Insights URLs or Handshake URLS are especially important)
  • Specific discrepancies you’ve identified (Exact counts and examples are best)
  • Any additional context, concerns, and details

Update a Student’s Institution Email Address

Student accounts are usually pre-created in Handshake by the school using the student’s institution-provided email address. Students cannot delete or change this institution email address themselves in Handshake

If a student wants Handshake notifications and marketing emails sent to a different address, they can change their primary email instead.

For step-by-step instructions from the student perspective, refer to Update Your Primary Email Address in Handshake.

Important: If a student’s account is also connected to an employer or career services user account, you will not be able to change their institution email address.

For students who need their institution email address changed, Career Services staff can update it in two ways:

  • Via Importer
  • Manually in Handshake
    • Example Emails

Via Importer

To change a student’s institution email via Importer:

  • Update the preferred institution email address in your existing student sync file.

  • Upload the updated file through Importer. For file requirements and required fields, refer to:

  • Importing Student Data Additional notes:

  • If your school uses an automated sync, make sure the new email address is also updated in the source file that feeds the sync.

  • You cannot change a student’s email address to one that belongs to a different institution (another .edu domain).

  • For guidance on updating graduating students’ email addresses, refer to:

  • Importer: Updating Graduating Students to Alumni

Manually in Handshake

  1. Confirm if the student is in your student sync file

You can check this in either of these ways:

  • Review your current student sync file, or

  • Open the student’s profile in Handshake and go to the Account tab. In the Account tab:

  • If a white Change Institution Email button is displayed to the right of the institution email, the account is excluded from the importer sync.

  • If the Change Institution Email button does not appear, the account is being synced via Importer. Important: Only accounts that are excluded from sync can be updated manually in Handshake.

  • If the student is not included in your student sync, continue to step 2.

  • If you want to exclude this student from future syncs so you can update their institution email manually:

    • Scroll to the bottom of the Account tab.
    • Select Exclude from Automatic Syncs.
    • Click the green Update User button in the lower-right corner to save.
    • Then continue to step 2.

  • If you later want this student’s profile to update through the automatic sync again, uncheck Exclude from Automatic Syncs, then click Update User to save.

  1. Start the institution email change. Click the white Change Institution Email button on the Account tab.

  2. Submit the new institution email. Enter the new email address in the New Email field, then click the blue Submit Request button.

If you receive the error “You do not have the permissions to make changes to this user’s email.”, the student has another account type connected (for example, an employer account). In that case, let us know you’d like the email change be initiated.

After the request is processed, a banner appears on the profile:

“Please check your new email address for your email confirmation link and code.”

What the student receives

The student will receive two emails and must follow the instructions in the second email to complete the change.

  1. Request confirmation email (sent to the current email address)

Subject and body will be similar to:

Hello [NAME],

Your account email address has been requested to change to [NEW EMAIL].

If you or someone you authorized (for example, your school) requested this, please follow the directions emailed to [NEW EMAIL].

If you do not recognize this request, please contact [HANDSHAKE SUPPORT LINK] immediately.

  1. Instructions to complete the change (sent to the new email address)

Subject and body will be similar to:

Hello [NAME],

We received a request to change your email address. If you requested this change, please click the link below and paste the email code in the form to continue.

Please note: in order to complete this change you will first need to log in with your original email address and password.

Your email verification code is [CODE]

[CHANGE EMAIL BUTTON]

When the student clicks the Change Email button, they are prompted to enter:

  • Email Verification Code
  • Password / Confirm Password Once submitted successfully, the institution email on the student’s Handshake account is updated.

What Happens When I Archive a Student?

We’ve updated our process on archiving students in Handshake. This article will explain how the experience has changed for students and schools. We recommend using archiving sparingly, this will give you the most accurate representation of data in Handshake. It also allows alumni opportunities to continue to use Handshake while connected to your school, giving them more relevant and plentiful job opportunities.

Topics:

  • Archive a student account
  • When you archive a student account and they don’t attempt to log in again
  • When you archive a student account in Handshake and the student attempts to log in again
  • Is there a way to prevent a student from using Handshake, but keep them connected to my school?

Archive a student account

To archive a student, go to any student’s profile and select Account in the upper right corner of the page

Scroll down and check the box for Archive This Profile, then select Update user to save the changes

You can also archive student accounts in bulk: Importer: Bulk Archiving Students

When you archive a student account and they don’t attempt to log in again

  • The student will remain archived and connected to your school
  • You will be able to locate them as an archived student in the Manage students page and their data will appear in the Analytics and FDS modules

When you archive a student account in Handshake and the student attempts to log in again

  • The student is disconnected from your school in Handshake
  • The student still has access to Handshake as an unaffiliated job seeker
  • Upon logging in, the student is asked if they wish to connect to your school again. That option will always be available for them as displayed in the Student article: Connect to Your School for Full Handshake Access
    • They will need to be approved by your school before they are reconnected to your school again, similar to the steps in Processing Student & Alumni Connection Requests
  • The student’s historic data will exist in the Analytics and the FDS module but data for activity after they become unaffiliated will not be available on the Manage students page

Is there a way to prevent a student from using Handshake, but keep them connected to my school?

Since archiving a student account has a modified functionality now, you can prevent the student from temporarily using Handshake if you block their account. Blocking encourages the student to reach out to your school or Handshake Support to identify what they need to do to use Handshake again. To learn more about blocking students, refer to How to Block a Student.

Student Job Search & Application Support

Apply for a Job on Behalf of a Student

Career services staff can submit a job application on behalf of a student directly from the job posting in Handshake.

Note: Applying on behalf of a student overrides any qualifications, preferences, and deadlines set on the job posting.

Add a student applicant

  1. Navigate to the job posting in Handshake.

  2. On the job overview page, locate the Actions list on the left side of the page, then click Add an Applicant.

  3. In the pop-up that appears, select the student you want to apply on behalf of.

  • Student names are displayed in alphabetical order, with the first 25 students listed by default.
  • To find a student not displayed, type their name or email address into the text field.
  • Note: You do not need to attach a document when applying on behalf of a student.

  1. When the student is selected, click the green Apply button in the lower-right corner of the pop-up.

  2. A green banner will appear at the top of the page with the message ‘Application successfully submitted.’

View application details

To view who created an application or when it was submitted, click on the applicant from the applicant list, then review the Created By column.

Download a Student Resume Book

Use Handshake’s student management filters to build and download a resume book for students at your institution, including options to export as a PDF or ZIP file.

Note: This workflow is intended for career services users only.

For employer-specific guidance, visit Downloading Public Resumes.

Download a resume book

  1. Click Manage under Students from the left navigation bar.

  2. Click the Filters button in the header bar to open the filters panel.

  3. Under Other, select Has public resume, then click Apply at the bottom of the panel.

4.The page will update to display only students with a public resume.

Note: There is a 500 student limit per download.

  1. Select the students you want to include in the download by doing one of the following:
  • Check the box in the upper-left corner of the table to select all students displayed on the current page (up to 25).
  • Click Select all [number] to select all students in the filtered list.
  1. Click the More button in the header above the student list, then select one of the following:
  • Download public resume (PDF): Downloads all selected resumes as a single PDF file.
  • Download public resume (Zip): Downloads all selected resumes as a ZIP file. A banner will appear in the lower-left corner of the page confirming the download is being prepared.

Once complete, the banner will update to show Download complete and the file will be saved to your computer. You will also receive an email with a link to the file.

EDU: The Applications Page

The Applications Page is where you’ll find every application that has been submitted by your students. You can search for applications, update the status of any application here, and export your findings into a downloadable file.

Topics:

  • Navigating to the Applications Page
  • Finding Applications
  • Updating Application Statuses
  • Downloading Applications

Navigating to the Applications Page

Before beginning, ensure that you have permissions to access student applications. You can learn more about this role in School Settings: Career Services Staff Roles and Permissions.

The left navigation bar lists the Applications button, located under the Students section. Select it to be taken directly to the Applications Page.

Alternatively: If you are already viewing a specific job posting that has applications associated with it, you can click the Applicants tab to be taken to the Applications Page, which displays the applicants for that specific job posting:

Finding Applications

On the landing page, the default layout displays all applications in descending order from most recent application submitted to least recent application submitted. You have options to search for an application and filters on the left side of the screen to help narrow your search.

Use the filters to display applications that fit the criteria you select. For example, we’ll use “Pending” to display all pending applications.

Use the keyword search bar to locate any specific student or employer-related application. In this example, we searched a student’s name and found that one of the applications is marked as late under the date column. Learn more about late job applications in the employer article: About a ‘Late’ Job Application

Updating Application Statuses

There are two ways to update applications statuses on this page. First, you can select any status in the table of applications and change it. The options are Primary, Pending, Declined, Hired, Withdraw Application.

Alternatively: Select the application you’d like to update by clicking on the student’s name. This will pop up the application window. From here, you can click the triple-line hamburger icon to display the different application status options.

Downloading Applications

On the Applications Page, in the upper-right corner there are two options to Export CSV and Export Documents.

Set your filters and choose one of the following:

Export CSV - Downloads the current Applications Page table contents into a .CSV file.

Export Documents - Choose one or many documents to download from the applications that were submitted:

*Non-required documents may not appear in the download, even if they are selected here.

  • Resume
  • Cover Letter
  • Transcript
  • Other Document

How to Help Students Filter for Jobs

In order to ensure students have a positive experience searching for and applying to jobs, we updated the Jobs page layout and filtering.

When students navigate to the Jobs page, they previously landed on an unpersonalized job search experience with results that are not reflective of the students’ skills or interests. As a result, most students (88%) ended up applying filters or keywords to find jobs. However, many students voiced that filters are confusing and unintuitive.

The new Jobs page provides personalized highlights per student based on their interests and introduces a more intuitive filter design and page layout.

On the left, students are presented with a list of all jobs approved at their school. Students may click on a job to load the full job posting on this page and apply.

Jobs matching selected interests

On the left of the page, above the list of jobs, a message indicates how many job postings match their currently selected interests. Students may click the pencil icon to the right of this to update their interests.

Filtering for jobs

Above the job posting information, students may filter job postings using a keyword search or one of the pre-built filters. Click All Filters to select from more filters, including Employer Preferences, Work Authorization, Industry, Job Function, Major, Employer, and Labeled by your school (jobs with public labels).

Additional Student Resources

  • Searching for Jobs and Internships
  • My Saved Jobs in Handshake
  • Saved Job Searches and Alerts
  • Search for On-Campus Positions in Handshake

How to See if a Student has Withdrawn Their Application Then Re-applied

This article explains how to identify students who have withdrawn and re-applied to a job or interview schedule at your institution.

To view all withdrawn applications, visit How to View Withdrawn Applications.

View applications from students who withdrew and re-applied

If a student withdraws their application and re-applies, their withdrawn and active applications cannot be viewed at the same time. You can view each record separately using the steps below.

To view the student’s withdrawn application:

  1. Access the applicants list for the relevant job or interview schedule.

  2. In the Filters side sheet on the left, under Categories, check the Withdrawn Only checkbox.

The student’s withdrawn application will appear in the list with a status of Withdrawn. If the student has withdrawn multiple times, each instance will appear as a separate entry.

To view the student’s active application:

  1. Uncheck the Withdrawn Only checkbox.

  2. Use the Keyword search to search for the student by name.

The student’s active application will display with a status of Pending, Reviewed, Declined, or Hired.

How to View Withdrawn Applications

This article explains how to view withdrawn applications submitted by students at your institution, including applications to jobs posted by employers and applications connected to interview schedules.

To withdraw a student’s application on their behalf, visit How to Withdraw a Student’s Application.

View withdrawn job applications

You can view withdrawn job applications starting from a specific job or from the Applications page, which shows withdrawn applications submitted by students at your institution across all employers.

From a specific job:

  1. Open the job you want to review applicants for.

  2. Access the applicants list by doing one of the following:

  • Click the blue applicant count under Applicants on the left side of the page.
  • Click Browse Applicants in the Actions section on the left.
  • Click the Applicants tab in the upper-right corner of the page.
  1. In the Filters side sheet on the left, under Categories, check the Withdrawn Only checkbox.

From the Applications page:

  1. Click Applications from the left navigation bar under Students.

  2. In the Filters side sheet on the left, under Categories, check the Withdrawn Only checkbox.

Tip: Use the Keyword search or any of the available filters in the side sheet, such as Employer, to narrow down your results.

Only withdrawn applications will be displayed. Uncheck Withdrawn Only to return to viewing all applications.

View withdrawn interview schedule applications

If a student withdraws an application from a job that is associated with an interview schedule, they are also withdrawing their application from the interview schedule.

  1. Open the interview schedule you want to review applicants for.

  2. In the middle of the page, under Review Interview Applicants for [your school name], click the Review Applicants button.

  3. In the Filters side sheet on the left, under Scheduling, check the Withdrawn Only checkbox.

Only withdrawn applications will be displayed. Uncheck Withdrawn Only to return to viewing all applications.

How to Withdraw a Student’s Application

Before withdrawing an application on behalf of a student, confirm the employer’s application method, as this determines whether the withdrawal can be completed in Handshake.

  • Applications submitted in Handshake can be withdrawn at any time by either the student or career services.
  • Applications submitted via an external apply link cannot be withdrawn in Handshake. If the student also completed the external application, the student or career services staff should reach out to the employer directly to request withdrawal.
    • Note: Withdrawing the application in Handshake does not impact the external application.
  • Applications submitted via an ATS integration (such as Greenhouse, Workday, or ICIMS) cannot be withdrawn in Handshake. The student will need to contact the employer directly to request withdrawal.

Withdraw a student’s application in Handshake

  1. Open the relevant job or interview, then click the Applicants tab in the upper-right corner.

  2. On the applicants page, locate the student whose application you want to withdraw.

  3. Under the Status header, select the dropdown for that applicant, then select Withdraw Application.

  4. In the confirmation modal that appears, click the green Yes button to confirm the application withdrawal.

To view withdrawn applications, refer to How to View Withdrawn Applications.

Leveraging Job and Internship Search Features

Handshake makes it easy for students to search and filter job and internship opportunities that match their interests, skills, and career goals. As a Career Services staff member, you play an important role in helping students make the most of these features — whether that’s during advising sessions, workshops, or one-on-one support.

For a student-facing overview of how to search for jobs on Handshake, refer to Searching for Jobs and Internships. Additionally, the following video walks through key search and filter features to help you guide students through the process: Tips for job searching on Handshake.

Student Suggested Job Searches

When students are searching for jobs, they will now see search suggestions listed underneath their search filters. These suggested searches are comprised of a list of popular keywords curated by a student’s major.

Why is the student seeing these suggested searches?

  • We noticed that many students don’t leverage keyword search because they’re not sure exactly what to search for. We analyzed student search behavior and the jobs we have on Handshake to compile a list of the top keywords that can help students explore popular jobs for their major.

  • Based on our analysis, students are twice as likely to find jobs they want to apply to when using keyword search. How can students effectively use these suggested searches?

  • Students can click on any of these suggested search terms to explore jobs with these keywords. They can also apply other filters to narrow their search.

    • Please note that suggestions will only appear when a keyword is unspecified.

Troubleshooting “Unexpected Application Error” in Handshake (Student Job Search & Application Support)

If you encounter an error message such as “Unexpected token ‘u’, ‘upstream c’… is not valid JSON” or “Unexpected application error!”, it’s typically caused by a temporary issue with your browser session or cached data.

Common scenarios where this may appear

This error can occur when viewing or managing job postings, applicants, or interview schedules in Handshake.

How to resolve the error

  • Use a supported browser
  • Handshake works best in the latest versions of Google Chrome or Mozilla Firefox. Other browsers, such as Internet Explorer, are not supported and may cause errors.
  • Clear your browser cache
  • If you’re already using a supported browser, clear your cache and cookies, then log back into Handshake.
  • Try an incognito or private browsing window
  • Open Handshake in a Chrome incognito or Firefox private window. This can help identify whether the issue is related to your browser session or an extension.
  • Log out and back in or refresh the page
  • If the error persists, logging out and back in or refreshing the page may resolve the issue. For information on browser compatibility, refer to Handshake Supported Browsers (for Employers).

Work Authorization Overview

Handshake collects work authorization information directly from students to increase transparency for employers and improve the application experience. This process benefits both students and employers:

  • Students avoid spending time applying and interviewing for positions they are not eligible for.
  • Employers reduce time spent reviewing and interviewing candidates they cannot hire, while gathering more applicant information without requiring direct disclosure of work authorization status.

When students are asked work authorization questions

Before a student submits their first job application in Handshake, they are asked work authorization questions. These questions determine their qualification for employer job posting preferences and virtual fair session requirements.

These questions also appear after a student registers for a virtual fair, if the student has not yet applied to a job in Handshake or answered these questions in the Work authorization section of their Settings.

Student responses are stored in the Work authorization section of their Settings. Students are not asked to answer again after their initial response.

Note: If a student answers the work authorization questions before applying, either through a virtual fair session sign-up or through the Work authorization section of their Settings, they will not be asked again during the application process.

The questions include three options:

  • Are you legally authorized to work in the United States? (Yes/No)
  • Will you now or in the future require visa sponsorship? (Yes/No)
  • Prefer not to answer these questions. (Checkbox)
    • Students who select this option are fully qualified for all positions or virtual fair sessions with work authorization requirements.
    • Students who select this option will still appear when an employer filters by work authorization preferences.
    • The student’s work authorization status will display as “Unknown” to employers.
    • Students always appear as fully qualified for jobs that do not require US sponsorship, regardless of their answers to the work authorization questions. A tooltip with a “?” icon is available on the prompt. Hovering over the icon displays the following information:
  • If a student selects “Prefer not to answer”, they will appear when an employer filters for students who do not require sponsorship or for students who do require sponsorship.
  • If an employer views the student’s work experience field, the status will display as “Unknown.” Students who have not yet answered these questions are also listed as “Unknown.”
  • Students with DACA status can find guidance on how to answer these questions at www.informedimmigrant.com/guides/daca/#employment-rights-daca. A student’s responses to these questions determine whether they are fully qualified for a job based on the employer’s preferences for the posting.

Note: The visa status field on a student’s profile exists for reporting purposes only and is not used to determine job posting qualification, unless both of the following are true: the student has not answered the work authorization questions, and a career services user is submitting an application on the student’s behalf.

To share work authorization information with students, visit Student Work Authorization Information.

Work authorization visibility and filtering

Student perspective

Students can filter job searches by work authorization requirements by clicking All filters on the job search page, then scrolling to the Work authorization section. Available filter options include:

  • Open to US visa sponsorship
  • Open to Optional Practical Training (OPT)
  • Open to Curricular Practical Training (CPT)
  • No US work authorization required
  • Unknown On the job postings page, students can identify whether a job requires US work authorization under the At a glance section of the job details page.
Employer perspective

Employers can review applicants’ work authorization qualifications directly from the job posting. Key capabilities include:

  • Filtering to view only candidates who meet their work authorization criteria using the Matching qualifications filter for jobs, or the Exclude Students That Do Not Match filter for on-campus interviews.
  • Hovering over the card icon in the Preferences column to review the work authorization status for individual applicants. Candidates who do not meet the employer’s work authorization criteria will display “Not authorized.” Note: When employers filter by work authorization, candidates who chose not to disclose their status will still appear in results.

For full details on how employers manage work authorization during the review process, visit Employer Work Authorization Workflows.

FAQs

  1. What do the work authorization questions look like from the employer’s perspective?

Work authorization questions appear for employers in three instances: fair registration, job post creation, and 1:1 schedule qualifications. For more information, refer to Employer Work Authorization Workflows.

  1. Can work authorization name still be imported?

Yes, however Handshake does not recommend importing these fields, as students are asked to provide the correct values directly.

The Visa status field still exists on the student profile but is only visible to career services users, not to students.

  1. Can a student edit their work authorization responses after submitting them?

Yes. A student can edit their responses at any time by clicking their account icon in the upper-right corner of the page, then clicking Settings.

They can scroll to the Work authorization section, make the desired updates, and click Save Update at the bottom of the page.

  1. How do employer work authorization selections impact students who are not fully qualified?

The impact varies depending on the opportunity type:

  • For job postings, students who are not fully qualified can still apply.
  • For virtual fair 1:1 sessions, students who do not match the employer’s requirements will not be able to view or sign up for sessions.
