Your Handshake Account

About AI-powered features in Handshake for students

Handshake offers artificial intelligence (AI) tools designed to support your career planning, enhance your profile, and help you build skills. These tools can also help you discover jobs and content that better match your interests.

This article explains where AI appears in the student experience, how it works at a high level, and the steps we take to protect your privacy.

How you can use AI tools in Handshake

1. AI assistant on jobs – get tailored profile and resume tips for a specific job

On some jobs, you may have an option to receive tips and coaching for how to make your profile align with the requirements for a specific job. The AI assistant is a conversational tool that helps you understand how well you align with that specific job and what you can improve in your profile.

What you can do with it

  • Ask questions about how your experience compares to the job’s requirements.
  • Get suggestions to better highlight relevant skills and accomplishments drawn from your background.
  • Receive recommendations for updates on your Handshake profile (for example, adding skills or refining descriptions) so your skills align with the role. What it uses

To generate suggestions, AI assistant may use:

  • The job description and requirements
  • Your Handshake profile and resume (if uploaded)
  • Any additional input you choose to provide during the conversation Third-party AI providers are under contracts that prohibit using Handshake data to train their own models, and profile/resume information is redacted to remove direct identifiers before processing.

How you stay in control

  • AI assistant is optional—you choose whether to launch and use it from the job details page.
  • You decide which suggested changes to accept, modify, or ignore before updating your profile or applying.
  • AI assistant does not apply to jobs on your behalf or make hiring decisions for employers. To Learn more about how to use AI Assistant on jobs, refer to AI Assistant on Jobs.
2. Conversational job search and queries

Handshake offers AI-assisted job search that lets you use natural-language search phrases instead of relying only on filters. For example, you could type: “A buying job for a retailer in California.”

This feature allows you to describe what you’re looking for in plain language. The system then translates your request into job searches behind the scenes

In these cases:

  • Suggestions do not change which jobs are available for you to view or apply to. They only affect how your searches are ordered.
  • You can edit the search at any time or return to classic keyword and filter-based searches.
3. AI Showcase (beta)

This space lets you explore how students and alumni are using AI in real projects. It’s designed to inspire you to build and share your own work

What you can do with it

  • Browse AI projects created by other job seekers to see how they’re applying AI across different roles and industries.
  • Explore individual projects to learn what problem was solved, which tools were used, and how the creator describes the project’s impact.
  • Submit your own AI project to be featured, allowing other students and participating employers to see what you’ve built. At this time, AI Showcase is not yet be available to all students or schools.

To learn more about AI Showcase, check out AI Showcase in Handshake.

4. Handshake Sidekick – AI resume helper (beta)

Handshake Sidekick is an AI-powered resume tool that helps you strengthen how you present your experience before you apply. If available in your account, you can upload a resume, chat with an assistant that analyzes it, get suggestions for clearer wording and structure, and download an updated version to use when applying to jobs on Handshake.

To learn more about how to access and use Sidekick, refer to Handshake Sidekick: AI-powered resume helper.

How Handshake uses AI to power your experience

Separate from the optional tools above, Handshake uses AI models behind the scenes to personalize your experience on the platform, primarily by ranking and ordering existing content.

These systems do not decide who gets hired and do not block you from viewing or applying to jobs.

1. Personalized job recommendations and search

Handshake uses AI to rank jobs by how likely you are to engage with them (view, save, apply) based on your profile and past activity. This helps surface roles that better match your interests near the top of your job search results.

How you stay in control

  • You can change filters, sort options, and use keywords at any time to see different results.
  • Updating your profile, interests, and location preferences influences which jobs are ranked higher for you.
  • The model’s output affects how jobs are ordered, not whether you are allowed to view or apply to a job.
2. AI-tuned feed and content relevance

Your Handshake feed shows posts, jobs, and other content ordered by how relevant and engaging they’re likely to be for you. AI models rank this content using signals like your profile, past engagement, and information about each post.

How you stay in control

  • You can follow or unfollow employers and topics, and choose which posts to like or save—these actions influence what you see more of over time.
  • You can still scroll your Feed freely; AI only affects the order, not whether content is available to you.

AI Showcase in Handshake

AI Showcase is a feature in Handshake that allows students and alumni to explore

and share projects that use artificial intelligence (AI). It’s designed to help

you learn from others and highlight your own work.

AI Showcase lets you:

  • Discover how other students and alumni are using AI across different roles, industries, and majors

  • Share your own AI-related projects with the handshake community

  • Build a visible portfolio of your work directly on your profile Projects featured in AI Showcase typically include:

  • The problem the project addresses

  • The AI tools or models used

  • A description of how the project works

  • The impact or outcome of the project Note: AI Showcase is currently in beta and is not be available at all schools.

For a limited time, Handshake is partnering with Google—click the expandable header to learn more!

Google AI Plus offer and contest

For a limited time, Handshake is partnering with Google to give currently enrolled university students in the U.S. and Canada a free year of Google AI Plus.

On top of the free offer, there’s also a contest: use Google AI Plus, make a video showing how you used it, post on Instagram or TikTok tagging @joinhandshake and @googlegemini, and you could win $500 and a Google career chat. There are 8 winners total.

To claim the offer, visit Google AI Plus in Handshake. For full eligibility details, timelines, and contest rules, refer to the Terms and conditions.

Access AI Showcase

  1. Click AI Showcase in the left navigation menu in Handshake

  2. Or go directly to: app.joinhandshake.com

You must have a student or alumni Handshake account to access this feature. If you don’t have AI Showcase in your account, it is not yet available at your school.

Submit a Project in AI Showcase

  1. Go to the AI Showcase page

  2. Click the Submit your project button

  3. Enter the following details:

  • Project title
  • Project link (URL)
  • Project description (optional)
    • Include the problem, how it works, who it helps, and AI tools used
  1. Click Submit to publish your project, or Cancel to exit

Note: Once submitted, your project will be added to your Handshake profile. Selected projects may also be featured on the AI Showcase page.

Tips for a Strong Submission

  • Clearly describe what you personally built, designed, or implemented
  • Highlight real-world impact by explaining how your project solves a specific problem
  • Keep your description clear and easy to understand
  • Do not include sensitive, personal, or confidential information Using AI Showcase is a great way to demonstrate your skills, explore how others are using AI, and create a portfolio of work that you can share with employers.

Archive Messages From Inbox

If you want to clean up your Handshake inbox, you can archive message threads so they no longer appear in your main Inbox. Messages cannot be permanently deleted right now, but we are tracking feedback about a delete option for the future.

Note: To archive a message, use Handshake in a desktop web browser.

Archive a message

  1. Click Inbox on the left navigation menu.

  2. In the list of conversations on the left, click on the message you want to archive.

  3. In the upper-right corner of the open message, click the three dots menu, then select Archive.

Once a message thread is archived, it’s removed from your inbox.

View archived messages

You can open archived messages at any time by selecting the Archived tab in the upper-left corner of your inbox.

Unarchive a message

If you archived a conversation by mistake or want it back in your main inbox, you can unarchive it.

  • Open your inbox, then select the Archived tab in the upper-left corner.
  • Choose the message thread you want to restore.
  • In the upper-right corner of the open message, click the three dots menu, then select Unarchive. Once unarchived, the conversation will appear again in your main Inbox.

Exporting Your Calendar

Handshake offers you the option to export your Handshake calendar to help you track upcoming events, appointments, and more by using the URL in your Settings. To initiate the export, follow the the steps below.

  1. Click on your account icon in the upper-right corner of Handshake, then click Settings from the dropdown menu.

  2. Select Calendar export.

  3. To export your Handshake calendar, you can either: copy the link by clicking Copy calendar link or, click the link Download a static iCalendar file to download a static link.

💡Note: The static file download link isn’t updated automatically.

There are many calendar applications available, and some are built into your operating system. We’ve included links to instructions for some of the most popular calendar applications below. If your calendar application isn’t listed, refer to the instruction manual for your calendar application to add an ICS URL.

Outlook Calendar

Google Calendar*

Office 365 Calendar

Important: It may take up to 12 hours for updates to be transferred to your Google Calendar from Handshake. This is a Google setting and can’t be modified by Handshake.

Handshake Accounts that are Deactivated or Blocked

If you receive a message stating that your account is deactivated or blocked when logging into Handshake, this means your school has taken action on your account.

Deactivated accounts

If your school deactivates (archives) your Handshake account, you can still access Handshake even though your school no longer manages your account. Instead of losing access, you’ll continue using the platform as an unaffiliated user.

What unaffiliated access means for you
  • You can still sign in and use Handshake, even though your school has archived your account.
  • When you sign in, you’ll land on the School Connections page, where you can check your school connection and request to reconnect if that option is available (for example, if you return for another program).
  • Your school will still appear in the Education section of your profile, but it won’t show that you’re currently enrolled.
  • The main change is that you won’t have access to your school’s career center features in Handshake (like appointments), and your school won’t be able to view or manage your account. Note: You may be prompted to add a personal (non-school) email address when you sign in. This helps to ensure you can continue using your Handshake account if you lose access to your school email.

Blocked accounts

If your account has been blocked, you will receive a message stating “Account Blocked”.

Common reasons your account may be blocked:

  • Late tuition payments or other payments
  • Misuse of Handshake
  • Student misconduct (not showing up for an on-campus interview, for example) If your account is blocked, contact support for more information.

The Handshake EMEA Migration: What You Need to Know

Handshake has consolidated its EMEA platform into a single global platform. If you previously used Handshake’s EMEA-specific platform, your account is now part of this global platform.

Your day-to-day experience won’t change. You’ll continue to sign in the same way and use Handshake as you always have.

What’s different after the migration

Your Student/Alumni account, along with your profile data, was migrated and is now accessible at app.joinhandshake.com (previously Handshake US). Historical activity was not able to be carried over, but we encourage you to explore the newly expanded network and opportunities available in our Global platform!

  • Peer messages: If you previously messaged with a student or alumnus, you should be able to locate them on the platform and re-start the conversation, refer to Peer Messaging in Handshake for more information.
  • Employer messages: Some employers may have different representatives from the previous platform, but you can find the relevant contact information on the employer’s brand page. Learn more in Messaging Employers in Handshake.
  • Applications: One change you may notice is more international opportunities in your job search. Depending on your preferences and activity, you may have access to roles from countries such as the United States, United Kingdom, Germany, or France. Opportunities in your primary market will still be prioritized, with international roles appearing when they’re relevant to your interests. Learn more about searching for jobs in Searching for Jobs and Internships.
  • Followers and Feed: Follow employers and other early talent users to access their updates in your Feed, and share your own posts to connect with the Handshake community. Learn more in Following Users on Handshake and Posting Content to the Handshake Feed.
  • Your personal data continues to be protected under the same privacy standards outlined in Handshake Infrastructure & Data Update. To learn more about your account, privacy, data, and getting your profile fully set up on the global platform, refer to EMEA: Your Handshake Account, Privacy and Data.

Handshake Sidekick: AI-powered resume helper

Sidekick is an AI-powered resume helper that is accessible when you are logged into Handshake. Sidekick helps you quickly create a recruiter-ready resume and land more interviews by highlighting your relevant skills and optimizing it for employer screening.

Sidekick is designed for students and early-career job seekers who:

  • Have a resume but are not ready to apply to opportunities with it

  • Need help describing experiences and skills

  • Want a stronger, impact-focused resume to use across many job, internship, or fellowship applications With Sidekick, you can:

  • Upload an existing resume or start from a resume already stored in your Documents

    • Document uploads must be 1MB or smaller, and files must be in PDF, .DOC, or .DOCX format.

  • Get an instantly improved resume

  • Chat with an AI assistant to get further suggestions for improved wording, structure, and how to highlight your skills

  • Ask for edits focused on a particular job or type of role (for example, “software engineering internships” or “lab assistant”)

  • Download an updated version and/or save it back to your Documents so you can use it when applying on Handshake This feature is powered by a third-party large language model (LLM); any text you submit will be processed by that provider in accordance with our data agreements and privacy standards. For more information on how your data is used and protected, please review our Privacy Policy.

Who can use Sidekick

Sidekick is available to logged-in Handshake users with a student account, and you must be signed in to access it.

Note: Handshake’s Sidekick is not available at all schools.

For the best experience, use Sidekick on a computer or larger tablet screen.

How to access Sidekick

Click Jobs in the left navigation, then select Optimize resume located in the upper-left corner, to the right of Saved.

If Optimize resume is not available, this means your school does not have access to Sidekick.

Get started with Sidekick

  1. Upload/Select a resume
  • If you already have a resume uploaded in your Documents, you can use it or select a different one by clicking the down arrow.
  • If you do not have a resume uploaded yet, click the upload resume button to upload a resume directly to Sidekick.
  1. Tell Sidekick the role and industry you’re interested in

In the chat, select from the pre-built prompt questions to get started — such as the kinds of roles and industries you are targeting — or type your own request in the text box.

Sidekick is designed to assist with resumes only and cannot answer questions outside of this scope.

  1. Sidekick provides a new resume with suggestions and edits

Sidekick analyzes your resume and suggests improvements to wording, structure, and emphasis. It may also recommend a more consistent layout and clearer phrasing to better highlight your qualifications.

Click Download to review the updated resume with these edits.

  1. Collaborate if needed

Keep chatting with Sidekick to refine your resume. If a suggestion doesn’t work for you, ask Sidekick to revise it or keep your original wording. You can also ask follow-up questions like, “Make this experience more results-focused” or “Help me shorten this section.”

  1. Download and/or Save to your Documents

Click Download to download, or click Save to store it in your Documents in Handshake. The resume will be available when you apply for jobs in Handshake.

Once saved, a notification appears in the bottom-right corner. Click View now to open your document.

Using your Sidekick resume when applying on Handshake

When you apply to jobs on Handshake, resumes that you’ve saved to your Documents are available to attach to your application.

To find a job, refer to Searching for Jobs and Internships. To apply for a job, check out Apply for a Job in Handshake.

Tip: to get the most out of Sidekick, be honest and accurate. Do not ask Sidekick to add experiences, degrees, or skills you do not have.

Important notes and limitations

  • Sidekick does not decide whether you get a job. It only helps you improve how you present your experience. Employers still make their own hiring decisions.
  • You stay in control. Sidekick will not apply to jobs on your behalf. You choose where and when to submit your resume.
  • Accuracy and tone. AI tools can occasionally produce suggestions that are repetitive, not quite in your voice, or not fully accurate for your situation. You are responsible for reviewing and correcting your resume before applying.
  • Sensitive information. Avoid adding unnecessary sensitive personal information to your resume or the chat (for example, government ID numbers, medical information, or passwords).

Handshake Student Account FAQs

If you’re interested in creating a Handshake account as a student, but you have a few questions or concerns before doing so, check out this article for more information! It provides answers to common questions about signing up and using Handshake, as well as tips for getting the most out of the platform.

Why should I make a Handshake account if I already have a LinkedIn account?

Handshake is so much more than a site to search for jobs! It also offers you the opportunity to connect with employers and alumni, sign up for events and career fairs, take advantage of your school’s resources, and communicate with your career services center.

Handshake is the ideal career site for college students and new graduates, as it offers more career options than any other platform.

Additionally, all the posted jobs are specifically targeted for students and new graduates - This means you aren’t applying for jobs that require years of experience.

Ready to create an account and explore jobs? If so, check out Getting Started with Handshake for more information!

Why should I fill out my Handshake profile?

Handshake will personalize job recommendations based on the details you provide on your profile.

Plus, employers often use Handshake to search for candidates, and having a complete profile will make it easier for employers to find you! Additionally, your profile will give you access to exclusive resources such as career fairs, networking events, and workshops that may require qualifications. By completing your profile, you can take advantage of all the amazing opportunities Handshake has to offer.

Which parts of my Handshake profile are most important to fill out?

We recommend filling out your profile in its entirety! This will ensure you’re making the most of your experience on Handshake.

For more information on filling out your profile, refer to Completing your Profile in Handshake.

What are the top things employers search for?

Employers may vary in their expectations, but in the majority of cases, they are interested in your:

  • Job interests - this provides the employer with information on what sort of position you are seeking. Your job interests consist of: the job type, the preferred location, and the job role you are interested in.
    • Job type: on-campus job, internship, part-time job, or full-time job
    • Preferred location: cities you’d like to work in
    • Job role: positions you’d like to explore. Example: “marketing associate” or “data analyst
      • Tip: you can update your job interests at anytime! Refer to Update Your Career Interests for more information.
  • Work experience - this lets the employer know of any past part-time employment, internships, work study, research positions, or volunteer work you’ve done. Employers like to acknowledge that you have accepted responsibility and have grown professionally through these experiences.
  • Skills and qualifications - this lets the employer know what you have to offer. Add technical skills like SQL along with soft skills like communication. The more skills you list, the better your chances are of showing up in an employer search.
  • Relevant coursework or certifications - if you have taken courses in your field, or have certifications, this can be a great way to show you have the background to perform the job. It also shows the employer that you are committed to your career and have invested in advancing your knowledge.
  • Clubs and organizations - these signal your specific interests, commitment to a cause, and participation and involvement on campus.

Why should I care about other students on Handshake?

Building a network on Handshake gives you the opportunity to exchange tips with others, pass along contacts, receive interview advice, and more!

Connecting with other professionals is an excellent way to identify your career goals and improve your chances of getting the job you want!

To connect with peers and start networking, refer to Peer Messaging in Handshake.

Why should I make my profile public?

Handshake offers you the option to choose your profile visibility at any given time. While your profile visibility is completely up to you, there are some advantages to having your profile public.

Making your profile public allows employers to find you and view your qualifications, which increases the likelihood of you being considered for jobs. It also offers others the ability to find and connect with you, which can lead to new opportunities for collaboration or networking.

To learn more about your profile privacy options on Handshake, refer to Profile Privacy Options in Handshake.

Can I use Handshake on my phone?

Yes! Handshake has an app that can be downloaded iOs and Android devices!

Check out About Handshake Mobile for iOS and Android to learn more.

What is the best way to use keyword search and filters?

The best way to use keyword search and filters is to first determine the keywords that are most relevant to what you are looking for. Once you have identified the keywords, you can use them in combination with filters to narrow down your search results and find the most relevant results.

To find events and career fairs of interest, refer to Discover Events & Fairs in Handshake.

To search for jobs and internships, refer to Searching for Jobs and Internships.

Handshake Supported Browsers (for Students)

This guide outlines the browsers and devices that work best with Handshake for students and alumni. It also covers our recommended browser settings, what to do if your browser is out of date, and step-by-step troubleshooting tips to try before reaching out to Support.

Mobile devices

For mobile, use the Handshake mobile app on iOS or Android for the best experience.

Handshake may also open in a mobile browser, but some features can be limited or less reliable compared to the app.

Desktop and laptop browsers

For the best experience on Handshake, we recommend using Google Chrome, which supports all platform features, including integrated video with blurred backgrounds.

If Chrome is not your default browser or is otherwise inconvenient to use, Handshake also supports most features on the latest versions of the following browsers:

  • Firefox
  • Safari
  • Microsoft Edge Note: We no longer support any version of Internet Explorer.

Outdated browsers

If you are using an outdated browser version, the following error message may appear:

“It looks like your browser is out of date and not fully supported. This may cause Handshake to work improperly. We recommend updating your browser for a better experience and improved security.”

You should be able to use Handshake features with most modern browsers released within the last rolling 6 months. However, there may be certain limitations or behaviors specific to the browser used.

It is recommended that you update your browser whenever there is a new version available, as these updates often include performance and security improvements.

Troubleshooting tips

If you encounter unexpected errors or unusual behavior while using Handshake such as “SyntaxError Unexpected token ‘u’”upstream c” is not valid JSON”, open Handshake in Chrome and try again.

  • If you’re already using Chrome, or if the issue occurs in multiple browsers, clear your browser’s cache and cookies. For additional guidance, refer to Refresh your Cache.
  • If you cannot clear your cache immediately, you can use an incognito or private browsing window:
    • PC (Windows 7/8/10/11):
      • Chrome: Press Ctrl + Shift + N.
      • Firefox/Edge: Press Ctrl + Shift + P.
    • Mac (OS X):
      • Chrome/Safari: Press Command + Shift + N.
      • Firefox: Press Command + Shift + P. If the issue persists after these steps, contact Support.

Note: If you’re joining an event, fair, interview, or appointment using integrated video on Handshake, Chrome is still the best option for performance on desktop web. For more specifics, refer to the dedicated section Attendee Resources.

How to Change Your Email

You can use different email addresses with your Handshake account over time—for example, starting with your school email as a student and switching to a personal email after you graduate. There are two main ways to update your email, depending on your situation:

  • Access to current account: Add a new email and set it as your primary.
  • No longer have access to your school email: Contact your career center to request an update.

Access to current account

If you’re a current student and want Handshake messages sent to a different email, the simplest option is to add a new email and make it your primary address.

This allows you to:

  • Add a personal (alternate) email
  • Set it as your primary so Handshake and your school send messages there For step-by-step instructions, refer to Update Your Primary Email Address in Handshake.

No longer have access to your school email

If you’re an alum and can’t access your old school email—or you’ve changed schools and no longer have access, contact the school’s career center and ask them to update the email on your Handshake account.

They’ll start the email change process for you.

Important: The new email address must not already be associated with any Handshake account (student, employer, or career services)

If you already created another account with that email:

  • You’ll need to request that the account be deleted
  • Once it’s removed and the email address is freed up, your school can update your original account to use that email

How the Email Change Process Works (School-initiated change)

After your career center submits the request, you’ll receive two emails from Handshake.

Email #1 (sent to your old email)

Purpose: Notifies you that a change was requested

  • From: Handshake handshake@m.joinhandshake.com
  • Subject: Handshake Email Change Request This email lets you know a request was made and directs you to check your new email for next steps.
Email #2 (sent to your new email)

Purpose: Confirms and verifies your new email

  • From: Handshake handshake@m.joinhandshake.com

  • Subject: Handshake Email Change Request This email includes:

  • Your old and new email addresses

  • A verification code

  • A Change Email button

How to confirm the change
  • Open Email #2 and click Change Email
    • Make sure you remain logged into Handshake under your old email address in order to make this update.
  • Enter the verification code from the email
  • Click Finish Email Change If everything is valid, your email will be successfully updated.

Note: The Change Email link expires after 12 hours. If it expires, contact your career center to restart the process.

Troubleshooting tips

  • Link not opening? Try a different browser (like Chrome or Firefox)
  • Not receiving Handshake emails? Check your spam and junk mail. Add Handshake to your address book with the following contact email: “handshake@m.joinhandshake.com”.
  • “No account on file” message?
    • Go back to Email #2 and select Change Email again
    • Make sure you enter your old email if prompted
  • Having trouble logging in with SSO after the change?
    • You may need to reset your password
    • Use the “Reset password” option on the login page and follow the steps in Reset the Password for a Student Account in Handshake. If you’re still unable to access your account, contact your school’s career center or Handshake Support for help.

Switching schools and using more than one Handshake account

If you start attending a new school that uses Handshake and receive a new school email, it’s best to create or claim a separate account for that email. This allows you to stay connected to both schools while each one manages its own data and services.

You can continue using both accounts—one for each school.

For your previous school’s account, consider updating the email to a personal address so you can keep access after you graduate or transfer.

Important:

  • Each email address can only be used on one Handshake account at a time
  • If your personal email is already linked to your old school’s account, you won’t be able to use it for a new account unless that email is first removed or the original account is deleted
  • Handshake does not support merging or combining student accounts from different schools into a single account

How to Create an Employer Account Linked to Your Student Account (Your Handshake Account)

This article explains how to create an employer account using the same email address as your student account.

Before you get started

Keep the following in mind before creating your employer account:

  • If you plan to create an employer account with your school email address, first confirm that your employer allows you to use that email for employer access in Handshake.
  • Sign out of your student account before you begin creating your employer account.
  • Using an incognito or private browsing window can help prevent your browser from automatically signing you back in to your student account during registration.

Single single on (SSO)

To connect both your student account and employer account to the same email address, you’ll need to create Handshake login credentials. Employer accounts do not use Single Sign-On (SSO) to access the platform.

Note: Your Handshake login credentials are separate from your school’s SSO login. Your Handshake password is unique to the platform and is not linked to your school’s SSO login.

  • If you already have a Handshake password or do not use SSO, continue to Create your employer account.
  • If you need to create Handshake login credentials, refer to How to Set Up Handshake Login Credentials (if you’re unable to use Single Sign On).
  • If you need to reset your password, refer to Reset the Password for a Student Account in Handshake.

Create your employer account

  1. Go to app.joinhandshake.com.

  2. Enter your first name, last name, email address, and the password associated with your student account.

  3. Review the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy, then click the black Create account button.

  4. A yellow banner will appear below the email address field with a message that your email already exists in Handshake and is associated with an early talent account. This is expected.

  • If you forgot your password, click Reset it in the yellow banner, then return to app.joinhandshake.com to complete registration.

  1. Confirm that the email address, first name, last name, and password match your existing account, then click Create account again.

  2. Check your inbox for a confirmation email from Handshake with the following details:

From: handshake@notifications.joinhandshake.com

Subject: Confirm your email address on Handshake

Body: “Welcome to Handshake! Please confirm your email address to get started.”

Confirm email [button]

If this is a mistake or you didn’t initiate this request, contact Handshake support.

Click the Confirm email button in the email.

  1. After confirming your email address, Handshake redirects you to complete your employer profile.

For the remaining registration steps, refer to How to Create an Employer Account on Handshake.

After you create your employer account

After you sign in, you can switch between your student and employer account from the menu under your name. For more information, refer to Switching User Views.

How to Locate your School’s Contact Information in Handshake

If you need to connect with your school’s career center, or a specific staff member at your school, you can find their contact information in Handshake.

If you are not logged into your Handshake account, you can look for your school’s career center contact information on your school’s website. Many schools publish the career center’s email, phone number, and office location there.

Find your career center’s contact information in Handshake

  • In the left navigation menu, select Career Center.
  • On the Career Center page, scroll to the middle of the page.
  • On the right side, locate the Contact Information section. In this section, you can find your school’s website, phone number, email address, and location.

Find contact information for a specific staff member

  • On the same Career Center page, scroll to the bottom.
  • Locate the Public Staff section. Up to five staff members are displayed.
  • To open a staff member’s profile, select their name.
  • To view all public staff members, select the blue View All Public Staff button.
  • On an individual staff profile, the staff member’s contact information is located on the left side of the page.

How to Re-Subscribe to Handshake Emails

Students and alumni may occasionally stop receiving emails from Handshake, such as job alerts, application updates, interview notifications, and other platform messages.

These emails are separate from messages sent by your university or by employers through their own systems.

Before requesting help, make sure:

  • You’re checking the inbox linked to your Handshake account
  • You’ve looked in:
    • Inbox
    • Junk / Spam
    • Other folders or filters
  • You’ve searched your email for “Handshake” across all folders If you find emails in spam or another folder, move them to your inbox and mark them as “not spam.”

What “email suppression” means

If you still aren’t receiving emails, your address may be suppressed.

This means Handshake is preventing certain emails from being sent to your address. Common reasons include:

  • You clicked an unsubscribe link
  • Emails to your address previously failed to deliver (bounced)

How to start receiving emails again

If your email is suppressed and you want to receive emails from Handshake again, contact Handshake Support and request removal from the suppression list.

How to Set Up Handshake Login Credentials (if you’re unable to use Single Sign On)

Many schools let you access Handshake through Single Sign-On (SSO) using your campus login. If you no longer have access to SSO, or you prefer to sign in with an email and password, you can create Handshake login credentials.

Your Handshake login credentials are is the email address on your Handshake account and a password created by you. It is separate from your school’s SSO password.

If you’ve already created a Handshake password but can’t remember it, you can reset it anytime. For instructions, refer to Reset the Password for a Student Account in Handshake.

Create your Handshake credentials

  1. Go to the Handshake login page.

  2. In the “Find your school” box, type your school name and select it from the dropdown.

  3. If your school uses SSO: Do not select the button to log in with your school. Instead, click Continue with email and enter the email address associated with your Handshake account.

If your school does not use SSO: Enter the email address associated with your Handshake account and click Next.

  1. Handshake will recognize the email address in the system—enter your password and click Login.

  2. A confirmation email will be sent to your inbox. Go to your inbox, find the email, and click Set My Password. If you have trouble receiving the confirmation email, refer to Troubleshooting Missing Confirmation Email.

  3. Once confirmed, you’ll be prompted to create a new password. Enter your password in the provided fields, then click Next.

Tip: Your password must be at least 8 characters long and include at least 2 of the following: letters, numbers, and special characters.

After you successfully set your password, you can log in to Handshake using your email and newly created password.

How to Take a Survey in Handshake

Your school may choose to create and conduct surveys in Handshake. If you are invited to take a survey, you can access it in two ways:

  • Directly from the invitation email
  • From the Surveys section in Handshake Note: some surveys may be required by your school, while others are optional.

Access the survey from the email

When your school invites you to take a survey, you will receive an email in your inbox. This email is sent to the primary email address associated with your Handshake account.

  • Open the invitation email.

  • Select the Take Survey Now button to be directed to the survey in Handshake.

  • Answer each question by following the prompts.

  • When you are finished, select the green Finish button to submit your response. Example email details:

  • Title: Survey Invitation

  • From: Handshake handshake@notifications.joinhandshake.com

  • Body: “You have been invited to take a survey on Handshake. A description of the survey and a direct link to take the survey in Handshake.

Access the survey from the Surveys section in Handshake

  • Click Career Center from the left navigation menu.
  • Select Surveys.
  • All surveys you have been invited to are listed on this page.
    • If any surveys are required by your school, a yellow banner appears at the top of your Surveys dashboard.
    • Required surveys have a red Required badge displayed to the right of the survey name.
  • Select the name of the survey you want to take.
  • Answer each question by following the prompts.
  • When you are finished, click Finish button to submit your response.

If you can’t find your survey

If you believe you have been invited to a survey but cannot locate it:

  • Check your email:
    • Make sure you are checking the primary email address linked to your Handshake account.
    • Review your spam, junk, and promotions folders for the invitation email.
  • Confirm in Handshake:
    • Log into Handshake and go to Career Center > Surveys to view all surveys you have been invited to.
  • Still not finding it?
    • Contact your school’s career center. They can confirm whether the survey is still open, whether it is required, and whether it has been sent to your account.

Log In as an Alum: Set your Handshake Password

If you are an alum, you can keep using Handshake after graduation!

To sign in without your school’s Single Sign-On (SSO), you’ll need to create Handshake credentials. This consists of the email address associated with your account and a password, or a linked Google or Apple account, which you can use directly on the Handshake login page.

  • If you already created a Handshake password in the past, sign in at the Handshake login page using that email and password.
  • If you used to sign in only through your school’s SSO, follow the steps below to set up Handshake credentials.

What to Do If You No Longer Have Access to Your School Email

Choose the option that matches your situation:

  • You had a Handshake account before: If you previously used Handshake but no longer have access to your school email, contact your school’s career center. Let them know you’re an alum who wants to continue using Handshake with a personal email address. Ask if they can update the email on your existing account. Updating your email helps keep your account connected to your school’s Handshake network.
  • You have never had a Handshake account: If you’ve never created an account, go to the Handshake login page and select Sign up. Then follow the steps in Getting Started with Handshake to complete your registration.

Steps to Set Up Handshake Credentials

Use these steps if you used SSO before and now want to log in with a password or another method.

  1. Go to the Handshake login page.

  2. Either:

  • Select your school from the dropdown, or
  • Enter your email address in the field provided.

  1. Click Next.

  2. If you previously used your school’s SSO, you might be redirected to your school’s login page. Look for options such as:

  • Alumni Login – sends an email that guides you to set a password and create Handshake credentials.
  • Log in another way – allows you to either:
    • Receive a one-time password by email, or
    • Sign in with your Google or Apple account, if available. If you do not receive the password setup email or one-time password email, follow the steps in Troubleshooting Missing Confirmation Email.

No account found with email

If you enter an email and get a message that no account was found:

  • Check that your email address is typed correctly.

  • Try other email addresses you may have used as a student (for example, personal vs school email). If the message still appears, it can mean:

  • You never had a Handshake account with that email.

  • You used a different email address.

  • Your school archived an older account. If you are not sure which applies:

  • Contact your school’s career center and ask whether you already have a Handshake account on file.

  • If they confirm you have no existing account, follow the Create a new Handshake account steps below.

Create a new Handshake account (when no account exists)

  1. On the Handshake signup page, click Sign up.

  2. Enter the email address you want to use for Handshake, then click Next.

  3. Select your school from the dropdown, then click Next.

  • If you cannot find your school, select Continue without a school to register without being connected to a school.
  • If you do not connect with a school, you will not have access to all school-specific features in Handshake. For more details, refer to School not Found on Handshake.
  1. If you continued with a school, you are prompted to:
  • Create a password that meets the requirements listed on screen.
  • Agree to Handshake’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.
  • Enter your new password in both fields and select Create account.
  1. Enter the following information to finish creating your account:
  • First name
  • Last name
  • Major
  • Education pursuing
  • Graduation month
  • Graduation year If your school has additional required fields, complete those as well. When everything is complete, click Finish setup.
  1. A confirmation email is sent to the email address you used for sign-up.
  • Open the email in your inbox.
  • Click the Confirm email button in the message. If you’re having trouble receiving the confirmation email, refer to Troubleshooting Missing Confirmation Email.

Once confirmed, you’ll be directed to Handshake!

Note: If your school requires approval for new accounts, your account might show as pending.

  • To check your status, open your account menu by selecting your account icon (your initials or photo) in the upper-right corner.
  • Select School connections from the dropdown.
  • If your account stays pending longer than expected, contact your school’s career center for help.

Managing Your Notification Preferences

Managing your notification preferences helps you stay informed about important updates that matter to you.

Open your Notification preferences

  • Click your account icon in the upper-right corner.
  • Select Notification preferences from the dropdown menu. You can return to this page and update your preferences at any time.

Review and customize your notifications

On the Notification Preferences page:

  • Review each notification category listed.
  • For each category, choose how you’d like to receive notifications by clicking the dropdown arrow and selecting or deselecting the options (checked = on, unchecked = off). Some settings are turned on by default for new student accounts. For details about which notifications are available and which are active by default, refer to Default Notification Preferences (Students).

Notification types

When you adjust a setting, you can typically choose from these notification types:

  • Email notifications – sent to the primary email address linked to your Handshake account.
  • In-app notifications – available in Handshake under the bell icon to the left of your account icon.
  • Push notifications – available only in the Handshake mobile app. Note: Not all notification types are available for every notification option.

After you update your notification preferences, you can move to another page or sign out. Your changes are saved automatically!

Navigating the Student Homepage

The Explore page, also known as your homepage on Handshake, connects you to valuable career resources and your school’s career center. It’s designed to help you discover opportunities tailored to your interests and career goals.

Explore page highlights

The content on your Explore page is personalized based on your engagement and career interests, with the most relevant information highlighted for easy access.

Depending on your activity and career preferences, your explore page may feature the following sections:

  • Trending: Popular posts from the Handshake feed with quick access to the full feed.
  • Jobs: Top job listings in your field, including opportunities from popular employers and roles well-suited to your major.
  • Events: Upcoming career-related events and career fairs.
  • From Your School: Curated highlights from your school’s Career Center.
    • If your school’s Career Center has personalized categories, you may also find the featured categories here. These categories include employers and jobs your school decided to highlight. To learn more about the employers and jobs that your school has curated, check out Career Center Collections At Your School.

School resources

If your account is connected to your school, you gain direct access to its career resources. You can visit the Career Center by clicking the link View your school’s resources from the banner on your Explore page or by clicking Career Center in the left navigation menu.

In the Career Center, you’ll find:

  • Appointments: Schedule meetings with experts to advance your career. Learn more in Request an Appointment with your Career Center.
  • Resources: Access curated content and career guides.
  • Experiences: Track your internships or co-op experiences. For more details, refer to Request an Experience (as a Student), Managing Your Experience, and Tracking Your Experience.
  • First Destination: Update your school on your post-graduation plans.
  • Surveys: Complete career-related surveys from your Career Center.
  • Career Journey: Complete tasks to progress along your career path. Additionally, you’ll have access to upcoming events, career fairs, and a staff directory, along with your school’s contact information.

If your Career Center has personalized categories, you may also find featured jobs and employers. To explore these, check out Career Center Collections At Your School.

Missing the Career Center option on the left navigation bar?

Here are a few possible reasons:

  • School not linked: If you’ve requested to connect with a school, check your status by clicking your profile icon, then School Connections. If it says “Pending,” your school still needs to approve your request.
  • No school on account: If you registered without selecting a school, features like the Career Center won’t be available. To connect, click your profile icon, then School Connections. Find your school and request to join.
  • School not on Handshake (yet!): If your school isn’t a partner, encourage your career center to join so you can access more features.

Request User Account Deletion

Before deciding to delete your Handshake account, we encourage you to explore a few alternative options that may address your concerns. These solutions can often help you maintain access to valuable features and benefits without the need for deletion.

Once you delete your Handshake account, it can’t be restored. You’ll also lose access to your school’s Handshake services like appointment, events, job listings, and more.

Recommendations Instead of Deleting Your Account

  • Not Looking for a Job or Internship?
  • If you’re not currently job-hunting, you can update your career interests to reflect your current needs. To do this, refer to Step 4 in Update Your Career Interests.
  • Concerns About Your Account or Data Privacy?
  • If you’re concerned about privacy, Handshake offers various profile privacy options. Setting your profile to Private completely hides your information from employers and other students while still allowing you to access your school’s career services. Learn more in Profile Privacy Options in Handshake.
  • Want to Adjust Notification and Email Preferences?
  • If you’d like to change how you receive notifications and emails, you can adjust your settings in the Default Notification Preferences.
  • Want to Step Away Temporarily?
  • If you’d like to pause your access but may want to return later, contact your school’s career services office to ask about archiving your account instead of deleting it. Archiving preserves your data and allows for future reactivation.

How to Request Account Deletion

To begin the deletion process, contact Support. Be sure to use the valid email address associated with your account. If you’ve created an account with a misspelled email address, you can still create a new account with the correct email in the meantime–if requesting deletion of the account with the misspelled email, use your valid email address and include the misspelled email in your request.

Important: If your school has partnered with Handshake, you’ll need to followup with your school’s Career Center directly to inform them of your deletion. Most institutions sync student information into Handshake as a service provider. When an account is deleted from Handshake, but not updated in the student information system, the next time the institution runs the sync, the account will be re-created (but defaulted to an unactivated account: fully private and not shared with anyone).

Reset the Password for a Student Account in Handshake

You can reset your Handshake password at any time—whether you forgot it or just want to update it.

Important: The following steps will guide you through resetting your Handshake password only. If you need to reset your school’s single sign-on (SSO) password, you must do that outside of Handshake. For help resetting your SSO password, contact your school’s Career Services Center.

Choose the option that matches your current status:

  • I’m currently signed in to Handshake
  • I’m currently signed out of Handshake

I’m currently signed in to Handshake

Only users who registered without connecting to a school can update their password directly in Handshake.

If your account is linked to a school, log out and follow the steps below under “I’m currently signed out” instead.

To change your password while signed in:

  1. Click on your account icon in the upper-right corner of the screen, then choose Settings from the dropdown.

  2. Under the Account access section, enter your:

  • Current password
  • New password
  • Password confirmation Follow the password rules shown on screen (for example, minimum length and character mix).

Passwords on Handshake must:

  • Contain eight characters, or more
  • Contain characters from two of the following three character classes:
    • Alphabetic (e.g., a-z, A-Z)
    • Numeric (i.e. 0–9)
    • Punctuation and other characters (e.g.,!@#$%^&*()_+|~-=`{}[]:“;’<>?,./)
  • Note: passwords are not encrypted.
  1. Click Save new password to update your password.

I’m currently signed out of Handshake

  • Go to app.joinhandshake.com to start the password reset process.
  • Enter the email address associated with your Handshake account, then select Reset Password.
    • If you don’t have the option to reset your password, refer to Why Can’t I Log in with My Password?
  • The page will show a confirmation message such as: “Check your inbox! Follow the instructions there to continue.”
  • Go to your email inbox and open the password reset email from handshake@m.joinhandshake.com.
  • Subject: Password Reset Request
  • Select the Reset My Password link in the email.
  • You’ll be taken back to Handshake to set a new password. Enter your new password in the New password and Confirm new password fields, then select Reset.
  • The page will confirm that your password has been created. Select Log in to return to the login page and sign in with your new password. Once your password is updated, you’ll receive an email confirming that your password was recently changed.

Passwords on Handshake must:

  • Contain eight characters, or more
  • Contain characters from two of the following three character classes:
    • Alphabetic (e.g., a-z, A-Z)
    • Numeric (i.e. 0–9)
    • Punctuation and other characters (e.g.,!@#$%^&*()_+|~-=`{}[]:“;’<>?,./)
  • Note: passwords are not encrypted.
Not receiving your password reset email?

If the password reset email isn’t showing up for you, we recommend to take the steps below:

  • Check your spam and junk mail. Since this is an automated email, some providers may filter the message from your inbox. If you’re using a common mail client, you can find instructions below.
    • For Gmail
    • For Outlook
  • Keyword search all mailboxes using “Email Confirmation” (the email’s subject line). This can better surface the email if it’s been filtered to an unexpected location.
  • Add Handshake to your address book with the following contact email: “handshake@m.joinhandshake.com”. After adding this contact, resend the confirmation email from Handshake (Step 3 on the thanks for signing up page).
    • This will help ensure delivery of future emails, and is important for keeping you up to date in your professional life.
  • Contact your institution’s IT department and ask if they know of any reasons emails from Handshake would be denied. If you’ve followed all the steps above and still haven’t received your confirmation email, let us know.

Switching User Views (Your Handshake Account)

Handshake users can create multiple account types using the same email address, such as Career Services, Employer, and Student accounts.

If you have more than one account type linked to the same email address, you can switch between them without logging out.

To switch between account views, each account must be created using the same email address.

Each linked account must also have a confirmed email address before you can switch between account views.

You may need to switch account views if:

  • you are in the wrong account view
  • you cannot access certain features, such as teammate management
  • you need to complete an action that is only available to a specific account type

Switching users from a career services account

  • Click your name in the upper right corner of the Handshake screen.
  • Select Switch Users from the dropdown menu.
  • All connected accounts will be listed. Select Switch to Students Account or Switch to Employers Account, depending on which account you would like to access.

Switching users from an employer account

  • Click your name in the upper-right corner of the Handshake screen.
  • Select Switch Users from the dropdown menu.
  • All connected accounts will be listed. Select Switch to Career Services Account or Switch to Student Account, depending on which account you want to access.

Switching users from a student account

  1. Click your account icon in the upper-right corner of the Handshake screen. This may appear as your first initial or a small photo if you have a profile picture.

  2. Select Switch Users from the dropdown menu.

  3. All connected accounts will be listed. Select Switch to Career Services Account or Switch to Employers Account, depending on which account you would like to access.

If an expected account does not appear

If an expected account type does not appear in the list, or Switch Users is unavailable, confirm that each account was created with the same email address.

If your accounts use different email addresses or different email domains, Handshake treats them as separate accounts and they will not be linked for switching.

Errors when switching accounts

If you receive an error message while switching accounts, review the sections below.

Email verification required

If you receive a message indicating that you need to verify your email address, you must verify the email associated with your Handshake account.

Click the verification link in the message to receive a verification email. Then open the email and follow the instructions to complete verification.

Common reasons you may receive this message include:

  • Support manually added your account upon request
  • Support assisted with a sync and your account was not fully verified Note: Each account created in Handshake must be verified before use.
Email confirmation required

If you receive a message stating that you have not confirmed your email address, you will need to confirm the email associated with your account.

Click the link in the message to resend the confirmation email, then follow the instructions provided.

If you are not receiving the confirmation email, refer to Troubleshooting a Missing Confirmation Email.

Unsubscribe from Handshake Emails

Emails sent by Handshake serve a range of important purposes, including:

  • Password reset emails
  • Job application updates
  • Career fair and event registrations and reminders
  • Messages that help you connect with employers
  • Recommendations for jobs, events, and opportunities from your school These emails help you stay informed about activity in your Handshake account.

Email Domains Used by Handshake

Handshake emails are sent from several email domains. An email domain is the part of the email address that comes after the @ symbol.

Handshake uses these domains:

  • joinhandshake.com
  • notifications.joinhandshake.com
  • mail.joinhandshake.com
  • m.joinhandshake.com
  • g.joinhandshake.com
  • cm.joinhandshake.com Emails from these domains are legitimate Handshake messages.

Manage your email preferences in Handshake

The most reliable way to control many of the emails you receive from Handshake is to update your Notification preferences in your account. This ensures you don’t miss out on anything important, while still tailoring the messages you receive.

For step-by-step guidance, check out Managing Your Notification Preferences.

Unsubscribe from a specific email in your inbox

You can also unsubscribe from certain emails directly from your inbox.

To use the unsubscribe option in an email:

  • Open the Handshake email.
  • Go to the bottom of the message.
  • Choose one of the options that appear (options may vary by email):
    • Manage email preferences – opens your Handshake Notification preferences page, where you can review and adjust more settings.
    • unsubscribe – stops future emails of the same general category as the message, sent from the same Handshake email domain. If you select Unsubscribe, a new browser tab opens. Confirm the change by selecting Unsubscribe again.

Note: Unsubscribing this way affects only that email category from that specific email domain. You may still receive:

  • Other types of Handshake emails, and/or
  • Emails from other Handshake domains To make broader changes, update your Notification preferences in Handshake.

Want to start receiving Handshake emails again?

If you unsubscribed or changed your settings and want to receive Handshake emails again:

  • Open your Notification preferences in Handshake and confirm that the categories you want are turned on for Email.
  • If you’re still not receiving expected emails, we can help! Let our support team know the email address connected to your Handshake account.

Update Your Primary Email Address in Handshake

Your school typically creates your Handshake account using your institution-provided email address (for example, your .edu email). You can have multiple email addresses associated with your Handshake account and use any of them to sign in.

One email address is designated as your primary email, and it’s where you’ll receive messages from your school, as well as Handshake notifications and marketing communications (based on your notification settings).

If you want to receive emails at a personal email address—or if you’re graduating and want to keep access to your Handshake account as an alum, you can add a personal (alternate) email address and set it as your primary email. Your personal email address cannot already be associated with another Handshake account.

Before you start

To add or update an email address, you need:

  • Access to your existing Handshake student account.
  • Access to the inbox for the new email address, so you can confirm it.
  • An email address that isn’t already associated with another Handshake account (student, employer, or career services). If you receive an error indicating the email is already in use and need to verify whether an account exists, contact us with the email address and our support team will look into it for you. 💡Note: If your school provides multiple school email addresses, they may upload them all to help prevent duplicate accounts.

Add an additional email address

  • Click your account icon in the upper-right corner of the Handshake screen.
  • Select Settings from the dropdown menu.
  • Click Account Access.
  • Click the Add email button. The new email appears in the list as Pending until you confirm it.

Handshake sends a confirmation email to the new email address. You have 7 days to confirm the address before the request expires.

Confirm your new email

  • Open the inbox for the email address you just added.

  • Find the message from handshake@m.joinhandshake.com with a subject similar to “Confirm Your Email.”

  • Open the email and follow the Confirm button. After you confirm the email:

  • Handshake displays a success message, such as:

    • “Your email has been confirmed.”
    • “You can now use any confirmed email associated with your account to log in.”

  • If you want to receive messages from Handshake, employers, and your school at this address, you can make it your primary email from your settings.

Change your primary email

Once you have at least one confirmed alternate email—or if your school added another email for you, you can change which address is your primary email:

  • Click your account icon located in the upper right corner.

  • Click Settings from the dropdown

  • Click Account Access.

  • In the Emails list, find the address you want to make primary.

  • Click the three dots next to that email.

  • Select Set as Primary email from the dropdown. What happens next:

  • The change takes effect immediately.

  • Your new primary email moves to the top of the list and displays a purple Primary tag.

  • Your primary email is where Handshake and your school send messages and notifications.

  • If your institution imported your original school email, that address can still stay associated with your account, even if it is no longer primary. Changing your primary email does not change your login method if you normally log in with your school’s single sign-on (SSO), you can continue using SSO even after you change your primary email.

Additional Tips

  • If you do not receive the confirmation email, check spam or junk folders, then search your inbox for the subject “Confirm Your Email” or messages from handshake@m.joinhandshake.com.
  • To resend the confirmation email, click the three dots next to the pending email, and choose Resend confirmation email.
  • To remove an unconfirmed email address, click the three dots next to the email and select Delete.
  • If the confirmation link expires (after 7 days), add the email again and repeat the confirmation steps.
  • If your school email address becomes inactive, and you’ve added an additional email, Handshake will automatically send your notifications to your personal email address on file, so you never miss an opportunity.

Using Handshake After Graduation

Graduation doesn’t end your access to Handshake. As an alum, you can continue using your existing account to search for jobs, stay connected with employers, and engage with your school’s career center. This guide outlines what you can do after graduating and how to make the most of your account for long-term use.

Note: Alumni accounts aren’t separate or different—there’s no need to create a new account. Simply keep using your current one.

What you can do as an alum

You can continue to use Handshake much like you did as a student.

  • Search and apply for jobs
  • Keep your profile up to date: Add new roles, skills, and accomplishments as your career grows. A current profile makes it easier for employers to find you and judge whether you are a match for their roles. Learn more in Completing your Profile in Handshake.
  • Message and respond to employers: Employers can still reach out to you, and you can reply to learn more about roles, teams, and company culture. These conversations can lead to interviews or future opportunities. Learn more in Responding to an Employer Message on Handshake.
  • Connect with other alumni: Use Handshake to reach other alumni from your school and in your field. Alumni can share advice, referrals, and insight into different career paths.
  • Access career services resources (when available): Many schools continue to offer alumni access to events, advising, and other services through Handshake. Availability depends on your school’s policies, so check with your career center for what is offered to alumni. Tip: Don’t stop using Handshake after your first role. You can continue using it to explore your second, third, and later opportunities as your experience grows!

Keep your Handshake access after graduation

To avoid losing access when your school email or SSO changes, we strongly suggest the below before or shortly after graduation:

  • Update Your Email: Your school typically creates your account using your institution email address. To maintain long-term access, add a personal email (such as Gmail) and set it as your primary email. This ensures you can continue receiving notifications from Handshake and log in even after losing access to your school email. To learn more about updating your primary email address, refer to Update Your Primary Email Address in Handshake.
  • Create Handshake Credentials: If you previously signed in only through your school’s SSO, you’ll need Handshake-specific credentials so you can log in without SSO once you are an alum. To create your Handshake credentials, check out Log In as an Alum: Set your Handshake Password.
  • Account Approval: Some schools may require approval for alumni accounts. If this is the case, you can connect with your school’s career center for more information. To locate your school’s contact information in Handshake, refer to How to Locate your School’s Contact Information in Handshake.

Why Can’t I Log in with My Password? (Your Handshake Account)

In some cases, you may be asked to sign in using a one-time code instead of your password. This helps keep your account secure and only takes a minute to complete.

What the login page shows

When this happens, the login page will show:

  • A message stating you can’t log in with this password right now and that you should use a one-time code to sign in instead.
  • An option to send a one-time code to your email address.
  • The password field, which will no longer let you continue with password. This is a normal part of keeping your account secure. Your account has not been locked, and you have not lost access to Handshake.

How to sign in when this happens

  • On the login screen, confirm the email address shown is correct. If it’s not, select Edit to update it.
  • Click Send one-time code.
  • Check your email for the code and enter it to complete sign-in.

Miscellaneous

Insights: How to Create a Custom Report and Dashboard

If you’ve checked the legacy reports in the Hub and were unable to find any reports that fit your specific goals, you can create a custom report to better suit your desired outcome.

  • Go to Insights.
  • Select +New in the upper right corner of the screen.
  • Select a topic from the dropdown menu title Choose a starting point….
  • You can either select dimensions and filters from the left side of the screen or run a sample query using the AI assistant prompt in the center of the page. Learn more about the AI Assistant in: How to use AI in Insights
  • To run the report, select the play button in the upper right corner of the screen.
  • For this example, we picked the Employer Name and Jobs Count fields. The report displays how many job postings are connected to specific employers in Handshake.
  • If you want to turn this report into a bar graph, you can select Chart to do so. The right side of the page gives you Chart Options that you can use to change how the chart displays. For more in-depth
  • details about Charts and Chart Options, refer to the Omni article: Line Charts.
  • Once you’ve achieved the desired outcome for your query, you can save this by selecting File -> Save.
  • Omni will automatically suggest a title and description, you can either choose this or create your own title and description. Select where you wish to save this report in your documents and select Save.
  • After your report is saved, you can select the + Dashboard in the upper right corner to convert it into a dashboard. From the Dashboard page, you can Share the dashboard with others, even if they don’t have accounts on Handshake, Edit the dashboard, go back to the Workbook display of this report, and Explore to make a copy of the report and modify the copy for additional reporting.

Additional Resources

- [Handshake Academy: Custom Reporting](https://academy.joinhandshake.com/path/insights-reporting/custom-reporting)
- Omni documentation [Creating & designing dashboards](https://docs.omni.co/visualize-present/dashboards/create-design#creating-and-designing-dashboards)

Navigating Handshake Created Dashboards

Handshake created dashboards help review data using a consistent interface across Handshake. While the dashboards provide different content, most dashboards use the same navigation patterns: top-level filters, pages or tabs, dashboard tiles, field switchers, and Explore. This experience is different from previous iterations of dashboards on Handshake so it’s recommended to review the information below before using Handshake created dashboards.

Topics:

  • Where dashboards are located
    • Insights Hub
    • Specific features on Handshake
  • Navigating Handshake created dashboards
    • Filters
    • Pages or tabs
    • Field switchers
    • Dashboard tiles
  • Actions
    • Three dots menu
    • Explore

Where dashboards are located

Insights Hub

On the Insights page, under the Hub path, dashboards are available in the Handshake - Dashboards folder.

Specific features in Handshake

Some features in Handshake have dashboards available in the upper-right corner of the overview page. These features include:

  • First Destination Responses
  • Collections
  • Employers
  • Appointments

Navigating Handshake created dashboards

Filters

Filters at the top of the dashboard apply to the full dashboard unless the page specifically says otherwise.

That means these filters affect:

  • Every page or tab in the dashboard
  • Every chart or table on the dashboard First Destination Outcomes Filters/Expanded Filters Example:

Pages or tabs

Some dashboards are divided into pages or tabs so related metrics are grouped together.

For example, one page may focus on summary data while another page focuses on a specific workflow or outcome area.

Note: When you go to a different page, the top-level filters still apply unless the dashboard says otherwise.

Field switchers

Some dashboards include a field switcher inside a dashboard section.

A field switcher can look similar to a filter, but it works differently:

  • A filter changes which records are included in the dashboard results.
  • A field switcher changes how the data is displayed or grouped. For example, a field switcher may let you change a chart from one breakdown to another, such as viewing results by employer instead of another dimension. Changing the field switcher does not replace the top-level filters already applied to the dashboard.

Field Switcher example:

Dashboard tiles

Each chart, graph, or table on the dashboard is a separate dashboard tile. These tiles highlight a specific metric or view of the data.

Depending on the tile, you may be able to hover, click, or open additional options to see more detail.

All-Time Engagement by Academic Year dashboard tile example:

Actions

Three dots menu

There are three dots menus available on dashboard tiles. These nest different actions like: Explore, Download, Alert, Schedule Delivery, and Copy.

Explore

Most dashboards include an Explore action in the upper-right corner of the dashboard. You can add fields and filters to find more specific information for your needs. Learn more about customized dashboards in Insights: How to Create a Custom Report and Dashboard.

Note: The Explore action does not appear for the Collections dashboard due to the fields that are pre-selected for that specific dashboard.
